My check-out was ok, I had a hard time getting to the cashier and there were many long lines. I used the self-check out and had to get an associate to scan the 1st item. Associate was very helpful and friendly.
 
I took public transportation (subway/bus) to Ikea and it worked out ok. Much faster than I anticipated. The Bus stops nearby, outside the mall parking lot.

I'll go again to get decorating/furnishing ideas and purchase more fun items such as the acrylic red cutting I got today and 99cent pillow I got today ; )

Ikea is indeed a dangerous place. To avoid the temptation of purchasing too many products, I always bring shopping list with me; otherwise I will end up buying anything but the products I came for. 
Any time of day and any time of year, Ikea is super busy; and not even its remote South side location is able to deter shoppers from coming. In fact, it is easy to make a day out of shopping at Ikea.
 Firstly, there is an upper level with all the fantastic showrooms. I adore Ikea designers and decorators' creations: showrooms look cozy, organized, without a single spot of wasted space. Everything is color coordinated without being too matchy-matchy, and there is a nice flow to all rooms. I love that every piece of furniture can be touched, opened, sat on and overall closely inspected. I also love stealing ideas from Ikea's showrooms: )
The lower level is where all furniture parts and home accessories are. I love how Ikea attends to every storage need a human being may have, and sells such ingenious items as shoe boxes, storage with compartments and closet storage systems. 
Ikea's famous buffet is another reason why people rush in every day. Everything on the menu is inexpensive, simple and delicious.

If you like things for your house then IKEA has it all.  They have beds, sofas, bookshelves, tables, chairs, desks, bathroom stuff, kitchen stuff, pictures and more.  It's a huge place so if you go you better grab a cup of coffee and go through the place nice and slow you can enjoy all the furniture.  They style up some rooms using the furniture to show you how a small room can look great and look like it has so much space.  My friends and I love to go through and mentally list what we would put in our own apartments.  It's the best place to go and pick up things to help you organize rooms, drawers, or closets; they have so many different boxes or shelves to use for storage.  If you are starting in your own place I suggest the sofa beds they have.  They look great and depending on how much you want to spend you can find a comfortable mattress.  

Not only does IKEA sell furniture, but they also have a restaurant for really cheap.  You can make a date out of it; kind of like dinner and a movie but at IKEA its furniture and a dinner!  They also make really good cinnamon buns.  You can also pick up some Swedish meatballs, which they are famous for.  They have a whole section on food products that have been imported from Sweden.  

Also the staff is very helpful.  They can help you with measurements or style ideas for the space you have.

Oh IKEA, I love you!

This is the place to go for furniture.  For the most part, they have cheaper furniture because a lot of it is self-assembled, but they do have some that is not.  

As much as I love IKEA, some of their stuff is pretty cheap.  It has to be for the prices they have!  But it's a great place to get furniture when you are just starting out or moving out for the first time.  If you're on a budget - go to IKEA.

I like the As-Is section of IKEA because it's even cheaper!  This is where they take floor models and slightly damaged goods and mark them down.  I can usually find a pretty sweet deal here.  

I also love the Swedish food store at the end of IKEA.  You can get 2 hot dogs and a pop for something like $1.65.  It's crazy!  They also have great cinnamon buns.

The actual food they sell is good too.  Some of the frozen desserts are really good and I really like the cheeses.  You have to try the meatballs too - so yummy!

I always love looking at IKEA.  It's a good time!

Don't try to schedule deliveries with this store!  They use some company called Urban Express that is so incompetent and unreliable that you can forget about getting your items the same day even if you live within the distance and place your order before 3 PM.  We bought a mattress today to have it delivered same day, and after spending hours on the phone with IKEA reps and Urban Express we learn that t we should expect it in TWO days!  Just horrible.

Ikea is a massive furniture super store. It is great and cheap and brilliant.

It is so big you could get lost, if not for the arrows on the floors leading you to the exit. Ikea is brilliant because it makes you enter at one end of the store and pushes you to walk through the entire store before you can make it to an exit in hopes that people will find things they didn't come for and buy them. The strategy works. My advice is to come here with a friend who has self control and can control you. Never come here if you don't need anything because it will suck you in and trick you into buying stuff. 

Now that I am done making Ikea sound like some evil being, it actually has amazing things inside. Trendy furniture and decor. Even if you don't own a home they have plenty of cool things for one's room.
It is a great place to come too if you need something but be very careful because it will give you more than you came for.

It is a fact that sometimes the hubs and I spend an entire afternoon at Ikea...just for fun. It is also true that the main reason we come is for lunch and to buy tubes of fish spreads in the marketplace.

I love the food at Ikea. I always have. I have fond memories of schlepping out to the Ikea in Conshy when I was a kid and eating gravadlax and the dessert sampler (no longer available much to my chagrin). Of course those memories also include the strange children I was forced to coexist with in the ballroom...

So anyway, now when we go to Ikea, we almost always get meatballs...but there have been the few odd times that I have indeed veered out of my comfort zone...I can safely say that a cheesesteak (gasp) from Ikea is just as good as one from Jims. Seriously folks, I have lived in the 215 for 24 years (save for the four dreadful ones spent in New England) and know a good cheesesteak when I see it. 

Also, the poached salmon is decent. I have a friend that swears by the shrimp salad on toast, and my mother still always gets the gravadlax. 

Also, saving the best for last: THEY HAVE THE BEST MAC AND CHEESE. It is so delicious and chemically infused and I do love it so. 

xo

Since there are many reviews on Ikea already, I'll just add my favorite parts.
Shopping here for convenience items like over-the-door towel holders, dish drying racks, trivets, knobs, organizers, etc. is brilliant for people that are coming into their own space. It saves a lot of money (particularly when compared to Bed, Bath and Beyond) while not sacrificing style or function at all.
That being said, I would not buy furniture items here, unless your an adept do-it-yourself-er. The directions for the cabinets we installed could have been more helpful, but it was a learning experience and I would most certainly buy from them again.

Have you ever had Breakfast at Ikea? Well you won't confuse it with Breakfast at Tiffany's that's for sure! I met my buddy PJ here for breakfast before going to Home Depot to pick out a nice house plant. Everyone knows a guy like PJ, or you may be just like him yourself. You know the type, his motto is "If it's free, it's me". 
So leave it up him to find a breakfast special that includes Eggs, Bacon or Sausage and Home fies for only 99 cents! 
That's not all, you can substitute different offerings like the Swedish Pancakes with the Logganberry topping or get a side order of anything for $1.00. I'm used to paying six to eight bucks for a simple average breakfast so the possibilities were swirling in my brain, calculating just how much I can scarf up for my usual breakfast tab. 
Ikea's Kitchen is set up like an old skool cafeteria, you grab a tray, utensils, and there's cold milk and orange juice available at the beginning of the line. 
I decided to break the bank and go for it and try to sample everything. Here's the list: Scrambled Eggs, Home fries with Turkey Sausage links, Bacon, Swedish Pancakes and some kind of Fish. I added a cup of coffee and some OJ and the grand total was $5.99 plus tax. 
But wait until you run out tonight and sleep on the payment in front of the store to be sure you get a place at the table. 
The food was OK, a notch above school cafeterias and the place was spotless with plenty of seating with a view of the Delaware River. The portions are small and and a little lukewarm for my taste. 
Fortunately there's a microwave right in the seating area. Overall it was a pleasant experience and PJ felt like Diamond Jim Brady when he took care of the check. I even got to buy one of those fake Chinese paper lantern thingys on the way out.

$ .50 hot dogs & the ligonberry soda are a good thing but the upstairs food is sub par. The soup was good as were the veggie pattys but the wraps were runny & bland, the apple cake was dry, fell apart, & bland, and what ever forgetable side we had was well, forgetable.

If IKEA was a theme-park, I'd buy the year round ticket just to visit it everyday! 

The first largest home furniture store in Tampa! I find the location of the store a little odd, I mean as if Downtown isn't small enough but how the cooperates and architectures can manage to fit such a monster in the area is simply in AW and brilliant idea, because it's the giant blue and yellow building is visible from miles away on the freeway! Parking is organized with IKEA's parking coordinators(?), assisting you to the right parking spot (just like DisneyWorld!) 

The magic happens on the 2nd floor of the build, displaying everything from spoons to sofas and everything in between. The Swedish furniture styles are modern and simple, all at an affordable price. That being said, the quality is obviously not up to par with Robb & Stucky or Kanes. The building is so well organized and entertaining that getting lost isn't something to fear. And if in deed you do  get lost, there are large yellow arrows labeled on the ground as well as maps located through out the store( it's THAT big!) They have a Kiddy Center where you can have your kids babysit by the IKEA babysitter while you shop and also a mini food court, also located on the 2nd floor (inexpensive). When all is done, you can head down to the first floor to retrieve your items all boxed up and ready to go.

It really is a wonderful joyous place to shop and be entertained! Its nearly impossible to leave IKEA empty handed. Even if you don't need anything, you'll end up wanting everything.

When I got my drivers license, one of the first things I did was go with my friends to Ikea...not for furniture but for their 50 cent hot dogs and $1 ice cream. Sure it cost more for gas and insurance, but it was still an enjoyable trek.

Back then this was a stand alone building in the middle of a field. Now the South Edmonton Common development is starting to catch up and engulf this building. It's not a bad thing, I just wish the roads were better.

Whether you're looking for furniture or just table top accessories (read: shot glasses), Ikea has everything you're looking for. They have a wide selection in every department, and it's hard not to find something for home, even if you weren't looking for something in the first place. One of my favorite sections is the bedding, as they try and recreate a bedroom feel by putting up walls with a fake tv on one of their desks- it helps you visualize how things could look like.

I like how there are short cuts through the store too. It is very big and can be easy to get lost. Ikea is definitely on top of my list for furniture, and stop in their cafeteria- their $2 pasta and $1 ice cream is a good deal!

This place was MOBBED yesterday- a Sunday at 3pm. It was too crowded- and they were out of what we were there to get. 

I know there are only two Ikeas in the area but this one gets WAY more traffic than the one forty minutes away in Conshy. (I know because we went there right after and they had our stuff.)

I was all ready to swear off Ikea all together...until yesterday.

We went to the Phila. location earlier in the day and quickly left after we found they didn't have what we needed in stock.

This location was MUCH less crowded and only forty minutes away from the city I'd suggest going to this location every time. 

We bypassed the Marketplace and went right into self serve to pick out our items- they weren't labeled as clearly as they were in the Phila location but there were several "co-workers" (that's what they call them- I think it's funny) available to help. 

Another plus- there were self-serve registers opened and we were in and out of the store with the car packed in a HALF HOUR.

Also- we purchased the Mammut baby crib- it was SO EASY to put together- only about 6 pieces and 40 accessories (screws and such.) I was thoroughly pleased.

The old IKEA was across the street from the old Holiday Inn The Palace and was a much smaller store.  When the present one opened up closer to the Airport, it was big and as Tim R. says it was all by its lonesome.  And now that the Borg Collective (South Edmonton Common) has assimilated most of the surrounding prairie, it's just part of a larger and disorienting suburban shopping experience.

Of course, where ever you go Ikea-wise, there you are.  They all pretty much have the same stuff and the food is good and cheap.  So if you need that nice looking and relatively inexpensive Chesterfield of acceptable quality for your den, what are you waiting for?

So...once again I am obsessed with furniture stores! So the opening of Ikea was like a little piece of heaven for me! What I wasn't prepared for was feeling like I was walking through a Disney theme park by the end of my visit. I also wasn't prepared for being completely lost and having NO IDEA how to get out of the place. 

But...once I found a map and convinced myself I wouldn't die cold and alone in aisle 47, I was back in business. 

[+] 
- Cheap prices & modern pieces (think Forever 21) 
- SHOWROOMS....they were fabulously put together 
- Cafeteria with cheap food 
- Tons of employees ready to help 
- Tons of parking 

[-] 
- The crowds, the crowds, the crowds. (my advice is go Mon-Thu in the middle of the day...but I am a college student so my schedule has a little more free time than most) 
- The place is a maze, there is no way around it. 
- Putting the furniture together is a pain. 
- I understand they are going the green route by not offering paper/plastic bags when you check out but carrying all my stuff in hand is very annoying...very annoying

at the end of the day...

If you come on a Saturday afternoon just prepare to have a horrible time. Honestly, between the strollers, the crowds and the confusion, the place is a mad house. But on a reasonable day you can have a really great experience. 

I love their textiles. They are cute, modern and cheap! And I absolutely love the showrooms and I like that they connect the rooms almost like the layout of a house or apartment. And while I probably wouldn't furnish my entire place through Ikea, they have reasonably priced items that are cute and unique!

Who doesn't love Ikea just a little bit? Even if you are not a fan of their "swedish-inspired" stye, it is still fun to go for a saunter through and check out their mini-rooms and lay on the beds.

I shop here often because I am a student and the thought of spending more than $30 on a duvet cover terrifies me. The prices here are amazingly cheap, but the crappy thing is that it reflects in the quality. It depends on what you are buying, but I would not spend money on a house hold staple (like kitchen cabinets, a leather couch or expensive chair) because even though it is cheaper than the "big guys", the quality is not there and it is not worth the money.

This place can get pretty crazy on the weekend-- Saturdays especially. If you are not a fan of screaming children and crying babies then I would try to avoid this place on Saturday and Sundays.

Food 1* - Its cheap and nasty.  It tastes like you're eating ground up furniture.

Service 2* - I have run into a few nice workers here, but most of them have bad attitudes, or pretend like they can't speak English unless I comply and use IKEA terminology.

Store Layout 1* - It's like a maze; it's meant to confuse but all it does is waste my time and forces couples to get into fights with each other.

Products 2* - Although there are very nice finds and cool looking stuff here, 90% of the stuff falls apart with a little use. Almost everything is made of VERY low quality compressed ground wood. Almost all fabrics seem like slave labor products.  Actually, the rugs are not Rugmark rugs and so ARE made by slaves.  The products are way overpriced for the quality. The plants from this place seem to die at a high rate.  They do sell dead plants and pots without soil in them, as in they feed them that fertilizer chemical crap so that they can grow without sun, but soon as you start feeding them water, they die.  Electronics, light bulbs or anything with a fuse in it dies at an abnormally fast rate.

Returns - No receipt = no return or store credit

I dread coming here. It actually feels like a chore or punishment

I gave it 4 $-signs, because there are hidden costs when shopping here.

Dare I say, you're better off shopping at Walmart....

You can think whatever you want about ikea but i have NO complaints.  Affordable yet stylish and tons of useful stuff.  I always get my shower curtain liners here (super cheap and lasts!), tealights (super cheap for a 100 pack), little potted plants ($1!!!!) and picture frames (great gifts).

Service here is friendly and helpful just like all ikeas (right?).  And it's never overcrowded so it's a nice shopping experience.
And you can always afford a treat after shopping...$1 soft serve (vanilla, chocolate or mixed) or cinnamon buns and 50 cent hot dogs.  All prices include tax!

Ikea, I love you.....but you're bringing me down.

I first discovered the existence of Ikea a good 10 years ago. I thought it was the most fantastic place on Earth. My heart still swells a bit when I enter through the sliding doors. That is, until I start walking around.
It's not even the store really, and really how can the employees compete with 2 billion indecisive asshats a day? Usually we just skip the showroom area and head right to the marketplace. Get in, get out. Except...getting out can never be that easy, can it?
The past few times I've been here, they've literally had maybe 10 aisles open (out of, maybe 30?) and at least 20 people in each aisle. This is the point at which I wait, while dude gets ice cream. Or dude waits, while I continue shopping. It's the only way to pass time. 
When you get up to the checkout, it's clear that the employees want to die...and I commiserate, because I also want to die. I recall one time being here, and being so exhausted from waiting and walking behind slow people and searching and decision making, that I dropped a vase after I had paid for it. I had expected the employee to call someone to get me a new one or tell me to go get a new one....but he ignored me. Nice!
All in all, whatever crap I have to say about this place doesn't matter, because I'll still go. We'll all still go. And we'll all wait in line together, complaining and staring at other people's carts of swedish junk. 

(I should mention that I also used to work here a while ago for a very short time....in the "food service" department, all until a coworker followed me home, thus I never returned. good times.)

IKEA has perfected destination furniture shopping.  It's truly enjoyable to go walk around the store, even if you don't have anything you need to buy.  The restaurant is pretty good--I always get the swedish meatballs, yum!

In terms of their furniture, for the most part, it's decent stuff at great prices.  There's really no better place to get cheap stuff that actually looks half decent; it's not going to last forever, but for what it is, it's great.

Cheap, tasty food.  I know, it's a store.  BUT, I come here to eat just as much as I come here to shop.  There is fat free frozen yogurt for 99 cents!  Tell me where else in the city you can find that.  You come in, go upstairs, have tasty lunch well under 10 bucks, shop around, and grab another tasty cheap snack after checkout.

I have been to Ikea for 2 geocache events recently. I have enjoyed both breakfast and dinner here. The price is right especially for an unemployed foodie like me! The breakfast was much more enjoyable than greasy overpriced diner food. I am trying not to eat carbs since I am getting married in a few months. I had 5 swedish meatballs for a BUCK! I also purchased a plate full of steamed veggies for a dollar as well. Both were very good. Not gourmet food, but for the price it was great. My veggies were a little on the cold side but still edible. The place is always clean and we enjoy coming here for Geocache events. They also have free cache size pencils by the bathrooms!!!

I go to IKEA for the food sometimes and for geocaching events because some geocaching events have been held at the dining area in this IKEA location. I think the food is okay. Portions are on the small side but prices are not unreasonable.

I'm a bit nervous about IKEA furniture because everything looks like it may collapse under my weight. IKEA accessories and knick-knacks are not too attractive to me, although IKEA batteries seem inexpensive. Watch for discounted items when you shop the marketplace. The long checkout lines have always been a problem. No idea when the best time is to avoid lines at IKEA. Maybe at night or on weekdays.

This IKEA was SO MUCH FUN. I never went to one before and this was the best experience I could have asked for. My parents and I spent a whole day shopping to furnish my apartment. They service was great and the location was perfect for where I am currently living. They delivered my big furniture for $60! 
The furniture is very basic, and yet they have accessories and styles that are way better then any shit you'd find at like Bed Bath and Beyond or whatever. It's more function over anything. I wanted a small couch that had a pull out bed for guests? They had it. I wanted a desk with shelves above the desk? Got it. 
OH, and one last thing: THE FOOD. I eat their lox on a daily basis. And they have a dessert called "Appelkaka" which is just funny. Oh those Swedes!

I love Ikea's products but this store is a mess. I can't find anything that I'm looking for in this mess.
I want to give you my money. Fix this.

I hope no one pays to remove the review.

So I go to this IKEA once a week. I suppose, I am little bit of an "Ikea-a-holic". Everything in my apartment is from IKEA and a lot of it is over 5 years old and holding strong. Much of it is also from curb alerts, or just walking home and finding IKEA furniture outside my house. I've been going to this IKEA for years, and my favorite things are as follows:

The As-Is department- like I said I go often, so I generally know what's in their catalog at any given time so much of the stuff in their AS-IS department is in perfect working order just for cheap. Hello cheap, we love you. 

The foodery. you can to IKEA, you're grueling through redecorating your friends place AND you didn't eat. Well IKEA has great cheap eats ranging from simple to fancy and all their hot cafeteria style food is really actually good.

The delivery section will hold your furniture for you for the day for free if theirs a really cheap as is piece you want and you didn't bring your car, or your car is too small and you need to go get a zipcar truck. no problem.

The rest of the store stands for itself as it is exactly like every IKEA everywhere. You find the piece of furniture you want in it's easily laid out upstairs showroom OR categorized section, you take down the location, then you go find it. If you can't find it, you ask an employee for help, it's so simple baby chimps can handle it.

I usually do most of my shopping online to find what I want and then just go to pick it up. If you you have a small car and have IKEA furniture already, definitely bring an allen wrench/ hex key that way you can disassemble your as is finds and load them easier.

Okay, this is a guilty food pleasure, but I recommend Ikea for a cheap, quick fix with actual good flavors for any family. Avoid the even worse trappings of a fast-food restaurant and the stress of child behavioral modifactions in a regular restaurant by heading up to the 2nd floor and getting swedish meatballs, a soup or salad, a nice drink and a dessert. Don't just get a kids meal b/c the kids love the swedish meatballs! The kids meal isn't as good, unless your child is super picky. Last, watch your kids swell with pride as they carry their own trays to their own child-friendly seating area. And relax as they are fully occupied and getting fully fed! Easy parking, too!

Besides the badly made everything, i dont see any reason to hate ikea. items are cheap, you change them every year or so after they are chipped from nothing.. really not reason to grumble. Every single ikea is huge, so it's fun to walk around and do some money throwing down the toilet :)

I bike here for their low-fat frozen yogurt for $1.  Usually don't need anything else but I love their kichen/dining dept.  They have really nice storage items, and I was impressed with some of the eclectic little gems (like fish-shaped ice cube holders) they had.  

But the yogurt keeps me on my bike, and it's a much better reason and way to get some exercise (no guilt, no gym!)

Bought a plant here a couple weeks ago and took a turn for the worse pretty quickly. I figured that it would not be an issue to get it replaced or a store credit. WRONG. After waiting in returns for 10 minutes or so the cashier told me that I could have purchased it anywhere since I did not have a receipt. The fact that the pot had the Ikea label on it did not matter.  She told me to wait for a manager - after 10 more minutes of waiting she showed up and then searched the computer for a record of the transaction using both my license and credit card.  After that she gave me an "Ikea Return Card" - it had that printed on the card so they must have people make returns without a receipt often enough to have need for the card.  

So - they get one star for taking almost 30 minutes to do what any other retailer would do in under 5 minutes.

I should have reviewed this store awhile ago. I frickin love this store!! IKEA is beyond cheap! If you are on a budget, then this is the place for you. The store is super organized, clean, and has almost everything you would need in terms of textiles, organization, furniture, etc.

I like the fact that it has a self-service feel, yet there are a lot of people working there to help you if you need it.

And did I mention their awesome food?? All I have to say is one thing: cinnamon buns! They were fresh and oh so delish and awesome.

Nothing spectacular. No different that any other IKEA I have gone to. Sometimes the register line is way way long even off hours. I do enjoy $1 ice cream and cheap breakfast though. I'm not too keen on furniture here.

We have enjoyed shopping at IKEA and also working with Debra for hosting events.  It has been a great pleasure working with her staff and inviting our clients to participate with our wine seminars and workshops.  IKEA is more than a store it is a community partnership and great way to have fun shopping and enjoying their special treats!

Charles "the wine guy"

IKEA basically rules when you're a broke college student.

I've had no gripes about it during the year or so that it's been open in Tampa, except for one exchange I had to make (which was promptly resolved). The employees are generally helpful and the sales that the store features are overwhelmingly awesome.

An aspect of the store that I very much appreciate is the home model section, in which sample homes are arranged. It's good for brainstorming for one's own home as well as pricing.

Great place to go shop for furniture. Love how upstairs they have displays with the furniture in order to get a visualization of how the furniture would look and then to make things easier they have all their furniture downstairs in aisles with numbers to make things easier to find. But be careful some items made be scratched and stuff so make sure you check your furniture and small stuff for scratches and stuff before you buy it.

I love IKEA! It's like a whole new world. I have bought so much furniture from them, its very affordable. They have a section for clearance/damaged items, and you can save lots of money even if it just has a scratch! Very helpful for a poor college student. I spend hours here, even when I have no money. They also have frozen yogurt on your way out.

I'm just not certain why anyone would go here when there are so many better options in Philly for inexpensive furniture.  I've had so many bad experiences with the low quality furniture at Ikea I can't possibly relate all of them.  Particle board book shelves that sag under the weight of a few paperbacks, cheap pine dining room chairs (I forget the cute name they gave them) with legs that fell off (I only weigh about 150 lbs) within a few months.  Come on, you can get much better furniture for half the price if you're willing to buy used.  Otherwise, you save money in the long run but spending a little more upfront to not have to replace your furniture every six months.  

They have some of the lowest quality furniture out there.  Add to that the lab rat maze layout of the store (That I think is common to all Ikeas no?) and the disgruntled staff and you have yourself one of the worst shopping experiences in the city.

I hate this store, it is what it is.  It's overpriced cheaply made furniture that you have to shop for, cart, tote, and assemble yourself.  The price for a bedroom set or anything other than one piece adds up so quickly that you're better off going to a furniture store and getting real wood.  I think if people took time to compare the price of real furniture that could last a lifetime compared to the pressed particle board that so easily bends, breaks, tears, etc., there would be no hesitation to buy better stuff.  Ashley or another reasonably priced furniture retailer should open up next door.  Also, every employee seemed miserable, which added to my own misery in this warehouse of crap.

Some people view IKEA as a mystical Scandinavian wonderland. Some people view it as an unholy pressboard hell. 

It is neither.

What IKEA sets out to do is to provide low-cost, moderate quality, minimal home furnishings for those of us who 1) like the look 2) can't, or don't want to, shell out large amounts of money and 3) change tastes or homes so often, it's not worth buying the higher-end stuff (college students and young couples, I am looking at you).

This location is much like the others around the country. In this case, the top floor is the model showroom and the bottom is the warehouse. If you have no need to traverse the whole showroom, there are shortcuts to skip whole sections; look at the provided store directory for help. The restaurant, where you can get reasonably priced wraps, salads, entrees, and dessert, is also on the second floor. There is also a little dining area on the ground floor near the checkout where you can buy hot dogs for $.50 and bottles, bags, and containers of food to take home. I recommend the Swedish meatballs and the cinnamon buns.

A note on the quality of furniture: I find it depends on the piece and the person. I don't consider myself or my household gentle but I have a few IKEA pieces that are not only over seven years old, but have survived several moves, including one from NYC to FL, and still look fabulous.

Overall, I give IKEA four stars for succeeding at it's goal. The last star is for it's catalog; If you like the clean, contemporary look or ever need to figure out how to stuff an entire apartment into 300 sq ft, the IKEA catalog is an amazing source of inspiration, even you end up buying your furnishings elsewhere.

Ever wonder what happened to all of that yellow, abrasive, smelly, un-soft foam you only used to see at your grandparents' house? Wonder no more--it's the primary cushioning material in most of IKEA's absurdly-overpriced furniture. 

If you're reading this and desperately in need of cheap furniture to sit on, don't get it from IKEA. There are lots of places in and around Philly where you can get a chair, sofa, loveseat, or mattress that is affordable, comfortable, and of good quality. IKEA is not one of these places. Or, hell, go to one of the hardware stores near IKEA and buy some real wood (not particle board) and build your own furniture--it'll cost less and you'll only have yourself to blame if it falls apart.

This place is slowly taking a decline for two main reasons.

1) Less variety
There is a smaller variety than they've had in the past
(For example, I was looking for shower curtains. Last year around this time, they had curtains in almost every color of the rainbow. This year they had 2 solid colors and 2 patterns (with those two colors) Very disappointing!)

2) Crowds. 
Word must be out because it's been so crowded the last few times I've been here! I've tried going different times of the day, but haven't been able to avoid the bulk of the masses yet. When all I'm buying is a pack of tealights or chocolate, I'd like to wait in a line of less than 10 people with 20 things apiece. Okay, thanks.

The chocolate at the register is still one of my reasons for going though!

So, just biking around the city, I found myself at the IKEA again for their great-tasting $1 no tax vanilla frozen yogurt.  Of course, there were about 10 other people in front of me, but I had my cone in hand in about 2 minutes.  Delicious vanilla!

I also found they have these really cute ziploc containers for an excellent price (50 small bags for $2.99, in various sizes, 30 larger for $4).  They are very cute as they are multi-colored with cute little geometric designs to make your lunchtime or organizing fun.

They happened to be out of the awesome stainless steel espresso machine I went to go look at, but I guess they sold out!

The lines are always long there, but the self check out is actually really fast.

I've a few more Ikea items that deserve gushing about, adding to my previous list: 

Record shelf. French press for my morning coffee. Round doormat made out of astroturf. Round bath mat. Pink cat food placemat with cartoons of skeletal fish.  Bright blue ceramic plant pot that looks perfect with an ivy growing out of it. DVD boxes that are perfect for storing 45s. Daim cake. 

And since when did Ikea serve marzipan? xo.

Answer two questions:

1) Do you want IKEA furniture?

2) Do you want new furniture but on the cheap?

3) Do you live within 20 minutes drive of this IKEA?

If you answered yes to any of these questions then you should go here.

Pro tip: Their cheesesteaks are actually pretty decent.

I am not a heroin addict. But thanks to IKEA, I have this mean looking scar down my left arm that looks like a once infected needle track mark. I was moving an IKEA dresser and it fell apart, and took a good chunk of the inside of my elbow with it on the way to the floor. After stopping the bleeding using some non-FDA approved Chinatown medicine, the dresser was nailed back together. 

The store itself is really fun to walk through but you either come away with a good deal, or you come away with a bunch of Swedish crap that you just don't need (e.g. a garlic clove peeler, really?). The food is really cheap. Fifty cents for a hot dog? That puts even McDonald's to shame, which just makes me wonder what exactly is in IKEA's food to where they can sell it so ridiculously cheap?

The actual items: you get what you pay for (i.e. it's cheap so you can't be upset when the pressed particle board crumbles because you looked at it too hard) and it looks chic (when it's not trying to kill you). The appliances and furniture are super flimsy but damn if they don't look sexy. It ultimately gives the illusion of style without breaking your wallet; assuming you have some sense of control when you're in the store and don't just start buying every useless trinket you come across. I'm still sort of a fan. Plus scars are hot on a guy right?

Gotta love IKEA!  Where else can you find everything to decorate your 'living space' at surprisingly low prices, enjoy a Swedish meal, and feel like you're in a different country?
Plus, if you change your mind about a purchase that is unused and/or have the original packaging, you have 90 days to return it, just save your receipt, and you're good to go!  Happy Shopping!

IKEA is a great company with very good business practices. They do what they do very well, and their product is the good value for the level of materials and workmanship.

The problem with IKEA arises when people don't take it for what it is: disposable, mediocre, contemporary furnishings. If you expect to wow your friends and family with your design savvy, or that your products will last more than 1-2 years, you're living in a dream world.

Even over a relatively short term, say 10 years, you'll end up spending FAR more on replacing IKEA furniture and lighting than you ever would at a reputable boutique like 29 Armstrong or Dwell Modern - unless you're the kind of person that would rather collect a bunch of junk instead of having a few special pieces.

Everybody know this place is great!

You can shop, eat, and entertain yourself by cute little house stuff.
Who would have thought that such tasty food could come from a country whose national pastime is committing suicide?

I could spend a day in Ikea. Picture lounging in the morning in one of their bedroom set-ups, stopping into the fast food lounge for a hot dog at lunch, going back upstairs to hang out in a living room, and rounding off the day with a full chicken dinner at the restaurant.

Not only does Ikea feature a massive warehouse of inexpensive furniture, its massive upstairs is a wonderland of room ideas to take home with you. Whether you are a modern sophisticate, you actually like the dorm room look, or you want your kitchen to be cozy, Ikea has set up a room that fits your tastes. What's really handy are the pre-made item cards and pencils at each station, where you can write down item #s from each room to pick up from the warehouse downstairs.

Ikea wins major points for being well-rounded. By that, I mean there is a huge range of products for every room in your house. Whether you are re-decorating your office, bedroom, living room, bathroom, kitchen, childrens' bedroom, guest bedroom, etc. you can find pieces for it at Ikea. Ranging from large pieces (entire wardrobe and conference sets) to dainty tea cups, Ikea really does have it all.

Swing by now and then to find their seasonal items, too. My visit earlier this week was a major scoop for the news on the cutest Christmas items. Ikea is carrying full Christmas trees as well as smaller decorations for shoppers on a budget.

You will be hungry, though, after your trip through this massive store. Luckily, Ikea serves cheap fast food (50 cent hot dogs!) and cheap dinner fare, too (full chicken dinner for $10).

Just make sure you think before you buy: that coffee table may take you three hours to put together! But it will be beautiful when you are done.

I'm a huge Ikea believer.  Let's focus on the furniture, first.  They have a decent range of furniture collections, from the cheap, college dorm kinda stuff to the trendy bachelor(ette) pad in downtown stuff and finally the reliable and expensive "real" furniture for those who own a home.  I love assembling Ikea furniture.  It's surely a lot of fun - but don't assume it's going to be done in an hour.  I think, as others have noted, even a simple looking coffee table could end up taking over an hour ... follow the instructions properly!! Unless you're the handyman kinda guy (gal).

So, yes ... the furniture is nice and all .. now the other stuff is also good.  Their "lower level" stuff that they sell are quite decent.  Cutlery, window panes, rugs, art work, lighting - oh wow..... what modern lighting, kitchen utensils.  Then there's the kids room stuff that's really cool etc.  All these things have a similar range in prices, from the cheap to the expensive.

Generally, it's a great place to buy things if you're in a transitory phase .. like just in town for a couple of years.  I'm curious to see whether serious home owners would buy furniture from Ikea .. i'm sure the lower level things are still great and they probably do buy that ... but the actual furniture that fills their home - it would be interesting to find out. 

Ah yes ... finally .. like many reviewers that go gaga over the hot dogs and breakfast .. I must say that they are a perfect compliment to a tiring and enduring experience at the store.  I personally wouldn't go to Ikea for the food but I definitely think it's a great idea, given that Ikea is like a family store ... it's nice that families can come with their kids and feed them some decent food and then get around to their business of picking the right sofa set.  By the way, Ikea's Småland is a great place to leave your kids, when you go shopping.  By the way, after checkout, don't forget to wander around in the foods section.  They have some nice stuff.  I've bought their cheese.  It's really good.  It's all so very unique and not-Canadian, that it sometimes is a good idea to buy some swedish gravy sauce or whatever from Ikea .. sure makes you feel like a global citizen :-)

Oh, Ikea, you sly fox. Always presenting me with things I never knew I needed!! And leading an entire area of mostly Italian South Philadelphians to attempt to - and effectively butcher - the beautiful Swedish language with your hilariously, seemingly phonetically named products!

When this Ikea opened within 5 minutes of my house, it was like something overtook the entire neighborhood. When there's absolutely nothing to do, there's Ikea! Do you want a side of food with your decor shopping? That's there too! Even with my horrifically bad stomach, I recommend the mac & cheese, which had me almost licking the real stoneware plate!

From when I was a reckless wee tot until now, a severely clumsy 22-year-old, I've always had Ikea furniture somewhere in my bedroom. I guess my parents' thoughts behind this was if I somehow managed to blow it up, or fall into it Molly Shannon-style and smash it to bits, it'd be easily replaceable. And yes, I have collided with tons of Ikea bureaus and dresses and mirrors in my day, and they all survived, looking sharp as a penny (me, not so lucky). 

The stuff is quite inexpensive to buy, and I imagine it takes a rocket scientist to put it together, but all over, it can really make a space look nice on the cheap. I've got tons of little cubbies, mugs, plates, organizers - you name it - and they've all held up remarkably well, most better than the very expensive pieces I own. They even sell ranges for the kitchen! None of which I'm allowed near.

This Ikea, while monstrously huge, is very easy to navigate. I love that in any Ikea I've been to, there are no pushy, LUSH-esque salespeople hounding you, but they are there if you need them. I love trying out the chairs, stools, dressers, even that awesome air bed I got stuck in as an 8-yr-old til my heart's content. This location is very clean it seems, and checkout, while the lines are daunting, is fairly quick and very painless.

This is a great location with a great selection.

And they don't get angry if I accidentally knock over a shelf of WAHL KLOCKS!

More than the furniture, I go here for edible goodies from Sweden. When I was in Sweden a few years ago I tried their smoked roe and cream cheese spread for breakfast and got hooked. After loading up on them at a Swedish supermarket, I found out that I can also buy it at Ikea along with crab pate, salmon, etc.

The lingonberry, elderflower, Swedish strawberries, etc are also worth trying. If you have a sweet tooth, try some of the marzipan sweets and the princess cake...yuuuuhhmmmm.

Not everyone loves Ikea, but that's cool.  I love Ikea not only because I'm cheap, but because I love to meander through the store and browse.  I remember when I was a kid it was always a big deal for my parents to take us to the old Plymouth Meeting Ikea.  It was so much fun.  I can never seem to spend less than an hour here.

Some people say their furniture is crap.  You get what you pay for.  They have different price brackets to chose from.  If you buy a desk for $20, you get a desk that's worth $20.

Last but not least- get a frozen yogurt for a dollar on your way out!  I can never say no.

This review is for Ikea's cafe rather than the store. Is it me, or do the offerings just scream "kids' food"? 

In fact, with the trays and the mediocre selections, this place reminds me of a high school cafeteria. I'm a vegetarian and the only thing I could see fit to eat was mac and cheese, and my friend got the same, plus chicken fingers, fries and chocolate cake. Exactly what a little kid would like. 

The two ice cream scoops of mac and cheese were mushy and the cheese was weirdly fluffy, which made me suspicious of the ingredients. The ligonberry juice was pretty good, but it wasn't cold enough. But what do you expect? It's an Ikea cafeteria. When we left I was still hungry.

I'm giving it three stars because I love Ikea the store and there's no seperate listing for the cafeteria, but I wouldn't bother eating here again.

This is a nice big IKEA, pretty standard as far as Ikea's go.  I believe it is about the same size as the one in Conshohocken.  Plenty of cool furniture, and cool things to eat, both familiar and foreign. I'm still confused and perplexed by some of the names for things..."holmbo"?

Ikea - you dirty whore.  

You entice me with your colorful, inexpensive, and sleek furniture, housewares, and decor.  I go to visit you, and you leave me sweaty (from lugging large amounts of merch), and penniless.  

I can't go on like this anymore, your stuff is all over my place.  In my kitchen,  living room, and even (blush) bedroom.

I... I, uh... I think I'm in love.

i want to live in one of their fake rooms! i love ikea furniture, mostly because it's inexpensive. the accessories and decor stuff are adorable. this store is way better than the one in south philly, by far. i think it is because the staff is friendly and happy to help. it gets a little crowded, and people tend to let their awful children run amok, but other than that, i make the trek here to stock up on essentials. the self checkout lanes make things easy too (but no matter what lane you get in, there will be a long line).

I love walking through Ikea.  There are all kinds of neat things that I never would have thought to buy.  They even have this set-up where they took a space the size of a prison cell and installed a kitchen, dining room, bedroom, foyer and washroom.  All to make a point about functionality in limited space.  Brilliant!

A word of advise though... Bring a truck.  My wifes Focus just about screamed at me when I started ramming bags of crap into it.

I absolutely love this place!  One of the places to spend a day off with my husband.  So many stuff with very affordable prices.  So far, we have bought a bed frame, a night stand, two dressers and a book shelf.  So far nothing wrong with the products.  I think they are sturdy and very stylish  If you do not mind assembling, this place has a lot to offer.

If you are in the grocery section you have to get the swedish meatball and gravy in the big bag.  If you want to try at the food court, they sell the meatball with gravy and a side of mashed potato with cranberry sauce.  They are usually $2.99 but sometimes $1.99!  I have to get them everytime we go there.

I've had nothing but good experiences at this IKEA (with 1 exception, but it's not the fault of the store). Each time I've gone in, I've been able to find exactly what I needed and for a decent price. If anything I wish I could've gotten more. As for the furniture, a couple of my bed planks are broken, but everything else is holding up just fine.

I really dig the dining area they have in there... the meatballs, garlic bread, mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce, and lingonberry juice are ALL on point! I went there just to eat one time honestly (after shopping at Best Buy).
I like IKEA because they are always having a 50% off sale; it's called Craig's List.

It's Ikea, I mean, they've perfected the process of finding the cheapest most mass-produced crap that is both palatable yet slightly unsatisfying to almost everyone equally. I'm not really sure at this point if I'm reviewing the food or the furniture, yet. Hmm, I used the word "palatable," I guess I'll go with the food.

So, yeah, it's Ikea. If you've eaten at one, they're all the same. Their cafeteria is best during school hours on school days (to avoid the herds of screaming children barely controlled by their parents) which is coincidentally, the only good time to shop for pressboard (oops, I mean furniture). I've had both breakfast and lunch, and neither were spectacular, but it filled the belly, thus achieving my purpose.

The most unique part of the dining experience is being able to sit and look out at the decaying SS United States on the Delaware. Or explaining to my wife why they don't have underground parking like every other Ikea (psst, it has something to do with the water level that close to the river.)

Great store, low prices, and love the do-it yourself furniture.  You can spend hours just looking at all the displays.  Give credit to Swedes for the elaborate designs and efficient business processes.

This was my first visit to Ikea and I am primarily reviewing their cafeteria.  Wow, they had a cafeteria!  So of course I had to try the "Swedish" food since Ikea is a Swedish company.  I put that in quotes because I am not sure how true to Swedish cuisine was my experience.  

Of course I had the Swedish meatballs with mashed potatoes and lingonberry jam.  Seven hours later I was still experiencing it in the form of belches.  Ugh.  I also tried the Swedish almond cake.  It was bland, and not too sweet, which I normally like, but it sure needed it this time.  It had a lemon frosting which was not very lemony.  It should have been.

We had been told that they have decent kitchen stuff cheap.  I tried to find a good-sized red wine glass.  None.  Even Target has red wine glasses.  I tried to find a decent-sized chopping block with grooves around the edge.  None were big enough, except one which was titanic and extremely heavy.  Ah well.  There are many stores that have chopping blocks.

I can see how some people like this place, I particularly liked some of the light fixtures both for design and price, but I won't be back.

Every time I've been in there the store is has been clean and presentable. I've never had a problem with costumer service there. I'm not thrilled about the location of store but, that aside, I'll be returning.

not sure how anyone could hate on ikea. its the best furniture store in the world. 

cheap prices. quality products. if you have an issue or missing a part, they'll replace it. ikea has never let me down. 

design is always stylish and modern. the design team at ikea is great. 

best part about ikea? the food court. been walking around all day shopping? end it or take a break with some delicious swedish meatballs. 
amazing.

I love ikea. Even if I don't need anything from this store its fun wandering around this store. Oddly, I'd come here only to eat...it's so funny really enjoying the food at a furniture store.

**Funny story, I'm redecorating my place so I want basic inexpensive furniture and I went to Ikea to buy some things an hour before closing time. I opted to grab some fries and chicken tenders but they didn't have a togo bag, so the person put the plate of food in front of me anyway. soooo I took it and I sat down and ate.lol I ate all the fries but I wrapped up the chicken tenders in napkins and put them in my purse.haha

Soo after my snack I journeyed into the store to find an entertainment center (of which I created using various items from Ikea), a table (got a bar table of which I need to find bar stools now) and a new bedding cover (I purchased a nice simple black one). 

I had to make two trips to Ikea to purchase everything but all in all I'm satisfied with my purchase. One of the store employees were really nice too, he helped me put this huge box in my car. I couldn't make sharp turns on my way home.lol! (sardine can mode)

My only negatives I have with Ikea is a lot of the furniture doesn't maintain its integrity if unassembled and resembled. The instructions annoy me (just b/c they do), my cart is always wobbly, I always get lost in the store. The expensive dresser I bought three years ago is crumbling.

Other than that, Ikea serves its purpose and I'll always be a fan.

It's been a long time since I've been to an IKEA.  Interestingly, we went here for food.  Strange, I know.

My sister was looking for caramel licorice for a gift to my son.  We found it.  It's quite tasty.  We tried some other treats.  I found some toffee that was awesome!

The lady who worked in the department could not have been more accommodating.  She gave us tastes of whatever we wanted.  This was quite convenient to get to.

I enjoy going to Ikea to pick up householdy odds and ends for really cheap. They actually have decent glassware and it only costs about $1 per glass. Bedding and bathroom stuff is pretty nice too. I ended up with a duvet cover, six wine glasses and six pint glasses for $25.

I wouldn't, however, delve into the vast particle board furniture selection - which is not THAT cheap but still breaks if you look at it the wrong way. The only directions for putting together said crappy furniture is a cartoon miming where to put in screws.

The best part about Ikea is the frozen yogurt, which is $1 and very delicious.

Like other reviewers have said, yes, you get what you pay for with respect to furniture (never eaten here). But I would like to add to their reviews with respect to plants, lighting and art work. There's a good selection of all three and prices are reasonable. I bought two plants for $20 each and they are 4 ft. tall in 10 inch pots. The quality is excellent and I'm so happy to see them in my house. I also bought two small nightstand lights for $10 each AND bulbs were included. They are better known for their contemporary pieces, but there were plenty of traditional light fixtures as well. Didn't buy any artwork, but I love to look at them (maybe once I paint, I'll hang a couple). I am particularly impressed with their botanical prints (trees, cherry blossoms, orchids, etc.).

I'm an IKEA fan, usually. Once in a while I get over it - usually when the place is slammed with people who are wandering aimlessly.

Sure, the joint is a bit overwhelming, but the cheap is equally awesome.

My last abode now has a lovely IKEA kitchen with all the extras - and my tenants (can't sell in this market) adore that which I installed. At this point, I'd be loathe to install any kitchen that wasn't of their design ethos. Course, in a high end home, I'd have it custom built - but I'd want their hardware.

ProTip: Go during the day, during the week. Weekends are HORRIBLE with snot nosed kids, blimps pushing strollers and meatball gobbling lumps in the restaurant. (Seriously - I'm chubby - need to lose 25 lbs for sure... and I was the skinniest person in the restaurant the other day. *shudder*)

ProTip2: Get one of the maps and you can scoot thru the place without having to walk the entire 'showroom death march' which might take you a day, given the throngs in the aisles.

My Mother is Norwegian, and so I feel a sense of kinship with this store and the items within it. Sure they have funny names, and the modern designs arent for everyones abode, but I believe that there is at least one or two items you cannot live without here. I dare you to leave empty handed. 

My boyfriend and I went here on a saturday afternoon, and it wasnt that crowded. I happen to like people watching so even if it was , its a positive. 

The place is huge, "rymlig", spacious. Two stories of well thought out maze like show rooms.  Upstairs first :You go through living rooms, to kitchen, to bath,  to lighting to bedroom to kids room and then you are in the middle and whats this? A Cafeteria? clever swedes!! how did they know we were hungry? We shared a Swedish meatball special (mashed potatoes, lingonberry jam, meatballs, side salad and a drink) Plus one drink extra. This is the food I grew up with and even though I love my grannys meatballs, these are still very yummy and comforting. 

After you eat, you clean your own trays up because the Swedes believe that by not hiring tiny vikings to take our trays away, we get cheaper merchandise in trade. 

Its onto the elevators to the first floor where you get more kitchen stuff, decorative items, mirrors, rugs, pictures, kitchen tables, candles, plants. And then its out of the showrooms and into the warehouse where you pick up the big items you have written down on little scraps of swedish paper. You must put together your own furniture at home, using just the power of your mind and easy to read directions that have dilbert or Iggy or whoever the character is on them. 

At the end you have the opportunity to look at the "scratch and dent" room, where during pillaging the swedes nicked a table or Stellan  Skarsgård returned a rug that he already had two of. You can self check out , which is so nice, and you can pick up some swedish foods like the meatballs, pickled herring, gravlax, caviar, or cinnamon buns. These people have you covered, you wont go home hungry OR energetic, you will take the best damn nap of your life afterwards and dream of frosted glass cabinets and blue and yellow cheap but attractive clouds of joy.

I'm kind of an Ikea addict.  I come here and walk out with things I don't really need - and that goes for basically any Ikea, no matter where it is in the world!  I've probably been in 10 different Ikeas all over America, and they're pretty much the same.  

I don't think I even own a piece of linen that isn't from Ikea.  

This location is in a pretty good area, but getting back to the main highway is a bit complicated if you are not from this area and don't know the side streets.

Well, you may have been to Ikea before.. but this was the first time I had ever had to return an item. I really thought this would be tough because I bought a home and in the process had Ikea bath items in the garage for just about six weeks. The home we purchased needed different items and Ikea was happy to do the return with NO problems...thanks to a big business for doing the right thing.

Thanks,
Mike Catalano

Okay, I admit with some guilt that I'm a fan of IKEA... but only want to "do" IKEA maybe once or twice a year, 'cause every visit there is a huge investment of time.  That said, it's just fun to walk around, look at stuff, eat the swedish meatballs, and even furnish an entire room with mod stuff for a couple hundred bucks.

Are you a glutton for punishment and want more details?  Okay then, here are some pros and cons.  Cheers!

Pros:  

* Amazing selection of affordable, even disposable furniture, and every year they roll out fresh new lines.

* The styling can be pretty cool.  Awesome, even.  And the way they've set up the furniture in displays really can inspire ideas.  

* I furnished my home office from here for about $500, have been very happy.  We also got a rockin' modular closet organizer that has worked out amazingly.

* I think it's fair to say that you get a bit more than you pay for here.

* They have babysitting!  Although it's first-come first-served.  

* Usually plenty of staff on hand to help, and I understand they treat their people pretty well.  That's a big plus in this era of WalMart abuse of employees.

Cons:

* Going to IKEA is a commitment: they've deliberately designed it so you can't get through it quickly, no doubt so that you find more things to buy and spend more money.

* It's nice there's a cafeteria: you actually need a break it's so big.  But the food is somehow lacking... perhaps because it's not completely unhealthy?  But it can be a bit bland and portions small.  Maybe it's a Scandanavian thing?  The Lingonberry soda is always a treat for some reason though, although it's really mostly like raspberry ginger ale.

* The checkouts are always a bit crowded, as is the store. 

* Getting back to your car with your purchases can be a pain.

* Then, when you get home, you have to put everything together!  Ya know, thinking about it, maybe it's better to just spend the extra money and get the stuff assembled.

There much be something in their meatballs cause when anyone mentions IKEA, I cant help but say, oh I wanna go to IKEA! This in the mecca for college students on a budget. Cheap products that require you to build it yourself and lasts for exactly three months before it starts to crack on you. (Maybe they have a self destruct chip in the furniture). Nevertheless, the furniture serves its purpose for the college years (then onto 'real' furniture). 

Despite the fact that I do not need furniture or any household gadgets, i find myself at IKEA in line for those darn meatballs. And you just cant leave without getting one of their frozen yogurts.

I love IKEA.  I'm starting with that because I love the layout of the store, how the displays are on the top and then you go to the warehouse to pick up your items.  There is something about seeing full rooms that makes picking things out a lot easier.  Plus, I love the price and it just feels refreshing in there.

On a slightly less positive note, this store has given me a few headaches as of late.  There have been instances where two items I go to the store for are not in stock and neither of them have any signage about when to expect them to be back.  

Secondly, the store must be understaffed on Friday evenings, because I had to wait for about 10 minutes before finding a yellow-shirted man to help me load a huge box on my cart, then when trying to get this same huge box into my car, there was no one to be found.  Wouldn't it be a good idea to have staff to help customers get these items loaded?  Perhaps I should have gone back into the store to find someone, but I would think they would just have people posted out there (hint hint).  

When you go, bring a buddy- I'm probably the only birdbrain that missed that memo- and have a list of the things you are going for, or else you will end up with a huge bill at the end.  It's cheap, but even cheap adds up!

This store is out of control.  Literally feel like I'm on another planet when I walk in.  Everything from the store layout, to the Swedish food store, to the fast food stands, to the way you purchase items, to the prices!  It's an experience to say the least.  Fiance and I split lunch for a total of 4 dollars.  Shopped for about 2 hours and got tons of stuff for next to nothing.  May not be able quality, but they are about simplicity.  Will be back.  This place is crazy!

This is for there restaurant . Me and my girl had there chicken and Swedish meatballs . It all tasted and looked like it was left out for at least a few hours .If you like frozen food heated up this place is for you

I'm not a big fan of Ikea.  Cheap furniture that falls apart after a couple of months.  Nothing is unique.  Things are hard to put together and the instructions are horrible.  I'd rather pay for quality and something that will last then furniture at Ikea.

I recently moved across country to tampa and needed quite a few things for my new apartment. Being on a budget, Ikea was my first thought. I found everything I needed from a furniture, to bed linens, to kitchen stuff. They seriuosly have everything you need under one roof! My advice to anyone whos young and just starting out and still wants a stylish place to call home.. go to Ikea! 

Also, the food is pretty good too. I recommend the chicken tenders :)

i work in Conshy and head over to IKEA for lunch sometimes as it is very reasonable and the food is an upgrade to any cafeteria style meal you ever had in High School or College. 
I recommend the open face shrimp sandwich with dill and a lemon slice.  Very tasty.

What can I say? It's exactly like every other Ikea I've ever been to- organized chaos. If it's your first time, plan on being there for hours just to pick out what you want from the showroom because they have so much to offer and many staging rooms. If it's a weekend, plan on long lines.
It's a great place to buy furniture when you're on a budget. Prices are reduced because you build it yourself and pick it out of the warehouse yourself (that part can be annoying as most boxes are very heavy, even to just get it on the cart)
Delivery service (ranges $90-110) came at the very last minute of my four hour window... At least my stuff was undamaged and the guys were friendly. Also, they called me several times to keep me posted.

Gave IKEA one star because I wanted to buy a bedroom set and walked out without one.  The reason being their "disorginized" way of buying anything.  Following the arrows on the floor which will take you through every department in the extremely large building, I eventually got to the furniture dept.  The male salesperson ignored me 4 times while he ran to other customers. One of his interests was the typical Mr & Mrs with the 2 teens.  .  He told them to make their parents proud and get good grades in school. Just the kind of advice that is expected from a saleman. I can only guess that males without female attached to them were considered "poor buyers."   
Finally, a female salesperson came over to me and asked if she could help.  I was starting to think that I was invisible. 
Now for the really bizzare part--Picked out the furniture which she put into the computer, out comes the form. Then she tells me to pick up the boxes myself and take them to the check-out.  WHAT???
Guess I'm showing my age, I dunno.  Just not my way of buying furniture.

IKEA was basically my toy store growing up in Germany. You American kids had Toys R Us, and I was the 5-year-old drawing terribly out of scale floor plans of my bedroom and picking out the latest unpronounceable Swedish accessories for my living space. 

Some of the thrill has died off since then, but I still love walking through IKEA and looking at all the things I can't fit into my little home or don't want to buy. I love the style. I love/hate the fact that they make you walk through the entire store before finding whatever it is you were looking for to begin with. I love the food (stock up on the lingonberry jam. You're welcome).

When I'm feeling thrifty, I walk through IKEA, write down the model name of coveted items, and then search for them in Craigslist. Seriously, Craigslist is like IKEA 2.0.

The Ikea here in the states aren't as good as the ones in Europe, but they'll do for sure!! I love all of their things and yes, even though it's a pain in the butt to have to put all of that furniture together, the price is sure worth it. A very well rounded home furnishings store with everything you could possibly think of getting for your home. And before you leave, stop and get the meatballs!! YUM!!!!!

Oh IKEA, if only you knew the joy you bring me!

I have so much stuff from IKEA. The great thing about the place is you can have the cheap, bare-bone basics or you can spend a little more money to get something classier. They have a really good price and style range. It's still cookie cutter furniture, but the quality is in my opinion pretty darn good for the price. The furniture is easy to assemble and the instructions are surprisingly straightforward for just being pictures. After years of shopping at IKEA, instructions with words frustrate me!

Their kitchen stuff is pretty much the best. I have potato peelers that were dirt cheap and work better than the expensive brand-name ones. I bought a lemon juicer for a dollar there years ago and it is still my favorite. Basically, most of the kitchen stuff is very affordable and of top quality.

The store is also a great place to go for a cheap, fun date! Decent* food for next to nothing, including frozen yogurt cones for a dollar! It's fun to just walk around and play in the show rooms. It's easy to spend several hours here wandering around and looking at all of the pretty furniture and accessories, fantasizing about your dream home.

One drawback: the lineups are horrible!! And you can easily get suckered in to buying a boatload of tchotchkes because they display them in rows beside the isles and you're standing there for so darn long!

(P.S. One day, EKTORP chair, you will be mine.)

*Update (2015), I got sick off the breaded fish, so maybe not so decent.

Oh, IKEA. Thank you for furnishing my townhouse. We have a dining room table and chairs, a couch, a desk, a nightstand, and a lamp. They're all in pretty good shape and look quite classy.

I love that some of the furniture is customizable. I bought a simple desk for under $50 but could have easily added bells and whistles if I wanted. I couldn't find any nightstands that I liked, so I built one by adding drawers to a small Expedit shelf. I've never had trouble putting anything together.

The quality (as long as you're not abusing your furniture too much) and prices are pretty acceptable. The designs are simple and right up my alley.

Whenever I go there I waste hours in the store because of the intentional maze effect where you have to go through the entire store to get the one item you need.  This is fun if you are a kid or just like to shop but not if you're a working adult with very limited time.  They also have virtually no staff to help you find stuff, and once you do you either love it or hate it, and/or can't buy it because special tools are needed for self-assembly for many items.

Sometimes I go to IKEA just to get a cheap meal and walk around the store, for no real reason and with nothing in particular to buy. I realize people might think that's strange, but I LOVE IKEA. like whit a passion.

This particular IKEA is normally very clean, and unlike others I have been to has a great parking lot. The shopping area it's in has other great options as well, such as Lowe's, Pier 1 and Best Buy.

The as-is options are usually pretty good, and the staff is helpful and welcoming. If you're looking for trendy, inexpensive furniture (and maybe even some delish food!) stop on by.

Who doesn't love cheap furniture? I mean, yes... most of it is made from particle board and won't last 5-10 years but hey, it looks good and it's cheap. The greatest thing I love is that it is so kid-friendly. I mean, kids can be in any department and you really don't have to worry if they're going to be bored while you're looking around. They have strategically placed puzzle boards in some areas and then you've got the whole kids section right by the upstairs restaurant area... Genius! We've spent quite a few days there this summer when temps were too high outside to play. It kept the kids entertained and our sanity intact.  Thank you, Ikea!

I LOVE IKEA!

OMGoodness... where else on earth can you go and look at decor to do your entire house at reasonable prices?  If you're on a dorm room budget or just bought your first house, you can afford to furnish your house at IKEA.   And heck, if you want to spend $600 on an armoire, you can do that here, too!

I love that they have a reasonably priced restaurant geared towards families with $1.99 kids meals - options include macaroni and cheese (and not KD - but real homemade stuff) and organic vegetarian sauce and pasta for $1.99 for adults.  If you want to spend closer to $10 for a large meatball or fish entree, go to town!  They also have $1.99 breakfast specials until 10am (I think) everyday.

They have changerooms with complimentary diapers for kids, offer a bottle warming service, and even sell jarred baby food in the cafeteria for 99 cents.  Truly family oriented!

Smaaland - a kid friendly ball pit staffed area to entertain kids while parents shop is completely free *as long as your kid is potty trained*  Ours isn't potty trained quite yet, so we've yet to experience this but we have a family member that used to work in Smaaland and even after working there a year had really positive things to say about it!

The only annoying part is when pieces don't fit exactly when you get home and you have to make due with what you've got or go back for an extra part - but you just cant beat the prices or the level of quality for the price you pay.  I mean, you can go to Walmart and pay the same price for a cheap dresser and it will be just that cheap and crappy - but from IKEA, it will probably stand the test of time!

IKEA gets 2 big thumbs up from my family!

IKEA is a shopping experience. Not only can you get tons of ideas from the staged rooms on the top floor, you can get 1 free hour of childcare so your ankle biters have something to do while you make decisions on how to decorate then childproof your home. When the hour is up, grab the kids and head to the restaurant. Kids eat free at various times and there's always some sort of deal for everyone else, too. My favorite is the 99 cent breakfast (scrambled eggs, bacon, potatoes) with free coffee. You just can't beat it. It also pays to get there early before the crowds. 

I've had nearly everything at the cafeteria-style restaurant, and it's all pretty good. The meatballs are always a hit. FYI, the meatballs do not have any soy protein in them, which is wonderful for allergic folks. Usually meatballs are a mystery food, but you can read the ingredients on theirs and get a bag of frozen ones to take home!

The Swedish market at the very end of the trip has some deals, too. Warm cinnamon rolls are must to take home ($4 for 6 cinnamon rolls). If the clan is still hungry, they have hot dog combos, soft serve ice cream, and other items for cheap. In the grocery section, you can find a lot of interesting items and we always take home something new to try. I like the shrimp cream cheese in a tube that you can squeeze onto some crisp bread. Yummy! The ginger thin cookies are good, too. 

The furniture and furnishings need a mention, too. Some of it is flat out cheap, some is amazing, and some is very nice. None of it is Thomasville or Ethan Allen, and it doesn't try to be, either. This is the perfect place to furnish baby/kid/teen/dorm rooms! If you want function and price point with a pleasing price point, this is it. This is not luxurious or flea market.

IKEA's best quality is its unpretentiousness.

Best tip: wear walking shoes and come hungry. Enjoy!

I love IKEA; putting my own cheap furniture is like grown-up LEGOs. (Or K'Nex, which I wasn't cool enough to own.) You never buy anything from IKEA expecting it to last forever, or to even re-sell it for a halfway decent price, but you keep going back, even if it's just for some ideas. 

Boyfriend and I needed a splatter guard and found one for $15 at another store. "Screw that," I said, "we're going to IKEA." $4.99. Done! (Of course we didn't JUST get a splatter guard; we always end up with way more crap than we intended to buy.)

I happen to like the maze-y layout of the store; maps are provided throughout the store for those trying to get their shopping done quickly. 

The line is the one drawback; it seems like there is always a ridiculous line, whether you're getting checked out by an employee or going through self-checkout.

I recently moved and thoroughly enjoyed getting my bed from Ikea.  The delivery charges are super cheap, trust me.  They charge $69 for delivery within Edmonton proper (I believe $79 for the satellite cities) and that rate is a fixed rate for up to 700 lb.  That's a lot of tonnage!  700 pounds would easily entail an entire bedroom furniture set, a couch, some side tables and possibly even a light dining table.

Although I only purchased a bed and some other small things (which I carried with me in my car), I still thought the $69 was totally worth it.  It takes a couple of days to get it to you because of the long waiting list.  I ordered mine on a Thursday and they delivered it on that Sunday morning.  Not bad. 

Also, it's worth mentioning that they have van rentals that start at a cost $20 for 2 hours, but it's better to call in ahead of time to make sure a van will be around when you do end up buying the coveted computer desk you've been eyeing.  Of course, that's even better than the $69, but since I didn't know anyone free to help me, I decided to just get it delivered.

The furniture keeps getting updated and upgraded.  Every season entails something new, something different.  It's really a great place for a single person like me, who's not planning on buying permanent life-long furniture.

dear ikea,

i love your cheap delicious food, your simple yet relatively sturdy furniture, and your cheaaaaaaap frames. your death trap parking lot could be better, but i dont blame you, sweetums. its not your fault.

xoxo
kp

As I've browsed the 1 and 2 star reviews, I realize that these people are usually complaining about the buying experience. 

As someone who's been going to IKEA for about 20 years, you get used to having to go pick your furniture boxes in the self service area. If the sales people had to go and get your furniture for you, you wouldn't be able to get an entire set of tables and coffee table (LACK) for your living room for under $30. It's called ease of use.

That being said, I always have a pleasant experience at IKEA. I know where everything is, and I know how to get though the store quickly. You get a good workout coming here, and that's why I don't mind going through the entire store to get to the home organization stuff or lighting. You always see something along the way that catches your eye, and that's what makes it fun!

So to the IKEA haters, go back to buying your overpriced furniture elsewhere and leave the bargains to the pro's.

This is a great place to go on a rainy day. My daughter thinks its a kids store as she climbs all over everything in here. That said I have bought a few pieces from here and while they aren't the highest quality, they are the right price.

Ikea is the place I come to when I want a nice $5 bottle of Stella. Yeah, it sells furniture too, but it's also one of the cheapest places to go for an import beer. My only complaint about this location is that it's a bit out of the way for pre-drinking purposes.

Beer aside, Ikea also has a great selection of furniture. It's a good spot to reenact scenes from 500 Days of Summer. I like to just wander and look at how the displays are set up trying to glean some interior design sensibilities.
