IKEA used to position itself, way back in the 80s and early-90s, as "'Swedish' for 'common sense.'" In that sense, the store remains a source of inexpensive, good quality furniture.

And while the behemoth of a store seems excessive and staggering, you needn't really go anyplace else to purchase furniture and homewares on a budget.

But what's really fantastics about this place is the dirt cheap food. A hot dog for $0.50? Yes please! Early morning breakfast for a couple bucks? OK, sure!

Nothing beats shopping on a full stomach, so in this sense, IKEA is filling two niches: your belly and your home.

I love visiting, even if it's just to browse their showrooms. And even with screaming kids and whole pile of people, it never feels too crowded.

And that, my friends, defies common sense, Swedish or not.

It's alright. Don't buy silverware or cutting knives here; they rust fast. Their glass cups break easily, as well. Their home delivery prices are great (especially if you live on the second floor: Same rate as first!).  The food is decent and at great prices. Where else can you get a decent sized frozen yogurt cone for $1!? IKEA has that and hot dogs covered. 

Furniture is pretty solid, and still holding up today. Overall, A-OK for furniture and food. Meh for silverware and other utensils.

The COUCH Saga!

4 months after we bought our awesome Karlstad couch, the arm pulled off of it. So with a heavy heart, we went back to IKEA and showed them a few pictures (it was huge, we'd had it delivered) and after some computer issues we were told they'd be sending us a new one two days later, a Friday, between 1 and five. 

Now don't get me wrong, our entire apartment is IKEA and we adore it. They'll probably be getting money for a bed from us soon. This is a beef with the customer service department. Currently the issue is unsolved, and I'll be switching around my review when it finally GETS solved, depending on what happens. 

So the epic begins. 

We were told they'd give us 24 -48 hours notice before they delivered our couch. We both work, so Friday was it. 

I get a call 2 HOURS before the delivery window that they had to change the times to between 5pm and 9pm, and that if I didn't call them back by 2pm (it was noon) they'd have to cancel the delivery. 

In a panic, I call the extension they gave me over and over and over again trying to get a human to no avail. The couch does not come. Friday night, no couch. Saturday, no call, no couch. I've left 3 messages at this point. 

Saturday night, my other half calls. This was supposed to be the backup line. He ducks into a back room and tells them they need to call me. Instead of calling me, they give him 2 extensions that he needs to give me to call. Happy enough to get actual human extensions, I try them both. Nothing. I leave messages. Nothing. 

Sunday morning, 11 am or so. Hallelujah. I get a phone call. The girl is very apologetic and gasps time and time again about how hard I've had it and promises me that she'd get it figured out once they found our couch. 

Wait...FOUND IT? How do you lose a 5 foot wide couch?!?!?! Anyway, I thank her, and she promises me she'll call me back by the end of the business day. This was Sunday. 

Sunday. No call. Monday. No call. Tuesday. YOU GUESSED IT!

Tuesday night, My famed chill tude is starting to wear a bit thin. I call IKEA. I push random numbers. Weirdly, I end up with the couches manager. He's very understanding of my tale, and apologetic. He pulls up my case number (which I've had since the 7th of August.) and puts someone else on the phone. I think her name was Heather. 

Heather takes charge of the situation. "I'm very sorry ma'am, when can we deliver your couch?" She quotes me a few times. I pick Friday between 5-9pm because we'll both be home. She PROMISES me someone will call me back that night. Within a day at the very least. In fact, she had another customer case in her hand and would take mine directly to the supervisor, where she was already heading! Joyous!

I thanked them profusely. This was 2 days ago. 

No call Tuesday. No call yesterday. No call today, the day before she supposedly told me she could have my couch delivered. 

Look. I know a new catalog just came out. I know you IKEA guys deal with insane bungholes all day long. I love your furniture and I love your deals but I most certainly DO NOT LOVE being told I'd receive calls back and not get them. I do not love my delivery being cancelled because it's impossible to get through to a human being on a Friday 2 hours before you're supposed to deliver my stuff. I most certainly do not love not knowing where the heck my non broken couch is while the broken one I paid quite a lot for is being propped up with fantasy novels. 


Thursday night. 9pm. 11 days into the nightmare. Right now, a stranger on the internet is giving you two stars on a weird little ratings website because she's really, really pissed. Probably doesn't mean much to you, but man it felt good to get it all down in writing. 

This review isn't over. I'll officially finish it when I get my damn couch. Will it gain a star? Lose a star? WHO CARES! Tune in for the exciting conclusion to..COUCH SAGA!

Update! Re: The Couch Saga....

For those of you who missed it, I wrote a novella about our couch being lost.

We decided to say heck with it and went down there today to chat with them in person after numerous unsuccessful phone calls. They got to us right away, treated us really well, and I'm fairly sure they were most thankful that I wasn't raving like a lunatic and threatening to alert the media. 

Our couch is being delivered tomorrow, and the manager gave me her personal email address in order to fix things. 

This was an extraordinary cluster effword, but after the treatment today..Oh IKEA..I can't stay mad at you. 

We're buying a bed soon...stay tuned. 

(Although I could skip a sequel of the couch saga and be no worse for the wear...)

In a nutshell, if you have the luxury of being able to fix things with IKEA in person, do it. Phone calls just don't work. Especially at a catalog release.

Thanks for fixing your mistakes, guys!

Of course they have great furniture, but the staff are friendly and very helpful, too, from couch advise (so honest they advised us to get a cheaper couch than we were considering) to mattress help (Frank helped us get a lower price than it should have been on a mattress because it was advertised lower somewhere else in the store) to a friendly loading guy that helped us with our huge mattress and heavy furniture.

Good as-is section, though I guess it's always hit or miss. Found a $65 desk topper (i.e. just the wood) for $3 and a shelf for $2.

I feel like I shouldn't, but I just love Ikea. Their furniture might not always be super high quality, but for the most part it's just what I'm looking for... something that will suffice until I'm settled down enough to spend a bit more.

I always seem to find a pile of things that I NEED whenever I go. Plant pots? Must have. Moose shaped cookie cutter? Yes please. And one can never have too many lint rollers around. 

Unless I'm shopping with someone who can't wait to get going, I always try to stop by the restaurant too. It's one of the few places where eating out doesn't really cost much than eating at home. Plus they have lingonberry juice. Mmm...

This IKEA was there for us when we first moved to Philly. So much cheap, yet durable furniture at low, low prices. How could we, as poor college students, resist? Putting together the furniture by myself gave me a sense of self-empowerment. And after a long hard day of looking at furniture and making decisions, what better way to reward yourself than with a heaping plate full of Swedish meatballs?

While the stuff in the Marketplace, are also cheap and well-designed, I wouldn't trust the fragile products as much. Like, a glass product might easily break. Although, we did get a stovetop grill that's been working out pretty well for us.

The lines can get pretty long over the weekends. Relatively clean and neat, nice furniture demos give you ideas on how to design your home on a budget with an eye for design. Don't forget to get a $1 soft serve frozen yogurt on your way out; they're delicious!

I like coming on thursdays, i've been coming for the past three thursdays for the $1.99 herb roasted chicken with mash..  and I get a side of the corn bread, it's yummmy.. there's also a really nice female associate that works with us..she makes the experience better.. I think some of the furniture and stuff is a bit over priced..but I found a really cool hanging storage thing for 14.99..its really cute, black and white stripes with a floral pattern on the inside..and the fruit scented candles makes me house smell awesome.. 

They're losing a star for the self check out only option after a certain time..even when its crowded..they should keep at least 2 lines open

It's your standard Ikea, but just messier and not as well kept as the other Ikeas that I've been to...could be because it's in the city.

Self check out lines are convenient. 

Parking - huge lot

My daughter is an unabashed Ikea breakfast fan.  Ok, she's actually more like a religious zealot when it comes to taking me to several of them for breakfast countless times when I visit her in L.A.   After all these years I still haven't figured out if it's because she actually likes the food, or just relishes in the thought of getting the Breakfast Plate of scrambled eggs, bacon, and potatoes for 99 cents.   Or sometimes completely free if we go on Mondays.  Or the free coffee before the store opens.  Or the swedish meatballls and other items we have at other times of the day.  Or maybe it's because she actually enjoys yakking with me for hours on end after we eat and sit around drinking coffee.  Yeah, that's it.  ;-)

But as much as she loves those deals and our conversations, I can give the L.A. Ikea a nod for taste, as incredibly every breakfast I've had there has been quite good, and the lunchtime meals we've had there (swedish meatballs, etc) have been good, too.   Especially for the price.

Fast forward to her recent visit here to visit me, so I decided to reciprocate and take her to the Tampa Ikea.  After all, there's nothing too good for my girl, especially when it means taking her out for breakfast for $2.  

So while I was anticipating a similar quality experience here to the ones we've had around L.A., but were both a bit disappointed by the flavors and quality.  I know, it's hard to argue those two points about a 99 cent breakfast, right?  And to some extent, I'll agree.   If it wasn't for the fact that I've consistently been amazed how well those Ikeas deliver their food, I'm sure I'd feel differently.   And it's not just the breakfast, it's the same for every meal I've had here whenever any family member drags me since.... swedish meatballs, etc, the works.

So not complaining, just still trying to figure out why if they can do it out there, why can't they do it here?  Hopefully they'll figure it out, as I know it's possible.

I love Ikea. For the furniture, and the food.

I've furnished my whole house with Ikea stuff. The trick is to NOT buy the cheap stuff because you get what you pay for. The cheap stuff will eventually come unhinged or become uneven. Drawers will become slanted, kitchen chairs will start to fall apart. But the more expensive stuff really does hold up. I guess because they make it out of *real* wood. I also got a sectional from Ikea because I like the idea of being able to change the slip cover if I want to change my decor. It's also nice because my cat's a spiteful vomiter, so I'll need to take the slip cover to get cleaned at some point.

Anyway, as for the Ikea food...you can't go wrong. I've had the .50 cent hot dogs. They're A-OK. I've had the meatballs, chicken fingers, french fries, and macaroni and cheese. It's all GOOD! And cheap. Seriously, sometimes I go here just to eat. There's no shame in it!!

If you're going to come here, be prepared to spend more than you planned. There are so many cool things you can't leave without picking up something you don't really need. Also, plan to spend a whole day. Or half day, maybe. Leave time to see everything.

If you want to do a big Ikea renovation (like a Kitchen), this is not the place to go. I live about 15 minutes from this one and drove all the way to Ikea Conshohocken to plan my kitchen...there is a reason. Customer service, and attention to detail. 

This place has a few great people who work there, and the rest could care less - and it shows. The place is often a mess, the food is often old (if you like to eat the cheap treats at Ikea) and people are not invested in the place. However, the products are fine....just be sure you check them, because they toss them around like a bean bag.

If you want to just pick up a desk, or some accessories, etc...this is a totally ok place to be - because you can select it yourself (and check it)...but if you want to do a major renovation or think you might need assistance with something - it's worth driving to another location - trust me.

IKEA cafeterias are a unique sight in the American landscape--cheap swedish delicacies located within the heart of the world's largest home furnisher. And this one does disappoint. You cannot find such a combination of cheap food, cheap furniture, and swedish modernism anywhere else.

Some pro tips if you plan to spend an afternoon eating and lounging (and if you're in the mood, even shopping) in this IKEA:

- If you're getting a soda, get it in the downstairs café. It's cheaper than in the restaurant section and you can take your drink with you wherever you go. Also, try a combination of half lingonberry juice, half pepsi.

- Signup for an IKEA Family card (located in a kiosk right before the checkout lines) and you can get a free coffee with every visit.

- Always check the calendar of events on IKEA's website for coupons and more. Of particular note is the annual Swedish Crayfish Party where you can get free IKEA buffet, including delicious dill crayfish.
Try the saith, it is a fish that tasted similar to cod.

Particle board city... great if you are a college student or trying to furnish an apartment for cheap, but not the type of furniture I'd buy for my home.  I do love walking through the display areas for decorating ideas.  Wouldn't waste my money on the lamps or pillows... everything feels flimsy.  I would rather go to a big department store sale if I am looking to get bargains.

Wish more parents would take advantage of the hour long, free daycare.  It's hard to check out at a tv stand when a bratty child is jumping up and down on the sofas.

The cafeteria is Ikea's shining point.  Sweedish meatballs, pizza, hotdogs, ice cream cones... all for a few meager dollars.

I love me some Ikea.  It sort of feels like I am Alice in Wonderland in there; everything is ginormous and most of the stuff you can't identify even with the name.  "I would like a flat brown box of smorken-flufen, please."

They lore you in with crazy good meatballs, cinnamon buns and custard that leave you  dazed and confused.  Personally, I think they drug them to make you put more sporg and sveta in your cart.

My favorite place is the as-is room.  It's like a bad flea market.  Yes, I think I will buy a sofa with one arm missing and people's footprints on it.  Only $600, wow, great deal.  

The BEST thing about Ikea is when you use the shopping carts.  Why is the floor so slippery!  The dang carts drive like bumper-cars.  Maybe I'll "accidentally" hit one of the children who are screaming because the've been stuck in a cart for 4 hours.  

One thing they just started which I think is pretty stupid is the new loyalty card.  Why?  I think it allows you to get free coffee whenever your there, but not sure.

I have a real love/ hate relationship with Ikea. I've tried to feel utter love for the place, but I can't do it. Am I getting to old? Am I not trendy enough? I just don't get the appeal of buying large pieces of everyday, high usage poor quality and will end up in the garbage within a couple of years.  

I love how clever they can be with their design and storage, but when it comes down to it, their stuff is junk. I know, I know, the stuff is not meant to be investment pieces, but even when they are freshly put together they seem so flimsy. 

I can't get enough of their frames. I love their smaller storage containers. I loathe their most of their art graphics. I love the store layout, but can't stand the crowds. 

It's just one of those places that I genuinely don't get the hype and the masses that flock there. I can take it or leave it. 

Yelp 30 Day Challenge: 13/30

I usually meet up with girlfriends at the South Philly Ikea because it is a central location for us. We get breakfast (great because it is cheap and our kids can watch TV in the kid area of the cafeteria) and then while we shop our kids can play in Smalland. While I'm not a fan of most of the products I have been able to find a few reasonably priced items for my home. I would not buy any major furniture there- we had in the past and the quality is pretty poor.

I never knew what the hype was about Ikea but after visiting this place for furnitures for my friends new place I realized how fun this place it. It's like a giant playground for adults. So many things to see and so many things to touch. If I had the money I would buy whatever I like but sadly I can only look.

They do offer some really cheap stuff and really cool looking items.

(This review is for the restaurant.)

Swedish meatballs here not up to par. The outer part of the meatballs were dry and slightly crusted. The sauce was okay, but how hard could it be making it out of mix?

Requested vegetables instead of mash potatoes. These were overcooked and disintegrated with the poke of a fork.

One plus point, the cashier was very nice and pleasant, though staff at Ikea in general are good.

I'm actually lost in IKEA right now. I 've been here since Saturday.

Can somebody help me?

I don't think I can eat another Swedish meatball.

Wait...how did I end up in the plant section again? This sucks.

What year is it?

Help.

My happy place.

Who doesn't like a cheap lunch at Ikea followed by a $1 frozen yogurt? 

Cheap furniture (yes, some stuff falls apart...but you really get what you pay for and Ikea has a big range of quality depending on your budget). The employees are generally helpful. This is such a wonderful store that I like to get lost in.

Best customer service ever!  Twice in the past month I went to Customer service for two separate issues that could have been made complicated but instead they took care of my queries with not even a blink of an eye - one being a price adjustment even though the item was only going on sale for their Boxing Week deals and another was a return of 3 items ( We had bought 40 frames for Christmas presents - family pictures) and 1 of them broke when I was framing the picture and 2 just weren't up to snuff.  To top it off... I managed to bring the WRONG receipt and they still let me return it - and gave me a store credit.  They did note that when doing a return without a receipt - they only allow one return per year.  

And in the past we have stopped in when we've broken a dowel after taking apart and reassembling an Ikea product and they've never charged us.  

Customer service like this what keeps us coming back again and again!  Plus, their prices are great, too!

Two BIG thumbs WAY up!

I wish I lived here. I would sleep in their already constructed bedrooms, play house in all of their fashionable living rooms, kitchens, & playpens. When hungry, I would go gorge myself on Swedish meatballs with lingonberry jam. I love you Ikea, don't ever change. Also kudos on your new deal, that if you spend $100 on furniture (before tax) Ikea gives you a free meal in their food court/cafeteria!


Okay I lied, maybe you should make sure that when your furniture is assembled, the furniture isn't all rickety & wobbly! That is all.

Ikea is for mea!! Love this place if you change your mind often as most of us females do this is the place to shop!! But having a handy man around may come in need..... It would have taken me months to put together a large painting I purchased from there recently. However once completed I would have paid twice what I did for it! If you need to add some life to your dwelling this is the place to check out.... I dare you to try to leave empty handed. ;)
love,love,love! but i always end up leaving with 400 bucks of stuff i don't need. to tempting. thats why the four stars. love it!
Did not like this store. Felt like cattle being herded around the store. Crowded and very cheap furniture. Not sure as bad as WalMart but very similar. No fan of either.

IKEA is a guilty pleasure - kinda like Disneyland, but it's free to visit. And it's probably more entertaining than a theoretical Swedish Pavilion at EPCOT Center would be. This is if you have daydreams about living in a recently remodeled condo.

IKEA sells cheap, practical furniture and household items that can last anywhere from 6 months to 20 years (My parents still have a BILLY bookshelf bought in 1990 in their garage), depending on how much abuse you put the furniture under (most of their particle board furniture cannot take much abuse without some damage).

And the guiltiest pleasure of all is the IKEA cafeteria. While they are obviously frozen, I always enjoy my swedish meatball meals whenever I go - the best part of which is the lingonberry jam they serve with it. I also ate a salad with goat cheese and dried blueberries, which was actually quite delicious. I need to add Dried Blueberries to my next salad - I may even prefer them to Craisins.

However, I also purchased a Princess Cake, because the pink marzipan cover was just too appealing. But the taste itself was just too creamy. It wasn't flavorful enough to be worth whatever exercise I would need to partake in to burn it off. 

I also need to point my thumb down to the Elderflower and Lingonberry drink boxes - both tasted more like sugar than the Elderflower or Lingonberry flavours.
Swedish meatballs good. Attitude at.Return/Exchange counter bad.

I love this location, plenty of parking and I don't have to drive all the way to south philly. ++!!  I mean what can one really say about IKEA.. it's IKEA! hate it or love it and I happen to love it :D
Great store, just hate the freaking maze you have to walk through to get from one end to another. Having actual Swedish woman walking around would enhance the shopping experience.

Walking into IKEA, I am always greeted simultaneously by the smell of warm cinnamon buns and the sound of high-pitched screeching children. Like biting into an ice cream bar, it's delicious but painful, and more importantly, WORTH IT. 

I shamelessly furnish and decorate with IKEA. Boyfriend and I decided to get all new plates and glasses when we moved in together, and IKEA was there with their $20 service-for-six. Nice enough to use but cheap enough to throw against a wall during a fight - which we have yet to have because our inexpensive dining room sideboard serves as the liquor cabinet, so we can just drink our angst away.

The hem-yourself curtains are perfect for odd-sized Philly windows. The ubiquitous Billy makes four appearances in our home. And those cinnamon buns...

I was particularly excited to discover on my last visit that the warehouse section has a helpful self-serve find-it-yourself kiosk that means you can pick up that one thing quickly without having to walk through the showroom. Between that, and the self-serve checkouts, I was in and out in about fifteen minutes.

Over the past decade I've been to Ikea stores in four different states. I know what to expect at this point. I willingly embrace the particle board furniture, maze-like store layouts, and trying to wrestle giant boxes of flat-packed furniture onto a cart. 

But until today, I didn't know a trip to Ikea could be this miserable. I realized I've taken the blue and yellow homogeneity of other stores for granted.

At 5:30 PM on a Wednesday, the South Philly Ikea felt strangely similar to a Wal*Mart at 2am. Their "marketplace" area is under construction, but that doesn't explain why the few marketplace items that were available were arranged in no discernible groups and strewn about like a small tornado had just come through. Many of the items in the self-service pickup area were unavailable - not because they were actually out of stock, but because no one had bothered to bring any down from the higher shelves. Pallet trucks blocked the aisles, but weren't actually being used. We were only able to find about 3/4 of the stuff we had planned to buy.

When we went to checkout we were informed that the line was closing and that we should get in another line. Except that there weren't any others open - just those infernal "15 items or less" self checkout machines - and we had two carts piled full of unwieldy furniture. Apparently it was time for the cashier's legally mandated break. Why no one had planned for this eventuality is beyond me, but after standing around for 10 minutes they managed to find someone else to open a register rather than funnel everyone in the store through the self check-out area. 

On a positive note, the gentleman who did ring us up was quick and friendly, and scheduling delivery was pretty painless.  But overall this is the most depressing Ikea I've ever been to, and I'm sticking to the one out in Consohocken from now on.

Swedish Capitalism with a smile.

--Saturday
I don't come often, but when I do, I generally leave happy.  In this instance, I was in a hurry and had a print out of $3000 worth of merchandise that I needed to buy and have delivered/assembled for a friend flying into a town.  I walked up to their home delivery department and was greeted with a smile.  The nice gentlemen explained my options for "picking service" which was a 100 bucks but they get all the items for me - awesome.  

He walked me over to sales associate.  I can't remember her name (I think it was Lisa) but she was super helpful.  She rang everything up but 3 of the items couldn't be put on the pick list because two of them were going through inventory and one item was under 5 in stock.  So, she grabbed a cart, took me downstairs and picked them up herself.  She then gave me the printout and cart and explained exactly what I had to do.  I tipped her - she saved me hours that I didn't have to waste that Saturday. 

I paid for everything then went back to the Home Delivery department.  It was really important to me that everything was delivered and assembled on Sunday (since she was arriving with her daughter then) so I asked if it was possible before paying for the service.  The nice guy behind the counter verified with with the company (Urban Express*) and let me know it could happen between 2-6 or 6-10.  Awesome!  So I paid for the picking fee 100$ (totally worth it), delivery which was $59 and assembly which was over $350.

*See my Urban Express review to witness the horror of that experience

----Sunday 
I came back into Ikea after being totally frustrated with Urban Express.  I went to the Home Delivery department to cancel the assembly order and get my money back.  They said no problem.  I also complained about Urban Express, which didn't take much for them to scoff and join right with me.  They even recognized the name I mentioned who didn't take care of me.  I got a lot of comments like, "Yeah, we've had a lot of complaints." or "Yep, this isn't the first time."

I won't give the details here, but Ikea totally took care of me in this situation and I made sure they understood that I was very happy with my entire experience with Ikea.

My only caution to you is read my Urban Express review before you decide on delivery and assembly.

It would've been nice for someone to have given me the head's up on here.

So, here's the head's up: Most of the first floor shopping area is currently under construction or something. The stuff I came here looking for was not to be found. They have a limited amount of merchandise usually to be found there out for sale.

Not sure how long this construction'll take. Better call first to inquire.

It would've saved me the trip had I known.

Who doesn't love Ikea! I can literally spend hours at any Ikea store, admiring all the displays and décor. Great value on modern furniture and super affordable prices, not high end stuff but definitely great for people on a fixed budget. What I loved about this particular Ikea store, compared to the one back home in Sunrise, is that they have a lot more items on inventory. That's always a plus for me.

Over the past year I have purchased over $2000 worth of furniture and products. Unfortunately, the last large purchase of kitchen cabinets left me with cabinets that were incomplete! So far, it has taken over 3 weeks for me to get this rectified and hopefully this time it will be done correctly. The hassle of accomplishing such a simple task has left me leary of ever purchasing from Ikea again. The shoddy service is just not worth the inexpensive prices. I guess you get what you pay for.
Also, the customer service person (for ikea not at conshohocken) was rude and ignorant.
Fine shopping experience for candles and frames and bedspreads but do NOT make big major purchases from this place!! You are better off investing in higher quality service.

I live in phila and have been here twice...the first time i hated it and the second time reinforced why i hate it.
  I'm not unsympathetic to people who can't afford quality..(i'm one of  them) but this place is horrible.  The kitchen stuff is just cheap dollar store items and the furniture is so over priced for the quality it's insane.  
  I have bought items at walmart  which were not only better quality but half of the price.
   As far as furniture it may be "unique" but it's junk..and over priced junk if i might add.  There are many  "reasonable" furniture stores in the phila/south jersey area that are reasonable also.
     I have no intentions of ever going back to this high priced/low quality junk store ever.

Nice job, Ikea.  I dread visiting you because you're usually filthy, your customers are rude and never get the funk out of the way, and your service is even worse.  But I have learned my lesson: just go on a weeknight.  

The store didn't look like a bomb had gone off, your bathrooms were clean, your fat free frozen yogurt was only $1 and was TASTY, you actually had the chair in stock that your website said you had in stock AND an employee was kind enough to assist us.  Also, the person who checked us out was very pleasant AND awarded us a 15% gift card based on our purchases speedily (that bad boy was $45!  I thought it would be one of those - "go to our website, do this survey, enter to win" bullshit that so many companies are doing these days, but nope - we checked out, a dude was there and took less than two minutes to process and hand us our gift card!).

THANKS IKEA!  VERY NICE!

It is impossible to go to IKEA without leaving or buying something... if it's not a decor/furniture piece - it's food! I love this place. I can spend hours just looking at everything and getting ideas.

Not everything is high end or of the best quality, but I recently redecorated my bedroom and visited over 8 furniture stores looking for a bedroom suite that was contemporary, but not crazy expensive.  I couldn't find ANYTHING under $2000 anywhere else that was made of wood and not the manufactured board with overlay. I ended up buying the entire Helmes wood collection in the dark stain and I absolutely love it. It's sturdy, well made and easy to put together. Light years better than most of the items I saw out and about at other stores for 2x as much $.

Over the years, IKEA has been my go-to for most kitchen items or gadgets and lots of miscellaneous furniture items around my house. 

It definitely turns into a madhouse on the weekend, but if you can get there during the week, it's much more calm. Be sure to take home some meatballs and eat a cheap lunch while you are there!
If I could give 0 stars I would just tried to change a delivery day and got hung up on - and now no one there is answering the phone... Pretty awesome will not ever shop here again

I feel guilty for liking this place. As a firmly anti-big chain person, this is entirely hypocritical, but this place has it figured out! Sure the furniture is mostly particle board, but the set up makes every room seem so damn cool. I wish I could go back to college just to fill a tiny apartment with this stuff.
The home accessories are another story - some serious bargains to be found on very interesting stuff. And their lighting and art section is beyond cheap for stuff I'd be happy to have in my office, maybe even some parts of the home.
Didn't try the food side, but will be back to do so soon.

Like most people in their 20's or 30's I became intimately familiar with Ikea when I moved into a house and realized that everything I owned didn't even reasonably furnish one room.  

I had been to an Ikea before but mostly to pick up a few odds and ends and grab something from the snack bar.  The set up is similar to every other Ikea in the world...look at the merchandise assembled and decorated upstairs, then hurt your pack loading it on your cart downstairs.  Eventually you will make your way to your car and where you will finally appreciate those hours you spent during your youth playing tetris.  I would suggest blaring the Tetris theme song from your car stereo to motivate yourself and others around you. 

As for the store itself, the South Philly location is a disaster on the weekends, super crowded and as a result impossible to find anyone to ask for help.  If you show up on the weekend expect to be handling everything yourself.  Weekdays are much calmer and while its still not easy to track down someone to talk to in the showrooms its not as bad as the weekend.  

As a result of being at Ikea 20 times to pick up everything for my house, I also had to make several returns.  Mostly because I realized something didnt fit where I expected, I purchased the wrong thing, etc.  While the line for returns can be really long on the weekend, the customer service workers have always been helpful and speedy.  

I haven't once had the experience of missing parts or pieces that people talk about with Ikea merchandise.  I also have not had any problem with the overall quality.  I think most people who proclaim Ikea as 'junk' are either unfamiliar with Ikea furniture or are just bitter about having to assemble the stuff themselves.  The fact of the matter is this stuff will last a long time if you don't mistreat it.

Like many other Yelpers, I'm in love with IKEA.  I have only really experienced two IKEA's to the fullest--- Brooklyn and Tampa.  Both, have almost the same view from the cafeteria.  So, visiting the Tampa IKEA after the Brooklyn... then, reminded me of being back in BK.  Which is all warm and fuzzy.

We always come here early to park up front.  And, eat breakfast for super cheap before the shopping gets started.  Check the Tampa IKEA website ahead of time for special deals.  Sometimes they will comp all of your food if you save the receipt and buy more than $100 worth of stuff.  Bring some grocery bags with you, otherwise you will be charged for bags for the small stuff.

"I definitely don't feel like I'm in Florida right now."

Where else can you get a 4 foot paper lander floor lamp with a foot switch for $14.99?  IKEA has such good prices, and fashionable furniture, that shopping for furniture has now become like going shopping for clothing on the weekend.  It is no longer a "big deal" to have to buy a sofa, bed, or end table.  It costs the same as a pair of jeans and a tee shirt.  I seriously purchased an awesome seven foot long entertainment center with glass front cabinets for $149.

The only really frustrating part of shopping at IKEA is when you find something you really want to buy and it super cheap, and you cannot fit it in your car.  Just... just bring a truck with you every time so you don't miss out.

As far as IKEAs go, this one is right on par. Same price and products. Clean, nicely mapped out. I just go there just to eat because i'm not a fan of the furniture (i'm rough on furniture so it always breaks on me)... If only going there to eat sounds weird I feel bad for you because you've obviously never ever eaten the meatballs..TRAGIC! Go change that asap.

Why 5 stars? Because what's not to like?

   ---   ---   ---

So I am not big on reviewing chains, but IKEA is near and dear to my heart. Just about my entire house is made up of so many IKEA furnishings, I feel the only thing left would be for my hair to turn blonde. IKEA has great style, unbelievable selection and is practically big enough to be its own zip code. Every time I try out the competition, I always come away realizing it was stupid to even attempt it. IKEA is and always will be #1 and there's no close second.

I consider myself to be pretty stupid when it comes to putting things together, assembling things, or working with tools in general. But despite many IKEA purchases, I've never screwed up the building process of any furniture item. I may have realized an error and had to back track five-steps to correct it, but I've never had anything fall apart on me. As for the inconvenience of having to build your own furniture, I usually just use that time to catch up on my highly neglected DVR. I also find it very rewarding once I finish up, which is probably because, like I referenced before - I am a monkey when it comes to putting things together.

I used to complain about how they only have self check-out registers open, but the last couple of times I've gone, that has not been the case. I also used to bitch about the fact that you had to buy bags, but after picking up a few...those bags are about the best investment I've ever made. I use them all the time... I feel like they could support about 500 pounds of weight in each one.

Thank you IKEA for building one of your amazing facilities in Ybor, if the nearest location was still in Orlando, I don't know what I would do with myself.

Northern Europeans must not like high-back furniture. That was my first impression. There are some great prices here but I have to wonder about the quality. 
There are some unique furniture options here that we will probably take advantage of. I can't help but think some of the infatuation with this store is the european hipster  appeal it has. 
I hate the layout of the store. I don't like the fact that they don't have more direct routes to many of the departments. Often you are forced to take the long way around a department to get where you want to go.

Nice-looking and functional furniture. Clean design. Many things you did not even know you needed. Dining is OK. Customer service is OK (reminds of Europe: efficient but not friendly). 

Warning: do not use their delivery & assembly service (Urban Express) - I had a horrible experience. The furniture was supposed to arrive between 8am-noon, then by 2:30pm, then by 4pm, then by 7pm, and finally got here by 8pm. Lost a whole day waiting and talking to customer representatives on the phone.

Ikea and I have a love hate relationship. I love their prices, I hate how long it takes me to get through that damn store. I also hate that in the past year they have changed the size of their chair and discontinued the black colour in their malm set (this makes it very difficult to find a black dresser). Regardless, as a young-20-something starting out Ikea is the perfect fit for furnishing a home. I love that you can furnish your entire home in that store, and I love that they keep up with most of the trends!

IKEA is an experience more than a store. Sure, they are world-renown for their low cost, flat box furniture and items. But, the magic happens as soon as you walk in the door. Two words: SmalLand. Okay, sort of one word, but it's an amazing place that is a play area for little kids so parents can kinda shop in peace. Basically, IKEA is part day-care service. Ascend the escalator to find a full service food court with full meals that cost $0.99.  WHAT?  Take that Super Value Menu.  Granted, I wouldn't want to eat the food (I think), but it's definitely amazing.  

Then, get lost on its two floors of furniture and home goods.  Check out their website for the 9 million or so items they carry.  Honestly, I bought a few items from them, and they're remarkably sturdy and definitely maximize use.  In fact, the $5 can opener is the best one I've ever used. It's fantastic.  

The hardest part about IKEA is the self-serve items area. It's requires plenty of hard work and planning to 1) acquire larger items, and 2) get them paid for/to your house.  Not to mention, there is a clear system to find the items, but it's not always a breeze. 

Finally, you've checked out! You bought your home goods, and you're ready to go!  Hold on...is that a mini-market and snack bar?  YES. Get the $1 soft serve. It's unbelievably good. Or, pick up some gooseberry or lingonberry jam.  How about some frozen Swedish meatballs to take home as a reminder of our Scandinavian furniture overlords? Their chocolate is also very good.  

So you think you're done with IKEA once you get out the doors. Not so fast. If you need to return something or pick up some extra parts that might not have been included in your packaging, the customer service area is efficient and incredibly helpful.  

So why three stars?  The items need to be slightly better quality for me to be happy, and it's a little too austere in terms of their designs. Lastly, I've seen so many of their items in people's places it reduces the real creativity or unique qualities homes should have.  

The bottom line: Go to IKEA.  Get some soft serve. Walk around and admire all the items they've managed to fit in a single place. Pick up some jam or a can opener. Experience the thoughtfulness that is IKEA.

I love IKEA!  Yes everything you buy there will break within a planned amount of time but hey, it's fairly cheap and will last almost as long as you need it.  Major props for their plant selection.  I got crazy awesome plants there for super cheap!   Food is cheap and plentiful!

Boy do I ever love Ikea.  I love all the furniture, bedding, knick knacks etc. that you can get there.  And you can feed two people for under 5 bucks if you quickly want to fuel up on hot dogs for your shopping trip or sit and relax afterwards.  However, my visit yesterday to Ikea was very disappointing.  I am a sales person myself, so whenever I get bad customer service it really bothers me.  When I'm at ikea and I see something I like, I quickly check the App from my phone to see if it is in stock before I bother someone about it.  I simply wanted to buy a rug that the website said was in stock.  I tried to ask a guy in the warehouse where it was because nobody was in the textiles department, and he told me to go back there because someone should be there.  Just because someone SHOULD be there doesn't mean they are.  And I had already picked my furniture so why should I have to wheel it through, going the wrong way, to get back to textiles.  He also answered the phone when he was helping me and asked me if there was much more to help me with because he had to take a call.  I just wanted to know where the other furniture I wanted was because they obviously moved it from the location where it was supposed to be according to its tag in the show room.  When I was waiting to ask someone else for help he continued to help the person in front of me without ever looking up once to acknowledge me or say he'd be right with me which really made me mad.  I also wanted to buy a mattress but I have a small car, and I noticed that some of their mattresses are rolled up so I was trying to inquire as to whether it was rolled up because that would make the difference between being able to take it home or having to come back with a truck.  They told me it was rolled up and they were going to get it, wasted my time and it turned out it wasn't (which I figured in the first place since it was a large mattress and it seemed it would have been impossible to roll.  The guys in the warehouse just didn't seem interested in helping me.  One of the guys was named Sean, not sure about the other.  Wish Ikea would have better customer service, because I also encountered rudeness when trying to return an item and trying to explain that they left out some hardware pieces, and I was talked to like I was stupid.

We go to Ikea to walk around and browse on a lazy evening sometimes.  Lots of good deals and a cafeteria with good food at good prices. We've bought candles, a highchair, kitchen stuff and the list goes on. A good place to shop for good value, even if the stuff isn't the highest quality it does the job.

Regarding the IKEA restaurant.

You got rid of the steamed new potatoes and replaced it with french fries.

That really sucks. Now it feels like I'm eating in some Swedish McDonalds-esque franchise instead of a quirky cool cafe in a quirky cool euro-ish shopping monolith.

Take it back.

I am thoroughly disappointed with IKEA. Like most people in their 20's, IKEA became the furniture I could afford as well as fit into my small city spaces. However, my most recent experience has tainted me, and I will NEVER go to IKEA again.
I recently ordered a PAX closet system. First, the order was wrong: they ordered me the wrong size doors. After being kept on hold for close to an hour each time I called IKEA, they offered me no solution. I was asked to pay the difference for the WRONG doors that they ordered, even though I asked they pay the difference for the inconvenience they caused me. 
I will never deal with a company that doesn't care about their customers again. However, I should have know that customer service was like this due to their cheaply made furniture, and even less friendly sales associates.

Up until recently this IKEA has been great. Lately it's been going downhill in terms of customer service and product availability. Yesterday we went to purchase a mattress pad. The customer service rep issued a form for furniture pick-up. We waited in line to pay and then waited again 25 minutes in the Furniture Pick-up area only to be told that it wasn't in stock and that they wouldn't deliver it to the house when it came in. Our only choice was to have the money refunded and come back on any random day only to go through the entire experience again just to figure out if another mattress pad is in stock. WTF IKEA, no one would put themselves through that torture! Please get it together because otherwise we'd love to shop with you.

Who doesn't like IKEA? You've got to be a pretty strange individual to not fall in love with their stuff. Ok sure it's not made out of the greatest material and most of the items you buy you shouldn't expect to have in 10 years, but it's so pretty!

Make your way through the model homes. Being someone with absolutely no creative ability, but who certainly appreciates well placed rugs, I fell in love! Walk up to the second story and walk through all the things you never really could afford and certainly don't need, but you buy anyways. For example, my friend came here to buy a potato peeler. Don't ask.

What would be equally as heinous as not liking the store itself is coming here and leaving without eating their food. BAD DOG. It's so tasty! Their Swedish meatballs are aMAzing. You get a dozen of those scrumptious balls rolled around in their gravy. Their desserts are amazing too! Ice cream is a dollar.
Ikea is a great place. I don't really need to say more other than if you aren't here for the furniture, get the meatballs

Where else can you get affordable furniture and delicious, comforting food that is ALSO affordable? 

IKEA of course! It is definitely much more of an experience than a store itself. 

While you're arguing with your GF about the best furniture for your apartment - take a breather. Relax. Head to the cafeteria and get some succulent Swedish meatballs with Lingonberry sauce ... mashed potatoes ... soup ... and a soft drink (free refills) for $5.99! Get a side of Mac n Cheese (two huge scoops). Heck ... go all out and get the chicken tenders with fries (think Burger King style fries on crack).

This is how 'fast food' should be. For all intents and purposes ... the Swedes can come take over that industry in the US.

I love IKEA! I bought my whole bedroom set for $2,000 including the mattress which is very comfortable! The delivery is a flat rate which is very nice when you have numerous heavy things that would never fit in your sedan. The organizational systems just make life easier and so do their prices. Sure I'd love my condo to be full of Kane's furniture, but for still being in school it's impractical. 

IKEA is what it is. The Mecca of DIY. There is limited staff, you have to get it yourself, and assemble it yourself.
For what it is it's great. The staff thats there will try to help you, assembly is fun, and the quality isn't bad at all. 

 I call IKEA the Furniture Theme Park, because I seriously have a great time strolling through the maze of visual stimuli, looking at the new stuff, and playing with the new stuff. The Sweedish Meatballs, cinnamon buns, and fro-yo are amazing too! 

After putting IKEA on a pedestal, bring it down a notch. It is a huge department store that has a great selection, ok staff, nice furnishings, and good food at an affordable price.

On Thursdays Ikea has a special - mashed potatoes and chicken for $2.99 and we decided to check it out.  I didn't expect much but for a cafeteria style meal it was surprisingly really delicious! 

I got a succulent breast that was perfectly roasted with golden skin and juicy white meat - the potatoes are probably instant but they still taste pretty darn good.  I also got a side of mixed veggies that was a huge potion and very tasty as well.  

There is no leaving without some delicious Ikea coffee - rich and bold and hot - love it!  We found out that you can get free coffee if you sign up for the (free) Ikea Family card.  We both got dessert - one chocolate overload cake and one almond chocolate butterscotch (my favorite) and both were rich and delicious.  

Of course the catch with eating so inexpensively is that I am in this giant store I love and the temptation to go fill up a cart with things I really don't need like some new farfennuggin picture frames and haagan daz wine glasses is strong  - but with hubby along this time he managed to point out how much we really don't need these items and I escaped with just a new set of sheets and a good dinner.

I love Ikea!

Have you ever wondered what being under house arrest feels like?...Just get home delivery from IKEA. 

DISCLAIMER: Review about IKEA customer service and home delivery service, not regarding the cheap Swedish furniture from China that we all love. 

Customer Service - I was trying to find out how to get home delivery and I couldn't get a straight answer. I talked to a guy in a blue shirt about home delivery, he told me to go talk to someone at home delivery section. Went to home delivery section, yellow shirt dude tells me to go see self-serve dude in another area. Turns out the self-serve dude is another blue shirt guy, and at this point I'm thinking these guys are playing ping pong with me. Luckily, blue shirt guy #2 said to pick my stuff, pay for it and then do home delivery. That's all I wanted to know, I don't know why blue shirt #1 or yellow shirt #1 couldn't tell me what the process was. Oh well. then waited in line forever at the home delivery section. They kept screwing up the delivery information for the lady in front of me. The lady kept telling them which items were missing, etc. It was a long wait. Why couldn't they get it right?

Home Delivery - while this is outsourced to U X home delivery, IKEA should be held accountable as it is advertised as IKEA home delivery. I signed up for the 10a - 2p slot, paid my monies, and anxiously awaited my merchandise. They showed up at 5p. EFFING 5 PM!!!! Effectively, I was under house arrest for 7 hours. The calls to customer service weren't helpful; 60-70 minutes they said.

...kinda regret not buying that truck.

Dear Ikea,

I never knew what true love was until you came into my life. My life with you now resembles a true romance novel. You provide me with inspiration. You feed me cheap and yummy food, which is the key to my heart. The path that you have created has provided me with decor ideas and ramdon trinkets. You are so diverse and offer so much to me that I'm eternally grateful. Please don't ever leave me.

Love,
Jennifer

I know I'm the minority here but I can't stand cheap furniture. Ikea is one step above Rooms to go. Particle board and plastic is their main themes. Want a lamp? Oh they have plenty of paper ones. PAPER? Really? I want to furnish my house with good solid classic pieces that last. Not some disposable college dorm crap.

Yeah, great, they have a cafateria, with darn good meatballs, but does that make up for the monster lines, the cheap furniture, the shoddy service (or lack theeof) No. not for me.

Sure, I can get some ideas from here to take elsewhere and sometimes I do find that one cute thing I have to get, but to furnish my house from here or buy kitchen cabinets? Forgettaboutit!

I bought a couch from Ikea, paid to have it delivered, only to take it out of the box and find the main support frame for the couch not connected to the frame.  I called customer service and was first told to bring it back myself - the couch weighed 140 pounds and I didn't have a car big enough to hold it (I paid for delivery for a reason!) Then I was told it would be 48-72 hours for a return call.  I finally received a call 5 days later and scheduled  a return for Wednesday.  No confirmation call the day before, they did not show up and they did not call.  Friday morning I received a call from the delivery company saying they were coming in a four hour window that day.  Unfortunately I could not be there the whole time.  I called the delivery company to reschedule and was told I would have to call Ikea directly.  I called Ikea only to be told to call back after 10 a.m.  I called back after 10, finally talked to a live body who told me the manager would have to call me.  I have been waiting over an hour for a return call from a manager.  THIS IS THE WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE EVER!!!  and for the price the furniture is cheap  - ugh!!!!!

This location is ALWAYS packed.  Parking is a bit of a nightmare but after you are able to find a spot, beware, your journey has only begun.
 
People in cars rack up points by hitting pedestrians, pedestrians get points by flicking people off, kicking vehicles, and elbowing other pedestrians. 

Once inside the chaos continues.  The store is FULL, simply put.  I sometimes fear the floor will fall out from under me from the weight of all the rude people with fantastic girth.

Food here is awesome, cheap and fills me up!

Same old IKEA things, but not as large of a selection compared to the Conshohocken store.
I really like IKEA overall, but this one is my favorite so far. I love walking around just to look at everything and pretend I live there like the weirdo I am..

I went here looking for a new Bed frame or Day bed -single  not knowing how the store operates. It's a beautiful store and I love it and the simplicity of Swedish furniture and the assemble it yourself gig. BUT you have to go look at the item, write down the item #'s and don't forget to LOOK at the piece  you are buying hard because if you don't know you need diffrent part's for different  things. Like for a bed you might need the pine flat piece under the mattrress and that is a seperate  cost, then you might need a metal support , that cost  is seperate. And once you find what you want you go down into the "self serve" area and try and find it first (follow the signs) they make you walk  a complete square to get to it and then it's like walking into BJ's or a huge warehouse place, you go look for the aisle your stuff is in and then lift the very heavy boxes yourself-SO TAKE STRONG HELP WITH YOU-and wheel to checkout.   WEW I was exhausted after being in there about 2 hours. It was HOT and not too crowded when I went during the week on a Wednesday afternoon. 

I give it 3 stars because of all the walking around to get to one area you must do. 
Other than that I loved it. And I do have to return something because I didn't have knowledge on the piece I bought and bought an extra piece.

It's good if you need a simple cheap bookshelf. That's it. Everything else is just too squared off and looks like it belongs in a hotel.

There is not one piece of furniture in in this store that is home-y. And all of it is cheap in quality and looks dated and beat up within two years.

I'm the type of girl who loves the outdoors and always being outdoors, but Florida is the type of place where it's sun or rain rain rain. When that happens I think and dream of ikea. Does that sound weird or what? Oh well! For one thing, ikea has the biggest strongest umbrellas for those crazy windy storms we have.
They also r fun to go thru to c the different modern designs that one can have in their house. Guess what too? We r building a house, so all the home ideas in the world makes for a happy me.
One other thing u may not think about when it comes to ikea is food.
Ikea has a cafeteria like restaurant for those times u need to take a break. Their food is gd and super affordable. I tried to not eat there so I can try something knew but that didn't work. Their meatballs w cream sauce r tasty. Their chocolate cake is heaven, other food I have had have also been gd! And the price oh yeah for sure. It's no fancy pansy food but it's still very gd to me!!

Came here few days ago after dinner to buy two tables for my work.  There was probably about an hour left before the store was to close.  Walking to the office furniture section took a really long time, IKEA needs to add more shortcuts!  I understand IKEA's marketing tactic to get you to walk through their whole store but I don't always have the time for that.  Despite the small crowd in the evening, there were only two cashiers open and the checkout process was REALLY SLOW.  We were in line for probably 30 minutes just to get our computer printout paid for.  Not only was the checkout slow, we were told to go to furniture pickup to get our tables.  The lady at furniture pickup told us it would take them about 10-15 mins to locate it and bring it out to us.  So I went to the garage to pull my car out front and went inside to wait almost another 30 mins!  I can't even imagine how long it would take when the store is full with customers!  I love IKEA and their styling concept.  Their quality has improved but their customer service in their retail store is poor!  Not as much a fan like I used to be....

You know how people always joke about couples breaking up in here? I totally can see it. You walk in and there are lots of young couples holding hands, eyes glazed walking through the aisle. Not I.
I dragged the lover here when we realized all our bookshelves were buckling from our massive amounts of books. He had never been to Ikea before--and if I could italicize this sentence I would because that amazes me!!! 
The trick to Ikea is to know that nothing you buy here will truly last, but because you cannot yet wrap your head around the idea of spending 3,000 on a couch, you drag your ass to the land of weirdly named things that can all be put together by a N-shaped metal tool, enjoy the smooth shopping carts, and marvel how people with a better eye than you can make such cheap things look so sweet.

P.S. my favy new thing about coming to IKEA now is that people take pictures of the tag of things they want and then use their phone to find them instead of madly scribbling down bin and aisle numbers and scanner IDs. So that's new, but the $3 meals at IKEA is still the same. Bleech!

P.P.S. every garlic press I've gotten here has rocked my world. I got one from Target two months ago and broke it with the first clove I tried to press. Can these comments get any more random?!

My mother wanted to get another piece of furniture, a night stand for one of the rooms,  I figure, why not..  I'll join her for the ride. She figured this spot would not be  as expensive as an Ashley's or a Raymour , well she was right.

My first time in here and I never knew how lazy the workers could be. I need a job like this I thought, don't help just point and get paid. ( minus the yellow and blue stripped uniforms) Gotta love arrows pointing you in the direction you need to walk. What would happen if you started going the other way..team Sweden would get pissed you are going against the grain. 

 We finally found the right area to go to, saw what she wanted, now its time to find a worker. Found a worker, had asked for this piece and he goes and hands me a piece of paper to write down the model #, stock # price, and what aisle it is in. Ok I comply this is something new to me, I am doing his job. I go and do what they ask, return it to the attendant and he looks it up.. yes we have it. He then instructs us to go downstairs to the warehouse and pick it up ourselves.

 Are you kidding me, what kind of system is this, what is your job here cause clearly you are making way too much. We now are downstairs in their warehouse looking for the right aisle, number and pray to god this isn't heavy. Now I am glad I chose to go with my mom, she would have never have lifted this or have found it. 

Now that we did 2/3  of their job it is time to pay, what a surprise another lazy cashier. She didn't bother to help people with the items in their carts, help  to place it on the counter to get scanned, nor did she help the customer afterward. Another easy ass job, do nothing and get paid to scan with a hand held scanner.

This is also a first for me,a restaurant built into this place, and of course they have " Swedish meatballs !

Not a fan of this place, I along with my mother will no longer visit an IKEA.

This place is great for any kind of furniture. They make quality stuff. Yes you have to put it together but that is the fun part (At least for me). I have had some of these pieces for years and they hold up very well. 

Now for the food. It is a great price and the swedish meatballs are great. (FYI, they also sell them near the checkout) You get a ton of food for not a lot of money. This location is easy to get to and lots of parking.
Great place for cheap furniture. Sometimes it's a pain in the ace to set it up though.

This IKEA location is about the same as the one in Southern California. They got a good selection of furniture to choose from. Most of their items are in stock and their products are fairly organized. The parking is ample and you can load your furniture at the front loading spots of the store. The food they offer on the second floor is pretty good for the price. I enjoyed the BBQ Ribs combo. The ribs were tasty and saucy. I would come back just for the food.

I always have fun here. I always regret moving any furniture I bought here though. The neat business model allows me to feel responsible for putting together the particle board together improperly. If you want actual wood you have to pay up, & still risk putting it together poorly or loosely.  

More importantly, they have removed the ball pit. Now there are wisks there. You can build an 18 piece wisk set instead of playing in a ball pit.

Affordable furniture with names you can hardly pronounce? That'll be IKEA for you!

Honestly: I do love the place when it comes to buying furniture and housewares that won't break the bank. There are some great pieces if you keep your eyes peeled! We have the Hemnes line of wardrobe and china cabinet in our house (definitely recommend them), and are probably going to add to it with the dresser for our bedroom. Is the quality above and beyond other furniture stores? Hm...nope. You'll find pressboard in the back of some pieces. But hey - I've had my china cabinet and wardrobe for 2.5 years now and they still look like new (even after moving them out of a 4 story apartment complex - no worse for wear)...just don't punch your hand through the back of them or something crazy like that!

Oh...and don't forget to pick up a frozen yogurt cone or a cinnamon roll on your way out. Yummmm...

Cheap furniture and cheap food. Woo-hoo!

The money you spend on food goes towards the total of your same-day purchase.  So eat first!!!  There were 7 of us and we had a $48 food bill.  Unfortunately, we ate after we made our purchase, so I learned the hard way.  Some lucky couple got a $48 coupon though.
Enjoyed shopping..but the food was horrible....chicken was like rubber....  I would never venture to eat there again.... returned it for a refund it was that bad...

I'm always on the fence when it comes to IKEA.

On one hand, you walk in and the displays basically suck you into loving just about everything, because oh hey that 400 square foot space can be filled with so much stuff and romg look at that cozy bedroom set and ahhh I want that useless dog-shaped pillow.

On the other hand, it's cheap quality furniture, cheaply made, and will self-destruct in approximately three years.  Plus, assembling a medium-size bookcase by yourself when it's about as tall as you are, when the holes don't exactly line up and the screws don't exactly fit into their places... yeah, not fun.

Still, the prize delight of IKEA is their gastronomically cheap restaurant, and who doesn't like swedish meatballs?  Plus, at the end of the long perilous journey through the store, there's a $1 ice cream cone waiting for you at the end.  Huzzah!

The Swedes know whats up.  I always heard everyone talk about Ikea this, Ikea that.  I thought to myself "How can a stupid old furniture store be so awesome?"  And then I went to Ikea.  The upper floor is set up like real rooms and it really helps to see the furniture in action.  The bottom floor is just a huge market of anything ou could use for your home.  Every time I set foot in Ikea, I end up buying several things that I did not intent on purchasing, just because everything is so inexpensive and quality.  I have bought everything from furniture to kitchen trinkets to meatballs here.  Speaking of meatballs, the food is pretty good here too.  They have a full buffet upstairs and a quick stop downstairs on the way out where they have soft serve (YUM), hot dogs, and popcorn.  Ikea really lives up to the hype and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for inexpensive, trendy items for your home.

It's Ikea! Why wouldn't it be five stars?

The store is fun to walk around and enjoy shopping.  In case you are unfamiliar with Ikea it is a home goods store that really shines with its furniture. Best of all the furniture is pretty cheap but the quality isn't that low.

Also, good food in the cafeteria. Definitely take a stroll upstairs to eat. I am not the biggest fan of Swedish meat balls but others are. I prefer the chicken strips. There is something for everyone

I have two problems with IKEA: One is that staff is very hard to find. The store is made to be mostly autonomous. Two, the store is a maze. Probably would be fine if I were browsing, but I came in with a set of items to buy, and finding them becomes a chore.

Nevertheless, IKEA has really awesome items at fantastic prices, and that more than makes up for the above.

(Also, for posterity, IKEA is really just fantastically designed all around, even if makes my style of buying hard. I really like how they were able to reimagine food!)

Yep, most everybody is in love with IKEA and I see why. 

Clean contemporary designs, I bet this place appeals to hipsters and yuppies alike lol. Not sure where I fit in, maybe you could say I'm bohemian and contemporary but no matter, we all like ikea and this is why;

-- low prices
-- wide variety of products
-- excellent dining -- love the restaurant and according to all the photos posted of food, others do too. what's nice is getting good food for a good price, if you're hungry and don't want to spend a lot, then there's hot dogs for 50 cents on the 1st floor

--good quality products; if my ikea bed was falling apart or the ikea mattress sagging or my comforter shredding i would have a different opinion but that's not the case. i paid the lowest price for my combo, even cheaper than walmart and it's holding up great. its comfy to me and has the nice clean line modern look that is so popular now but i've preferred all my life. the only thing with ikea is if you don't like to buy items that your friends will have the same thing, you may want to try somewhere else, but who cares about that when trying to find a quality product, that has the right look for the lowest price?!

--hey, ikea really knows how to cater to families. period 
there's an awesome playroom for the kids to play while you shop, however my little one is too young. the kids have to be older and potty trained. yet, i would not want to leave my kid there without my supervision because there is not enough staff in the play area to observe all that can happen when you have a lot of kids present. i may be alone on that one because there was a parent upset because the room was full and their child was unable to go in until the numbers went down. sorry, parent ikea is right, wait until there is a smaller number of kids in there before you allow another one to come in. 

i really love the dining area for children, there's a flat screen tv playing disney movies and has colorful tables and chairs just for kids, and is also equipped with rollers on the walls for kids to give a spin for fun. 

-- ikea is a warehouse, but yet the system of using display rooms on the 2nd floor gives potential customers a vision to work with and caters to our inner-likes which is why they are so friggin successful. with so many items they've put to use a system where you see the product beautifully displayed on the 2nd floor, you write down the info (paper and pencils, even tape measure is everywhere if you need it), then you get it from the warehouse on the 1st floor. the company constantly encourages you to write down the magical product numbers each time so it's a whiz to get what you need and know exactly where to find it just like you're in a library or bookstore promptly turning your inspiration into reality.  

At the end of day when I'm putting my Ikea furniture and products to use, I'm enjoying them everyday and my child is too. 

Whimsical artistic designs, yet always a practical use, they will be booming in business for quite some time.

Who doesn't like getting lost in Ikea? Communists, that's who! I like to come here whether I'm moving, or looking for a cheap accent piece, or just killing time. They do a good job with displays, so you have some decorating ideas to start with. A lot of the things at Ikea are generic, but I'm in to modifying the pieces I get. I have a TV stand that I removed the sliding drawers from, and spray painted the legs gold to create a unique sofa table.
The stuff you get resells on craigslist faster than something you'll get a other stores. Bring a reusable bag. They don't offer plastic. Food there is mediocre but cheap. The supervised play area is great for families so you can shop in piece.

I have always loved Ikea's style.  I thought to myself that one day, I would have a home that was 100% Ikea.  I love the clean lines, love how everything is reasonably priced, and love that with around $3,000 I was able to FULLY furnish, and accessorize my entire apartment;  living room, dining room, everything in my kitchen, bedroom and full office.  On top of the delivery charge for all the furniture, I paid $700 to have the furniture assembled by UX Home Delivery, the company that Ikea recommends. (April, 2012)

FLASH FORWARD SIX MONTHS (October, 2012) to my king size Hemnes bed frame falling apart.  The foot board was crumbling, so I called Ikea and they stated they would open up a "claim" for me to review the case.  I needed to email them pictures and a copy of my original receipt for them to proceed.  No problem, I stated.  The next day, I emailed scott.lofgren@ikea.com then pictures, a detailed email, and my receipt for purchase, delivery and assembly.

FLASH FORWARD TWO WEEKS. (Mid-October, 2012)  No word from anyone.  I email scott.lofgren@ikea.com AGAIN.

FLASH FORWARD ONE WEEK.  I get a call from a woman who states that Scott is not handling the issue anymore, and she wanted me to resend my original email with pictures, description of the problem, and my original receipt.  I told her that she needed to get the information from Scott, since I wasn't at a computer at the time.

FLASH FORWARD ANOTHER WEEK. (Halloween Week, 2012)  I get a phone call.  The woman I spoke with stated that the integrity of the Hemnes bed frames WAS a recurring issue.  She stated that they will send a truck to pick up the OLD bed frame and drop off a new one.  I would be responsible for taking the old bed apart into "manageable pieces" and assembling the new bed.  I stated that I paid to have the bed put together by the company they recommended, and would like the new bed put together since I already paid for the service.  The woman stated that is not their policy.

Since I was not left with the tools that came with the bed to assemble it, and apartment living does not warrant having a bigger tool set than a 108 piece whats-it-who case of tools that helps me hang pictures,  (I do have tools, but none small enough to fit), I had to physically break the bed apart.  (Manageable Pieces!)

FLASH FORWARD FOUR DAYS:  The company that came to pick up the old and drop off the new was UX HOME DELIVERY, THE SAME PEOPLE THAT ASSEMBLED ALL MY FURNITURE TO BEGIN WITH!  I was told on the phone that the people picking up did not do assembly, which was a LIE.  It was the same company that spent seven hours in my house in April putting everything together.

The fact that this "warranty" took over a month to be resolved is ridiculous.  On top of that, I was promised that additional compensation for the amount I originally spent on assembly would be considered.  It is now December 27th, and through countless emails, phone calls, and frustrations, only yesterday did they tell me I am s*** out of luck and they will not do anything to reimburse me for the assembly charge.

Three full months of aggravation.  I would never recommend the Hemnes bedroom set to ANYONE.  All of my other furniture is beautiful and is standing up well.  This one stupid incident has left such a sour taste in my mouth.

If I ever have another issue with any of my Ikea furniture, I'm just going to throw it out.  Paying for something of higher quality is much less aggravation.

You would think that when one customer spends nearly $4,000 with their company and an assembly company from which they receive a nice kickback for pushing, they would have better customer service.

I will never stop buying their home decor items, but furniture?  Never, ever again.

I've never been thrilled by the food. I get it. It's Swedish. It's also the McDonalds of the Swedish world, in my book. Other than that, the place is always pretty busy which isn't a bad thing. I think some stuff is pricey while other items are awesomely priced. This is a pretty massive place and I've always had a fun day here, believe it or not. If you're looking to waste a day, come to IKEA but don't bring your wallet (or your credit card).

Large IKEA. Pretty  much what you'd expect out of an IKEA. Furniture that you can use for an entire stay in one location, look stylish while you do it and then toss when it's time to move. Very good cinnamon buns - you can get 6 for $4 and then microwave them back to gooey warmth at home.

I love ikea! They've got a great product for the price! TONS of parking and there is plenty of space to pull your truck up and load it. They've got great prices on pretty much everything. A lot of their furniture is a bit chintzy, but still worth the price. Just don't expect to make it a family heirloom.
This is the 3rd ikea I have been it & its just like the rest. Clean & easy to get around. The cashier was very nice. If I need anymore odds & ends I will go back.

I like to think that as an adult, I can do better than IKEA, but we still end up here about once a month and usually walk out with a few odds and ends. I've bought some new furniture pieces from there over the years, but as we all know you get what you pay for, and if you know you're going to be moving a lot, don't even bother. 

These days, I'm a little more environmentally conscious, but still a sucker for IKEA, so I get the stuff I want off Craigslist for a third of the price when I need my fix.

We don't eat there often because the boyfriend doesn't like it, and even though I do, when we went last weekend every single dish and cup was spectacularly crusty. I tried about four different mugs for my complimentary coffee, settled on the least filthy one and rinsed it out with hot water until it was tolerably gross. Seriously IKEA, if I wanted to eat off of dirty plates I would have stayed at home.

I hated my first visit here because this store is a true maze...it's build so you have to walk through the whole store to find what your looking for...very frustrating. Once you realize that then you can go in with the mind frame of "let's see what I can find". On the other hand I look for what I want online then just pick it up at the main floor it saves me an unwanted walk.

In a nutshell: not worth the drive, the time, or the energy spent assembling.

OK furniture for an average price, which comes in a million pieces with missing pieces and wholes drilled in the wrong sizes. We had to go back 2 additional times for missing parts and we even had to redrill our own holes to make the screws fit.

Not worth the price or energy.

I was familiar with the Swedish wonder of the world thanks to the Orlando location, so I knew immediately where I would go for my cheap college furniture. My roommate freshman year took up our entire room with random ikea stuff, and when we found an apartment together, we knew our summer work money would be spent at a certain yellow superstore. 

The concept is simple: buy the stuff at base price (like my all-time favorite Billy bookshelf), and you'll be good in regards to the great value. When you decide to get all the add-ons, the special doors, etc, you rack up your bill big time. 

Also, I've bought the Malm bedroom stuff, and I absolutely love it all in the brown-black color. My full size bed frame was $150, and the dressers ranged from $70-$150. And I'm totally happy with it all. 

The downside is that it can take you an hour to get through the place even if you can bypass jumping on every couch and bed on the upper floor. The downstairs is where it gets dangerous: there's a whole area of $5 and under... That bill racks up quickly! But definitely worth a visit if you're into that kind thing. I'll prob be back as soon as my next paycheck drops in.
