(4) ~ very good overall food & service.  NOTES: Probably the lowest cost meal you'll find in PA...The bill for the above menu was $10.00;-)  And yes they take Credit Cards.

OUR MENU:
** Elderflower Drink = (4) very good
** Coffee = (4) very good
** Swedish Meatballs = (4) very good
**  Cinnamon Bun = (4) very good
 * Lingonberry Drink = (3.5) good
* Swedish Pancakes w. Lingonberries = (3.5) good
* Mashed Potatoes = (3.5) good
* Milk Chocolate Bar = (3.5) good

I like coming to IKEA for the Swedish Meatballs. My wife loves this place. When my two girls were toddlers we'd come here often, they loved all the colorful toys. The furniture is lovely, it looks beautiful - but not a fan of it. I guess Ikea furniture is good for college dorms. But I don't like the idea of using a tiny little S shaped tool to put my furniture together. But that's just me.

Are you a starving student or low-income 20-something that doesn't care if your apartment is furnished the same way as all your low-income 20-something student friends? Then IKEA is for you. Cheap and classy (or cute, if that's what you prefer), I don't deny that IKEA is my number one go-to to keep my apartment fashionable in an affordable way. I particularly love the dishes, and how they sell them in sets and piece by piece so if I break a bowl or two, I can replace them without investing in 6 more with matching plates. I own a lot of things from IKEA, including all my bedroom furniture, so obviously I'm a fan. But at the end of the day you get what you pay for and eventually your table legs begin to show wear and the chair will break on a rowdy night with friends and you'll notice that your knock-off jewelry display really doesn't look as good as the one on your mom's vanity. IKEA is for college, it's not forever. Make peace with that and you have all you need.

I know I will be a grown-up when my furniture is no longer made of particle board, but today is not that day yet.

I was plenty excited when IKEA decided to open a store in the Tampa Bay area, and have made several pilgrimages even after surviving the Grand Opening Day bonanza.

For those not familiar with this temple of Do-It-Yourself furniture awesomeness, IKEA is located along Adamo Drive in downtown Tampa at 22nd street. It's kinda hard to miss the giant 2-story blue and yellow building with the swarms of people moving in and out of the parking lot.

As you walk through the front doors they hand you a map, a paper measuring tape, a pencil, and a sturdy, disposable bag for carrying "stuff", and then point you up the escalator.  If you don't know any better then you follow the crowds in front of you, like lemmings marching to the sea. Follow the yellow brick road, and all of that. Sure enough there is a painted line on the floor to guide you past every single showroom display and turn you all around like a walk through a haunted house. You might want to go faster, but you're trapped behind the people in front of you with their double-wide strollers and 37 family members all stretched out across the aisles. *shudders*

Thankfully there is a better way... a quick study of the map shows you "secret routes" for dodging the crowds and arriving though a back entrances into the showroom areas of interest. One 5-hour trip around the store on opening day in Tampa, and I was begging for another way. The concept is pretty simple......let's say you'd like to look at bookcases, or kitchen tables, or entertainment centers. You find that section of the store on your map, and then weave through the side entrances till you are there. 

I have a lot of IKEA bookcases scattered around my condo, but today I was looking for a new entertainment unit for the living room. I spotted a Hemnes 3-drawer TV unit that was the perfect height and width for the cubby hole along the wall. I've built the Hemnes bookcases, so I had a pretty good idea about the quality of the materials and the look of the finished product.

After copying down the item number and location I zipped downstairs to the warehouse area, located the carton, paid for my merchandise, loaded that into the back of my SUV and was off. It took just over 2 hours to assemble, but I'm real happy with my new entertainment center - and just in time for tomorrow's Super Bowl party!

Photos of the finished entertainment center sitting in my living room are attached.

I want to start off by saying that I love Ikea and their products. However their home delivery system is a total waste of time and a source of extreme aggravation. Do yourself a favor and rent a U-Haul truck and  bribe your friends to help you load and unload it for you. My sister's furniture arrived damaged on Tuesday and when I called the number on my paperwork it said to call if there were issues, no one answered the phone (she was working so I waited on the delivery guys for her). I called a few times the first night and was sent to voice mail every time. We didn't get a call back so she called again the next day and guess what she got sent to voice mail again. After leaving 6 messages without a call back someone finally answered the phone on Friday and she was told she would get a call back within the hour. Surprise of all surprises, no one called back. So about four hours later we called again and got transferred around to someone who finally put the information in the system that she had received damaged merchandise - IKEA had nothing on file showing that there was a problem with the delivery. She then told me it would be 1-3 days before someone would call back to reschedule the delivery. She told her that was unacceptable and she said she would change my status to high priority. Someone finally called back on Saturday afternoon and we were finally able to reschedule for delivery on Monday 5-9 pm but then she gets a call on Sunday confirming the delivery on Monday from 12-4pm. She let them know that the time is wrong and I can't be there at that time and the delivery time was supposed to be from 5-9pm. The guy basically says well that's what time we are coming, it can't be changed, but I will put a note in your file. So Monday there is another call saying they are running late for the 12-4 pm delivery but they will be there as soon as possible. Again she tries to tell them they got the time wrong and there won't be anyone there before 5 pm and the girl gets snotty. After a week she finally got the replacement piece, I totally regret advising her to use home delivery, and will never use it again. All the Ikea reps said they were sorry but no one offered to refund any of the delivery charges or give a refund of any sort. 

So like I said in the beginning rent a truck from UHaul and beg/bribe your single guy friends to load and unload the furniture for you BUT DO NOT pay Ikea to deliver the furniture for you. I promise you will regret it.

I don't like the "consumer as worker" model that stores like IKEA have. I have to find the stuff in their warehouse, carry it to my car itself, and then assemble it at home. I can't find an employee and I usually have to check myself out. It's irritating.

But I do love the stuff they have--confusing as it is to find anything in the maze of a store--the design aesthetic is sweet. A lot of furniture in our house is from IKEA and its lovely. (Certainly not durable or intuitive to assemble though.)

I also have a disdain to all of the waterfront big box stores in Philadelphia. I hate that Walmart, Target, IKEA, Home Depot, and some strip clubs are how our waterfront is developed. If Baltimore can do it, why can't Philly?

As a student and part of a young couple starting out, IKEA is a godsend. I love walking through the store, I could spend a LOT of time here. Almost all of my furniture is from here and I've never been disappointed. 

Their "build yourself" tables where you choose your own tops and legs are awesome- I have two- one I use as a desk, and one I use for my hedgehog's large cage. It's easy to change out the legs too to change the look of it- they're very inexpensive.

This is not the place to go if you want attentive customer service, but as long as you know what you're getting into, it's awesome.

If you want some overpriced DIY furniture, then this is the place to go. I purchased a bed frame here with slats and a mattress for around $800. Recently one of the slats broke in half on the bed frame.

 I did nothing but sit on it. I am not a large person by any means, and am likely under the average adult weight. For the price, I expected better quality. The price of the IKEA hype is included in whatever you're buying here. I suggest avoiding it altogether. If you're patient enough you can usually find better furniture at thrift stores anyway.

If you are looking for average quality furniture for decent prices, then this is the place to check out. A lot of their stuff tends to be of the more modern style, but for certain rooms of the house, it's good enough. Over the years, we have gotten some furniture here for the kids playroom and some home accessories like lamps, mirrors, kitchenware, etc., from their marketplace. The furniture that we've purchased here has held up fairly well. I do recall it being a bit difficult to put together, but it's survived seven years of kids so far and still looks in pretty good shape (admittedly my two boys aren't overly rough on stuff though). We have purchased things here that when we got them home, just didn't put together well and we ended up returning them. We do like some of the live plants they sell in the marketplace in addition to things like their cutting boards, glass jars, etc. We don't come here that often, but when we do, we rarely walk out empty handed. This is a huge store that's a bit of a pain to get too. I actually liked their old location better. They do have a child watch area and as long as your kid is at least 37" tall without shoes, you can drop them off there while you do your shopping. Otherwise, if you have little ones in toe, keep a close eye on them, as you could easily lose them in this store!

No matter what I've been told over the years and still today--"Ikea is only good for college kids or young people" "You're an adult now, you should have adult furniture...not Ikea stuff" or "Ikea stuff is cheaply made"--I still really LOVE Ikea and they have never really let me down.  I think Ikea has really grown over the years and their furniture styles have really become more sophisticated in style.  I love their prices and designs and even though the assembly and their "no instructions" instructions can be a pain, none of the pieces that I have purchased from them over the years has ever let me down.  I've had more expensive items break down before any of my Ikea pieces even budge.  My only gripe is that I can never get cell phone service inside (makes it hard to text pictures for 2nd opinons) and it's always soooo hot (I'm conviced this is their tactic to make you thristy and buy a drink before you leave).  But whatever gripes I have, a $1 yogurt cone makes everything all better at the end of my shopping trip :-)

Visit time/day: weekday evening
Atmosphere: Ikea

Ikea is Ikea is Ikea, right? The thing that can set a big box retailer location apart is the people who work there. I received 'above and beyond' service last night at the Tampa Ikea and decided to break my 'food only' habit and yelp about it. 

My rental house backyard has no exterior lighting and my dog, who is elderly and now afraid of the dark, walks 1 foot out to do his business at night. I've been stalking the Ikea website for the outdoor solar lights and they finally showed up as 'in stock' yesterday. I was told they sell out immediately so I quickly drove out there after work. 

I couldn't find the coveted solar lights anyplace in the store. I asked an employee in Lighting who walked me over to the one solar desk lamp. I explained I was looking for the outdoor lights - she told me they were in the process of putting them out in the self serve area but that they weren't 'officially' for sale yet. She told me to go to the self serve area. When I got there the huge Sun n' Fun display area was completely roped off and 2 employees were 'guarding' it. I noticed a few boxes of the Solvinden lights that I had stalked on the website. One of the employees asked if she could help me and I told her about my mission. She told me she could let me into the roped off zone to let me look around for a few minutes. She listened politely to my stupid story about my dog and patiently helped me find the lights I had seen on the website, spending about 10 minutes scanning barcodes on unopened shipping boxes, opening boxes, and looking around the entire roped off area to find the styles I was looking for. She could have easily said 'Why don't you come back tomorrow when these are actually for sale?' or 'If I let you in here then everyone will want to come in', but she didn't - she helped me (and my dogger) immensely and I really appreciate it.

Hurray for an Ikea employee going above and beyond - thank you!

It's IKEA.  I actually rarely buy anything because a 550sq ft apartment is rarely laid out as they have it on their showroom floor.  I do like the meatball combo in the cafeteria & the food at the front of the store though!  I go back & walk around about twice a year.

This isn't the largest IKEA I've been in (no shoppingcart escalator), but it's not tiny either!   There are two floors of awesomeness!  Be sure to get a pencil and paper to write down your item numbers because it's a 'self serve' kind of store. 

The merchandise isn't of the highest quality, but has the 'look' of high quality.  
I personally love the kids section.  Plenty of bedroom/toyroom items!

I LOVE IKEA! And honestly, it's not even because of their furniture. It's more because of their food. More specifically, their meatballs. After wandering through the maze of perfectly setup kitchens, bedrooms, and living rooms, you could work up an appetite. Well, perfect placement, the cafeteria is right at the end of that maze before going downstairs. I always want to try something new, but I can't get away from the meatballs. Dinner for 2: meatball platters for both (meatballs & mashed potatoes), mac & cheese, chocolate cake, almond cake, & waters. $15. Nice! And everything was just, ugh, so amazingly delicious. 

Now that you've inhaled those calories, you can work it off by lifting the heavy boxes that your desired furniture comes in. This is the first time I actually purchased big furniture (desk, bookcase, and a chair). A girl my size can't do that lifting, so that's what the boy is for. I guess this is the only annoyance to IKEA. It's pretty heavy stuff, which makes the cart a little difficult to maneuver and load into the car.

Boys love to build, so I let him do all the assembling. (Seriously, is that fun for all boys? I was not having fun at all.) Took quite some time for everything, but we got it done. Apparently, he's heard complaints about the directions and now he agrees. (What? Men follow directions!? jk.) The various pieces could be built in a different order so you don't find yourself trying to screw in pieces in hard to read places.

They've found ways to cut costs, which may inconvenience the consumer a bit, but they must be doing something right if everyone loves it.

Ikea seems to cater to all demographics, toys for the kids, sleek sexy furniture for adults and affordable good looking furniture for students, pretty much covers it all. If you generally have any idea what you are looking for, like a dresser, then you probably will find it at Ikea. I hate the location of this place though its always packed, always. The setup of the store sucks too because theres only one way in and one way out. Essentially you are forced to look at the whole store when you might just need one thing. So when you park you ask yourself do I want to walk now or later? Usually later because your almost always walking out of Ikea with a purchase. Some of the furniture of course is cheaply made and will bust on you as you assemble it, BUT some looks durable as well. Will I be back? of course who does not ever visit an Ikea

This review is going to hit all aspects of Ikea.  My wife and I recently decided to make some major purchases from them, and we've visited this location several times as a result.  I've been able to not only utilize their in-store customer service, I'm also going to review their delivery and assembly, their web service, and their cafeteria all in one swoop.    

We decided we wanted a king size bed, and wanted to see if we could get a less expensive option here.  We don't need anything extravagant, just something that will properly keep my fat ass from hitting the ground, thank you very much.  Also, since we had only recently bought our queen mattress, we decided to get a small frame for that to move it to the guest room.  So we went off to search for a king size mattress, king size bed, and queen bed frame.  

We started by browsing the website.  I do have to say that the website service leaves a lot to be desired.  Even the associate in the store told us not to trust the website when it came to determining if something was in stock.  It gave us conflicting information.  Best to visit the store in person, always.  

We did eventually visit the store, and decided on a king sized foam latex mattress for $649, a Hemnes king pine bed for $239, and a Lerkvik metal queen bed for $139.  Along with accessories, we grabbed $1,227.99 in merchandise before tax.  

Now, one snag.  The mattress wasn't in stock.  Luckily at the time, we had a very helpful associate who directed us to pay for the frames we wanted, set up delivery, and then call her back two days later when the mattress would be in stock and she would reserve one.  Then we would come back to the store, pay for the mattress, and attach that to the delivery order.  Mild inconvenience to me though. 

We got the items (one was full serve which had to be brought to us), went through the checkout line, and went to the delivery area... and waited.   They weren't well staffed here, and they backed up.  Once we got through it, we set up delivery and assembly.  Since we were getting a half decent deal on our purchase, I figured I'd splurge for the assembly.  Total cost for delivery is $59 for all items, and assembly for the two frames was $149.  And they then charge the 8% tax on delivery and assembly. Tack on an extra $224.64 for the full service.

The good news is that when I went back for my mattress, I wasn't charged any extra to tack it on to my delivery.  The bottom line... all totaled for furniture, tax, delivery, and assembly, my bill in the end came to $1550.87.

Price-wise, I'm estatic.  I recently checked Sleepy's for a similar quote.  To get their lowest end king sized latex mattress, a basic wood bed frame with a headboard, and a similar metal queen bed frame was $2200 just for the products themselves without tax, shipping or assembly. 

I did sample the cafeteria meatballs on my return trip for the mattress.  Can't beat them for the price.  And yes, I concur the frozen yogurt is excellent.  Free coffee with the family card, and I even could have gotten a second free yogurt with it too.  These were also good deals.

But in the end, what matters is did they come through on their promises upon delivery? 

We scheduled it for Easter Sunday.  I've seen some horror stories about their carrier, Urban Express.  Called them the night before just to check, and they told me they'd call back by 7:30 pm with a delivery timeframe.  I got a call at 8:45.  They told me that they would be there between 1-5pm on Sunday.  

They showed up at 3 on Sunday.  And as they brought my furniture in, I asked them how they were going to do the assembly.  

"Ummm, we're only the delivery guys. We don't do assembly. you have to call our office for that."

I call Urban Express.  Guess what?  Ikea only sent them an order to deliver.  THEY NEVER SENT OVER THE ASSEMBLY ORDER.  As a result, I now have unassembled furniture delivered to me on a Sunday afternoon.  This does not bode well.  

So I call Ikea's call center.  The associate determined that yes I did have assembly paid for, but the date was entered wrong by the previously mentioned inefficient delivery associate.  Therefore the system never sent over the assembly order with the proper delivery date.  

They got me in touch with the manager on duty at the store.  I was given the option to call back and MAYBE they could set me up in a couple of days for assembly.  I said the heck with it and asked for my assembly charge to be refunded.  They did so apologetically.  

So as a result, I spent 4 hours of my Easter Sunday putting together a king bed.  I still have a queen bed to assemble later.  Ruined my dinner plans too.  I was a bit steamed over that. 

An inefficient delivery associate turned what would have been a 4 star review into a 2 star experience.  On the bright side, the king bed seems very sturdy for the price and the mattress is comfy.

I'll probably go back again and get more stuff.  I just won't buy assembly ever.

Free 1.5 hours of child care and they actually engage them in activities from what I've noticed (coloring and that sort of thing). The food is cheap ($.50 all beef hot dog or $1 frozen yogurt anyone?). Picked up some of those $4 spice racks for holding hair products and creating a mini children's library. And the rooms are fun to look at--yes, a lot of the furniture is cheap and poorly made as we all are well aware of, but it's fun to look at how small spaces are configured and organized.

I do like ikea, they have everything you need and more! Our bedroom is pretty much all from there, and coffee tables. I really have to be in the mood to go here otherwise I don't like to go, it's either I know what I'm going in for or it can wait for another day. The big delema I've been having recently though is that the only thing ill eat from the cafeteria is the fish n chips. Sometimes when I go there they don't have it? And other times they do? .. I do like the fact that it's cheap food too.

Great fun to wonder around.  Unfortunately the last 3 times we went to ikea and found something we loved, they didn't have stock.  All 3 times!  Left disappointed and had to go check 3 other stores. 

We have decided to save our time and not go there in the future because of this...

I have a love/hate relationship with Ikea.  I really love the prices and can always find something that I would like to have in my home.  I struggle with one thing though; it gets to me when you can point out all the pieces in someone's home (or often business) that were purchased at Ikea - I like the modern styles but I also prefer to have some level of uniqueness in my home.  I bought a super nice picture of the Paris skyline (if you know Ikea, you probably know exactly which one I am talking about; if not, you likely have seen it at least once before anyway) - a few years later and I am seeing it everywhere; friends' homes, hair salons, banks, car dealerships....sorta takes away the charm, sadly.  

Could be because I have recently moved so I have literally been at Ikea at least once a weekend (if not more) for the last month and a half, but depending on my mood, and when I know exactly what I want, I have ZERO desire to walk through the entire store.  Mind you, being a regular lately, I am getting a little better at finding the shortcuts.  Also being a regular lately, I have experienced more than once an unadvertised shortage of stock...which can add to the frustration of having to walk through the entire store just to check if that one thing is there yet!!

Ikea has great stuff for great prices - so it's no wonder you see their merchandise everywhere.  Although I do believe we need some time apart, I will certainly be back to Ikea with an open wallet!

even if you're not shopping for a specific item, Ikea is a great place to go for inspiration.  They have simply an amazing if not overwhelming selection of products for home. Heck, just come here and but a complete room decorated by Ikea designers.

The restaurant is also good eats.  Love the Swedish meatballs, extra gravy and french fries!

Don't go if you're tired.  Also, keep an eye for shortcuts around the massive store.   

I meant to review this as a store and not as a restaurant.  The restaurant is fine, 3 stars - a place to go several times and they have many promotions for budget minded folks.  As for the store, I'd give it 4 stars.

Besides the amazing display and the affordable priced furniture the cafeteria is also pretty hoppin! I get pretty exhausted whenever I go to ikea and I love that there's food served near by for a mini break. There's always something going on so be on the look out!

Over the past couple of years, I've come here to pick up some furniture. My wife and I just purchased their Malm bed with storage drawers, and it is working out pretty well. The products aren't great quality, but I really appreciate their pricing model. You avoid a lot of the gimmicks with other furniture stores. This specific IKEA is pretty much what you come to expect. The staff is good, the store layout can be a little confusing, although the signage is helpful, and the meatballs are terrific.

Aside from Ikea being a little bit of a maze to get through ( I have become a MASTER at the cut throughs) IKEA is full of great ideas & pretty much everything you need for making your home efficient and swanky! I've hit IKEA hard lately to make my downsize affordable and adorable. Great linens & bedding, shelving units, kitchen wares, decor....

Love the Ikea family card! Special deals, discounts & free coffee/tea with every visit. I didn't think Ikea would be a destination to eat/ snack...I was wrong. Awesome fro-yo for a dollar!

I'm a fan. I'll gladly hit up Ikea for whatever I can, be it home necessities or a quick lunch/snack :)

**I wish this place had been around when I threw wedding & baby showers a whole bunch. Awesome ideas for decorating and favors.
Always torn @ Ikea, but like Costco you always end up with stuff you didn't know you need! Typical store, with a decent enough "in stock" items. Helpful staff when you can find one free.

Had a wardrobe home delivered. Product arrived broken and when I called to get it exchanged they told me I would have to wait 5-7 days to get another one sent out. I was also told that I'd be contacted in 48 hours to set up a delivery time and when I hadn't heard from them in 3 days, I called again to set up delivery myself. Besides apologizing over and over like a moron, the customer service lady was rude and not very good at her job.

My sister told me that Ikea got in trouble for serving horse meat in their meatballs that I've eaten several times before! But even as she said that I drooled because I was starving! I felt better seeing a sign saying they only use beef and pork in their meat (I guess they have to so people still eat it).

Anyway, my review is mostly just for the food court. The guy was reserving me meatballs the previous customer cancelled all while muttering "I ain't gonna waste this". I didn't say anything because it's not like it was just sitting there. He just rolled it onto a new dish for me so it was messy and not tasty looking.

The cashiers are even worse. No smile, no eye contact, and rude.

Their warehouse is also a danger zone, they have open boxes everywhere.

Enjoy the USA headquarters for IKEA because you've found it! I've only once made it through this location without buying something. It's much more of a challenge than the South Philly location. This tells me that the selection is bigger and better. Also, fun tip for people who need ideas but won't sink as low as pinterest. Look through the catalog. Lastly, the meatballs. I'd love to buy a special girl those meatballs someday.

Oh, Ikea. How I love thee. Your furniture brings many joys and many frustrations. There's never a time where I'd come and go without a single thing. Almost everything in my apartment is Ikea furniture - bed frame, tables, chairs, desks.. Even the little cardboard boxes. Dish ware, silver ware, cups and plastic ware I've also bought from here, and for excellent prices! 

Their restaurant upstairs is amazing. Swedish meatballs are a must when you visit Ikea, they're very good. I also enjoy their smoked salmon salads, chicken tenders, and ribs. A lot of their dishes can be bought in their frozen food section downstairs. And if you check out their website, Ikea has cute little events for adults and kids. Speaking of kids, there's a supervised playground inside Ikea for your toddlers to play in while you shop.

A couple of the only aspects I'm disappointed with is that many Ikea products in the marketplace are made in China (before I went I always thought Ikea prided itself on Swedish designed and made stuff), and majority of their foreign employees are very rude. Usually not directly, but the way they'll talk to you is very condescending and discourteous even when you try to be cheery.

If you don't mind building your own furniture, definitely stop by here. Either bring your own bag or buy a bunch of Ikea bags (big blue ones!). They will save you! And be sure to take your potty break at the entrance - both floors of Ikea are a complete maze!

Talk about a daft location!  I heard that government somehow messed things up, as well as the management of Plymouth Meeting Mall, so it all ended up in this industrial area, after a intensive site cleanup.  It's off the beaten path, to be sure.

I used to shop the Plymouth Meeting store and it was a bit crowded and traffic was too much, trying to load boxes.  The company only had 3 U.S. stores then.

Of course, the inside of the store was fine, and it's nicely big.  I noticed that they even had a "rest area" to go with the rest rooms.  That's something I haven't seen at the other stores, but maybe after their remodeling they'll have them.

I went for lunch, and had the Midsommar Salmon Lasagne, which was good.  It's great to be able to buy something interesting and not pay $60 for a meal.  I wished that they had Almond Cake but it wasn't there today.  In fact, the restaurant employees were friendly, but a lot of things seemed undone.  Maybe, it was that I was there after 2 p.m.

Still, what really goes wrong at IKEA?  They've got it under control.

as a contractor i have installed many kitchens that my customers bought from here, they are low quality and do not last,they look good in the catalog and showroom floor but buyer beware ! the furniture is also pretty low in quality.

When I go to IKEA I know what to expect do it yourself items that may or may not turn out s great. The past couple of times we have experienced nothing but pure bliss. All the items we have purchased are working like they are designed to and have not broken. We have shopped at other stores like IKEA that it will not mention that simply do not get the job done. The Omar that we purchased is the perfect accessory for our garage.  They have the variety that is needed to decorate your whole house for any type of style.

I was running in to grab some bedding for my daughter for her bday & as I knew it was kids bedding so I was able to pop in & get it right @ the top of the stairs by the restaurant, get breakfast for $1 & had time leftover for a quick look around! I ended up picking up a coordinating cushion & a mirror that was a good size for $19.99 when a similar smaller one was $29.99 @ bouclair home. All in all a successful trip!

I like the concept and deals here. But the products just don't last. One year is the life of most of the dressers and tables. If you unassemble, your product is no longer good. lol. The food in the cafeteria area is good. Very friendly and good staff.
Good furniture. I like how cheap everything is. They have really good food, and this place is a great place to look around because of the massive size building.

It's IKEA. But I'd rather drive to the one in Baltimore. I'd really rather go to the one in Cincinnati. Here's why the others are better

-Food is all the same across my IKEA experiences - BUT this cafe was dirtier and less maintained than others. Soda fountains were broken, ligonberry juice was watery and not correct.

-This is a rather small IKEA in comparison. Less selection than others.

-No self checkout! The checkout lines were awful - I forgot about IKEA lines before self checkout (not that they are always great, people are hilarious).

-Parking lot is REALLY weird. We somehow parked in an area where there were no cart corrals, the only one around was on the other side of one of those paved grassy dividers. When you enter, people just turn and start driving through parking places like crazy. Bad planning.

-Not much space for loading (in comparison to other IKEAs)

-Information stations more scarce throughout the store.

I'm sad that this is the HQ one. There are SO many better ones, even in PA (Pittsburgh)!  Also, is it embarrassing that I have been to this many IKEAs? I've been to the original one in Sweden too, and I was hoping the HQ one in PA would be more like that. Not at all.

If you are looking for a review of the furniture, I don't think Yelp is the place to look. But my house is pretty much furnished by IKEA, and I'm cool with it. Works well!
Great cafeteria food, at very reasonable prices.

While it's true that coming here on a Saturday borders on insanity, I live within twenty minutes, so I can visit this IKEA HQ whenever I want to! And I do return on many an occasion. 

IKEA has been my happy place since I was a kid and my mom would drop me off to hang out in the kid's area while she shopped. Now that I'm too tall to join the ballpit, I spend my time here perusing the feng shui rooms and checking out every new item in the warehouse. My first stop is always the As-Is section, just in case that thing I came for has a floor-model or gently-used version for 50% off. 

In 2008, we redid our entire kitchen with IKEA cabinets and it looks amazing. We ended up using the contractor the store recommended (Chuck), and he was incredibly helpful both for the beginning process of design through the finishing touches. To this day, everything is in beautiful shape. The drawers shut quietly and with the slightest touch. The pantry with mobile shelves is an engineering marvel. 

I'm currently eyeing a beautiful couch but I have to sell my only slightly old Raymour & Flanigan model first. There are so many reasons to choose IKEA over R&F and other furniture stores, but the top reason is the freedom to shop without being swarmed by overeager salespeople. Additionally, I've noticed that the fabric on IKEA furniture is very natural feeling, it never has that chemical off-gas feeling of upholstered furniture from other stores.

Total lovehate relationship, Ikea and I have.  I am heistant to buy furniture from this store based on the reviews of fellow yelpers, but I went trying to solve a closet space issue I am dealing with in a new home I'm about to move into.  

I'm still at square one.  Couldn't find anyone to help me.  I roamed the display floor looking for a few items Ikea posted on Pinterest.  

Home decor items are decent, though, including lamps, mirrors and wall-hangings.

Great value and variety on almost anything you could want for your house or office! It's a bit overwhelming. Definitely check it out! I docked a star because they didn't keep storage containers stocked when I needed them... And they renovated and it became confusing to find things.

Wander here many times usually after lunch around the area (good for digestion & burning calories). I have only eaten at their cafeteria twice in the past, their swedish meatballs were delicious and inexpensive. For $4.99 you get 15 meatballs? They also have quick service on the main floor where they sell hot dogs, pretzels, and ice cream. 

Nice showroom, pleasant to look at or rest if you get food coma like me. For their price, you shouldn't have any high expectations. You get what you pay for. Despite their quality, their showroom offers many creative ideas on interior decorations for your home. In short, a perfect cure for food coma ha It's like a big playroom for adults :)

This is your average Ikea, pretty much. They have a good selection of furniture and items like they have at every Ikea. Every now and then, the Tampa Ikea will put on some good specials, but I haven't ever tried them out.

The customer service I've experienced here has been a little off-putting. I got an item of furniture delivered to my house and when I went to go schedule the delivery, the woman working at the customer service area acted like I was putting a huge imposition on her and made me feel bad for not knowing exactly how the process worked. She acted like I was an idiot for not knowing that I had to go take the 150 pound sofa I was buying out of stock by myself and then bring it over to her so I could schedule delivery.

I searched around for a good 10 minutes looking for someone to help me move the sofa so I could buy it. I'm a pretty small person and although I am strong for my size, I would never have been able to lift or move the sofa by myself. 

I got the furniture delivered to me but if I had to go back, I'd go with the mindset to not be helped by anyone at the store whatsoever.
I love IKEA. They have nice furniture at reasonable prices.  Love their Swedish food store.

IKEA is wonderful. Their products, food and employees services are the best.

Their delivery service leaves a something to be desired. I decided to try it out and the guy input my contact number wrong. As a result, they're charging me an extra $59..

I know it's not much but it's pretty annoying that I'm getting charged for an employee's mistake.

Double and triple check your information on deliveries BEFORE you leave the store. It's their policy that once you leave the store, it's your job to do the diligence work.

**Update**
After several calls I was advised to go on site to move forward in any way. Mainly to repay the delivery cost. Once I got there, I explained my situation and about 40 min. later they were able to set up a redelivery for me at no extra cost.
You probably won't get that. I think I was the calmest person in a room full of other customers that were yelling/being extremely frustrated.

They still should add a process in their delivery to clearly re-verify contact information before you leave. But apart from that, they just moved up to 5 stars in my book

I am so incredibly irritated with IKEA.

On Saturday, August 24th, I went in and purchased a new mattress, foundation, and legs.  I paid for delivery and the shopping service as my friend and I were not able to move the items onto the carts ourselves.  the $40 extra seemed completely worth it.

Delivery was scheduled for Monday, August 26 between 5 & 9.  

At 8:50, I called their customer service line to make sure that it was still coming.  their initial response was "you still have 10 minutes".  I told the I got that, I just wanted to make sure that it was still coming because it was getting late.  After a few minutes of "looking into it" I was assured that my product was on it's way and would be there soon.

At 9:15 I called them back - still no bed.  They kept me on hold for almost 20 minutes.  The first girl I talked to said "it may be there in 10 minutes, we don't know - it might not come".  Obviously that answer was not sufficient after a 20 minute wait so i asked to talk to their "resolution desk".

He finally admitted that their delivery service is contracted out - the delivery company was closed, and the driver was not answering his cell phone.  the long and the short of it was that they did not know where my bed was, and had no way of knowing if it was still coming or not.

I was really upset with the events of the evening, so this morning (August 27) I called them again to find out what had happened.  They still had no answers for me.  I cancelled the delivery and the order and they refunded my Credit Card - but they refuse to credit the shopping service fee - because *I* chose not to accept the delivery?!?!?!

Most of my house is furnished by IKEA, but I'll be going to Sleep Country Canada tonight to find my new bed.

I never realized how much of an attraction the food was here until talking to my friends. I thought this was a home store. Well after visiting the first time, I realized why. The food is super affordable! Although everyone raves about the Swedish meatballs, I am not a fan of meatballs so I have never tried them. But there are plenty of options other than that for folks like myself.
 
They specials each day of the week including kids eat free on Tuesday and family night on Wednesday.

Ikea is the kind of place where you have to be skeptical about everything you buy. Some of their lower quality products will leave you regretting your purchase, so what I do is stress test everything before deciding whether or not to buy it. You know, see how flexible the pots and pans are, or put a little weight on the bookshelf to see if it will bend if I use it for its intended purpose i.e. books. On the other hand, they do have some quality products, which are not cheap, but still inexpensive compared to most other furniture stores.  Most of the furniture they offer has to be assembled. They do offer shipping through a third party company, but it seems expensive.

They have quality customer service here, and great amenities as well. There is a play place for children and a cafeteria with a few different dining style options. The food is pretty good, and very affordable. If you are planning to spend $150+ at the store, they will refund your lunch bill! Out front there is plenty of parking and dedicated spaces for loading up your vehicle! Very convenient if you hate walking your carts across the parking lot.

The service at this Ikea is the worst.  
Last time we went, all the Ikea family kiosks were down.   We tried one, it was broken, we asked a nearby associate what we should do to get our Ikea family card, and she said to go try a different kiosk.  We tried the next nearest kiosk, it was also not working, so we asked another employee, and they sent us to customer service.  We went to customer service and they told us to go try another kiosk.  "But we already tried a couple, and they're all down".  "Go try one upstairs".
I'll give you one guess as to whether or not the upstairs kiosk was working......

This is just one example of one time we've been to Ikea on Columbus, but it pretty well encompasses our customer service experience each time.

There two things that I like about Ikea: 1) is the place is full of ideas; and 2) you can get your walk in.  I think the zigzag pattern of the store really gets some men.  However, like most men they probably didn't pay attention to the signs (there are shortcuts).  

The ideas in the place abound there must be an entire staff that creates rooms for tight spaces like dorm rooms, small apartments and condos; along with space saving ideas.  That is the benefit of walking the entire store because from the beginning the displays are available.  A great deal of the time there is information on what the price for an entire display will cost.  So you can either mismatch and create your own or pick an idea and buy it.  Unfortunately, these items are all available to pick-up (self-service) in their warehouse.  Which means when you pick something out you need to identify the item number, aisle number, and bin number.  I use the note feature on my phone but they provide pencil and paper; along with measuring tape to assist in your shopping experience.  That is upstairs.  The downstairs is the same zigzag except you buy off the shelf and there is less displays.

One of the draw backs is you have to put the stuff together unless you use their assembly and installation options for an extra charge.  They also offer delivery and "do-it-yourself" trucks options on-site.  I did experience the "do-it-yourself" truck option once and decided the delivery option was better.  The price is comparable and you don't have to make the trip to purchase, drive the truck home, drop purchase off, return truck, and then finally go home.  The delivery option seems much simpler for not that much more.  The difference is with the delivery option there is schedule and you will most like not get your purchases home the same day.

Ikea offers something that used to be in a great deal of the large department stores in the United States. A cafeteria!  I know, I know, cafeteria food!  But if you get passed the "cafeteria food" part it really is not that bad.  Plus on different days Ikea will either offer something free or your receipt will be deducted from your store purchase.  I know I went on a Monday morning before the store was opened and the cafeteria was offering free coffee (I think that is always) and free breakfast.  Also, the normal prices are nominal.  The cafeteria is upstairs.  They also have a snack bar and small grocery section just after you get through the cash registers.

I think the only two downsides at Ikea is their long cash register lines and you have to put the items together.

I am dividing this review into 4 parts.

Furniture quality:  Hit or miss really. I've gotten some really solid pieces from here, and I've also gotten some things that have fallen apart.  Basically, you get what you pay for.  If a 6 foot tall cabinet is $20, it's probably not gonna make it through the year.  But, some of the more expensive stuff will.  Have some patience and read the directions when you're putting stuff together.  I actually consider myself quite a whiz with an all purpose ikea tool, but some may find it challenging. 

Variety of products: Awesome.  You can get anything from a toilet brush to a bookshelf to a full kitchen.  Anything you could possibly need for your house, you will find here.  

Restaurant:  LOVE me some ikea swedish meatballs and mashed potatoes.  Actually sometimes I crave them and have been to ikea solely for lunch/dinner.  The ease of the food line is great. Lots of options for cheap.  Only minus is that they have pepsi products.

Overall experience: Very very overwhelming.  I have finally figured out all the shortcuts, and can navigate through here pretty quickly when needed.  But, it's definitely not a "run in and grab something experience". The parking lot is almost always crowded.... and finding things can be challenging if you don't know where to look.  When you're there for something specific- pick up a map and follow the shortcuts.  Also a sneak tip: When you walk in, you can go past the escalator and straight into the marketplace through very non descript doors next to the lockers/kid drop off.  

All in all, I appreciate having an ikea nearby- but it's definitely a very stressful experience for me.  I often have to nap after a trip here- it's kind of like an amusement park.

Quick update - I sent IKEA an email on August 27 2013, outlining my displeasure with what had happened.  The website says that emails will be responded to within 48 hours.  It is now September 12th and I have not heard a thing.

I am sooooo addicted to this crazy maze store!  Right, Left, around the corner....you can go anywhere but you can't get out!  LOL, I just love it!  Well if you hate shopping I would advise you to stay as far away as possible but if you are like me you will come out with a new living room set, new friends and a full tummy!  They have really good Swedish meatballs in the cafeteria and a wide variety of food.  This store is a marketers paradise, I found things I never even knew I needed but purchased anyway!  Yup like I said a marketers paradise!  There are 2 levels, a kids play room, cafeteria and even a clearance section.  The only down side to this store was they only had 2 lines open to check out and it took me about 30 minutes to actually pay for my items.

Great place to shop looking for unique stuff but be careful when looking at buying things that they say they are on sale because when you get to the till you find out they are not and they will not discount  so you end up either buying it at the regular price or returning it

I like Ikea; it always give me ideas to what I want to do with my space, but never could because of a budget or just not needed. But one can dream? Ha. Anyway, this is the only Ikea near me and that I've been to and overall I had good experiences. Ikea is clean, organized and service was good. Although I must say that the parts to furniture are hard to assemble.

Damnit, I do like IKEA. Listen, its affordable furniture and housewares that actually look nice. It's not lifetime stuff, so don't plan on moving any of it with you if you move to a new place. A lot of the wood is terrible and will warp when it gets wet. The picture frame sizes are weird, but you can make it work. 

Things I really like buying from ikea: 
1. Blankets and duvet's. I know other who have them, and I just invested in some and am thoroughly impressed. The pillow cases that i got have button closures, or fabric closures. Score.  
2. Dish scrubbers. They have this one that has a suction on the bottom, and comes in fun colors. They are $1.
3. Fun paper plates, napkins, straws.
4. $1 soft serve frozen yogurt
5. kids stuff. Toys, dishes, etc. I even use the littlest stuffed toys as cat toys.

Things I have learned not to buy from IKEA:
1. Pots for plants. They do not have drainage holes.
2. Cardboard storage boxes
3. $7 end table (if you have been here, you know which one I am talking about)

I'll be the first to admit, most of our furniture is from IKEA, and it's not always about the price. IKEA has the beset solutions for small spaces, and we are in need of a lot of storage in  a relatively small area. Also,with a baby on the way, we needed somewhere we could get a nice looking, safe crib that didn't cost a million dollars. IKEA had just what we needed, and they also have a lot of really clever toy storage. Did I mention that I love storage? While we don't necessarily like going to the store (especially my husband), we always find what we came for and the staff is always helpful.
Ikea has really inexpensive food. Most is actually pretty good. Ikea is so big it's nice they provide very inexpensive food to eat during what some times seems like an all day shopping trip!

the furniture is of varying quality and sometimes can be a pain to put together. but for the price, u know what ur getting. its not stuff that u should expect to be able to move with you since it sometimes breaks when u pick itup and load into moving vans. but its more than adequate for my purposes. but really what i love about the place is their cafeteria. they have 99 cent breakfast sometimes and they always have a dinner/lunch special like 1.99 meatballs/nashed potatoes or 2.99 chicken fingers/fries. i sometimes just go there to eat and not to buy furniture. and im probably not the only one.

Please check everything before you buy something from this place!! I saw bed bugs on the pillow container, i loved this OFELIA BLAD white cushion, but when I was about to get it I noticed this little bug and I realize it was a BEDBUG.
I had bed bugs in the past and you don't want them believe me!! 
Also be careful with the mattresses and bed frame! 

I think they have good stuff, but I won't  risk getting this awful Bed Bugs

I just moved to philadelphia and didnt bring much furniture so the last weeks a have been purchasing almost an entire new home at IKEA, both at the warehouse and online. Most of the products have been working out great, for those who were not perfect or missing in the online delivery, new ones where sent by Fedex right away, their employees at their call center are really helpful and professional. I also had a sofa bought online I though was to hard. I took it to the warehouse and got money back so I could buy another sofa. When something is not working or you are not fully satisfied, the employees try to help you in all ways to fix it something I really appreciate. During the last weeks I have been in contact with at least six employees to get help with my purchases and they have all been very service minded.

IKEA is IKEA, so this review is mainly About their customer service. I was there a few times at their customer service desk. There were many people waiting and only ONE (then two) employees behind the counter. This means one of two things for me: employees don't take customer care too seriously ( several employees were walking by seeing this huge line and ignored us completely) OR the management is really poor and not attentive. Not happy.

It is always fun to shop at Ikea no matter where you live. The only problem with this Ikea is the location, it is inconveniently located and tricky to get to, I wish we could have one in another location so it will be less crowded and easier for people on the other side of town to get to.

IKEA.... Home Decorating Paradise. An Interior Decorator's Heaven. My favorite place to get lost and spend lots of money on things I don't need :p

When they finally built this IKEA in Ybor a few years ago, we were all very excited to check it out. While it is the closest one in the Tampa area (besides Orlando), it's not located extremely close to my house, so it's a bit of a production to come out here, but I still manage to make it 1-2 times per year. 

The store is a bit of a maze and you really can spend hours in here. They have everything from small home decor items, to bedding and bathroom accessories, kitchen appliances, all kinds of furniture and artwork to decorate the walls. It really is possible to furnish an entire home from the items found here. I also like all the space saving ideas and mock small apartment living scenarios they have set up to demonstrate different decorating and furniture placement ideas. The prices are all what I consider to be very reasonable for good quality items.

The service is usually pretty helpful and nearly anyone in the store can help you locate a special item. One of my favorite parts of IKEA is the delicious cafe that they offer for hungry shoppers who have worked up an appetite after a day of walking around this endless maze. The swedish meatballs are yum, yum good. Some of the other food I've tried has always been good too.

The only not so fun part is trying to get items out the door and into your car after your purchase if you buy something big like the 7 foot tall bookcase I got last year. Assembling the items yourself isn't too fun either. Besides that, this store is a really fun adventure to find everything you could need for your home decorating necessities all under one roof.

Although a great addition to Tampa bay, I hate coming here. Just like any other ikea, this is NOT an easy in, easy out process. Even if you know exactly what you came for, allow 20-30 minutes. 

People aimlessly wander the aisles oblivious to who is around them and act like they're in a trance. 

The checkout area is horrendous and takes way too long. 

Avoid at all cost unless you enjoy crowds and people ramming their carts into you.

Extremely disappointed with this location! I visited on Black Friday- with a healing csection infection and two small kids, after checking the stock on a item that was on sale with my ikea app for my iPhone. The app said there was 96 in stock. After driving all the way there I was informed by their rude associates that there was something wrong with the app and they sold out hours ago. I asked if there was anything they could do, again very rudely they told me there was nothing they could do. I contacted head office and despite the fact that it was their error they refuse to do anything for me. My house is mostly furnished with ikea products but I think I'll be avoiding shopping there from now on!!

Why oh why do they insist on making this place so maze-like, it seriously took me ten minutes to figure out how to get into the actual store with a cart! Also it is frustrating to navigate the store. The prices are pretty good though so it evens out.

I live close enough to it, and has become my go to spot for.. "stuff"
have a kids play area , and a restaurant. The food is Ok  - don't expect too much now.

I kind of like IKEA in general, but there's nothing commendable about this place.
the staff is helpful , and know where "stuff" is!

What is not to like about Ikea???  I like Ikea because if you need help, there is someone there to help you; however, there are no pushy salespeople trying to push anything on you.  I love that you can see, touch, test and try anything before you commit to the purchase.  Also, they make it super easy to find the items that you see on the showroom floor in the stockroom part .  

I have never had an issue with the checkout lanes.  If this will be your first visit; bring your own bags if you are buying small items as IKEA does not provide bags.  However , I recommend buying an Ikea bag as they are awesome!  I have one that I use all of the time because it can carry so much weight without tearing or breaking.  

I am also convinced that anyone can follow their assembly directions.  They are follow by picture; what is not to love???  And you do not need to have a tool kit to put it together.

I am an Ikea fan.  Just beware of the carts - all four wheels swivel for easy navigation!
I shop here at times for somethings for the house this place has nice reasonable items good place to shop!

Like any chain, when IKEA first came to Edmonton, it was quite shaky, wobbly and new on its feet. It made mistakes and was often unsure of itself. However, as it evolved, it grew more mature, confident and complex.

I've always found IKEA extremely easy to use. Between online, print and in-store denotations on materials, there is no shortage of indicators in which aisle and subsection a particular item is stored and to be found. Can't find it/moved? Ask a staff person. At first, the store was sparsely populated. On my most recent visits in the last 3 years, I've had no shortage of available and surprisingly friendly staff, not only willing - but ABLE!, to assist me in my endeavours. 

Also a very tasty, yet extremely frugal restaurant in each location?! A very large liquidation/clearance area for final sale items (largely cosmetic damage). Hell yes! IKEA is my go to gal for gems and it's semi-annual 50% off sale!!!

I am in love with IKEA. When we lived in CLE we drive a couple hours into PA just to go. Tons of cheap, but sturdy and modern furniture. We just went back today and got a ton of kitchen organizing stuff, two dressers and some other odds and ends for $300. Ridiculous. Go to the cafe to sign up for a family card. There are specials you can save extra cash on and you get free coffee and such. There is a cafeteria with so-so food if you need a mid-shopping snack. Also, this location has a kiddie play area where they will watch the little ones (potty trained) for free. My kids love it there. Get there early, it fills to capacity fast!

Formaldehyde City
If you want to fill your home with toxic cancer fumes imported from who knows where because it's "cheap", this is the place to go
I tried that route and gave it up. Got tired of putting things out on the curb once I looked at it the wrong way. And having learned how the chemicals in their stuff are the same that were in the FEMA trailers, never again. Just not worth it. A cool store just opened not far away from my home in Paoli(Bookcases Plus) that carries natural wood furniture for great prices. It's made in the USA, not in Asia.It seems more right paying for actual quality made in US than paying for what is mostly the costs to ship something of much lower quality 5000 miles.  I painted my book shelf with acrylic paint from Benjamin Moore and it looks fantastic. This was already assembled as furniture should be and my late dad always pointed out. No funny missing connectors. Painting it to match my wall was a much better use of time than assembling Ikea garbage, as I know this will last forever. Cost $176 for everything
Sitting for 2 hrs and still waiting for my kitchen. This sucks. Ikea needs to figure out a way for people to order online for pickup.

Yeah...a 5 star review for IKEA, well...this particular IKEA.

So why the 5 star review? Because this IKEA in Philly is ridiculously big and empty!! No line at the cafeteria! Have you ever seen the line at the IKEA in Hicksville, Long Island?? if you have, you'll know what I'm talking about. The people who work here are much more friendlier and helpful unlike the one I goto in Long Island and Brooklyn. 

There's not much more I could say other than their big ass parking lot, well displayed showrooms, huge cafeteria, and no lines. Also, their restroom is clean as hell too. We had a much better experience shopping here than the IKEA in Brooklyn and Long Island.

Verdict - Good to be in Philly.

IKEA is a great place to go when you have no time constraints. What I like about the store is that it's huge and so many choices. What I hate about it is that it's huge and so many choices!  Realize that most of the items are made of particle board. You get what you pay for.  So while it may look nice, it may need replacing sooner rather than later. I do like their bookcases but I hate that  you have to find which bin your item is in and try to lift heavy it and figure out if it will then fit in your car.  They do offer delivery at a starting cost of $59. After spending time looking for a bookcase I wanted, I get to the bin and it was empty!  I still prefer amazon for quick and easy shopping option but it is good to get out and walk around ikea once a year.

I was thrilled when this Ikea finally opened in Tampa - decent furniture at a decent price.  And it has lived up to that promise - I own several pieces of furniture bought from there that look great and have held up well.  

My major purchase last year was a big 3-piece PAX shelving unit.  It took 6 hours one Sunday to put it all together, but I loved that I would be able to adjust the interior shelving & accessories for years to come - or not?  Because when I went in today, every unit was marked down, and the piece pickup shelves were scavenged through.  Luckily, a worker helped me find one piece I wanted, but they were out of another, even though his handheld inventory computer said there were 8 units left.  Pretty disappointing.

I was also in the market today for desk legs.  Found some I liked, went to pick them off the shelf, and nope, no luck, didn't have them in any of the three colors.  Ikea - get your act together and track your inventory, sheesh!  Or at least remove an item from the showroom floor while they are out of stock.

So, all in all, not a very successful trip, although their delicious milk chocolate bars and awesome lemon ginger snaps managed to make me feel a little bit better. ;)

Final thought - today was the best checkout experience I have ever had there.  Only 2 registers open, but I was second in line and got through quickly and efficiently.   Normal experience is to wait in line about 10-15 minutes - which is why I visit here so infrequently in the first place.

While I despise putting together the furniture from Ikea, I do really like their designs, so time and time again I buy their stuff even though assembling it drives me to madness.

That being said, whenever I need a tchotchke for my house this it the first place I'll look. Cheap lamps, picture frames, mirrors, you name it. Their downstairs marketplace is where it's at! Though I admit I do spend too much money on junk, at least it's fun to do. 

I vastly prefer this one to the Conshohocken one. It's surprisingly usually less crowded. Also it honestly is more nicely laid out, and you can even see a rapidly rusting ship on the river from the cafeteria window. Food is alright, not gourmet but at least an experience. Their food market though has a lot of prepackaged interesting stuff. Those damn Swedes certainly know how to make pastries.

Time and time again I find myself here, and usually it's a pleasant experience. Just avoid the weekend crowds and you'll be golden. Sometimes I hate admitting I love Ikea.

I think this was one of the first (possibly THE first) IKEA to come to the Philly area, and it's massive. Just off 476, as in, it's obnoxiously close to the highway, so it's easy to find. 

Inside, it's the typical maze of half-English, half-Swedish signs and teeny tiny shortcuts.  Then you get to the furniture area, where it looks more like the lumber area of Home Depot than anything. Finally, you pay and escape back into the parking lot (or the underground garage) and breathe a sigh of relief.

The amount of product they have is staggering-- and there's a lot more than just furniture. There's kitchenware, bedding, stuffed animals, you name a furniture item at IKEA, and they're pretty much guaranteed to have four accompanying accessories for it.

Minus one star for the ridiculously intricate maze that ensures you see EVERY display, but four stars for cleanliness, stock, and amenities.
If I could, I would have given Ikea half a star!!! the furniture is CHEAP!!! Awful. They will never get my money again!!

I am disappointed with Ikea. I bought a bookcase from the store, got it home and went to assemble it but a piece was cracked. I called Ikea. They told me to bring the damaged piece back. I made a 60 mile round trip to Ikea in Tampa. When I got there they didn't have the piece to replace the damaged one. They told me I'd have to wait a month for more replacement parts to come in or just return the bookcase. That was on a Tuesday. I came back on Thursday with the bookcase like they said and I was told they can only returns on Monday through Wednesday. 
I checked on their website and it says nothing about specific days to return products. Nothing on the receipt either.      I am really disappointed in Ikea. They have lost my business. I can just as easily buy a bookcase at Walmart and have no problem returning it!!!

In IKEA, you do not pay for in-store or out-store workers and end up with lower cost with a good quality. You search, you find, you make, you pay less. And yes it is located in far south of the city, so it is not worth to travel from north to buy just a chair , and return to your home. You have to wait and go there to buy several items together.
Anyway, I really like the downstair coffee shop, very good to buy a drink and specially an ice cream to end your buying experience with one buck per item.... and don't forget to take some bars of chocolate, it is not the best, but you know you are paying 1$...

We just needed a few things but mainly went for dinner! They have some great food! Tonight we had the Swedish meatballs which are delicious! We also had some of their chocolate cake for dessert which was very good as well. It's a great idea to have cheap good food in a place like ikea where you can end up spending the whole day there!

I was in dire need of a dresser, so I came here. This location is enormous! Quite honestly, I could walk around here all day to look at all the fun stuff but for some reason there was a large amount of children here with their parents. I don't mix too well with kids, as in, I don't like them. And there were a lot of screaming children. I can only assume it's because they have a play area (?) downstairs for them. 

I didn't eat all day and was starving so we stopped by the restaurant to grab a bite. I got the chicken fingers and veggies since I didn't think you could really mess them up. I was wrong. The food was atrocious. The chicken was super processed and chewy (EWEWEW). The steamed veggies were weird, too. The carrots didn't taste like carrots. It was strange. I actually dipped my veggies in BBQ sauce and honey mustard so they weren't so gross. And that, in itself, is pretty gross.

I'm giving this place three stars for the furniture. I don't mind the process of pulling your own furniture parts, since that's just the way it's done here. I'm happy with my dresser! It's cute and was pretty inexpensive. I just really, really do not recommend getting food here. Please don't do it.

The Conshohocken IKEA probably will always be my favorite since it was the IKEA that took my IKEA virginity. hahaha. I just the atmosphere in here while browsing this " furniture museum." By the way great stress reliever walking through here when it is less busy.

Ikea is what it is, a factory warehouse full of a bunch of cheap and inexpensive products.  I get overwhelmed every time I walk in there, so I'm not sure why I do.  I want to find good things when I stop in, but I always end up leaving especially when I see their lines to the back of the store.  Sure, if you want to buy some inexpensive furniture made out of particleboard and other fake wood materials, this is the place to go.  Just don't expect it to last a long time.

Uuuuuuugh I love this place so much (Yes, that was pain in my voice). My Ikea addiction started in Chicago and has migrated back to Florida with me. Their furniture just makes sense. And if you are the least handy of your friends, it STILL can't possibly take you more than half an hour to put together a piece of well made, minimal, STURDY furniture. I have yet to actually/accidentally destroy something from Ikea. And I am clumsy-ish. 

That being said, this particular visit was for a new 'desk.' I am an illustrator and freelance artist, so space and clean lines are important. So is storage. I have come across many a 'desk' that claims to fill my needs. And thank GOD i didn't fall for Overstock.coms shenannigans when they promised me a writing desk for $250, because what I put together for myself for $165 was leagues better. That is another thing I love about Ikea. With a little know-how, everything fits. A table top on  shelf. Some legs prop up that shelving unit. 

My 'desk' turned in to a standing 'Ikea-hack' work station that makes my 18-year old self jealous of me. 

I will ALWAYS look to Ikea first.

It's a real fun store to be in and they have everything you can think of and the food is not too bad either. 

A lot of the products are made in China but the prices are great. I really couldn't compared to Walmart as Fars the quality and because the products are made in China but I do think the design of IKEA is great!

I wish the IKEA store and the cafeteria could be rated separately. I found the actual store to be nice and enjoyed walking through the showrooms and trying out the beds. I even bought two nice picture frames. I'll give it four stars.

The cafeteria on the other hand sucked big time. The food was cheap but didn't look that good. I should've gotten the pre-made  Tuscan turkey sandwich like I planned originally after I got a glimpse of the hot food. But no, I wanted  to give the food a chance and it all ended up being a waste. I asked for the salmon lasagna and the girl just slapped it on my plate to the point the lasagna fell apart. There was even waxed paper stuck to the bottom of it.

IKEA is a nice store but the cafeteria isn't that great and the food is dried out. Take a tip from me: if you're truly hungry, stick to the sandwiches.

Next time you are at Ikea, eat lunch at eyeball level with the SS United States. The dining area at the front is a unique space flooded with natural daylight and with a panoramic view. I had a salmon wrap with crunchy cucumber bits. It was not half- bad!

On my recent trip to IKEA in Tampa I was extremely upset with the lack of customer service and the sheer unhelpfulness of their staff. I understand that to have such low prices on their goods the staff are not expected to provide concierge service, however, the fact that I could not even ask for help and was talked at not to, shows they care not at all for their potential future customers. I called the day before I made my purchases to confirm that there would be delivery available that same week, as the furniture was part of my spring break improvement project. When I reached the home delivery service desk they informed me that they could not deliver until next week even though the previous day the spokesperson on the phone said they had same or next day deliveries on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays. I asked if I could return myself tomorrow to pick up the merchandise since they could not deliver for a week. "No" cannot do that either. I would need to have someone to help me load the items into the truck anyway, since that is also not something any of the dozens of people wearing IKEA shirts and talking amongst themselves appear to do. Actually, I am not sure why there is staff at IKEA? There were two registers open, at the furthest possible location away from the exit and the area where you have to drop the items off for home delivery. When I was contacted by a customer service representative their sole consolation was to give me a gift card to their food court, which I can assure you I will most definitely not be visiting again. Were it not for the fact that I invested 5 hours of my time, $2000, and had a new bedroom all picked out for my daughter I would have returned my entire purchase and taken my business somewhere more reliable. That was my first and last visit to IKEA
If you ever wanna do something really nuts get stoned and go to ikea is all I'm saying

Humongous store filled with lots of cheap stuff.  Furniture is very trendy looking, but very cheap quality.  Lots of furniture, storage, bathroom, and kitchen items.  Perfect for items for a college dorm or first apartment.  You have to put everything together yourself.  Some great pictures and artwork and very reasonable prices.

I love this store!  They have such neat items!  Easy to find!  The restaurant is very clean and the Swedish meatballs are delicious!  Try the Linderberry soda!!  It is really good and the meals are very affordable!

Overwhelmed first Ikea visitor. Forgot to give our food receipt at checkout for refund. Crazy busy on a Sunday and the manager and cashier went out of their way to get us our 20$ back without having to wait in more lines. They were so sweet and patient. We will def be back! Love ikea!

Jana (Yana) helped me out yesterday with all my shopping since I had a list of large items. She did helped me with finding all the items, getting everything on an organized list, and even arranging my delivery times this week! She was so helpful and personable and helped me get exactly what I was looking for! Thanks Jana!

Pretty good option for your furniture needs, as you'd expect.

Pros:
Shorter lines than Atlanta's IKEA
Great prices
Good cafe/restaurant upstairs with quick service

Cons:
Lines still freakin' long
Staff is helpful and friendly but seems unavailable (almost avoid you)

Ikea a great place for the whole family! We come her because it's a great place to go, shop with the wife and best of all "infant friendly". It's getting harder to find a place to eat without my 2 year old freaking out after 15 minutes sitting down. IKEA has just enough running around and quick cafeteria to get him good to go! The food is different and comfort food all mixed up in cafeteria line form! Smoked Salmon with dill mustard sauce is amazing! The half rack of ribs for only $7.99, extra Swedish meat balls for only $.99, and the amazing lingonberry juice to wash it down! My infant son ate all of his Mac and cheese, which is great! And my wife enjoyed her salmon lasagna, which I tasted and it was generously stuffed with salmon. I was looking forward to their apple pie but they were out, that's ok because the tiramisu was amazing! All and all we all enjoyed what we got! Going on a weekday is a lot less stressful than the weekends! The little guy got to run around and enjoy all the neat kooky stuff Ikea has to show! Staff was very courteous and friendly!

Is there really anything left to say about IKEA that hasn't been said? No, not really. This specific store has been well-organized and staffed every time I've been, but I really hate the parking lot layout. I feel like it's a bit of a mess half the time. The bathrooms were clean, the food always seemed fresh, and there's honestly not much you can complain about (unless you happen to have a king size bed and nothing they sell fits it).

I am solely using this review to air a few grievances, but in reality I love ikea! 

So this is the flagship store in the USA! Why they picked Conshohocken for this honor, I'll never know! It is huge, as in deserves its own zip code, huge! There is no such thing as a "Quick trip" to IKEA. I try to go on the weekdays because there is never a line both in returns and at checkout! 

Ikea pioneered the BYOB, Bring Your Own Bag thing and it is a bloody nuisance! Ever try to buy a few candles, a picture frame, and a new set of coffee mug only to get stuck having to spend 99 cents on a blue bag that's large enough to park a Volkswagen in? It sucks!

Also, why can I not take my cart to my car? People are nice enough not to steal your stuff if you leave it unattended in the loading zone. When I shop alone I try to leave my things near the mother with the screaming child who was not ready to leave småland - no ones going to approach them anyway!Honestly though, why does furniture shopping require a buddy system?! 

And if the no bags, bring a friend thing wasn't frustrating enough now you have to go build your furniture with a wordless instruction manual! If you have ever put ikea furniture together and used all of the bits and pieces please become my friend - I would like to pick your brain over a plate of Swedish meatballs and Lingonberry jam.

Actually the food is surprisingly good, especially the meatballs - I usually buy a bag to go!

Staff is super helpful, thanks to the guys in the customer service in helping me assemble that pesky drawer! About the rest is Ikea what else do you expect in regards to the quality and how pack could be! Well at least this place does not get as pack as the one in Elizabeth, NJ.

I'm sorry but I'm just not a fan of cheap furniture made of chemically treated particle board. Don't get me wrong. I understand the appeal, especially when you throw in a few swedish meatballs. But, it's just not for me.

Good looking furniture and accessories for cheap. Got to love this place. I prefer the European contemporary style furniture and Ikea is the place to go if you don't want to spend a bomb. And while you are there, don't miss their meatballs, cinnamon buns and frozen yogurt.

When a toddler and kindergartener BEG to go to a store, they must be doing something right for the whole family.  Adults can wander the maze at their leisure while  the kidlets are being entertained in the "ball room" - where they can play in the balls, watch kid movies on large screens, do crafts, and make new temporary friends.   They are carefully checked in and parents are given a pager in case they are needed for any reason.  Great peace of mind and happy kids, what more could you ask for while you shop?

There's a kid-friendly cafeteria upstairs, complete with a small play area.  I'm not personally a fan of the food, but it's inexpensive and others in the family seem to enjoy it.

Shopping itself is good if you're the right customer - you need to be willing to spend time comparing items, find the boxes in the warehouse, haul it home and then assemble it.  If that describes you, then you'll love the prices and experience.
