There are sample "rooms" throughout the store with beautiful displays - the kitchens are stunning and I'm willing to move into one there any time they'd let me  :-)    I am also always impressed by their "small spaces" rooms - anyone just starting out in a small apt would get fabulously inspired ideas.

All in all, every city needs a store like Ikea.  It's not for everyone, but it's the perfect solution for many and offers something not elsewhere available.  Thumbs up!

Just your standard IKEA. If you've been to any, this one is set up pretty much the same. Certain days there are more customers than others but I have found that I can usually get a spot in the loading area without a problem.

I recommend stopping for a bite to eat at the IKEA cafe. The food is delectable.

This was my first time to Ikea and I was most defiantly overwhelmed with the store. I had heard from many of my friends how extraordinary Ikea was, but I have seen some of the furnishings that my daughter had bought from there and I was unimpressed. This being said I was strongly encouraged to go. 
Upon my arrival I was greeted by a very nice young lady and she somewhat explained where I should start my shopping venture, however she failed to mention exactly how I was to go about shopping. The system of how things were laid out in the showrooms was a bit confusing. There was a plethora of little items in each display that did not necessarily belong to that department. This made it somewhat difficult to locate the home of the item I wanted to purchase. Alas I was save by another very courteous employee from the work spaces area that took the time to calm me and explain in great detail how the system worked for finding what I needed. Once I had solid information on how to locate small items I was able to set out on a shopping adventure of a lifetime.
The shopping commenced and it was a wonderful fun filled time. I will be returning to shop another day at Ikea.

Ah... I don't think a girl will ever forget her first IKEA. This place is truly magical. I walk in for one thing and come out with a thousand. It's so big and beautiful. Make sure you check out their "as-is" room by the register. Sometimes they have a lot of great stuff!

I don't care what anyone says, I love IKEA. 

I know the store can be stupid busy (particularly on evening, weekends, and during holidays - try coming on a weekday morning if you can). I know the store is huge and can get you lost and confused if you've never been there before (they're also renovating, so that just makes it more confusing). I also know that their furniture isn't the most long lasting furniture and trying to assemble it with those diagram instructions and an Alan key is like trying to solve a complex algebra equation while you're blindfolded and drunk.

Still I love Ikea. I love wandering around at the display models and sitting on the chars with my friends. I also love how all the books in the display model living rooms and bedrooms are in Swedish. I love the fact I was able to pick up a travel pillow, some packing bags, and a reusable shopping bag (best travel investment I've ever made) for $7 last time I was there. Ikea now has a free membership program and there are computer kiosks upstairs where you can register and get a membership card. I love that I can pick up furniture, art frames, candles, desk lamps, kitchenware and almost anything you might need for a home/office at a reasonable price. No the products, mainly the furniture, won't last 50 years, but I have a 13 year old poang chair and it's doing fine. I also love going upstairs to the cafe and getting a Daim torte and some lingonberry juice.

I used to live close to Ikea and would go there often. I don't visit Ikea as much, and I usually try to go when it's not as busy, but when I do go to Ikea I always enjoy the experience.
When I go to Tampa/St. Pete, I make sure I stop at Ikea. This is the best store. Loads of great ideas and even more great items. I never leave here empty handed.

"We just throw in extra parts to screw with you." - Ikea.  I'm not sure that Ikea needs or deserves a review.  You either like Ikea or you hate it or you hate assembling it. 

Tip: Check in on foursquare and get a discount.

Prices are great, place is absolutely huge.  Only encountered a few employees. One gentleman we asked for help was very friendly and was a great help to us. Passed eight or nine other employees that didn't bother to even say hello. If it weren't for that nice gentleman that helped us I'd say don't go there for the service. I love ikea but this isn't one of their strong points. Selection and ideas are everywhere and the place is enormous! Everything from brand new kitchens to candles and cooking utensils and curtains.

I love IKEA, but not fan of their maze exit. Anyway Coffee it's always free!! Can't miss the day of you eat free, when you are planning to spend chunk of money at this store, make sure you check the eat free date.

What's not to like about IKEA. If there was ever a complaint it'd be the fact sometimes they can go overboard with their pricing, though for the most part they are rather reasonable. I don't like the life span of their furniture either, like anything else you really want to take extra care of the stuff you buy here cause at the end of the day you're paying for the look more than the authenticity.  Having said that, IKEA is still one of my favorite places to shop. They just seem to have it together, the entire inventory at IKEA is terrific, they have a great return policy with very little if any hassle at all. The food court is another bonus, the food is nothing to brag about, but it's always consistent and well priced, at times you'll can even get free stuff for the kids or a 99 cent breakfast. There's also a kid care area known as Smaland, they will watch your kids at no cost for a few hours while you shop (who else does that?). The layout of the store is among one of the best around, they have a clever way of allowing you to see how certain items will look inside your home. You will find practically everything sold in the store from inside the bathrooms to the food court. IKEA is highly recommended, especially for those living on a budget and small spaces, there's stuff here that'll jazz up your place. So, for those that have never been to IKEA, you need to get to out here now so people wont laugh at you... seriously, don't fool yourself. We're fortunate to have one here Tampa Bay.

It's always busy, and to be honest you can find better looking furnature for more reasonable prices elsewhere.

I get why they have the layout like they do - so you have to walk through everywhere to get to where you want, but it's also a pain when you only need one or two little things (like picture frames).

Ikea is one of my guilty pleasures. 

Of course I don't like the furniture, and of course I don't like the food, but it reminds me of being young, and without means.  I like taking Lady Mary there for a stroll, so we can reminisce about love's keen sting. Fortunately for Lady Mary, I have excellent taste; but if I could only afford Ikea, she would love me anyway.  I have therefore, made an irreparable connection between Ikea and love's innocence. So...although I have no desire to assemble my furniture with an allen wrench, or fit all my furniture in a closet, I do like Ikea.

My little sister and I ate at the ikea cafeteria. Though I'm usually not a fan of freezer foods, which is what I think the food from ikea is prepared from, I was pleasantly surprised by their salmon lasagna and meatball dish. The salmon pieces in the lasagna tasted delicious and the meatballs were yummy. I like the fact that their elderflower and ligon berry juices were organic. For dessert we hade the tiramisu which was really sweet but I enjoyed the princess cake which was made with marzipan.
Love ikea. Cheap stuff that's just as nice as anywhere, as long as you don't mind assembling things yourself. My daughter also loves the play place. Cafeteria is a little dirty though.

Wow...people working there behind the kitchen are miserable.  Trays were nasty had ketchup stains on some and grunge.  Serving staff couldn't be bothered.  No Swedish meatballs and they didn't care to put out more.  Not prepared at all!  We walked out.

Plan to make a day of it if this is your first time going to an IKEA store.  This is not just a store, it's really more like a lifestyle art statement piece.  The place is MONGO HUGE with concrete floors and there is no short path to the exit (or the restrooms!) so wear COMFORTABLE shoes and limit liquids 2 hours before going, especially if you are over 40!  I was hobbling on our way out the first time...the next time we went I knew better and wore my walking tennies.  

The cafeteria-style cafe is a fun stop with interesting IKEA Food like salmon, Swedish meatballs, and lingonberry sauce.  Cute.  The food is tasty and actually pretty reasonable.  

Staff for the most part is friendly although once we got downstairs to the stock room it was harder to find help.  Our first-ever IKEA purchase was a daybed which was displayed with a mattress that unfortunately was no longer available so that was disappointing. We had even had a staff member verify stock numbers and give us a printout - but this apparently has nothing to do with actual inventory so just beware that even a printout is no guarantee that the item you have selected will be available.  At this point though we had company coming and had to get a guest bed in place so we purchased the "similiar" version.  Unfortunately there was no way to test it there in the check out area so we had to just hope for the best.  Uh, no -- we have found it definitely is not even close to as comfortable as the discontinued/displayed version.   We always give our bed to our guests and take the guest bed ourselves anyway, so thankfully we were the ones who were miserable that week and not our guest.  The daybed itself however assembled nicely and looks/feels solid.  We haven't used it much, but we are pleased so far with how it looks and how its holding up.

There are kids and family oriented activities here too, such as a sort of play room area and things like Easter Bunny visits, holiday buffets and events, etc.  We don't have little ones so can't comment there but seems like cool stuff.

I'd like to see more restrooms - it was a huge trek back to the restrooms throughout the day, especially with sore feet and an over-40 bladder.  But other than that it's a fun place to experience all that IKEA has to offer.
Try to avoid the weekend rush but otherwise better layout than Conshy store. Bonus for the cafeteria & 50 cent froyo & hot dogs

A good place to lose an afternoon. The food is pretty good if you want to eat there before shopping (brilliant money maker on their end). I never asked anyone for help because I didn't need it. I had to return something once and I was a little put off because the women working the return counter was sweet as pie to the people ahead of me, but she was very short with me.

Honestly, I just really loved the smoked salmon that was $7.99 for 7 oz. I usually pay $6.99 for 4 oz. 
I came here for plastic storage bins. They were $6.99 with the lid. Although I am unhappy with the fact that the lids do not click or lock, they will do. The only reason I bought them because I end up taping bins anyway. 
I also bought my trusty Tupperware set for $3.99 for a bunch of pieces. I bought this set and swear by it because of the variety of sizes. I make sauces a lot so I like that fact that there are smaller containers. However MR IKEA, can you please start selling them in a color other than green?!

What's not to like about IKEA? 

It's not fancy-pants furniture, but for shelves and bookcases, I love it. I've bought bookshelves for my office, my living room and my bathroom. I've bought pantry shelves for my kitchen. And it's served us very well. It's a maze of a store to venture through, so sometimes I get disappointed when I can't just walk in and go directly to what I need, but they really do make it a shopping 'experience' rather than a shopping 'trip'. 

On our most recent trip we were looking for additional storage for our kitchen. While I went in with a plan to look at one piece, I actually found a less expensive shelf that offers a nice pop of color to the room. IKEA keeps me on my toes. And it let's my not-extremely-handy husband feel like he can rule the world.

I love Ikea because you can grab some really cool ideas for an interior and they sell everything in a one stop shop. Now, I'm not vouching for quality - because I'll tell you some of my finds have been nothing short of college furniture quality.  Although sometimes you can find some really cool things. Most things have the Swedish flare, which makes them extra cool. 

They have a really great food court. It's huge, lots of room for the little ones and pretty decent food. If you can go on a Tuesday, you can get a really cheap kiddo meal for the little ones.  They have great soft serve ice cream too.  Hey it's a one stop shop!

Ikea is middle of the road for me. 

Pros: Great return policy, food in store is always a plus, some of the products are truly built to last if you pick the right things, staff are friendly, and a huge selection for your entire home. I have a dinnerware set and some cooking utensils as well as bookshelves that are still in great shape. 

Con: Some items are cheaply made and overpriced. You have to watch what you purchase. Quality of certain items is a major con for me. 

Overall, it's a great place to shop for items you need for your home, but pay close attention to certain items like furniture before you decide to buy. The upside is you could probably return it anyway.
Swedish meatballs are horrible you possible could not eat good tasting food if you like these.. I love ikea but REally???

We love Ikea for all the same reasons everyone else does. Be inspired to decorate any room in your home. Find perfect items that you must have. Or just enjoy the Swedish meatballs, eclectic desserts or frozen yogurt on the cheap. Oh, we grabbed a tray of 6 cinnamon buns for $4- so happy we did because they were pretty darn good as a late night snack hanging with my family.

What's to say about IKEA that hasn't already been pontificated upon?  The showroom is outlandishly slick, the furniture hilariously terrible (as I type this on my Fyorntig desk and look at textbooks on my Kvarshlok bookshelf) with the worst assembly instructions ever, but their cheap, modern look meshes with my decor, so I love these Swedes.  

Even if you're not going to buy anything, just looking and enjoying the bedlam is reason enough to go here.  Plus, the cafe is dirt-cheap with lunch for two coming in under $15.  Not enough cheap food for ya?  After the registers, get some cinnamon buns, 6 for $4.  And a hot dog for the road.  And a slice of pizza.  And a Barfslamp.

Ok who doesnt like Ikea! I furnished my new apartment with all things ikea, its so affordable and chic its crazy! I now have a white fabric couch and wont be too upset if anything happens to it since it was such a good price and the covers are washable!
They have a flat $99 for delivering (straight into whatever room you want) which is really good if you buy multiple big pieces all at once.
For the smaller stuff I just went in the store and drove them back home.
Their wooden cubes for storage is amazing and so versatile! As is basically everything else.. ok I just love this place!

It's an IKEA, it is what any IKEA is anywhere in the world. That's either creepy or comforting.

This review is specifically for my experience at returns yesterday. I had ordered shelves from the website, then decided I didn't like them, & that I wanted other shelves instead. I had no paper receipt, just an email on my phone. I was nervous.

Needlessly nervous, apparently. Easy peasy to return, & she made sure to indicate that I live in Philadelphia to be certain that I got ALL of my tax monies refunded to me as well. Walked away with a giftcard, easily found the shelves I wanted instead, paid with said giftcard, & was out the door quickly. That's my kind of shopping experience!

JUNK furniture! Never seen so many "sheeple" in one spot spending their non-union, minimum wage earned dollars lol.

I'd rather throw my money out the window and get a dirty used couch from salvation army than to buy from here again. 
THEY WILL NEVER GET ANOTHER PENNY FROM ME!!!!

Too crowded on the weekends. Parking sucks. Food is ok if you can stand watching the kid in front of you pick his nose while his mum is grabbing another piece of cake from the case. Get in line sheeple.

I really don't like ikea. I avoided the store in Chicago while living there  and when I moved to Philadelphia I wasn't able to bring all my furniture so  I decided to  fill in the missing items by get them here. Needless to say I will not be shopping here again.  The employees are rude and mad at the world. I had purchased a large mirror and it didn't fit in my car so I had it delivered, along with the other items I purchased. I was given a delivery time between 12pm-4pm. The driver didn't show up until 5:30pm. I only found out they were going to be late after I called. A courtesy call would have been appreciated.

I bought all new office furniture parts missing...actual furniture missing too...don't try to call customer service unless you have almost an entire day to be on hold over and over again. Although the merchandise looks good the level of anxiety and frustration dealing with the employes reduced the value to ZERO! Delivery was also a disaster since they use urban express, third party, you are stuck royally when they dint show up......not good for anyone that has a life past ikea!

While IKEA's furniture is price point savvy and highly functional, they are way behind in using technology to 1) provide inventory as one shops and 2) proper staffing. Check out lines are always long both midweek and weekend, staff is rarely visible in the showrooms, service booths overwhelmed , and the return/ exchange counter understaffed.  Personally I had to go through 3 layers of bureaucracy to prove I left a purchased item at the checkout counter! They need to "check "their video footage and miraculously the third viewing showed that i did in fact leave the purchased item, the cashier failed to log the abandoned item, and IKEA dragged the ordeal out.  So much for Scandinavian efficiency! This was the Philly store. I've had better luck in LA.

If you are thinking of purchasing a quartz countertop from this store, don't.  I recently did just that, and the end result is a shoddy install for which I am currently looking for ways to remedy.  I've tried contacting both IKEA and the contractor they sent to resolve the issue,  in the end they threw a disclaimer in my face, as if a disclaimer somehow excuses incompetence.  You'd think that being a big company that cares about providing quality products, IKEA would screen contractors and only work with those who meet certain standards.  I thought that too, that's why I chose to purchase my quartz countertop at IKEA.  It was not cheap and it wasn't the lowest price I found, but I trusted the IKEA name.  I was wrong.  I am now paying for that misplaced trust,  I have to look at the shoddy work everyday.

I think its unfair to have to assign STARS to IKEA because the experience is never bad.
AND, the experience is never great.
The experience is just IKEA.

Sometimes the place can be overly annoying because of the "trapped rat" feeling of never being able to exit quickly.
Sometimes I know where something is and want to run in and grab it. I am like a trained soldier in that I can arrive at the spot I want to and I find a short way down to the checkout only to find I was wrong and I now have to do the entire exit circuit . LOL

Other times I exit quickly and the lines are enormously long and I have only one item. Why don't they have express lines?

With that said... I have a 21 year old and there is no better place to purchase hip, inexpensive things for her shared apartment. I just paid .69 for coffee cups she loves. Also, cheap curtains.  

I will say I prefer this location over the newer one in South Philly so yes I am a fan.

To bitch directly at Ikea and avoid the 800 number: Call Direct Line 215-551-4532. I hit 1111 then 0 to get to a human receptionist. Also try extensions 1452 or 1930 to get a live person. I'm pretty pissed off at Ikea right now. Hopefully this will help you avoid getting any more pissed off by trying to call the 888 number on the website.

Ikea, the mysterious draw that has people lining up before the doors open and winding their way through the maze of showrooms.  The products are smart,  and the prices are affordable,  so anyone with an appreciation for organization will feel at home here. The quality is okay,  but the selection is hard to beat.  Luckily,  I've been able to control myself in this store and the most I've spent in one trip is $30, but in my mind I've reorganized my whole home,  including the kitchen sinks! Great place to kill an afternoon,  but not a good place to try to run in and grab something.  It's set up like a rat maze in that they pretty much force you to meander through most of their store in order to get to the finish line,  which is annoyingly a long checkout line. Food is okay, but not appealing in a cafeteria type setting.
Ever tried getting through to customer service here and getting disconnected 3 times in a row? and there is no backup phone number to try, you are just high and dry.

It's IKEA - there's not a whole lot to say.  Tons of stuff, relatively cheap, yada yada.  Main complaint - the lines for checkout.  Seriously, 35+ lanes available, Saturday evening - they have 7 lanes open, each about 25 shoppers deep.  Has happened multiple times.  I have considered walking out and just leaving my cart full of items sitting there but the hubs is a good line vulture and manages to swoop in quickly when they finally open another aisle. So aggravating.

Love ikea! There are no words! Great quality, totally fun store. Functional products, low prices. I absoultely love thier plant section! They have great houseplants for crazy prices! You wont find plants like this at Lowes or Home Depot ! They have a cafe and snackbar with some amazing treats! The cinny buns are fantastic, chewy and divine! You will be pleased! Get there early... Place gets packed!!  This location does especially!

Amazing first experience! It's like a giant museum. Nice show rooms that displays everything from bedrooms to kitchens set up. It's neat seeing how things can be set up, and you can buy everything that you like. It's like jumping in a catalog. They have everything you'll ever need in any household but for a very reasonable price. No need for waiting and delivery. You can just mark what you like on your list and go to their stock room and pick it up yourself. They even have a cafeteria! Lol Definitely a must try if you're moving!

Ikea is like a trip to the dentist. It's never pleasant, but sometimes necessary. I'm not trying to hide it, not a fan of ikea furniture in general. I think their designs are boring, it takes too long to put together, it can be so packed on a weekend that it can make a Walmart seem like an open space and the payment line ups are so long you have to brace yourself before waiting to pay. However, they are cheap and relatively basic. So occasionally I find myself here, although admittedly more than I would like to.  

A nightstand and a tv stand were my recent purchases. The night stand had a number of naughts in the wood which made drilling the screws in a challenge. In one case I had to fight so hard to put the screw in, it cracked the wood. Should I return it and spend more time and money dealing with this? I choose not to, because it is still functional. The tv stand was easy to put together. Very basic, but I did swear a lot putting it together.

I know this is probably obvious, but this Ikea is much better than the South Philly location. It's cleaner, seems slightly bigger, and isn't located in a crappy place. 

Plus they have the standard mac and cheese and meatballs, so they're A-OK in my book!

Don't forget your reusable bags...

I love IKEA. It's great for a young professional who is living in rentals and also good for new home buyers. If you have some assembly skills, then you will love this place. I like to stop by the returns section first. If you but something from Ikea and take it back because it didn't look right in your space or didn't fit, this is where it will all go. In addition, when the Ikea staff switch out store displays, the product gets sold for nearly half price in the returns area. I gave them 3 stars because the ATM/debit/visa machine's are crap! You don't always have the option to pay with the card that you want and it has nothing to do with your spending habits(maxing out cards or going over limit on a bank account), there is just something plane weird with their machines. If you ask to go to another cashier, you might as we'll ask to be knived by the Ikea staff because they will glare at you like a high class criminal! I highly suggest that the store manager give some proper training to their staff on why they should apologize when the debit/credit machine craps out on the customer and politely walk them to the front of the next line to be rang up. I spend over $800 a year at IKEA and deserve to be treated with respect!

I found it completely frustrating that Ikea demands that you enter their store to speak with someone about scheduling a kitchen measurement and design.

I don't understand why this has to be done in person. I've seen the cabinets, I want the cabinets, why does this have to be a production?

I live far outside Philadelphia. So in order for me to SCHEDULE a measurement and design session, I have to travel 3 hours to the location???

IKEA. If you've never been, you sure won't understand what all the hype is about. Once you go, you'll always want to go back! 

My first trip to IKEA was when I was in the 9th grade, many years ago. I begged my mom to buy my a comforter cover and it was the best thing I ever did. 15 years later I still have that cover and I'm still in love with it! It's basically like a sleeping bag for your comforter, who wouldn't love that! 

Let's list the awesome things this place offers:

-Huge carts
-Under building parking (who likes to get wet when it rains, let alone have to pack up the car in it?!)
-It's next to Cracker Barrel (if you're into that kinda thing)
-They have a resturant inside. Up you read that right.
-They have a grocery store, which has the BEST swedish chocolate chip cookies
-They have set ups of all the rooms in a house you could ever think of! 
-They have everything that you could ever use, need, want or think of and then some!
-Their stuff is dirt cheap. Like, I'm living paycheck to paycheck, but still leave here with a car filled with goodies
-They sell their gigantic reusable bags for cheap
-I LOVE their gigantic reusable bags that are cheap
-They offer a drop off for your kids so you can shop in peace
-They offer a drop off for your kids so I can shop in peace

Cons:
-The directions are pictures of weird naked men putting your product together. 

I think we're done here, go check out this awesome place for yourself!

Easy signage from Ridge Pike.  Spacious, clean, most all of the staff were helpful, friendly, and welcoming [read: not the checkout individual], huge parking lot, easy pull up and load, easy to find the items, easy to shop.  Individual snack and meal cafes.

A bit confusing to maneuver around.  But a quality IKEA, as they go.

Why is it always so difficult to find help in this store? 

I shop here on average 4-6 times a year. Usually for random household needs but it's a great place to shop for last minute gifts. Their new section of household goods is great. I got a rain poncho for under $10 and it is fantastic! 

The layout of this location is great. I love browsing the showroom before heading to the warehouse to pick up my goods. Stopping halfway to have lunch at a very affordable price! Dropping the kids off in the play area is a great way to get shopping done without having to chase around the wee ones. 

What's frustrates me is how difficult it is to find staff when you need something. 

In the payment area there are TONNES of staff to help you, but throughout the store it seems like a difficult task.

My rating does not reflect my experience in the store, instead the rating is about how safe I felt visiting the store. I'm sure many visit without incident, but it's a risk. Please read on....

The IKEA store is great, however in my opinion, your vehicle is not safe in the parking lot. My vehicle was broken into in the parking, vehicle damaged, and items stolen from the vehicle.  I'm sharing this concern with others since the very same day, multiple vehicles were vandalized in the IKEA parking lot in broad daylight. I learned vehicles are vandalized in the IKEA parking lot too often to consider this location safe.  

I suggested hiring a third party security company to drive around and monitor the IKEA parking lot to improve safety for customers. It's a small price for a retailer to pay to improve parking lot safety for customers, especially in areas with this type of negative activity.

I will not go back to this particular IKEA store until such changes are implemented, due to the high risk my vehicles will be vandalized in the parking lot.

Best of luck if you park your vehicle in the lot to shop at this store.  It was an expensive visit if you factor the lost items and cost of repairs.

Always great deals to be had here at Ikea. I like their food too. You will need at least 3 hours to get through the entire store. It is like a maze but is well worth it. Check this place out next time your in the area.

ProTip: go on a weekday afternoon. The weekends, particularly Saturday, are absolute madhouses but you practically have the place to yourself at 3pm on a Tuesday. 

The LED bulbs to replace coils and tiny halogen bulbs cost half of what they do at Lowe's and Home Depot. I swear nearly half the stuff in our house is from here. Cabinets, plates, shelving, chairs, decor, outdoor lanterns for candles, hell...PASTA!! Frozen meatballs, smoked salmon, and envelopes of cream sauce!

I eat dinner here several times a month because I like their salmon, veggie medallions, saithe fish, 130 calorie froyo cones, and the Swedish fish candy are a steal at $1.69 a bag! Seriously...I cannot make myself a salmon dinner for under $8. 

GREAT storage solutions, LOVE the money I save by assembling stuff myself. I really love the clearance area where they sell everything from plants for a dollar to 67% off furniture because it was on display. I've heard people bitch about quality, but if you pay $8 for a new end table...are you really expecting it to be an heirloom piece? I think the pieces are priced very well based upon the quality. I even found something the other day that was made in the USA! 

Recently I witnessed a girl and her parents spend $580. They bought EVERYTHING for her wedding reception. Vases, candles, mirrors, tablecloths, twinkle lights, glass rocks. I think they bought glassware too because it was cheaper than renting it all. 

The Christmas stuff is really charming too and the live plants look pretty healthy. I've bought Christmas and birthday presents for kiddos here and they loved them too. 

The main reason I LOVE Ikea is that it's closer to my house than a Walmart is and has been able to completely replace that wretched, wretched store. Associates are WAY better than those you'll find at Lowe's, Home Depot, or Walmart too. 

Did you know Copper Tail Brewing is right across the street? It is! Just across Adamo from the back of the Ikea store! You're welcome.

This Ikea is okay.  They have a pretty good selection and the store is always clean and welcoming, but finding employees to help can be hard sometimes.  They need more cashiers and I hate their carts but I love to shop here and so do my kids.

I love Ikea Family so all the discounts they offer.  I do hate that you have to walk through the whole store to get out so "running in quickly" isn't really an option.

We first word that comes to mind when I think about Ikea is clusterf$#k. Every time I'm here I feel like a lost child whose mother needs to be paged on the intercom, as I inevitably venture off the prescribed path and get terribly lost. 
Another gripe-they seriously need to get more cashiers. I spent 45 agonizing minutes in line whilst buying my sister furniture for her new apartment.  Then, when it was finally our turn, we find out that the piece we plucked from the self-serve warehouse was a three piece set, of which we only retrieved one piece.  Back in line we go.
I guess Ikea is cool if you like Swedish meatballs (I don't) or are good with a screwdriver (I'm not). I'd recommend them for odds and ends like cheap colanders or wall art, but as far as furniture goes, it's not my first choice,

We bought a huge Pax closet system from Ikea & decided to have their service put it together. The system was delivered & assembled. However, AFTER it was assembled they said the doors will be delivered on a later date. I had to then go to the store to figure it out what happened to the doors & why they weren't delivered. That took about an hour of my time. The doors were finally delivered weeks later. My husband was going to put the doors on...no big deal, right?? No!!! The doors should've been put on FIRST!!! I've tried calling customer service but you end up sitting on the phone for 20-40min with no resolution & you can't call the store directly. (The guy in customer service said that's because the stores get a lot of calls..hmmm I wonder why!?) So now my husband has to disassemble the entire thing only to reassemble again. Thanks Ikea! Great job!

As a graduate student, IKEA is roughly synonymous with my idea of heaven. I'm pretty sure around 90% of the things in my apartment are from this particular store.

If you've never been, prepare for the experience of a lifetime. You will find yourself daydreaming about the store long after you've left. 

This location might be the mother of all IKEA stores--it is ridiculously huge. You are sort of forced to wind through the entire store, like a hamster, by virtue of the layout. This can be very annoying if you come for a specific item, but it's fun to browse otherwise. 

I love the housewares floor! Whenever friends or guests compliment the cute things in my kitchen it is a pretty solid guarantee that whatever they picked up is an IKEA item. The prices are always amazing too.

Since IKEA has figured out that you will spend roughly 20 hours here each time you come, there is a cafeteria upstairs. It's pretty outstanding for a furniture store, I must say. Plus, your meal is free if you spend over $100 at check-out. 

I am so happily addicted. Send more money to my IKEA fund, please.

Though I only shop here occasionally, I really like this place. Always filled with a lot of cute, useful household items. The upper floor at this location features staged rooms for display  of their furniture and other household items. I'm not too much of a fan of the  pointy rectangular furniture style , but I see how others like it. The store definitely feature is an array of funky  modern styles. Their furniture kind reminds me of dorm furniture. 

My favorite part of the store is the lower level where they have a wide variety an assortment of their individual items categorized for each part of the house. There, I can pick and choose what I want manually without having to order anything in advance. The items sold here are trendy and practical to suit your household needs. There are some items featured here that I can never find anywhere else. My favorite part are the storage items, especially for the bathroom, closets and kitchen.

There's not much more here that I can say about the store that isn't already advertised in their catalogs/website. I would not recommend coming in here if you are looking for a quick in and out shopping experience as this place is a maze to go through. Luckily, there are shortcuts, but even those may not be long enough to get out of the store at a convenient time. Be mindful of the check out wait during weekends and holidays. They tend to be a bit understaffed during off season times. Another warning is to bring your own shopping bag as they do not provide them at the checkout counter.

 I would recommend that you reserve about two hours of your time before setting foot in here. That has been my estimated maximum time spent in the store, whether you are just windowshopping or really looking for something specific. You might end up getting an item or two no matter what. :-)

This is a very budget friendly type of place for many of the things, but in the end you get what you pay for. The products overall are okay quality wise, the store does not keep many staffs around to help you out, it takes 15 plus minutes sometimes to find someone to help you, and these staff don't have much technical knowledge on things. The cafeteria is good and cheap but nothing there seems like it's made from scratch, for example milk for your coffee comes from the powered milk machine. In the end if you can afford to go somewhere else, just do so.

Who doesn't like IKEA?  I mean really, even if you don't want to put together your furniture, you can still walk around the show rooms and get ideas, really good ideas for your own personal domicile.  When I was just starting off in the world as an adult, I literally would spend all of my extra cash here.  Now that I am established, I still go back often just because most everything sold by IKEA is made intelligently.  Not everything they sell will last for generations, but anything they sell will get you through to a time when you can afford something that will.  I do have items in my house that are well over a decade old.

South Philly Ikea is a different type of store.  No matter how Swedish the corporate philosophy, the Rocky Balboa vernacular and mannerisms of the area show through.  It's a good thing.  It makes the shopping experience real and offers the flavor of the city.  If you shop at the other IKEA, in the burbs, you would think that you were on a different planet.

I prefer the South Philly version because the people here are real, customers and associates alike.  In the burbs, I see the more affluent customer, who is usually more full of themselves arguing with cashiers as to why they need to bag their own purchase, or better yet why they have to bring their own bag with them or purchase a reusable one separately. 

I always thank my cashiers by name, anywhere I go.  Nothing sounds as sweet to a person, than their own name when they are doing everything they can to make their way in the world.  South Philly Ikea gets most of my business, even though the tax is higher in Philly, than the burbs.  It's just a better experience for me.

This review is specific to the return process. I was there on a Saturday afternoon, I get it, there's a lot of people. So should the management staff at Ikea and make sure they staff the return department with enough staff members to keep the lines moving. I had to wait twice in the line and they were 25 and 40 minute waits with very slow moving staff members.

I stopped by Ikea today after a hiatus of nearly two years. The showrooms looked as good as ever, but the cafeteria is looking a bit shabby. I did end up with a big bagful of merchandise to purchase, but left it all at the front when I saw the absurdly long checkout lines. All the self-checkout machines seem to have disappeared. What's going on? Is Ikea trying to discourage people from actually buying anything?  What a shame.

Sold incomplete cabinet with shopping list for discontinued doors. Salesman promised secret phone number to another store but never provided. Had to return items but when I ordered the cabinet online for $49 more, only received hinges. Everything else apparently was discontinued. Can not call stores or check orders online. Have to send an email and ask for update. Are the Swedes so backwards?

I admit it, I was an Ikea virgin. When I hit the doors and smelled those incredible cinnamon rools, I had to have one. It was warm and fresh and soon good. Staff wasn't very friendly.
I think there is only 1 way in and 1 way out of this store. It was a Sunday and the store was packed. You kind of get swept into the crowd and pushed along. Thankfully there wasn't a fire. I saw a whole lot of varied items from Christmas decorations to toilet brushes to furniture and all things in between.
It certain ally has a vast and varied selection of numerous items and it is a good place to get some decorating tips. I wish I read Dutch, as much of the language is not English, on various items. I saw some good buys and some I felt were overpriced.  What I did not see were any sale items, except on the ground floor there is a small clearance area.
I Kea isn't just around the corner for most of us. I wasn't driving but, it was Southeast of Ybor, so my guess is between Ybor and Brandon.
I can see people's fascination with this store. It defiantly has some unique and specialty items, as it is a Dutch chain store. I usually can never make it through a store this size and not buy anything, but somehow I had no problem. The other 2 only picked up a picture frame and a toilet brush. That was a lot of effort and driving to get a cinnamon bun!
I am keeping an open mind, but personally, it's a bit far for me to go for a picture frame. Now if you were remodeling... maybe, I am open to the possabilities.
Another problem I had with the store were the nonexistent sales people. We tried to get assistance several times to no avail and many products had no price marked on them.
Like I said I am keeping an open mind, but I felt I had blown part of my Sunday, by partaking in a peoples tight space crawl.
What's a girl to do?  Keep an open mind & try it on a week day.

IKEA is an interesting place its filled with inexpensive furniture and some fun designs. But it's hard to find an employee to ask her directions. in the first hour I was there, the only employee I found told me "no English". Finally after searching both floors I found an employee who directed me to the section that I was looking for and had previously missed. I found out they have these secret doorways that look like they're an entrance to a private employee area that actually lead to other display sections of the store and they're not labeled. 
Soon after I was ready to leave, I found another friendly employee who cheerfully directed me on the path to exit the second floor after I told him I had been lost there for four days. I think their secret marketing plan is to get you hopelessly lost so that you just give up and search out every square inch of the store and you'll buy something before you leave. I had nice healthy walk and headed to Ybor to get a drink!

We love IKEA but there are just way too many things I want to buy!!!  We've bought a couple nice dressers from there that are of pretty nice quality, and recently got an end table and a cute little desk and chair set for dirt cheap!  Going to IKEA is always an adventure for us, and we always make a point to have lunch in their restaurant.  It's not bad at all (food, service, and price-wise) and is always jam packed!

Quite possible the worst checkout system I the continental US. It's so long, always. All lines are never open despite a plethora of staff. 

The maze in the market place that forces you along a path that's too tight and jammed is the 2nd most annoying behind the checkout system. 

Staff and store are nice and clean. 

No other issues but the checkout system is An easy fix. Managers? Are you listening?

Sometimes i wonder if Yelp inadvertently reregisters businesses because Ive checked in here at least 5x before. Regardless, this is IKEA and i am not sure a rating applies because IT IS WHAT IT IS. IKEA. 
Food used to be a 4 now a 2 or 3   Tables Only cleaned whenever. You usually have tp clean yours before eating. 
Long checkout lines make it a 3   Typical is today when cashier has to call someone and 20 people patiently waited or went to other lines after 10imins on the phone 
 But for fun and the fact I've finally found the short cuts to circumvent the maze here i give it a 4.
Honestly never buy anything here i have to put together anymore. But the glassware and lamps and other items make the visit worthwhile.

So yeah, we all know the stuff is good. It comes in a million pieces but once you get it together, it's cute and it works.

But this location absolutely sucks.  One, it's too big.  Way too big actually. It's poorly laid out. And then the warehouse room where you have to fetch your own boxes is so damn confusing.  

As if all of that didn't suck enough, it took us about an hour to finally get to the register the line was so long.  It was crazy.  

Terrible. Buy online and get it shipped to the house.
As usual, the check-out lines are ridiculously long... Love the store, hire more cashiers for the main check-out and returns. You just lost a sale because of it. Sad.

Ikea happens to be one of my favorite furniture stores around. I just love it..
So glad we have one conveniently located here in Tampa !!
Anytime I need something furniture wise I find myself there.

I just moved into a apartment so its pretty often that I visit. I always find what I'm looking for. I like the quality and pricing as well.

Drove over from clearwater for breakfast. The server told us with a straight face that there were no pancakes. I assumed this had to be a joke. She called the manager guy and he confirmed "we haven't had them for months". Are you freaking kidding me????? Go downstairs to the food store, but the batter / mix and make me some Swedish Pancakes!!!!!

Such horrible customer service. Wasted so much gas and travel time. Trying to have family purchase items for us off our registry has become nearly impossible because their is no option to pick up items from a store. There are no electronic gift cards. You cannot purchase items in advance online or over the phone. So family members in other states are only left with the option of paying $100+ extra to have items shipped to us. Needless to say I am beyond aggitated, especially with being placed on hold for over an hour with Customer Service to be told nothing is going to be done about this. Ikea, you have made it nearly impossible and extremely inconvenient for people to shop for the holidays and gift giving. Even the option of getting a gift card is a pain and we would have to wait for it to be mailed to us. So instead of jumping through all these hoops to get these items we are just going to remove the several thousand dollars worth of products from our registry and move on. If you are creating a registry for weddings, house warmings, holidays, birthdays, baby / bridal showers or anything else.. Don't include ikea products on your list. You won't be able to receive them without being robbed of extra cash for the shipping up charges. So thank you ikea for giving me a headache, wasting my gas and my time. You have just lost two loyal customers who have shopped with you for years. And I will be sure to tell others not to buy from you.

We got a lot of help while in the store picking out cabinets for our kitchen. The items were to be deliver. On delivery day, the order never came. We called the customer service center and they said the delivery was cancelled because there was 1 part of the stock (all items were in stock when we ordered it). We never received a heads up the delivery was cancelled so we wasted a Saturday. A simple call or email would have been nice. IKEA really dropped the ball.

Why would you start a major remodel around xmas time . Half the store is closed for remodel. 
Dumb

The show rooms are beautiful and the rooms make me envious of all of the inventory in sight. I can't wait for the day I buy my first empty home because some of the concept rooms are stunning. Most notably, the carpets are very beautiful while still affordable. I noticed that one was even made in Egypt! How cool!
There is an incredible selection of household/kitchen accessories as well. I tend to avoid most of the things that are made in China because of the fact they've been known to use lead paint. I picked up a coffee press made in the Czech Republic for only $7.99! It works very well, and you can't beat that price.
The cafeteria offers free coffee for IKEA family members. It's very good, and the coffee is available for sale in the market downstairs. The cafeteria claims to offer a "taste of Sweden", however I don't think chicken tenders with fries are very Swedish. Normally the food in the cafeteria is very good, however today the mash tasted like it was made from an instant powder mix and the whitefish I ordered was tough and it tasted like it was nearly expired. Yikes. The veggies were steamed, but not fully--they were still hard and cut far too large to be bite-sized. The ginger-carrot soup was absolutely terrible, and my basil-tomato soup had way too much basil and the tomato inside were tasteless. Maybe it's better to stick with the food choices that are more popular--the food that's not Swedish that moves faster that's more likely to be fresh, albeit far less healthy.

Oh IKEA! What a fun furniture wonderland that you are. Although it seemed like a lot of your items need fixing up to avoid being a hazard to your fellow guests  - your show rooms are a wonder to walk through. Due to the way things are being laid out- picking a favourite out of the many items was like a spoiled trip to the ice cream store but with ease. 

At the end of our adventure- my companion hurriedly rolled me, a bed frame, an office chair and a multipurpose mirror towards the exit - out into the wintry weather for fear we might submerge ourselves into more spending spree. \(^.^)/ but before he could do so- I sneakily grabbed a bunny for less than $3. WIN!!! 

Now, the real fun in all of this is fixing the pieces together like one fun jigsaw puzzle. All furnitures usually come with a manual and right screws for every holes. Follow the manual and you'll never go wrong. 

Happy days IKEAans!!!

Being the only location in town you can expect it to be busy. If you have never visited an IKEA before, just a heads up, it is a DIY (do it yourself) furniture place. Be prepared to put everything together yourself. Also, if you plan on stopping in for small decor type items, bring bags with you. They can supply you with bags but you will have to pay for them.

I love Ikea! I was amazed from the moment I walked into the store. It has a very impressive size. I like how they have the path laid right out for you with little shortcuts to get you where you need to go faster. 

They merchandise there items well. When I went I saw a few of the smaller items used in different ways in each mock room. The food is also really good. My girlfriend and I have been there a couple times for shopping and we always find ourselves being sucked in by the smell of the good food. I think it's a really cool idea to have food at a furniture store, and even cooler that they sell the food down stairs. 

I used to think IKEA furniture was not very reliable and that you got what you paid for, but we recently bought a bed frame and a couple night stands and I was really  impressed with there construction. It's been a few months and everything is still holding strong and hasn't needed to be re tightened. 

My only criticism would be that it's not always easy to find an employee if you have a question. I usually have to walk over near the kitchens where they have the computers to design rooms to find somebody. Other than that I love going there and shopping!

Sometimes I dread going into this place as at times I feel like a mouse in a maze, lol.  Once you have been here enough times you learn which corners to cut to get to where you need to be. The staff is always friendly and shopping here is easy once you know your way around. 

I do prefer the pizza downstairs as to the food upstairs. I have eaten there three times and all three times I would have preferred I had eaten somewhere else.
Typical Ikea except no express or self check out.  If you are coming for one or two things budget your time accordingly.  Usually not worth it

The furniture is not top quality but for the price they where perfect.  I mean they dont really look cheap, they look pretty fancy, but when you open some of the drawers they dont feel firm.

Also, I have to add that I wasnt gonna buy here because some people told me that they where really hard to assemble.  I assembled all of my furniture in my apartment (every single one is from ikea) without any problem or missing parts.

My reccomendation is to buy a small (or big if you want to) drill so it makes it faster and easier to put in the screws.
It would be more fun if it was adequately staffed.  The lines are ridiculous and by the time you get to the checkout, everyone is cranky.

I love love love #Ikea. I love the items, my son really likes his Ikea kids bedroom... however I felt like this location is going downhill really fast. The employees were a bit rude and there are numerous check out lines, but only 5 open? On a Sunday? When its packed? Didn't make much sense. The lines to check out were horrendous. If you can, go during the week. When employees acknowledge you and aren't rude.

Not bad...

Who can say anything bad about Ikea? This particular location is humongous and a little tiring to navigate through, but awesome because there's so much stock. I always recommend perusing online before heading to an Ikea because otherwise, it's overwhelming.

Get the meatballs. They're so terrible but awesome. Lingonberry sauce!!!

Having only ever been to the Baltimore IKEA location before, I wasn't sure what to expect from visiting this one... Would it be the same? Would it have different things in stock?

I was pleasantly surprised that it had different room displays and items set up, compared to Baltimore, especially an area dedicated to display cases/buffets (which is what I was searching for specifically).

My only gripe is that the bathrooms seemed grungy and more like an afterthought. There was no latch on the door of many of the stalls, so you had a hole in the door and anyone would be able to take a peek at you through it. Not cool.

The only bad thing is the amount of time you have to spend waiting in line to check out. Other then that- they always have things in stock that I need. Those computers in the stock area are a god send.. I can never find an employee to help me but with those computers I just find whatever I need.

This location is so big and spacious- even when its crowded there's so much room so you never feel bothered! 

The restaurant is awesome as usual- also sometimes slow but again, that's the only issue. Food is always good-- prepackaged though.

If you're a first time get the swedish meatballs. 

Price is good. The quality obviously is not fantastic, but you should know that if you're going to Ikea.

Oh and couples beware- it's been said that Ikea makes you fight.

I have bought almost all the furniture in my apartment from Ikea, and I am happy with everything. The only problem I have had is with my Trysil bed, the metal legs broke. However, I just took the broken piece to Ikea and they gave me a replacement piece for free. I thought I would have to pay for the piece, so I was very pleasantly surprised. Customer service just won Ikea big points in my book. Also, the fro-yo they serve here is some of the best fro-yo ever.

Whats not to like about ikea. Only con associates dont speak to u just walks by u like ur invisible ( maybe im just used to having to speak to all customers & be polite at my job) even cashiers having their own conversations not paying customers any mind.

After living in Germany for 2 years and seeing the best IKEA stores there and Sweden, I really have to step outside myself to remain objective.  I wish I could say IKEA is IKEA. Same product. But, much more of it.  I'm just happy to live in a town that I can go to one.  With that being said, I LOVE IKEA with all of my heart.  This one is no exclusion.  GOOD STORE! TOTALLY WORTH CHECKING OUT because it's here.  I always find something I need for my place in here.

Ikea is always a step ahead in terms of design. I'm about to start a kitchen reno, and I'm finding myself planning on getting just about everything from Ikea, despite having looked at a few other stores. With well designed products at a great price, it's hard to go wrong. The only drawback is that their products are so popular that everything you buy is so immediately recognizable. Even so, I'm an unapologetic Ikea addict. 

I may have to remove a star when I find myself back into a relationship and go back to Ikea. It's a great store, but a relationship graveyard. :)

If you are new to the Philly area, this IKEA will be a godsend.  All IKEAs are identical, so no point reviewing their stuff.  Be prepared for a lot of screaming children and long lines... interspersed with crappy meatballs.
What is there to not like about IKEA? I love their room samples for ideas and the food is cheap and good!!! I do so much of my furnishings here!!

I love IKEA and how can you not?

This IKEA is like most IKEAs except they served cheesesteaks.  Wait, what???  Good cheesesteaks at IKEA and maybe the best in the city?  Yes.  They were portion controlled and tasty.  Then they stopped making them.

Seriously, IKEA bring back your cheesesteaks!

Also, the lines here are awful on weekends and I ended up buying the items I needed at your Conshohocken location the next day.

What an awesome place! 
Its like an amusement park for shopper ! 
How start it is for them to come up with an idea of everyone have to follow the arrow to move forward. I sure didn't miss looking at everything ! 
Didn't mean to buy anything but .... Of course with in 2 min I already grabbed a big bag to put stuff in, another 2 min later switch over to a cart! The deal is so good and everything is fashionably basic. I got a set of plate set for only $24. Few other nic-nak .
2nd floor was like a bunch of little living room . all the prices were reasonable. I want a new bed set and living room set.! 
I wish there is IKEA in jacksonville. Defiantly will go back when ever I head that way again !

IKEA and its products are the greatest invention since sliced bread for sure! The South Philly store is great in many ways including its view from the Cafeteria to the Delaware River. The food at the Cafeteria is truly affordable and of decent quality.  On the down side, checking out of this store is a nightmare, long lines with edgy people. I would recommend shopping early!

It's an Ikea. 

Nothing special. 

The staff seems fairly unenthused but are pretty responsive once you can find somebody to assist you.

I don't like the way they seem to change the set up of the already difficult to navigate store .

Whatever. If you need inexpensive furniture that you have to put together on your own this is the mainstay for something like that. 

On the plus side, the food is tasty if you choose to eat there. That $1.00 fro-yo is delicious. I've gone there specifically for the yogurt. 
Not sure exactly what that says about me though. :)

Would you believe that this is one of the better places to eat in this area? Just kidding, I've never eaten here but apparently a lot of other people reviewing this IKEA do,  so maybe it's worth coming here just for the food?

Apart from the forever confusing store layout, and the wild swings in prices from low tier quality to anything of actual quality- IKEA solves a huge problem that everybody has had for years: where to get cheap furniture that still looks like you care about how your room/apt etc look.

The other surprising thing about their stuff is that it retains resale value, but only if it cost more than 100 bucks to begin with. I did buy a couch here once for 150 bucks which I ended up selling for 165 on craigslist. I wasn't sure whether that was a craisglist fluke or IKEA fluke. Anyway, if you keep your mid-range ikea junk in shape, then you might come out ahead when you try to sell.

Employees also work here, but they like to play hide-and-seek like 90% of the day and are amazing at it. And they should be, with all the practice they get. Some of they like to hide by the registers, but I guess because it's close to the exit. That's usually where I find them.

Kids Club is Terrible! We took our 2 kids to eat came back doesn't close until 8 but the employees said they closed at 7:15 it was 7:15 on our phone. This wasn't the first time the Staff changing rules. Wouldn't want to Leave our sweet kids with RUDE Employees.  Don't Plan on Kids Club

Love the products. We had a personable, helpful and knowledgeable IKEA associate in living room furniture on Sunday afternoon. He was great! Only drawback to the store is way too much walking for those of us with health issues. But I got my steps in!

The customer service is horrendous. It's beyond a joke. The delivery services are careless and indifferent of your trust. We had bought a perfectly acceptable As-is shoe cab and wanted it delivered to us since we don't live in Philly. Unfortunately when it arrived, it was in shambles. The delivery men laid it on the side so I couldn't see how damaged it was. After putting it upright, all the compartments were about to fall off. Screws were missing and the wood was stripped so all the compartments were supported by the bottom ones. I called the customer service to see how we can fix this and they were indifferent of the problem. I understand that it was an As-Is item so no returns but it worked perfectly and barely scratched when we bought it. It is as if we let you baby-sit our child and you return him/her back to us with missing teeth! Who is to blame? This is the last time I will purchase anything from them. The policies are ridiculous and outdated.

Sometimes places surprise you. You walk in not expecting to see the Virgin Mary appear on a taco and, lo and behold, she appears. IKEA is not one of those places. Every time I visit I see the same atrocious parking situation, particle board furniture and icing glazed cinnamon buns. I also see the same long line of impatient shoppers waiting to check out and must maneuver through the same maze of a showroom where a family of four lines up straight across the only aisle and slows your progress to a crawl. Needless to say, I've had plenty of time to look for the Virgin Mary at IKEA and I have yet to see her. 

But that doesn't mean IKEA is a bad place. I actually am okay with it for a couple of reasons. If you shy away from the high end, particle board stiffened furniture and take a look at some of the smaller pieces, you can actually find some things that are quite sturdy and last for more than a few months. I've purchased a couple chairs, easels and a table for my classroom and they are still going strong two years in. My wife and I also bought our bed there. It has been supporting our sleep for six years now, although we did have to rig it slightly because of a design flaw. 

If you go even smaller than easels and children's chairs, you can find some cool little buckets, kitchenware, wall hangings and storage containers. After a visit to Capital Tacos in which I was served chips from an IKEA bucket, I decided to go buy some buckets of my own. A few went into my classroom to store pens and scissors while one stayed at home so I could reenact my visit to Land O' Lakes every night while watching the Wire on my couch. Something about tortilla chips from a bucket makes them taste so much better. 

I also love the prices at IKEA. I won't say they are dirt cheap but they aren't far off. In fact, I'd say they are only a step above the dirt cheap label. I've googled "what's the next step above dirt cheap" to get a fabulous descriptor for IKEA's prices but all that search mustered is some bad Trip Advisor experiences and a St. Louis liquor store. For now, I'll just say they are extremely reasonable. 

Another thing I really enjoy about IKEA is their cafeteria. This place doesn't serve gourmet food by any stretch of the imagination but there are definitely worse places to eat in town. IKEA's cafeteria is full of fries, bread, pasta, cake and their famous Swedish meatballs. What's in it for this vegan? Well, their newest menu item is VEGAN/soy-free and gluten-free Swedish Meatballs. Yep, you heard me right. These guys are made from chick peas, green peas, carrots, corn, kale, and red bell peppers and served in a sweet potato and cauliflower sauce. The meatballs are not as good as what I make at home, but they are the best vegan meatballs I've eaten out since coming to Tampa (spoiler alert, there aren't any other restaurants in town that currently serve vegan meatballs that I've come across). IKEA has also set it up so you can essentially eat for free. If you are planning a purchase of a hundred dollars or more and have some daily calories to spare, stop by the cafeteria. They will deduct the price of your meal from what you pay at the register. 

Take my word for it, a full stomach makes checking out and leaving the parking lot so much less emotional.

Customer service is horrible.  Waited in line a long time for a return while the staff fooled around.  One employee talked to a friend for 5 minutes, then went outside calling a coworker to come out too and then called a customer to the register and went in the back with the other cashier and left the people standing there.  The products are ok and inexpensive but if you have to make a return it's a pain.

I have to give it 5 stars because it's just so awesome of a place.  We've furnished 3/4 of our home with the Hemnes collection, which is solid wood and surprisingly high quality.  We've also eaten at the restaurant a bunch of times and we've never had a bad meal.  

If you've never been to an IKEA, it can be pretty overwhelming.  Expect to do several hours of walking, often while dodging people who are all over the place.  Still, you can't beat the price and the value.  The kitchen gadget section is my favorite, they just have so many cute things there!

It's huge, it takes forever to get through, you do have to put most of your stuff together, but I do like EVERYTHING we've gotten from there.  I don't think the price is that great if you are like me and have to pay for delivery and set up but I still buy from there at times.

They sell the ultimate, best, most useful toilet accessory in the world - look for the PP Shots, it's a photo holder that mounts inside your toilet allowing you to urinate on the picture of your choice. Maybe you can put a world leader on it! Maybe you can print out a Google Images search result for a car you don't like. Or maybe you can flatten some flowers and grass, allowing you to have a more natural experience in your porcelain sanctuary. The world is yours to piss on.

As an IKEA veteran, I know you feel many emotions while shopping here. Therefore, I present you the five stages of shopping at IKEA. 

Confusion: Why is this place so huge? Why can't you buy any of the stuff on the showroom? Why is there food in a furniture store?

Love: wow. This furniture is so nice and functional. The food is so good! I love how you can get a healthy plate of chicken for $5. This $4 salmon wrap is the bomb. The prices are so low! I understand how IKEA works and its so easy!

Desperation: I can get rid of my current dishes for these new ones right? This cool ice cube tray is only 99 cents so its OK if I can buy it?! I can have 10 carpets in a room, right? I might need these sheets for when we have family over. I need 100 candles in my life!

Motivation: OK, aisle 31 bin 2. Got it. Aisle 15 bin 17. Check. I can't wait to assemble this awesome furniture at home!

Shock: OMG!!!! $2000?! I only bought new dishes, a new bed, a wardrobe, 100 candles, a down comforter, ice cube trays, a grater, orchid, new pillows, and a knife. I don't think I can even afford that $1 frozen yogurt.

Ikea has a great selection of affordable furniture and i love how easy to assemble their furniture is. Sometimes i love browsing the whole store but sometimes when i want to go in for something specific, i am thankful that they have a map so i can take shortcuts to my specific destination.  So far i already have a sofa and (my recent purchase) a dining set. They have great dining sets that include 4 chairs for less than $200 but they seemed too small for my liking and decided to customize in order to get better Bang for my buck. I liked the price of Rydenbäck and how spacious the table top was but wan't wild about the Orange Backaryd ($40) underframe. In the dining area there were no employees in sight if i had any inquires (which i had). When i found an employee, she came with me to the dining section where i showed her 4 dining tables which all have 
inter-changeable under frames and table tops. She claimed that the table combination on display were the ones that were compatible. One of the table on display was Grebbestad with Ryggestad. I checked the bottom of the table to see how the underframe was and then examined the bottom of Rydebäck. At first she wasn't very helpful and seemed like she just wanted to go back to what she was doing but then upon telling her "Pleaseeeee check the system so i can know compatible options"...she ended up printing my compatible options and the Grebbestad underframe  ($80) WAS compatible with Rydebäck table top ($49). We got a spacious customized dining table with dining chairs that looks elegant and minimalistic... for less than $200 - WIN !!  We went to the self serve area  to pick up our murchandise and proceed to checkout. Going in a weekday afternoon was by far a better idea than coming during the weekend. There is less traffic of customers and the line to pay is shorter. The chairs, Grebbestad underframe  and Rydebäck table top ALL fit inside my Nissan Versa Note. And of course, before leaving we purchased two non fat frozen yogurts ($1 each).  The assembly was fairly easy and even enjoyable. Would i return? Hell yeah !! As a matter of fact, next stop to Ikea calls for Area Rug, Place mats, and some home decor & accents.

Great deals on furniture and the food court has a lot to choose from at a pretty good price! Was a big fan of the Swedish Meatballs! The store has 2 floors: Top floor is a show room showing what is available and how it can be used in your home based on the mock display. Take note of the item number and location and then venture over to the 1st floor. Here you can find your chosen furniture packaged up in the warehouse by aisle and bin number (matching your item ticket) and then a final mock display of outdoor furniture right before checkout. So far that whole experience had been fun, but at checkout the cashiers were incredibly rude to their customers and it was incredibly unprofessional.

Originally I had thought about giving 3 stars, but right after checkout they have ice cream.....so a star bump they get!

Our family enjoyed purchasing several chest of drawers for the bedroom and baby items here. The showroom is clean and the staff is friendly.

It was easy and free to park.

What's not to love about modular Swedish furniture?  I got all my outdoor furniture from Ikea because the prices beat most other places, and it's cheap enough to replace after a couple years if I need to.

Also, my dear Swedish fried said that Ikea's Swedish meatballs are pretty authentic.  For $5.99 (if you have the free Ikea family card), you get 15 meatballs in cream sauce, a scoop of mashed potatoes and lingonberry preserves.  That's not a bad deal.

This place is the same as all Ikea's. The problem is that they do NOT have enough employees working at the checkout counter so I spent more time in line then I did wondering through the store maze. Customer care should be a priority for big business. Clearly Ikea wants to resemble the low level Walmart type service. Lost a lifetime customer!
I love the fact that this is never so packed that I can't get help or move around without running into others with 4 wheel drive shopping carts.

I love Ikea. Just so you all know. Their stuff is awesome. Great prices and all that. But this store had the worst associates working. Unfriendly and kind of mean. One girl tried to take my cart, that I had left for a minute. I said that's mine. She proceeded to tell me park it over there or we take it. I almost took all my stuff back. Couldn't find any help in the sofa section. And the other customers seemed upset every where we looked. Even the cafeteria workers were grouchy. So go buy your stuff and get out quick.

The things you would find here are great for small space.  Most of the furniture designs can double up as extra storage space.  Some items are inexpensive because it is of lower grade and needs assembly.  However, it is of good quality.  I find that some of the chairs and sofa are a little pricey for what it is.  Roaming around the place can provide setup ideas for those needing a little inspiration.

We purchased our loft furniture here and it came together real nice.

My parents are from Sweden so perhaps my review is a bit biased, but IKEA is great on more levels than one (literally). The store is huge, so I recommend making the trip to the store and creating a day of it. Make sure you visit the cafe before you begin shopping; trust me after 8 different warehouses full of stuff you will be hungry! If you are businesses minded individual like me, the first thing you will notice is that their marketing strategies are brilliant (the store is set up like a maze so once you are in you will be forced to see all ikea has to offer). Also, make sure you come to the store with money to blow; the items are priced very cheap; $7.99 doesn't sound like a lot of money, but after 25 different $7.99 items you are looking at about 200 bucks. My hubby and I bought a kitchen and a bedroom set from the Tampa location so far AMAZING!! I have heard the IKEA customer service horror stories, but so far I haven't really had to deal with that department. If you can, I would try to buy from the store directly instead of online. Overall 5 stars, also don't forget to sign up for the IKEA family card, you get tons of kick backs including free coffee and tea! :)

IKEA offers a very different shopping experience when it comes to furniture, so understanding what to expect will make for a better experience.  First off, the store is laid out in a way that forces you to meander virtually every department.  It's like a salmon swimming upstream if you forgot something and want to go back.  The advantage to this layout is that you don't have to worry about missing anything, but on the flip side if you need to run in for just one thing, good luck.

IKEA has a restaurant and cafe with nearly at cost prices as an incentive to take your time, eat and shop a little longer.  Swedish meatballs and lingonberry jam?  Yes please!  If you sign up for their IKEA Family membership card, you also get a free coffee or tea during every visit.

Prices are reasonable, but understand that is because you provide the labor.  As long as your expectations are in line, IKEA can offer a great value and experience.
A good bang for your buck. Stay away from their Ribs and Chicken though, they're not good. Fish and Chips, Mushroom Soup, and Garlic Toast highly recommended!

Ikea and I have a very dysfunctional love\hate relationship. I love their prices and a lot of their options, but I don't necessarily love the quality, and I absolutely hate how much I spend when I go there. Oh, bring your walking shoes because if you follow their suggested path, you'll be doing a heck of a lot of walking. Last time I was there I bought a 4 cubby\cabinet type thing to hang on the wall above my desk. It was fairly easy to assemble, but a little tricky to hang overall I was pretty pleased. I tried the food here once, I was not really a fan. They definitely have some unique items and at their low prices they're worth a look unless you are a super stickler on quality.

Fairly well organized, as is to be expected. Staff if super helpful, but of 21 checkout lines, they seemingly never have more than 3 or 4 open; even when the line is 10-15 customers deep. It's never worth spending more time in line than you did shopping.

I have bought most of my furniture here because it is cheap!

Got a bed, mattress, desk, and coat hangers. I always come here for the breakfast because that is awesome. Also if you are buying furniture they give you money for food based off of how much you spend but you need to spend more than $100.

That is really easy to do if you are trying to buy furniture.

It's hard not to like Ikea. I mean where else can you find inexpensive furniture of all types and of reasonable styles for affordable prices? That said if you're anti-particle board the options are much more limited. I generally like the textiles that are available (especially the bathmats) and find that some of their more inexpensive options for furniture are rather useful. That said this location isn't the most transit accessible making this trip a rare one if you don't drive. The store has good food options at the cafe upstairs and good treats at the restaurant downstairs too. The food prices really can't be beat for what it is worth.

Finding staff to aid you in making purchases is a bit more difficult than one might otherwise imagine, but generally if you're shopping at Ikea it's unlikely that you need much help: just write down all the info marked beside the items you're looking for and pick these items up downstairs once you get there! And don't miss the As Is section as you might find a steal of a deal for something that might be preassembled or slightly damaged or old.

I've discovered th perfect time to go to Ikea is on a weeknight, around 7pm. This is when there are no crowds, you can peruse the store leisurely and checkout with no lines! Perfect and painless! 

My boyfriend and I came here last night after dinner at The Keg nearby. It was around 7pm. We found ample good parking right near the exit. We were able to walk around the store without running into crowds of people, please upon checkout, we were able to walk directly up to a cashier with no lineup! Bonus!

This store is always fun to walk around and dream about what you wish you could have. The prices range from easily affordable to as expensive as you'd like!

It's too bad I didn't have room for frozen yogurt on the way out as it was a hot evening and it would've been perfect!

I went here to purchase a closet system for my house, and my experience became a bad one ever since I walked though the door. The employees here are not helpful at all, and nobody knows what they're talking about. The lady inside the door made us walk though the entire showroom, even though we already knew exactly what we needed to purchase from the self serve area. 

Once getting to the self serve area with our list, we went through, grabbed the boxes we needed that were on the designated shelf, and proceeded to checkout.
