The cashier didn't scan each box, which caused a difference in price. After we got home, we realized the boxes we bought weren't even the right ones! The stock employees didn't put the right boxes in the designated place, so we had to drive an hour back to exchange. 

We waited an hour and 15 minutes just to return the 3 boxes that were initially incorrect. Since the cashier didn't scan the right boxes, it was hard to even return it because they weren't correctly on the receipt as they should have been. Then we had to wait in the checkout line for another hour just to purchase the correct items. 

Needless to say, I will never go back to this store again, and don't recommend this location at all!

Meh. It's an average ikea. Displays and sells ikea stuff. But Smaland is a pain. This is only 3rd time we've tried to use it, and the other two times were in the Winter and store was understandably mobbed. There were waits but we got in.  Today, store is not so crazy. But, they are only allowing 6 children at a time into Smaland. We were initially told 25 minutes, but it is first-come-first-serve, so when we came back 20 minutes later, they said 45 minutes. Why they can't do a buzzer or overhead system, or just hire more damn staff so that all kids who want to can just play already! What a pain and a letdown for my kid who really wanted to play in the ball pit. Well, I'm getting my free cup of Ikea Family member coffee and not buying a thing from them today!

Ikea is awesome. They sell 50 cent hotdogs and $1 frozen yogurt - how awesome is that? This is just some of the rad snacks they offer in the mini cafeteria in the lobby. Upstairs, ikea offers real dining food and the most expensive dish is probably around $8, that's how cool ikea is. I also enjoy the house showrooms that they showcase; it's very hands-on and great before you actually purchase their products!

Very disappointed in the service I received while shopping in the store. When I was unable to locate the item I was looking to purchase I asked a sales associate - Jennifer - to help me. She directed me to the section I had just looked in - I politely asked if she would please take me over, because I had just come from that area and couldn't find it. I explained that I had people waiting for me in the car and l appreciated her helping me. She however was very patronizing and looked visibly annoyed to have to walk me to the back wall. When she arrived at the spot she realized the shelf was in fact empty of the item I was looking for. She did spot the display which she scanned and told me there were 24 of the item located at the top of the stairs. I asked if there was anyway to just purchase the display since I was in a hurry. She said no and did not offer any further help such as directing me to the stairs or offering to call up to someone in that department. I took the display with me and tried to quickly navigate to the upstairs. I was very frustrated to find that the "kitchens" were not in fact at the top of the stairs as she had indicated. It took me a few minutes to find where she was talking about and once I did the next sales associate insisted that they did not carry that item in their section. I explained that Jennifer had scanned the item and sent me there specifically. She then took me to sales associate - Michael - who was on the phone for several minutes before confirming that they didn't have the item upstairs. I asked again if I could purchase the display and again explained that I had several people waiting for me in the car and was trying to make a quick purchase. His response was to "let them out" which wasn't particularly amusing to me since I felt locating the small item I needed to purchase should not be this complicated or time consuming. He said he would need to create a price label on the computer. When the computer froze, he retrieved a piece of scrap paper from the trash can! And hand wrote it. It was completely frustrating and I felt like an inconvenience to everyone I asked for assistance. If I could give a 0 star review I would!

Ah, IKEA....I personally have always had good experiences at IKEAs in general and at this IKEA, specifically. 

Although I'm not a fan of super-modern looking decor, I do love a lot of the furniture and decorations at IKEA. I also like the home essentials, candles, frames, etc. I like it that they have pretty much everything you could need to set up a home, lots of options, and really fantastic prices. I have a hanging bar that i purchased a wile back and always get compliments. Ive also bought organizers,silverware, rugs, and patio furniture. Im pleased with them all and Im sure i will buy something there again.

An added perk of the IKEA experience is the food!!! I remember how shocked I was when I found out how good their food is! I know there's that thing about the meatballs beings made of horse meat....and I have no idea if that's true....but even if it was, aren't we just opposed to horse meat because we're not used to it? I'm not saying I want to eat horse meat, I'm just saying how is it different from eating a cow? 

Anyway, their non meat food items are great too: ice cream, chocolate bars, cinnamon rolls, etc. I love the little Swedish grocery store that's downstairs. And the food is just as affordable as the home goods. Where else can you get a 50 cent hot dog!

So, yes, I am a fan of IKEA.

It's an Ikea. It's always packed, you can count on seeing at least one toddler on a leash(!), and once you find what you want you walk and walk through the whole store (I guess it's to try and make you want to buy more, but for me, it's mostly just slogging around people) to get to the pickup area. Then you load up your pallets and check out. 

This store had utterly uninterested sales staff, but the cashiers were awesome. The home delivery people were nice and the delivery fee is only $59! I saw people trying to shove  pieces that clearly didn't fit into their cars. To each their own...

OMG, their hot dogs at the counter by the checkout lanes are the absolute worst! Horrible!
-Brian Seide
rambrian at the yahoo dot com

This has got to be my favorite place to buy furniture. My boyfriend and I have furnished the House with most things ikea. One thing I love about the store is you can match colors throughout the house. 

There is a selection of everything you can think of and if you are a family card holder you get some really neat stuff. My favorite is when you can eat for free at their restaurant.

Where are the EV Car Chargers?!?
I recently moved and needed new some furnishings. Decided we would try IKEA. Did a quick google search and opted for the Conshohocken store given that it is next door to Corporate HQ which might add a little pressure to be top notch. Also chose this store over other area stores because I believed it had EV car charging stations as announced in their press release from 2003. This was widely spread across the internet to help add to their green/sustainable mystique. 
http://www.csrwire.com/press_releases/35845-IKEA-to-Grow-Presence-of-Electric-Vehicle-Charging-Stations-with-Units-at-8-More-Locations-Extending-Reach-Beyond-the-Western-U-S-

No such luck as we drove around the lot and garage, No EV charging anywhere except the publicity hype. But what I did find was 110v outlets all over the garage. I plugged in and went shopping. While I lost in the center of the maze inside I overheard a page listing my car. I immediate dialed customer care as directed and received a rude message that I needed to unplug immediately. I agreed and explained to the "facilities rep" that we came here under the impression they had chargers. He stated he's never heard of it at any Ikea store(with attitude) and those outlets weren't set up for car charging just cell phones. We then proceeded to negotiate our way out of what felt like the center of the store, took a longtime. During this time we heard 4 more pages from the same guy even though we told him were on our way. On approach to the car we noticed 2 uniformed managerial employees and one jacketed bystander next to my car. The NON uniformed guy immediately began telling me to unplug while I was already on my way to do so. One of them stated their reason was a fire hazard, another stated grid surge might damage my car, and the third the power the car's pulling is too much for the grid. As I complied and unplugged, I explained that the charging system was designed for these concerns and that the New Green Ikea had a press release from 2013 that they were installing at this location. The three stated they never heard of such a thing and they also new of no Ikea's with EV charging. At the end of the exchange the non uniformed guy sarcastically said   "We thank you for going green". I was annoyed to say the least. 
Why was I confronted by three people at my car after agreeing to unplug with facilities rep via phone? Why were these three digging for argument/justification points after I agreed to unplug? I guess at the public marketing level Ikea is solar/sustainable forest/ev charging supporting but at the "real" grass roots level their local employees are unaware and obstructive. Do better guys. 

BTW, The furniture is great, sales reps helpful, and it's packed with great deals.

Where else can you find reasonably priced furniture and really reasonably priced food options in one locale? The answer: IKEA. IKEA is akin to a toy store for adults. There are countless home furnishings and everything from lighting to batteries and kitchen supplies to plants all at your fingertips. You can walk into IKEA and find something that you didn't realize you needed or wanted and you don't feel bad about buying it in the end. I like their range of styles of furniture and kitchen components and variety. 

One of my favorite things about the store is perusing their kitchen design/areas. I enjoy seeing the layouts and models of kitchens at the store. These Swedes were clairvoyant when they started this company and knew their different concept furniture store would be a global hit. I must warn you, however, that furniture you buy from here must be put together yourself. If you aren't good with tools or directions then this clearly would be an issue for you. I believe IKEA still offers a assembly crew to put together your items for $99, although I'm not sure how that works if you have multiple items to be assembled but I could see that $99 charge being for each item.

For items that don't have the box right next to the display, there is a labels location with an aisle and bin number so you may locate the item/furniture piece that you'd like to buy. I know in the past IKEA has offered cards and golf pencils to write he locations but id you find yourself devoid of writing materials you can just out the location coordinated into your smart phone as a memo or note. The said aisles are found at the end of the store before the checkout area so be sure to bring a cart with you to retrieve your selections. 

I have gotten a wide variety of things from this store, like lighting and plants to name a few. The bedding and pillows seem to be very comfortable however I have ever purchased those from there. There is an assortment of artwork/wall hangings and rugs as well as other home decor like frames and candles that is worth checking out as well. 

Another facet of IKEA, the (upstairs) cafe: on the second floor and to the right, upper part of the store once you ascend the stairs, the cafe has something for every taste and hunger level. There is the traditional cafeteria setup where you grab a tray and move through the line. The cafeteria has many diverse offerings and pretty much stays true to the Swedish style of food. Smoked and baked salmon, salads, vegetable based soups are some of the more healthy offerings. They also offer hot meals like chicken, Swedish meatballs, chicken "balls", and vegetable balls. Recently they have added more vegetarian entrees on their menu. First up are the cold case items, smoked salmon plates, smoked salmon salads, salmon wraps and cold desserts to name a few. Next, you find the hot food line. On my most recent visit I had carrot and ginger soup and I sampled the vegetable balls which came with a cauliflower sweet potato sauce and some steamed vegetables. These items were delectable and my dining partner who was new to the IKEA cafe scene was impressed. We also samples the cornbread which was very airy and good. By way of desserts, there are some offerings in the cold case but they also had a hot apple crisp if you were interested. We tried an apple cake and vanilla cake bomb type thing found in the cold case. These sweets were a great ending to a satisfying meal and we couldn't even finish them. All these items including soup, cornbread, two entrees and two desserts was under $15 (we only had ice water as our selected beverage).

The drinks are fountain style and provided at the drink stations in the seating area. There are straws available and other condiments such as Cholula in this area as well. The seating area is first come first served and make sure to grab your silver wear before you begin to eat (there are flatware caddys near the cash registers). 

Downstairs Snack Area: To the left of the exit of the store there is a little snack area near the exit past the cash registers for those people who made it throughout the whole IKEA experience and could use some nourishment by way of slices of pizza, cinnamon buns, fountain drink, or frozen yogurt for $1. This is a popular spot for shoppers to come and relax and take a load off from your what I imagine was a lengthy shopping experience. I feel that time just melts away when you are in this store, there is jso much to see and peruse. 

Adjacent to the snack area there is a little food store which houses some IKEA delights. There are frozen food offerings as well as shelf stable items like pasta and crackers and jams and sauces. I feel like this is worth browsing if you are a fan of their food.

All in all, there is so much about IKEA that is great. If you are wanting to furnish a new home or dwelling space and want the best price on new furniture and home decor, IKEA is worth checking out. Parking lot is huge but expect to walk.

I LOVE IKEA! What a concept! Look through half the store, feed me, look through the rest and make me work a bit to fill my gigantic cart...feed me again - and this time it's cinnamon rolls. warm. with extra icing for .25 and a way to take home more for the family so I don;t have to cook dinner OR breakfast tomorrow while i'm setting up all my cool furniture with directions that have no words. AND I CAN DO IT! You just exude cerebral intelligence when you walk out. Literally. People must, they MUST see you as a Master...of...ummm...something! But, you don't care what they think because you just had an amazing day long experience and lived to tell about it! 

As an added bonus, at the end of the food aisles (toward the bathrooms) there is now a candy dispenser that you can fill and weigh out Swedish candies! The Swedish licorice is to die for. Seriously. I have a very good friend in the Netherlands that sends it to me and, well, I'm still going to let him, but I have backup!! 

DO NOT MISS IKEA! But...try to go during the week so you can walk into all the faux rooms and actually pretend they're yours without being bothered by the strangers that keep popping into your party! ;-D  (unless that's your thing...)

I love this place.  Really neat home décor ideas and furniture that you just don't see anywhere else.  Lots of great "space saving" ideas, that seems to be their forte.
The cafeteria is even really great with very affordable food (try the Swedish meatballs!!!!!).
Set aside a couple hours though, this place is huge!!!!

This is a review of IKEA as a restaurant, because, I have been known to take trips to the store solely for a cheap meal when I am in the South Edmonton Common area (and I totally know others have been doing this as well - all the Saturday morning brunches with the grandparents I see waiting at the door before opening?).  NO SHAME!!!

First off, Breakfast.  It's $1 for a plate full of scrambled eggs, fried potatoes and 2 small breakfast sausages.  ONE DOLLAR.  If, like me, you don't like powdered eggs (I highly doubt those things are real), they will sub extra potatoes for you.  They open a half hour before the store opens (restaurant opens 9:30, store opens at 10), and if you go in the first half hour, you also get a FREE coffee or tea.  It's not revolutionary food by any means, but it's ONE DOLLAR.

The rest of the day, things get a tad more expensive.  Ask if they have the $1.99 pasta special anymore, it's pretty much just pasta and red sauce, but, hey, $1.99.  Fountain pop/juice or coffee/tea is $1 with unlimited refills while you're dining upstairs.  For those who like fruit juices, the Lingonberry juice is highly recommended!

The Swedish meatballs get the most raves overall - they're alright, but dipping them in Lingonberry jam is a must.  Their mushroom soup is rich, golden and chock full of mushrooms.  I've had some of their other salads and salmon dishes, and while the quality is ok, prices are relatively higher, so I usually stick with the cheaper offerings.

Moms and dads, there's free baby food with purchase of an adult meal, too.  Oh, and they serve WINE.

Downstairs near the exit, there is a little IKEA cafe where you can pick up a frozen yogurt for $1 (or Lingonberry sundae for $1.50), a 75 cent hot dog, $2 cinnamon bun and coffee combo, or $1 drinks to go (the ones upstairs are in mugs and glasses you have to finish drinking there).

The annoying parts are that: 1) it is cafeteria-style, so you line up to get food on a tray and have to clean up after yourself, 2) you have to walk the whole way through the downstairs 'marketplace' before you can get out of there, and 3) there are separate entrance and exit doors, so that no matter where you park your car, you'll always have a bit of a hike either there or back... but a small price to pay for ONE DOLLAR BREAKFAST!!!
Absolutely love this place ... as much for the entertainment value as for the access to a very wide variety of creative products.  So lucky to have an Ikea in Tampa.

I had the worst experience at this store. At first I was really stoked, having found a good deal on a couch. But, when it came time for delivery everything went horribly, horribly wrong. Not only was the line for delivery horrible, the worker was slow and incompetent. He gave me tragically wrong information. I told him I needed a Monday evening delivery. He said he couldn't do that, but that the delivery company would give me the time I needed when they called on Sunday. This was false. The delivery company, when they finally called Sunday night, stated that they do not provide any flexibility on time. When I told them the time they gave me was one I had no hope of making, they had no sympathy and told me to call IKEA to reschedule. By this point, IKEA was closed. By the time I gave up on trying to get a person at IKEA, I was unable to get anyone at the delivery company, even though they were still open. I called first thing in the morning, and they said that they would alert dispatch. They apparently did not. They marked the delivery as me not being home, despite my repeated warnings to them. IKEA insisted I physically go there to reschedule. When I got  there, and after dealing with them for an hour, they then tell me I need to pay a second delivery fee. I refused, and returned the couch. They refused to refund the delivery fee. It was a terrible, upsetting situation. I will never set foot in any IKEA again.

IKEA is not a department store.  It is really an OUTING.  Even if you don't buy any furniture or accessories, it is delightful to wander around and look at the unusual designs and latest trends in European style items.

The food is reasonably priced but the enjoyment part is there are some items that make you realize this is not an American franchise.   Service has always been friendy and helpful.

Fun, fun place! Amazing to see how they create liveable spaces in such tiny areas. Love the market place because there are so many great deals. Happy with all furniture I bought from IKEA, and its easy to assemble.

Let me just start with, I joined my long lost family, IKEA!! I have no idea why they didn't find me in Alaska, where they would've profited greatly by our reunion,". But that's okay, we are here now. If you are remodeling, shopping for a college student, shopping for your first apartment, or just looking for an amazing day, START HERE!! I made the mistake of going to three other stores first in the Philly area. 
I found myself wishing I was Corduroy (the children's book character - a bear) so that I could move in. The prices were reasonable, the products and food right up to date and yummy, and the selection like a kid being in the most giant candy store! I especially want to write that I spent less than $10 on a huge and delicious meal (see pics) and had a great time spending lots of money on super deals and FUN things that are environmentally friendly, reasonably priced and cool to give to my daughter starting school and wonderful gifts to bring home. What more can I say: lonely, girl's day, date? It all works!! Go to Ikea and definitely join the fam. I saved more then $20, I won't tell you what I spent!

Swedish Meatballs.  $2 hot dog combos.  Cinnamon buns.

I admit, 75% of the time that I go to Ikea is just to eat. 

Much bigger, cleaner, and less crowded than the one in South Philly.  PLUS... suburb tax is 6%, compared to the South Philly one with 8% tax.
You walk both floors.  You check out and pay.   Just when you think that you are finished, that smell of cinnamon bun baking !!!! And only $1 you ruin your diet!
Returns here are always a nightmare. Expect 30-35 minutes plus for any issue. On multiple occasions only 2 or 3 of the 5 available customer service registers are ever occupied.

I just moved to Tampa. I called the store in advance to make sure that if I bought furniture it could be delivered same day. I had to go with next day delivery,  no big deal until they delivered the wrong item and it was broken so now 5 days later I'm still sitting on the floor waiting for the correct item to be delivered. Step it up ikea.

I was very surprised to learn that not everything displayed at the store is available.  I have been waiting for over 2 months for one part of an assembly for which we bought all of the parts 2 months ago.  No apologies and no customer service for this issue either
This place is absolutely amazing and the staff is extremely helpful. The largest selection of very interesting and cool designs for your home ! Well worth the trip!

I was very surprised to learn that not everything displayed at the store is available.  I have been waiting for over 2 months for one part of an assembly for which we bought all of the parts 2 months ago.  No apologies and no customer service for this issue either

This Ikea is horrible.  The first time my husband and I ordered furniture from this location we paid for assembly but when our furniture was delivered they said we didn't pay for it even though it was on our receipt.  XPO (their delivery service) Laid out our items and demanded not to out it together.  I showed them our receipt which had proof of assembly paid for and they still declined saying they needed to make sure IKEA was going to pay them and they wouldn't do it because their paperwork didn't show we paid for assembly, mind you I am also 8 months pregnant and they could care less about how rude and inconsiderate they were being. We thought we would  buy a bed a month later which was going to be our last purchase with IKEA and yet again it was a horrible experience.  The mattress had two big stains on it as soon as it was delivered. They proceeded to tell me that I would not get a mattress for 48-72 hours and then told me that the mattress i originally ordered was now sold out.  This store is a piece of crap and honestly not worth spending your money.  I never write bad reviews but this has been such a bad experience I will never go back.

I entered looking for an entertainment center, but left with many more items for my kitchen.  Ok so I have to say it is very difficult to not pick up those little items that scream "don't forget me", "try me", "you sure you don't need another one?".  My fiance and I always find very useful items at incredible prices.  Overall a great one stop shop for household goods.

I was very surprised to learn that not everything displayed at the store is available.  I have been waiting for over 2 months for one part of an assembly for which we bought all of the parts 2 months ago.  No apologies and no customer service for this issue either

My first time setting foot inside an IKEA was yesterday (my sister, who is an IKEA member, invited me as a guest for the pre-opening/practice celebration.). For several months, I heard so many people get excited about St. Louis finally getting an IKEA. This includes people who call themselves 'anti big-box stores', so you know it had to be a big deal. Despite of it all, I still wondered what made some Swedish furniture/goods store better than anything. What was all the hype about? Well, I got to find out four days before it officially opened to the public.

As you step inside from the outdoor parking lot, you'll be entering a big room: parking garage in front, escalators (exit) on right and the entering escalators on the left. You'll be greeted 'Hello!' in Swedish. And then you are on to the Marketplace! Maps, shopping lists and writing utensils are usually provided. It didn't take me long to realize that the place was like a maze. If I wanted to go to a certain department, I would have to cross some other depts to get there. It didn't really sit well with me briefly but I got over it. Plus its great to see what they have anyway. Just about everything they have is low priced....actually, I don't want to go as far as calling it 'cheap', but 'reasonably priced'. I was never told how long the furniture and stuff lasts, but I trust that if its cared for well, then its mighty useful. 

After the marketplace, you'll end up in a huge warehouse-like room. And then, finally the checkout. There are two restaurants and a kids playroom, and the restaurant by the check-out lanes has one that sells inexpensive snacks. Frozen yogurt cones and cinnamon rolls for a $1? Yes please! 2 hot-dog combo and a sodie for $2? Absolutely. This just shows why people love this place; again, for the reasonable prices. My conclusion? IKEA definitely lives up to the hype. 

I hope that this place helps revive St. Louis' economy as it brings more people into the city. I will admit that I'm not too crazy about its location (at the crossroads of Vandeventer and Forest Park Dr), but you never know as only time will tell. Robberies are known to happen in that part of town, so definitely lock up your car! (I don't take cameras seriously...)

Allow yourself plenty of time to look around; I would average it 45-60 minutes if you are curiously shopping!

IKEA has finally arrived in St Louis and they did not disappoint us. I was luck enough to attend the preview opening. Tons of staff on hand to assist with parking. You can spot the staff from the bright yellow shirts that they wear. I have never been to IKEA, after all of the newness wears off, I will go back. One can almost build a house through IKEA. They had bathrooms, they have kitchens, they have bedrooms, they have living rooms and everything to fill them and bonus they are very reasonable priced.  CHECK IT OUT!

I'm thrilled IKEA is finally in STL. I got to visit as part of a friends & family event and they really  made the day fun despite the long waits to get in the door. For those who haven't been before, the store is divided into zones and you can easily hit them all if you just stay on the path with the arrows. On our preview day it took about 1 hour to get from the line through the first 5 zones so expect to spend a lot of time inside. The first five zones are some of the heaviest for displaying full room designs so you can speed up the process if you know what you are looking for.

The top level is nearly all showcase where the bottom level is nearly all pickup. You'll find things like dishes, plants, art, lighting, and decor on the first level for easy pickup. If you kept your list with you then you can go to the self-serve pickup bays and grab your smaller furniture. It's all very easy. The checkouts don't have bags unless you buy them or bring them from home so come prepared.

The IKEA food was pretty good. They ran out of some desserts with all the crowds but I don't see that being a long-term issue. The food court doesn't have a great flow with the crowds so workers were directing us and did a great job of being friendly under pressure. 

Parking is pretty good here. I love the urban model with parking in a garage under the store, just like the IKEA in Atlanta. The entrances off Duncan and Vandeventer aren't being used until the opening crowds pass but again, I don't see this being a problem once the crowds die down and the roads reopen. Just be smart if you are getting off at Boyle or Vandeventer and don't mess with the people who work in the area.

We have always been going to IKEA and were so happy that one opened near us! Everything is so perfect and couldn't  be any better! We went to the grand opening today and it was amazing! Glad we came! Got pictures with manager and overall one of the best IKEA's we've been too!

I love this place!!! Grand Opening Day was a blast! I've been to Ikea in other cities, but having one in St. Louis, is awesome! Cool and unique items for a great price...you have to put some of the stuff together, but it's fun if you're handy. The energy in the store is amazing and I heard the food was good. This store has something for everybody!

Finally a store in St. LOUIS, the have so pretty cool stuff and some very cool displays, to get ideas from!!! IKEA, Thanks for coming to the LOU!!! Store is beautiful and ample parking, covered and lot parking!!!
Great store with great prices. I love the how they make small apartments look so big. Take the trip to visit and believe all the hype.

Such a fun outing. The furniture quality varies from horrible to pretty good, so its great to be able to try before you buy. 
The downstairs with the all the smaller items is my favorite! $1 wine glasses and cocktail glasses can't be beat!
The food court is cool too and the food is pretty dang good!

What can I say...Meatballs, Meatballs, and Meatballs....This is what makes IKEA restaurant very unique and it feels like home when you visit their building. Glad I ended getting a years worth of free meatballs which will come in handy for my future visits.

Oh yeah!!

IKEA! The land where dreams come true...kind of. 

I went to Ikea for the first time this past Sunday evening. My girlfriend recently moved to a new place so I went with her to help her look for something (i.e. desk, bookshelf, stools, lamps, office chair) etc. She was looking for budget friendly items so, of course, Ikea was perfect. 

I act like I know I'm talking about, but this was my first time visiting one. My first impression is that I'm truly blown away by how efficient, large and well staged everything us. They have really fined tuned this whole consumerism thing. Second, yes a lot of stuff at Ikea looks cheap but there are a ton of items that are great deals and you can hardly tell the difference from a higher priced item elsewhere. 

The staff was all super friendly and smiley despite being the end of their miserable opening weekend. I ended up getting a some decorations and a houseplant despite not looking for anything in particular. Maybe one day I'll come back and try the food ;)

I love this IKEA. It is huge, and has a fantastic showroom. I find it easy to navigate, and I have rarely had an issue with items being out of stock. The prices are fair and the staff is friendly and helpful. 

The cafeteria is a great spot to grab a bite.  The food is okay - but it hits the spot.

They suck. Went to purchase some things, that I looked at a month ago, and they put "new" on everything and doubled thier prices! 
I am pssed!
I bought a couch and it felt like putting together a puzzle. Their Swedish meatballs are actually Italian, like honestly.

Since I don't need any furniture (we could not put it together anyway), we decided to stop by for lunch.  We figured on a Tuesday, it wouldn't be that crowded.  WRONG!  It was packed. They have outdoor and indoor parking.  After going upstairs, there was a place called Smallville for children to play in.  I'm not sure if you were able to leave your kids while you shopped, so I would check that out.

This was my first time at an IKEA and we both wanted to try their Swedish meatballs.  We went upstairs and got in line.  It was an organized line and when you reached the end, Jordan would tell you whether to wait or what food line to get into.  From one line to another.  Surprisingly, it really didn't take that long to go through either line.  I was amazed to see how many children were there.  Then a sign informed me that on Tuesdays, with the purchase of one adult meal, you received two children's meals for free.  What a deal that is.  

Since everyone raves about the Swedish meatballs, both of us got them and Mike added on with macaroni and cheese and a Swedish apple cake.  I would have like to add the cream cake with marzipan, but they were no where in site. The meatballs came with mashed potatoes and a little cranberry sauce(?) and gravy for $4.99.  With a soft drink, the total for one person came to $7.04.  If you are watching your calories, without the soft drink there were 550 calories in the dish.  They also had chicken meatballs, veggie meatballs, chicken tenders and a few different wraps and salmon plates.  The meatballs were everything people said they were.  Do they have Swedes somewhere making these meatballs?  The mac n cheese was standard fare, and the apple cake was good but a little to cold for me.  When we left, Jordon must have been taking a break because the line was getting a little out of hand.  They also have a frozen food section where you can buy some to take home along with other frozen foods.

We didn't really explore all the areas but I'm sure that if you need anything, you can find it here. They do sell so much more than furniture.  I'm thinking I may need a new refrigerator.

Horrible service. Waited for an hour for a single item, because it came from the kitchens department, the staff had to pick it. No sense of urgency at all, very disappointing. 3 people standing at the counter doing absolutely nothing but leaning on it...where is the management in this place, probably eating meatballs in the cafeteria! Unbelieveable!!!! They need to supply beds in the kitchens waiting area so we can nap, the couches are full with sleeping customers. They've probably been here since lunch time. Wake up, Ikea!

Very glad to have this store in our area!  Thanks to the big blue & yellow box company for deciding that STL was a good place to open a store.  There are numerous metropolitan areas that will wait years to get their own Ikea.

Stopped by on a weekday afternoon - certainly a much better idea than going during a weekend shortly after their opening.  Even on a Tuesday afternoon there were still thousands of people in the place.  Maybe once things settle down somewhat an obvious best time to shop there will become evident.  

We really like their tableware.  We've had our current stuff for a while now and it was time to replace some of it due to wear and the fact that we would like to have more flatware.  Accomplished both on today's visit.  We also needed a better way to organize some things in our kitchen and solved that problem today as well.

Sometime in the next year we will remodel our laundry room and plan to get the cabinets from Ikea as well.

Left with a couple of packages of cinnamon rolls that proceeded to smell up my car and make me droll a bit while driving home with them in the vehicle.  A half-dozen of those yummy things for $4 is a steal any day of the week!

IKEA definitely is a shop till you drop type store. This store has everything you'll ever need for your home. If you cannot find it at IKEA, chances are you may not need it. I have never been to an IKEA, so I was blown away by the massive variety and selections available. I was also amazed at the prices, they totally put discount retailers like Wal-Mart to shame. 

Normally, I am not a fan of RTA (ready to assemble) furniture, but I think IKEA may win me over.  I like the fact that you can go to their website, click on the instructions for the item you are considering and see how difficult the assembly will be. 

The housewares department is by far my favorite. So many gadgets and gizmos to make your kitchen complete. They also have a great selection of pots and pans, dishes and flatware. I was shocked to see that they also sell appliances. I fell in love with one of the gas ranges. 

You may be able to shop till you drop here, but shop wisely and keep in mind, "You get what you pay for". The prices may be rock bottom low, but take a look at the quality before putting it in your cart. 

IKEA is a great addition to the city, I'm glad they choose the city over a county location. It now gives those county residents another reason besides our sports teams to come downtown.

* My 900th Review on Yelp

This place has everything. Prices are very reasonable. Everything is coordinated by the rooms. 

Parking lot & the store is huge, it almost seems like you're walking into theme park. 

You almost need to take two to three trips to see everything in detail. This is not "in and out" store it takes you through all 26 sections before exiting. 

Love the store.

I mean, it's Ikea. There's decent food that's cheap, great deals on everything you could possibly need for your home with a wide range of price points. The furniture all requires assembly but the design is very good and the prices are great.

This was my first visit to an IKEA, and I wasn't disappointed. After finding out that there was going to be an IKEA in St. Louis and seeing it slowly go up (along with the hype built up from all of my out of town friends), I was excited when I finally got to check it out. 

I will start with some useful tips as a newcomer to IKEA that I learned through my visit.

Some useful TIPS for people relatively new to IKEA:
1. If you don't want to, or don't have the time to go through the majority of the store, you can go straight to the warehouse by going right instead of up the stairs as soon as you get in.
2. You can look online for the items you want and write the item number down and location so when you go to the store you can go directly to the warehouse and find the location of the item in the warehouse and pick it up. A lot faster than going through the store.
3. There are shortcuts in the main store that you can take to go through faster.
4. Take advantage of the free pencil and paper to write down the item number and location of what you want to buy.

The first thing that I noticed when I got there was that it was very crowded. It was the second weekend since it opened, so I wasn't surprised. I was pleasantly surprised at how well staffed they were. They even hired event staff to direct people to open parking spots. There was literally a person along the parking every 20 yards. It almost seemed like overkill, but I didn't mind. The inside was also crowded, but there seemed to be sufficient staff to help the customers (I did have to wait about 10 minutes to have a question answered about a bed frame, but that was because I didn't try to find another open employee).

The following two paragraphs describe the layout, for those who have never been to an IKEA.

The inside of the store is designed so that you have to go through the majority of the store before exiting. The first part of the store is designed in a show room style. You walk through different sections of the store divided by the room the furniture is for (ie: living room, dining room, bathroom, etc.). They have designed show rooms where you can either purchase everything in the room, if you like their design (I can't see myself doing this), or you can pick out any item in the room and write down the number. This number and location will help you find and pick it up later on in the warehouse.
The second half of the store is more like a traditional store where you have a traditional shopping cart and can grab any item as is and put it in your cart. This section obviously consists of smaller items that you can actually carry in a cart. 

I ended up buying a couple of things during my first trip. It was actually really fun putting the furniture together with my girlfriend (everything comes in parts to assemble from IKEA). 

I will definitely be back here just to try out the food court and the meatballs, as it was too crowded when I went. And of course if I need more furniture. :D

I love ikea, going there always makes me giddy knowing we're getting things for our first place! Lots of cheap modern looking furniture at a decent price. So far the bed that we have from ikea is wonderful and we're looking forward to getting our tv stand and bookcase setup sometime this week, I will just say that sometimes the instruction can be a little hard to follow and I'm always missing a random part. Other than that, ikea is awesome and def my go to store for any home goods or furniture.

It's IKEA.... It's not like we are talking Saks! You get what you pay for & that's that. If you want high end then go somewhere else. Service has gotten scarce in past years. There used to be at least 1-2 people per department. Now finding one in any area can be hard!

I've been to many IKEAs, this one's a little bit off the beaten path coming from Clearwater. Every IKEA of course is different, I think it's hard to mess up a show room, so essentially just boils down to the cafeteria and the amount of foods available for purchase down by the cashiers.

The lines were too bad but then again I went on a Monday night. My only complaint is that a lot of the bulk candy they were out of. And there was no way to ring me up in the food section so I had to go over to the cashier deli part where they serve hot dogs and ice cream and be rung up.
Absolutely love Ikea.  Good thing it is not that close to my house or else I would be there all the time.

I have been to Ikea before as they had one where I lived before.  I love Ikea and couldn't wait to get a chance to go.  I had several items in my cart but was trying to find one more thing. After asking 4 people and being sent on a wild goose chase, I left my cart and walked out.  I have never come across such a group of rude people in a retail store. On the drive home, I was thinking maybe they're just busy and overwhelmed but....they better get it together. IKEA is ALWAYS busy!  This is just the beginning. It doesn't slow down!
Beautiful store.  Found what I needed. Had a bit of a mouse in a maze feeling trying to find my way to checkout. Love the products. I like to be able to get out quickly & that doesn't happen here.

IKEA's products are cute like Target but it costs about as much as WalMart. It makes me happy -- mostly. 

I'd never been to an IKEA until the beginning of October. Now I've been twice. The store is a bit daunting and it's still really crowded on the weekends, but now I know better than to arrive at 1 p.m. on a Saturday as I did on my second visit. I spent about 2 hours there on my first visit, but unless I'm making some big decisions or purchases, I don't think it'll take me longer than an hour on future visits. That's good, because every time I return from IKEA, about 5 hours later I want to go back and get this or that. 

Yes, they have nearly everything at IKEA, but not necessarily the best range in a product or the greatest quality, so you have to be careful. I bought a magnifying makeup mirror for only $20 and was so excited! Well, the light isn't very strong and it only magnifies to 3x, which I hadn't realized isn't very much. I've already ordered and received a 7x mirror with a stronger light from Amazon, and it's also larger than IKEA's, for a few dollars more than IKEA's. I like the bathroom rug and various jars I purchased. They have great details on candles.  

RTA furniture is not my style. I don't buy particleboard. I'm at antiques stores or Carol House because I like nice things. (If you think that's dorky, you should hear me at a Wehrenberg. Wehrenberg.) IKEA's metal shelving, however, is so me. 

They have a final sale section near the cash registers. I'll be checking that out every time. 

IKEA is a welcome addition to my STL shopping experience. If they sold clothes, I would about have it made.

I was in awe at the size of this place. Another warehouse shopping house, but they have very good prices and have their showrooms set up with wonderful ideas. I'll be going back for some of the items that have been put on a list. I will be updating my bathroom in the future and have found the right sink cabinet, cute decor and even the most simple of items that are very useful.

What can I say about Ikea that hasn't been said? I visited the brand new location in St. Louis, and LOVED every second of it. There was very friendly staff around to help, and treasures galore to be discovered. 

Checkout lines went quickly, bathrooms were clean, and the parking garage provided plenty of available spots for our Sunday morning shopping spree. 

I'll be back, Ikea, on my next visit!

This is my favorite store. I like everything about it, including:
1. The recycling cans
2. The car loading docks
3. How everything is organized- you can easily find the bin number 
4. The price of the items
5. The checkout line isn't too slow especially since so many people are there
6. The clearance section ;)
7. The cart escalator and the big elevators
8. The delicious food
I can't think of any more right now but I'm sure there are some. 

IKEA is more for people that need a bunch of stuff rather than Target or whatever else. 

IKEA is awesome.

I have been to many Ikea's in my lifetime and all in different states and cities. I have to say that they did a very good job at designing this Ikea for St. Louis. 

I love the parking garage first of all. I love the option of parking underground when its snowing or raining outside and I don't have to haul a huge box in the temperamental weather we have here. 

I love the large food court and the layout. The servers and staff are incredibly friendly and nice and happy. If you have a family membership card you get a free coffee or tea so remember to take advantage of that.

I think the location is perfect. I have had a lot of county friends and family complain about it being close to the city BUT an ikea is always close to the metro area and downtowns. You do not see an Ikea in the middle of the fields like where the outlets are.....no its in the city for a reason, to cater to the city dwellers actually living in 500sqft.

I love this ikea, I really do I love it even more than the one in Northern California.

Worst experience ever. Tried to gather necessary parts of a desk I wanted only to find out that the pieces were still wrapped in plastic on a palette two selves up. Ask if the crew of store stockers could take them down as they were all standing around doing nothing beside a fork lift. Was told the store doesn't allow operations like that during store hours because fork lift drivers kept crashing into things and that they might get to it that night if they didn't forget. Stupid store policy, awful costumer service. Get some competent operators so you can work efficiently when you're supposed to.

It's so exciting to have an Ikea in St. Louis, especially since it's actually IN TOWN, not a 45 minute drive to the burbs (that's how it is in Cincinnati)! I even decided to check out the grand opening - a band played and there were all sorts of big-wigs there to make speeches. I got a $10 gift card when I entered and began my exploration.

I'm really excited to go back with my husband so we can continue to live our real life romantic comedy and play house in all the example apartments, kitchens and bathrooms. But just going on my own, I enjoy the kitchen sections and clearance more than anything. I ended up using my gift card on a set of new glasses that I simply love!

I feel like this place is full of surprises! Be prepared to look at everything and find things you didn't expect. 

I haven't eaten at an Ikea in years, but I remember going for breakfast once and really enjoying their french toast sticks - it was like being in elementary school again! I look forward to trying their famous meatballs at some point and taking home other interesting treats!

The husband and I went here to price out some new kitchen cabinets. I really like how Ikea has literally everything we want, but it's always a bugger to meander through every single department, especially when we are under a slight time restraint. The pricing seems odd, but that's because it's all completely separate: Cupboards, then doors, then hinges, then hardware. It gets overwhelming, but the 25 year guarantee is very appealing. I guess we will see how it goes when it comes time to get them!

Holy crap, IKEA is amazing!
I decided to drop by a few days after their opening day. This place was still packed with people.
This place is a huge blue and yellow furniture and home decorating superstore with tons of different things to see and experience. 
All of the products displayed were arranged much like an art museum. Parking was very easy as they had several security people outside directing traffic.
They had greeters outside and a live band outside. There was a DJ also inside. Prices on most of their products were also pretty affordable. 
Also there was a section where you could get Swedish food. I probably would have bankrupted myself buying all the Swedish candy alone.
The cafeteria was also very affordable. $1 for breakfast. $2 for lunch. And $3 for dinner. I don't think Costco could even beat that. 
It's definitely a place that I would come back to if I needed new furniture if not to get stuffed on Swedish food.

I wanted to update my review. I LOVE Ikea! I love the showrooms! I love my new desk and duvet covers! The cafeteria just serves crappy food. I like to go downstairs by the EXIT and get a hot dog or a frozen yogurt. The food isn't healthy, but it's cheap and taste better.

There's several flags that read "Ikea" in the front, as if the building itself wasn't enough to grab the attention of St. Louis. IKEA is an experience. That is their brand. Cafeteria style eating area - Swedish meatballs better than the veggie quinoa, but the attempt was appreciated. $18 for a meal for 2. I would come for the palm selection, even though there were more fake plants than real. Lamp selection was limited for the size of the place, but they had single bulb hanging lights for under $10 and other industrial stand up lamp worth going for. I was eyeing the shoes and clothes and the mock set-ups more than the furniture. Closets were impressive. In all, Ikea's not really my style. I left with just the $1.79 candle. Still go. Personally, I'd rather spend $ in a West Elm - if not resell / antique.

My husband and I had a great time shopping/eating here. We probably wouldn't visit on a weekend again - this place is gigantic - however the crowd was gigantic as well. Airport speed ramps would fit right in. Wear comfy shoes! 

This store is unbelievably well planned. There are flow-chart location signs above the walkways and QR codes with corresponding videos of merchandise. For the first-time visitor, the signs aren't perfectly planned, though; we went the wrong way twice to exit and check out. There is a big play area for kids at the entrance and over-sized, tactile toys fixed to the floor throughout the different departments. You should go to the second floor first to look at tons of displays, then shop on the first floor based on what you're interested in. 

I took a double take on some of the prices. $20 for a sturdy, adorable stool-type chair perfect for a young person's apartment. $40 for a trendy, suspended lamp with a knit shade. Personally, it's unlikely I would ever furnish my entire living space with IKEA. If I were shopping for a leather couch, for instance, I wouldn't expect IKEA's version for $1,000 to compete with those lifetime "investments" at other stores for thousands more. But I will definitely be a regular customer for storage items, textiles, kids' furniture, and more. 

One of the best things about IKEA is their space-saving designs. They have pseudo "apartments" (one is approx. 270 sq ft, another is approx. 700 sq feet, etc) to showcase IKEA's knack for maximizing any square footage of space. Some items expand (even children's beds) and there are lots of shallow shelving units.

The displays are inspiring and fun. On the other hand... yikes, we saw some shoppers sprawled out on the furniture with dirty clothes. Other people opened cabinets or handled merchandise like bulls in a china shop. What in the heck. And what modern store would be complete without a little kid here and there with no parent in sight? (Isn't it odd that these are the kiddies who never get kidnapped?) 

My husband doesn't like shopping but he didn't get antsy here until the 3-hour mark. That is yuge. About halfway through, we stopped in the cafeteria. You grab a tray and slide it along like high school. It's efficient with only a few entree choices to choose from. The portions aren't very big and my sons would probably eat two or three, but the prices are about $5 or $6.  

Chicken meatballs: good  
Mashed potatoes: great 
Vegetable medallion: great
Unnamed, round, strawberry, cream-filled cake with pink icing: killer

The cake was $1.50. Psst, IKEA: I would pay $5.00 to eat that again.

They could definitely have used more cashiers. There were at least 30 people in line and only one cashier. Before we had paid, two cashiers were added, but so were about 75 people ordering.

While shopping, the staff can be tough to track down. I didn't notice any stations or something to find them whenever we had questions about merchandise. Each time, we wandered around to eventually find someone. Surely there is an app for that. 

An IKEA kitchen is probably in our future, thanks to those displays. Question is, will we assemble it ourselves or pay someone to do it? I googled that question and one of the first results was entitled, "Assembling IKEA Furniture Will Destroy Your Relationship."

It's really fun to have an IKEA in St. Louis. Honestly, I wouldn't go on the weekend because I hate crowds, but otherwise I love it. The cafe is fun, and there's always some cool (and cheap) house stuff to impulse buy. 

My inner-urbanist absolutely hates that big parking lot out front, but otherwise it's a great addition to the city. 

Also, watch you head when you're in those room models--I hit mine a couple times on different objects...so many objects!
Went to Ikea at 6:00 on a Friday evening. Surprisingly empty. This is definitely the time to go if you do not want to deal with the crowds found on Saturday and Sunday.

Yeah for IKEA arriving in STL!!!!!  LOVE LOVE LOVE this place!

In case you didn't know, IKEA also has a cafeteria.  The food is not out of this world, but the prices are amazing!  If you're shopping and need a little break, check it out on the top floor.  Huge breakfast for $1???  Yeah - not bad!

Sign up for their loyalty card and you get a free coffee every time you shop as well as many other discounts!

I am so very excited St. Louis finally has an IKEA.  It is a destination that you can spend hours inside no matter the weather.  The St. Louis location has some work to do, it is not operating like a well oiled machine as of yet.  It would benefit you to study the floor plan before you arrive.  Skip the showroom or take a short cut to what you actually need.  

The BEST part of IKEA are the products under the $20.00 price point.  Inventive, cute, funny, space saving, cheap things you really do need.  Candles and Picture Frame prices are better than most other places.  Kitchen gadgets, coffee mugs, party napkins- SCORE!   Polka-dot rugs for $19.99. I am not in the market for IKEA type furniture, but they have some impressive displays on how to make small spaces work.   

For some reason the food at IKEA is getting WAY more press than it deserves.   The Cafe opens daily at 9:30 am.  Coffee is free until 10:00 am.  Free coffee and a $1 cinnamon roll are a good way to get into the store BEFORE opening time.  That is where the food at IKEA should be kept, only as a plan to shop early.   The lunch was terrible.   The line was too long for terrible food.   We had not planned on lunch there and should have left.  Also, there are no to-go coffee or soda cups, bring your own cup in for the showroom and marketplace.  

Check out had it's issues.   I was overcharged  for three items and it took quite a while for two employees to get the refund correct.   They forgot to scan my IKEA family card and could never get it applied to the purchase.  Not necessarily the employees fault, however there were not enough employees in any department from food to check out to handle issues.  Seems staffing could, and should, be better on a weekend before the Holiday Season.

Still happy to have IKEA in the STL.   Everyone should go at least once.

I don't see why everyone loves IKEA. The place is like a tiny maze and people are EVERYWHERE. It was hard to even move from displays because there were so many people.

The furniture looked like dorm furniture. Everything was small like European furniture and seemed to be horrible quality. I'm not sure I would put anything from there in my house.

I live in a real house so I want real furniture for it. Not doll house sized couches.

I was forced into stopping by the new IKEA on a Sunday afternoon. I came, I saw, I moved in the same direction as the rest of the herd, and I doubt I will be back.  I had been to one before so I knew exactly what to expect except that as others have mentioned this one seems to be understaffed and not quite as efficient as others because I didn't get that "move them in and move them out" feel I had previously.  Never have I seen so many people gawking at such well designed and poorly made mass produced home goods. 

The positive of the experience for me was a stop at the bulk candy bins on the way out. Lots of gummy candy varieties and licorices for $7.99 per pound. Love that but hate the 2 moms blocking the entire thing with their shopping carts.  If you love the experience then more power to you...I can't hang.

We visited IKEA opening week. Who knew that an approach to a furniture store could feel like TSA security at an airport terminal parking garage? Who knew that a furniture store could be laid out like a museum, with galleries of exhibits? Who knew that the downstairs of said furniture "museum" could open up into a warehouse like the one where the ark of the covenant is stored at the end of National Treasure? And, who knew, best of all, that all around the checkouts you could buy lots of sugary carbs, like jams and gluten-free cakes? We left with food rather than furniture, having enjoyed our visit to Swedish Disneyland.

The design of this store is one-way, so you have to go through almost everything they designed for you. Stuff were standard IKEA, no more comments. Staff were friendly to help you.

I bought two beds (one wood, one iron), two spring mattresses, and some beddings 4 months ago. Right now I am very satisfied with both beds and the beddings, but not so satisfied with the spring mattresses. They seem to degrade very fast, and I wonder after a year or two will I still be able to sleep on them.

Kinda cool with parking on the first level, then take an escalator up to start shopping or have a meal.  I've only been here to have lunch so far so can't comment on much else.  I would definitely recommend the Swedish meatballs; they let me sub mac-n-cheese to replace mashed potatoes.

The much anticipated, obligatory IKEA review. This is for all of you IKEA newbies like myself. 

First, the store is mega huge- I'm talking Home Depot ate Lowes with a big parking garage underneath big. So go with an open mind, comfortable shoes, pen & paper to take notes and smart phone to snap pics. Here are some tips:

1. Get there at 9:30am. 30 min. before store opens you can go up to the cafe and get free coffee and a very cheap but very delicious breakfast. You can also start shopping early. 
2. Snap pics of items you like/want on the top floor that are in all the little display areas. Because you'll later have to find that same item downstairs in the inventory section and this can be daunting.
3. Go with the flow. There are lighted arrows on the floor showing the direction you should travel. Do not go against the tide. You'll be sorry, fair warning! (Yes it happened to me) 
4. Go with friends. Not too many but a couple of your best gal pals- sorry guys but this place is mostly for the  ladies. Because no one can see everything and your friends will point out cute stuff you miss and vice versa. 

I really enjoyed my visit. Found some great little gadgets I couldn't live without for an extremely cheap price. AND finally got to say I went to an Ikea! 

I can't say I've exactly drunk the IKEA kool-aid but it was a fun adventure that I hope to repeat soon!

IKEA is rather therapeutic, who else loses track of time inside? Seriously. I enter at 11AM and can walk back out at 2-3PM unknowingly. 

*Bring bags for your items at checkout, otherwise you have to buy them. 

First stop at IKEA though? SWEDISH MEATBALLS. Everyone must check out their dining area located above the floor you walk in on.

After a happy stomach, let the adventure begin! Everything is well organized, designed, and clean inside. Whether you want to take the journey slow or fast, there are paths that ensure you see everything on the floor or you can take the shortcuts if you follow the signs to get your checklist accomplished. There are two floors total. 

At checkout, enjoy your purchases, and a delightful $1 ice cream cone on your way out!

I really love Ikea for furniture and household shopping. They have such inspirational set ups and ideas that it's hard not to overhaul my house everytime I visit! I really like that the furniture is customizable. My husband and I bought an entertainment center at their Seattle/Renton location about 2 years ago that we customized by adding doors and drawers and an additional segment. Just this past week, we went back to find a cabinet for the set of China we received from his grandparents and hoped to find something that we could also use to increase shelving for our books and DVDs.  We were able to get a cabinet set that matched the entertainment center (Besta) and were able to customize the number of shelves, add glass doors, and make it our own. My only complaint about IKEA furniture is that it is made with engineered wood and particle board instead of hardwood, but honestly, I will take their versatility over hardwood most days.

Love this place. Furniture is "assemble yourself" that is great quality, price and everything has been super easy to assemble. Get so many compliments on ALL of our furniture and accessories that we've bought from here

I totally love IKEA! I love how so many things they have often have more than one type of use or are just efficient in design. Very smart stuff sometimes. I love the prices, too. I just recently redecorated my living/dining room and got three pictures, two throws, a rug, curtains and a chandelier for about $200 and it looks super awesome! They have a kids play area. They have a huge cafeteria with really good food. One word: MAC-A-RONI! That stuff is the best macaroni I have ever had. I heart it! Or course they have the show rooms upstairs and the rest of the stuff downstairs that lead to the warehouse. Most of the stuff is really easy to put together. The only two things that bother me are #1: I really wish they had stuff in English. It makes it very difficult to ask for something by the Swedish name and so I really don't like that. And #2: I think they should make it easier to go into the first floor and skip the 2nd floor altogether. I usually have to go through a checkout lane and then through the warehouse and then to the stuff on the 1st floor. If you go through the main entrance, there is no way to get there. You have to go upstairs and then downstairs. It's just a little annoying, minor really. There's a loading area for larger stuff and there's employees to help out.

This isn't a furniture store IT'S A COMPLEX! 

Wowzers...I finally made it by this infamous IKEA and I must admit the rumors have done no justice. This place is amazing. Offering everything your life needs:

Daycare for all the baby mama shoppers 
Lockers for safekeeping 
Groceries 
Full restaurant 
Kitchen décor
Dining ensembles 
Bathroom necessities 
Children's rooms 
Closest assortments 
Living Room furniture 
Bedroom furnishings 
Accessories such as rugs, lamps, dishes, flatware, mirrors, storage consoles, appliances, throws, accent pillows, lighting, knobs, cooking utensils, glassware, desk, house slippers, luggage, teddy bears and so much more I'm just fresh out of typing energy.

Plenty of lot parking with easy signage to navigate you through the complex. There's also a parking garage so you don't get wet on rainy days (we all know sugar melts). 

Customer service reps are readily available throughout the entire store to answer any questions (I noticed you don't even have to ask for assistance) if you stand still and look slightly puzzles an IKEA rep comes to you and ask if you need help. 

I love this place...can't wait until the recession is over so I can go shopping on all 3 levels. 

~Christy

I took the plunge down the rabbit hole to explore the big blue box some call a Wonderland. 

There were many positives about IKEA that lend to a decent review. They had lots of merchandise, helpful staff, yummy cinnamon smells piped through the store, beautiful displays, and ample parking (both in an outdoor lot and covered underground garage!). 

However, there were also a few things about the blue box that just gave me the blues. For one, I found the kitchen merchandise to be a little pricey. Also, if you're looking for a few small items with a quick in and out visit, this is probably not your stop. The store is so huge, and a 15 minute shopping trip elsewhere took 45 minutes here - and unfortunately they were out of the main item I was looking for. Finally, as I left the store, that delicious cinnamon smell from the food court area turned into an awful stale cigarette stench on the exit escalator. They really need to clean up that area and ventilate it better. It was my last impression of our IKEA, and it took 30 minutes to get that awful smell out of my head.

Overall, I'm so glad to have the store in our city, but personally I'm not going to be spending a lot of time there. I'm sure I'll go back, but it will be limited visits. My wallet will thank me for that. To make up for my personal lack of enthusiasm, I'll encourage all my friends who love IKEA to shop there. They probably won't mind the things that bothered me. 

Welcome to the Lou, blue box. Best of luck! I'll upgrade you to 4 stars once you fix that stinky stale cigarette smell at the exit. Then maybe you'll be more of the Wonderland I've heard so much about.

First timer!
We ate first and I thought it was just ok. Went really hungry so we got the Swedish meatballs, chicken tenders, fries, Mac n cheese,salad and chick pea soup. 
Everything was just ok. Not a big fan of cafeteria style because things sit and get served almost cold. 
On to the shopping. Every thing looks good. My husband and I got some good ideas. It's a great place to get cheep candles, picture frames and lamps.
All in all I will be back
Restaurant was ok. Fun to window shop! After lots of walking, it wasn't fun to wait in the very slow lines (only 3 open) to buy two items. Tiring, but an different experience worth doing once.
I love this place! I come here for their Swedish meatballs and home decors! and they have a bunch of DIY organizers and I usually get ideas from them. Glad they finally have it here in Tampa!

As a life-long SAAB and Volvo owners the store has always had a special place in my heart. Swedish clean lines and utilitarianism at its best. Coupled with all the kitchen gadgets how can you miss?

Over the years, we have lived near both Philly locations and Baltimore too. Glad to see one made it to the gateway city. 

While the furniture never makes its way to our home it does not prevent us from finding other items. 

Go spend half your day in the blue and yellow world of IKEA you will not regret it.

This was my first time ever in an Ikea, so I really didn't know what to expect. We had a couple hours to burn on a Saturday, so decided to stop by the Ikea and look around, and maybe grab lunch as we had heard they had food there.

Well, when we walked in my first impression was that this place is really big and really clean and orderly looking. The cafeteria was right by the entrance/exit, so we decided to stop in there first and check it out. They were still serving breakfast when we got there, and wow, the prices were really cheap! $1 cinnamon rolls and breakfast with eggs and sausage. They had another breakfast plate with Swedish pancakes for a couple dollars more. It was really good, and for a few bucks, we ate quite a bit!

Then we started walking through this labyrinth of home furnishings. get ready to walk, because this place is huge! It really keeps going, and there is literally everything you can think of that would go in a normal home. most of the stuff is really modern and clean looking, and the prices were a lot more reasonable than I expected. 

Well 3 hours later... We finally made our way towards the exit, but we decided to stop by the cafe once more, this time for a $5 plate of Swedish meatballs with mashed potatoes. We had heard that was something worth trying. I thought they were just ok. Good, but not great. 

 My first Ikea experience was interesting, and they had a lot of really nice stuff. I plan on coming back and buying a few things soon.
Pretty amazing place.  Gigantic warehouse and unique environment is the best way to describe it.  Surprisingly good prices relative to the high quality.

I am not sure how I lived in Tampa for so long and am just now discovering IKEA. My husband and I just opened up our own business and needed lots of furniture that was sturdy but inexpensive. I was in heaven when I finally checked out IKEA. The prices are amazing and for the price, the quality is decent. I do find the layout annoying as you are forced to pretty much wander through the entire store to get to any department. This forced marketing is probably effective for them as I inevitably run into something that "I had to have but never knew I needed." This makes going to IKEA a laborious process as you can never just run in and out. 

I was told by my business minded husband that IKEA keeps their prices low by making the customer assemble all of the furniture themselves. The Swedish company makes the furniture, boxes them up into easily shipped boxes and then they are on display in their expansive warehouse stores. So each time I buy a piece and open it up, I am greeted by a cartoon man who in place of written instructions shows me how to put things together in very animated cartoon actions. Sometimes he has a very angry look on his cartoon face and a there is a big X on the a part of the lamp that I am putting together. I know this means I shouldn't do something but what exactly is sometimes a mystery. Whatever, it is, it makes the little cartoon man very upset so I really try not to do whatever he is trying to tell me. It can be stressful. 

All in all, I love this store. The prices are great and the quality is good enough depending on what you need the items for. However, if you are looking for luxury pieces that you can pass onto the next generation, I probably would not get those pieces from here as I don't think they would last through decades of use.

I've only been to IKEA in California until this one opened. I love IKEA. I love seeing items on display for ideas and the ridiculously low prices. My husband likes to assemble the furniture. 

We stopped here on a whim when passing by on a Saturday evening. Parking was easy - we got a spot right in front. It was the least crowded IKEA I have ever been to! We walked right through the checkout line and out the door. It was clean and large (with covered structured parking as well).

Where to begin, this place is amazing. For all the interior decorators around town this is the place to go. They have everything you could ever imagine for a home from towels, kitchen stuff, furniture, to plants, etc. The food is also amazing. We had Swedish meat balls with mashed potatoes and Mac and cheese. All was very good. The one thing we didn't like was the apple pie we tried. But it was still a good experience. I would go back a million times and spend a lot of money in the future here. 

Cleanliness: 10/10
Employees: 7/10 (the lady in the cafeteria messed up our order and made no effort to fix it, she just said her manager had to fix it but she just left the room so it would be inconvenient to ask her back in)
Environment: 10/10

Hair hair everywhere! My husband and I were excited about the super cheap breakfast, but were disappointed to find human hair stuck to the tables and chairs. I believed this to be a static issue, but when I found a big long hair tucked in my swedish pancake, I decided that Ikea must be moonlighting as a barber shop after hours. Great merchandise that lives up to the hype, but avoid the cafeteria.

Awesome store! 
Went while visiting my mom with my husband. Went through the whole maze and looked at just about everything. Amazing prices for things you'd hope to get for a new house or wedding or while remodeling your house! Will definitely come back when we decide to buy a house. Bought some things for our apartment already, great for reorganizing your whole home. Loved that there's a restaurant/cafe inside, it's basically cafeteria style but decently good for the prices you get it for. 
Mom loves the gluten free stuff at the little market at the end of the store by the cafe.

This place is a little PACK.  But that will only be right now.  Seriously Love IKEA, and they did a great job on this one! 

BTW you can get FREE coffee if you go in early!

It's the same Ikea you'd find anywhere in the world. However, I like this branch much better than my previous branch in Brooklyn because there's tons of available parking, it's not nearly as crowded, and the staff are much more pleasant to deal with. The bathrooms were a bit on the disgusting side, but that was the sole downside of the afternoon. 

In the end, instead of leaving haggard and irritated we left in good time and got our shopping done without much fuss. All around good Ikea experience.

IKEA is an experience. There is no "run in and grab something" here. You could spend HOURS here, walking around and looking at things. I recently came to this location for the first time. I had a couple objectives: return a crib mattress that was recalled; get a new crib mattress to replace it; and look at high chairs. My mother in law came and wanted to look for stocking stuffers. We ended up being here for 2-3 hours. 

It was not that busy on the Friday afternoon before Christmas. We were helped pretty quickly at customer service. The person helping us was not very with it. Couldn't find the mattress and just kept pecking around on the computer while I stood there. Took a minute out to hug and chat with two people who came up to say hi. Uhhh ok. I'm waiting here for FOREVER for you and you're hugging. Annoying. Finally she "found" it and gave me store credit. I'm pretty sure she didn't find it because I know the range in which I paid and she refunded me about $40 more than that. Ok then. 

We went and found the baby stuff and stocked up. It's so cheap! We spent a long time on the lower level where the small stuff is, getting more items. We ended in the warehouse, where we got the mattress and high chair. We were helped quickly when we couldn't find what we needed there. 

The cashier went quickly and I left spending only $10 on top of my store credit, and with many items. IKEA is cheap. I like cheap. It was fun, and I'll be back.

Good store, usually tidy, helpful staff. They never seem to be out of stock of things, which is my pet peeve for other large stores in St. Louis.

One unique thing is that they have items across many scales of quality. There are items for every budget and price range here. Some are beautiful and high-end, while others offer more value.

IKEA is an event that you must experience by coming to one!! The quality of the merchandise is very good! If you are not handy with putting things together, they can do it for you for a nominal charge! Also, while you are at IKEA, the food is pretty good!!

Oh how I missed IKEA. This store and its location are wonderful. Easy access of HWY 40/64, plenty of parking, small land child care:) & excellent customer service. 

It took us approximately 2 hours from start to check out to get through the whole store which we expected. We cannot wait to go back and check out the cafeteria.

If my review were just about their products and the portion of the store prior to checkout, I'd give Ikea a solid four stars.  However, the ancillary services and checkout really drag them down to a place that makes me not want to come back.

First, the products.  Some are great; five stars all the way.  However, some of their furniture/decor products really are garbage, so that detracts from the experience.  Fortunately, those are usually easy to spot and avoid.

Regarding the store itself, let's focus first on the showroom side.  This place is massive, and if you're just there to browse and want to take it all in, you can easily spend an hour or more just walking the store and checking everything out.  It's organized logically so you're able to focus on specific rooms of your home as you work your way through.  Upstairs is mostly large items; furniture, beds, mattresses, kids, etc.  Downstairs is mostly the smaller home accessory and organization products.

As you work your way through, if you want something, make sure you note down exactly what it is you want, including dimensions, and the red tag numbers below the item name, size and price.  Many of their items come in a variety of sizes, such as desk tops, and vary considerably in price if you get the wrong one or don't remember which one you wanted.  The red tag tells you which aisle and column you can find the one or more pieces you need to put that item together.  Beware that some items come in multiple boxes and it may not be immediately obvious if you don't notice the (1) and (2) on the boxes.  In the warehouse area, there will be  a box count listed on the item tag on the storage shelving.
