Everything is downhill from there.  Ready to check out?  Good luck.  The store has about 20 or more rows of checkout lanes, and, if you're lucky, four will be open.  I've been on week nights, week days, and week ends, and this store is simply horribly lacking in checkout personnel at all times on all days.  Just last night (a Tuesday evening at 7pm) I spent 20 minutes in the show room looking for a kids chair for my daughter, and 30 minutes in the checkout line.  I came back this morning around 11a and spent 25 minutes in the checkout line.  If you're hungry, it's even worse, because as you serve your 30 minutes in the penalty box, you're going to be staring at the deli area on the other side of the checkout lines.  You'll be wishing you could leave your belongings in the line and watch them creep towards the register while you enjoy a hot dog or some Swedish meatballs.

Hey, there's an idea IKEA, if you refuse to properly staff your checkout area, then put an automated cart mover in that gives you a number so you can go relax and know when it will be your turn to come back to the register to pay.

Just when I think the checkout area is the only problem, I start to assemble the Norsborg couch I bought for my office this morning.  One of the four threaded retaining receivers for the couch legs is the wrong size, so the leg can't screw in.  Hmm, what do I do about this issue?  The couch base box was huge and I box cut the cardboard and strapping to open it up on the floor, so no easy way to put everything back in.  Call the store.  I remained on hold for 20 minutes without an answer, so I gave up.  I guess their customer service is staffed about the same as their checkout lanes.  I then sent an email; it's been about six hours, no response.  I'm going to have to make a trip back to the store on the way home, probably wait in line, just to find out how to handle the exchange since I don't want to haul the one bad piece back if I need the entire box, and don't want to put the box back together with tape if I don't need it.  I'm sure this will end up with another round trip tomorrow once I get the answer to my customer service question tonight.  So all in all, my two purchases are likely going to involve wasting about three hours of my time, between the two checkouts and the resulting round trips to the store for customer service.  My time is more valuable than what I saved by purchasing the couch there, so this likely means I'll never be back.

One last update: I sent an employee back to the store with just the couch base to exchange it.  After 30 minutes in the customer service line (Saturday morning), an employee walking by asked what the issue was.  He told this person the issue, the person said he could take the couch base and put a new screw receiver in.  My employee said well, I was supposed to just swap the piece out, to which the IKEA employee replied well, it will take me five minutes, but if you want to wait to swap it out, you're at a point in the line where you've got about an hour to go.  Seriously?!  90 minute customer service line?!  He took the former option and was out in 35 minutes overall.  

Oh yeah, I got a reply to my customer service email three days later...

This was a very cool experience. Very awsome show floor and brilliant that you cant get out, unless you walk throught it all. I returned my couch that conveted into a bed for guests, due to bad stitching, and I was charged $100 more becasue I ordered black.  We like our night stands, tv stand, small desk,  table that coverts from small to seating for six, metal racks, and bogo chars. We did not like any chairs for the desks, tables, computers, and or bar stools. I would not buy things like that or couches. The rest was a great deal and the instructions were easy!  The food was like something you would eat in a cafateria, however i enjoyed their chocolates :) Yes i would shop here again. It took us 5 hours our first time. You walk thru the show room floor and write down what you want. Next you go to the warehouse  and pick your own stuff. Delivery was $59 and thats decent. :) Its a fun outing, but you will need a full day!

For such a large place, they only have one bathroom which is in the cafeteria. They could've at least put another one somewhere else. Bathroom was a little dirty, but was in the process of being cleaned. I would recommend this bathroom to a friend. Would shit again.

It's IKEA. So you'll get A-OK furniture at a decent price. I do find this location a bit frustrating. A couple of times I found a piece of furniture that met the eye. Headed downstairs to start collecting the pieces. But sadly in a few occasions, it's always out of stock on box 1,2,3,4 of----. If a customer is suppose to collect all those boxes for one furniture, why is one certain box out of stock? Then i end up putting back the other boxes because it's not complete. 

Their exchange/return line is also long too. Make sure you get a ticket, and.. wait. The process is decent, as long as you have your receipt and within the 90day time period.

The furniture is what you pay for and super cheap. I knocked on different pieces and they all nearly collapsed on me. The store is massive but when you walk in viewing show rooms, it's a cluster fuck mess.

What's not to love about this place?  The food is inexpensive and fast.  Its always the same.  Its kid friendly.  I brought my service dog in with absolutely no trouble, several times.

Today, they were out of iced tea and never made any more for 20 minutes.  Minus a star for that and the other thing I will get to later.  The ice cream with berries is approximately 1/3 of the size of the one they sell at Sam's club, for the same $1.50.  

The products are IKEA.  If you have been to one, you know what I mean.  I am not a fan of pressboard but their actual wood products like the Hemenes series are nice.  I got a white iron bed frame for like $130 a few years back that has been sturdy and durable through the abuse of a collection of kids using it in my spare room.  

Its always fun to come here and look at all the stuff.  Their set up kitchens are nice, makes me want one, and I'm sure that's why they do it.  The mini houses are interesting.  I just don't think I could live like that but its cool to think about.

You have to pull your own boxes and that can be a challenge.  I didn't buy anything like that today so it was not an issue but in the past I have found myself with a pile of boxes on a cart barely managing to move the thing.  You can get help if you ask but it sometimes takes a while.  Shipping is expensive, probably not worth it.  

The other problem, other than the inevitable long lines at the checkout, is that to get the sale prices you have to have your "family card".  So I left mine in the car.  No problem right?  Not.  They cannot look it up at the checkout like every other store on the planet.  The cashier suggested I go to a kiosk and quickly print out one, (with the giant line behind me) so I did, only because I had a bunch of stuff so it was taking her a minute anyway.  Guess what?   Printer out of paper at kiosk, so after all that it didn't work.  I ended up having to go to customer service to get the prices adjusted AFTER the same.  The customer service rep was not really nice, and demanded my ID to do the price adjustment after I had gone to another kiosk and printed out my temporary member card.  I didn't have it. She refused to give me the price adjustment.  WHAT?  I have the  receipt AND the debit card I just used 5 minutes ago WITH MY PHOTO ON IT...  I complained, asked for the manager.  The problem is that the hotel I was staying in took my ID for checkin and forgot to give it back.  So no ID for me.  Wow.  Eventually I showed them a picture of my ID that I keep on my phone and they grudgingly accepted that after waiting 10 minutes for a manager who never came.

So all in all, I still love IKEA, but you have to come prepared....

Honestly, if you don't like IKEA, there might be something wrong with you. Stylish, modern furniture that's cheap! You can't go wrong. The furniture is super easy to assemble, even for those of you that aren't handy. Hopefully you come with a big truck because you'll want to leave with everything. Everytime I come to IKEA I want to redo my entire home lol.

The food in the cafeteria is pretty savory too, and they always have special deals going on like Kid's Eat Free and free meals for IKEA family members (on select days). Even if you don't go on a free meal day, the food is pretty cheap. Downstairs by the registers, they even have a small grocery section if you don't want to have to drive out to IKEA for some Swedish meatballs. And again, everything is at a great price. There's also another cafeteria downstairs too but it only serves quick food like pizza, hot dogs, pretzels, frozen yogurt, etc.

I really appreciate how they have family parking off to the side, which are wider stalls. It makes coming to IKEA with the kiddies so much easier.

What can I say? I love IKEA! I moved to the Tampa area almost 4 years ago and needed to furnish an entire 2 bedroom/2 bathroom house. Coming from the NY area, I was very familiar with IKEA and the different levels of furniture and home decor items they offer. I love the layout of the store and that you can see, touch and feel all the furniture and decorating options you have. The prices are great and the showroom makes it easy to distinguish good furniture from the "cheap". The prices for the nicer Hemnes line of dressers vs. the particle board Malm dressers are not that different and they are both much more economical than going to a furniture store that delivers your items put together. I feel like you are saving money at IKEA because you have to usually spend an hour to two hours putting everything together yourself, which if you're a determined woman like me, you enjoy! 

When I'm in a hurry and I know what I am looking for, they have great little cut-thrus on the main level so you don't have to maneuver your way through all the droves of people that are in the store on the weekend. Also, if you check online, they give you the location in the warehouse where things are stored, so you can essentially skip the entire upstairs if you are in a rush. 

The instructions in the boxes are pretty self explanatory and I have had no issues assembling my furniture with the packaged instructions. All in all, IKEA is awesome. The prices are great, the quality is good, and I love the food at their café.

This Ikea is great, though my personal experiences have all been had during the week when everybody is working. 

Great staff, a lot of selection, the shipping option was great. We purchased a bed frame, desk chairs and a couple desk tables from them and had them bring it up to the apartment. Was a fair price, super fast same day shipping too. We live about 1 mile away though so it makes it much easier and affordable.

The food is not the best, (tastes almost the same as every other ikea i've been to) but if you're going to eat, i would highly recommend the swiss meatball dish with all the fixings. It's actually really good though it looks slightly questionable. 

Also, be sure to grab one or two of their Ikea bags because they are incredibly useful for laundry, grocery shopping and all the things. Those bags are so helpful. I can 1 man all my food upstairs with one of those things. It's great. Every ikea has one though I just thought I'd throw that out there too.
Are you kidding me?  IKEA serves good food?  Believe it--everything our party tried was good, and the prices are very reasonable.

Adore IKEA Tampa. Always seem to want something that is oversold to use IKEAS terms. Aka out of stock. However I have re-decorated with Ikea products ans its by far my favorite room to be in. Always start with IKEA!

The lines are long, the parking lot is a mess, and I do not like their products. A bookshelf I bought was impossible to put together and looked cheap. I must admit the meatballs are fantastic. I would pay more to be able to shop in non-peak hours.

I had planned on going to Ikea this Saturday with my Sister and Nephew. My Father went last week and purchased a small table that does not work as they hoped. I was to return it this week so I tried calling the store to see if I needed the credit card or just the receipt. First, the lead in recording and ridiculous amount of options spoken was bad enough (over 20) but you are forced to listed to a disclaimer about anchoring Ikea furniture to wall and where to get the anchor kits. Someone must have been injured but why are you subjecting everyone to this unbelievably long and frustrating process!!! I have a simple question and there was not one option to cover it. Then I was on hold for 18 minutes listening to a guy tell me how Ikea is making the buying experience so easy for every customer, bull crap!!, i hung up. It was anything but easy, it was a terrible experience and based on that, I will not be going to Ikea for anything except the return. Sorry Ikea, you lost a customer without even letting me in the store.

Oh, Ikea, I pretend to hate you but I actually kind of like you.

So the good - they do have everything.  Their quality has improved significantly in the last decade.  So much so that when I needed a kitchen cabinet to turn into a furniture piece (and nearly fell over getting prices at the local big box and cabinet stores), when I saw a piece I liked at Ikea, it got logged on a sheet and picked up (in pieces to assemble, of course) at the furniture pick up on our way out.  Staff is friendly.

The bad - this place is monstrous.  I find it difficult to just get in and out for one thing.  There are short cuts to an extent but I normally end up on a long wonder (and always choose the wrong shoes and end up with sore feet).  Consider it a maze - they want you to see everything and wear comfy shoes!  Staff can be hard to find (especially on the weekends - it's a busy place!).  When we bought the cabinet, they pulled one of the wrong pieces (we ordered 2 medium & 2 small drawers - ended up with 3 and 1).  We should have double checked the cart that they gave us at furniture check out, but still annoying to have a piece built and not realize the drawers aren't closing right because they gave you the wrong pieces.

The ugly - nothing.  Except that if you are tired and hangry while you are finally waiting to check out after a few hours of wandering, you will be even hangrier as you watch the cafe selling ice cream in front of the registers. :)

Love the place. I used to even bring my kids to Small land. You get that one hour of sanity without running after the little ones. I wish they would do the same with teenagers. 
We usually go in the evening and enjoy the restaurant first and then shop.
Never leave without their cinnamon rolls from the cafe!
I just did my entire kitchen in Ikea. So easy: just don't rush and read the instructions or you will get frustrated.

First off, I love coming here. I have been here many times. IKEA has given me so many great ideas for when I move into a more permanent living situation. I currently am living in an apartment while at school and might be going back home for my last year of schooling. I love all the different furniture and ideas that I get from that furniture. PS: I've already found the bed frame that I want after I graduate. All of the furniture seems like good solid pieces that could withstand a lot of use. I like looking at the first floor just to get some different ideas that I want, which is mainly on the third/first floor.

I also enjoy their second floor with all the different little items like kitchen utensils, rugs, storage, candles, etc. Seriously, don't know what to really call it. I have found things on that level that were super cheap and were exactly what I was looking for. This is also the level where you pick up the big pieces that you would like to buy that you saw on the first floor. This level is a little more tricky to move around in as there is so much stuff in such a tight area. I enjoy being able to pick up all my stuff on this floor as needed.

My friends and I typically like to come here for a quick, cheap-ish lunch. Hint here: If you have the family card, you can get a free coffee/tea with your meal. The food is good, but it's also the reason as to why it loses a star. The cafeteria ordering style is fine, but I came recently on a busy Saturday and they only had two cashiers ringing out there. This caused a huge back up. They really should have all lanes open on that kind of day. Also, if you aren't a big fan of fish or meatballs you are kind of SOLed on the food. My dad was only able to get chicken tenders because there wasn't really much else. I like the meatballs, enjoy them really and you can always pick up some for when you are home. The food overall I would say is decent. It's not bad, but it's not overly amazing either. 

One more thing before I forget, remember to bring your own shopping bags. The bags that you can buy there are a really good size and are 99 cents, but if you have them at home bring them and save yourself the dollar. Really though, looking for good furniture and some decent food. Just come here! It's a neat experience overall and I do enjoy it.

We love Ikea.  My husband has find a new home.  I swear, even when we need a new spatula, ladle, napkins or window hardware we have to go to Ikea.  I love everything and just updated my home with new furniture that can be changed by adding accessories from the store.  Oh, and be sure to have lunch......food is yummy

i frequented the one in cincinnati.  ikea has good prices, you can easily assemble it yourself, and it should fit in your car/in the door.  watch out that fully assembled you can remove it from your living space.  i've run into that problem before.

parking is great with the underground access, it is in a great central location, and the fun food is always a plus over competing furniture stores.

the preowned or clearance section in Saint Louis has been sad each visit so far.  i think it gets better the longer they're open.  Many people are flooding this location for now.

I am so happy there is an IKEA in St. Louis now!  Everyone should go at least once and try the meatballs!  They have a ton of decorating and storage ideas, I have a great time just looking.  The prices are reasonable and my favorite part is the kitchen gadget area!  I always find something I need.

Always a fun place to visit.  It feels like an amusement park.  I swear unless you are only buying one thing, you will spend a few hours browsing here!  I am a loyal customer and even did my kitchen with ikea cabinets.  the Soderhamn couch is very comfortable and I love the versatility.  My only advice for kitchen design is to be more thorough about rough costs before someone gets started.  It seems the prices vary widely from what i originally expected to pay for such a small kitchen.  In the end, I am overall happy.
A fun place to visit and shop and don't forget to eat, nice food.

Good food, well-prepared. Servings are reasonable and the price is remarkably low. I had the smoked salmon with bean salad, and my wife had a salmon wrap. Both were delicious. Long line for the cafeteria - wish it moved faster.

Ikea is the go to place for inexpensive, modern and simple furniture. They've got everything you could possibly need to fill you house. Everything from sinks to silverware, couches to candles, bed frames to picture frame, and then some. 

Ikea even has a scratch and dent section, which could yield the perfect piece of furniture for a serious DIY project. 

The majority of Ikea's furniture is displayed on the upper level, then broken down into various boxes on the first level in a warehouse like setting. Keep in mind, you're going to have to assemble the furniture yourself.

The Ikea cafeteria is a hit or miss. Either the food is delicious & leaves you lusting for more, or is just below mediocre & leaving you wishing you just kept walking. That being said, the ice cream is always on point- smooth and creamy for just $1.

This is the most awesome place on earth for people who like to live well but small! Experts in small space living, IKEA helped make my tiny, closet like bathroom a functional space with loads of storage and character. I LOVE my bathroom now!

My first time at ikea was amazing I've never been in one of your stores before and they just opened one in St.louis MO
But no one explained to us what the store was all about it was incredibly hard to find a worker anywhere on the display side ... When we finally found a lady and asked her "how to we purchase items" she explained you had to write a number down then go to warehouse side and find it ... Ok cool I ask her if I can have a pen and paper to write it down and she tells me to look for an I station and that's where I'll find what I need and dismisses me ... Ok great so we go back to were the desk is I want to purchase & we take a screenshot with ours phone because we can't find the I tower she was talking about and at this point we had already spent so much time trying to get help that we were a little frustrated... So we finally get numbers try & find our way back outta the display part to wonder around until we find the warehouse part still no one to help ... We find it only to arrive at a place were again there's no help ... We finally get what we need off the shelf almost killing ourselves to stand in one of the four lines open ... I mean at this point since you have to do everything yourselves can't I self checkout ... Instead of standing in line for forty minutes on top of the hour an half it took me just to find then gather my desk??? Wtf ... You should have someone stationed at the entrances with paper & pens & maps !!!!!!! & maybe hire some helpful people or any people !!!! To explain how you lovely store works.,, I watch five people that were going to buy something leave because they didn't know how to purchase it and there wasn't anyone explaining again !!!

First time I had ever been to an IKEA and I have to say I love it. Just moved and needed to pick up some furniture for my new apartment. Walked around looking at some of their displays and picked up what we needed for just under $500. Walked out with a queen sized bed, kitchen table, and some kitchen supplies. While inside decided to try out their food upstairs. Picked the Swedish meatballs with mashed potatoes. Good prices and the food was really tasty. I also had a cup of coffee and it was one of the best cups I have ever had. Will most certainly be going back here for all of my furniture needs.

So my friend and I were waiting for the IKEA to open forever, and I had never eaten there. So we decided to go get lunch, probably one of the better fast and spontaneous meals I have had. Service was fast and the dining area was clean when I went but it's kinda food court ish so I can't really say I expected much.

Walking through the store was similar to most IKEA ventures I had made in the past, busy, full, brightly lit, and lots of goods all over. Got a chefs knife because I have been needing one, totally worth it, better than my old knife, and the miles I've been putting on it. I look forward to going back for more stuff soon.
This place is sooooo big it was fun, the food was good also.....

The Swedish meatballs and veggie balls were warm and delicious! The server stacked my wife's plate with more than the expected amount of veggie balls and the server didn't give an attitude about substituting the veggies with fries. The food tasted great and the split-pea, kale soup was better than I expected. Get the ikea card so you can get a discount on your next meal!

IKEA is fun to visit. The nordic food offerings by the entrance include smoked fish, lingonberry items and Wasa crackers. Sven and Ole would be proud. They also have reasonably priced $1 cones.

IKEA furniture is mostly cheap particle board from China that falls apart soon after assembly. They also have a wide selection of home decor items. 

It's an experience shopping here and interesting to browse the large exhibition spaces. Sadly they don't source or invest much in the local community or buy anything (as far as I can tell) from local artisans. Giant parking lot and giant store. If you're like Brett and love mega-chains this is the place for you.

I've always been an IKEA fan, so when this one opened we had to check it out.

First off how great is it that they have a supervised play area for your kids? That's 5 five worthy by itself.

Honestly it's so much more than just a furniture store, they sell kitchen supplies, pillows, down comforters, lighting supplies and the list goes on and on. And the prices are typically much better than you'd pay at a Target or Bed Bath and Beyond.

Much nicer than the Philly IKEA. It has everything you need as well as a great cafe area. I like that they added a lot more healthy options as well. It is so cheap to eat there! It also feels more open and less crowded than the Philly one. So it makes for a good weekend browsing trip with the family!

This is the first IKEA I've ever been to and it lived up to the hype! You can smell the food as you walk in, so I wouldn't go hungry. Unless you're planning on eating first, then by all means make that your plan. 

As you ride the escalator up you're dropped off by big yellow bags and pencils and papers - to write down everything you want, of course. I went just going to see what this massive store was all about, so I didn't actually purchase anything. I walked around and followed the arrows to see what there was...and there's A LOT. Everything is very organized and I was pleasantly surprised things weren't more chaotic. Don't go if you're in a rush. But if you need a few quick items (frames, lights, etc.) go on a weekday evening and follow the shortcuts to get to the room you need.

Ode to IKEA

Let me count the ways I love you:

1)  Meatballs

2)  Free drop-in chid play (except when you close early you bastards because then I have a tantruming toddler)

3)  Cube shaped storage units (I think every room in my house as one of these)

4)  Bulk Swedish Candy

5)  Sparkling Pear Drink

6) $1 ice cream cones

7) $1 breakfast

8)  Free diapers in the washrooms

9)  Easy pushing carts

10) For being in Canada

See you soon Ingamar.

It's like every other IKEA I've ever been to (shocking, I know). The best part is the showroom where you get to walk around and marvel at the tiny apartment set-ups and the organization hacks.

Like every other IKEA, it's an absolute madhouse on the weekends. SO. MANY. CHILDREN. And strollers. And tears. And arguing couples. If you must go on a Saturday, go as early as possible. And plan to get a beer afterward. Meatballs, schmeatballs - you're gonna need a drink to recover from the chaos.

This place is very awesome! Cheap furniture, lamps, food, etc. The food here is very tasty and cheap! I came here in the morning for breakfast and I got potatoes, eggs, and sausage for only $1.99! It's not like those restaurants where they give you a small amount of something. They give you the whole thing! This place is great for eating and shopping! 2 in 1... If your looking for a place to shop and eat. "I love IKEA now! Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner has now been served. You know what. I'll eat before going to the kids care center."

Great addition to STL. It is nice to see new things are coming to St. Louis, when many are moving out.
Great selections.
Interesting place to go. Staff is ridiculously useless. Had to move and lift my own bed and dresser. No help at all.  Horrible customer service. Very unwelcoming.

Really terrible location. 
Yesterday we were shopping there around 7 pm and someone broke into our car, broke the locks the door handle, and stole my school beg with my laptop in it and my wallet and other stuff that was in there. I am beyond devastated , there was so many people around the parking lot was full and NOBODY saw anything. The ghettoest place ever, I never had anytime stolen so this was really new to me, that someone would actually brake a door in the car to get to your stuff at a parking lot of a place like IKEA, just so disappointing. My whole life was in that laptop, I do graphic design so alllll my work was there all the pictures from with my family everything is gone. 
And when I called to tell them what happened after I filled out the police report, they refused to even check the cameras. 
thanks a lot .

I love Ikea SO MUCH! If I had the funds I would probably have an entirely Ikea furnished house! 
On my last visit a lady dropped an entire box of wine glass and a young employee came by and cleaned it right up. No fuss no muss. He told her it was no issue and she went on her way. Not many young people would happily accept the task at hand these days so kudos to him! 
I'm obsessed with the very reasonably priced duvet covers that are so very cozy. Next I will be trying out their sheets!  
If you have the time, stop for a $1 cone and enjoy some people watching.

I was thrilled and worried that they brought an ikea to this part of the Midwest. My family have been to quite a few, each out does the other. You get engrossed by all the possibilities of decorating your home. It is easy for one to personalise to a more simplified modern style, something I don't really see in the homes here. It's just not the type location that allows it, hunting and Walmart are more fitting in my opinion. We enjoy ikea for the experience and the quick bite to eat after going through the maze of possibilities. Which brings me to the reason for the low rating, the cafeteria. I can't complain about the food, but the employees customer service is lacking. They seem like they don't want to be there and much rather gossip about how they should be making $15 an hour. They were quite rude to my wife when she asked for a glass for water. They equally were annoyed when we asked what about one of the dishes. If not for our hunger we would've walked out right then and there. I think the employees do not understand what kind of company ikea is and just countdown till they clock out. We will never be eating there again and I will gladly pay extra online for shipping to avoid that type of customer service. IKEA is so much better in California and London.

This is one of my favorite IKEA locations ever!  We've visited here many times with friends and family over the years and never cease to be amazed at the selection of items, the cleanliness of the facilities, and the quick checkout lines.  The food in the cafe is out of this world at a very reasonable price!

The only downside to this IKEA is the service at the food court.  Although overall it's good, they often only have one checkout register open, which can make for a long wait while your food gets cold.

The parking garage is gigantic and there's plenty of space for loading up all your purchases without bumping into someone else.

Awesome location, highly recommend, we'll be back here soon!
It's in a great location not to far from work or home. I can run by if and when I need to. The food is pretty good. I have made a few things which is hard but worth it in the end.

The two-way traffic is frustrating. Customers are entering the wrong way from the restaurant area and clogging traffic on the main aisle. Why not post signs directing customers to the proper entrance? 

Also, the IKEA Family kiosks only allow you to type in uppercase. This prevents you from entering lowercase characters in your password!

I'm a fan but with some reservations. A lot of their stuff is  pretty cool. Some is cool and inexpensive, but some is cheaply made and don't expect it to last. In some cases, that could be okay but if you want furniture, for instance, that you'll be able to keep for a long time and move it from place to place, it might not be the best choice. Also, the modular stuff may not look that expensive but when you add all the components up, it can end up costing a lot more that you expected. And then you have to get it home and assemble it! You can find better quality for less at antique malls and it's already assembled. One reason to go is to get ideas. And I love the cafeteria. The food is really good and not very expensive. 

One thing I really dislike is that their map is not helpful. It's hard to find your way around and hard to find your way out. Definitely don't go if you're short on time. 

All in all, I'm glad they came to St. Louis and glad they chose the location that they did.

So Glad I live close enough to swing in for a quick pick up item during the week. We served guests on new salad bowls, and table linens we picked up the same day. I prices for small decorative items can't be beat. The room set ups are great for brainstorming a future remodel of our kitchen. Once you learn the shortcuts it's easy to get in and out fast if your need. The cinnamon buns cooking near the check out are a well planned and affordable indulgence on the way out.

This rating is directed at Ikea's delivery service; not necessarily the store or the company itself.  I wanted to write this review sooner, but hadn't gotten around to it. I am very pleased with the bed that I purchased through the store.  It's a quality product. My sales associate was very helpful and knowledgeable. 

I had a delivery time slot for which I had to take a foodless lunch break from my already physically active job for; not a huge deal.  Also, they made the delivery in the allocated time.  The two guys get to my house and the first thing one of them does is ask me to use my bathroom.  I obliged but they seriously couldn't have stopped at a wawa? 

They told me that they couldn't (or wouldn't) haul away the old bed.  They set up the frame pretty efficiently.  I had to sign off on a sheet that had my name spelled wrong which didn't seem like a big deal to them.  Plus they were rude.  

I find that they left the mattress standing up, backwards, against my dresser, in its packaging, for me to do myself.  Mind you, I'm 5'4, and on the slender side.  I also have three nosy cats that I was fearing for as I had to wrestle with the damn full-sized mattress.  After that, I come outside to find a huge pile of trash laying out on my front yard.  Really, it was that hard to even take this away? I had paid for delivery... but I guess that was all I had paid for.  I had a ten set aside for the guys for their troubles... but needless to say my troubles seemed to outweigh theirs.

Who doesn't love IKEA? Some items are a steal, pure steal, and other items you are better off making yourself...why?? Bc it looks homemade already! IKEA is one of those places you just cannot get sucked into everything because of the price, you are getting what you pay for!!! Like all IKEAs this one follows the same floor plan of walking through and paying at the end. This location has friendly employees and is in a good area I think to appeal to the masses and the ppl who drive from far and wide to get their items (shipping costs online suck). My only gripe with this place is that their inventory is not on par with whats online. Also, you HAVE to come here as soon as they open, so you can shop peacefully. After a while the ppl who stop, look and take up the aisle space will come with all their children. There is specifically a place to drop of ur kids and this is not frickin Macy's!!!!!!!! You have to be conscious of other ppl when you are browsing Midwest! I leave with a whole attitude and a happy purchase :)

Damn you ikea! Why are you so awesome?!?! 

Yes, the furniture isn't expensive, or of the greatest quality. Once you build your furniture piece. It must stay in its place forever. It's not made to be moved or it will fall apart. But you pay for what you get and for the minimal price. It's good design. 

I love how the company makes efficiency of all types of space.  They give people great ideas on how to maximize. Even the food waste is managed properly.  Honestly, we and all restaurants should implement similar values to help our planet. 

Sweden is one of the top 10 cleanest countries in the world and that is something everyone should learn from. I love their great prices, innovated designs and easy assembly items.

So I went to the store and gathered my order. The staff were very friendly and very helpful. You put your whole life history in to the computer along with an order, they print it out and you go to the check out. And that's when everything turned to manure. First it was really hot. I realize its getting to closing time but come on. Then there were lines - long lines. You would think the manager would have someone open another register. Saw some chairs on the way out so I picked those up. Turns out the price on the display is good only if sign up for their program. ... missed that sign! So there was an issue at the register and I couldn't get my order. It was late and a Friday so I left. I've called and e-mailed trying to get to a real live human being. All I want to know is - Is my order still in their system or do I have to start from scratch? I'm trying to give them money and getting zero help. BTW - I went to the website, typed in 'Customer Service' and descriptions of espresso machines come up

I like IKEA the company, but this location gets 1-star. I was overcharged by my cashier. I purchased 2 lamps and when I got home, the receipt showed I purchased 3. Thankfully IKEA is cheap, but still the cashier charged me an extra $10.80

IT'S A TRAP!

One of the first things I think about when I step foot in this monstrous warehouse full of pretty things that you probably don't need. 

The Swedes are geniuses. This place is a serious maze not for the faint at heart. If you know exactly what you want, you need to be a modern day Indiana Jones in order to get out in less than an hour. 

There are tons of furniture options that cater to all kinds of budgets. The furniture is modern and very customizable. Of course, the less expensive furniture is going to be well... less nice. You really get what you pay for. The same goes with the other items that the store offers from storage containers to lighting to plants. IKEA has it all. 

IKEA makes it really easy to spend a whole day here. There are no carts in the main walking area, so you won't get irritated playing bumper carts with other customers. Everything just looks so darn pretty that you just wish your room, kitchen, or house looked like their mock set ups. There's a cafeteria that serves pretty good food. Actually, I've driven here for lunch before. My favorites are the Swedish meatballs and the chocolate cake (which I struggled to eat in one sitting, it was really rich). IKEA also has... childcare! Enjoy your shopping experience without having to watch your kids. 

This place has done so many things right. If you are looking for furniture or other household items, it's a definite recommendation in my book. Just make sure you have at least a couple of hours to half a day to spend here.

A great Ikea! I've been to a million of them and this one's clean and efficient. We're renovating our kitchen right now and through every trip they've been fast and effective. I've bought tons of cabinets and shelves and every tim I've had to make a replacement because of damage or incorrect sizing on my part, they've been a joy to deal with. Not even that crazy on weekends. Great shop.
Swedish meatballs are great furniture is well furniuture its cool though

Got the Swedish meatballs. Was not impressed. What's the big deal? Had some sort of chocolate butterscotch thing for dessert and, again, not impressed. However, their prices on furniture and homes goods are impressive as is the quality and ingenuity. Just don't bother with the food.

Love coming here to get ideas for rooms and decor. The showroom is fun to play in...I mean to look at. Some of the furniture is not so bad and seriously, if you are on a budget, you can't go wrong with IKEA. Their more pricier furniture pieces look nicer but is still a lot cheaper than going elsewhere.

You can get lots of inexpensively priced random household things. $2 trash can for the bathroom?! Heck yeah! They carry pretty much anything you might need for your house or office. As well as items you DON'T need but get anyway because it's cute. Their children's section is adorable. I would have definitely come here if I had lived in the area before I had my son. They sell lots of plush toys at a low price.

Food court here is cafeteria style. Food is not that bad. I had the Swedish meatballs and an almond cake on the last visit. $1 frozen yogurt cones by the exit. An easy way to spend a few hours. It was actually nice visiting during the week because it wasn't as busy as it usually is on the weekends. Would definitely recommend coming during a weekday if possible.
So much fun, but not set up in an intelligent way. Workers are extremely nice and will help you with anything you need!

My first encounter with IKEA was intense. It is an absolute madhouse, but entertaining nonetheless. Be prepared to get lost. I felt like I was in an eternal maze of home goods, lol. They have EVERYTHING you could possible need. They even had these damn euro pillowcases I could not find anywhere else. When I had asked an employee where they were, she told me without a problem. I feel like it's a place everyone has to go at least once.

I like ikea but not this location only because of the service. Great products but good luck checking out with warm customer service. When I got home I was missing an item that I purchased and waited on the phone for 25 minutes to talk to someone.
Perfectly chaotic!   Shopping was great, food was delish and bathrooms were clean.  Definitely kid friendly!

IKEA is good for cheap furniture that you will never move (because it won't hold up) or for other cheap household items that you don't want to splurge on. They carry a wide array of products from furniture to light fixtures. 

My biggest issue with IKEA is navigating the store is a chore. It's basically a maze that you have to weave through until you find yourself at checkout. Yes there are some short cuts but it's definitely not easy, especially if you are unfamiliar with the store. 

They do have a two food options. One upstairs which is cafeteria style and one downstairs which is a better deal (think Sam's/Costco style: hotdogs and soft serve) but less options.

Okay so I was in the market for a shoe cabinet, decided to stop by ikea.. Bad move.

First, I'm a fan of ikea. They always seem to have the odd things I'm looking for. Yesterday I stopped at the store in Conshocken, it was packed! Literally crazy in there, fortunately I knew what I was getting. My nightmare started during checkout, I get in line and they are very long. I notice the line next to me is credit/debit only, there was a yellow sign hanging from the register number. Im in line and the cashier starts scanning, I have a child in the cart and a few odd items. The cashier could not reach the box, I offer to help. She then yells at me and says I need to do it. I just looked at her and said okay. She insisted on having the box removed, I do so and as she is putting the box back in the cart she hits my daughter in the arm. Ridiculous! No apology or anything. She was too busy talking to the other cashier across from her. After all that I go to pay. She says swipe your card, I said I would like to oh cash. Not uttering a word she just points to the yellow sign (below eye level) and it's a credit/debit sign. The other lane was clearly marked credit/debit not this one. Whatever things happen, I figure she made a mistake hitting my and as did I. No, she cancels the order and makes me go into another line. She even had to have a manager come over to cancel the order, I had to wait another 15 minutes in line. Bad move by manager and cashier. Will not be back

Pros:
Huge 
Clean
You can get lunch while your shopping 
Most furniture fits my style 

Cons:
I spend way too much money every time I make a trip to Ikea.
Those picture instructions can be awful. 
 
As I said i can spend way too much money in this store. The top floor is the showroom, you casually stroll through and get inspiration. The bottom floor is where i get into trouble. That's where you can buy kitchen gadgets, curtains, room decor, rugs, etc. etc. After you wonder through all that you come to the warehouse, here you can find your big furniture pieces. They are all organized by bin and aisle numbers. 

I do recommend bring a big truck if you plan on buying big pieces. Shipping can be very expensive. Also build it yourself once you get home. They offer to build it for you but that's $$$.
Very confusing store.  Took me a half hour to find checkout.  Won't return.  Ask for help and was directed to read the signs.  Too much walking.  Cheap furniture.  Rather shop at Carol House.

Customer service is really really REALLY bad.
I was on hold when I called for about 55 minutes before I got a CSR on the phone. I needed replacement screws for a Poang chair.
She told me she couldn't help me unless I gave her a part #. I said I was driving and I couldn't. She said I was out of luck then.
I said why can't you look it up on your system - and like a broken record she said I had to tell her the part #. When asked again why she couldn't look that up in the system she said its bc she wasn't sure which screw I wanted.
I said well - how about if I wanted all of them - there are only so many types for that chair right? She said well in that case I should just go into the store however she couldn't guarantee there were any in the store.

Can someone please tell me how any of this was helpful?

IKEA - fix your customer service. This is 2016 - we don't have time for this nonsense.

Ikea-

I have a love/hate relationship with Ikea.  Overall I'm a huge fan.  Started my Sunday morning with "Oh man, I need to grab more closet-system shelves".  Time to go to Ikea!  BTW, only an insane person would go to Ikea on a Sunday and brave the 1/2 day trip, but I put on some shorts and a comfortable set of shoes and set out to the land of Sweden (and in this case, Ikea Tampa which is close to Ybor City).

So, Ikea pro-tip #1: Make a list.  Go online, find what you like before you go. OR make a list while you walk around (if you don't use pro-tip #3) otherwise you will forget what you came to get once you get to the checkout area.
pro-tip #2: If you spend more than $100 go get yourself some free food afterwards in the cafe.  I recommend the Swedish Meatballs or the Chicken Fingers.  It's fairly fresh and they also have some nice salads too.
pro-tip #3: walk in reverse - this is frowned upon, but if you have a list, you can go in the out door and straight where you pick up stuff!  If you don't know where it is, they have little kiosks you can look stuff up on right there in the warehouse!  You can thank me for saving you 4 hours later on.  Unless you happen to be a fitbit user and have run low on steps during the week :)
pro-tip #4: Don't go on the weekend.  I know...sometimes this is not avoidable, but like any huge destination store, during the week things seem less busy.
pro-tip #5: there are secret passageways in Ikea.  If you look off the path of some areas, you can see shortcuts through areas.  So for example, you're not into bath towels and curtains, you can just cut through and go straight for the lamps or the checkout isles.

Oh and from previous Ikea's in Michigan, North Carolina, etc this is by far my favorite one.  Staff is friendly, people are willing to help and things seem to move pretty fast even on a Sunday afternoon.  They also offer free child care while you shop as well.

This IKEA location is great. Although it's been around longer than the South Philly one, it has everything you need. The showroom is cavernous and amazing all at the same time. But, it's tough to get through (unless you know the shortcuts) if you have to run in for one thing. 

The restaurant is great. Fast and (generally) friendly service. The previous time I went here, the main person service was very rude and almost threw my plate across to me. I can't recall her name, but she was female, average height, 25-35, slightly heavy build, and oozing of the attitude "I hate my job." 

This time I went, the main person serving was much nicer. Very pleasant and didn't try to throw dishes at me. She was blonde, thin build, older, maybe in her 40's. I got the Chicken Meatballs and hubby got the chicken florentine. Both dishes were great for a quick (and cheap) bite to eat. I've been here a lot generally my food experience is good (aside from the previous time). 

Overall, I highly recommend this place!

Please understand that this is not a one star review for the Ikea products.  I have shopped at Ikea forever and have spent over $10K over the years furnishing my home as a 20 something in the 90's shopping at their Potomac Mills, VA location, furnishing my now grown children's homes in the 2010's and still love their products. Nothing like the design and thrill of the Ikea experience!

This review is regarding the return policy.  

I've since moved to Cleveland, OH where the closest Ikeas are either Pittsburgh, PA or Canton, MI.  Both over 2.5 hours away.  This past weekend, we rented a truck and went to pick up 4 Pax wall units to create a dressing room in our home.  Canton had everything in stock (at least at the time we designed the units online), so we chose to go there, over Pittsburgh.  Upon our arrival, only 4 of the 7 Bergsbo doors we needed were in stock.  What a bummer!  Looks like it was a big shopping day and someone beat us to them.  We decided that we'd just order the remaining 3 doors online when we got home and would wait the week or so to add the doors to the units.  Total bill is just short of $2K including the doors ordered online.  Our last name is NOT Rockefeller....that's not chump change!

Upon assembly at home, we found out that one of the doors had experienced a crush injury on the edge of the panel (not something that could be hidden or overlooked), so we went ahead and ordered 4 new doors, instead of 3, online.   We anxiously await their arrival.

So I called Ikea customer service this morning regarding the damaged door.  Waited a good 10 minutes to speak to an actual human being.  The rep informed me that I would have to physically drive back the 2.5 hours to receive credit for the unusable item (which would never be able to be resold in it's current state....it's a 4 inch crush right on the front center of the door).  I asked if the shipping company from their website that would be delivering the new doors would be able to return the door for us.  They said no, it was a third party vendor (yet the only shipping option on their website?).  I asked if we could take a picture, provide a copy of the receipt, and be refunded.  They said no.  I asked if they refunded shipping?  They said no, and a half hearted sorry.  

So the $60 door would likely be upwards of $30 or $40 to ship back.  Not really an option.  

Overall, really really disappointed in the customer service. Unless you live close by, looks like you're out of luck if you find anything damaged upon opening product.  Not cool, Ikea.

We've been to Ikea three times and it's been fun! Love seeing the tiny apartment set ups for ideas on living in a small space. The quality of the furniture and other products is decent for the price.  Recently purchased 2 Poang chairs and footstools and a dropleaf table.  Building them was easy.
 The store itself is a fun field trip! Go early to avoid the crowds.  There are shortcuts throughout the store (if you can figure them out, lol) but it is a fun place to wander through.  The only negative was the checkout process.  Our cashier was busily talking to her friend (another cashier) and pretty much ignored us.  As we tried to leave with our heavy cart full of furniture, the second cashier could hardly be bothered to move out of the way.  It was very Walmart-ish.  Then we got outside, looked at the receipt again, and realized she had made a mistake and charged us twice for delivery of another item we purchased.  So yeah. I had hoped the staffing would be on par with the rest of the store. Maybe it was an isolated incident. Hope so, there are enough places with crappy service in this town.  We will definitely go back to Ikea!

Worst customer service experience of my life. Bought a toddler bed and got delivery and assembly service. One of the 3 parts delivered was the incorrect color (I picked this from the warehouse where each color was its own section, so it was incorrectly placed). When the delivery guy realized this, he left everything in the middle of my daughters room and said we had to call ikea. IKEA has set up their customer service so that you can't actually contact a store. Instead, you get put on hold forever and then talk to a representative that can't do anything. I called and logged a good two hours only to find out there was nothing that could be done and they would call me in 48 hours. When I asked for a refund on the delivery service, the MANAGER told me it was a customer error because I should have double checked the boxes. Well, I never got a call in 48 hours so I called them back (another hour on the phone) and found out that the store was out of stock of the color I needed for my missing piece and they didn't know when it would be available (still a customer error though right?). Meanwhile, when I picked it out, it was in a pile of other toddler bed boxes labeled as the same color, so I can only assume that all of those have the wrong color as well. In the end, I'm having them pick up the parts and refund me my money. The customer service was the absolute worst part of this. No one seemed to care or actually try to solve my problem because why bother? They don't work at the store and they probably get paid nothing to get yelled at by customers. They set up the system to try and get you to give up. IKEA is the absolute worst. Never again.

I really enjoy going to IKEA. I got a tea frother for three dollars and it does a good job helping me make froth for my chai teas. I also bought the chicken meatballs from the food part of the store and they are very yummy.

I loved the store as a whole. It was so nice to be able to go in and look at most everything already set up in a room instead of imagining what it may look like outside of a box. The place is HUGE I felt like I was walking forever and we still skipped through parts of the stores. But lets take a moment to talk about the cafeteria. The Swedish Meatballs are AMAZING and the prices are so cheap. I loved the view from my table as well. I would definitely recommend that you check out IKEA and stop by the cafeteria before you leave, you will not be disappointed.

I could walk around in this store for an entire day if I had the time! There's so many different things to look at, it's at first a little overwhelming. I went on a Sunday and it was like I was in a herd of animals heading towards food. (I of course mean that in the nicest way!) 

I love their products and the fact that's it's budget friendly is pretty fantastic. Their style is so much 'younger' then the old school furniture stores and no one is following you around waiting for a sale which takes the pressure off of you as the buyer. 

The layout is great, having the display cases of rooms is a great way to display their items in use instead of just having the warehouse portion by itself. I do appreciate the self serve portion too. I can just get my stuff and not have to wait.

Great store, great pieces and great prizes!

Over the course of a week, I placed 2 orders of items in their South Philly store. Both items were to be delivered on the same day, today. Along with delivery, I paid for assembly on both. An extra 600 dollars. Today  the crew arrived at the end of the 4 hr window. Had both items with them but stated only one of the two was scheduled to be assembled. I showed them my receipts but was told I had to call IKEA to resolve the issue. I spent the next 1.5 hr on 2 separate calls and several times customers service telling me that I did not pay for assembly to finally get some resolution with a reschedule of the second item. As for the two guys that arrived, they refused to stay even after it was clarified that assembly of our second item was part of our order. They hastily slapped together the wardrobe and caused several nicks and dents on the wardrobe parts. They then rushed out demanding my signature before I had a chance to review their assembly job. Not happy at all would never recommend.
This place literally has everything for s house, including live plants.  Amazing selection, some stuff kind of cheap, but great ideas for decorating and so many different items, plus a restaurant!

If you just bought a new home or if you're renting a new place, IKEA is a go-to place to get your essentials inexpensively.  Kitchen supplies, bedding, furniture - you name it, IKEA has it.  But be prepared to spend A LOT of time there.

We went to get food first.  I have to say, although most of the food was good, they stopped putting out desserts closer to the time of closing.  Even when we asked about the cakes, they basically said that was all that was left.  I highly doubt that.  They were cut up on plates, and I'm sure they had others ready to go for the next day....

IKEA's layout is simple enough to walk through, but you can cut into other departments if you want to skip over certain things or go backwards to something you already saw.  It is good in that way, but it can also make you feel like you're in a maze.

Overall, a great place to go if you're just starting out somewhere but not really the best quality if you're trying to upgrade your home.

Suggestions for quick "what is Ikea?" visit after my experience (followed by review)
1. Park beneath the building on the 1st floor
2. Go to the 3rd level cafeteria first and order a side of Swedish meatballs for $1 plus a water or drink of your choice (free refills on some with purchase & getting glass/mug)
3. skip the using cool maneuverable shopping cart to just quick browse
4. look up at the hanging map sign... Store is not linear but actually one-way loop (explains the "short cuts" that are just doors to the other side of the loop)
5. Make the 3rd floor loop
6. Make the 2nd floor loop
7. Go to the 2nd floor cafe & order the $1 fresh cinnamon roll plus water/soda or 75 cent coffee and decide if there is anything you want to buy today

Review- weird place with a very confusing layout that seems to force newbies into browsing while letting the experienced quicker visits...  MARKETING!

Food-
3rd floor cafeteria provides more selection including larger meals & only place to sell the $1 side of Swedish meatballs (get the glass or mug for drinks with free refills or water). There is free wi-fi to go along with free refills in case you need that.
2nd floor cafe sells cheaper snack style pizza & hotdogs plus is the only place to the $1 fresh cinnamon rolls.
Swedish meatballs were very good for $1, but not the best meatballs I ever had... Same with cinnamon rolls
$7 salmon plate was tried & thought it was under-seasoned & tasteless overall.
$2 side salad was OK for the money.

Shopping/selection
Nifty or thrifty things are everywhere, but finding the nifty & thrifty combination is a bit harder.
The 2nd floor can be thought of as a upscale & larger Target Housewares.  However, buyer beware because I was not impressed by the pots & pans.  Later in the loop is kids toys that had miniature usable kitchen items for younger aspiring chefs.
The 3rd floor has furniture, actual kitchens and module living (think buying pieces of furniture that fit together) was actually more interesting.  They have patio furniture at reasonable prices.

I will return for specific items or maybe to browse & snack during the week day.

Typical corporate company, it's really easy to buy things, either in store and online. BUT if you have any issues and want to voice a complaint, you actually have to write a letter. They're online "let us know how we did" section, literally doesn't have a send button. It's basically a blank page for you to complain to yourself. Being a company that only sells furniture in pieces I find it fairly ridiculous that you can't get parts for anything. ALL THEY SELL IS PARTS. I'll be taking my money elsewhere next time.

Came in around 10:45 and went to the cafeteria upstairs as the kids play land was not yet open.

All the monitors in the cafeteria were showing breakfast. The chef informed us they had just switched over to the lunch menu, but he could still pull together a few plates of breakfast. So despite the line being changed out we still got what we wanted because the chef was willing to go above and beyond for us. We really appreciated that!

I had the Swedish meatballs and Mac n cheese and it was delicious as always.

The breakfast sausages were not that great but it's not like I was expecting fine dining...it is after all IKEA.

Service was good food was decent.

Wouldn't mind coming back again...

Wow what a horrible experience.  The lady working the Playland forgot to give me a beeper then tried to make me go through the line again because of her error. The other lady working there just stared at a tv screen inside the playroom that was empty.
If rude with attitude is what they are going for they've achieved it.

IKEA is a magical land of affordable furniture, colourful home accessories, & interactive displays that make you want to decorate your home all day.

They have an affordable restaurant upstairs with some much needed snacks. My go to is the kids meal. It might be a faux pas, but I still do it. You can get veggie balls with mashed potatoes, a chocolate milk, & a froyo from downstairs for $2.99! Or sub out the veggie balls for Mac & Cheese. Can't go wrong there.

It takes some time to learn the lay of the land as it can seem like a maze especially when it is busy. Bring a knowledgeable friend as back up and always come with a list. Good luck!

IKEA is a mixed bag but has some great things that you won't find anywhere else.  For example, the Muesli cereal in the food market is the BEST you can find in the US aside from home made.   I have searched Whole Foods, Wegmans, all the other grocery chains but IKEA is the only place to import Finax cereal from Sweden.  It has much less sugar and more whole grain than anything I have seen.   Also the Christmas display has lots of neat Scandinavian stuff you will never see at other stores.  I love that they carry lots of small things (shelves, sinks, storage units, tables) which will fit into places that most things won't.  The only bad thing is the customer service wait time....and prepare to hold for an hour if you try to call.  Some employees are definitely better than others.

UPDATE 10/2016:  IKEA had stopped carrying Finax muesli for a bit but as of last weekend IT'S BACK!!!   I bought 8 bags.   Stay away from the Ikea branded Muesli....no where near as good as Finax.

IKEA. Home of the Big Blue Box. Let me just put out the disclaimer:  I may be partially biased because I was once a former "IKEAN" as I liked to call myself back in the day. Yep, I saw it from an employee point of view before this time, I saw it as a customer.

I was super excited to be making a trek to this IKEA while we were in town and even more so since it had been over seven years since I had been back to one. 

Let me say that IKEA isn't for everyone. But for those who do like it, like myself, it offers everything under the sun. From ice cream cones to cribs to kitchens, it's all there. While it does make the customer work (walking, carrying, pushing, schlepping) it also rewards customers with low price items. Quality is not the finest, but the prices reflect that. It's great for college students, setting up an initial house, or for those who want to down size and need minimalistic furniture. People are often "freaked" out or "overwhelmed" if it is their first time experience. Breathe. It gets better after one understands how IKEA works. It's not like walking into just any home goods or furniture store.

We did the entire upper floor "pathway" stopping to evaluate TV stands. While we didn't find anything to purchase, the prices were definitely on point. IKEA has a great way of attractively setting up to show the customer what and how it could look and then allows the customer to create their choice.

While we only purchased a few household items, the store was still neat and organized at 4 o'clock on a Saturday afternoon which was amazing since weekends are usually the worst times to visit. Check out wasn't too bad either with only 2 carts ahead of us, it flowed smoothly. Our cashier wasn't the friendliest or happiest lady, but oh well, some days are better than others. There's ample parking. A small food cafeteria and a little market to take care of any hunger pangs. For larger purchases, customers can back up their vehicle and load everything in without going all over the parking lot in the rain. Overall, we left intact and happy with our purchases. If it were closer, I might be in trouble because I'm sure I could always find something to buy!

IKEA!  Great store!  We really needed this in our area!  Finally a store that caters to our style.  All the other furniture stores try but no one can pin down that minimalist style like IKEA lets admit it.  Stop trying.  Please it's embarrassing.

Have you ever been to a store and been amazed at how genuinely friendly and helpful the staff is?  Well, this is not one of those stores.  It was difficult to get help loading up furniture inside the warehouse and then into the car.  Staff members literally looked the other way and ignored another staffer who was signaling for help.  There were plenty of people working in the store, but they mostly walked around or stood in groups.  Only one guy helping to load the cars--and only the people with the neon green shirts can help with that, while the dozen or so people in the striped shirts nearby cannot help or help you find someone to help.  At the end of the day, though, it's not the fault of the team on the sales floor--it's a management issue.  Everyone looked tired and stressed and so unhappy to be there.  It makes me wonder how IKEA treats its employees.  Two stars because I love the products and prices, but shopping at this IKEA is a downer.

Ikea is top drawer (nice pun) for many things home furnished. Items are, if you are unfamiliar, self-assemble but that's part of the fun - and the cheaper price. I like the fact there's the least expensive and more expensive version of just about everything. You can mix and match as well - I redid my home futon 'couch' with sold separately cushion for a different sofa they had along with the covers and viola, a new couch for me! Equally creative ideas ooze from every department. You could spend a day there just exploring. There's a restaurant which went down hill a while back - stopped serving inexpensive tasty pasta - but now selections have doubled. Staff can be slow to restock the items so you might have to prod. Prices are fairly  low for a decent entree. Near the check out there's a little food stand which carries fast-food semblance items - hot dog, frozen yogurt, and there is a small selection of take home food items like their famous swedish meatballs and gravy. Soft drink choices are on the short side, but hey, its not a Wawa or Acme. I downgrade one rating for inconsistent customer service - most people are nice and helpful - and a pesky problem of spending too much time trying to figure out the actual price on an item. You also may have to hunt and peck in the warehouse to get it, too. Item quality can be fair to low as well, but if you'd purchase utensils or a shower curtain at Walmart or Target this place will have something competitive.

Their online stock count is a lie, they refuse to re-stock their most popular dresser for a month and a half, and refuse to do a transfer from a store that has more than abundant stock. Horrible customer service. Avoid this location definitely.

We always manage to find some things here to pick up when we come. Today we got a $.99 watering can and a couple 6 pack of drinking glasses for $4.99. Prices are very reasonable I find for everything from small household items to furniture.  You can get some really neat decorating ideas from the staged showroom and there are always plenty of workers to assist if you have questions or help finding items.  Wear comfortable shoes when you come because you will do plenty of walking as this place is HUGE. There is also a cafe where you can stop for a bite to eat during your shopping or when you finish.  Like the parking garage, no sun in the summer and no snow in the winter which is a plus.

Today i write about my dining experience at the Ikea of Saint Louis, MO. 

I will first speak to y'all about the atmosphere created by Ikea. The envorinment fostered an innate love that one only feels when they meet the person they will spend the rest of their life. This instantly made me feel connected to not only the food but the nation of Sweden. I felt more close to Zlatan then ever before. 

The food was out of this country. They provided me a taste of supple lignon berries with a dash of meatballs. Their wraps where as if chance where dishing them out himself.  The chicken tenders gave Ikea an American feel, while still giving it, their own Swedish twist.  Ikea provided an affordable dinner, my only other option from here is to check out breakfast. Until I return good morrow fellow yelpers.

3.5/5

I've only been to 2 IKEAs in the United States. Both of which are on the East Coast. With total disregard to the lower sales tax rate, I'm sorry to say this is my 2nd favorite out of the 2.

Try to avoid going to IKEA on the weekends like it's your in-laws family reunion. Way too crowded, but if you gotta go you just gotta go. Food is great as always though, so at least there's that :)

For some reason, I thought I had already reviews IKEA but I haven't. I have been to this location a few times and all other locations many times. The STL location is one of the smaller IKEA's I've been to but it's a good size for STL. Everything here is nicely display....every time I enter the store...I literally want to buy the entire store LOL! I love  how they organize and decorate everything. I like how they have "directions" and a pathway where you follow so you walk through everything. 

The IKEA foodcourt has decent and very cheap food! Some of the food reminds me of grade school cafeteria food. My favorite is their almond cake! it's absolutely delicious and a must have! They also have a small foodie area downstairs along with food for sale in bulk that they provide in their cafeteria.

Great addition to the STL and I will be back!

I don't know what I can say about IKEA that hasn't already been said. I furnished my entire apartment top to bottom at IKEA for just about a grand. Well, technically that was at the Orlando location, but I wound up having to return a bunch of stuff and the Tampa location is much closer to me now. In fact, two weeks in a row I had to return items to Ikea and I wound up being waited one by the same guy - he had a terrible haircut and beard, but he was actually pretty cool. One of the little end tables with drawers I was returning kind of fell apart in the car - I didn't think they'd refund the full value, but sure enough they did! Wow!

I've been to this particular store at least four or five times now. It's soooooo much better than the Orlando store because it's so much easier to access. Just take Exit 2 off I-4, then take another exit after that and the store is literally right there! It really couldn't be any easier to access unless the ramp went right into the parking lot. Getting back ON I-4 is a bit of a pain, though becuase you have to go trawl through all these blocks that have been under construction apparently since the Carter administration.

Anyway, the Tampa location is definitely better than the Orlando store. If you live along the I-4 corridor, I'd recommend going here instead since it's easier to access, there is way more parking, and the lines have always seemed to move much more quickly than another other store.

I haven't dined at the cafeteria, though I always try to pick up some chocolate and drinks and they're always good. No point in commenting on the actual store inventory because it's been done to death by now. This is a great place to get furniture and housewares. Some of it is comparable to Walmart or Target in price, but much higher quality and of course in cache.

The furniture is cheap and the place is very confusing.  They do a good job in providing the best low quality furniture in the business.  However they do a great job of providing damaged merchandise if your looking for a little DIY project on an old couch or table.

Terrible service.  Spent our valuable time looking for bedroom furniture found all we were looking for in the showroom and then went downstairs to get the items and the bed was out of stock. No where in the showroom does it show out of stock upstairs where it should be.  We asked two gentlemen to help us and got the run around. No one seems to know anything in that store. It has a furniture pickup but when we asked if we could order the bed the gentleman said no and it was first come first served. Never seen such bad customer service.

Visited last weekend with my husband on a whim. We'd been meaning to stop down. He was an IKEA virgin and assured me he packed his credit card. 

Was a nice sized store, everything was well displayed and the staff that we encountered was friendly. We purchased a few basic things for our home and my husband now has "new kitchen" fever. Hehe 

Definitely will be back soon to make some more purchases as we continue to change our home around.

Love!  Love!  Love  IKEA!  Ikea is an ideal place to walk around to trigger ideas in your head about storage and clean lines and organizing that 'space' you have in your garage, bedroom, bathroom, kitchen - insert noun here.  Makes me want to do my own DIY house flipping show.  

And then there's Pinterest, which shows IKEA hacks.  

*sigh* wished we lived closer to one of your stores but it's either Tampa or Orlando for me -- with limited car space only means I have to make many trips - that is, until next year when an IKEA store opens up near us in Jax!  You can bet that Ikea will be on my weekly shopping list!

I spent roughly 6 hours in this IKEA yesterday trying to buy furniture for my new apartment. I found a couch that I really liked (sofa beds are where it's at) and after some struggling was able to load it into my friend's car. We got back to my apartment building and got the couch up to my 4th floor apartment, not an easy task, only to discover upon opening it that the base was severely cracked. Customer service informed me that they could not come pick it up because I hadn't paid for delivery and that I needed to bring it back to the store myself. I did NOT want to do this. After calling back and speaking to a different rep I learned that I could come back to IKEA, buy a new couch, pay to have it delivered, and the delivery people would take the broken couch when they dropped off the new one. Once the broken couch was returned to the store I would receive a full refund for it. This seemed like a big old mess to me, but also my best option. However it wouldn't be an option for anyone who can't pay for two couches in one day, even when you'll be refunded within 3-5 days. Overall this seems like really bad customer service policy to me, however everyone who I actually interacted with in the store was very helpful and apologetic, which is why they still get 3 stars. I'll likely post an update when the new couch is delivered and I see how quickly they get me my refund.

The customer service here is the worst I've encountered. Don't go to this IKEA if you can help it. They do not care about customers as people but view them as expendable and as a nuisance. I was talked to in a patronizing manner and was not heard. The other two (Elizabeth and Paramus) are at least decent and will treat you like a person and talk to you respectfully. They were willing to listen and help.

I've been wanting to try the meatballs, not that I was expecting a 5 star restaurant, but they could have some taste. They were bland, more like sawdust, the gravy was also bland and didn't look very appetizing, the apple pie wasn't any better. I had coffee which was good. I have had the wraps there, those were good. I'll stick to the Mud House, Shameless Grounds, Lulus Local Eatery, Lonas Lil Eats to name a few.

This place is madness, but in a good way. Was quite blown away by the vastness of this store. I don't even think it's a store or superstore.  It should have its own zip code it's so huge. Definitely some great buys. Great options, and great prices. Though it was interesting, annoying, but cool all at the same time when you hit the self serve area. It blew my mind we actually go around the isles of the warehouse and pick our own parts after winding around the show room floor for hours. The way they have the system set up it works pretty well even though I worry I would come home with different color parts on accident. You can even enjoy a full meal in the eatery while there. You can literally make a day of it, and trust me we did.

I'm just here for the food while my wife does some shopping.  This is a quick trip, no time for their delicious Swedish Meatballs, so I had to settle for a Cinnamon Bun sold down by the registers.  For the price of just $1 it is a sweet deal.

I only go to IKEA a few times a year, usually following a move or major reorganization.  I've been consistently satisfied with the service there.  No matter what the task at hand, I'm always able to find something to meet all of my needs without having to go to another store to find more parts and pieces.  Assembling the furniture myself is a whole other story though.

I just love IKEA, because I can always manage to find a few choice deals and leave with a smile on my face. The bright cafeteria is a great place for breakfast or lunch, and who can pass up a free cup of coffee (for IKEA Family members)? Convenient location, plentiful parking spaces.

Cheap furniture, cheap food, and a playplace for kids???? YESSSSSSS... i could spend all day here if i could. Not going to be bothered by employees, you are alone to your own device and it is simple and easy to shop here. The layout is easy enough but you can get lost. The displays will make you want to redecorate whole areas of your home.  There is a nice playroom for kids but space is limited for how many. Feed a family of 3 for under 20. What else can you say...it did live up to the hype.

Service can make such a difference!
Here are two very different service providers: one that enjoys his job: Jose; another one that hates it: Toshi.
We asked Toshi if Ikea's kitchens could have a lower height for a shorter client. His answer was NO! Our kitchens are standard and they're made for the regular people (lol! The regular, 6 ft tall people)
Then I asked Jose since I felt the lack of concern from the first "helper" and, surprisingly, he said "of course, you may just cut the base a little bit and that'll do!"
