This world is filled of Toshis( reason why I took off two stars to my rating) but thankfully there are also Joses to ensure Ikea gets the 3 stars!
Thank you Jose in the kitchen department. Toshi, I think fast food restaurants need some laconic, one word people like you!

IKEA is one of those places that you get excited about going into, especially if your looking to do some decorating. The concept is unparalleled to any other American department store. There's just a plethora to explore and creativity and ideas are illuminated. It's good for all ages too, especially to brighten kid's imagination. Whenever I go I enjoy being inspired by the decor and interior designs displayed. The prices are sometimes good, even great, and other times not so good. The cafe area is absolutely wonderful; there's great prices for awesome taste and portions. On the lower level there's a mini frozen food section and cafe area for quick eats. IKEA is massive, so wearing comfortable shoes and clothes is advised! Oh, and remember to not get lost. Overall, it's really a cool place to shop--helpful employees and unique finds.

I've been going to Ikea since I was a kid in various locations. I frequented the location in Hicksville, NY for many years with my family. Also stopped at the one in Baltimore, MD on my way to college on I-95. When they finally opened up in Tampa, I rejoiced!!! Finally, my go-to furniture and textile store was here!

As with any Ikea, the traffic inside and outside is horrific (this is to be expected). If you are in a rush, don't go to Ikea. It is built like a maze and there are zombie families walking through the aisles, making it impossible to swiftly move about. Moseying is what this place is all about. Aimlessly walking through each decorated department of the store is the best way to approach this shopping experience. There are two floors and it is very hard to navigate if you haven't been here at least 5 times. Not to mention a 'warehouse area' to pick up larger items that you see on display while on your journey. 

So you may ask why I would still give Ikea 4 stars despite the navigation frustration? Because I love a good deal and a decent product. Ikea has that! I have bought my couch, futon, TV stand, dresser, cookware, silverware, lighting, batteries, bedding, towels, and half of the other stuff in my house from here and have never had an issue with quality. Ikea has great prices and great products if you aren't too picky/fancy and don't mind putting things together yourself (make sure you have a screw driver!!). Also, get ready to carry your stuff since Ikea does NOT have bags. Bring your own or buy a giant blue bag for 99 cents. 

This location is on Adamo Drive in Tampa, south of Ybor and across the street from Coppertail Brewery. My best advice is to grab a beer or two and head out for shopping with a mellow attitude. Oh, and if you get hungry they have amazing food for excellent prices! $1 sodas and ice creams and 50 cent hot dogs! Don't forget to take home some giant cinnamon rolls!

I was introduced to ikea years ago in Chicago and was sad to know I was moving where no IKEA was! But now I am happy... Well, I was always happy just a little more now. 

Not sure if it's the big sized warehouse, the people, the furniture or the food but I just like going to IKEA. I enjoy that you can actually see a set up of different rooms of your house or office. Gives you ideas and have your blood flowing of what you want and/or need. 

I think IKEA is great for College students, start up home and those on a budget. Not to say no one else can shop there. Some of the items do appear to be cheap but I have to say I purchased a kitchen table and 4 chairs 8 years ago and it's still standing. After putting your creativity (or theirs) together, you'll come out with something nice. 

I hate shopping alone so I always seem to have someone with me when I go. This last trip was just to grab a desk and food. Ended up eating that delicious triple chocolate cake ((BEWARE)) it's to DIE for! Grabbing a desk, flatware and getting spinned around in the aisle at the self serve station while sitting on the cart. Don't think it was safe or allowed but it was fun! 

At the end of the day.... Yes. I will always go back to IKEA. On or off a budget!

TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE. I've never left a one star review before, but after being hung up on twice, on hold for 20 minutes, and then hung up on another two times, I am FED UP. I was trying to buy my whole kitchen from them, but apparently they aren't interested in my business. That's fine, I'm happy to take it elsewhere.

I took my young son knowing there was a kids club .  I was expecting to be able to drop him off  and enjoy the shopping experience I've heard so much about .  When we got there they told us there was a 45 minute wait  before they can take any more kids .  That's okay I thought  this won't take that long. At first I was so impressed with this store. I felt like I was walking into a shopping Wonderland.  Since I had my son with me I decided to take advantage of the cafe  before the shopping adventures began. When I got to the food I realized it was simply bad cafeteria food. It tasted just like it looked, terrible.  From there we moved on to the showroom. At first I really enjoyed looking at all the different designs. But soon I started to feel like a rat in a maze.  There was no map or salespeople to direct me to the area that I would find what I was looking for.  I find found myself getting frustrated because I felt like I was being forced to go through every section.  Finally I found my items I wanted and they have no tags on them to tell me the price or the item numbers. After what seemed like forever I made it to the warehouse. Finally, I think someone will be here to help me find my items. Wrong, look it up yourself on their slow lagging computers. Finally two out of the three items are in stock. The computer tells you the aisle and a shelf number (similar to Home Depot.) When I locate where items should be  every pieces out of stock! What an utter waste of time!! I really don't understand how this place is so busy. The prices aren't that good, there's no one to help you,  you have to put it together yourself, and oh yeah go ahead and load it yourself too. Give me a real furniture store any day you can keep your Cafe and kids club.

I've been to a dozen or so Ikea locations up and down the east coast. One thing is for sure, one is not better than the rest.  They all offer the same stock, are about the same size, and have the same set up - displays upstairs, inventory downstairs.  In the 20 + years I've been a customer it's been a love/hate affair.

LOVE the displays providing room design ideas, the multiple ways they use the same pieces, and the fact that you can see and feel how each piece functions.  Love the options and choices.  Love the prices and abundance of inventory, the way things are packed to make transporting home in a car easy.  Love that they also have Swedish food to eat there or take home prepackaged.

HATE the return process (if you can even get them to take something back), the hunt for the merchandise on your list, the complex assembly with limited instructions.  Hate the poor quality and the fact that inventory and parts change often and chances are if something breaks you can't get replacement parts.  Hate the long lines that are present at every location, the lack of help loading.  Hate that you have to buy their bag if you want your items bagged.

One thing I have discovered is even if you scour the catalog for days on end, make a list and check it twice once you get to the store all will change.  You'll see a piece in a display different from the catalog and fall in love, or the opposite - you'll see the piece you came for and the display isn't how you envisioned.  Either way sometimes too many choices equal too much frustration.

This coming from a woman that once packed up my car, measured the space remaining, and went back and purchased more.  That drove home two hours down the turnpike smack dab against the windshield because the driver's seat held not only myself but a box.  Or that I once loaded my car so full I couldn't even see my children.  Yes, all this has happened and happens all the time.  If you want a good comical reality experience just sit in the parking lot and watch people load for a few hours....

Overall as I aged so did my style.  While the catalog and displays are nice, rarely if ever does that same piece look like that in my own home.  My daughter's bedroom was entirely Ikea and in less than a year we had to do multiple repairs on our own.  Drawer bottoms are week, side rails are plastic, beds and dressers are no more than particleboard wrapped in a laminate skin.  Wheels on trundle beds are undersized and the design faulty.  What works for the Swedes unfortunately doesn't work for American children.

As a middle aged woman I now come for the inspiration.  For ideas that I can take home and rework with more structurally sound pieces.  I come for the accessories, the candles in bulk, and the furniture pieces that are inexpensive and will only get occasional use.  I come for the unique - things that can only be found at Ikea.  For a day browsing with girlfriends or killing time in a vacation location.

So this love  affair for the most part is over, or maybe just categorized to friends with benefits.

Ohhh IKEA..... I believe IKEA provides the best affordable furniture option for college/graduate students. 

The good: Basically an eye candy store because most things look beautiful in the rooms IKEA designed. I appreciated the very clear labeling of sections and how they made a scene for the kitchen, living room, bedroom, etc. It made it easier for me to see how I would incorporate the furniture or items into my own apartment. Also, the quality of items does vary but most of the times if you pay big bucks for something it will have great quality. The joy of shopping comes from finding the inexpensive items that still have awesome quality. For example, I recommend the bath mats/rugs (BADAREN); they hold up very well and feel great on your feet out of the shower! 


The bad: They force you to walk through the entire store almost (there are ways to take a shortcut) before you can pay for your items. You almost always have to assembly your furniture yourself. Obviously, you could pay for someone to do it, but if you aren't great at assembly you can end up with a product that doesn't seem to be as good as the furniture on the floor. Lastly, they don't have any free bags for small items your have to purchase them...

Ok, I may be biased being married to a Swede, right off the plane, not boat.  I have visited Ikea restaurants the world over and they have great food for a reasonable price.  I don't think I have eaten in any of the places that they offered horse meat in their meat balls though.  I do know the menus by heart so it would be just too much to type if I gave a blow by blow description of all of them.  They have days/nights when kids eat for free.  Certain holidays are celebrated with an all you can eat buffet like Jul, Pask, Kraftor festival etc.  Desserts are yummy and not too sweet.

I LOVE IKEA!! Always have.

Everytime I go in there, I'm blasted with ideas and new delights to behold. I remember the first time I walked in there and marveled how they seemed to think of everything. My brain went into imagination overdrive.

Pencils and wish lists, tape measures, and shopping bags dispersed all over the store... I loved how everything was set up so you could see exactly how it would work. I just noticed the lockers and recycling stations. And did you see the kids puzzle stations in various places? I never noticed those before.

And so much stuff! Everything from appliances and wall tile to candles and drawer handles. ALL the details. They seem to think of everything. Oh yeah, and there's a built in daycare. Smaland.

Even the restaurant, with their Swedish meatballs and gravlax, is set up with ease and organization in mind. The food is good and cheap too! And you can buy the stuff for your own home freezer.

Everything in this place is streamlined to be practical and inexpensive. I love it so much!! Have you received their catalog yet? Its got articles on food and design. 

And did you know they are expanding? I can't wait to see that! I was disappointed to know it's not a new location, but an addition to the old one. Oh well...maybe that's a good thing for me. If they had a location closer to me, i'd probably be there every week.
Returns at ikea are such a pain. I stood in line for a little over a half hour just to get to the cashier. Definitely not a quick return option.
modern looking furniture for a reasonable price, you must be prepared to assemble though, this location has a small deli like restaurant and a restaurant.....

Pretty darn disappointed in their pillow selection! Other than that, I love that they're highly organized and have a dandy map and paper handy for you to write on. There is a kiddy area too so you don't have to worry about your kids running off or breaking anything. Throughout this HUGE store, there are mock set ups of all rooms in your home- very ideal! I myself know that shopping for the home can be extremely stressful when solely envisioning "what if" furniture options. hands down, they have amazing (and cheap!) food in their "restaurant" area. I love their cheesecake and my carnivore friends seem to enjoy their Swedish meatballs! They have a row of loading spaces right on outside the exit so you can easily pull up and pile your new home furniture and decorations into your vehicle. My biggest suggestion is to avoid going there when you're short on time. Commit to spending at least 1 hour in there! P.s., the chocolate bars you can purchase upon paying are phenomenal. Especially the hazelnut milk chocolate! Nom nom nom. Enjoy! Xo

We like to go here to eat....oh and shop too! Lol Where else can a family of 5 eat a pretty darn good meal for only $23.50. I love their ribs and my wife loves their Swedish meatballs. This kids dig the mac&cheese! All and all a really good bargain!

Went to IKEA on a Sunday afternoon although it was still busy not as busy as going on a Saturday I was shopping for a new desk of course I found one.    The place was very clean and there was plenty help around definitely  will be going again.  Looks like Sunday is a good day to go but also I'm told if you can go in the middle of the day on a weekday will be even better.

My reason  for rating this ikea a two star is because I had my pieces ordered to set up my bed awhile ago. They told me it would take about 7-14 business days but it has now been almost over an month. I have called and emailed customer service several times about this issue and all they can say it wait till the end of the week. I am tired of waiting for something that should have been delivered  awhile ago. I have asked for a tracking number but for some odd reason ikea doesn't have access to this. I am really disappointed with their service to just deliver a few pieces. I have been sleeping on the floor for the past month because I can't even set my bed up. :(((((

AH IKEA... We swung by IKEA while in St. Louis for the weekend.  How could we resist?  My word of advice- go in with a plan or you will fall victim to their low prices and walk out with things you didn't know you "needed"!

We bought 6 fake plants. We can't wait to get one in Fishers, IN! 2017 I believe!

Can't really give this IKEA more than one star. I did a pick and delivery order, and one of the items was input incorrectly. Called up to change it the same day of the order, and they did make the correction. Three days later, when the order was delivered, it had the wrong items still. Delivery service gave me a bunch of trouble about not wanting to accept the incorrect items. When I called IKEA back, I was told that they will redeliver it, but that I cannot choose a date or time for the delivery. Given that my wife and I both work, this is unacceptable. But now because of IKEAs screw up, we have to take a day off from work to get our correct sofas redelivered. I will gladly pay more to buy furniture from somewhere else in the future. I will not be returning to IKEA.

For all of IKEA's creative efficiencies, the furniture pickup area is always painfully slow.  Lots of co-workers standing around while you wait 30min+ for one item.

It is also common to see only one or two checkout lines open with excessively long lines. 

One would think that a flagship store next door to IKEA's US Corporate HQ would be much better.

IKEA is all things right with your morning breakfast! This is a throwback to the old style of department store cafeteria. You grab a tray and step up to the glass cases to choose from any number of breakfast items including bagel & smoked salmon. If a hot breakfast is what suites your fancy they have a number of items to choose from all under $3. 

I'm a total sucker for the Swedish American Breakfast for $2. This is comprised of 2 Swedish Pancakes a side of home style potatoes, scrambled eggs, & 2 chicken sausage links. I know most Midwesterner's will initially recoil in fear of any non pork sausage but don't. These are some of the best sausages on any breakfast menu. 

Finally, the plate is topped with the optional Lingonberry sauce a traditional Swedish fruit topping for pancakes. If you are unfamiliar with Lingonberries just think of a smaller more flavorful cranberry. Of course, you can get a more state-side tradition of syrup at the condiment stand. Top this meal off with a 45¢ cup of Joe and for under $2.50 you get a very satisfying & delicious breakfast.

IKEA is famous for their $1 cinnamon rolls, people are known to drive hours to get a half a dozen of these delicious gems. Unfortunately, this IKEA location either has their ovens to warm or they cook the rolls too long because they are rock hard. In all my visits there I have only bought one roll that was worthy of the IKEA tradition. This is the only thing that needs improvement.

If you want the best value breakfast in town head over to IKEA before 10:30am to get a taste of Swedish deliciousness. By 10:31 it goes the way of the Swedish meatballs.

What a crazy place. Imagine 3 WalMarts stacked one on top of the other, with a forward motion kind of walking pattern, no discernible indication of what department you're in or headed for, and signs designed to mislead you. Seriously, try actually following the signs, I dare you. At least two of them steered us straight into walls. I was looking for one kitchen item, but it seemed like every department had kitchen stuff. At long last stumbling onto the thing I was looking for, I was told it was out of stock. Of course they couldn't do anything customer-friendly like sell me the floor model: that's what a good store would do. The young woman who tried to help me said they might be in stock again in a few weeks, but she couldn't put my name on it. Then she offered to put my name on it. She said it would be in stock the weekend of September 3, but they were having a production problem and it wouldn't be here until October 27. Which was it, I asked? She reassured me it would be in stock on September 3, and I would get an email then. But due to a production problem it wouldn't be in until October 27. As you probably guessed, I am still waiting. The item in question is very nice: but I don't hold out much hope of ever getting it.

Made it through the visit without breaking up with my husband so that rumor is dispelled! Would have been nice if the item we were looking for didn't have a red go pick it up yourself tag only to go round the woods and over a hill to grandmother's house and be told that item isn't in that area anymore and hasn't been for weeks but they should have it updated in the next two weeks and could we trek back through the forest and search the shelves where the item was displayed. 

We did, pushing against the flow of human salmon, and found the item on the floor under other items. Clutching it like lost treasure we fled to the checkout and to our car. 

IKEA isn't a place to wander unless you have a support group. Don't go alone. Always tell someone you are going and how long you think you'll be so someone will start looking for you if too much time passes. We've all seen those survival movies. Don't be a hero.

This review is directly addressed at the gummy candy wall at this Ikea. This section is a lot of fun, and you just fill a paper bag with what you want and then pay by weight. I have tried every one of the gummy candies on this wall except the licorice ones (I can't stand the taste of black licorice). My personal favorites are the fried eggs (lemony orange yolk with a wonderful marshmallow bottom), the gummy frogs and mice, the red flat pieces with the S on them, and the forest berries and the gummy berries, and the social media candy. 

Ones I wasn't particularly impressed with were the racecars (basically a lump of hard wax with a tiny strip of hibiscus flavoring in the middle), the vanilla marshmallow (it was a little hard and dried out), and the rolled up sour strips (it tastes like a weird combination of watermelon and bubble gum).

the store and furniture is fine, i found what i needed on my own basically with the help of their website and looking up where the item would be in the store. and thank GOD i did because the staff at this ikea that i dealt with was horrid! I asked one worker to direct me to the aisle i was looking for, since it was my first time being in there, and she replied back with an attitude telling me to "follow the arrows" in a tone that sounded like I was a idiot for not knowing that. Then the cashier screamed at me saying "next" so i would move up in line. She also proceeded to treat me like absolute crap, and like she had no time or patience to ring up my item. just ridiculous, as a supervisor at a retail store, it really isnt THAT hard to help customers with respect and a good attitude.
The cafe upstairs is amazing and the wide range and selection ikea has for home improvement and even for restaurants is exceptional.

We all love IKEA as long as one does not need help from anyone or return an item. There are 8 counters, 7 closed. 1 open and literally over 20 people waiting in line. That sucks.  And no manager to be found. How sad.  I hope somebody at IKEA does something about this.

What can I say...their products are cheap and decent quality. Service is horrible. Waited at returns for 30 min with 2 people in front of me. Employees are very very slow with no sense of urgency. Ridiculous

My family and I always been buying our house equipment and mostly everything there. But I don't care much about the equipments as long it's good. Every time I go to Ikea I must have there meat balls and there mash potatoes it's like a must have food for me. Or the visit there is not complete.

Cashiers are understsffed and not trained to do their job. Shopping experience at checkout gets worse everytime I come. 15 minutes wait to pay on a Monday afternoon.!!
Thumbs down to cashier 10049194 and to store manager.

This is the worst place ever. Whatever you do DO NOT buy a kitchen through this place. The worst experience of my life. First off the delivery was trashy and all of our pieces were brought to us wrapped in beer cases. When we asked the delivery guys if all of the pieces were here( it's their job to do a piece count and they never did) they said yes and encouraged us to sign off the waver.  And of course we didn't have all the pieces. We're missing 3 cabinet doors and all the legs to our kitchen. So when we want to ikea to explain what happened they initially blamed us and said it was our fault we didn't count all 108 pieces when they were delivered. ( did I mention that was the delivery guys job?) that's not what I want to hear. So after 4 hours of bullshitting about how we can resolve this issue so that everyone is happy we left IKEA again only to find out the guy that helped us, didn't really help us. He didn't know what he was doing and let us leave with the wrong sizes and different color than our original plan. So we have to go back once again. My advice to everyone out there is make IKEA your last choice. Even the prices suck.

9/30 paid cash on a purchase of a sofa bed w/delivery and assembly set up for 10/1. Must to my amazement on 10/1 when the delivery company showed up they do not assembly.  When calling IKEA I was told their sales person set up the service wrong and I could refuse delivery, which I did, was also told it would be 48hr before I could get my cash back.  

What I didn't understand or appreciate is on 10/3 I was told my case would not be looked at for at least 48hr and I could not get a refund until the items had been counted back into stock.  It's not like I hire the delivery company IKEA did so why did I have to wait what was not longer than 48 hrs for my cash.  On 10/4 I was told by someone in their customer service department that I could pick up my money -- only when I got to the store again they told me their employee had made a mistake, and the items which mind you were place back on their truck still had not arrive to the store.

I waited from Sat until Thurs to get money back for their mistakes.  Where is the customer service these day---- it was their mistake.

Make sure if you buy you are able to pick up and return item yourself.  Don't pay cash at least on your credit card you have the right to stop payment. 
  Personally I will never shop there again -- the Dump has far better service.

The review largely reflects the return/exchange center and the staff there. They are all extremely knowledgeable about Ikea products and helpful when it comes to returns/exchanges.  We had an issue with part of our bed and they made the replacement process easy and quick. They also were extremely pleasant.

I like this store otherwise (clean, great selection, products are always in stock, etc) however the checkout lines are ALWAYS ridiculous. (hence the lack of five stars) and I think they should have more cashiers on hand most days.

Best IKEA in North America, as far as I'm concerned.

Why?

Because, like everything else in St. Louis, it arrived 10 years later than everywhere else, there's plenty of free parking, you can drive there within 20 minutes from anywhere else in town and it's never that crowded.

It makes shopping at the IKEAs in bigger cities seem like a barbaric experience by comparison.

I've been putting off going to Ikea since it came to St. Louis because it was so over-hyped and EVERYONE seemed to be just way too enthusiastic about it. Like, calm down. Of course, I finally caved and walked in last night. Now I get it. 

I only came to browse, but I could have easily blown an entire paycheck and then sold some plasma to come back for that medicine cabinet. Everything was so adorable and hip and modern. I wanted it all! They have it all set up so well, and you can tell they have top-notch designers making that place extra cool. I want my apartment to look that nice.

Prices were great for most things. I mean, let's face it... I'll probably never spend $1000 on a sofa even if I had that kind of cash to throw around. But there was plenty in my price range where I don't feel like I'm losing out on quality or aesthetics.

I'm moving in two months, and everything I'm buying for my new place will come from Ikea. My cashier was funny and friendly and we made effortless banter. All in all, I'm happy I finally got to shop here.
I can't complain about this place. They have such reasonable prices, a huge selection, and affordable food. The employees are also friendly. You can make a whole day out of IKEA.

I've been waiting to experience IKEA. I was soo excited from pulling in the parking lot and being able to grab a great spot, to walking in the door and riding up the escalator. My first stop was to be the food court, so I could try those meatballs so many people rave about. Our first stop was the mini food stand where the cinnamon rolls are made, of course we had to try one for a $1. The BF really liked it. I prefer Cinnabon. We were informed that the food court was another level up. Unfortunately the rows and rows of food cases weren't filled with a variety of items, actually they were mainly empty. It worked out for me because I would have tried some of everthing in the cases if it looked good. We were in luck though to try the meatball plate and since the chicken tenders looks pretty good, we were able to snab some of them along with a slice of swedish apple cake. Of course the food prices are a steal, very affordable for a meal. The meatballs weren't bad, I guess I would get a plate again if I were hungry, seriously hungry. I could easily skip the food court again unless we went for brekfast so I could try that. I really enjoyed walking around each area and playing in the room displays, YES I said playing in the room displays. I love how they setup each room to give you ideas for your own home. Ohhh wait, what I really love are their prices and the selection of items!!! The bathroom sinks and options were great, the prices for the shower curtains were a steal. I grabbed a quality shower curtain for $9.99. I paid the same $9.99 at Bed Bath & Beyond for cheap plastic. And of course I loved all the kitchen items since the kitchen is my spot. I would definately go back for certain items like bathroom accessories and kitchen utensils, etc. I do not think we would buy any furniture there though. The items look nice but various chairs, tables, beds, etc upon closer inspection seemed cheap and uncomfortabe.

IKEA has always held a special place in my heart, but the handful of trips I've made here over the last few weeks has made me fall in love with it all over again. Just to clarify, these visits were mostly either to grab stuff I didn't initially buy on my prior visit, or to return things that didn't fit once I got home. (All my fault, not IKEA's)

At this point, you should know what IKEA is all about, so I won't go into that, but instead leave you with a few helpful tips & comments...

If you come on a weekend, you WILL wait in long lines both at the checkout & returns/exchanges counter. It's a fact. If you can swing it, come on a weekday/night and it'll often feel like you have the store all to yourself. 

However, the trade off for coming on a weeknight is the food is not as plentiful or fresh. Avoid the garlic toast on a weeknight, since it's likely been sitting there all day and now is as hard as a rock. They lose a star for removing the Lingonberry juice from all soda fountains in the store. This juice would often times be my sole reason for visiting in past trips. Very, very, very sad they removed it!  

If you are returning something, grab a number ticket from the red deli-style ticket dispenser to the left of the returns counter. And don't be that a-hole who throws a fit because you were waiting around for 20 min before you even noticed it. (There is airways at least one!) IKEA has one of the best return policies, as they accept returns for one full year from purchase, just make sure to save that receipt!

Also, IKEA Family... this store membership card is totally free and grants access to sale prices on certain items. It also gives you some free stuff (free coffee in cafe, and extra time at the in-store daycare), so make sure to sign up for it at one of the orange kiosks near checkout!

I have been usually pleased with the food court at IKEA , but recently they have made some changes . They no longer serve Lingonberry juice from the fountain. You have to buy a single serving. Why the Change? The cashier was even rude. I asked about my rewards cards and asked if he would accept a phone # while he was ringing me up . The food item had a discount . When I asked him again ., He shorted " You have to have it with you " i was surprised at the tone of an Ikea Employee. I am so disappointed.  First time I had a bad experience.

The veggie balls are not worthwhile.. disappointed... can't believe you can't get the same set up as regular swedish meatballs but with veggie balls. The staff seemed extremely confused at my request. The veggie balls were soggy and lacked flavor... veggies were microwave equivalent and the lentils were the only good flavor on this dish. Not what I envisioned when I heard there were now veggie balls. 

Furniture is alright, I came here for the swedish meatball experience. Going to stick with the original!

BEWARE!!!  These people are unbelievably bad. If you order comes delivered properly then things work out fine. If not, then disaster. I purchased an entire apartment and spent tens of hours picking out furniture only to have the delivery be totally incomplete. They were missing 10 items and had 5 wrong! Their solution was for me to rebuy the sofa and the have it delivered the next day and receive a credit for the missing item, what happened? They did not show up at all for the entire day!  Don't buy from these people!!!

I love ikea but they might as well shutdown small land if they're never going to have enough help to watch the kids that are being brought there.  Every time I've come they have a few kids there but claim a 1 hour wait.  Why have a daycare that never has open spaces?

Remind me to take a Xanax if I ever step foot in an IKEA ever again. The feeling of being suffocated by cheap Swedish furniture will haunt my dreams for the next few weeks. I couldn't even find anything I was looking for. I've never not wanted to be at a place more than IKEA.
Ikea quality has been going down hill for a few years, prices seem low but items are dollar store quality. Restaurant used to be good but not anymore, associates are rude.
This place is awesome. You can find Home,furniture, kitchens, appliances in a reasonable price. Also  try out their Swedish restaurant they have very good there.

Big place... lot of stuff to see. Found a nice new cutting board, and some cork trivets for some excellent prices. Just sort of rushed through and looked at everything... pretty cool First time here... will come back when I need something.
Love this place to shop.Very clean place. Price not too bad.I never missed to eat my favorite yummy swidish meat balls everytime i visit ikea.

I'd rather use dumpster scraps for furniture than deal with this place again. 

I've been ordering from Ikea in Brooklyn for years and never had any issues, even with enormous orders for furnishing my entire home. I placed a straight forward order from Conshohocken and boy did they screw it up! They delivered a sofa cover for a sofa I don't have and forgot a table and a chair. The delivery estimate was a week off (I know what the word "estimate" means, but a week late when the delivery estimate is two weeks? A three week wait for furniture is ridiculous.)  I wont even get into how awful the delivery service (XPO logistics) was. Thankfully nothing I ordered was breakable! Every box was crushed, filthy, and some even had muddy footprints all over them. Unacceptable. Imagine muddy boxes sliding across your newly renovated apartments crisp white carpet. *Insert internal screaming here*

I had to call customer service (an hour on hold) because they forgot the chair and table, and now it's two weeks after the first delivery and I'm still missing things I purchased 5 weeks ago. I could have chopped down a tree and built the stuff from scratch faster than this. 

I called today to find out where the stuff is (15 minute hold) and they tell me it's going to be ANOTHER week. On top of that they said the replacement order is for TWO tables and the chair.  Two tables? You already gave me a free sofa cover, now you're giving me a free table? I don't want your free furniture!!!! I just want what I paid for in a reasonable amount of time!

Do I believe when the rest of my order is delivered that it's going to be what I ordered? Am I actually getting two tables and a complete chair? Or will I get some random surprise? Perhaps the sofa that the free cover is for? Is it actually going to be delivered this week? Only time will tell.

My Love and Hate relationship with IKEA
.   It is worst than walking through a corn maze 
I also worry about an emergency situation.  You cannot cross over or easily find an exit.   There are arrows on the floor.   How about in case of a power outage.  You cannot see arrows.    This design is very flawed.not a good flow 

My LOVE is their selections  quality and pricing   Their staff is friendly and helpful.   And my LOVE for IKEA is bigger .  I wish someone would look into the floor design and understand the need to change it.

This store is definitely NOT user-friendly for the handicapped or senior citizens. While they have wheelchairs, which is fine if you have somebody to push you around in it, they do not have motorized scooters like most other stores have available. The first time I visited and asked about them, I was told that the powers that be at IKEA have concerns that someone might drive one down the stairs. As a senior with arthritis in my hips and back, their concrete floors are a real pain to walk on for any length of time. 

I would give them one star, except for the fact that they do have a wonderful cafeteria. I usually stop in for Swedish meatballs for lunch when I'm in the neighborhood. Also I like the little market place on the first floor. Otherwise, I don't bother with IKEA.

This is the fourth or fifth IKEA location I've been in and this is by far my least favorite. The dining location is huge, however; the service is not comparable to other locations and the tables were clearly not bused in hours. Parking was simple and in a garage which I appreciated. I think the layout of the store was consistent with the other locations I have been at, but it was clear that displays were not up-kept.

This is our first time to go Ikea. Show room is great feels like i want to buy everything but we know what to buy cabinet and bed for our teenager. We easily find what we our looking for. Some of the people in the showroom are not that friendly (maybe they are in a hurry to go home for Christmas). One guy help us very nice. Are done in no time printed out all the items we wanted. Problem came when we are in the warehouse. A lot of attendant just chatting to each other and make faces when we ask for help  (every poor customer service). We "almost" got what we wanted (wishful thinking) but we cant find the bed head board. We ask for help and 2 guys just look up and said oh we dont have that. Hope there is coordination on the showroom and warehouse  that when they printed those items we wanted they can tell  if the ITEM is not in stock. Now we have to go back. One star for customer service

I experienced the absolute worst shopping experience at IKEA today.  They had a product in their scratch and dent section, clearly marked with sales signs for $34.90.  It rang up as $49.99 and they would not honor the sales sign.  At this point, the cashier who had rung up the first item, became rude and closed her drawer and a new girl took over.  Bad move from a customer service stand point and by the store managers admission, but did nothing to correct the matter other than to allow another customer, in a different line to chime in where she had no business and escalated the conversation with the manager allowing the conversation to get more heated.  We ended up not buying what we came for and I wanted to publicly condemn the Christian spewing busy body who had no business in our conversation with the store manager.  I have been a Christian for over 50 years and have never seen a so called Christian intentionally cause such an issue, nor have I seen such an inept manager who let sales be adversely affected like this one did.  I am glad that IKEA feels that they are at a point where they can give extremely poor customer service, allow other customers to escalate what had been a pleasant experience up till checkout and allow customers to leave with an extremely sour experience and not even tried to resolve the issue.  -5 stars on customer service and the absolute worst fail for the management at the south Tampa store.  They are just about at Rock bottom in customer service.

We bought 2 kitchens at IKEA. My parents house and ours. First one was just ok, second one is still a disaster. First we were not happy because they told us they can't go all the way to the ceiling with the install of our first one but it's custom cabinets so then they did it for us anyways. They should tell you that immediately because we were under the impression that was ok Because Who wants a 3 inch gap between their cabinets and the ceiling ? So once they raised our cabinets we were happy. Convinced our parents to buy a kitchen then this happens.....our island was glued with cheap glue it's been 5 months and it's falling apart! We called install company and they said we must make a claim. We made a claim it's been a few weeks no word on when it will get fixed. So much for 20 year warranty. The second kitchen is the biggest mess I've seen in my life. The 200 we paid for someone to design the kitchen was a waste. The guy totally blew it off. He didn't give them the carousel which they wanted in corner cabinet. He didn't utilize the enormous space they had in their kitchen. Parts were missing and everyday during a 5 day install they sent my parents to exchange parts for them at IKEA each trip inside the store took about 2 hours. 5 days in a row. The installers didn't install the lights in the cabinets, the hood above the stove and they were paid for it! The lights job is a huge job and they were left to dangle under the cabinets so now my parents are forced to remove the lights and return them at least get back the money for that! Also we had 3 electricians come And we tried to get the lights installed they all said that it should have been done before cabinets were mounted. I'll leave pictures with this review of those dangling lights under the cabinets. Very unhappy I would give negative stars if I could. We flip homes and an IKEA kitchen will never be an option in my house again.

Visited IKEA yesterday looked like a big box store from the outside . Inside it is the world of organization . You go upstairs  to find How to fit more in with less . It has a cafeteria with great Swedish meatballs and fish dinners , for a break from all this  shopping . the layout are rooms designed and each piece is marked with s skew which will help you locate the product downstairs . It seemed to b dominated by Swedish design but I found more made in china than I wanted to . The furniture I did not think much of  square and plain and more utilitarian like first time buyers or apt owners  with limited space would find appealing . Some of the kitchen designs were very cool. Or you could design your own  room  Lighting was small led to large and luminous .  Down stairs they serve hot cinnamon rolls to take home and other goods from Sweden even smoked salmon .The potato chips made  like Swedish chips  but made in the USA ??? . It was a nice visit  you can certainly find things you need want and may need in the future, nice relaxing day didn't break the bank and picked up some bargains . Some food is frozen bring a cooler and ice . Enjoy

Food is good and for a family of 6 it is the same price as McDonalds with better food and options.  We are late so most of the deserts and sandwich options were gone but we had salmon, chicken tenders, and of course Swedish meatballs and it was all good.  It's cafeteria style and even with long lines it goes fast.  The only negative is that they are slow To replace silverware, cups, and trays as they were running short but beyond that it's good food for the money.  Come for the experience!

The part in the movie 500 Days of Summer where they are in IKEA is amazing and I think about that whenever I go in the store. I always get lost and/or find the longest way to get to one section of the store. Honestly, I don't mind losing my way in IKEA because it's such a great store and if I had more time this past visit, I would have gotten a meal here. It's a very unique buying process and I appreciate having to look far and wide for items because they are great products.

I realize IKEA isn't a restaurant but I had two slices of pizza there today that I loved sooo much I wanted to make note of it here.  Besides tasting good each was a nice size (portion) which I appreciated. Enjoy  definitely!!!!

We spent several hrs there and $500 later even before leaving the building i realized I forgot to hand my reward membership card. When I went to the returns/exchange area a lady said the transaction was locked in and I'd have to return all the items and then she said I would've to go back in the store and purchase everything because once I return the items, they need to go back in to the inventory.  What kinda BS is that!? And she said all that with a straight face! I walked away. I went back to the original cashier told him the saga, he called he supervisor and voila! It literally took her 1 min to do the receipt correction! 
Guess what lady at the return/exchange area?!?! You have no clue how to talk to a customer. You've no right to lie to a customer. You think we are all stupid?! I knew there was no point in argue with you. However, Very disappointed!!! Thank you to that nice gentle man and the supervisor for fixing the receipt for me.
Cool store for college and city living. Not impressed with the swedish meatballs. Taste like processed sausage.

Every once in a blue moon we get the hankering to walk around Ikea and look at stuff we don't really need. I have been going to Ikea for a long time now and remembered the buzz when the first US store opened in King of Prussia. I am glad I don't have to hike it up there and the South Philly store is pretty convenient and close.

Ikea is a good time and I actually dig their food, guilty pleasure admitted. We were not too hungry as we just came from Kanella, so we just had some dessert and coffee in the cafeteria. As full as I was, I almost went for the meatballs and Loganberry sauce. I had this raspberry mascarpone cake treat that was pretty darn good. The Swedish apple pie was decent and the coffee was not great but not terrible either. Prices are reasonable in the cafeteria.

Ikea has lost some of its shine as Home Depot and Lowes offer some similar products in the same price range. I do think Ikea does a great job with their displays and room set-ups. I have always liked Ikea's concept and over the years I have become pretty efficient at assembling my families and friends furniture. My woodworking, Lego and origami skills have found a good fit. 

This store does seem to always have long lines at checkouts.  They could use a little help with that aspect. Also returns are usually a nightmare with a long wait. They need to do a better job with both of these aspects at this location.

Just under 4 stars.

IKEA is definitely a store for the modern times, a lot of people go a little crazy over the store which at first I didn't understand but after being in one several times its easy to see why.  It's a very addicting place to shop, and for the college student or family just starting out, it offers a lot of great furniture and decorating choices without gouging your wallet too badly.  

If you are expecting to just walk in and walk out of an IKEA and you haven't been before, that is not an easy task to achieve. between the size of the store and the layout of the departments, and the displays, you can easily and I speak this from experience, get lost quickly in the store.   be sure to utilize the guide signs, and follow the arrows on the floor and the department numbers and you will navigate yourself nicely.  

IKEA is loaded with all kinds of great items from furniture to rugs and bedding. a lot of items are made to be built by you the consumer. but speaking yet again from experience, the directions are easy to follow, and even the less brainy can comprehend and get the job done.  One thing I have found is don't expect IKEA furniture to last forever, because it doesn't. however with proper care, it will last you as long as you treat it well.    

There are plenty of helpful sales associates on the floor to help you with shopping and answering your questions, and there are plenty of signs scattered all over the store giving you simple yet informative directions around the store.  If you get hungry while shopping be sure to stop by their cafe and have a delicious lunch and its reasonably priced. and at no extra charge you get to enjoy your meal in a beautiful windowed setting...  

I don't make regular trips to IKEA simply because I don't need to spend money which would happen each time I entered the doors. IKEA is definitely a good addition to the growth of St. Louis, its a shame it took so long to get one. if you haven't been to it yet, do yourself a favor and at least check it out, you will most likely like what you find, and will definitely be returning for at least 1 more visit...

So I went into Ikea trying to find hardware for the bed I purchased in 2009. I knew it was a long shot but I was amazed with how knowledgable the staff in bedding was. 

Soon as I showed him a photo of my late model sleigh bed he knew exactly what it was called. He gave me the instructions and I was able to collect all of the hardware in the returns department!

This is an amazing Ikea, i'm so glad I live so close! They are going to get too much of my money now.

I went to ikea today for one purpose.  That was to get some of their famed cinnamon rolls.  I won't eat cinnamon rolls unless all the fat they are made of is butter.  I don't want palm oil or vegetable oil or anything but butter.  I did a Google search for ikea's recipe and it showed butter only.  I was thrilled.  I made a special trip out there and found that all their cinnamon rolls, fresh or frozen, none have butter.  I feel like this was false advertising.  I left w/o buying anything.  

Does anyone know of an all butter cinnamon roll in St. Louis?  Even Panera's are not all butter.  Neither are trader joe's or schnucks or dierbergs.

I just did a kitchen renovation using IKEA. Worst customer service experience I've ever had. Very disorganized and they contract out everything. The people who put the cabinets in did a great job but I will never use IKEA or purchase anything from them again. I wouldn't recommend using them for anything.

This review is strictly for the food court in IKEA and not for its products, that will be featured in another review. IKEA food court is one of my favorite places to eat in the city. One of the biggest perks of eating here is being able to enjoy a modern dining area inspired by IKEA's design. It is very awesome that the place is located across from the navy yard, overlooking a huge ship. The place is so clean and spacious and it helps you relax so much when you're here. Food wise, the quality is amazing. Their menu offers fun and family oriented cuisines. My favorite is their Swedish meatballs. They are light, flavorful and feels good to eat. That goes to most of the food here, they are on the lighter side. I never felt better after a meal other than here. Make sure to try the salmon and their dessert. Their pies are tasty and not overly sweet, which I love. Stop by for lunch, even if you're not buying from IKEA. It is fun just to walk around and enjoy some meatball snacks at the food court. Highly recommended for anyone, especially those with kids.

Crappy products that fall apart in a month!! Bought the white pedestal round table and matching chairs. Literally cant even wipe the chairs with a damp rag all the paint swipes off! Same thing with the table! Spent over $700 on the set and none of it even lasted 3 months!! Ive had other furniture from there too and same thing...guess thats what happens when you buy cheap molded wood chips.. terrible quality and not even worth the price they want. Never stepping foot in an ikea again!
Why always one or two registers for such a big store. I have had to walk out numerous times.

Ikea is a great spot for so many things. You can spend hours in hear. And get so much for cheap. They have much more to choose from then on the website. After you look around a d find what you need. Most of the big items you have to walk downstairs and get in the warehouse. 

It's very easy to get lost in hear. So loom at the maps thru the store. It's beats target, Walmart or really for that matter any other store...

Over the past year, I wonder how much time we have spent in IKEA?  It is never a quick trip and for a second I think I am getting lost, but then I see the light.

We have purchased bed frames, night tables, the BESTA series of cabinets for our den, kitchen  hardware, a wardrobe, some cups and glasses.

We have found the store to always be bright and have usually found someone to help us when we had questions.

As far as the quality goes- it all has been good so far.  And I do not think it looks like stuff you have to put together.

At first, it is a bit difficult to figure out the directions, but we eventually got the hang of it.

We have had dinner once in the cafe and it was good.  Note- we now go on a full stomach and I always bring a snack in case our decision making process is longer than we planned.

Parking and loading is good.  There always seems to be both that is convenient.  We had to return a couple things and that went well too.

A few times they have not had the items we wanted in stock.  

All in all IKEA is a good experience and good product.
good cheap frustrating furniture. Tried the food, don't see the hype, but it's a nice convenience. .

I have such a love/hate relationship with IKEA. 
Their products - love. Their website - hate. Their cafe - love. Their service desk - hate. I bought 27 items tonight that needed to be picked up at the service desk--we waited almost an hour for them. Meanwhile, half a dozen employees are chatting around me, meandering around, and the store is preparing to close with very few customers left. If this were an isolated incident, no problem, but I have never experienced efficiency at that desk. 
9:00 pm+ and my 82-year-old mom and I are finally loading our car below, where they said there would be someone to help me. Well there wasn't. 
IKEA needs to go Undercover Boss!

Horrible delivery company!! They were scheduled to deliver my things between1-5pm and never showed their excuse being they lost my order. Now rescheduled for tomorrow for delivery, not getting my hopes up! I will never order from them again!!

I mean, ikea stores pretty much all the same. The food at this one might have been a little above the quality of the food at some of the others... But it's the same deals. I did notice at this one they had an espresso machine not just coffee. That is impressive.

I feel like the as a selection at this store happens to be less interesting than that of the store I usually go to in South Philly. I'm not quite sure why that would be... A lot of what I buy from the address Department is floor models. Obviously every Ikea has the same floor models, but maybe they do not turn them over at the same time?

Oh well, Ikea is Ikea.
Love, Love , Love!!!  Inexpensive and great design storage options.  Love the restaurant too.
Had everything we needed! The biggest IKEA I've ever been in, everything was well kept.

WHAT AWFUL CUSTOMER SERVICE. at all cost- do not ever get the home delivery- we're now on 4 days of no couch and customer service has done nothing but kept us on hold for hours at a time and had no answer for us to where our couch is or when it's being delivered after false promises of same day delivery. Very upsetting.

I had a wonderful time shopping at IKEA with the assistance of Daniel to make experience easy-going informative he assisted me with shopping picking out things for my customers house he followed me all the way to the end was funny humorous and would definitely come again thank you so very much Daniel for helping my shopping experience to be a wonderful shopping experience

Return department needs to improves. There is only customer when I was there and  cashier working on the person for more than twenty mins . Then 4 peoples showed up for return and still one one cashier. You guys should learn from Costco on how to handle returns from customer. Stop talking BS and get your work done. You talk more than you moved your hand. People next time when you are there, see how "FAST" they move they hand while working but if you see them on their cell phone texting, holy crap that is speedy. IKEA, should pay them by the number of returns then you will see that they don't even want to sweet talk with you. Hi...ping, next.

IKEA maybe the next best place to people watch besides the airport. The Swedes have Americans figured out, despite our differences, our accents, our political views, open up an IKEA in some city & everyone shows up. Anthropologists & sociologists take note for future studies. 

I go to IKEA for a few things:

Ideas 
Storage 
Plants
Frames
Accessories
Warm cinnamon rolls

The above items are inexpensive & will easily transform your room. The downside, the minute someone walks into your home, they'll know you shop at IKEA. 

I'm not a fan of the furniture (embarrassing, unfortunate accident w/ a slat bed many years ago), but it'd be a great choice for those just starting out or with a specific budget in mind. Just note, installation is a !

Spend the extra time and drive to Philly, much more worth your time and money. Here, the service is consistently bad with workers that don't know the products. The employees always forget parts of our orders or give us the wrong parts, that is if you can even find an employee to help you out. Always out of stock on items.
I have now tasted the Swedish meatballs everyone loves so much.... not impressed. Tastes like the meatballs that come in spaghettios.

Returns and exchanges need to get it together. I had a 20 lamp that needed an extra screw and they gave me improper directions for 40 minutes. I ended just going to lowes to buy the screw. I will never shop at IKEA again.

If you are into saving a few bucks and putting furniture together yourself then you found the perfect place.  All the packages are easy to assemble and I have yet to miss a screw or have a missing board.

The store offers a kid care area which is great.   

The store is designed as a maze which works out good because you don't "miss" anything.  You see how different rooms are set up in case you have a smaller apartment or home.   It also gives you decorating ideas for the smaller items like frames, lamps and vases.

The quality of the furniture has definitely improved over the last 20 years.  I can build a bookcase without worrying about it breaking from the weight of my items.

They have a nice hot food area which is reasonably priced and always crowded for good reason.

If you don't have a big car and you want items delivered the delivery fee varies but is reasonable.

There is also a small food place on the way out with ice cream and hotdogs.

I wish I could give this place a 4 star but my few negative items are :
~ parking -  You have to leave your merchandise by the front door since the carts don't go more then 5 feet past the building.    Which wouldn't be a big deal if you a) had a second person with you and b) didn't have to wait for a space to open during peak periods.
~ cashiers - NEVER NEVER NEVER seem to have enough people at check or at the return desk.  The return desk is so long that they installed the number ticket system.    The regular cashier lines are so long that it helps you practice patience.  Just remember how much fun it will be putting the furniture together and how much patience you are learning.

Will I be back?  Yes   .. I do like the quality of the products and the prices.

Worst experience ever in a store.  I went to buy a desk and a hanging folder cabinet.  I was told to go to three different places to get the hanging folder cabinet. I returned $800 worth of merchandise before I left.  Never saw the hanging folder cabinet yet was able to be charged for it.  I was told I needed another piece of paper after providing my receipt.   The return was even worse. I left the merchandise and receipts with yet another incompetent ikea rep as they could not figure out how to return the merchandise without the phantom piece of paper.  So far everything but $43 has been refunded.  Philadelphia location

This review could probably apply to any IKEA in Canada, or even the world. They all seem to have the same blueprint.

I have a love/hate relationship with this store.  They have some great furniture and household goods at very reasonable prices, but I dislike the crowds and the rat in a maze layout.  I counter that by trying to go during off-peak hours and knowing my shortcuts to get around the store.

They have great products and probably contribute a lot to saving the environment in a multitude of ways. Their product design saves a ton on fuel and transportation costs which saves in the use and impact of fossil fuels. They are trying to have all of their stores  be energy independent. By 2020 they will be producing as much energy as all of their stores combined use. They also source their food and materials as responsibly as possible. They provide electric car charging stations. they are starting to sell solar panels (in Europe right now anyway) and as well hydroponic plant systems (also Europe).

IKEA as a company is a very interested to read and learn about. I saw an interview with the CEO a few years ago. It was an hour long program and talked about the companies history and plans for the future. It really is a great company and a great corporate citizen. 

So how do I score IKEA???

Products: 5 (huge selection)
Parking: 4 (Parking lot is massive but always mostly full it seems)
Food: 5+ (so much good unique stuff)
Quality of Goods: 3-5 
Staff: 5 (Always pleasant and helpful)
#Checkouts and speed: 4 
Cleanliness: 5 (Always clean and organized)
Bathrooms: 5 (Always clean)
Customer Service/Parts: 5+ (sometimes a bit of a wait though)
Corporate Policy: 10 out 5
Your #$%^#% Maze layout: -5000

It hard to not love you IKEA. I will give you a reluctant 4 because you really deserve it despite that maddening maze layout.

Please software developers make an app that will guide those of use that don't want to be trapped in that store that will show us the shortest path from A to B so we can get in and out very quickly.

I love this place!! I was worried about it being pricey but they have excellent prices!! Everything is flat boxed when you purchase it and that's what saves you so much money! When I put the sofa together that I bought, it was fast and easy.  I also bought a mattress and when I picked it up, it was rolled up and so easy to move!  The store is humongous so when you go, I would have a game plan as to what you are looking for. If you don't you will get sucked into the IKEA time warp and end up spending 8 hours there just looking around.  They even have a restaurant you can eat at but i wouldn't really recommend it.  The 2 times I've eaten there it wasn't very good.  But if you are just looking for great deal on items for the house, THIS IS THE PLACE TO GO!!!

Swedish meatballs with mash potatoes and gravy with a side of Mac and cheese and lingonberry juice/pop

I'm only posting this because today I craved Mac and cheese, and Ikea has a decent one for really cheap. It ain't no Craft mac and cheese with gouda, poblano peppers and bacon. The meatballs are pretty small but you get alot. And then mash is always good when it's covered in gravy and cranberry. This ain't fine dining, but food at ikea is always so good maybe because you know you're getting a deal. LPT - they serve alcohol here, Stella Artois to be exact and it's really cheap too.

Atmosphere is hectic cafeteria style and its self serve and self clean. Don't eat too much at the cafeteria so you can get a cheap hot dog on the way out. #FatSal

Sal says: Just eat it

I never had any desire to go to Ikea.  I thought all they had was very modern, hard edged furniture and I love vintage finds, but my hubby talked me into going to check it out.  Oh Boy was I wrong about this store!  We went on a week day so we practically had the place to ourselves.  I was overwhelmed as we walked around.  This place is huge and the first thing I think of is that saying; A place for everything and everything in it's place!  If you want to get your life organized, this is the place to start!  I have never seen such organization and well thought out items in my life. Even the shopping carts have these special funky wheels that make them glide.  I had to have things I didn't even know existed!  We first went around the top floor and then the bottom floor scoping out the joint!  Then we stopped for a snack at the restaurant.  The food is so cheap, you can't not eat something!  Hubby loved the Swedish meatballs.  Lets just say, I wouldn't go there just to eat, but if you get hungry while shopping, it's a good place for a snack.

If you go to one of the kiosk you can join Ikea and they give you a card.  You get special discounts and free coffee or tea at the restaurant.  Also, you grab a paper and pencil and it has places to write down the name of the item and the bin # it is in.  You do this for the large items.  It's all very organized!  lol  The prices are insane cheap!  It makes you want to buy two of everything.

Now we go and get two flat carts and head out again.  I am embarrassed at how much we are grabbing and putting on our carts, especially after saying I didn't want to go.  I got wooden spoons, a baking kit, tins to keep my dog treats in, knives that are really nice, tea towels, and baskets galore.  I got storage baskets for the garage, kitchen, living room and a new coffee table, new chair and a non stick skillet!  Hubby got a new beautiful black TV stand with two glass doors on the front.  I also got 3 frames, a cutting board and French pictures.  They have wonderful frames in all sizes.  I got this plastic thing to hang on the wall that holds plastic bags and a lint roller and two rugs!  I know, I said I was embarrassed, shud up! 

Now are carts are full and as we round a corner I see my dream couch!  It's part shabby chic and part beachy!  I gasp and give my hubby that "I have to have it" look, and it's on sale! He rolls his eyes and writes down the name and bin #.  I am now giddy with joy!  By the time we collect all our treasures from the Bins, we are starting to get tired.  It's been a long day and as we push and heave our way to the check outs I'm starting to think we went overboard.

The checkouts are......say it with me now....Organized!  There are signs telling you how to have your items for quicker scanning.  They get you through fast, even with all we had.  Now we make our way outside and they have special parking for loading up your vehicle.  Hubby goes and gets our Jeep and backs in to a spot.  We are standing on the sidewalk, it is late and dark now.  We are gazing from the open hatch back of the jeep to the two huge piles of stuff.  We must stand there at least 15 minutes when we both come to the same conclusion at the same time.  This isn't going to work.

Luckily for us, they will hold your items for 24 hours.  So we decide to leave half of it behind.  The nice man at the counter gave us that," You idiots got carried away in the wonders of Ikea and lost all common sense....didn't you?"  YES we did, shud up!

Okay, now we have to load the couch.  Have you ever tried to get a boxed couch in the back of an SUV?  It's not pretty.  Ikea has lots of string for your convenience!  Now we are both hot, tired and cranky.  We finally sort of get the couch loaded and we are sitting with our noses touching the windshield.  I am thinking that if we have a wreck we are going to die.  But I don't say a word, because I know my hubby is on the edge and one wrong word from me and he will return my dream couch.

We slowly and carefully make our way across the river and back home.  To make things easier on us, we unbox the couch outside  and carry it inside in pieces.  To my surprise, hubby puts it together and it was easy!  It looks amazing!  I sit on it, I lay on it and I love it!

We go back the next day and retrieve the rest of our stuff.  Thank goodness this trip goes smoother.  Ikea has not seen the last of us that's for sure.  I saw a kitchen I want, but this time we are renting a big truck!  We are now officially Ikea addicts!
Ikea I love you and your cheap food that is actually really good. I could actually live here if it wasn't so close to the PPA.

This store is amazing. We toured the store with friends and enjoyed seeing all the different ways to use furniture and especially all the gadgets. We took time out to have a lunch. Their food is very good and reasonably priced. We had the stuffed chicken w/green beans and mashed potatoes. If you are a member you get a discount on your meal and free coffee. We didn't buy anything but, maybe we will in the future.
One person serving each buffet line with a queue of 20+ in each line.  Ridiculously poor service.
Love love love Ikea!! I just wish there was a bus without transfers that traveled from CC directly to Ikea

Not my favorite IKEA store but I needed a place to kill time before lunch.  Overall I am VERY fond of IKEA stores.  They always have some great gadgets & I try to grab them when I can before they are gone.  Got my fix today & really enjoyed it.

One of the only IKEA locations in the Tampa location.  Very happy that theres one period and this place has everything remember from the IKEAs ive been to in illinois.  Its two floors with the showroom for couches, beds, kitchens, and all home decor upstairs with the cafe located upstairs as well.  The associates are very nice and always well staffed every time we come here.

I feel like once you go to one IKEA you've been to them all, which I guess is a testament to their level of consistency. Everyone's probably got a Billy bookcase somewhere in their house, or a Poang chair that they got in college...so it's a household name that is easily recognizable. 

This was my first time going to this IKEA and I really only went because my friend needed a shelf and I wanted cheap meatballs. The store itself was a bit disheveled even though we came fairly early in the day. Makes me think that they didn't do a great job of tidying up from the night before. The signs are easy to read and follow if you want to take shortcuts instead of going through every single corner. The cafeteria was pretty fast moving and I got my food in record time. My biggest complaint about the food was the soggy garlic bread. I hate soggy garlic bread. The veggie fritter thing was surprisingly good.

We didn't have any staff interaction because we loaded up our stuff ourselves and then we went through the self checkouts, but there were a lot of staff floating around if people needed them.
I like Ikea but service is horrible at this location. If you are buying anything large bring somebody with you because they do not help.

Truly a good value. Food is good. If it's too much food, you can grab a to-go box in the drawer under the microwave. They keep the busy place clean. The line is long and the selection is limited to what you see. Upstairs restaurant is set up like a cafeteria. 
We had the chicken tenders and the BBQ chicken wrap. Not bad. Downstairs we grabbed some cinnamon rolls on our way out. 6 for $4.00. This is a deal they're huge and yummy. Can't wait for breakfast tomorrow.

Kitchens are great, customer service is worse than a third world country. Twice the exact same problem, and they still have no resolve. Never their problem. IKEA in Sweden must not travel to this store.

We love IKEA. I have built so many IKEA objects I could be an assembler for them. Once you get used to their "directions" it's a breeze. Love the engineering and that you can put almost every item together without power tools. 

Only 4 stars because on our initial visit we signed up for their orange loyalty family card. It emailed us a coupon. We proceeded to spend the next 6 hours walking through their store. We purchased over $1200 worth of items. We went to use our coupon on the email, clicked the link, and it said it had already been used. ??? Ok, so we told them we definitely want to use the coupon and so we would like them to call a manager to make this happen. Manager came over, proceeded to try and tell us how to work our phone and get to the coupon, to not avail..... Manager went to the office and called the staff back and said 'this one time we will make an exception and for her to use another customers coupon. There is no way for me to override the coupon and enter it in as $25 off.' Hmmm, I am not sure I believe that but whatever. She scanned another customers coupon and gave us the discount. It was super frustrating having to do this to staff. It was an IKEA coupon, that THEY sent us via email when we signed up for THEIR card. We could not have printed it off as we have been in THEIR store for the last 6 hours. Ugh. We hated holding the line up and we hated being 'those people' but dang it, if you send us a coupon for $25 at least let us use it! 

So, we left and got home and proceeded to put together several shelving units and such. All went together smoothly and without issue. One of the shelving units (yellow one) was built slightly differently even though it was the same unit. Maybe a different manufacturing place or maybe it was a different assembly line since it was an unusual color? No idea but it was a bearcat to assemble compared to the other ones we bought which were black/white, green and gray/blue. When I slid the pegs in it managed to crack the surface causing the yellow coloring to come off. Frustrating. 

Other than that I noticed how the directions have gotten better since the last time I assembled these items (10 years ago.) And some of the items they have had long term (12 years old) are now made much better and are much more sturdy. I love that they continue to improve their items even though their old items still 'worked.' Well done IKEA. 

Thank you for keeping your prices reasonable. Thank you for thinking 'outside of the box' on a lot of your items. Thank you for NOT being Amazon and packaging your items smartly. 

We have since this visit been back once. We intend on returning yet again for our bathroom components. I have honestly thought about applying at your stores as I love your items, love your stores (clean), love your food and love the concept of well engineered items that are not over priced. Plus+ I can assemble everything we have bought thus far all on my own without using ONE power tool. 

Oh, one more downer... why do you send items out without mounting screws such as the toilet paper holders and the magnetic knife holders? I am stuck with them sitting on my counter because every single screw I have at my home is black and does not match the silver of the items. 

No matter, I still love IKEA. And you put this store in a wonderful location for where we live. The last home we owned we had to travel about 4 hours to get to a store.
Great stuff at a great price. Unfortunately they will not answer the phone. The "Contact Us" is nothing more than a revolving door which makes it impossible to leave feedback or get answers.

I loved IKEA until recently I went shopping and think I've met the most awful employee ever, in retail. This maybe 30y/o lady had  a terrible attitude, turned me away. I would never shop at IKEA again, unless it was online. I'm an African-American woman, and this lady was also African-American, so completely not race related, I only describe her in hopes management will pull her aside or notice. I don't remember her name, but she wore a big, long, blond wig. Unprofessional and spoke to me as if we were in a nightclub.  I should've complained right then, but I was too excited to get out of the store and never return. Very unprofessional, and an embarrassment to the company, I used to furnish my home, on many occassions.

Service is lackluster. No worker seems like they really want. No one wants to help. But Ikea is Ikea. They have all the things you would need and then some! I'll just help myself I guess. A fun place to spend a day looking or shopping or ideating. Don't forget to stop for some Swedish meatballs!

I like going to Ikea,  but today I find that their background music is horrible. A lot of screaming guitar, heavy rock.  A little too loud for me.  It's not a bar or a cocktail lounge. I'm sure employees work long hours but it's not a way to keep them awake and lively. Sorry that's my opinion

You know this is my first time at an IKEA in over a decade. I was a young lad back then and now I'm a little older I this is one of my favorite stores. This store in particular is awesome. They have it all. They are really friendly too. Very helpful workers. I could stay in this store all day and buy everything.  Everything is reasonably priced too and even the food court was pretty decent. I recommend coming here if you need to do any shopping for your home decor type stuff

Walking into Ikea made me feel like I was back in Germany! Lived there 3 years and had to buy a lot of furniture for our house at that time. 

This Ikea was set up the same but the cleanliness did not compare to the one in Europe. I kid you not there are no trash on the floor but at this one there were. There were also boxes piled up in some of the exit walkways. I know, I'm being way critical but I notice small random things like that. I still love the organization and the aesthetics of this Swedish company!

We only walked through the cafeteria but I did notice they served the same things you could find in Europe. I think I'll try their food next time!
Love this place and shop here every month for small stuff. For the most part it is always organized and clutter free, and staff is friendly.

If you've ever been to more urban locations of IKEA in Brooklyn, NYC or Elizabeth, NJ you will appreciate the wonderful employees of this location in the heart of PA. You are greeted with "good mornings" and "hellos". People are ask if you need help. You can readily receive assistance even if the item is not on the shelf. If the employee you happen to ask does not know - they will actual consult another person who does know. The store is clean and we found the online inventory to be accurate. It is well organized with areas under renovation clearly blocked off with signs and barricades. The nursing room could use some work - it's a comfy chair with a changing table and no windows or discernible ventilation which can make it a little smelly when you are trying to feed your baby. Other than that - this place is many steps above its urban counterparts.

The Returns and Exchanges department of this location is the worst.  Understaffed and the staff that works (I use that term very lightly)there meanders around at their own speed with no sense of urgency.  They are almost saying, "I have to be here all day and now you will be too."  

Unbelievable.  It's like the waiting room in Beetlejuice, but way worse.


Worst place ever.
