This place gets 2 stars because IKEA as a store is amazing. Unfortunately they hire rude, ignorant people at this location. I had 2 bad experiences in one visit. 
First, the server at the restaurant asked us what we wanted then passive aggressively spent the next 5 minutes refilling all of her hot food items. Then slow as molasses finally served us. Funny enough the veggie balls and rice were both stale and tough to eat!
Secondly, we decide to look for batteries. We found them in lighting but were not able to locate the specific one we needed. We asked at checkout if there were batteries anywhere else. We were told they were also in isle 1. After 15 minutes of only finding furniture I asked another employee. He stated emphatically that batteries were only found in Lighting or occasionally at check out.
This store has terrible customer service.  Also, although they publish a return policy, they refused to follow their own directions.  Cannot recommend this store, and will not shop there again.

Understaffed. Always. Their workers are nice and helpful as can be but when it comes to efficiency from the checkout area, furniture pickup, customer service, etc. IKEA management (or management's management or maybe the President of the Netherlands) simply drops the ball. I've wasted away hours of my life at IKEA. And yet... I keep coming back for the budget conscious, half decent furniture. Even when they short their deliveries or force me to memorize each and every picture of that days Instagram feed while sitting on a not-so-comfy IKEA bench. If only their approach to service and checkout could match the planning that goes into their puzzle piece particle board panels!!

Super easy to get to, just over the bridge - but don't get lost exiting the parking lot. It's a really bad area.  The store is very well organized and clean. Saturday afternoon, it was really busy but they handled it well. 

Checkout lines were long but efficient. We don't eat there, ever.  We are in and out with what we need and on our way.  I found great deals on a set of picture frames, USB outlet station and a hand soap dispenser. 

Love this store!

Their online inventory system is horrible.  They had a 15% off sofa sale (significant amount for a large purchase).  I went on a Sunday and they were out of stock.  Online the system said Monday they would have it, Monday came, and they didn't.  Same for Tuesday, and then BAM, sale over.
LOVE!!! Check out the 'as-is' in the self-service warehouse. Also, go try some meatballs at the cafe!

A typical IKEA store - large, gets very crowded on weekends, and has a ton of items. They have a large cafe on the 2nd level and a smaller one near the checkout area so you can purchase cinnamon buns before you leave. Both areas have seating. I find that they have great, reasonably priced curtains.

I know IKEA isn't a restaurant, I had two slices of pizza there today though that I loved sooo much I wanted to make note of it.  Besides tasting good each was a nice size (portion) which I appreciated. Enjoyed definitely!!!!

We love this ikea! They have great selection and the cafe also has vegetarian options. The store was organized and the clerks were helpful. We enjoy coming here. We'll be getting a couple of items in the near future! Can't wait!

Giant store with cheap offerings.

I love IKEA. The bright colors, the cheap prices, what's not to love. Granted, I am wary about buying furniture from IKEA. I once saw an article cutting into IKEA furniture and showing how everything is hollow. Seriously, for those prices, what do you expect. I tend to stick with buying their goods that are on the first floor (e.g. tupperware, dishes, etc.), but if you're furnishing your first place, IKEA isn't a bad choice.

They literally have everything you need for a home. They also know their audience isn't looking for massive furniture to fill up mansions, so they design accordingly. There are tons of simple, minimalistic designs. I was looking at desks and they have a variety of small desks that would fit in a Brooklyn apartment (I thank my lucky stars we live in Clearwater, so I don't have to go that tiny, however, the option is there). 

They also have a food court with a ton of food options. I haven't tried it, but there was a pretty decent line to get food when we were there. Like the furniture, the food is cheap.

To the far right of the check out lanes, they have an As Is section where you can get discounts on floor models/returned goods. Might as well stop by to see if they have a great deal.

The parking lot is massive, so you don't have to worry about finding a spot. Additionally, they broadcast bird of prey sounds so you don't have to worry about birds pooping on your beloved vehicles!

Like every IKEA, this one carries the full range of household items and needs. Don't pass up the kitchen furnishings and utensils! Everything from food storage bins,  pots and pans, kitchen decor,  and kitchen knives is a great price and will fulfill your every kitchen need! A unique part of this IKEA that I haven't seen at others is a "fill your own bag" of Swedish gummies and treats. Get a little of each for your drive home :)

How do you not like this place. 
Well if you hate walking and shopping I know how. 

Fun place to spend the day looking at cool gadgets and furniture and bookshelves and lamps and bedding and knives and toys and office furniture and blinds and pans and linens and kitchen ideas and stoves and beds and curtains and rugs and can openers and picture frames and tables and chairs and forks and placemats and ........ you get it. 

I like shopping here but you can easily end up buying crap you don't need or something that looked cool there but terrible at your home.

Always excited to visit Ikea, and this one does not disappoint.
Once you learn the layout, taking shortcuts to your desired place makes for  a much shorter visit.

Ikea family card can sometimes give you a good deal.

It's IKEA.  what's not to love?  On our most recent visit, we ate in the restaurant.  Our family of four enjoyed Swedish meatballs, a BBQ sandwich, salad, kids chicken fingers, and kids pasta.  One of the kids did not care for the mashed potatoes, but otherwise we were pleased with the food and the price.  
As for the store, the maze of the showroom is always fun, but be super careful while strolling through the marketplace.  It can be quite dangerous (for you and your wallet)  when items jump off of the shelf and into your shopping cart.
One of the items we wanted from the warehouse required assistance from a team member because it was available in the pick up section after purchase.  The wait wasn't too bad, maybe 5-10 minutes, even on a Saturday afternoon.
Great customer service and the staff helped me find the TRÅDFRI Smart Lights.  Food was alright but not as good as usual.

Absolutely awful service. DO NOT USE THEIR DELIVERY SERVICE. WORST DELIVERY SERVICE I HAVE EVER USED. NEVER SHOWED UP FOR DELIVERY, THEN LATE, RUDE STAFF, NEVER ON TIME, LOSES ORDERS. 

XPO LOGISTICS (IKEAS DELIVERY SERVICE) REVIEW:

First, after taking the day off of work to receive a delivery, they told me they were 3 hours late but ensured the driver was on my way with our IKEA delivery (couch and table). They said the delivery truck was on the way with my package. Then they called me that the driver FORGOT MY PACKAGE. The driver DID NOT ever pick up my items from the warehouse. They told me they would deliver it two days later. But the gentlemen assured me I would be the first stop regardless of the route of the deliveries that day to make up for their MISTAKE.

So, having to leave work early another day AGAIN, I called in the morning at 9am (my delivery was scheduled for 9am and they told me I would be first) they couldn't find my order on their computer. They didn't have my delivery as rescheduled. Then after waiting 30 minutes on the phone with customer service (I've spoken to the customer service team four separate times, speaking with four separate women, whom were very rude and told me they couldn't call the driver, then they could call the driver, miscommunication etc), they told me I would be the second stop. At this point its 9am, my delivery was scheduled for 9am-1pm (remember, I was the FIRST stop), now they're running late AND they CAN'T CALL THE DRIVER. They tell me they can't get a hold of who it is.

Then I call back, they tell me the driver IS STILL AT THE WAREHOUSE, AT 10AM, the delivery man is still loading his truck. When I asked "Don't they start the loading process at the warehouse at 8am?" The customer service woman replied "Yes, but they have a lot of packaged." What a joke! How can you have a delivery scheduled 9am-1pm if they're still LOADING THE TRUCK AT 10AM. The delivery was late, after already being rescheduled for not taking place because a mistake on their part.

THIS PLACE IS A MESS. THEY ARE LATE AND RUDE. THEY MISCOMMUNICATE WITH THEIR MANAGERS AND DRIVERS. THEY LOSE PACKAGES. THEY HAVE NO CONSIDERATION FOR THE BUYERS TIME AND MONEY. 

THEY ARE ALL OVER THE PLACE AND UNPROFESSIONAL. AND ONE OF THE CUSTOMER SERVICE WOMEN LIED TO ME AND TOLD ME THEY CAN'T CALL THE DRIVERS, AFTER I CALLED BACK AND ANOTHER WOMEN CALLED THE DRIVER. WHAT KIND OF COMPANY IS THIS?

PLEASE DO NOT USE THEM. YOU WILL HAVE A TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE. ANY OTHER DELIVERY SERVICE IS BETTER.

This was my first time at an IKEA and I loved it!!! We have been thinking about building a tiny home and this store with the little displays really gave me an idea about size. I am also very OCD and all of the organizing bins and baskets... I was in my happy place!!! We signed up for the family card and saved $5 off a work bag that my husband was going to purchase anyway. We bought everything from jam to wooden hangers....if we lived close to one I could see it being a great place to shop about every other week for large food purchases. The small grocery section had many of the things that we eat often such as cheese, crackers, and jams.

Great place for buying bargain furniture and home decorating and more. Coming to IKEA is an experience in it self.... and you have a year to return mostly anything. But the reason for only three stars is the long slow small staff to handle returns....be prepared to wait an hour or more.. IKEA can do more by just increasing their staff, and maybe motivate them to be more productive ( one person was walking around getting water etc between each customer.)

I arrived a bit early, before the store was open at 10am so decided to sit in their dining area. I saw a lot of people getting breakfast so i tried the Swedish American breakfast. Sausage, eggs, pancakes etc.. not bad at all. 

I like the Philly Ikea, it's never crazy busy, you won't run out screaming after getting the back of your your heels hit by one too many kids pushing their own strollers either. 

I had a return and it was quick and easy. No wait, no questions, very straight forward. The employees are super helpful, one even walked me downstairs to find something in clearance instead of paying full price for the same item! Very impressed! 

Will definitely come back to this location. I can't tell you how much it differs from the Elizabeth NJ store.

Wow, lazy and scattered employees here lead to an exceptionally horrible experience today. First of all, the piece I wanted was stocked on the self-service shelves in two colors I didn't want. The one color I did want was in the secret backroom for post-purchase pick up. Fine. I had been standing at pick up for 10 minutes and could see my item on the hand truck in back. There were two employees fussing with fork lifts and hand trucks in back. Then, Tamira and Kimora come out together and couldn't have been more scowled and irritated when they saw me waiting. They barked orders at me and shoved the hand truck and paperwork back in a rude manner. There are so many other complaints on Yelp about the furniture pick up desk, I shouldn't have been surprised. Still, to see the disgruntled employees in action is a shock. I blame IKEA for this, not the employees.

Okay, I can't be gourmet all the time. Sometimes, you need a quick and budget friendly meal that's pretty good.
I love to waste time and find things for the house here at IKEA and get affordable grub. Today, my mini me and I had lunch together in the IKEA Bistro. If you've been, you know that it's mostly self serve with the exception of hot items. The girls/ guys will take your order and plate up you food. Don't forget your glasses (or coffee mug/ tea & coffee is free to IKEA Family Members) silverware and such. As I said, it's self serve. There are trays and tray carts if you need help. No servers here, you deliver your food as well as clean up after yourself. When you're done, you bus your dishes over to an area. There aren't trash cans either, so you leave it with your tray. Oh, and there is plenty of seating so unless everyone in the store is eating at the same time, you shouldn't have an issue finding a seat. They have small tables to big family tables. Low tables and high tables. Arm chairs and sofas. You get it, right?
Today, our lunch was a kids chicken salad plate (green leaf lettuce, chilled sliced chicken breast, baby carrots, strawberries and a cheese stick) for $2.49 I prefer to get this over the regular salad cause, well it's great! Plus I have my kid with me. He snags the cheese, carrots and strawberries. I went with the special, Chicken and Waffles (three crispy chicken fingers, fries and two heart shaped waffles. Drizzled with a hot honey sauce) it was $5.99 on the menu board, but my Family card got it knocked down to $3.99! He get the traditional meatball plate (8 meatballs, mashed potato and gravy with a side of veggies) for 4.99 They have a chicken and a veggie version of meatballs as well. I've had them in the past and they are pretty good. A slice of chocolate cake is $2.99 and they now put out small desserts pastries for 49 cents. I tried the chocolate oat/ coconut and I love it! A glass of water (free) and a fountain drink $1.49 and we had our lunch for $17.59
You can save a few $$$ by not getting fountain drinks and opting for water or the free coffee/ tea. Skip dessert (or share) and pass on the salad and it goes down to less than $10. 
Get your grub on before or after your long walk into the showrooms.

I have an IKEA obsession. We go for the $2 breakfast with free coffee when you have a membership (also free) and then drop our 4 year old off in SmalLand while we leisurely shop or just grab another free coffee! I Love IKEA.

Always have a great experience at this store. Food is also good as the kiddos love the froyo. 

This time was particular good in that we met Brian in the kids furniture department. Not only did he help me with my order and selection he also gave me a bunch of ideas to customize the space and work with the IKEA furniture. You can definitely tell he was passionate about his work which is not something I can say about the people working next door at Home Depot!
Don't buy anything that requires staff pickup. They'll tell you 30 minutes and you'll wait for 3 hours while they bring out items for people that have already left.

Unfortunately the staff has been very unfriendly lately. I felt uncomfortable with the attitude with the food service staff but even more so the SmallLand check in woman. My husband and I were both dropping my son off and she said that if so didn't show my drivers license they would not give my son back to me. My husband had already given his ID and like I said we were together. I completely understand and appreciate the safety aspect , however telling a mother that they could refuse to give me my child back got a maternal nerve. 
I have been taking my children to SmallLand for about 10 years and and have never been spoken to this way.
Professional staff. Merchandise is good quality.  Pieces were delivered and assembled as promised.  Will use them again.

Poor customer service... cashier charged me twice for an item... I unfortunately realized after I had already paid. She told me to go to customer service. I waited in line for 30 minutes, only for customer service to tell me to go back to the register for a refund. When I went back to the register, a different cashier was there. He was apologetic, and mentioned they could have done the refund at customer service. Get it together Philly IKEA!

Ahh IKEA, you either love it or hate it. I love strolling thru and taking in all the accessories that you'd miss if you're not taking your time like little wooden pop up tables that are different heights you sit plants on in a room, just gives it that extra finished look. Of course i always want to buy everything i think is cute but it's a good lesson in self control. 

We went today to get ideas for the new house in terms of bathroom and kitchen accessories and lighting, to floor to ceiling wardrobes and furniture for the bedroom. 

So hard to remember everything you like so i always take pictures of the item and the hang tag with name and price showing. 

Checkout is always long lines and i agree with a previous reviewer, Why are there no express lanes?

They have a great play area for parents to leave their kids to play while they shop. Makes sense, if the child gets tired of the store the parents will leave sooner and not buy as much, but with the kids completely entertained the parents have all the time in the world to spend their money. I see what you're doing there IKEA. 

Unfortunately they do not have electric scooters and where you borrow a wheelchair is at 'Smalland' so there was quite a wait bcuz of the constant checking kids in before my better half went up to the counter and just asked for a wheelchair. They are very thorough in checking kids in and making sure they have the proper wristband and sticker on their back but it takes awhile to be that thorough. An express line for wheelchair use would be nice! 

Overall we got tons of new ideas, i picked up a few things and i was happy. There was an issue on a clearance price not showing up and the wait for the runner/ supervisor to go check the item took some time but in the end I saved that $20 and was proud of myself lol

Parking lot is huge, didn't know they had underground parking, but for the size of the parking lot there are definitely not enough handicap spaces. I think our regular Wal-Mart actually has more than this IKEA.

As far as the layout of the store that's IKEA! There are maps all over the place that show where you are currently and also how to shortcut to the exit. I actually do not mind the mouse maze that is IKEA bcuz as you move along from department to department you notice accessories or complimentary items you would otherwise miss

Staff is great.  Food is great though my one friend hates it.   Reminds me of eating at school but even better food.   Prices are great.  Plus you can interior decorate shop after.   College stuff will sag after a while like book cases.  But their mid tier and high tier are great quality.

In my opinion, I felt ashamed at myself for believing in IKEA, their business model and their customer support, but after following the strict (and as it turned out, incorrect) instructions on the do-it-yourself furnitures and unable to be refunded or get credit back, we felt incredibly wronged and will never come back to this place or any other IKEA until they have the opportunity to reflect on their practice patterns.

As a backdrop, my wife and I just moved to Philly and we decided to give Ikea a shot before buying more pricier, adult-oriented furniture in our little apartment in center city. At first, we signed up to IKEA, got a bunch of coupons, and were excited to furnish our new apartment with these amazing deals. However, we were wrong.

This Ikea was much more disorganized than the ones I've visited in the northeast, with missing inventory, disinterested (and often missing) staff and also poor communication between the store and the website. When we initially visited the store, the staff told us that one of the items was in back-order and told us to call over the weekend to confirm its restocking process and appropriate pickup date. We followed their instructions to the letter, but even after calling in the store and confirming its availability, we showed up on the appropriate date and found out our item was not in stock.

Our next grief arose when I built one of the bookshelves per their instructions, but based on the manual error, which I took images of, part of the visible shelf was facing the wrong direction. I took pictures of the shelf and the instruction manual and requested credit-back since it was almost impossible to bring the actual 8 foot bookshelf back to the store, but they rudely denied our claim and I felt incredibly humiliated as a customer.

At the end of the day, I will never come back to shop here. But on a good note, their salmon dishes were actually quite delicious and affordable, so if all else fails, I do recommend coming here and sampling their cooked salmon plate for less than $6, which is the only saving grace to this place.

I came here with my uncle to exchange a lightbulb and we had lunch in the dining area. He ordered a pulled pork sandwich with French fries, which he rated a 5/5. It was bloody delicious. I ordered the Swedish meatballs with mashed potatoes and gravy and mac and cheese. Holy cannoli they were divine. The blueberry cheesecake was also heavenly. It was one of my best dining experiences.

To make this quick. Ordered a patio set 17 july delivery was no call no show on 24th, over 2hrs on hold to get a rep, said they would reimburse delivery fee and reschedule 27. New delivery day part of the order was missing, another 1hr and 45min hold wait and a rep to tell me they would contact me about delivering the rest of the order. Now its aug 1st, no refund has been recieced, no clear expectation on delivery, and 1hr 26min on hold with no answer. DO NOT BUY FROM IKEA...you've been warned

TIP: If you go directly upstairs to eat the food, you're trapped! You can then either suffer the ignominy of taking an elevator down one floor, or else walk the entire g-damn maze; there are probably people who've died in that maze. If you ask the staff for directions (even to a bathroom, for pete's sake), they 'helpfully' point to the 'map' hanging from the ceiling. Look - I'm a graphic designer, and that 'map' is a level of abstraction unknown to human-kind. They may as well be pointing to a globe: 'You are here' has never meant less. I'm convinced if you find staff in 'the maze' they are only there to discreetly dispose of the bodies of those who didn't make it out.
I didn't buy any furniture the first three times I went there, and I already knew what I wanted. I gave up and felt happy to merely escape. I have friends who similarly vowed never to return, but I persevered enough to write you a guide:

PRO TIP:  (How to actually buy furniture onsite at IKEA)
1. Find your items-to-buy on the website. Use 'check location' (for St. Louis) and 'item location' to find the aisle and shelf numbers. This works on your iPhone only if 'private' is NOT set for your browser window. Do this from home. IKEA does not have good wifi from the restaurant- ok, fine, maybe it does if you register your phone and set up a whole account thing - I just want furniture not some kind of commitment. Write down the aisle and shelf numbers before you go.
2. Drive there. Park your car in the garage (entrance is way off around the side) or in the loading areas up front - you are doing this quick. You'll eat after. 
3. Go up one escalator. There's a small display room. Turn right.
4. No! Don't do it! Don't go up that second escalator. It's a trap. I know you're hungry. Walk past it to the bathrooms. Keep walking. Magically, you are at the check-out lines. You've circumvented the entire maze!
5. Go through the check-out line backwards. You may get yelled at. Run.
6. Go all the way back to the far wall. Turn left. Go until you see a flat-cart dispenser apparatus on the left.
7. Get a flat cart. Use those numbers you looked up before to find your items. Careful you don't get too many large boxes - they have to fit in your car, remember.
8. Buy stuff.  Fun with elevators. Put it in your car. Yada yada.
9. NOW you can go back upstairs for a well deserved meal. Leaving: Take the elevator. I'm not even sure those stairs next to it lead to the same dimension. Then take the escalator or the second elevator down again.
10. Go home. Put furniture together. Huzzah.

One thing you can say about IKEA, they feed you well and keep you in their store to spend money!

Whether you stop in for an inexpensive breakfast or lunch here, the prices are great and the food is fresh and plentiful.  The classic meal here is the Swedish meatball dinner, which includes 6 meatballs, some mashed potatoes, mixed veggies, and a smattering of cranberries.  You are full after this meal, and it's around $5.

They offer breakfasts that are around $4.  They don't gouge you on the price which is great, and as well they shouldn't.  It takes forever to get out of their store and they know it.  :)
So much going on here. Beautifully designed furniture. Decent instructions. Keep in mind that you CANNOT finance at IKEA in the USA. boo hoo.

I really don't understand the hype of this place. It's not that cheap. Products are cool and modern looking but a lot of it looks very cheap.

Also, buying their light fixtures there locks you into their bulbs, nothing else will fit so beware.

I did go try a small dessert from their cafeteria which was surprisingly good. Unfortunately I came to shop not just eat. Huge place but really didn't have anything I wanted. Nothing worth the price anyways.

Happy shopping.

PS - careful of who helps you on the floor. I ended up buying a bed frame and was told I didn't need the headboard and it should still be able to be assembled. Got all 4 boxes home in my truck, opened 2 of the main boxes only to find out you do need the headboard. The headboard was an additional $200 on top of the $200 just for 3 sides of a rectangle bed frame. Ridiculous. Will be returning it and never come back to an IKEA.

Alright. Didn't really like Ikea before but the more and more my wife brings me here I tend to find more and more little things I like. We just moved to Tampa not too long ago. We bought a trundle bed for my daughters along with two mattresses. We loved it so much, we went back to ikea to purchase our mattress for a reasonable amount. And... we loved it. Replaced our 5 year old pillow top which was starting to sink in. I'll tell you what, we sleep a lot better now. They have a lot of neat things here. More than I expected. Well thanks a lot for the experience.

Ordered a MALM bed set and a mattress for a whopping 783$. After waiting a week for this set to arrive to my apartment the delivers were not ikea but a third party. I looked over the invoice and noticed that it said there should be six pieces. The boxes were even labeled "X of 6" but when I pointed this out the deliverers insisted that was all and left. Upon reviewing what was supposed to be included I noticed the bed slate was missing. Obviously if you've got a bed frame and a mattress but no slate to put it on its pretty useless. I called the deliverers four times and left a voice mail to no avail. I then spent 50 minutes on hold with ikea before someone answered and took my order information in like two minutes before placing me on another hold to go place the request for the missing part. Save yourself the time and effort and buy whatever furniture you need from somewhere else or go pick it up in store.

This IKEA store is going downhill. It used to be great and my favorite. Things got changed over the years. It doesn't have much stock as before, it looks like they going out of business. A lot of empty shelves, I mean A LOT. A lot of product out of stock,  bathroom lock did work (the individual door in a single customer room), the lock was actually absent and nobody seems to care.
There were few registers open on Friday evening and even then.. the belt didn't work. And many other things to be considered as a down experience.

C

Ridiculous waits in the off hours. Returns and exchanges was ridiculous. Don't buy from this store unless you know for a fact your not returning anything. The manager sat in the area and did NOTHING to help. Have some boo hoo story how people didn't show up but did nothing to help. The only person helping people proceeded to tell her life story to every customer even the ones who clearly didn't care to hear. NEVER AGAIN WILL I SHOP AT THIS LOCATION!

Did an IKEA stop on the way to bring my daughter to college. Got great things for her dorm. Stopped into the cafe for lunch. Very long line!
I had the Swedish meatballs with mashed potatoes and green beans and my daughter had the stuffed chicken. Both were good and inexpensive and the dining room was large and bright.

IKEA is like a grown up fun house. Enticing and exciting but ultimately scary. IKEA - the brand itself - has moderately priced home furnishings at a mediocre quality. It all looks nice, definitely not the best quality but it's cheaper than most other stores. The place is a giant maze and no matter what time of day you go you will feel claustrophobia and you will wait in a long line that will take a long time to get through. They never have a lot of cashiers so despite how long it takes you to walk through the mouse maze, you will inevitably spend most of your time in the checkout line. This location seems to be worse than the Philadelphia location - for lines at least. There is ample parking and the staff was helpful at the returns/exchanges - but again, long lines. If you need cheap furniture and don't care much about quality and like to wait in line then IKEA is your place. Sometimes you'll get lucky with a real gem. They do have great organizational products and decor.

Do not get delivery from this store. They have deceptive business practices.  They provided me a day and time they had no intention of delivering during.  They called me twice that day saying they will be there between 1 and 5 when they had no intention of coming at all.  I called to find out they did not send all the items to the delivery company, so the delivery company knew the day before they were never coming.  And they still called me twice saying they will be there the day of.  I then had to call IKEA 4 times, as they do NOT call back.  I am now on hold again for a 5th time, and going to ask for my $900 back and shop through someone else.

I love Ikea as much as I hate Ikea. OK, maybe I love them a little more than I hate them. But for their stuff, they're awesome. Do some price digging ahead of time because for some things they're super cheap but for others, you can get better quality elsewhere. I wish this place had more things in stock as far as silverware and picture frames. So many empty boxes every time I get there. 

The reason this store misses two stars is attitude. In the 8 million trips I've made there recently, I've encountered exactly one friendly employee. Everyone else is just rude and giving the bare minimum of effort. For example, I put my stuff on the register and pushed it through and then came down to the other end to start bagging it and pay. As I'm loading my cart and I've paid, the woman behind me is like "Miss, is this all your stuff?" and like 8 items were still on the conveyer belt. They did not get rung up because it would have meant that the cashier would have had to reach out and grab the items to pull them closer.  So I had to pay for a second order. Then another time, they didn't push the stuff down the conveyer to get it bagged so I paid for a shelf and it was left there.  Then the website says you can get same day delivery.  I went and asked about it on a Friday and was told "We can get those to you on Tuesday" - Friday and Tuesday are not the same days. Like maybe don't promise "same day delivery" if you can't actually deliver on the same day. 

So an A+ for the stuff and a C or D for the employees.

Great store for furniture, decor ideas, etc. I can spend a whole day looking through the various staging, and departments.Their cafeteria is a hit with extremely affordable prices and options. My one huge complaint is their parking lot- they either have to invest into a multi level parking or have more organised way of getting a place to park and leaving, yes leaving the parking lot especially on a weekend is ridiculous. It takes at least half an hour and it looks like they need someone to police the place giving the right of way as people do not seem to know how to do this on their own.

It is Monday morning, 9/18/17, 12:41 pm, I am waiting in one of only two checkout lines, each of which is at least 40 feet long, extending into the self serve area. I have been standing here for 6 minutes and the line hasn't moved yet. Apparently management is blind or doesn't care about their customer service!  I will never again set foot in here again!

Remember when IKEA opened in Philly? Everyone was so excited! People working there were friendly and helpful and everywhere. Well, a recent visit made me long for those early days. Because IKEA and it's employees have gotten a bit lazy. The store itself is a mess. It's hot. Whole areas are blocked off and covered in plastic, creating a maze in an already difficult to navigate space. Stock in many areas is low or nonexistent. See that bag on display? Try to find it anywhere. Try to find a employee who might be able to locate one or tell you when they might restock. Go on, I dare you. If you should spy a worker, they will be hiding in the least likely spot in whatever department they're supposed to be in, pretending to go over paperwork while avoiding eye contact. Perhaps IKEA is in the midst of prepping for the holiday season. Here's hoping they have plenty of elves on standby because they will need Buddy himself to transform this sad store into a destination worth visiting.

IKEA is IKEA no matter where you are in the world, and this store's inventory and layout are no different from any other. But, they're an excellent option for practical, affordable furniture that's reasonable quality for the price, and if you need something affordable and cheap in a hurry you just can't beat IKEA. I love the fact they also have recycling bins where you can drop off things like lightbulbs and batteries that are a pain to safely dispose of, and bins of spare screws, dowels, and other bits and pieces that you can help yourself to free of charge if you need extra. I also had to return a couple of items that were damaged, and had absolutely no issues with the staff who were happy to exchange the items without charge and even gave me a gift card at one point in an apology for an unusually long wait. Thumbs up, IKEA is the place to go until you're ready to invest in some real high quality furniture that will be with you for years.

Website incorrectly listed available stock items. Brought three kids into hectic store where very few people are available to help. Then the items were not there. On top of that, there is a policy that doesn't permit employees from getting items off shelves while Store is open. So we weren't even allowed to buy items on display. Go with Amazon so your time and energy and money isn't wasted. Whatever expense is spared, you pay for it dearly.

Seriously turn the radio down. I can't even concentrate to calculate any measurements for my project while I am here. Sadly, one of the employees told me she complains all the time and IKEA doesn't listen. 

All the shopping carts go east and west instead of forward. How am I suppose to navigate? When your pushing a heavy load it's impossible to navigate unless u are super strong person. I wish this would be addressed. 

The return desk is very helpful but the general floor is nearly impossible to find help. 

I wish IKEA would seriously address it flaws. Just because you have decent pricing doesn't mean we will go out of our way to shop. Customer Service is so important.
The restaurant is very very bad my  food has a hair that's was very nasty I  almost throughout never came in back to this place

This is just for the restaurant.  I've been in Ikea stores all over the states, and the store is the store.  This is our first visit to the St Louis store, and we really wanted some apple cake.  They don't have it here.  Bummer.  The chocolate cake was good, though.  Otherwise this restaurant does not have its act together.   They ran out of glasses for soda, and nobody really cared.  The soda machine ran out of ice...again, nobody cared.  There's only one register open, and it's SLOW.  The coffee maker is out of order.  Generally this has been a big disappointment.

I freaking love IKEA! I'm so excited St. Louis finally got one. I took my mother and aunt to the store for the first time last week. We shopped al day. 
What I love most about this brand is how they demonstrate a small, cute, completely functional space. Most places make you want to expand your rooms and the house, but IKEA makes you just want to clean things up and make a room function. 
They sell everything you could ever need. 

We also ate lunch here because we were taking our time to shop. The food was really good. I ended up even purchasing some of the meatballs and cream gravy sauce for home. Definitely recommend a visit or two at this store.

I bought a Myrbacka queen mattress on July 4th and it was delivered yesterday in a dirty plastic casing. When I took the plastic off, the mattress was dirty on all sides and the top of the mattress. I have photos.

Ikea is such a fun place to imagine your dream home and make it come true for way less than what you could imagine. Honestly, it's a good thing my home is mostly done as far as furnishings go because had I come here while still planning on the decor, I would have had many sleepless nights thinking of all the fub ways to decorate the house and a sickly, light wallet.

But seriously, who doesn't like purchasing a dish towel for 79 cents?! Or a cutting board for less than $2? Perhaps a plastic container for all your recycled plastic bags from the grocery store for also less than $2? Holy Swedish meatballs! Even I can't resist that. 

Walking around Ikea is simply amazing to me.  There are literally all sorts of knick knacks you can buy and adorn your home with for such low, low prices.  

The topmost level of the Ikea building is the showroom.  Until I've visited Ikea, I honestly did not know that I really want an awesome closet space with all the drawers and random spaces I probably will never use.  Or that my shoes can have their own dedicated shelves. Thanks to a visit to their showroom, I am now unsatisfied with the current residence of my hundreds of pairs of shoes hanging out in bins like hobos. Also, I believe my yearly bonus have found a new purpose!

Once you're done with the showroom and you start to feel a little rumble in your stomach, then head on over to their restaurant and grab a bite to eat.  They have a wide selection of hot menu items to choose from including some Swedish meatballs or really cheap breakfast if you happen to be in early enough.  They also have salads, sandwiches, cakes in several different flavors, drinks, and small snacks.  It is cafeteria style.  You walk with your tray through the line and grab your drinks, salads, snacks or desserts then if you are getting an entree or just a side of Swedish meatballs perhaps, you go to where the hot food items are and an associate with plate your food items for you.  Then you proceed to checkout and grab a random table.  The place is spacious enough that even on a busy Sunday, around lunchtime we were able to get a table away from where the large families with their noisy children were seated.

The main level is the market place where you can purchase actual things. If you're looking for it, they will most likely have it! Kitchenware? Plenty of them. Dinnerware? Insane selection! Office needs? Uhm... Yeah, aisles upon aisles of them. Furniture? Yes and yes, they have them. As long as you're not looking for very high quality item such as those you pay thousands of dollars for (for 1 piece of furniture), I'm sure you can find anything you want to furnish your home with at Ikea.

I've purchased cutting boards, several ceramic bowls for my dog to use because she's sophisticated like that and they were only 99 cents each, a little decorative indoor plant, a fake potted flower for decorations, some really cheap dish towels I can throw away and replace when starts to look not so great, some cheap machine washable rugs, a plastic holder for my recyclable bags and a few other knick knacks. Shopping at Ikea is truly enjoyable.

So if you haven't done so already, check this place out! You never know what you will find!

Shopping with my High School age daughter while she carried a clip board with grid paper for a room design. She was confronted several times by store employees saying they don't allow scavenger hunts. We explained that she was just browsing while trying to lay out a room on paper. The employees were rude unwelcoming and just plain unpleasant. They also kept following her around like a criminal. 

Too bad you insulted a young woman with cash in her pocket and 5 bedroom home. 

We will never be a customer!!!

yes yes I am an Ikea fan. how weird ! happy to walk through and see their new decor ideas. obviously I buy something, I never had a time when I walked out with empty bag. 
I have tried their mattresses at my father house and oh I can't wait to get it for my house too . 
some say their quality is not good. well, does every store has 100% quality for every product? so same with Ikea, some items are better some worse but over all I am a fan !

I have been waiting expectantly for this store to open and was lucky enough to get a preview invitation to come to the store a few days before the Grand Opening.  It was just me and a few thousand f my closest friends.  IKEA did a great job managing the traffic flow.  This is one of the smaller IKEAs but it did not disappoint!  Loads of cool things at great prices.  Unlike other IKEAs that I have been to, this one is only one floor.  The restaurant is strategically placed in the center of your journey through the store at the end of the showcase areas.  That way you can get your energy up before the serious shopping begins.  If you have an IKEA Family card (their rewards card), you can get a free hot beverage in the restaurant.  I didn't take advantage of it today,  but I am all about free!    What a great addition to the Indianapolis area!

First things first: you can't go wrong with an IKEA. The Fishers location is no exception.

As they usually are, this place is massive. I feel like I got my full step-goal with my fitness tracker by walking through this place just one time (slightly exaggerating, but tells you how big it is). 

Before the Fishers location, I always went to the one near Cincinnati, OH. One thing I didn't like about that location was that there were different floors / levels so it wasn't as accessible. Luckily, the Fishers location is all on the same level, so there are no stairs/elevators/escalators to handle.

I came here for a sneak peek for all IKEA Family members and my, oh, my, it was B-U-S-Y. This place is going to be packed for the solid next three months or more. 

The location is great, very convenient. It's right off of I-69, has lots of parking, and it's a very open area - with lots of growth available. 

The staff were all very, very helpful and friendly. It seemed that there were staff around every turn and corner you went on. Not sure if this was just for the opening, but it was a nice touch.

They have it all though: furniture, furnishings, decor, home supplies, plants, tools, Swedish food pantry, etc. 

Can't wait to go back - I'm so happy we don't have to drive 2 hours anymore - but I'll give it a few months to calm down and let the storm of IKEA-hungry Hoosiers to pass over first.

I was so impressed with the Ikea Family member preview!  First of all, I was the 261st person in line and only waited about 15 minutes, if that, to enter.  The initial few sections were a crush of people, but then it thinned out a lot.  

We asked staff a lot of questions and everyone knew the answers or were quick to find someone else who did.  They did a great job of being fully staffed and it was clear that staff had a lot of training.

The cashier lines were short and they got people through pretty quickly.  As is custom with Ikea, the have stacks of paper to wrap your delicate items, which is so handy.  

You can't get lost in this store.  They have subway-style maps in every section, which show all the sections and the cut-throughs to quickly move across the store (ex. there is a passageway from section 18 to section 12 to get you to the restaurant).  

The products themselves were very impressive.  I hit the Chicago location frequently enough to know their inventory in certain things like pillow cases and kids' duvet covers.  The selection here is bigger. I don't know if they waited until this Ikea opened to release the products everywhere or if we have exclusive items.  Either way, super pumped for the huge selection!

We left the toddler at home, but they did have the play area open.  I'm not sure of the minimum age or other requirements, but what a great idea.  The kid plays while the parents shop.  Seems like a win-win.

The food.  My mother went on and on about the food. I told her it was good, but she didn't believe me that it was SO GOOD.  Our only complaint was the time it took to get our food.  We stood in the food line longer than the time it took to get inside or check out.  I think with many new restaurants, they just didn't have enough dry runs.  Or perhaps they anticipated more varied orders.  It seems like everyone ordered the "Ikea special" of Swedish meatballs with lingonberry sauce.  They had plate after plate waiting and it looked like they were holding for either the Swedish sauce or lingonberries.  

One feature that some may love and some may hate - the carry out food section.  Here, you can buy frozen meatballs, the packet to make Swedish sauce, desserts, various mixes, fish, candy, cookies, etc.  It has its own cashier line.  This is great if you want to quickly run in just for food.  However, if you have other purchases, you have to go through the regular line for your other purchases, then you have to go through the food line for your food purchases.  You MAY be able to buy the food in the regular line, but this was not clear and there was no signage to indicate this is ok.

One bummer was that they did not have electric scooters/carts.  They did have a ton of manual wheelchairs, but they were heavy and hard to steer.  My mom has a bad knee, so she was going to use a scooter, but they didn't have any.  There was no way she could walk the length of the building, so I pushed her in a wheelchair.  It was difficult to maneuver her along with my purchases.  When she tried to push herself (along with the purchases on her lap), it was really difficult for her.  I hope they consider adding at least a handful of scooters.

Ohh, the whole state of Indiana and nearby states have their knickers in a twist for their grand opening in about T minus 10 hours as the ticker on the IKEA Fisher's page counts down. IKEA hopefuls are biting their lips in anticipation as they finally get their dream come true. The fanatics are already setting up camp waiting for their free couches/chairs/what-nots and the lighted traffic signal as I was driving home on I-465 N from work changed from "Slow traffic at 56th Street" to "Increased traffic on I-69 Wednesday". I was like WHY?!, then I realized, "sh+t it's the Ikea traffic. Kinda like the ridiculous Portillo's traffic on 116th."

Last weekend, it opened it's doors to Ikea family members who were able to claim a session and literally shop, ooh and ahh at showrooms, taste Ikea food samples, and eat meatballs in their modern dining space. Of all the Ikea's I've been to domestically and abroad, I'm actually surprised how easy it was to navigate through a 1 story design and use the shortcut doors. While the cafeteria is pretty much central, there isn't a great way to get there unless you cut through the hidden lighting area doors. There's no stairs, elevators, or those escalators that bring your shopping cart up and down different floors. For a one story floorplan, it seems more "spacious" rather than the multi-floor ones. For once, you have to pay for those blue bags unless you push your cart out. It's Ikea's concept of being environmentally green. Great step for Indiana - as we don't have access to recycling in public areas and we're creating waste with those plastic grocery bags that attendants seem to put one item in a bag. By the time we walked to the end of the store, we amassed an ungodly amount of things that we couldn't hold all of them. The worker at the end was super friendly and went out of his way to grab a shopping cart for us. We walked out with a few of those Ribba picture frames to create a gallery, cactus, planters, an artist dummy, food, and a few other "necessities". It's hard not dropping $100-200 every shopping trip. Thanks for robbing me. Just take all my money, Ikea. At least I can eat $1 breakfasts, $4 lunches, and like $6 dinners.

Camped out the night before and ended up in the first 145. They promised coffee and cinnamon rolls to us but ran out. They could have prepped better to ensure that every person in the 145 had something. Other than that it was pretty organized and they handed out Ikea bags to everyone. They had a live band going, Boomer showed up, the Pacemates were here. Probably one of the most eventful grand openings I've been to.

OMG!!! This place is amazing! I had the awesome honor of camping out for 3 days before the store actually opened! I received a free chair and other awesome goodies!!! I was supposed to get the couch but there was a HUGE controversy- but I'm ok with it :)

This is the first IKEA in Indiana and I am so glad I get to experience the grand opening! This IKEA seems smaller than most as it is a 1 story store. The prices are UN-friggin-believable here!

The staff is pumped up and ready to serve :) I was looking for a coffee table for my living room and some other odds and ends (shower curtain, decor for our bathroom, and stuffed animals for my LO)

You MUST try the cafeteria and the Swedish meatballs!! This place is sooooo legit!!! And of course I'll be back... in about 7 months when the crowds die down!

Ikea opening day in Fishers was great!!! There was a band and a DJ.  Traffic was not bad.  The lines were very long, from where I was on the side of the building it took a total of 14 min to get in, mostly because they were going in waves.  The interior is all one level which was great, Cincy and Schamburg are on multiple floors.  Ikea has good customer service as usual.  I will be back multiple times I love Ikea!!!

People were joyful and friendly during the grand opening. Spent almost 5 happy hours exploring and hanging out with friends. More likely to return after crowds dwindle down before making a serious purchase. Tip: even if you don't plan on buying anything, grab a shopping bag anyways because you're going to buy something. 

Snacks at the store front, cafeteria in the middle of the store. The food was very good for the price point. I didn't know there's a separate menu for breakfast and dinner as well so I'll have to come back! I'd get the gravy and ligonberry sauce on the meatballs instead of Thai coconut curry if given the choice. The daim cake was my favorite of the desserts. Tasted like a chocolate candy bar and lo and behold, there's a Daim chocolate bar near the checkout... which was very far to get to lol. Everything was on one floor but shortcuts were available in some sections. There a play place for the kiddos where i think you can pick them up when you're done shopping (i mean you should take them back). During the grand opening the kiddos got their face painted and balloon art.

Very impressed how organized and smoothly the grand opening went. Felt fun and relaxed. Police helped direct traffic and shuttles were available because we had to park 0.8 miles away due to how many people showed up and we came at 11am! DJ at the checkout line made waiting less annoying and actually fun cuz we were dancing haha. There was also a live band at the dining area too. Free ikea shopping bags were given to ppl who came out to the grand opening. Happy you're here Ikea!

I opted to avoid the morning grand-opening crowd and visited IKEA around 7:30 on opening day. Crowds had died down by then, and it was an enjoyable shopping experience, comparable to any other IKEA on a weekend day. 

I hadn't been in an IKEA in a couple of years, so it was fun to shop around and see what new things they had since I'd last visited. I ended up buying a few kitchen items, but the close proximity of this new location kept me from impulse buying a whole bunch of stuff that I really don't need -- I can always come back whenever I want to get more stuff!

I feel a little bad for people who live really close by because I'm sure traffic during peak hours will be a nightmare, but I love that there is an IKEA in Fishers now. With all of the new entertainment complexes, shopping and restaurants coming to Fishers and Carmel, it's a great time to live & work north of Indy!

This IKEA is one level. I guess that's the thing that shocked me the most, because I've never been to an IKEA that wasn't at least two levels. I was prepared to be aggravated. (Like, really? You're going to build a brand new IKEA in the Indianapolis area and it's not going to have two levels? I need my fancy escalator for shopping carts.) But after visiting this single-story IKEA, I think I can live with it. Who am I kidding: I love it! IKEA is one of my favorite places to be, and I'm so glad there is an IKEA within a sane driving distance. 

One of the interesting features about this IKEA in Fishers is that the "bistro" (restaurant) is in the middle of the store. So as you meander through the layout of the store, taking in the artistic and inspirational room displays, you encounter the familiar smell of Swedish meatballs and lingonberry sauce. It's actually kind of nice to find the restaurant in the middle of the store, because by the time you see it, you're getting hungry and fatigued (or, at least, I am). 

Did you know: If you sign up for IKEA Family, you get free coffee and discounts on food?! See why I love IKEA so much? 

Speaking of food: There is a separate little cafe just left of the entrance that sells hot dogs, cinnamon rolls and soft-serve vanilla frozen yogurt. All of these things are $1 (or $.50 if you're an IKEA Family member). 

My favorite area when visiting with kids is the kid bedroom area, because they let kids climb on the beds (respectfully), sit at the desks, play with the toys and hug stuffed animals. They're so friendly to families here.

IKEA welcome to Indiana!! We are so glad you're here. The restaurant has great food for great prices. And the store is fantastic. Anyone who hasn't travelled to an out of state IKEA you must go at least once. And make sure you go one a pay day lol. You're going to need it! 

Ps. Make sure to sign up for the IKEA family card. You get free stuff/special discounts through the year

Want to know how IKEA Fishers works and store tips?  If you aren't familiar, let me help you...read here: 

Purchasing: 
-Grab a map, a pencil and a bag at the entrance area.  
-Look at the lower section of display item price tags for locations on where to get things.  Do not take display items for purchase, as you will not be able to purchase them at checkout.  The bottom of tags will tell you where to find things. (i.e. market place, self serve, etc.)  Write down the item #'s and location on the back of your map.  
-1st half of the store is the showroom and 2nd half ( after the cafeteria) is the marketplace.  Showroom is mainly for looking and gathering ideas, although there are some take away items. The marketplace is more like your traditional American shopping where you grab what you want.  The cafeteria is in the middle of the store.  The self-serve area is at the end of the store, and this is where you find mostly the items to assemble.
-IKEA has services!  You can get delivery, delivery with assembly, or have them pick your items for you, deliver them and assemble them.  
-Look for people, in yellow shirts, if you have any questions.  They have all sorts of tools to help you!!
-Stroller style carts at the beginning of the store are for children.  Regular carts are provided 1/2 way through the store when they are most needed. 

Tips: 
-Take an immediate left, inside the entrance to find the restrooms and bistro.  Going potty, grabbing a drink and snack is a good idea. 
-Don't take display items...save frustration when you check-out. 
-Carts aren't needed until the marketplace, after the cafe. 
-Store closes at 9 pm, so many sure you plan your timing properly. 
-Try the meatballs!  They are so yummy.
Very busy for the grand opening. They had activities for the kids like face painting, balloon animals, Boomer from the Pacers, games, etc.  Get there early as the parking lot fills up quickly.

It's here, it's here! Finally, the Hoosier state gets an IKEA. 

I had the opportunity to do a sneak peek tour without the masses of people and this IKEA is awesome. Everything you would expect from a normal IKEA, just on one level. I thought this would throw me off, but it really didn't. 

+Step one: the showroom, with sleek "neighborhoods" set up with furniture that make you immediately want to redesign your entire home/apartment. I guess that's the point, right? It's a maze, but with shortcuts and frequent subway signs should you need to "escape." And arrows on the floor to help you navigate your way. 

+Step two: the restaurant, conveniently at the halfway point of your journey. Grab a drink, some Swedish meatballs (yes, they are all they are cracked up to be and you must get the lingonberry sauce) and take a bathroom break.

+Step three: the marketplace. This is where you actually buy the things. Plates, glasses, wall decor, throw pillows, etc. The accessories are my weakness. 

+Step four: the warehouse to get your flat-packed, assembly-required furniture. 

+Step five: checkout, with more tantalizing items to add to your cart as you wait.

+Step six: the bistro/food store at the front with candy, frozen Swedish meatballs, etc.

All in all, everything we know and love is now in Fishers, Indiana. Come with comfortable shoes, a full wallet and an empty stomach. Leave happy. Yay IKEA! 

+Tip: get an IKEA Family Card. It's free and there are cool perks. Just do it.

Well, it's IKEA. If you've never been to an IKEA you will probably enjoy this place a lot. This particular store felt smaller to me than others I've been to but I think that is due to it being only one floor. It was quite busy as it was opening weekend but not so bad that you couldn't walk around. It did get pretty crowded in the "marketplace" area and all those people walking around remind you how many people sneeze and cough without covering their mouths. Lol! 

Nothing amazing but again if you've never been in an IKEA, I do think it is worth the trip.

You know a metropolitan area is coming up when IKEA comes to town. We hit it on the Friday evening of its first week, and it was not as crazy busy as we expected. I mean, it was still crazy busy, but the parking attendants guiding us through the lot and into a space definitely decreased the parking madness.

So, if you've never been to IKEA before, familiarize yourself with the layout of the store and the DIY putting it together of their furniture. Grab a pencil, notebook and ruler they offer (note: the ruler is metric because, well, Sweden), make note of things you want to grab and their location in the warehouse, and grab them from the warehouse before you check out. 

The Fishers IKEA is one floor, different from the others I've been to. This threw us off a bit as we know our usual layout of IKEA like the back of our hands. If you follow the path that is laid out for you, you'll have no problem seeing everything. There are handy shortcuts if all you want is some Swedish meatballs from the restaurant, but you really have to look for them if you want. They don't disrupt the flow of the floor at all. 

I have no idea what the restaurant was like because the line was at least an hour long, and we weren't feeling that at all. But I'm sure we would've loved our meal of meatballs and fries smothered in gravy with a side of lingonberries. 

If you're looking to kill an hour or two by yourself, with your SO or with your family, IKEA is a fun place to go. I'm so glad it's finally here and I don't have to go to Cincinnati or Chicago! Definitely on my radar for housewarming/wedding gifts.

Brought ny sons for the first time.  They couldnt get over how BIG the store is.  Everyone wanted to push the cart.  They like how everything was hands one. (Kids like to touch everything anyway).  I picked up an end table and some kitchen gadgets.  Next time we will eat in the cafeteria.  Things are so affordable here.

The day that I've been waiting for has finally arrived. IKEA is open!

The Fishers IKEA seems a little smaller than some of the other stores and feels a little more compact too. Most of the other IKEA's that I have been to are more than one floor. This one is different with just one. 

The layout is somewhat similar with the showroom material in the first half of the store and the Marketplace in the second half, separated by the cafe in the middle. The store may seem smaller, but if they were missing items, I certainly couldn't tell. Everything I was looking for was there.

Going to the store and buying the furniture was great. But we only received one bag of hardware. I called the corporate office they sent me the rest of the hardware but it turned out that it was the same bag. I have called twice now and have been placed on extreme waits to speak with someone, or I talk to someone and they put me right back on hold. What kind of customer service is that. For the past month I have had the in convince of three boxes laying around my house since I have no way of putting this together.

What's not to love about this place? Everything you could possibly need for your home at GREAT prices with GREAT warranties. For example, the mattresses come with a warranty AND, you can exchange it for another mattress for up to 365 days! Items are easy to assemble, lots of great gift ideas for everyone in the family, there's as-is and handy-man sections with discounted items, and there's even small spaces set up for ideas on how to decorate your home/dorm/studio apartment/nursery, etc. The restaurant is also awesome, with great food (and desserts) for great prices. Their fountain drinks aren't Pepsi or Coca-Cola, but the "Cola" is similar to RC Cola. Don't worry about the craze of it being new. They have attendants to help you find the closest parking, it's not bad inside either (even on day 2), and they use every check-out when it's busy, so the lines move quickly. Also, their $1 ice cream cones are often $.50 and are quite delicious! Don't forget to join the IKEA family for free, which provides discounts and freebies all year long!

First time here.  Since it was early morning, my wife had breakfast - $2 for eggs, sausage, potatoes and pancakes, coffee was free.  What a deal.  Noticed immediately that it was very LOUD, though.  Apparently playing pop music at high volume is their thing.  We found the items we wanted after realizing that you have to follow a path that takes you through every department.  If they tried this in Home Depot guys would be knocking down walls.  So this is a girls' store, I guess.  Very, very nice things at ridiculously cheap prices.  But did I say it was LOUD?  Didn't take long before I realized that I just wanted to get out of there.  So we did.  Got a catalog so hopefully if we want something else we can order it online and get it shipped. Nice store, terrible auditory environment.  Never again.

If you like ultra modern this is the place for you.  I visited for the first time today.  Sorry to say it will be my last time.  I found the store to be to stacked and piled.  I did not like all the little rooms.  In my opinion, if the store ever caught on Fire there would be many deaths because of these little rooms.  The exits were marked but in a fire they would be covered with smoke.  I had a very uncomfortable feelings  in this mega store.

Of course, go. Here's why I love Ikea: much of their stuff is a system and they are all about keeping you organized  (OCD Heaven), trendy accents at an affordable price (trendy is just that and I'm not one to have an entire house of trend but some pieces that I may not want a year or few years from now. Don't spend big bucks (save that for the classics) for trendy. Ikea can help you in this), outstanding customer service and staff who go through intensive training to maintain standards. I can't express enough how customer service can make or break an experience. What quality may lack in much of their furnishings, they make up in customer service and this is worth something to me. 

I'm not one for crowds or warehouse-like rooms but if I can do it, I assure you, you'll be fine and you'll be glad you did.

One word review is disappointing.   It may jut be to how busy it was and growing pains.  We arrived just after it opened and the parking lot was already 3/4th full, but getting in and out of area was very confusing.  Many police  officers and they had a lot of access blocked off by cars, but none directing traffic.  What I assume are IKEA team members were directing traffic, but when we were leaving it was hard to get out since the team member was busy on her phone instead of directing traffic.  Might be temp workers based on how some looked.   Not sure a football cap on sideways is really a look Ikea would want.    Inside the store it was so busy it seemed like we were being herded like cattle.   You follow a path and seemed hard to really take the time to look everything.    I hope by Holiday shopping season they figure out the auto traffic flow.    Maybe once the newness is over the enjoyment of a shopping experience will be there

This is the 5th Ikea I've been to, and it exceeded my expectations. We visited on a Sunday around noon, and the place was packed. Somehow, the traffic inside the store was moving smoothly none the less.

Whether you have redecorating in mind, or you are just in the mood to browse and pick up some cheap household items, there is something for everyone, on every budget.

The staff was pretty friendly, despite being overwhelmed. If you have small children, be sure to grab a hotdog and a cinnamon bun so they can munch while you shop!

What is there not to love about IKEA? Not only do I love roaming around the show rooms but the market place is actually fun to walk through. There are so many useful household items that are very reasonably priced. The food downstairs (hot dogs, ice cream, and cinnamon buns) are the perfect way to end a shopping trip.

I was born and raised to be an IKEA fanatic. Growing up, my family planned vacations around what cities had IKEA stores. Words cannot express how happy I am to have an IKEA here. 

This location stands up to all others and did not disappoint! Although smaller than most and on one story, they have short cuts throughout the store and maps everywhere to help with navigation. We went 10 days after opening on a Friday night, and even though it was busy the store flowed well and they've done a good job of funneling traffic different ways to prevent back-ups. Staff was super friendly and helpful! The meatball dinner, chocolate cake, and lingenberry drink were delicious as always. 

I do wish that the Swedish market was a little larger and a bit better organized, but they still had everything I was looking for. SO happy to have this so close!

What can be said about efficient Swedish design? The warehouse is huge. Furniture and the big cafeteria upstairs.  Accessories dishes, candles, lamps and the snack bar with the best cinnamon rolls is downstairs.  Lots of walking.  I walked the entire store in about 22 minuets.  I didn't stop often.  I wanted to see everything and the store announced it was closing soon.  The pre made  bookcases and tables are downstairs.  I had the best Swedish cookies.  I don't remember the name of them.   I would redo my entire home in ikea if o could.  So far just my bedroom.

This is the first IKEA I've ever been to, and it's pretty awesome. I just come here to organize my place more and get inspired by their sleek, fancy designs. 

The top floor is the show room and the bottom is where you can actually shop and throw items in your cart or trolley. You can also get a tasty meal on the top floor, and I recommend their traditional Swedish meatballs!

If you see a short Caucasian woman walking around with a look of wonder on her face, that's probably me, walking around for fun. Haha.

A one-story IKEA?I I'd never heard of such a thing! It's not like Fishers doesn't have the room. While the store flows nicely from the showrooms to the cafe to the self serve area and finally to the warehouse and check-out, this location's size made it feel more like an IKEA pop-up shop than your traditional IKEA store experience.

That said, they have mostly everything in stock. I found their plants selection to be lacking and they were out of stock on most cutting boards and some side tables I had my eye on. But I love the IKEA brand and I'm happy to have one closer to home than Cincinnati, so I'll take what I can get!

Side note: I went on a Wednesday night to avoid the crowds! Highly suggested.

I. AM. OBSESSED!!!! 
Yes, IKEA deserves all of the hype ! I love the fact that they have show rooms so that you can realistically see what their products might look like once you take them home. They literally have EVERYTHING and I was surprised to find that the prices weren't outrageous. The place is HUGE and honestly... it's sort of like a maze.  The place is also flooded with shoppers on the weekends; so if you go, make sure you're not in a rush.

Went back today and much better.  Only one issue.   When we arrived there were no employees or police officers directing traffic and we had no issues parking.   No where near as busy so we could enjoy and shop at our own rate.    We found some small items in kitchen area that we were going to purchase.    Issue was checkout.     Only had five registers open and lines were about 8-10 people each.    Looking at some faces it appears that it was slow moving and frustrating.      We did not want to spend 20 minutes in line so we left all we were going to purchase behind and left and went to another business.    Don't know why so few check outs open.

So, maybe I'm used to other IKEAs (Chicago, Cincy)...but I wasn't super impressed. I forgive the fact that it is still jam packed busy with people being a new location. Here's my cons: one level, marketplace items throughout versus bulk at the end of the "trail," and you have to walk thru the cafeteria (really not a fan of this one). Pros: always find something, lines move fast, and helpful employees are literally everywhere right now. Maybe the cons will be more tolerable post holiday season, but I will definitely wait to try again until 2018.

I was way super excited for IKEA to open to see how they pulled everything together in the space. I was pleasantly surprised. I enjoyed the entire day just browsing, asking questions and piling my cart full of awesome finds. Of course I had to have lunch during my visit and my food of choice was the swedish meatballs. Everytime I visit an IKEA its the meatballs or the salmon. I loved that there were so many food options offered. All of the staff that I encountered was extremely helpful, friendly and knowledgeable. After having had an amazing day I had to make sure to grab some frozen meatballs to take home to my son. Im so happy we have our very own IKEA in Fishers and I cant wait to return...

Finally made it here on an early Tuesday afternoon. It was chilly with a bit of rain so the store wasn't overly crowded. Matter of fact, two different employees commented on how I picked a good time to come. Yay me!  IKEA can be an all day affair. I was there for a few hours for my first visit. The first half involves walking a maze of showrooms. The items in the showrooms are all properly tagged with their location to be picked up later in the warehouse. IKEA has some neat items at great prices. I already had a list of items that I wanted, but quickly found more to add. After the showrooms, you run into the cafeteria. Perfect. I tried the chicken fingers and fries. Chicken fingers were very good especially considering you're at a furniture store. They had a good texture and taste, better than expected, and reasonably priced. I also tried the chicken chili since it was cold outside. It was good as well. After the late lunch break, I walked through the marketplace to find more items at awesome prices. After the marketplace, it was time to pick up the big items I wanted in the warehouse. It was very easy to locate the items, load them on the flatbed, and checkout. There are employees waiting outside to load your purchases into your vehicle if you pull it into the loading area. Store is massive, clean, and well organized. All of the employees were friendly and helpful.

IKEA is awesome. This place opened here less than a month, still very busy! 2 new businesses opened around same time so traffic and parking is still crazy and needs work.  It was very busy inside ikea and hard to look around at everything plus it's a huge store - easy to get lost hah. They have an attached restaurant that looks and smells good and will definitely be back to check it out, perhaps next ikea shopping trip. Of the few items I saw, prices were reasonable. I like how they set up certain rooms to give you an idea of square footage and how much you can fit in such a small space if smart about it.  Glad to have it here, such a cool place. Will be better overall experience once traffic lessens.

Don't buy something if they have to get it from the back. The literal entire premise of this store is you deal with terrible customer service in exchange for cheap prices and quick check out. They are happy to take your money quickly but you have to wait for your furniture. The quality of the stuff in the back is not any greater, you just get to pay for the honor of sitting and waiting an hour until they decide to get the furniture you already paid for. Stick to what you know at this joint.

I've been to two other IKEA's in two other states. The Fishers store is nice, but not as nice as  the other ones I've been too. It was hard to track down someone to ask where a product was or help getting a product down or checking to see if they had anymore items in stock. Lines were really long at the registers as well. I wish they would've made this IKEA a two story one.

The layout of this store is a nightmare, particularly if you have children. "For your convenience and everyone's safety" they do not have carts available until you are halfway through the store. It took us 10 minutes to find an employee by the front door so we could inquire about the carts. The tiny, narrow walkways which make you feel like a cattle being led to slaughter were only made more miserable by the squirming child in my arms. I'll never know what the first half of the store is like because once we finally retrieved a cart, we were not about to walk back against the flow of people to see everything we missed. This store is nothing like the spacious ones in Michigan and Ohio and you have no choice but to walk the entire store, all the while having no idea if it's ever going to end. If I do ever shop at IKEA again, I will be driving to another state to do it.

Okay so I've never been to an Ikea before so I wasn't sure what to expect! I was kind of worried about the traffic butttttt they had it under control. As you enter they have people directing traffic and even point you to a spot to park. Getting in and parked was no hassle at all. The walk through the store is mapped out with a path kind of like the wizard of Oz. You follow it through the mock up rooms into the cafeteria and then into the stock rooms. It is what you expect it to be a giant crazy place full of random
Things at a discounted price. I bought some plants and some cook wear. Checking out was pretty easy you just lined up and then you needed to buy a bag for things which I didn't know about. But all in all interesting experience. I think if you're wanting cheap furniture or accessories you can find it. But don't be discouraged about the traffic cause it won't be a problem!

I went in the first week they opened. If you go at opening time you will have no problem parking close or waiting in line at checkout. The key to shopping at IKEA is to look at a map ahead of time and map out your route. Get in and get out. Checkout was simple but you have to pay for bags so buy one and bring it when you go. They had lots of staff on hand to help. When leaving they directed you way south, you couldn't go out the way you came in.

Well don't even try to order a new mattress from IKEA and have it delivered.  Apparently they hire the dumbest people possible as delivery service.  So like when they go to the wrong address they don't even call you they just decide they are done for the day!  So I get to sleep on the floor for 2 days!  I already don't sleep well because I have Rheumatoid Arthritis, which is why I bought a new mattress anyway!  IKEA Customer Service says "there's nothing they can do"!  Nice!  At what point is THAT a solution?!  What has happened to customer service these days and why are so many employees so effing LAZY?!?! My boss nor my parents would ever allow me to act like that!  So very sad. I guess so many are so blinded by IKEA that my problem doesn't even matter!  Have a comfy night sleeping in your beds IKEA and stupid delivery guy!

I absolutely love Ikea and I can't believe we finally have a store of our own here in Indy!  Over the years I have made many road trips to this home furnishings store mecca!  I love the simplistic style of their furnishing, their lighting, all of their kitchen items, reasonable prices and more!  It's a 290,000 square foot ready to assemble Scandinavian design furniture dream!

The warehouse style store is filled with many vignettes of different rooms types showing various uses for their furniture.  Its a fabulous way to come up with ideas for your home! You follow a path upon entering the store that twists and turns through the various departments.  They have everything you need for your home!  Furniture, curtains, bedding, towels, complete kitchens, cookware, dishes, art, clocks, lighting, outdoor furniture, and plants!  And if all of that made you hungry don't worry they even have a small restaurant!

Ikea in one word is fantastic!  Go, go now!
