I just can't with all the people, holy crap!! I know this store is new, but the amount of people coming here will always be super high because that's just how IKEA's work. 

It's a convenient place to buy lots of items for your home at once, but honestly I like very few things here. To me, most items look like they were made cheap. Also, I feel like they are selling you entire rooms and that doesn't work for me since I have most items I need. It's hard to picture what they are selling fitting in my home. But I feel like I'm one of the few that thinks this way!

I visited IKEA on a weeknight and was pleasantly surprised. Parking was easy, there were a lot of people but it never felt crowded and the lines were short. 

IKEA prices are amazing- especially for home good items (vases, wall hangings, candles, etc). The food prices are also really inexpensive. The food was also pretty tasty and all natural so I felt good about eating a lot of it. ;)

If you want to see the whole store and all the displays, you'll have to walk around for several hours. It's a great way to get your steps in ;) it's an excellent way to get design ideas and see things differently. It was really cool seeing apartment set ups with minimum square footage. Definitely a fun place to visit even if you aren't looking for anything!

IKEA has its own way of doing things.  It must work for them since the place is very crowded even 3 weeks after opening.  I have never been to one previously and had only scanned a few reviews before trying again on a Monday, late morning to make my first visit.  I was mainly interested in trying the Swedish Meatballs that everyone was praising.  (A full plate of meatballs, potatoes and gravy, lingonberry sauce, and seasonal veggies for only $4.99 is a great deal.)

So after finding a parking spot in the massive lot they have surrounding the store, I entered the east entrance and quickly figured out that I started at location 1.  What I did not realize until I made my way passed the endless meandering shoppers who were blocking the aisles was that there are no straight hallways until you reach location 21 which looks like the inside of a Lowe's or Menards.  That large warehouse area leads to the checkout area (Location 22).  

The significance of this winding pathway is that you can't just go to the area you wish to shop directly.  You have to go through the entire store to find what you want and then pay for it on the other end.  Sure, if you look closely enough at signs, there are a few double doors that let you short cut (like through a maze) to save time.  But as I found out that the restaurant was at location 11 (the middle), you have to do a lot of walking to get there.  Oddly, you can see the street from the windows of the restaurant, but there are no doors there.

The restaurant was clean and bright, but only one side was opened as I waited nearly 20 minutes (on a Monday) to get to the order counter.  I noticed that the other side opened after I was well into the winding aisle for my side, so bad timing on my part.  

I will say that the food is very affordable and the portions were quite enough for a lunch.  I enjoyed trying the Swedish Meatball plate (see above for details).  The gravy and berry sauce both worked well with the meatball flavors.  I also ordered a small berry cheesecake slice that was again, very affordably priced and tasted very light for a cheesecake.  Admittedly, the cream cheese layer was thinner than most, but it did have a layer of baked in berries and was topped with a sweetened crumble.  (4 stars for the food flavor, 5 stars for value).

After lunch, I decided to look for the Swedish Market after picking up a household item along the way.  They have stations of bright yellow bags for hauling your items around if you don't wish to push a cart throughout the entire store.  The overhead guides/directories count off which location I had reached and I kept seeing the Swedish Market was in location 23.  But since the checkout is in location 22, where was the market?  I doubled back and finally stopped an employee and was told that the Swedish Market (23) and the Bistro (24) were outside the checkout area.   So, I stood in line for one of the 7 open lanes (15 possible) and waited for about 15 minutes before two more aisles opened.  I made like a madman for the counter and was second in line.  I paid and looked at my purchase just sitting there.  I asked and apparently, they don't put your purchases in bags for you.  Some Eco friendly reason, but not very helpful for shoppers.  So, I grabbed my purchase and receipt and wandered over to the Swedish Market.  There I picked up a few items. Again, I wasn't sure what I was supposed to do.  Where was I to pay for them?  I went to the bistro and was able to pay there.  Apparently, someone had gone on lunch break who was supposed to tell people where to pay and to sell them reusable bags for carrying purchases.  Good thing I only got the three things at the market!  

Sure, there are lots of items for sale and some even had great prices.  But it was odd having to make purchases at the restaurant, at the checkout, and at the bistro for the market.  Seems like a very inefficient way to run a business.  It apparently works for them, but not for me.  

I made my way out with my purchases literally in my hands through the west exit.  Note that if you want to go to the market or bistro, I think you can directly enter the west side and avoid the long walk.

Review #434

I seriously love Ikea. You can find anything you need and even things you didn't know you were looking for
From furniture like couches and tables, to blankets and rugs, to foods and batteries-they have it all!
I also enjoy stopping in for the $0.99 breakfast. You get eggs, potatoes, and sausage links. I usually end up getting some other things as well. They have other delicious foods too! Breakfast, lunch, and dinner!

Timing. Timing. Timing. That's the biggest thing when going here. Go anytime after work and it will be busy. Go on the weekends after about 10-11am it will be busy. Remember that when going here, IKEA has amazing prices and quality. Everyone wants to take advantage of that so be patient. If you're in a hurry to get to a certain part of the store, ask an employee how to get there. Every IKEA has basically passages that get you around areas and to other parts of the store. This will save you lots of time if you know where you want to go. Also, remember to grab a big yellow bag and a pencil and paper to mark what you want. They have hem for you right when you walk in.

This IKEA is unique because it is a single story. When you go in the layout is really well done. You meander through the "maze" to see all the layouts. There are no isles but rooms completely built. You can see how pieces fit in your home. Each item is marked with a tag and the location you can buy it. So finding what you want is easy. 

After you've wandered through the store you get to the warehouse section. Here's where you pick up everything you saw in the floor displays and why you need to write down everything you want. After picking everything up, you get it all there in store you make your way to check out. This is a great part of IKEA. Typically all the registers are open. There will be some lines but go wide and make sure to use all the lines. Occasionally people will all file into a few of the middle ones making some long lines and shorter ones on the edge. 

P.S. Don't forget to check out the discount section. It's right by the registers and you can find some amazing deals. Floor products or defects, some very minor. But a good place to check out

I love furniture decor and ginormous destination box stores, so I'm an easy sell on this  review!  I'm just so happy that we have one relatively close!

Additionally the attention to efficiency and the unique food items make this a real win to have.  It's not everything to everyone, but provides a full range of low to middle end furnishings, home decor, and almost anything you put in a house. I just realized they even have some appliances!

This is a great destination if you're looking to satisfy a few items on your home shopping list or furnish an entire room or apartment.  However, if you just want to buy one or two things, I might not consider the amount of time it takes to get through the store worthwhile unless you're getting ideas.  

HOWEVER, if you become familiar with the store and want to make your stop quicker, keep an eye out for the doors that help you do skip walking through the entire maze and get your visit done quicker. With the size of the store, it might take me a while to get to that level of expertise! 

I recommend making your first IKEA visit at least a half day trip to get the full experience ... don't forget to stop for meatballs and lingonberries!

I feared parking, but it wasn't bad.  The roads leading to and from the parking lot are a bit confusing.

The lay out of ikea is like no other furniture store. After walking through the displays you go pick your own items from the warehouse. The prices are competitive but it's usually a pain putting the stuff together. They also have lots of home decor, organizational items, and kitchen utensils. The place is huge and you may even get lost in there. The girlfriend will buy buy buy. That means I will be cursing all week, putting this cap together.
Worst lines and not enough cashiers no matter what time of the day. Not enough people on the floor to even ask questions. Horrible...not going back.

I visited while seriously hangry so the fact that I can look back on it and still be impressed really says something about IKEA. To be honest, there was so much hype, I was kind of over it before I even visited. I knew I would eventually visit, but I was in no hurry. 

I don't think you'll ever visit on a day where there ISN'T a crowd. (Keep in mind, Hoosiers used to go to Cincy to get their IKEA fix so we'll always have out of town visitors here.) We went on a raw, rainy, fall Sunday just before noon. The parking situation is pretty well done with traffic being directed as needed. That said, sometimes customers take things into their own hands and block traffic when the pick up area is full. 

I walked through a model space that was 376 sq. ft. and I do have friends that have that as their entire living space so it was SO COOL to see all of that laid out in a livable, organized way. I was really blown away. I am not super thrilled about the whole DIY trend so I'm sure I'd pay more for setup and/or delivery if I decided to make a purchase. 

You walk through the store with a bag or a cart, mostly in one direction, but there are shortcuts you can take and directional signs throughout. The entire store, about 22 sections worth, takes about 30 minutes to walk through. They do have childcare for those parents that need time and space to get what they need. 

EVEN THOUGH I was starving when I walked through, I resisted the urge to smash a cinnamon roll. I mean, those are my jam, and I saw plenty of people in line with multi-packs to take home. Maybe I'll come here for a cheat meal and see what that's all about. 

At the end of the day, I did see a few things that caught my eye, and I'm now thinking about a return trip or at least checking things out online.
I was sad their meatballs weren't all beef because i couldn't eat them so 4 stars for me.

A real disappointment! First, there was no silverware or napkins available where one picks up the tray. Second, a dry tasteless almond cake was being stocked and sold as Daim [a Danish candy bar similar to a Skor bar] pie. Third, the meatballs tasted like they were from GFS rather than made in-house. Fourth, there was no salmon available on the day we visited. How is this possible? Fifth, the lingonberry fountain drink was so heavily diluted it could have been any berry. We were really looking forward to eating in the heavily-promoted restaurant during our visit and were very disappointed with the meal we shared. We shant return.

Can't say enough about IKEA. My wife LOVES this place and we always seem to leave with more than we went for. We have purchased several pieces of furniture and they have held up wonderfully and were easy to put together. This store is well organized and the never ending maze thru the store ensure you see everything there is in the store. The staff is friendly and have always been helpful!

Finally I made it to Fishers IKEA.It was odd to walk in and not see the escalators to the second floor because this one is all on one floor.  But we were greeted by IKEA employees and ask if we had questions. 
You can grab a cart or a bag to put your goodies in. 
Make sure you have a couple of hours to walk and look because they have so many ideas in there showrooms you won't want to miss a thing.
Then you come to the cafeteria and it was packed so the food must be good. Maybe next time I'll try the famous Swedish meatballs.
Next is the shopping area and this is all the smaller thing that in can put in your cart. 
The next area is the warehouse were pick up the larger pieces. Like furniture,they are in flat boxes you might have several boxes for that piece so it's not so heavy. 
Now you are at the end. You can pick up last minute things and pay for your findings. The lines went quick. Don't forget a catalog so you can shop at hone. 
And just remember for a fee they will deliver and assembly your furniture.

So we're an IKEA family and have been for decades. Heck, I have been to the Almhult location (on business of course). But this store is disappointing in just so many ways. 

First off, it is the first store we've ever seen being only one floor. As such it seems much smaller than any of the others we have been to.

Secondly, the staff is still struggling even weeks after the opening. We could not find stuff that is normally on the floor. They could not find stuff using their computer. Granted you don't expect IKEA to always have everything in stock but just about everything we needed wasn't available. 

Ended up buying some new bath towels and crisp bread. But man what a disappointing experience. I really hate to say it but we may be driving out to the West Chester, OH location instead of shopping locally at this store. Or maybe even just shop online and sucking up the delivery cost. Because driving to this store just seems like such a waste of our time. Did not expect to spend an hour here and only come out with dish towels and crisp bread.

My first visit ever to IKEA; selected  item that was out of stock, ordered and paid for at this store, slated for home delivery in approx 2 weeks. 5 days later, i chose to cancel this order and obtain a refund to my credit card. Now after nearly 3 weeks, and hours of waiting on hold at IKEA customer service 888#, can not obtain my refund. First call to cancel delivery was answered promptly. Two weeks later, calls to inquire about status of refund have required 3 hours wait time to speak to a human person, only to be told they would "call me back at the end of their business day". Also told they do not have any credit card info on me, and would need to obtain that info at a later date to process my refund. Never received that call. Next i will contact Better Business Bureau of Indiana. For an international company this is a poor way to do business in America!

I ordered online.  They charged my credit card and then never sent me an email confirmation nor did I receive the product I ordered.  I tried to call their customer support but just sat on hold without anyone ever picking up the line.  I tried the "track your order" form on their website and they never responded to it.  Now I have to contest the charge with my credit card company.

I thought this was supposed to be a major company but I feel like I got scammed

Let me start by saying I've been a long time customer of IKEA, but recently (11-21-17 around noon) I had a horrible experience trying to by some kitchen curtains. The manager would not sell me the display curtains because they were "custom made" but said that it was from a line of fabrics that they sell. Ok. I ask where the fabric is so I can buy some, and he tells me that they don't sell the fabric anymore! At this point, I'm confused and asking why I can't just buy the display or why they even still have it on display with a price tag if I can't even buy the product!! It was a fabric called berma-ruta, (a gray buffalo check pattern). The manger of the IKEA Tampa store was very unprofessional and also had a very smug tone with me when I was just asking a few questions in a very polite tone. There was also a girl named Justine who was very rude and refused to show me where something I couldn't find was. She just kept saying "it's downstairs in textiles" and when I told her I had already looked down there she wouldn't help me any further. Just gave me this stupid look. Needless to say, I won't be wasting 2 hours of driving time to go to ikea anymore! Home goods is way better

Very neatly organized and cool to see the ideas they put together for every room. It's very busy in there, but grateful to have one near by, as I use many of their products! Dressers, end tables, picture frames, pictures and many kitchen gadgets all for decent affordable prices! Thanks for joining us in Fishers!

The only reason I cannot give IKEA 5 starts is strictly from the lack of enthusiasm their employees display. I love IKEA and come here a few times a year to see what's new and to update my home goods. The employees at the cafe serving food rarely smile and act like they hate their job. We came here on a Sunday in the afternoon to have lunch and look for a dinning table. The food was very good. I love their meatballs and potatoes! We tried a raspberry mascarpone cake for dessert and it was very very sweet, but still tasty.

Even on a very busy weekend they NEVER have enough registers open. I do love their selection of lighting, I have purchased lots of lighting for my home from here and I have never been disappointed.

We were driving to pick up my son from college. When we were in Indiana, we decided to stop for breakfast. I really had a taste for a Swedish breakfast, especially Swedish crepes. However, when I googled Swedish breakfast, the only result that came up on the way, was the IKEA store in Fishers Indiana. That is when I realized that in addition to serving the famous meatballs, IKEA Cafe also serves breakfast! This is a brand new store that just opened last month. All the employees we encountered were helpful, friendly and polite. The  breakfast included eggs, potatoes, sausage and my favorite Swedish crepes for an extremely low price of $2.00. We also signed up for the IKEA family card, and got free cappuccino. On our way out, I bought a lingon berry preserve for a little taste of Swedish breakfast at home.

I was really looking forward to this IKEA opening so we'd no longer have to drive to the one in West Chester. We took the day off work to go and avoid the crowds that we saw at the weekend. 
First impression was: why so small compared to other IKEAs? Another person commented about not having an upstairs. We'd specifically gone for sofa covers and a book case. However, they don't have the covers there, so I'm really not sure what happens when you buy the sofa, and the book case display was pitiful and I couldn't see what I'd seen in the catalog. The IKEA staff was not particularly helpful either, and so we came home yo order from the catalog and pay for delivery. My impression was that the lack of help was not from lack of trying but lack of training and experience. I normally love to get carried away, checking out all the different kitchen options, but not here.
There seemed to be more open space to move around in than other IKEAs, but that doesn't really help if the number of options on display suffers. 
The bathrooms were nice and clean, as you'd expect at an IKEA, and the staff at the marketplace/ bistro were really friendly. At least I could get the crispbread that I just love!
In future, unless all I need is crispbread, I'll be heading back to West Chester.

Waited in line 30 minutes for a credit. Employees walking in back instead of taking care of customers.
Crystal, and Marina were the representatives. They are rude and to top it off, the manager Tiana was just as rude no apology only that this is the process. I asked her do you see this line.
She says she sees it, I asked her how long does she think I'm gonna wait.

Rude no apology.
Crystal was asked to contact a manager and she was rude w Susan that was standing in line w me.

I'm gonna write about this tire until everyone hears what I gotta say

Visiting IKEA in Fishers, IN.  Pretty happy with selections.  Went to get sink choice for our bathroom and were told 4 left.  Unable to get for us because in customer area.  Either we will have to come get another day, pay to ship or wait till after hours and they will get it down.  We waited two hours since we live out of town.  We got it home.  Since it was midnight when we got home we opened the box the next morning.  Sink completely broken.  Split two ways.  Seriously are you kidding me?  We will be calling today.  If they do not help us out.  Then we are calling Better Business Bureau.

Super pleased with the lack for crazy crowds!  We waited a while before our first visit because of this.  We were able to find the place pretty easily and parked reasonable close to the exit doors.  There was someone waiting inside that gave us shopping instructions.....    which we needed.  We then spent about an hour weaving our way through the store.  There were staff members readily available in all ox the areas.  We'll be back!

Dont buy from them if they told you that they have to get if from the "Back"  for you to pickup at the pickup area. I always love shopping at ikea but i recently move to this area and this is the WORST shopping experience ever. I went with my 5 months old son to purchase a shoe cabinet which i already lookup online before i go. I went to the self service area to look for it but was being told that the staff have to pick it up from the "Back" and i have to pay first at the checkout and go to the pickup area to pick it up. I paid and went to pickup area. I signed in with the pickup area staff and he told me he is going to get it and ask me to wait for my number to be call. 30 mins later, still no sign of anyone calling my number. I went to the desk and ask if they can check where the item is. This girl told me it's coming just have a seat and wait. Another 20 mins passed and my baby started getting fussy because i didnt plan to stay there more than one and a half hour, we were suppose to get home by that time so i can feed him. I went to the desk again and ask if they can bring my item out now because i had waited 1 hour ,if not, i want my refund and leave this place. She told me they are busy while there were 3 employees standing there chatting about where they are going to shop for black friday. My baby started to cry and i got angry and they finally got my item from the "Back". I guess the "Back" must be a enormous giant place for them to take 1 hour to get the item for me. If there is any IKEA MANAGER reading this post, please do something about the management over the pickup area. You guys are paying emoloyees to stand there and chat, instead of serving your cliengs.

IKEA comes to the Circle City.  

This is a 1-story IKEA and is a little smaller (with room to expand into the future) than some of the other stores I've visited. 

The 1-story setup forces you to walk through pretty much the entire store (to sell you more stuff) although there are a few shortcuts you can take to get to where you need to go.    It's easy to get lost in here if you don't stay on the normal path (indicated by the footprint decals on the floor).

Otherwise, the products are exactly the same as you'll find in their catalog. 

The best thing you can do is sign up for an IKEA Family card. 

You get free beverages (coffee, cappuccino, espresso, tea, milk, soft drinks) with your card.

Such a great store. Though it was hard to get into. It is set up with such precision. The products are both sturdy and affordable. The staging rooms make it so easy for you to visualize your house and what you want in it. Plus the food is amazing and so affordable as well. A++

This was my first time in an Ikea and I was blown away with the amount of items here! I thought they mainly sold furniture, but they had kitchen items, rugs, bath & bed textiles, lighting and more. It was overwhelming to walk through and the staff were few and far between. We needed help locating a specific item and it took about 20 minutes to find someone to assist us. Then, the checkout area only had three lanes (out of many) open. It took forever to check out.

Okay, I love IKEA just as much as the next person and really don't have any negative comments on about the store itself. My two star review reflects my experience with the staff. Don't get me wrong, every interaction I had with a staff member they were kind, respectful, and all things you'd expect, however with the exception of extreme lack of knowledge of how to do anything! 

We went about a month or so after the grand opening, just in time to still receive the free shipping deal on certain purchase totals, fell in love with the large sectional sofa and placed the order. I understand there is a learning curve in all things new, however it took 4 staff to work together to place the order and track down parts of the sofa and like 20 minutes. Then when we went to check out at the end, I showed the order paper and the cashier had to call back to the sofa department to figure out how to ring me up. 
Unfortunately just 3 days later we returned to the store to cancel the order since family would be giving us their couch instead and save the cash. I explained the situation to the staff and they were super friendly, however not so helpful! After standing and waiting at the desk counter for over an hour, I was only able to get a small portion of my money back because they did not know how to track down the order and cancel it all at once. They didn't know how to utilize the computer systems or call other departments, so instead they were physically running around the store to figure out my case. When I suggested calling other departments instead of running around, they said "but we don't know the extensions." What?! 
They made sure to cancel the delivery, but over a MONTH later IKEA still owes me $900+. They informed me I'd hear from them in a week or two by email or phone. Didn't happen. I contacted IKEA, spoke with someone who was helpful for over an hour, however she didn't work at Fishers location. She let me know I'd be hearing from them that SAME DAY. Four days later and I still haven't heard from them. It shouldn't be this difficult. 
I genuinely believe their kindness is true, I just feel bad they are this clueless on how to do their jobs. There's training experience lacking or a gap in leadership. Something! Something needs to be done, I can't be the only one experiencing this!

IKEA gives you exactly what you're looking for ... inexpensive furniture that lasts relatively long. This is a great place for contemporary starter furniture for all ages. We have purchased furniture for all three of of our children's dorms and first apartments. It has held up relatively well and has even been handed down. 
They are also very forgiving with their return policy. Quality is a 3. Their business practices push them to a 4 Star.

I have shopped at many Ikea's. The South Philly Ikea is the worst ikea i have ever been too. I have a Trysil full size bed, I am missing two bolts to connect the wooden side parts to the bed-frame. When I asked if they had the extra pieces. they said NO! I would have to order them online to be delivered to my house. Or buy a new bed-frame and take the two bolts out. A girl needs to sleep but I am not spending 119 for a new bedframe just for two bolts. that is ridiculous. Ikea check yourself! all you care about is  making money.

We've been to this Ikea store a lot. Sometimes it's for something serious like a sofa, sometimes it's for something for the kids rooms. My most recent trip was to replace the sofa cover I spilled a whole glass of red on, after I was in the doghouse for golfing earlier that same day so a speedy replacement was necessary! 

I walked in the exit like usual and went right to the computer kiosk so I could get my slipcover.  Turns out an employee has to set that up. So Matthew took care of me in a flash. I had my sheet for pickup and off I went. While I went to pay my wife went looking for lamp shades. After checkout is when the disappointment kicked in. 57 minutes later I get called for my item to be picked up. As I'm approaching the counter the attendant points to my box behind the wall. I go over to pick it up and hand her my sheet and I get scolded "get behind the yellow line" when I turned around there were two ladies that heard her and their eyes were huge in amazement. Since it's been 57 minutes I just wanted to leave. 

My experience with this side of the ikea experience was further eroded when I went to return the lamp shades today. I walked in at 10:55. I was number 69, they were on 56. I made an online purchase at 11:33 and they were on 66. At 11:45 I got called. Why does it take this long for a return, I waited 50 minutes in the middle of a Tuesday for a return.  Get outta here ikea. 

IKEAs offer decent stuff at a reasonable price, all of my experiences have been positive when on the sales floor but the return procedure and the pickup area is a disaster and the pickup area need major tending to as they are a horrible last experience at this Ikea.

It's IKEA. I mean. What else is there to say? It's something you just have to experience. They have a little bit of everything. The prices are fairly reasonable although on some products the quality is questionable. It gets crazy packed, so not really worth a trip if you just want to go and peruse the store. Although there are arrows to help lead you through, I still manage to get lost in the IKEA matrix. There is stuff everywhere. I completely get distracted as ooooohhh and ahhhhh through the store. I have yet to stop at the cafe, so can't comment on that. IKEA is, well, IKEA. I love it with its flaws and all. Plus, I no longer have to travel to Cincy to visit one. Whoo hoo!!

A behemoth of a store. This place could probably fit a CostCo and a Menards and ask where Sam's Club is at.

I'm not an Ikea cult member but we did bike there (yes, we biked to Ikea) and have lunch, all the while laughing at the massive lines of cars stuck in traffic while the cops waved us thru. Needless to say, there were no other bikes at the Ikea bike rack.

The Ikea cafeteria is fine and has Swedish meatballs galore. The food is nothing special - there's a reason you don't see a lot of Swedish restaurants around. But the food is perfectly fine and very reasonably priced.

I do have some Ikea furniture from years ago and the description of the food above is pretty fitting for their furniture as well - they are fine/ok, of sufficient quality, and very reasonably priced. And there's nothing wrong with that. At all.

I'm still new to the whole IKEA-craze. I've only been to the one in Cincinnati once before this visit. The design ideas and miniature rooms they have set up throughout the store serve for great inspiration. I'm trying to see past the whole "it's just a furniture store" feeling that I initially had/have, so it's growing on me. My girlfriend loves IKEA, so I'm sure we'll be seeing lots of their items in our future house. Maybe even on a wedding registry. Hah.

Like others have said, timing is everything. I came on a Sunday in the middle of the after-church crowd. Never again. Parking was an absolute nightmare. But I guess that's the territory with IKEA and the surrounding new business with similar cult followings (Portillo's, Top Golf, etc...). 

The "flow" of the store leads to a lot of bottlenecking and congestion, especially with the restaurant in the middle of the store, which is the main reason why I was in. Swedish meatballs and fries!

Overall, I can't knock IKEA more than one star. It's a brand new location, so obviously it's gonna be a little nutso. However, you can't beat the prices and products available. It's great to have one in Indy.
Swedish reindeer meatballs and gravy? Fried taters and reconstituted powdered scrambled eggs? Free senior coffee with a view of SLU? Try IKEA $1 breakfast!

Wow. Love the stuff. Hate the customer service and delivery service. Spent over $1500 in store for delivery. The sales rep in the store was excellent, confirming all information, showing and confirming the next day delivery window, and the whole procedure. None of it happened. Instead, I get a cryptic call saying order cannot be delivered and to be rescheduled. I had two numbers to call. Neither were identified as Ikea numbers but instead went to two cell numbers which were never answered nor did anyone return messages from the voicemails left. 

I'm cured. I'lll head down there tomorrow and get a full refund. I should be thankful I am spared from Ikea assembly hell and I will just go to a more traditional store and order the rest from Amazon online. Adios Ikea.

First trip to this IKEA. It wasn't crazy as I anticipated with it being so close to Christmas. 

Great deals and yummy food. I love Ikea!!

Drove over an hour to go to new store only to find out they were closing 4 hours early for their holiday party. There was no information about this on any of their websites!! HUGE DISAPPOINTMENT AND INCONVENIENCE!! Drove over an hour for less than 15 minutes. If information had been put on website we could have planned for another day.

Ok let me start by saying for many years I have thought IKEA is amazing. On vacations we go to IKEA if there is one near. We will drive to one for a weekend get away. Yep we love them but this location let the wind out of my sails. 

First off it seems so small. They do not seem to have many of the kitchen and bathroom gadgets that I love. Just all the small stuff in general. I also could not find employees any time I needed one. 

The cafe did not have take out cups bc we wanted to grab some coffee when we found it. Or at least we didn't see any. 

So yes it is nice Ikea is here but I just feel ours is missing something. 

I am gonna go back maybe we just didn't take enough time to actually take it all in. We will eat and enjoy the food. But it gonna be hard to have ikea with portillos right in front. 

Oh but the check out ppl were on top of it!

I think maybe part of the ikea excitement is traveling hours to get there. When it is so close maybe it takes the thrill away.

It has been a while since my last visit to any Ikea, and after spending two plus hours in their Conshohockon maze, I remember why I stopped shopping there.  Their warehouses are enormous, and there is so much stuff to look at that it can be overwhelming. But, the kicker comes when you have had enough browsing, decided not to purchase anything in order to consider the possibilities, and try to leave the premises. 

It is then you realize that you are lost somewhere on the second floor and don't remember how you got to the office furniture area. The signs say the check-out and exit is "that way," but that just leads you through every other department in the hanger, past the cafeteria, down the only flight of stairs, and through a second maze on the first floor. The maps sparsely displayed look like a game of Candyland or Chutes and Ladders, with little dots meandering through every corner of the building. It was at least 10 minutes before I reached the cashiers and saw the exit doors beyond them. Someone with claustrophobia could easily panic before reaching fresh air. 

Yes. I did see some desks, bookcases and lighting that might work well in the new office, but not as much as I had hoped. Prices were good, but I had the definite feeling that I would be settling for things based on limited choices, rather than true love of the furniture. And, by the time I made it out of the warehouse, I had little desire to go back in. 

Make it easier to escape and I would have no problem going back in smaller doses to explore and find what I want. Absent that, why would anyone voluntarily submit themselves to such torture?

Absolute craziness when we went! I'd definitely wait for the crowd to die down before making another IKEA trip. I felt rushed because there were so many people there. The IKEA is very large and I'm surprised how neat and tidy they kept it despite the large crowds of kids running around. Great selection and good quality furniture. Didn't check out the cafeteria at this location, but I'm sure it's like the others. Great place for students to by furniture! Similar or cheaper pricing to Walmart and WAY more variety. Only an hour or so away from Purdue. 

Took us almost 30 minutes to cash out. Our cashier was very friendly and apologized for the long wait - so sweet :) keep up the great customer service!

Through sheer determination and busy schedules, we waited two whole months after the grand opening to come check out our new Circle City IKEA. The first thing that struck me is that we have a ground floor IKEA. I've never been to one that wasn't two floors. It was strange, but we didn't feel slighted. There were still plenty of beautiful things to oggle. 

i really liked blue YOU ARE HERE maps hanging from the ceiling. I found them easier to get a big picture perspective than the arrows on the floor.

We didn't try out the restaurant which is located in the center of the store because we were on a mission that evening. Definitely next time. Overall, it was a pleasant experience and I'm glad we waited. 

Cue Janet Jackson's "Lets Wait a While."

The Fishers IKEA seems a bit smaller than other IKEAs I've been to, but it's still awesome. I went a couple of times when it first opened and it was mass chaos, but I went again on a Wednesday night around 7pm and I was able to find parking easily, the store wasn't crowded at all, and there was no wait at all to check out. Another reviewer mentioned not being able to find an employee when they needed something--I didn't find that to be the case at all.  I would probably avoid the store on the weekends for the foreseeable future, but definitely check it out sometime. Prices are reasonable, making it really easy to add some stylish pieces to your home without breaking the bank.

Finally stopped by IKEA... no regrets... bought too much stuff as always. This store is smaller than the other stores I have visited. Ground floor only. Still a pleasure as always. 
Wish I had a house big enough to buy all the cute stuff, alas I am limited in space, but I did score an unusual coffee table. Looks somewhat industrial and has rollers. Can't wait to put it together. Yes, I actually enjoy putting the furniture together. What can I say, I do enjoy puzzles and this is always one huge puzzle, especially if you don't read the instructions. 
Anyway, ample parking. I don't think half the folks realize that most up front spaces are family parking for small kids. I say that because I saw several single adults park in those areas. 
Besides the fabulous furniture, I highly recommend the store for anybody looking for linen, rugs, toys, kitchen stuff, entertaining in general, decorating, even gardening... tons of planters and flower pots and even live plants.
Ikea purposely makes their directions hard to read so the customer can pay the extra $100 or so to have a builder come and build your purchase.

Not as nice as the one in Ohio. I did like the new displays and flow thru was good. I like that they draw you into the cafe in the middle of the store if you follow the arrows. Nice way to sell snacks / beverage while shopping. Disappointed they didn't have the shelf I wanted in stock. On line it projected they would have 11 of them. I should have know better then to believe the data base. I had back surgery a month and half ago so it's not like I was going to get it put together anytime soon, but my e-mailed IKEA family coupon expires soon. Maybe I will get a late Christmas present in January or Feb.

IKEA is the McDonalds of home furnishings, the consistency of layout and presentation is at least half the attraction. The tiny-house people-sized dioramas are the other part. And the relatively inexpensive items the third part.

Sometimes a stroll through an IKEA, through the entire winding worm of a layout, is an urban version of a zen garden. My mind goes to another place, and I see but don't see the individual items, and sometimes flashes of kensho result in something in my shopping cart. :-)

This IKEA is a good IKEA even though (I learned tonight) that Canadian IKEAs don't offer free Family Club coffee as our American IKEAs do. :-(

IKEA is IKEA is IKEA. Love it or hate it, it proudly is what it is.

I happen to love IKEA, with all the promise of happy family life through the careful order and cleanliness that come from thoughtful home furnishings, or so the catalog would have me believe :-)

That some IKEA items are incredibly useful in my home just makes me more susceptible to the lure of the next IKEA item, especially in the kitchen. So, from time to time, a stroll through IKEA is called for, even when I'm not sure what I need, safe in the certainty that IKEA will have something to offer me that heretofore I couldn't have lived without.

The only bad thing is that I always want to spend more money than I have. I love their demo rooms and often imagine myself living in them. Its one of the most brillant marketing techniques I have ever witnessed. Simply genius. And its been working on me since I was 12. I am pretty sure I will always have something IKEA in my home, for the rest of my life.

IKEA, where you feel like a trendy socialite, hip decorator, Swedish meatball, and a maze rat all at once. This IKEA is all one level and seems a bit smaller than some other of their locations. That said, it's still a big maze and you can wander for hours. Lots of furniture and housewares, both functional and trendy. Big selection of styles and colors. I purchased two dressers and the price was decent for what you get. Some of the items are press board, which is cheap but the color veneers hide that.  The quality of material and hardware is higher than what you find in other brands. Check out the cafe by the main exit. Fun dye-free candies and other goodies such as pizza, chips, cinnamon rolls, etc...

I went into IKEA with my Ma and we spent 3 hours and still didn't make through the entire store! This storage is  huge! You could fit Costco and Sams in the same building! There are arrows that help guide you through the store to help with your shopping experience.


As said by other Yelpers that this store goes in a maze to the point you start at the show room and work your way through the store until you can pick up items and buy them. 

A lot of things in the store is affordable. I came in for lights and left with those plus some! Everything was affordable and good quality to be on sale. 

The staff is nice and helpful but it always seems like when you say "excuse ma'am/sir" they don't like that but almost everyone was very helpful and informative but didn't push sales in you which is great. 

During our excursion, we stopped to get some of these meatballs that everyone raves about. The food is setup cafeteria style where you get a tray and work your way around starting at desserts. Now why would they do that and start off with the ish we don't need! We got the veggie meatball meal that came with curry which was not hot but was ok, quinoa and steamed veggies for $3.99!!! Pretty good considering. 

After walking so long we decided to shortcut our way out of that place but will be back to get more! 

Oh p.s. Don't forget to sign up their rewards program. Oh and bring your own bag like ALDI. Or you can buy 1 for $.99.

Once you learn your way around this store it is so much fun. From hands-on showrooms, delectable cafe offerings, bountiful market place and warehouse to Swedish groceries and daycare, this domestic wonderland is a one stop shop! 

Conveniently located next to downtown Tampa, the giant blue building is easy to find and provides ample parking. Unlike the over crowded stores in the northeast, I've never had an issue at this one. 

One of my favorite aspects of the browsing experience is the lack of sales people. Recently, associates have asked me if I needed help finding anything -which I love. They're still not trying to sell me anything. They seem to appreciate the overwhelming amount of merch. 

The layout is relatively easy to follow. The showrooms were designed for the customer to experience. Everything's clearly labeled. Use the map and pencil handed to you upon entering to jot down the products you want or take photos. 

IKEA products range from super cheap and a bit flimsy to more expensive higher quality. It's important to remember that their furniture costs less because they don't assemble or ship it. This is awesome for those of us who enjoy adult legos. I tend to select their nicer dressers and coffee tables, and have yet to be disappointed. The lighting and kitchen appliance departments are my favorites. Useful items like cutting boards, cheese graters and tongs are inexpensive. Dazzling energy efficient lamps and LED lights of all home decor styles. The market place is where you fill your cart. 

The cafe offers satisfying and cheap breakfasts, lunches, snacks and dinners that feature traditional Swedish cuisine. I like the Swedish pancakes with lingonberry jelly. Sometimes IKEA promotes a free meal when you spend $100 or other food related discounts. The food is conveniently located in between the showrooms and market place to replenish you before you shop.  

Checkout can be tough. The lines are long and the registers are short. You have to wait for the person in front of you to pay before you have room to place your belongings. No shopping bags unless you buy one. The hardest part of the trip to IKEA is leaving without buying their freshly baked cinnamon buns. The tempting fragrance of cinnamon and sugary pastry heaven fills the check out lines every time. Perhaps I'm weak, but I regret nothing!
I used to love this place :( customer service and attitude has went down the shitter. So ghetto now

Everyone we encountered was very nice and helpful , starting from when we came in all the way to check out and the hot dog area. I knew exactly what I wanted to get and someone was readily available to assist.

They need electric scooters. My mother walks with a cane and this store is too big to go through. There's wheelchairs but I can't push a cart and wheelchair

Swedish reindeer meatballs and gravy? Fried taters and reconstituted powdered scrambled eggs? Free senior coffee with a view of SLU? Try IKEA $1 breakfast! Shop to your heart's delight and feast on very reasonablely priced breakfasts and lunches with a great view of mid town.

My experience with IKEA, one which has been dragged out over a month now, has been entirely negative and upsetting. I am downright disgusted with this company. I ordered a bed and a mattress on 11/24 from IKEA online. I was sent one confirmation email saying my order has been processed and that I would receive additional emails once it had shipped. A couple of weeks went by, I didn't receive anything additional. I finally bit the bullet and called IKEA customer service on December 10th to check on my order status. I waited on hold for 1 hour and 20 minutes only to reach a representative who vaguely explained there was a "glitch" in their system which is why I hadn't received any follow up emails. She told me that unfortunately my order had not been processed correctly and that the original approximate delivery date had been 12/20, however that was no longer going to be the case due to the glitch and therefore my new delivery date would be 1/4. I received an email confirming this date the same day. A few days later, contrary to what she had told me, I began to receive emails stating my order would be delivered on 12/20. These emails had no time window (they always give you a time window option) or tracking information. I was confused and of course given this conflicting information, I called and again after waiting on hold 45 minutes, I reached a representative who called the third party delivery company XPOlogistics and confirmed they had not taken shipment of my order and they were not going to deliver it and the emails I was getting were received in error. Then she confirmed my order wasn't going to be delivered until 1/8/18 (notice how the date conveniently changed yet again). So on 12/20 around 11am to my surprise I get a phone call while I am at work from a man who says he is at my apartment asking, "Where Am I, he has my bed to deliver". So after I was misinformed by IKEA for the second time, this delivery company randomly shows up at my apartment, after I was told they didn't even have possession of the order, with literally no warning, no phone call or email ahead of time with any tracking or delivery information AT ALL including what time window they would be there in, etc. So I have to spend 30 minutes at work trying to get this resolved with IKEA, and so after no apology and no explanation of their incompetent mistake they give me another delivery date of 12/26/17, a week later and 1 month and two days after I originally ordered this bed, which is ridiculous. I confirmed with 3 people, (1 manager from IKEA, 1 CSR and a supervisor at XPOLogistics) that my order would be delivered 12/26 and my delivery window was 5 pm to 9 pm. I also have 2 emails confirming the same. It's 12/26 and 10 pm and let me tell you this bed STILL hasn't been delivered and after calling XPOLogistics and IKEA, again waiting on hold 60 minutes with IKEA alone, I was told that somehow they screwed this up for the third time and I won't be getting my delivery today because the delivery man, going against everything I was told, tried to randomly deliver my package today at 12:45 pm, well out of the delivery window I was given by 3 different people, and of course I wasn't there, so their only solution again, was not to apologize, but to say they would reschedule another delivery date which is 2 weeks out. So I immediately asked for a refund, which will take a whopping 7-14 days. This company is a TERRIBLE joke. I will never have any future dealings with IKEA. They are an absolute nightmare. Their business transactions are horrific, their customer service representatives are misinformed and poorly trained on how to do their jobs. Their managers are unsympathetic and unapologetic. I highly regret ever placing this order with IKEA in the first place and I can guarantee they will never receive any future orders from me. This company is a sad pathetic excuse for a business. I guess in the end you get what you pay for, if you buy cheap furniture you get cheap lousy service with it. Even the simple things like delivering they can't even get right, after 3 chances. I'll be gladly be buying a bed from a company who actually cares about their customers.

This is one of the worst stores that I have ever purchased from.  I purchased a large order from them and after I came back to my office I realized that I had to exchange one of the desks for a smaller one to fit into the office.  I called the store in Conshohocken where I just made the purchase and found out that there is no way to get through to the store.  Since I did not know the extension number for the sales person I dealt with it said that I can dial by name by putting the first three letter of the first name.  I did and the message I got is that there is no such person in this store.   Calling their customer service call center I was on hold for 45 minutes before a person picked up the phone and advised me that he could not help me as he only deals with purchases online.  I asked him if he could transfer me to the store and his comment was that they really don't like that and that I should just go back to the store to make the exchange.  He said that he will transfer me, he pushed some button did not have the courtesy to wait to see if the transfer sent through and an error message came up that the transfer could not go through.  I now have to go back to the store which is a gross inconvenient since I am far away from that store.  This was my first and now the last purchase I will ever make from this store.  They have no services after the sale.  Amazon is where I will continue to go to as they don't have any of this nonsense.

IKEA (South Philly) is the worst furniture store we have ever visited.  They couldn't deliver items because our phone number was wrongly written down "by them" and they couldn't reach us when they tried to deliver them.  The employee was absolutely not experienced, and was not helped by anyone.  It took more than 30 min to arrange shipping of a mattress, a book shelf and a small table.  Also our primary contact we requested was email, but we did not receive any emails from them when they tried to deliver them. The customer service said that we should come back to the store (not on the phone) and pay $59 for the shipping fee again.  This was absolutely not acceptable, because this is not only matter of service, but illegal.

Only go if you are feeling patient! Everyone loves Ikea! Tons of great household deals are available. There are rooms set up and you can purchase everything you see from appliances and furniture down to the drawer organizers and dishes. There is office furniture, items for kids rooms, bedroom accessories and furniture,  kitchen gadets, and so much more. If you are hungry, about half way through there is a cafeteria and the food looked delicous.

It's too much fun, you guys. I can't help it, I'm loving this big box store and I have to say it's more for the Scandinavian vibes and eats than it is the furniture- not that the furniture and designs aren't great as well. My recent visit to Finland has me geeking out over the little touches like the simplistic Christmas decor and lingonberry everything. I even picked up a box of their frozen veggie potato pancakes to eat at home after my latest visit.

A few other nuggets that leave me loving IKEA:
-none of their toys in the Children's section require batteries- very educational focused

-the rig selection is top notch- specifically the Turkish rugs made by Turkish women using old pieces of rugs from turkey 

-the cafeteria is very reasonably priced and offers several healthy and vegetarian options 

-the fresh plant section was surprisingly impressive and rumor has it its one of their top selling categories in the store

-programming throughout the month like a Swedish inspired Christmas dinner for $16 (super affordable and festive rolled into one)

First time ever visiting an Ikea. Honestly, not sure I understand the hype. It was crowded and somewhat confusing to weave through and around the displays. I wasn't impressed with much of the products but did notice their cheaper price tags. I might be more satisfied if I needed cheap furniture right now but I don't. Didn't find anything in the home decor or small products that screamed "buy me!!". The people I was with had to pay for their items and we waited in the check out for nearly 15 minutes. Not my style, but kudos to those who enjoy it. 3 stars because it was clean and service was friendly.
This furniture is all great in all ,but wtf is a Swedish Meatball and why is it different from a regular meatball.

I, as another customer mentioned, waited around 45 minutes to make a return. The returns area, at least, is very depressing and dingy, and there was only one other person working, the other employee was talking to a friend the whole time. People were so aggravated and annoyed, but I found it a good opportunity to practice some mindfulness on a not-very-comfortable, and aesthetically blah sofa.

IKEA seems to be démodé right now, and I can't imagine wanting to shop there. Maybe 15 years ago, but it needs a reinvention.
Herded like cattle for hours through this never ending maze of cheap plastic and particle board furniture. It was horrible. I am scarred for life.

Going over Christmas break wasn't the smartest choice we learned. I had waited for the hype to die down and a friend mentioned it wasn't busy in the morning, but we didn't get there till about 3:30. We actually lucked out with a parking spot, but the entrance was jammed with people. 
I am not sure why they only made the Fishers location one floor. I have only been to one other Ikea, but it seemed so much better to have it spaced out. There were just so many people. 
We actually went to eat first. Not sure if there is an easy way to get to the restaurant part, but we eventually found it. The line to get food wasn't long, but tons of people eating so we must have just missed the craziness. They do have 2 lines, but had just closed the 2nd one. They did still have 2 check out people so it was an easy process. I got the meatball meal with mashed potatoes and veggies. It had 8 meatballs. My husband got a $2.99 salad! He helped me finish off my meatballs. I only ate half. I thought it was a great deal for $4.99. 
They have these really awesome tray carts. We didn't need one, but it was great for families. They held I think 3 trays! 
After we ate we made our way to the kitchen area. I liked looking at the setups and hope to get a new sink soon. I'd love if my drawers and pantry could be like the ones we saw at Ikea! 
Then we left. We went back at the entrance. So I am not sure we saw much of the store. All the spaces with couches had people sitting on them. I actually saw a few guys napping. And there were so many kids. I was surprised since they have a kid area. 
I will go back after the holiday break to actually shop and look around more. I do wish there was an easier way to get to the restaurant part. maybe we will discover one on our next trip. 
You can sign up for an Ikea family card at the front of the store. I got a free hot tea with our card!

After spending years of traveling a couple of hours to the nearest IKEA, I was extremely excited that Indy finally has its own. As far as IKEAs go, it functions in the same way and has the same excellent level of service. 

I will prewarn those who are used to the size of some other IKEAs that this is a smaller one, but it is in no way lacking for availability of goods offered. 

My main concern about the location of the store was from a traffic perspective, but that concern was squashed the first time I went. They thought through the flow with having customers exit towards 106th street instead of automatically funneling them back to 116th.

I'm sure I will be enjoying this IKEA for years to come.
Who doesn't love Ikea? Cafe had good options. Can't beat the prices. Spent at least 3 hours here.
Great location!   Love the child sitting service!   1:30 hr for IKEA Family Members!!!

Terrible customer service. I ordered some bathroom accessories and faucets online. They charged over 50 dollars to deliver for a small package. The products where not manufactured with quality. I returned the items (at my cost $26 with insurance). Its been almost 5 weeks and the package was confirmed received 2 days after it was sent. I called for a status update, that took 3 hours of my day while they put me on hold, hung up on me, put me on hold again and again.. finally they confirmed receipt with me verbally but where not able to provide me with a confirmation #. They where also unable to process the return because they where "busy". They promised to send a confirmation the next day and told me to keep an eye out for 7-10 days for refund. I've gotten no email confirmation and no refund. I reached out through their facebook at next attempt. When I got a response the next day I immediately followed through (literally 1 min later with the order #). I did not get a response until the following day. Again, the customer service is poor, now the story i'm getting is we can't find your package, can you provide us with the tracking info. So I send it and now i've been waiting again with no response. How hard is it to service a customer? Why does every question a rep from that place come with getting put to the back of the line? Why are they so unreachable? It's a simple return.. This process should take all of 5-10 minutes tops. I would unequivocally not recommend IKEA. This is ridiculous!! They have no regard for my time.

Who doesn't love IKEA?? The customer service is always great!

I thoroughly enjoy walking through the showroom & getting design ideas. Food is always very cheap n convenient. They have a daycare too! If you wanna leave your child while you shop & lift the heavy items from warehouse.

This was an amazing place to shop for interior things such as beds, kitchen, living rooms, storage and much more!! This place has wonderful staff & is very neat & clean.

The cafeteria is amazing & spacious. Everything is beautifully planned inside cafeteria. They have a tray holder which holds up to three trays at a time.
   
Even though place is really big , they have great directory of the place. The warehouse is pretty big so before you go into find your furnishings you might want to write down the number of the products or download the IKEA app which can help you keep track of your things you want. Overall, this place was fun, enjoyable & just an amazing & splendid shopping experience!!

I wanted to see the place for years and I think I should have seen it back then. It's big and impressive from a size standpoint, but it is too dirty and worn out to be pleasing. A lot of empty bins where I was looking. The food deserves a special mention for being mostly terrible. Grilled chicken on the salad; gray and rubbery, stale tasting. Salad wilted. Beef short rib, dry to the point of toughness. French fries soggy. Mixed veg mush. Fountain soda off brand, off taste. Going to be hard pressed to go back.

I will say IKEA is IKEA. They are the same no matter where you go in my opinion. I think that could be a good and bad thing. On one hand the set up and everything is pretty similar so it is easy and familiar to navigate. On the other hand I do feel people go for an experience and that experience is going to be the same no matter which store you go to. 

In my opinion the prices are either VERY fair, where you'd say "I can't believe this is only __ dollars", or its VERY pricey, where you'd say "Who would pay __ amount". 

One downside to this location is that it is only one level so to me it feels like they have less because you aren't covering as much ground. 

When we went it was very busy. of course on the day of the opening (which by the way we were one of the crazies who camped out for three days). We went about 2 months after it opened and was still pretty busy which we expected.

One great thing about IKEA is the price of their food. You can't beat the price of it! If it was closer we would eat here more regularly.

Trying to eat vegan this past few months. I'm doing quite well but man do i need a new taste for it. So I was recommended to check it out over at this place. The best part in this place is the food is good and the cost is fair. However, located at the checkout area is their small food market. Containing frozen meatballs and vegan ones too. The taste is phenomenal when cooked well. I use the oven method. Plus they got vegetable cakes that taste great with the meatballs. As for dessert, lots of cookies but I usually like leaving the place with frozen yogurt. In any case, this is just my review on the food. As for furniture and housing decorations, you need to check it yourself because they have a wide selection of choices. For example a light ball which expands when pulling the string. Keep in mind though that the prices vary on how unique the item is. 
Recommended for home decorations and healthy food in their small marketplace.

The system for buying a simple cabinet had us waiting in line 3 separate times. Long lines.  It was horrific. 

We usually enjoy a light meal here.  We waited in line for 15 minutes and they were out of half the food. Every single table and chair was filthy.  When we finished the dirty tray shelf was overflowing with no space.  

Terrible. What happened to you, Ikea?

I was excited about making a good review. However, I am back here at 8:45pm to get the remainder of what I need. Purchased a platform bed and asked if the slats came with the set. I was told they did. I get home, my boyfriend gets everything set up and there are no slats. I called customer service and was on hold the entire 29 mins it took me to get here. No one ever picked up the phone. I probably should have asked another sale associate when I grabbed all the boxes. The first girl that helped me was in a rush to get me going so that's probably why she said the slats were already included. The sales associate next to her was complaining about being at work for 3 hours and not given a break. Doesn't seem like the employees have good attitudes about being at work. I could have let all that go and probably would have written a good review had the associates been more helpful.

Every time I walk into this store I feel like a million bucks. Now if only that could translate into my bank account so I can buy everything I want. 

There never seems to be enough staff or check-out lines open, similar to the Walmart down the road. There's nothing spectacular about this place. All IKEA's look the same. 

Out of habit any time I go to IKEA, I get the dollar Vanilla Ice Cream Cone they make. Don't know why, I can't resist.
Love ikea!  This location even has underground parking to keep you from the elements when loading your car!

I was told they did. I get home, my boyfriend gets everything set up and there are no slats. I called customer service and was on hold the entire 29 mins it took me to get here. The first girl that helped me was in a rush to get me going so that's probably why she said the slats were already included. The sales associate next to her was complaining about being at work for 3 hours and not given a break. Doesn't seem like the employees have good attitudes about being at work. I could have let all that go and probably would have written a good review had the associates been more helpful.

Displays have changed up a little since before Christmas. Nice they keep it fresh. I love the pear apple candles, but they don't burn long. The packet of gravy mix makes a very small portion.  Biggest complaint would be the line. Even today when they were slow the line was stupid slow. The gentleman cashier in our line was taking his drawer out with people in line. The young lady talking over had zero sense of urgency putting her drawer in then she had issues. She moved the customer in front of us to the next line and still had issues. She then went back to the first one she tried as lane next to her opened. That second cashier should have taken the customer in front of us and us but instead called people out of other lines. We moved to a credit card only line and finally got checked out. I bought enough candles and gravy mix I won't need to go back for months thank god.

Just wanted a  munch,
One day around lunch. 
The downstairs  IKEA 
Snack bar's my idea
Of where I could eat in a crunch.

For  one - eighty three
(Includes  GST)
I got a hot dog
And instead of their  glogg:
Soda,  coffee or tea. 

The frank didn't thrill,
But the drink did refill,
So I lavish three stars
On IKEA snack bars.
But next time its McDonald's for me.

Horrible experience today at IKEA. I had a return. They do have an outstanding return policy! BUT I waited over 30 minutes to be waited on.  When I was waited on it was a rude and very slow customer service rep. It was so bad it could have been a Saturday Night Live skit.  She was rude in her interaction. Bottomline, I had my credit card stolen so when I tried to return on the new card she told me I would have to call the credit card company. (I am now late for an appointment because of how long I have waited. I asked to speak to the manager to share my experience. She called the manager explained my situation and hung up. She then repeated I need to call my credit card company.) Fine, so I asked to use their phone to call. She turned it toward me and said yes. I dialed...to then hear the call didn't go through. I then asked her, is there a number to dial out. She smiles at me and says yes...then pushes the number, and says "I think it is 9". While waiting I told her I would still like to speak to the manager. Finally after verifying my card number the return was made. A manager did come up to talk to me, but she was, in my opinion, she was kindly rude. I told her I had to go. So I have placed a call to the store manager. It was like pulling teeth to just get to her voice mail. So I will see if they call me back. I am not sure at this point if I will return. I don't care if their product is good and reasonable...the return policy is outstanding, but if your customer service is horrible (wait timing) and kindly rude I choose to go somewhere else. Yes, I am only one of the IKEA shoppers (we furnished many rooms with their products), but it is a principle.  Very disappointed! And I forgot to push the button to rate my customer service experience!!! :(

The ultimate retail store, brought to you by Sweden!

This place is madness - I suggest eating at their cafeteria before embarking on the epic journey through their shopping Mecca.  The meals are inexpensive and filling.  

Know going in: if you're purchasing furniture or large items, bring a friend and grab the palate cart instead of a grocery cart.  You'll need the friend to grab stuff from shelves at the end, and the cart won't cut it for heavy, bulky items.

They snake you around their store on purpose - it's an internal marketing scheme to force you through the various departments with the hopes of you purchasing items you otherwise weren't their for.  

Many kitchen items on the 1st floor are quite a bargain and you can really save some money if you shop wisely.  Some others appear inexpensive on the surface but a cursory Amazon search while in store will keep the prices true.

One of the best places for matted picture frames - perfect for the artist looking for an inexpensive way to frame their finished works.

I've been to this Ikea an insane amount in the last two weeks because I just moved into a new place. The facility is huge and clean, just like any of their other stores in different cities. 

Getting an Ikea family card gets you discounts on certain things (saved $4 on a duvet cover for my son) and also gets you a free coffee each trip. Their prices are always pretty reasonable on most things and they have a huge selection of all items for your household needs. 

The only reason I'm giving four stars is because the customer service is a bit lacking. My first trip, I was by myself and getting the very popular Malm set in Queen size. I went up to the computer area to see if I was about to get all the pieces I needed. There were two people there and neither offered to help me put the very large pieces onto my cart. Instead, another customer saw me struggling and offered to help me. The next two times I went, I had similar experiences. My last trip, I loaded up my cart and my car all by myself with a kid's bed that you can see in the pictures (it was not light or a small package at all). I was also accompanied by my two year old and no one offered to help me. Hiring one extra person to help around the store would be make the customers feel a bit more at ease.

Like a kid in a candy store, but for adults! GIGANTIC store! First area has rooms that are preset up so you can get an idea of what goes together. If you see something you like take a photo of the purchase tag. This will come in handy at the warehouse. 
Next area is each individual piece in a store like setting. You can grab anything from a knife to a couch.
The last area is the warehouse. Your tag you took a photo of in the beginning is connected to an isle number and then a shelf number so you can find that piece much easier.
There is a nice restaurant in the center with great deals on delish food entrees. Desserts are amazing and not the norm. Drinks are $1, unless you have a IKEA card, then coffee and cappuccino are free. Salads are $2.99. Most entree's are $4.99.
The last area has discounted returned or damage items at 25%off retail. Worth it to check out.
There's a small deli at the front that has $1 items. Hot dogs and cups of ice cream. Yum

Glad to have an IKEA finally in Indy, after making occasional trips to Cincinnati and Chicago over the past years.

Since not moving any more, and kids older, I have far less need of IKEA than previously but know the chain well.

Strange that this IKEA is single level, most are two. Parking all street level too.

This store is still new and hence packed, full of folks who seem unfamiliar with the IKEA setup. Traffic flow is weird.

Everything new, bright, and the merchandise was very much in-stock despite the considerable business going on. Lines were long and a bit slow, though.

Restaurant did the typical IKEA no-frills meals. Salmon, meatballs, etc all on target as usual.

My biggest beef was with the self-serve grocery by the entrance. It is way smaller than average, limited selection of Swedish groceries, and no cashier. To pay you have the go to the take-out line nearby. Total disaster. 20 minutes in line to get your frozen Swedish meatballs. It's not right.

ok here's the thing. i love this place, don't get me wrong. the food is delicious and low priced, and it's definitely lots of fun. i could easily give it 5 stars, but here's the thing. customer service is AWFUL. i was sitting in one of the office chairs on display, and one of the workers came up behind me and shoved me out of the way. it was a chair with wheels so i completely slid to the side. i kid you not, the worker grabbed the back of my chair, and pushed me to the side. she had the angriest expression on her face. all of the workers have been pretty rude. yes, they may have just been having a bad day, i don't blame them, but shoving a customer out of the way isn't a great way to cope with your anger. still a great place, but don't expect much from the workers.

First time doing business here, opted for delivery & assembly and made purchase yesterday.  Pre-scheduled delivery for the 2-6pm slot today.  Received 3 calls and 1 text in the morning - 3 of the contacts to move my scheduled delivery time up.  I had out of town business in the morning and did not appreciate the interruption.  There was a reason I requested the afternoon!  I returned the delivery guy call once I was back home in Philly, we agreed on delivery at 1pm.  The guy doesn't show until 2:20pm and only has 3 of the 5 pieces I paid for.  He's carrying 2 big pieces by himself and not exactly smoothly. This wood dents easily.  He cannot mount a piece without the other 2 pieces so I'm left with an extra piece of furniture taking up space in my livingroom.  Cannot get in contact w anyone at Ikea.  I have to move things back into my hallway & then move them out of the way AGAIN whenever Ikea schedules for the rest of my furniture to be sent & FINALLY get everything assembled.  I hope these are all of the inconveniences - DO NOT want to have to change my work schedule over this as well.  So far this has been hands down the WORST customer service EVER!  I hope that Ikea corrects this nightmare.  Think twice about their delivery option!!!

Shopping in person with IKEA is amazing but if you're unfortunate not to have one close by, they do now offer online ordering.  I have to say that the online ordering takes forever.  Don't expect to get anything within days.  It will actually take weeks.  It's disappointing too because I have a property that I want to stage and I won't be able to do it in time because of the late shipment.  I don't understand why the length of time?  I'm ordering very simple things like throw pillow covers, etc.  I really wish there was a store close by that I could go to.  I was so excited to see that they started online orders but it's really not a benefit unless they can speed their process up.

Sadly  disappointed in the customer service, I was told they were helpful and knowledgeable about their product and cared about their customers. Good ideas in the store but they had 16 of a product on the shelf and refused to sell it because they were displays. They showed 12 in stock but none were there and nothing would change their increasingly bad attitude that we were bothering them. First visit was our last, called and asked to see a manager, I was told they do not work the floor and would just ask an associate, really???? beyond disappointed since I traveled from the South side just to visit this poorly run retailer,

Get it together IKEA!  Several employees walking around playing on their cell phones.  Only 5 cashiers with each line being about 15 deep. Took over 20 minutes to check out at 1pm on a Thursday. Employee with pink hair kept coming out of her office to check on the cashiers, but never called for additional cashier back up. Not sure why store management doesn't have a better handle on this ongoing issue.

So glad to have IKEA in Indy! The cafeteria could be more organized. I'm always a little worried about finding a place to sit, but the food is delicious. I bought a couch a few months ago, and it took forever for all of the pieces to come in. However, I don't think this was the employee's fault and they handled my frustration very well. I live close, so even just walking though the store is a lot of fun. I could easily spend hours here each time (in a good way).

IKEA is fantastic. This one is one of the nicest we've been too! And it's a huge time saver having it in Indy rather than Cinci. 

Pro tip, if you know what you want just head in through the cafeteria area and then walk right into the warehouse. This will save you at least 6 hours of your trip. You can find your things by  looking up it up on the IKEA website.

The Cincinnati Ikea was always a treat when I visited on the occasional weekend. I was soooo excited when the Fishers Ikea opened however, so was my mom so I had to wait until thanksgiving weekend when she came to visit e in Indy to go! I will say, I don't like the one floor layout as much as the Cincinnati layout. The first floor layout seems smaller. The food in the cafe was still delicious. We love the meatballs and mashed potatoes and this time it came with grilled mushrooms too! I also love love love their berry soda! Walking around Ikea is always fun- I love interior design and it's amazing what they can do with such small places! The only complaint I have is the lines were so long and they only had like 2 registers open. We only had a few things so we put them down and left. We did enjoy it though- love seeing what they have each season!

I love Ikea! You can find any and everything you need for the home, the patio, the garden... Whatever!! The styles are not traditional, but modern, clean and simple. Prices are good too!
