Lots of options! Come prepared to shop and to stay for a while. Also wear very comfortable shoes, as this Ikea building is so large there will be a lot of walking involved! But always great finds and cool stylish ascessories for the home!

I had every reason in the world to not enjoy IKEA, the Fishers, Indiana location of the cultishly popular Swedish-founded superstore known for self-assemble furniture and other items that are high quality yet surprisingly affordable. 

First, IKEA is huge. I'm in a wheelchair and typically alone - thus, I tend to get exhausted and shopping for larger items in such a situation is a major pain. 

Secondly, IKEA is crowded. I mean really crowded. Indiana has wanted an IKEA for a long time and Indiana is still seriously responding to IKEA's opening in the area that is about 30 minutes north of Indy. 

Thirdly, and somewhat embarrassingly, my gifts for self-assemble kind of resemble my gifts for walking. I have 0% of a tech brain. 

What happened? I took an unexpectedly warm January Sunday afternoon with no real obligations and ventured up to Fishers. You know your business is a major player when the street's name is changed to match your business - IKEA Way. However, you can rest assured that Lantern Road will get you there.

The parking lot is huge and the parking lot was packed. Being disabled paid off a bit in this situation as there's two long rows of accessible parking directly in front of the main entrance. The spots are all ADA compliant and I believe they were all van accessible with some very specifically saying it. It's also nice that they have a sidewalk between the two sides - meaning that those with mobility impairments or in chairs don't have to walk in the street. 

I'd love to thoroughly describe IKEA, but upon this first visit I can honestly say I couldn't begin to tell you how to make your way through the place. Essentially, all the different sections are numbered from 1-26 and you keep following your way through the store visiting one of the most delightful, immersive showrooms I've seen. It occurred to me at one point that because you really only have outside windows in the cafe area and toward the checkout area, you really get a sense of being immersed in IKEA. I quickly wasn't looking at clocks or looking for windows or thinking about leaving - I was enjoying the shopping experience. 

Rather than try to describe the rooms, let me tell you what I loved:

1) The accessibility is amazing here - seriously. They have wheelchairs available and while I won't say every specific area/room is perfectly accessible, I was amazed at how much this place was accessible even with a crowd. Is a huge place? Absolutely. You need to plan for that, but if you're in a wheelchair you can easily find your way around. 

2) As packed as this place was? It was surprisingly stress-free. Baby cries? You hear it, but it's not piercing like in most stores. People talking? You hear them, but you can do your own thing and I found it all rather peaceful.

3) Because it's lower stress? I'd dare say that customers are friendlier. Of course, there's always exceptions. But, seriously...I was amazed at the courtesy. 

4) The pricing has something for every budget - sure, there's high-end stuff here. But, I literally shopped for three hours and spent five bucks on my first visit for a candle, a pack of batteries, and one of their bags. I found lots more I wanted, but I wanted to do some planning first. 

5) Employees - you know how godawful the HHGregg folks were? Intrusive, high-pressure? It's just the opposite here. They are casual, friendly, well-informed and quietly present. You know them by their shirts and name tags, but not a single time did I feel pressured. 

6) They don't just "sell," but they help explain the practical side of their items. I mean, sure, they want to make a profit. But you get a "people" vibe here - not a "profit" vibe.

7) The cafe is very cool and has been described in many reviews. I visited it, but didn't get anything this time. 

8) Bathrooms are all wheelchair friendly and, I've never seen this before, the disabled stall has a "medical emergency" button at the commode. How freaking brilliant is that? 

They offer an IKEA Family Card that is free and comes with special perks (like a free coffee/tea) and discounts; they offer a play area for kids and for inept folks like me they do offer, for a fee, delivery and assembly. 

What didn't I like? It was a minor issue, but I found the check-out process slow and tedious and a little too close to Aldi's for my liking. They are friendly and helpful, but the lines are long (but again, relatively stress free) and you definitely need to be prepared for a lack of plastic bags. Europe is way ahead of the U.S. on this issue. 

While I may not have spent a fortune today, I definitely fell in love with the place and the experience. As a customer with a disability, I felt like this was a place I could easily go and really immerse myself in the experience. Wouldn't it be cool if they did something like start a companion shopper program for shoppers with disabilities? That would really make it easier, but there's so much to love here and I can't wait to go back.

Ok, I must be in the minority here, or I just visited on the wrong day and at the wrong time, but I was super annoyed by this place. Parking was horrendous. Seriously, we drove around for 15 minutes looking for a spot. Once inside, the cattle call was in full force. Throngs of people being weaved back and forth at a snails pace. We originally went to look at a desk but upon seeing it in person, realized it was cheap and wouldn't last more than a year or two. As we wound our way around, I found myself getting more irritated. Maybe it was the crowds, maybe it was my mood but I just didn't see anything else that piqued my interest. I really am having a hard time understanding the attraction to Ikea. I may wait a few months and give it another go, but I don't see myself going out of my way to visit.

I liked the items they have there- good price and modern looking design. But every time it took a long time for me to check out. This trip I got a frame and 3 other kitchen items. I saw they have 20+ registers, only 4 opened. Each line stood more than 10 customers, the management didn't bother open more registers.  And there were no "less than 10 items express lane" nor "self-check out" lane. One lady in my line ran into credit card problem, the cashier took 10 minutes + still can't solve it. People waited on the line losing their patient (including me), some of them yielding "angry and hungry" (it was lunch time). Finally manager came and opened a new register. It wasted 25 minutes of my time to pay for the 4 items. The lady right in front of me only bought one $2 shower curtain and 30 minutes of her precious time was wasted in  waiting. 
No wonder the retail are losing ground to on-line shopping. Check out system need improvement for IKEA.

I approach IKEA differently than most. I have had so much time wasted there, that I now always make a strict plan before setting foot inside. I look things up online, check to see if they're in stock, make a list. I have a mental map of where departments are, and plan accordingly. I enter through the exits (not hard, someone is always going out), or right next to it, by the returns area. This way, I am not forced up the escalator to the showrooms, where there is no product access, except for a rare few items (there is no need to go to the 2nd floor, unless you are browsing). I then walk in through the checkout, where there is a pile of discarded carry-bags to use, and head to "As Is" first (on the left), then to the warehouse/marketplace (on the right). I leave a mental bread crumb trail so I can remember how to get the heck back out, and I go directly to what I need. (I have learned a few "shortcuts," and those help, but still are never as the crow flies.)

Through trial and error over the years, we have tried products from all departments (furniture, lamps, linens, plants, patio, kitchen, bathroom, dining, rugs, pets, storage, laundry, decor, kids).

When I first met him, my husband had one of those apartments mentioned in "Fight Club" with the IKEA flat-packed MDF furniture all over. It disintegrated in a few years, and was/is the worst waste of money, IMO. We have bought some all-wood pieces there, but, IMO, "IKEA" is Swedish for "crap" when it comes to furniture. I don't recommend furniture from IKEA, but, disclosure, I am an antiques/thrifting person for furnishings, so IKEA will just never do it for me.

What I now buy after years of "testing" IKEA product offerings:
LED Edison bulbs, linens (down in particular), plastic shelf liner, gift wrap, "As Is" items (explained below), plastic storage containers, curtains/drapes, some hardware items (wall hooks are a decent deal), and an occasional kitchen need (their stainless roasting pan is a great buy), or other home decor piece (their all-wood storage boxes are useful). We also used their pre-cut oak butcherblock countertops for a portion of our kitchen, another win. All these are items whose price is great for the quality provided, making it a value that surpasses comparable options elsewhere.  

"As Is" -- This section is located by the registers. It is between checkout and returns, because returns get marked down and thrown right in the "As Is" bins. In addition to returns, they also have floor models, damaged items, and discontinued stuff. I go there for upholstery. They always have sofa cushion covers, which I clean, and cut down to make throw pillows. The price per yard for that quality of fabric is unbeatable. I purchase their $1.99 bed pillows, and shove the weakly-stuffed filler into one corner, then sew it down to a 14"/16"/18"/whatever square to use as throw pillows. If you sew, this all makes sense, and I am giving away my secret. IKEA sells pillow inserts in all sizes, and at ~$5 they are half the price of sewing stores, but my $1.99 + a little sewing trick is cheaper than anything else.

My overall rating is based on current experience, after trial-and-error-ing everything, and getting into a groove that works for me at this store.

*  *  *  TIP  *  *  *
I do NOT recommend shopping carts unless you absolutely NEED one. The wheels rotate 360 degrees and swivel all over while you try to push, giving you the ab workout from hell. I have stubbed my toe or twisted an ankle too many times to ever want to use those things (notice no homeless person ever steals an IKEA cart). 

*  *  *  TIP  *  *  *
I do NOT recommend IKEA's heavily-fertilized plants, which die pretty quickly.

*  *  *  TIP  *  *  *
Seasonal items always go on mega-sale the day after Christmas (gift wrap, etc.).

*  *  *  TIP  *  *  *
Avoid weekends if you can. It is filled with lollygaggers, completely unfamiliar with the maze effect, or the marketing tactics designed to daze and confuse (on them, it works). They end up getting in your way, and making things take twice as long, not to mention lines at checkout.

I really missed going to Ikea since moving to Indianapolis.  I literally used to live a stone's throw away from one and made weekly visits to meet family on "Ikea Fridays" !

Having put off visiting this location since it's opening last fall, I took the plunge because of Ikea withdrawals setting in. However, I didn't expect it to still be crazy busy. Seems like there were more 'touristy' shoppers rather than real shoppers, so navigation was difficult. 

 There were more showrooms to add to your imagination but I will have to find a slower day to peruse these.
Although there were plenty of Ikea workers, very few asked to assist shoppers. Annemarie in kitchens gave a 'little class' on drawer organization which was pretty interesting. 

Check out lanes crazy as usual; again lots of groups purchasing one or two items, so it took twice as long to get out. Hate that the food items are after check outs, I almost missed it. Hate that there was nearly an hour wait in cafeteria and 30 minutes in bistro. So no meatballs or ice cream this trip.

I love everything about IKEA.  Children eat free on Tuesdays.... and honestly, Tuesday nights are not too busy.  

I ran into a bit of a frustrating situation recently.  I was looking for several shelves.  They would show "in stock" online, but when I got to the store, they weren't there.  This happened three times.  It's so frustrating!  They do not *yet* offer the ability to order online and pick up in the store, but as soon as they do, I will bump this up to five stars!
I am very disappointed with Ikea Tampa. I was promised a delivery of a sofa on a specific day. The sofa did not arrive. Very upsetting. Delivery is suspect.

My wife and I visited tonight while in Indianapolis on business From the start, our hostess greeted us with a friendly smile and was very knowledgeable on the store and where things are located. We enjoyed this more than the other store in the Chicago area as it is all one level. Keep up the good work.

Seeing is believing.  Meaning all the great ideas that come from their amazing set ups are inspiring.  The show room lets you walk through this maze of living rooms, bed rooms, bath rooms, kitchens and dining rooms.  It lets you see what could be, and for those visual people, like me, it gives me decorating ideas that I wouldn't have thought of.  

No, they do not have the best quality furniture.  A lot of their stuff is made from particle board, and other inexpensive materials in order to bring the customers the best possible prices.  By going here and testing out the product, you can make the decision for yourself on if their furniture is the best fit for your home.  

The employees were helpful and nice.  Though I didn't need help with anything, I would get asked occasionally if I required assistance.  

Being able to have fun and imagine a new space for my home is what makes this store one of my favorites! :)

Love the return policy. The place just floods my mind with great ideas for my future home.  The breakfast there in the cafe was really cheap. You can't beat 1 dollar plates.  Hard to ask for more but I do wish they had a little more variety when it comes to some of the products.  Cool place!!!

Never never order online with IKEA. I have been waiting over a month for a dresser that I paid for and still haven't received it! You can't get through with the phone number they provide and have to resort to Twitter to get any help. I made arrangements to have it deliver an a Saturday twice now and today is Saturday 2/3/2018 and I still have nothing to show for the money I paid! I strongly suggest you do NOT order from their online platform. They say it's easy to order online and have it delivered to your door. More like it's easy to take your money with no accountability on their end to help you. I feel it's false advertising in my opinion. At this point I would rather they refund all my money and keep the dresser. 

Sincerely,

Extremely disappointed customer

I can't believe I haven't already written a review for Ikea! How is that possible? Ikea is one of my favorite places on Earth. I will admit I'm a modern furniture and modern aesthetic kind of girl. But Ikea is not just for the person who is into modern furniture. They have so many clever, reasonably-priced products: from dinnerware to kitty condos, to mattresses, to rugs, to towels, to kitchen faucets, to food to outdoor furniture, to lighting... the list just goes on and on. I love so many things about Ikea: their clever store design, the fact that they have places for you to back your car into to load your furniture with free twine to help you attach it to your car. I discovered IKEA about 15 years ago. People who know me know that my house is probably 75% furnished with Ikea items. Just makes me smile to walk in the door. I will say their customer service is hit-or-miss, and their furniture can be difficult for some people to put it together, however I find it quite easy if you just follow the directions. But other than that it's fantastic! And I highly recommend the cornbread in their Eatery, it's some of the best you'll ever taste, near-perfect. If you're bringing the kids, talk about kid-friendly, a few things to be aware of is that they have a family parking lot to the left of the front entrance and they have an area called Smallland where they'll take care of your kid for you while you shop, as long as they're potty-trained. If you don't want to leave the kids with strangers then just take them up to the Kds' Department and  let them run around and play for an hour.  They'll have a blast!  They even have little sinks in the bathrooms for the kids!  If you are visiting for the first time, be aware that the store is set up differently than most, with a showroom upstairs where products are displayed to give you great ideas.  Then you head down to the marketplace where everything you saw upstairs in the Showroom is available to put in your cart.  While you are in the Showroom use your phone to take a pic of the red tags on the merchandise you like.  When you go downstairs, you can use those photos to find the items you liked.  Also sign up to be part of the IKEA family, by doing this you will be eligible for special sales throughout the year and for a 90-day return. Also be aware Ikea does not have bags so bring your own or invest $0.59 in one of their giant blue bags which are fantastic for using later for other things.  There is almost too much about Ikea's to tell you it all, some of it you're just going to have to learn yourself through exploration. Have fun!

IKEA is a wonderful place to shop for furniture but I am reviewing it only on basis of food. They serve delicious  and affordable food. If you have IKEA family card, you get coffee free. Swedish meat balls are a must try. Besides that they have fried chicken, salmon, sandwiches with many options for sides. They have plenty of options for drinks and desserts. Overall if you are going to shop for furniture, make sure to have your lunch at ikea.

I'm in the middle of a complete remodel of my new home, so yesterday I went to embark on my next phase....... furnishing the entire upstairs. I have been to other Ikeas in Southern California and Las Vegas and had a brief walk through of this store a few months ago, but this trip would be much more in depth. I had already prepared to get my steps in for the day and had dressed comfortably enough for a good walk and to get my fill of meatballs in the cafe. But shortly after arriving in the bedroom section I met an angel by the name of Devon. I got to sit down and Devon helped me order every piece. Six beds, three dressers, night stands and eight mattresses. All I had to do was give him an idea of the look and feel I was going for. He left me with a sense of accomplishment and my order will be delivered tomorrow with the smallest delivery charge I've ever seen. After picking up some meatballs and apple and pear cider (and accessories of course), all I needed to do was take the print out to the register. I was expecting to have to work and instead I got to totally relax and got it all done in a matter of minutes.

The system for buying a simple cabinet had us waiting in line 3 separate times. Long lines.  It was horrific. 

We usually enjoy a light meal here.  We waited in line for 15 minutes and they were out of half the food. Every single table and chair was filthy.  When we finished the dirty tray shelf was overflowing with no space.  

Terrible. What happened to you, Ikea?
This place is one very long maze that you can easily waste time in looking around.  It's been forever since I had been an IKEA.  Lots of decent showrooms and inexpensive price points...

We came on a Sunday , be prepared overwhelming crowded. I did purchase a few items  but really couldn't look around maneuvering through the people. We tried the cafeteria and had the chicken and Swedish meatball meals which were good and reasonably priced. Plan to come back on a week day morning to really explore all they have to offer. We are happy with what we purchased and love the prices.

I love ikea in general and have been to the respective Chicago And Cincinnati stores. I prefer those stores over this ikea. The thing I can't stand about this ikea is the layout. It forces you to walk through the show room before you can get to the cafeteria, marketplace, or stock area. They say there are cut throughs but that isn't until you get through the showroom. The cut throughs aren't that efficient either when it is busy and there are people confused and crowded. We have often decided not to take advantage of ikea family member deals just because going through the horrible layout is so aggravating. If you are a first time ikea shopper this store will seem great and wonderful but if you are a seasoned pro you will likely just roll your eyes. That being said I find the staff at this ikea to be very nice and possibly more pleasant than the other locations. I also enjoy the grab and go food area better than other locations. I would give this store 5 stars if the layout would be changed.

I first experienced IKEA a little over a year ago, when we traveled all the way to Cincinnati.  Prior to the Fishers store opening, Cincinnati was the closest IKEA store to Indianapolis.  I've been a fan ever since then.

The Good:  IKEA caters to customers who want to maximize their space efficiency, and they also appeal to budget-minded customers.  I've been very impressed with the quality of the products I've bought from IKEA, and there has always been a consistency of experience from one store to another.  Their furniture seems to be decent quality, judging from the night stands and other items we've bought at this location.

The Bad:  The crowd can sometimes be overwhelming, especially on weekends.  I was there recently on a Saturday afternoon, and I felt like a sardine.

The Ugly:  The parking lot.  When it's crowded in the store, parking spaces start to become scarce.  We drove around the parking lot for 20 minutes last month, trying to find and maneuver into a spot.  We resorted to following (stalking) a family as they exited the store, watching them the entire time as they approached their car, and then we pounced on the spot as soon as they were halfway out of the parking space.  

If the store manager is reading this, please do something about the parking situation.  You may not think you need more, but you do.  Trust me.  There's no reason why an otherwise civilized person like me should have to resort to such behavior just to park, and it kind of tics me off that you made me do it.  Normally, I would just bail and cancel the visit to your store, but I had already invested 25 minutes just to get here from Westfield, and I wasn't giving up.

Had my first visit to Ikea yesterday! WOW! I am obsessed with this place now! Everything is so affordable and so stylish! So many different styles there is something for everyone! 

I got a tv stand, and my husband and I put it together in about 45 minutes (with the help of a youtube tutorial!) The instructions that came with it were hard to understand since it was only pictures, but once we looked up a tutorial it was much easier!!

The food court is the bomb, and the food is so cheap!! I got a juicy chicken sandwich and mac and cheese under $6! So affordable!

If you havent been to Ikea yet.. it is a must!
Love the customer service, good food (the chocolate cake is amazing!), and a vast variety of furnishings.

Have you ever thought to yourself, "If only I could find a giant maze, where everything is written in Swedish, where I can stop and eat horse meatballs for lunch, push around a cart that goes in the opposite of whatever direction I push it, and also buy a dresser that is capable of killing small children?" Well, my friends, look no further than IKEA. Here, you will find a conglomerate of Capitalistic whoredom disguised as Scandinavian "hygglig" in the form of overpriced furniture that you have to put together yourself. You will look at the professionally-designed showroom and think, "my living room will look just like that!" But then you will go home, look around at your LACK tables and hard-as-a-rock sofa designed for people who despise comfort, and wonder how it is that you spent $1000 furnishing your apartment with this godforsaken cheap crap. What a waste of a college financial aid disbursement, you will think. And then, someday, as if waking up from a deep sleep, you will break through the particleboard walls of your awareness with the epiphany that IKEA is a portal to Hell.

Lately they have been only keeping 2 - 3 registers open with each line about 15 carts deep. WTF? After shopping for an hour, then looking again at lines that would take 45 minutes to pay, I left my full carts on the warehouse floor and walked out empty handed. I will not be going back for a while.

My husband and I just had a house built in Lakewood Ranch.  We had a wonderful experience purchasing a gel king size mattress and all the trimmings.  We were so lucky to have Emily helping us.  Clearly, she is  extremely knowledgeable, professional, personable and loves working with customers.  She measured and explained the differences between the mattresses, etc. so that we could purchase exactly what we needed.  She made the whole process fun and she could not have been more informative.  We left knowing that we had made an excellent purchase.  Also, we will be having everything delivered two days later!!!  What excellent customer service and we owe it all to Emily's expertise.  Thanks again!

This place is like an adult play place! If you're looking for cheap semi-reliable furniture and decor this is your place. Also, before you check out new stuff pop into the "as is" room with discounted stuff. 

If you have kids it's also fun to walk around or drop them off in childcare. Once you're done shopping you can grab some dinner in the Cafe area and relax. 

If you're in for a quick vist or a long one make sure you grab some ice cream or a cinnabun.

We decided to go to IKEA on a Sunday. I know, I know, what we're we thinking? Wouldn't it be crazy busy? Well, we arrived just after it opened and while it was busy, it did not feel crowded. 

We parked near the exit and then walked over to the entrance. This is all a mind game because essentially we are walking the same distance either way, but on the way out we will, in theory, be pushing a cart with our purchases, so we saved energy. Or at least this is what we tell ourselves. Told ya it was all a mind game. 

We knew we were going to be making a Farley large purchase today as we needed a dining room table and Uncle Sam gave us our tax return. Let's be honest, we aren't the only ones spending more this time of year. :-)

We did this trip with our three year old and IKEA has a great kid area that was CLOSED TODAY, whomp, whomp, whomp. They were removing all the ball pit balls, not sure what that means for the future of the kids area. 

It wasn't an easy trip, but he did pretty good helping us out. The hardest part about IKEA is it is basically a rat maze. Normally, I am okay with it, but with a toddler that needs to go potty every few minutes, it was not fun. There are short cuts and things, but toddlers are not known for their patience. 

We managed to find a dining table, chairs, a curio, and two night stands. For under the price of just a table at a typical furniture store. We were bummed they only had this table in black as a brown color would have been better, but we will live. 

When we checked out, we were able to save money from our lunch. Basically if you go eat at the restaurant before shopping, you "save" that same amount from a purchase over $100. Essentially, you get your meal for free!!! I am all about the free stuff! 

We had Swedish meatballs meal, chicken meatballs meal, and chicken tender kid meal. They were all delicious! 

Pro Tip: if you have a kid and need a bib, plastic utensils (smaller than their metal ones), a bottle warmer, microwave, or toaster, they have them all in their food court area upstairs! I have never seen this at any other food establishment and love it. 

I was sad to see the kid friendly food area was no longer in the food court area. There used to be kids tables and a tv in a section where parents could sit at an adult table. 

If you made it this far, kudos to you. I know that was a lot of random facts. 

Here is another one, check out the "AS IS" area to the far right just before the check out area. There are many hidden diamonds in the rough there. Floor models for sale, or anything returned. I have found some great things there throughout the years. 

One last tip! If you ever lose a screw, lose a dowel, need instructions, or a part gets damaged, you can get it from the parts area which is also at the guest services area. I have gotten these items sometimes free or for a very low cost. It is just past the cashier area on the right or to the left of coming in the exit. 

Happy shopping! Ikea is truly an experience!

What a disaster!!  Order online and wanted the furniture shipped to Sarasota.  First they told me to expect delivery in less than a week.  Then they sent me an email saying to expect delivery in 11 days.  No word or update.  Spent 40 minutes calling customer service only to be told that now delivery would be another 7 days.  This time I got a confirmation but on day 6 no word from the delivery company.  Another 40 minutes on the phone and was told that the furniture left Georgia but they did not know where it was or when it would be delivered.  Although on an Ikea truck they said they had no way of determining any status update and I would have to be "patient".  This is the worse service experience imaginable.  AND...  they don't care.

Edit--they fixed the moderate headache (read 4 hours of our time) so kudos to them and back up to 4 stars. 

----

I have spent over $15k in IKEA over the last 6 years furnishing 4 separate homes.

My experience with IKEA Cincinnati West Chester Cincinnati is the following:

We ordered furniture to have it delivered to our home. Upon arrival the delivery team notified us that they could not assemble the furniture due to the old plaster walls of our house. We were not informed in the store that this would be an issue even though they happily accepted our payment at the store for the assembly. We were forced to refuse an item of furniture because of the inability to have it assembled. We were reassured biting delivery crew that both the non-assembly and the one item we reused will be promptly refunded. We called the customer service line and were informed that within a week we receive a phone call to document the refund and resolution of this issue. 2months have elapsed and no phone call was received. When we called back, and were left on hold for an hour, the new customer service representative informed us that she will be unable to help us and that we would have to go to the store to have this issue resolved and have our money refunded. Therefore we are over 1 1/2 months from the purchase of our items and have yet to be refunded over $400 in assembly And non-received furniture.

I spent most of my time waiting to be checked out --this was during weekday--they only had three registers opened. Also, when returning they asked to see my ID and entered in their system ALL my private information including my address just to return an item?  Not sure I like all the trouble.

IKEA is a great place to find a great deal and quite an experience just to walk through. Also - before I became vegetarian I LOVED the meatballs and gravy...now I love the Veggie balls...very flavorful for a quick little lunch or dinner while shopping.

I just hate the layout. It's ikea so it's an awesome store and the prices are great, but I feel like you shouldn't have to walk through the cafe to get to the marketplace. It's really crowded and a hassle for the diners. They should separate it with a door or something.

Having redone a room in our house, we have been here twice recently.

The store is still in-stock on most items, which I appreciate. Crowds are down on week days but weekends still uber busy.

Please IKEA--get more people at check outs. There is no self-serve here at Indy! WTF! Lots of people with just a couple of items are stuck in line with those buying room loads. Even on weekdays the lines are brutal.
Don't use their picking service. Made multiple mistakes on one order. Returns/exchanges took +45 minutes. Plus over an hour on phone.

IKEA is a nice looking fun retail establishment. Very nice sales floor associates and customer service associates. My experience for receiving, by delivery, damaged shelving was not so nice. Especially when we had set time aside on the weekend to install the shelving. Spent additional time being on hold to have damaged merchandised picked up which cost an additional 70 minutes on the phone. Again, very nice customer service associates but clearly no decision making or influence with the IKEA decision makers for making right the inconvenience of the whole IKEA transactional experience. My experience with Amazon has been the exact opposite of IKEA. Amazon in my experience appreciates the customer service experience and made right one of my complaints concerning an item that I received from them in the past. IKEA has not learned customer care in a way that respects customer time and inconvenience. I will stick with Amazon going forward. Sad face.
Another "gun free zone" that thinks guns jump out and hurt people. Not a fan of the store in general and I've been a couple times.

My first trip to Ikea in South Philly is my last. I knew this store wasn't located in the best part of Philadelphia but thought there was safety in the large number of customers shopping there. Not so. I never made it into the store. Although parked near the entrance, the moment I stepped out of my car, at least two (there may have been a third) pre-teen/teenage boys began harassing me. One kid deliberately ran up and bumped into me. Then another kid who looked around 16 years old (I soon figured he was the ring leader), started verbally harassing me, name calling, etc. Since I did not feel safe leaving my car while I shopped, I immediately got back in to leave. As I pulled out, one of them threw something that hit my car. It didn't appear to cause damage. No matter, I kept on going. Based on this experience, I do NOT recommend Ikea in South Philly to any woman shopping alone, or to anyone who may be vulnerable to this kind of harassment.

It's surprising to go to an Ikea and it not be 2 stories. It's a bit out of the way from everything  but there's enough parking and the crowds aren't too bad. The layout is a little confusing to maneuver through the shortcuts, ended up going in through the exit to get to where I wanted. Didn't realize you can get a discount in the restaurant with the family club card, I'll be sure to use it next time. The food at the restaurant was good but the drinks could be improved, flavors were a little bland.

This place sucks!!! You would think with how big of a company they are they would actually have their shit together. If you can't make next day delivery don't advertise for it! Also waited on hold for 4 hours within 2 days and still don't have my furniture. They gave me 8-6 time frame and no driver ever called to give 30 min warning like they said they would. Showed up at 7 and I didn't have time for assembly like planned so they just left. They then wanted to charge me a redelivery fee since they showed up even though they were an hour late. I've dealt with 3 other furniture companies and had no problems at all like this place has given me. I really would like to get a refund but can't even get anyone on the phone while my furniture is floating around somewhere. So glad I did not buy my bed here and will probably never shop Ikea again!!!! Most everything is cheap crap made from china anyways. Dollar store quality products and even worse customer service!!! If you like wasting your time and money check out Ikea today. I would give zero stars if had the option!!!

I love Ikea , I buy many things at AVON  MA Ikea and I think their goods are great for the price. last year I got my kitchen there and service ,delivery and outcome are great. This year at the TAMPA Ikea my experience has been horrible!!! I bought a sink base and sink for my bathroom online I got an e-mail that it would be delivered March 3rd,( three days latter) On mach 2nd I got a call from 1888-888-4532. When I called back an auto response told me that my sink would be delivered March 4th, between the hours of 4-8 pm. I thought that it was strange that they deliver on Sunday but I shrugged my shoulders and went to the beach. while I was there(on the 3rd) I got a call from a delivery guy saying that he is half hour away.I told him that I had called that morning and was told that delivery is for March 4th next day but that I could make it back to the apt in 1 hour, or he could deliver on the next day.His English and communication skills were bad after he put me on hold to confer with his boss he said you want today or tomorrow? I restated what I told him ,he answered tomorrow, next day I called the 888 #, 3 times waited over half hour each time, no one answered. Got an email that it was delivered on the 3rd then got another e-mail with another tel #
1-877-686-6998 got through fairly easy the lady was very nice she even removed the delivery charge, but she could not rechedule till  7th I asked for the 8th.On the 8th I called again because I had not gotten a call or e-mail for delivery .I was told that It won't be delivered because they have sent the e-mail for delivery at the wrong delivery Co . So I hope it will be delivered tomorrow 9th. I am so disappointed at their delivery practices
In Tampa so even though I love Ikea this might break our relationship forever if they don't come through this time .I have had to cancel with the plumber 3 times
It's a smaller story with only one floor but has everything! I love the use of wallpaper in the show rooms.

This store is still amazing. We went back with our friends and since we went early we decided to have breakfast. The pancakes were great and the price was very reasonable and the coffee is free with our card.

Please spare yourself the agony and don't buy anything from here that involves Delivery. We bought/paid for our furniture 10 days back and they set us up for delivery the next day. They were supposed to come between 5-9 pm. I cleared my schedule and waited. At 9 p clock I called ikea and after 1 hour 30 minutes of hold time my call was returned to the main operator. Apparently the person who took the call first put me on hold and left for the day. I requested to ask for the manager and he promised he will email me the details on what happened, which he never did. I call again the next day and after only 30 minutes of hold I was told the delivery company, a 3rd party ikea uses, dont even have any record of our purchase or delivery. Spending another 2 hours on the phone over 3 calls we got it rescheduled and was given a date a week later. We were called again and an automated message was given for a date and time a lot. I am not available at that time and been trying to tell them that and it's been 1 hour 45 minutes on the call trying to get it rescheduled. I am probably going to cancel the order but that means another hold time of God knows how many hours. It has been a terrible experience and would strongly advise to arrange own delivery

Finally, Indy has been graced with the gift of IKEA - everyone's favorite place for food, fun, and furniture all in one place.

I mean seriously, what's not to like? Sure, it's often full of people and that can make parking a little difficult. But that just lets you know that IKEA is the place you want to be.

The furniture is affordable and easy to put together. The home goods section have pretty much everything you can think of, especially if you're a kitchen product fanatic like me. It's even harder to say no to impulse buys with the price tags here. 

Every store should have a restaurant in the middle. After walking through such a maze of a store, you definitely work up an appetite. I'd grab a bite at IKEA even if I wasn't already there. The meatballs aren't just hype- they really are as good as people say. And the lingonberries? I could just eat a bowl. I love the chocolate cake. It's almost unbearably rich and enough to satisfy your sweet tooth for days.

Every trip to IKEA is it's own adventure. Go out and join the fun!

I was really nervous & excited about getting an Ikea in Fishers. I was nervous that it would bring a crazy amount of traffic into Fishers. But I was excited to have an Ikea and also excited to see what else would come to Fishers because of the Ikea! 

Hoenstly, traffic hasn't been as bad as I expected. I avoided it for the first several months of opening to let the hype die down. It doesn't seem to have caused too much extra traffic. 

Ikea should DEFINITELY be avoided on the weekends. It's just so ridiculous in there. So hard to get around, no shopping carts available, people just stop in the middle of the walk way, etc. But if you can manage to go during a week day especially in the morning. ahhhhhhhh. I love Ikea. Some people really hate the show room aspect but I love it. It gives me so many ideas I had never thought about. I will say the maze through the showroom can be a little frustrating if you just have to get something specific. 

During my most recent stop I purchased some grey pull down blinds for my guest bedroom. I'm completely obsessed! These are perfect! And the best part is there are no strings to pull on the blinds. But this is an Ikea review, not a product review haha. 

The staff seems very willing to help. Although, again, beware - if you go during busy hours you won't be able to find someone available to help you. 

make sure to bring your own bags. I always forget and end up spending $1 on a huge bag. 

I'm really excited about this addition to Fishers. I'm even more excited for all the restaurants it will draw to the Fishers area. I'm tired of driving downtown for good food! Get it together Fishers!
Unlike most IKEAs this is only one story. Makes for a very long walk as there is no good way to get to the marketplace area.

IKEA is great..but you know what's better? The free coffee by signing up for their rewards! IKEA is like going to a mall for me..just walk around for hours and hours and look at everything and buy something I don't need.

I've had the opportunity to go to several IKEA locations in California, so when I heard that an IKEA would be opening up here in the Indianapolis area, I was preparing myself for the constant search for a parking spot, rude people trying to get the same item as me, and enormous waiting in line to finally pay for my purchases.  Boy, was I wrong!!!

I've been to the IKEA Fishers several times since it opened and so far all of my experiences have been AMAZING.  The store is conveniently located off the freeway, and it's very easy to get to this location.

When IKEA Fishers first opened, I thought that it was a sure thing that I would be spending 15 minutes, at the very least, looking for a parking spot. That has yet to happen, considering every time that I have gone there has been more than enough parking.  

The staff has been courteous and helpful each time that I have been here, and the inventory count through the IKEA app is very convenient.  

The cafeteria is inexpensive and the food tastes great.  If you are a member of the IKEA Family program you can take advantage of several coupons and even freebies.

When compared to the locations I have been to in California, the lines here move quickly, including on weekends. The cash register staff is very accommodating, even when I have to split payment options between my wife and I.  They are knowledgeable, considering that they have not had a long time with their products and services.

When we first moved to Indiana this past July I was really sad to find out there was no Ikea! I was really happy when I found out one was in the works and I didnt have to wait long for one  

With that being said, I love Ikea. Whats better? I love Ikea in Indiana. Why, you ask? There is plenty of parking and the crowds are not too bad. Especially during the week. Compared to Ikea in my home state of California, Ikea in Indiana is a walk in the park. Trust me. 

This 1-story location is very clean and there is tons to look at. From couches, to desks, to beds, etc, etc. and all very affordable. The display rooms and kitchens are very well decorated and give tons of inspiration for decorating and furnishing your home. We can seriously spend a couple of hours here and leave with some decently priced furniture and a full tummy! 

With that being said, An Ikea trip is not an Ikea trip if you do not try their food! I loooove Ikea food!  ESPECIALLY their meatballs! So delicious and affordable! We always make it a point to stop and get lunch or dinner when we visit. We also make sure to purchase a pack of cinnamon rolls to take home. They are delish! Try them. You will not be sorry

This is a really cool place for furniture and its actually affordable while being quality, sturdy furniture. I love how the "model rooms" are all different and it tells you what the entire room of furniture and such will cost as well as each item being labeled.
Horrible pickup service  Have been waiting for 45 min to pick up one item.   Will not be back.

Sometimes you have to give a one-star review just to get someone's attention to get a bad company policy reviewed and changed.

I purchased close to 2k of products over the past month to furnish my new place.  On my last trip, I purchased a fintorp paper towel holder. It did not come with all the pieces! Literally just the base was inside. 

I called customer service because it's ridiculous to go back to the store for one $10 piece that THEY messed up.  After a ridiculous wait, I asked them to send me a replacement.

Ikea doesn't DO that they said.  The online dept. only deals with ONLINE purchases.  I know they send things through the mail all the time. What kind of awful company policy is this?  I would have to be on wait for another hour just to speak with her supervisor.

Here's the kicker. She put me on a long hold to call the store to check if they could send it to me.  Then she told me that they could send it to me if I paid shipping- fine how much does it cost? "well sir, we don't take payment information on the phone- you'd have to go into the store so that they can mail it to you."  WOW.  What a horrible customer service experience.

IKEA makes furnishing a home the easiest thing to do! 

I recently purchased my first home and if that were not stressful enough, now I have to decorate and furnish it. Every store I walk into makes me feel like i need to spend my life's savings in order to decorate my home. Enter: IKEA! This store is your one stop shop for home needs with prices that won't send you home with buyers remorse. 

The store sells literally anything you could ever need (or want). From furniture, to lighting, to utensils to live plants you can rest assured that IKEA will have what you are looking for. 

When you first enter the store, you'll wander through a series of show rooms. These rooms have different items in them (fully decorated bedrooms, patio set up, etc) and everything you see in the rooms is for sale! So, if you like what you see (and you will) be sure to make note of where to find it in the store (the item tags are marked with where you can find the items). 

Wandering through the 26 different sections might make you hungry and you'll be wondering where the delicious scents and aromas of Swedish food are coming from. Not to worry- halfway through your journey you'll walk into the food court! And yes, you MUST try the Swedish meatballs. They are the talk of the store. 

Post snack/meal break you will continue your way through the second half of the store. You might find yourself hungry again after check out and you're in luck! There is a snack bar right before the exit offering sweet and savory items! 

PS: don't forget to bring your IKEA bag for all of your items purchased. But, if you forget, you can always purchase them at the register.

IKEA is great..but you know what's better? The free coffee by signing up for their rewards! IKEA is like going to a mall for me..just walk around for hours and hours and look at everything and buy something I dont

So excited Fishers finally got an Ikea. My husband and I loved Ikea when we lived in Maryland and the Fishers location does not disappoint. The cafe is delicious and even has healthy and inexpensive options for the kiddos! We haven't had a chance to use the smaland child area yet because it's very popular and full when we go but the kids think it looks fantastic. (Kids must be potty trained and between 36"-54" tall) It can be confusing to get around if you're looking for something specific, or you can just browse for hours. Luckily there are maps, including directions to cut through sections, and everyone we've interacted with has been so helpful and nice. If you don't like crowds I would definitely explore on a weekday or weeknight as opposed to the weekend.

I'm a big fan of scavenger hunts, so I'm always game for the challenge. I would have never thought a furniture store would be a fun place to have one though. The atmosphere here is awesome and surprisingly the prices are very reasonable. This was a great excuse to bring people out to IKEA!

A co-worker and I did the Ikea scavenger hunt and it was soooo fun!!!! Who knew wandering through furniture would be so fun! I had never been to ikea but I feel like I learned a lot from the scavenger about how to shop at ikea for the best deals! Employee love the fun too! They are so nice and I can't tell you how many times I said I'm lost and they directed to me the right area. Also I'm pretty sure I just found my entire wedding table center pieces at IKEA and they are only $3.99 a piece!!!! Any brides out there definitely check out their decor. Also consider doing a registry with them they have literally everything you can think of. I'm kinda mad IKEA wasn't open when I did my registry, I'm actually thinking about doing a last minute one of things I forgot my other registries. Plus they deliver which is awesome for guest out of state who can't fly or travel with a large wedding gift. 
Definitely make a whole day out of and take the time to look at everything because you will miss deals that you can't pass up! If you do take a whole day for IKEA and need a snack the food is amazing! I got the chicken cordon blue dinner with meatballs. Best thing was it was only $4!!!!!! Also before you go, sign up online for the family membership. You get free coffee and tea, free wifi, and discounts on certain items. Another perk is it is free to sign up and they send you a $15 gift card on your birthday!!

All the hype about this place is completely true!!! I can't wait to go again and I just left. So many amazing things for your house! Every single room in your house is covered at this store!! So many ideas for ways to decorate, organize and furnish your home. 
   The food is also a must do when you are here! Such good prices on amazing food. The meatball are definitely worth all rage people make them out to be! 
I will definitely will be returning very soon! I can't wait to redecorate my house!

I have been to Ikea stores all over the country, but the fishers one takes the cake! First off, the moving information screens are so future like I feel like I'm in an episode of the Jetsons. Second, there is a mini food store plus a mini cafe right at the entrance of the store. I have never ever seen an IKEA mini food store before! I love the layout of the mini fully furnished rooms first and then fully furnished homes throughout the store. Everyone who works at the store is so happy to be there and extremely knowledgeable. I specifically went to check out the IKEA store with the yelp group and had a great time! At this event, I learned so much about IKEA, for example, they use cardboard for the palate material. This gives them the opportunity to recycle. IKEA has a wonderful children's play area that's supervised so the parents can shop. The different colored tags on the furniture have different meanings when it comes to the availability of the item. There are shortcuts so you don't have to go through certain sections if you don't want to. IKEA in fishers is an EXPERIENCE to say the least! So excited to visit again!

I know on my next move or remodel, I will be taking a trip to IKEA! At first the store can be a tad intimidating but once you start on your adventure you forget your worries. The real bonus is their model display rooms. This was a great way for them to feature their items and show you what you could do with the items in your own home. 

The kitchen/ restaurant half way through the building is genius! Because everyone gets hungry during all the shopping and walking! ( and no one is fun to shop with when they are hangry) Don't pass up their famous meatballs! Their meals are incredibly reasonable price which makes you able to spend more on the furniture/ decor ;) 

The staff is extremely welcoming and helpful when you have questions on an item or navigating the store! Can't wait to go back!
I might have bought *15* of these Kafferep when they were on sale in early Feb. Happy Valentine's day to me! They're crispier than a Pepperidge Farm Verona, and just as quick to finish!

Used to love shopping here. Today, bought a new duvet cover. I wanted something white on white, and very basic. Found the most gorgeous design online, and went in today to get it. 

Impossible to tell from the packaging, but it is not white. It's IVORY. It looks dingy next to the white sheets and accessories I've used to accent the blue in the room. 

No problem. I mentioned it to my husband, who had helpfully offered to carry the package for me (I had just left a pain management clinic, so was having problems with heavy items). Unfortunately, somewhere between the store and home, the receipt got lost. When we called, because we have no receipt and the package had been opened (I couldn't tell inside the packaging how it would look, and hadn't known he'd lost the receipt), we can't even do an exchange. I am now out $70, and still don't have the white duvet I went in for. Husband is in the doghouse, and I'm furious. If I need cheap crap, I'll go somewhere else from now on.

IKEA is the place you go if you need to decorate the house! You can buy everything you need here! You'll find stuff that you didn't even know existed here! I could easily spend my whole day here looking at all the stuff! The place is set up like a maze. Follow the arrows through the show rooms to see the endless possibilities. The checkout process is very simple. If you see an item that you like, scan the barcode with your ikea app or take a picture of the barcode and have the employee scan it at the end. The prices are reasonable for the quality of the items. This store allows you to build your dream home from scratch. Choose your color and finishing to personalize your home! The maze takes you right through their food court and bistro! The merchandise are all very chic and stylish! There is even a garden section if you want to freshen up your space! Everything is very clean and organized making the process very simple and convenient!

Puzzled why IKEA feels it necessary to hold customers captive by making it so confusing to exit the store without considerable frustration and confusion. The self assembly of featured furnishings is also made made more challenging by using hardware unfamiliar to most North Americans. If you're looking to make a quick purchase this is not the place to go. The cafeteria offers some good choices at economical prices. Lots of parking but at times it's still hard to find a spot.

Great Swedish meatballs and always worth swinging in to get some fancy watering pots at the same time. I think their cafeteria is often underrated , but the values you get and the quality make it almost irresistible. 
But then again, maybe it is just because I'm exhausted from walking around the whole store. 
My recommendation, grab the salmon fillet when they have it. And a pack of meatballs to go.

Although the store personnel are knowledgeable and helpful, the delivery process is absolutely god-awful. I purchased a bed base with storage, arrange my schedule to be here for its delivery, paid for the delivery plus tips, and received the bed slats only. I got two different estimated delivery dates, and now it appears it will be almost 2 weeks until the bed is here. It's unfortunate to have such terrible service when the store personnel are so good. To be honest, I will probably never purchase anything from IKEA again. The hassle is truly not worth it. I spent two hours today on hold, not counting the horn 1/2 I spent trying to find a phone number for  IKEA. Definitely not worth it.

Worst customer service ever! Ordered a chair online they charged me immediately and 8 days later nothing, no email nothing. Terrible website and try calling, over two hours on hold only to find out that they can't tell me when it will ship. Requested a refund and they transfer me to "supervisor" for another interminably long hold! Never again will I shop IKEA !

Great week at IKEA. They had a spring break series of events this week for kids out of school. Each day a different craft was featured. Today they did glass frame painting. You paint on plastic glass and can slide the painting in the frame they give you. My grandson loved it. The staff working these events were super friendly. The events were free. 
           I enjoyed my pre craft lunch today. The salmon was perfectly cooked and the dill sauce was very tasty. The vegetables were fresh and not over cooked. The potato pancake was also tasty but on the cool side my grandson always enjoys his kid portion of chicken tenders and fries which he almost always cleans the plate. The portion is a good size and the price is right. 
        After crafts and lunch we enjoyed the $1 soft serve cones and the free samples of hazelnut chocolate.

Always nice and clean with friendly staff in my experience. For some reason this location has a problem where people go against the arrows when browsing the store, making it difficult to get around on busier days. The food is excellent, as always.

I am happy that IKEA finally opened in Indianapolis metro area. It's a fun place to go for getting your simple bookshelves, having Swedish meatballs and desserts or just strolling around for your lazy Sunday evening. I love their "showrooms"'as they offer you plenty of ideas how to decorate your room . Though the quality is not heirloom quality, there are always something you can find here that are useful and or functional for your home. This IKEA location has only 1 level to explore, but it is still pretty big and has ample parking. Be prepared with your drill and spend hours of building your dresser. Fun fun fun ..

This store is HUGE. It's interesting to look at their showroom to see how to furnish small spaces. Everything u can think of for your home. Pretty decent prices. I still haven't tried the restaurant yet. That is a future goal.

Ikea is always fun to walk through, although they do structure it in such a way that you can really only go one way. It's pretty clever how they lay out their stores to make you see all the cool stuff they have in their rightful settings.

The food court serves good food, and it's very affordable! Being such a big store, they could take the opportunity to charge a lot for food, but they don't do that. There are also good discounts for being Ikea Family Members!

We didn't walk in intending to buy anything, but we walked out with some stuff!

Some say "fancy Walmart" other says it is a great place to find furnitures you will not find in other stores. Quality is not the best and most of time your furniture will last 2-3 years but if price is very affordable, so if you looking for quality I will look somewhere else but if price is what you care about I will definitely give IKEA a chance. Home appliances are good and most of the time price is very competitive with other stores. Give it a chance and see what you think...

Very disappointed with there shipping. I spent $6000 on a new kitchen and they stated it would be delivered today. I took the day off of work for delivery and now they stated somebody should have contacted me telling me there was a back order. Never again will I have something shipped from IKEA.

I'm a big Ikea fan, and this location gets extra points for a pretty solid "As-Is" section (discounted products that were either floor models or returned by other customers. 

The showroom is pretty standard, and can be inspiring if you're wondering what to do with a small space.  The real fun is downstairs, where you can find all sorts of things you didn't know you needed, like a $20 wok or $3.50 silicone oven mitts. 

We often come for one or two specific things, and typically leave with a cartful, which I suppose is good or bad depending on your view ;)

Pro-tip: Park in the garage in the back. It's always way less crowded than the front lot!

OH BOY!!! Not a whole lot to write about here. It's IKEA. This is a single level store, which is different from the West Chester and Frisco locations I am used too. So, to me, it seems smaller, but I think it's about the same. Now, the cafe is absolutely smaller than the other two locations I mentioned. The food in the cafe is awesome, but there is also a Portillos nearby, so...
Anyways, starts off with the showroom then transitions into the warehouse. Everything is typical IKEA. Anyone who has been will get it. Just buy all the things! 
We also found out that the return process is pretty easy and painless.

I would call ahead prior to any "clock and collect" order. My order was supposed to be ready at 5:00pm, I showed up at 6:30pm and they couldn't find my order, etc, etc, and didn't receive my order until around 7pm. If you're going to charge me a $5.00 "picking fee" please make sure it's on time. I'm thoroughly displeased.

The worst customer service. I was on the phone for two hours of which 1:55 minutes , I was on hold waiting for a supervisor who never came.
I would never buy from them again.

I am extremely disappointed. After waiting for my dresser to come in for over a week, I begin to put it together and soon realize there are missing pieces. I only had two drawers with my FOUR DRAWER DRESSER. After waiting on hold for over an entire hour, a rude woman answers. She then begins to sarcastically question me as if i'm stupid, asking if i have even looked in the box. I told her yes and that I would like the two extra drawers. She then goes on to tell me I will have to wait a whole another week to get the rest of the parts. Ridiculous !!!! I WILL NEVER BUY AGAIN. Hopefully you all have better customer service in store. I spent $200 of my hard earned money to be treated like I am unimportant, and now I am expected to wait another week while I have no where to store my clothes. I will be returning and buying elsewhere.

Lots of people come to Ikea for the furniture but I usually come for the food. Their dining area is clean, comfortable and has big window walls making the whole area very bright. You get the food like how you would at a school cafeteria, wait in line, get a tray and order your food to the servers. Afterwards you would go up to the cashier to pay. * if you have a Ikea family card you get free coffee or tea!! It's really easy to sign up for one, they have machines around for you to sign up. 

Their breakfast is affordable ($2 for a plate of eggs, sausage, potatoes and Swedish pancake). The breakfast food isn't the best quality tho, it's like the breakfast you would have at regular hotels. Still good but eggs aren't fresh eggs and the sausage is kinda dry, however for $2 it's pretty worth the money. 

Their lunch is a whole different story, the food is fresh and delicious. The price again is affordable ( have the menu attached so check it out if you're interested!) There are many different options but you can't go wrong with their famous Swedish meatballs (beef and pork). It's $5.99 and comes with mashed potatoes, veggies, gravy and their delicious lingnoberry sauce. You can also buy their meatballs home too! They have chicken meatballs (personal fav), veggies and the ones they serve at the dining area- Swedish meatballs.
Not much to say about IKEA.  It's IKEA. I do think it is weird that you can't get to the grocery type items with out paying first. Then you have to get in line again.

Great place for so many home things - really they have sooooo much here. It's not just furniture. Plan to spend at least an hour just browsing. I like coming here for inspiration, the styles, layouts, room decor and designs - it's neat to see it all.

You gotta stop and visit the "as-is"room on the lower level to find some good deals on items. And grab a $1 ice cream cone while you're at it!

If you come during the week, during the day it's usually calm and not crowded. Weekends can get very busy.

They have a huge cafeteria with great prices on lunch and breakfast. And pretty yummy. 

There's no reason not to become a free ikea family member - it gives you discounts on merch and food. And you can always grab a free coffee or tea any-day anytime.

The fav part for our kids is getting dropped off in their free supervised kids play area called Smaland. It's on the first floor when you come in the main entrance. Gives us an hour and half to walk around and sit in the caf without kids :) (extra time if you are an ikea family member)

I love this IKEA. It's even better than the one I went to in Sweden (my Swedish fiancé agrees, and yes, I make him read me all the name tags on the furniture and tell me what they mean). It's always clean and well-organized, and the staff are super friendly.

In the cafeteria, there are at least three staff cleaning and bussing tables during peak lunch hours. No table is dirty for long. The cashiers in the cafe are also really nice. They remind you to grab water glasses, instruct you where to find utensils and salad dressing, and even reminded us to grab an extra knackebröd from the buffet, because they were 2-for-$.34. 

The checkout lines get really long, unfortunately, but you'll find yourself waiting for less time than at Walmart. And you get to smell the amazing aroma of the cinnamon buns while you wait. Ahhhhhh... (they smell better than they taste though.)

I've had to visit customer service twice, but the wait is never that long. The staff there are helpful and try to keep the line moving along.

Make sure you stop by the clearance section before the registers! I've found some great deals there.

Also, make sure you get the IKEA Family card! It's free and gets you amazing deals! I just recently got a $20 coupon, and it was much appreciated, since I had a big purchase to make anyway!

They also have days when you can get your entire family's meals for absolutely free in the cafe if you make a $100 home furnishing purchase. My fiancé and I had to get a new dresser and happened to visit the weekend of this amazing deal. We had a huuuuuge lunch for $21 ($23 before the normal IKEA family discount) and then were reimbursed at customer service. ($23 is a LOT of food at the IKEA cafe, where everything is silly cheap.) We did this process backwards. You're supposed to eat, then shop and get reimbursed at checkout. Whoops. If you mess up like us, just head to customer service!

Overall, I love this IKEA, and although it's about 45 minutes from where I live, I don't mind, since it's a well-maintained store that provides an excellent experience every time.
The staff is always welcoming. We've used smaland a few times for my 4 year old son, and he loves it. I love to eat here ( swedish meatballs)  and browse the clearance section!

I have mixed feelings about this place but my wife and I are trying to make a commitment to never go back. I think the products are great if you don't mind the agony of putting them together. However, the customer interface (at least at this location) is a joke. When my family and I went in last week, all we wanted to do was to order the cabinets and counter tops  we had already picked out (and recorded in their system) on a previous visit. Once we get to the kitchen section, they told us we needed to get our IKEA family card before we could complete the order. I asked, "You have a computer right there, can't you pull it up? We have shopped here before." No, you have to find your way through the maze in order to find a kiosk that will spit out your card. The instructions the employees give on how to find your way around are just laughable. Just take a right, and then a left through the secret doorway, go through the warp portal and the kiosk is below the catwalk. Ok, seriously I could not find the secret doors and had to go through half of the maze that is IKEA to get where I thought it should be. Couldn't find it, went to the cash registers which are like a half mile away and an employee told me that she could not pull up an IKEA family membership and I had to go to the Kiosk. Almost all of the employees I have interacted with at this store have the same level of disregard for actually helping the customers there. It's almost like IKEA told them 'listen, don't worry about doing a good job because the product IKEA makes is so good that people will buy it from you even if you treat them like dog poop'. Anyway, I found the kiosk, finally figured out how to login after I reset my password, walked back to the kitchen section (this time I managed to hit all the secret doors and got there in like 5 seconds), we got the order put in, paid for it, and then walked the 5k to the pickup area, stopping halfway through that journey to grab a bite. Once we got to the pickup area and waited about 20 minutes for our number to be called, we found out that not everything was in stock, so the employees told us we would need to "return" the items that we had paid for and were not in stock, so then we had to wait in line for the returns. By this time our toddler was melting all over the floor and people were all staring at us like "yeah, that's how we all feel". I cannot explain why we needed to return the items that they did not have in stock only to pay for them a again a couple days later. I can't explain why we were switched between cashiers three times before we could get the unnecessary return done. All told, we were there for over three hours for what should have been just us going in, ordering what we already picked out, and leaving with it.
 
But wait! We had to go back to the store two other times! Once because one of the cabinet doors was completely scratched up inside the packaging, and then once because they did not give us all of the materials we needed to install our cabinets, even though it was a very simple order that was well communicated to the kitchen department lady.  So the total time for this one order ended up being around 6 hours, not including driving time. ALSO, they didn't have the part I needed when I went back, so I am going to have to go to home depot and figure something out.
 
This store fails based on the fact that (1) the people who are in the departments selling stuff have never done an installation of anything in their lives and are not properly trained on what is required, (2) things that should be simple like pulling up your customer info is unnecessarily complicated by the fact that you have to carry around a big dorky orange card or have to navigate the maze of the store to find the one kiosk to print one out, (3) none of the different departments within the store know the capabilities of the other departments; the guy at item pickup said "just go to the returns guys and they will pull up the schematics for your order and figure out what you need". I moved to the returns line and 30 minutes later when my number gets called the guy might have well just said "duuuuuuuuuuuuuhhhhhhh" when I told him what I was looking for, (4) on a related note I am constantly underwhelmed with the effort level of the staff (I was in customer service for a long time and therefor have a bias on this).
 
My family and I (sort of) love the products but we will be making a concerted effort not to go back to this store.
Just like every other Ikea, has everything you need and everything you don't need as my husband would say.. if you want to avoid crowds and out of town travelers, go during the week..
It's fun to go here sometimes to get ideas when remodeling, but the quality of the products aren't great. Also, if you go on the weekends it is very crowded and hard to get through the crowds.

Last Saturday April 7th, 2018, I went to IKEA in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania and purchased two items including delivery and assembly. I was assured delivery would occur on 4/13/18 within a four hour window. 

On 4/12/18, I received a confirmation call to which I confirmed the delivery between 11am and 3pm on 4/13/18. 

At 3pm, having not received the items or even a phone call, I reached out to the delivery service. After waiting on hold for 10 minutes, a woman answered and said she'd transfer me to someone who could help. This transfer was to IKEA Customer Service. Another 30 minutes of waiting on hold and a woman told me my order would need to be rescheduled and that the particular IKEA I shopped at would need to be contacted, although they were apparently unable to be reached. 

At this point I asked to speak with a supervisor. Another wait on hold and finally a supervisor picked up. She reiterated that the local store would need to be spoken to and that they were currently unreachable. It was 4:30pm at this point. The supervisor said she'd call me back by 6:30pm when her shift ended to update me. 6:30pm came and went with no phone call and another expectation set and missed by IKEA. 

I can't believe how unbelievably poor this experience has been from start to finish. First and most importantly, I don't have items that were critical to my move so that I can work on Monday morning. Second, I took a day off of work to receive these items and sat at home between 11am and 3pm, which was at a cost to me. To top all of this off, the horrific customer service experience with multiple agents being unable to rectify this absolutely abysmal situation is just plain unacceptable.

I really love Ikea! I've been here a few times. They have a lot of cool cheap stuff & going through the store, looking at the showrooms/displays is alway fun. They literally have almost anything you're looking for. 

One thing that they didn't have that I have been looking for is a rocker for a nursery. They do have those poeng chairs but I was wanting one that is more of a swivel. Other than that, they've had other things that I looked. 

I would not recommend going on a Saturday because it is very busy, and they run out of things. There were a couple things that the system said they had in stock, but they were actually out of. 
I would also recommend wearing comfy shoes if you are going to walk through the entire store. You could easily spend 2 hours just walking through.

Never really paid any attention to this chain. Heard the stories about people driving great distances to shop at one. Heard how it was easy to spend the day there. Never really got. Well, post first visit I get it! This place is large and fun to go exploring in for all your household needs. Scandinavian style at very reasonable prices. Nice big Swedish cafeteria in the middle to have a nosh and break. Swedish Meatballs: beef, chicken or vegetarian. Salmon. I look forward to going back; the table lamp and floor lamp I purchased look wonderful and all were easy to assemble with no tools required!

The prices have gone up considerably and the quantities have gone down. 

Waiting in line for 15 minutes for one item is ridiculous  Why not have an express lane? Very disappointed.
Love going to this place!! It definitely gives our family a lot of inspirations of how to decor our house and the prices are very competitive! We are so glad IKEA opened one here in Fishers!

My favorite place to spend money on things I really don't need! I love the concept of IKEA and the European influence on furniture (notice everything is a little below lower like couches, beds, etc.). You can find so many great things for your home, garden, children's spaces here from top to bottom if you are looking for a full renovation. Great prices on super trendy items that you won't be able to find anywhere else! If you don't mind putting it together- you will love this place! If you visit even just to browse- I guarantee their displays will inspire you in some way! Make sure if you plan on making a stop  you have comfy shoes and and a couple of hours to shop! Also be sure to stop in the cafe for their Swedish meatballs because they are good!

How can you not love ikea?! If you don't like crowds or you have little time - this is not the place for you. If you do - check it out. There is always some tips / decor styles that you can take with you from their designers. Everyone was extremely helpful when needing to figure out how i wanted my floating TV shelf. Definitely will be back!

Everyone loves Ikea - IDK why. But the store was clean and it was... OK to look at the things. But my friends just wander around looking at stuff! One thing I will say is it was confusing like if you just wanted to run in and grab something. Like you have to wander around the whole store - and where to pay?? It was a little weird for me. I also had the food. Just mediocre. 

But clean! and some stuff was very convenient or a good price. Give it a go.

Normally we havent had any problems with ikea, until they needed to order hinges because they ran out.   We purchased a cabinet on 3-31-18 and where told the hinges would arrive on 4-9-18, after three calls and three hours on hold still no hinges.   Their after care is horrible.

IKEA is my favorite furniture store 15 years ago. This Swedish company was originally open their door in America at 1985 in Philadelphia. I first bought their furniture at Houston IKEA when we have vacation there. Soon they open the market in Florida then Tampa. 

IKEA provide nanny care while you are shopping. There also have their restaurant inside the store make shopping or lunch there easy. It is very convenient to many customers for easy strolling and look for the furniture. 

The furniture is great for small apartment. There are many space saving ideal. I would said their furniture required a person can follow the instructions of assembling and time to put it together. Their furniture is good price. Since it requires assembly, some people just don't have the time. But I like it to make it my weekend project. 

I would said their furniture are not great for house moving. Once it assembled, they just need to left it in place. Because once you move it too much, you will damage the furniture assembly Joint or connection. Their furniture do look great. And they are very contemporary and modern look.
