Another crazy thing about the returns department is that, even if you have the original receipt and credit card used, and the item is intact, clearly has never been used, and has the stickers still on it, they want to see your driver's license and enter your information into their computer-- something I find unacceptable unless they're going to guarantee they have ironclad cyber security that is immune to hacking/breaches and that they won't sell or disclose my information to anyone else for any reason. Of course, they provide no such guarantees. So, I err on the side of not buying stuff unless I'm absolutely, 100% sure I will be happy with it... Which means it keeps my impulse buying in check, and causes them to lose out on money.

Overall, as far as IKEAs go, this is a 3, but giving it a 4 because I'm just glad to finally have an IKEA in the area.

Great for college kids, temporary living situations but I have a kind of love hate relationship with this store. It's great that they have reasonably priced furniture, it's terrible if you want it to last for a long time or have to move it to a new location. Unlike slightly more expensive furniture pieces, IKEA furniture is not structured enough to move well. We have owned a few pieces that we purchased and had to move and they just don't hold up.
So, furniture only I'd give it a one star for quality- for hard goods you'd be better off spending a little more to get pieces made from wood and not MDF and heavy cardboard.
For other things, glasses, artificial flowers, dishes, rugs, towels, etc I'd give it a five star rating. The stuff is cute, well made, priced well and fun to have around.
The only other things I'd say is that, don't go there if you're in a hurry. Even with shortcuts, you still have to walk a long way to get to pickup items and pay for them. Take a few hours, stroll around, enjoy yourself.

This IKEA seemed a bit disorganized to me . I love some of the ideas they give you, but every time I went to look for something they were out of stock . Need to restock better and make sure things are in the right place.

There are lots of things to love about IKEA. The food in the cafeteria is very nice, extremely good value, and gives a taste of Sweden. Their products for home and garage organization are exceptional. The furniture is affordable, but rather flimsy. The displays of rooms are very impressive. It takes quite a while to make it through the store, and the checkout lines can be brutal if it is crowded. I always spend too much when I visit.

This is just a store, it's not a religious place of worship. They won't really 'improve your life'. They are there to take your money and sell give stuff in return.

Having said that, as far as stores go, it's a pretty good one. They give you pretty high-quality stuff and don't take too much of your money.

When you go, put on your walking shoes, take your own bags (or you'll have to buy them), don't go on an empty stomach, and plan to be there a while. By design, there is no way to get in and out quickly.

Not sure IKEA needs my review - they stand pretty well on their own! I'm there ALL the time for organization and decor goodies. Bonus - IKEA friends and family (free to join) up to SIX cups of amazing coffee or hot tea a day. For very-awake shopping.

IKEA blew me away! They have everything, EVERYTHING! Even a food court. My mind was blown. I am about to move into my first home and was recommended to go here to shop for it. 

They have all the different sections, with room displays to see the merchandise and visualize it. There is kitchen displays, bedroom, dining room, and kid rooms.You can also buy the whole room display if you're wanting to redo your home that way. When you first walk in you grab a pencil and paper to keep track of what items you'd like. If it's big furniture items you write down the description, aisle #, and bin #. You can grab small things as you go, but the furniture you have to get at the end as you head to the check out area. At the very end of all the sections, you enter the warehouse and it's just all the stocked inventory and you find the aisle and bin of each item you want, and load it in your cart. You do have to build the items you buy. 

There is also a mark down aisle. So items that have been returned or may be going out of stock are marked down. It's just like a clearance section. There is even a grocery section!!

I like Ikea furniture. But customer service is backwards here. They make you wait for issues that are simple to resolve. I waited 20 minutes to have a forgotten coupon taken off yesterday. I get it busy store but really?  

Then I tried to call today to see if a delivery came in. The wait again!  No wait time communicated nothing. Just terrible really.

DO NOT purchase from a wedding registry at IKEA.   Total run around for the bride when they go to the store to pick up the purchased gift!   I spent over 2 hours on the phone with IKEA "customer service" trying to track down my purchase while the bride was standing in the store!   Apparently the purchaser is supposed to give the recipient a confirmation number so they have proof that there was a purchase from their registry?!  ARE YOU KIDDING ME?  No more IKEA for me!  They can keep their cheap crappy furnishings.

Ugh.  I used to love Ikea.  However, the long lines and inexplicable inability to open up more than 2 cashier stations makes this place unbearable.  Last night the line (for the only 2 cashiers willing to provide check out!) wound so absurdly around the warehouse space that I decided to abandon my cart full of goods in favor of sleep.

Shopping at Ikea is already a time-consuming experience, and after meandering through dozens of staged rooms, I don't want to have to spend more time in line than I have to.

The first trip to IKEA didn't disappoint. This place has an ambiance that pushes the brink of amusement and convenience; rather, it's exhilarating. Food was amazing if you'd like a quick bite, and the place offers a variety of home items that are high quality but low price. Try the chicken meatballs!

DO NOT order countertops or kitchens through IKEA While I've had decent experience with furniture purchases in the past, our experience ordering countertops was awful. 
1. The salesperson lies to us about additional charges we asked specifically about that were added later.
2. The company they contracted to (Intelco) was just as bad - the guy that came to take the template up-charged us, refused to speak to me (a woman) and insisted on speaking to me through my contractor (a man) though we were all in the same room, and then didn't even do his job right and had to come back.
3. When we tried to contact IKEA to dispute the up charge, I spent six hours total either on the phone, on hold, trying to find numbers that worked, and eventually going to the store to demand answers.
 
The whole experience was disgusting. Don't bother.

First, I'd like to say my family and I have been shopping with Ikea for 20+ years; in multiple locations and states. 

My most recent purchase with Ikea was absolutely horrible. I visited the Tampa, Fl store on August 4, 2018 to make a fairly large purchase. Since I was buying some large items I applied for the Ikea Credit Card to receive the free delivery to my home. 

I was purchasing two mattresses, box spring, bed frame, and bookshelf. 

The sales associate (Gio) in the bed/mattress department was very distracted and kept walking away from me to start my order before I had decided on what I was actually purchasing. Because of this, and their lack of focus this caused me to not order everything I needed. For the box spring and mattress I got, I stated that I was going to have the box spring on the floor with no legs and no one told me that I would need the support leg due to the size of the mattress (queen). I thought that the support beam would be on the floor as well. 

Next, when I placed the order downstairs they did not tell me I would need the support leg either. 

About an hour after I left Ikea, I received an email stating that the bed frame I ordered was out of stock and I would be issued a gift card for the amount of purchase - after I had put my entire plus purchase on the Ikea Credit Card. (Which makes absolutely no sense) 

At that point when I called customer service the wait time was 90 minutes. I did not have that kind of time to sit on hold. The next day August 5, I drove back to Ikea Tampa and spoke with Trish in the returns/exchange department who was extremely helpful and told me the bed frame I ordered would be back in stock Tuesday and added to my order, which would be delivered the following Monday August 13. 

The day of my expected delivery finally arrives and all that is delivered is the bed frame! What the heck, Ikea?! Where is the rest of my order?
We then proceeded to waste 8 hours between two days waiting on hold for Ikea and the shipping company XPO. We kept getting run away in circles with no clear answer. Why was this my responsibility? I did not loose the delivery? And all everyone had to say about the situation was "I don't know". 

The rest of my ordered was not found and delivered until Wednesday (which might not seem like a big deal) but I had to take time off work to wait for both deliveries and make all these calls and wait on hold for hours on end. 

All Ikea did for this situation was issue me a $75 gift card. That isn't going to pay my $1500+ Credit Card bill. That isn't going to get my time back. That isn't going to make up for my missed days at work. 

I am very disappointed with my last visit and purchase with Ikea. I don't know how soon I will visit again. Or recommend Ikea to friends and family.
Check out takes FOREVER. Seriously that line is what nightmares are made of. I like the concept of IKEA, but walking through that store makes me feel like a mouse trapped indefinitely in a maze.
How can you have lines this long to leave? 21 lanes to checkout and on Saturday afternoon you have 6 open. I won't be back.

Great prices, well organized, people in the store were much more enjoyable to shop aside than the people in Elizabeth, NJ which is our other option for IKEA.  Pick up of items was a little chaotic, but lines moved quickly.

*This review is based off of 1 bad experience*

So basically I came to this Ikea earlier in the day to walk around and get ideas. I found a super cute table and chairs for my balcony reasonably priced. I didn't have my car with me so I came back later that day to get them and when I went to the aisle there were none in stock in the boxes below. BUT they had 5 on display (see picture) and 1 on display in the showroom (see picture). Soooo I went to ask someone at the information desk if we can grab it off the display and she told me no because it isn't in stock. Which I don't understand. Because 1. It is in stock. Y'all are just placing them around on display and 2. Me, a customer, is willing to buy it and you're turning down the sale???? Ok. Makes ZERO sense. I literally said I wasn't leaving without it and she said she COULD NOT sell me it. I went back over to the tables and another employee walked by so I asked him why was I being told I couldn't purchase the tables and he was able to make it happen for me. And I got $10 off. So yes I am happy I was able to get the table and chairs & get a discount and they look great on my balcony (see attached photo) but I'm very disappointed that one of their employees was refusing to sell something to me.

Was charged twice for an item, by the time I realized, my cashier was serving someone else. So I went to customer service to hope to be refunded. There was no system for taking people in order, as many people who arrived after me were seen at the desk before me. I was then told that I needed to return to that cashier and get a manager to do the refund. I find it hard to believe that customer service is unable to refund this. After waiting for 30 minutes my cashier was no longer there, meaning I was unable to receive a refund for a mistake that was not my own. Ridiculous

What in the Birds-Eye-Frozen-Vegetable hell is this, IKEA? I've always looked to you for affordable, ethical, edible meals and this mess just isn't acceptable. The drink machine was out of order, the children's pasta has been discontinued, and the dining room was dirty. What a disappointment. On the one plus side, the salmon was tasty and well cooked.

I went in for a few things for my kitchen. I went through the doors by the kid play center. If you know you want to get stuff for the house go through this door! Right there was everything in its own piles and I could go and pick it up!  I was in and out within 30 minutes!!!  I was so happy to find everything that I was looking for and spent under $30!   
I also went around 1130 am on a Monday so there were not a lot of people there which was nice!!

I needed a pillow and I am pretty sure IKEA has the cheapest pillows in town. The quality is actually quite bad, but you cannot beat the price for a pillow you only need for a short visit and not take back home - $2! Apparently, they were $1.50 last week. $2 was still a great price. I also got $1 swirl cone on the way out the door.  Lastly, I was impressed at the selection of fake plants.

If I didn't know any better, I'd think IKEA was a scam. Our couch we purchased has a problem and we've tried calling and emailing but haven't had any response. At this point our only option is to drive an out to the store, instead, they are losing our future business.

Second horrible experience in a row at South Philadelphia store! Two months ago I purchased picture frames. The cashier pushed each frame down the belt into a metal piece that the belt went under. Every frame became dented. When I drew her attention to it she said I could go back and get more. I said it wasn't me to go back through the store for her mistake. As soon as I said that another employee walked by and said he would pick more frames. As he was doing so the cashier turned her back to me, began talking to the neighboring cashier loud enough for me to hear. The neighboring cashier looked at me and snipped "I would wait until they went and got them." I spoke to a supervisor on the spot who said that wasn't protocol and he would talk to the cashier. Two evenings ago I went back to Ikea to use my birthday meal voucher and shop the store. At 6:30 the line for the food was reaching the soda area. Only one side of food serving was open and the few people working didn't seem to have any urgency about moving the line. Two cashiers sat idle because the line wasn't moving. I asked one cashier what the problem was and she shook her head and said they ran out of food and had to cook more. She suggested I go downstairs for food or across the parking lot to Chic-fil-a. So my family and I walked the store hoping the line would be better when we returned. at 7:10 we returned to a slightly shorter line. We decided to eat. Once in line we saw a completely empty cake display. Not one cake of any type. And I was supposed to receive a free piece of cake. Then we went to pick our food. No Salmon. One very poor looking piece of garlic bread. Then we went for coffee. No regular or decaf coffee. No cappuccino. No cream. Sodas were all mostly carbonated water as the syrup was either out or too low. NO FORKS! Just a dirty mess. See pics.

I purchased an in home visit for Kitchen Measurement & Design. It is refundable. I paid $199.00 for the visit. I decided to cancel. I called the number they provided for cancellation. 
First attempt was in the morning,  it took 36 minutes for them to pickup. The person said he cancelled the order and went to get me a confirmation number. HE NEVER RETURNED.


I called again this evening and was kept on line for 42 minutes and I gave up. I will try again in the morning

Making the appointment took 2 minutes but trying to cancel the appointment will take  you MUCH longer.

IKEA is great.  It seems you get a lot for the price.  All around well rounded for your home shopping.  IKEA is great....until it's not. 
They have a 1-888 customer service number.  They also have an email customer service form available....will respond within 72 hours. NOT. Nine days, no response. Three phone calls, four hours plus on hold and finally a human, a rude woman who said she couldn't help me even though I was missing a single part...the leg of an item, not an insignificant part. I drove the 30 minutes to my local store and was able to get the help and leg I needed.  Store customer service said they have to call same number even though they are a store.  
IKEA is known for items that require assembly.  Missing parts must be common place.  I sure wish they had better remote help out there for people like me who are standing with a screwdriver in hand and not enough parts.

The IKEA has really helped the area around it become more built up, and while it's a furniture store, it's almost like a tourist attraction at the same time. It's such a massive place, and they have literally everything here. There's a grocery area and a restaurant too, where you can try their famous Swedish meatballs. I also got a really nice chair from here, and it is comfortable yet it looks sleek and modern. Overall, it's a very fun and cool place to go.

Really happy to see the European furniture store in Indy. It's just like all IKEA's - huge, simple, and crowded. You can also get some Swedish / Nordic foods at their mini-mart and don't forget to sign up with IKEA Family to save a few bucks.

We placed an order for a cabinet for our office to have delivered. They delivered it two days prior to the agreed upon delivery date and out office building was closed.  And they delivered on a Sunday? Why would they do this?  Now we are trying to get our cabinet delivered now that we are back from vacation and we cannot get through to anyone at IKEA. We have made phone calls to no avail. Very bad customer service.

My go-to place for home decor. The way they set up the store makes the shopping experience nice and you can feel relaxed looking around for whatever you want. Also great selections of merchandise and reasonable price. You can spend a hundred bucks and get a buch of value items or spend a few grands for quality design items. The only drawback is that this place is always crowded, which I personally find annoying. But thats inevitable.

The cinnamon rolls are always amazing! I didn't even bother walking around the store. From what I could tell it's a nice location. The food section was a bit understaffed and needed a second cashier. The lady running the cashier was moving quickly but the line was very long due to such high demand. 

Overall great experience. I just wish they had a few additional staff members to make the process of checking out even faster.
If you don't want to work a job, stay home. Worst IKEA customer service experience I've ever had.

Huge store where you can walk through various rooms to view furniture and appliances, etc. they also have various household items and kitchen utensils you can purchase as well. To me, I hate how you have to walk through the rooms to finally get to the area where you have to then grab a cart and pull your own inventory. I am still not completely sure if they have staff available to help individuals that cannot pull their own inventory. They do have drive up areas to make loading of items into your car easy however they have railing that are in the way. So you really can't push your cart directly up to your car for loading. You have to park at the railing then carry over the railing to load your car. Such a hassle. Nobody around to assist in loading either. The people that shop this store tend to be rude, taking up the full aisles, walking in front of you while trying to get a cart from the cart area. There is also really no cost savings going here. The only reason we visited is because they had the desk my daughter was looking for. 

Not really a place we routinely visit.

Need to seriously revisit the return line situation. This is the second time I brought a simple item to return. Take a number, their are 25 people ahead of me in the return line. 3 people working the counters, looks like an hour wait just to make a return. Then I ask if I can shop first and return my item at the end, but if I miss them calling my number, I'll have another hour long wait at the end. This place is ridiculous.

I have to start by saying I have always LOVED IKEA so naturally when I found out Fishers would be getting our very own... I was over the moon! I bought an IKEA mattress probably 5 years ago and it's still perfect, which was surprisingly when you consider how inexpensive they are. I ended up moving recently and my goodness did IKEA come in handy. My entire living room is furnished by IKEA. Be prepared to spend your afternoon at IKEA because you will be so thrilled by everything they have. Don't worry there is a food court half way through! They have low fees to have your furniture delivered and installed! Which was great for me because I drive a small car. I have taken a chair home and built it myself though! Not too difficult, even for someone who isn't handy. I would recommend going on a weekday morning if you are not a fan of crowds!

The place is a cluster FoxtrotUniformCharlieKilo.  Stay away, way far away.  Everything is cheap and poor quality.  Meatballs have no flavor.  Restaurant is understaffed.  After waiting several minutes in line to pay for our food, our fries were cold and soggy when we sat down.  Also, it is claustrophobic with no clear directions to the nearest exit without sounding an alarm.  I don't understand why this place is not a fire hazard.  If you like wandering through a maze with no cheese at the end, this place is for you. Never again.
I came to Ikea with my nephew he said let's go eat. I was like not cafeteria food but I was surprised. I work close to Ikea so I have been a few times

This post will focus on their terrible customer service at this branch. (Didn't have the food here though know its good at other branches, and of course the furniture offerings are the same as other branches. I have enjoyed the experience at the Philadelphia IKEA and have generally been a happy customer previously.)

We initially went to our closest IKEA in Philadelphia, but because the item we wanted was out of stock, we went to the Conshohocken store. We saw in the computer that the item was in stock, and were able to pay for it, and were told that it would be in the furniture pick up area. You can imagine that all this took a fair bit of time and standing in lines. Because it was extremely busy, we asked if we could come back later and the staff was supportive of that idea. So we went to another neighboring store for about an hour, came back and saw that the item was in the "ready for pickup" cue on the monitor, and then went upstairs to look at one other item in the IKEA. When we came back down and got to the front of the line to pick it up, we were told that the item was actually not in their stock (or they couldn't find it), and there was nothing they could do. We were speaking to the manager of customer service Diedra, who gave a very insincere apology, blamed us for leaving the area so they couldn't tell us this earlier, and seemed completely disinterested in righting the situation in any way with a coupon or any other discount, not even a symbolic gesture. We asked to speaker to her manager, so we talked to the store manager, who also did not have any ideas on how to make things better. We (not they) offered the idea of buying the floor model with the As-Is discount, suggesting that usually the floor models go for 50% off; they (seemingly begrundgingly) agreed, but said they could not commit to the level of discount. I get that they are not the authorities to price the As-Is section, but the manner in which they communicated this and basically stated they had no interest in even trying to suggest a discount was adding to our frustration. 

The piece of furniture was unbolted from the display, and the As-Is section manager immediately priced it at 50% off. Despite some minor difficulty with the label and spending more time trying to get the item to ring up in order to pay for it, we finally did and were ready to dissamble it to go home. When we went to grab what we thought was an empty box next to where the unit was displayed, we found that there was indeed a boxed version sitting there (albeit a different color). We found this to show to Diedra, who responded by basically saying 'well I already apologized, there isn't anything else I can do.' 

I get that there can be inventory mistakes. That part is frustrating, but hey it happens. I am not even one who believes that the customer is always right. But the utter disregard the customer service department has to serving the customers is pretty absurd. There are really easy ways to make customers feel heard and valued (don't blame the customer for your inventory issues,' at least try to make your apologies sound sincere; even a $10 cafeteria voucher can be something to offer wronged customers and basically be free to you - better than absolutely nothing). it shouldn't be up to the customers to come up with ideas (ie in this case, buy the store model). I am surprised that such a large branch (the headquarters in fact!) does not have better training in customer service, or selection process for their managers. 

Everyone else in the store - the As-Is manager, the cashier, the woman who helped unbolt the floor model - was great and perfectly nice. It was the customer service department that was The Worst at customer service.
Ok for a small IKEA and the layout was more confusing than in some of their larger stores

Just got 2 tables for my LEGO collections!  One was discontinued :( but clerk suggested As Is section and got it for $100 off and shorter table for $49! Solid wood and I couldn't see it online - so bricks and mortar stores work.  Not so happy w getting charged twice for kid but hey, it was $1.59 so I'm still ahead! :)

This rating is for the FOOD! IKEA cafe is pretty popular specially because of the pricing... very cheap! I loveeeee the Swedish meatballs - sooo yum!!! Also loveeeee the chocolate cake - or should I say slice of cake lol 

Other things on the menu that I have not tried:
Chicken tenders
Fries
Corn
Mashed potatoes with gravy
Braised pork or beef (not sure which one)

You get kid meals too.

Coffee, tea, sodas are only $1 each. 

2 chocolate cakes (slices) cost less than $8. Sooo worth it!!!

My love/hate relationship with Ikea continues. I love the selections, prices, and what you can get (which is basically about anything and everything under the sun). I haven't been in over 20 years - my first experience was in college in Philadelphia and I enjoyed decking out my dorm room without breaking the bank. What I hate is the size and lack of customer service, which I found pretty appalling at the Indy location over the weekend.

Took the family there since it had literally been raining for 2 whole days straight and we needed to get out of the house. I understand that it's a HUGE store, and you could probably spend 8 hours in there and still not see everything, but sometimes bigger isn't always better. We walked around, taking our time looking. We thought about checking them into the "childcare" but they were full. Have to admit we did get lost a few times, even following the signs, and were just walking in circles. 

I did want to get some meatballs so we went to the restaurant and waited in line. I was pretty confused as why on a busy Saturday, only one line was open and 2 people were working. After standing in line for 10 minutes without moving, we decided 4 meatballs were not worth it and left to check out. I think Ikea should have an express line for people who buy just a few things, not a truckload like others. I think this would really help with getting people in and out. We stood in line for 45 MINUTES. Of course we chose the line where a couple were arguing with the cashier over prices of tea cups for a good 20 minutes. I was getting so frustrated and a few people behind us were even commenting how a manager should have helped out a bit more and tried to get the situation handled smoothly. All the lines were super slow and had a long wait. Finally paid for our 3 items and thankfully got out. 

For a Saturday, they definitely needed more staff. I didn't understand why in  the self help furniture section half the aisles were "closed." They were either stocking or doing inventory but they had the bars down so you couldn't walk through them. You would think they would do it on a less busier day/time, but nope they decided to do it on a Saturday. Go figure. Granted, we did end up finding a shoe cabinet we liked but I ordered it online. If I do go back, I'm going to just go to eat as the food in the cafeteria looked really good and for the price, you can't beat it. Oh Ikea...

This is the worst Ikea i've ever dealt with. I ordered furniture for delivery August 20th, they called the day before it was supposed to arrive and delayed me two weeks, which was frustrating not only because i've already paid for this on time delivery but now I have absolutely no furniture in my apartment. Two weeks goes by, and I get yet ANOTHER call, my furniture will be delayed until September 13th. I'm beyond pissed at this point,  but there is nothing I can do. Today I get a call (September 12th) that the "trailer" is "broken" and now my furniture will be delivered this Sunday instead. I have no furniture in my apartment, spent over 1,000 dollars just to be sitting here waiting on their time. Im BEYOND disgusted with the customer service here and I will never be using ikea unless it's in store pick up ever again. Ikea should be absolutely ashamed of themselves. This isn't food delivery i'm waiting for a BED

Oh what an adventure you can have at IKEA! When you first enter this ginormous store they have carts for your toddler and a check in area for your older children (height requirement noted on the wall).
The food in the little cafe is cheap and tasty. My kids love having lunch here as it is very child friendly. 
The store can be super overwhelming, especially on the weekend when it's full of people and the lines are long. But today, much like other week days we had a great time exploring room to room and playing in the children's department. Even the lines at check out were quick! 
Our favorite items to purchase here are small furniture items (big ones are too complicated for me), kitchen utensils, home decor and rugs (especially for the play room since they must be replaced frequently). Oh and don't forget to grab a delicious chocolate bar with hazelnuts!!!

Not a bad way to spend a Saturday afternoon! Whether you're here to get some interior design inspo, looking for something specific in the marketplace, or hungry for some Swedish meatballs, ikea has something for everyone. Basic Affordable products and furniture to fill any white space in your home.

My fiance and I recently moved into our first house and were debating whether we needed to splurge on some bedroom pieces like the dresser and chest. We went to competitive stores, but ended up liking the simple 8-drawer black model at ikea best. Ended up getting both the chest and dresser for under $600. The only downside of buying  furniture from ikea is of course, the assembly part, since each set comes in 3 boxes and comes with picture instructions which can get confusing. Once you get over that hurdle tho, you we really enjoy the furniture! Lasts us years and doesn't look too shabby!

The first time I came here it was packed and overwhelming, but I went a second time and was pleasantly surprised at the ease of getting in and out my way thru the maze. 
Of course IKEA is a treat and all their stuff is cool. It just tough to figure out where I'm at at any given time. It makes it tough to shop. 

If you've been to other IKEA's, this one my feel a little disappointing. Its only one level and there isn't quite as much stuff. That said, is cool to have around and bears going all the way to another city just to experience it.

This location is fantastic. The displays are clean and well thought out. Nice place to browse without being hassled. Prices are suitable and they have the best return policy I have seen. You can return/exchange an item within a year if you change your mind on the product. No hassles, no questions, as long as it's not damaged. In the box or put together, it doesn't matter. That's extremely fair. The staff is friendly and the cafeteria area is convenient and well priced. I would definitely recommend this location to others. I will be a regular here for years to come.

This was my first time in this location and I have to say, that it is much nicer than the one I've been to in South Florida where I live. 

I was there at lunchtime on a Monday and the store was relatively empty which made it easy to meander and browse.

The store itself is very open and bright. The "rooms" are decorated beautifully.  The staff members were so friendly. Maybe because of the area? 

I would definitely return the next time I'm in the area!
So the wait here is horrible. They only have 3 registers open and the lines are 10-15 ppl deep. I love there stuff but I hate shopping here. And they have a ton of ppl just walking around.

I go to IKEA 3-4 times a year now since there's one in town, which is more than any other furniture store.  I love their Swedish meatballs and some of their products e.g cookies, pots, wine glasses etc....and one of the best perk is their free coffee.  I guess this has changed since the last time I went to IKEA, maybe a few months back.  Today's experience left a bitter taste in my mouth and I was very annoyed.

I usually stop by the front to pick up my free coffee before I start shopping.  However tonight, the cashier said that it has changed and I must go to the cafeteria for the free coffee.  So I went to the cafeteria to get my free coffee.  Of course, they don't have the "to go" cup but the mug is only available.   Got my free coffee in a mug, and I figured I'll go up front for the "to go" cup, kinda didn't want to walk around IKEA with the mug and possibly have an accident.  The guy said I have to pay for the cup, it's not free.  He gave me this look, like...I'm trying to cheat IKEA (ugh....so uncomfortable).  Geez, I get it....it sucks that people take advantage of the free coffee thing that IKEA had to change their free coffee thing. Hahhhhaaa...can't be me since I'm only at IKEA a few times a year, right?!?

My recommendation......maybe a reusable mug that we can bring for our free coffee if cost is an issue for members, or I can bring my own!!!  Also, would be nice to get an email/reminder too that free coffee is only available at the cafeteria....so I don't feel ...ahum silly (Maybe I missed that email, Ooops).

I love ikea. Honestly like it's so much fun and I always get the most amazing deals for furniture and my kids have a blast here. However, I was getting something for my one kid and couldn't find it in the marketplace so I asked an employee. He told me that it was out of stock so I said ok and planned to leave. But just before I went, I decided to take a quick look around the area just in case I found a similar thing to the object that the employee said was out of stock. I was looking around and I actually managed to find the thing I was looking for. So moral of the story don't trust employees because they're bitter and tired???

I am not a huge fan of IKEA because how things are set up. I get lost all the time and I hate that I am forced to walk through every department before making it to where I need to go or the checkout line. I've been about 3 times and they had the same stuff except for the outside summer items.

The prices in IKEA are way too high for you having to grab the item yourself, and assemble it with barely any tools given. The prices just aren't reasonable at all.

Their clearance is just damaged junk which I don't understand because it still priced like nothing is wrong with it. I wish thy would put more of their summer items and clearance.

On the plus side I enjoy walking through and visiting their room designs and how they incorporate the items around the store in these rooms. They do a great job designing!

I bought $4349 of kitchen cabinets from Ikea.  As I assembled the cabinets there was one entire panel missing from one base csbinet, and some dowels and screws missing from several base cabinets.  I went to Plymouth Meeting and they were able to quickly help me.  Then I moved on to wall cabinets and now a small panel from corner angle was missing.  I got my roommate to send me a pic of my receipt and this time went to S Philly Ikea straight from work.  I showed it to the customer service lady Claudia but she said a picture of a receipt means nothing.  I told her I have my Ikea family card # and even pulled up my credit card transaction from my account but she said she couldnt find my transaction.  I asked to speak to the manager so she called and told me the manager said no.  Im not sure why you wouldnt let me speak to the manager myself (this by itself is a bad sign from the manager) so I asked to speak to her directly, she calls again and then puts me on the phone (hmm phone?) and the manager Karen was extremely unhelpful and give the typical "our policy blablabla".

1) First of all, whats with all these missing pieces?  People dont have the time to be making trips back and forth to put their project on hold for missing pieces.
2) Plymouth Meeting was able to help me quicker because they have spare parts inventory (their returns area has bins full of them unlike S Philly).  Esp when you have drunk packagers(see#1) S Philly needs a better way to address missing/spare parts.
3) I can understand policy but were talking about one small piece from a $4349 purchase.  Do they really think its a good idea to holdup someone kitchen project even longer over something so small?  I even showed the Ikea lady the picture of the cabinet installed with the missing piece, picture of my receipt, my family card number, my credit card transactions but they are too focused on policy to use common sense (or are just lazy).

IKEA has always been a staple in my home decorating. Their furniture is reasonably affordable (some is extremely affordable) and always looks lovely. 

My favorite things about IKEA:
You can get a ton of decorating ideas just walking through the store. I love seeing different room layouts with all the finishings- it always gives me new ideas of what to try at home. Their product pick up is easy to understand, and they have measuring tapes conveniently located throughout the store and paper/pens to write things down. They also have an AMAZING cafeteria with cheap and delicious food. You can't go wrong with the Swedish meatballs. I also find their return process to be straight forward and simple, and they've even been able to help me find assembly pieces years after and initial purchase.

The cons:
Plan to spend a few hours here. The store is huge, and although there are short cuts you still won't be able to go directly to any specific department without visiting several others first. 
There also doesn't appear to be many staff around, which has never been an issue for me, but heads up if you need help!
The worst thing about IKEA is their product assembly. It is time consuming and extremely frustrating. They have a new service where you can hire them to construct your new furniture, but if you're doing it yourself I hope you have an adventurous spirit!

Dear IKEA, every experience is more and more disappointing. Today I managed to pick an item that has to be picked up from the order pick up desk. Here I am sitting around waiting for someone else to bring me my box. The guy next to me has been here for 45 minutes. I despise the fact that my entire day is taken up by waiting for furniture that is, at most, sub par. Their has not been an enjoyable IKEA experience now in over a year. Going to stop shopping here. Only thing going for you now is that there isn't any other store in the Tampa area with inexpensive furniture.

Listen- don't judge me...but this was my VERY FIRST Ikea experience and I am all the way here for it! Sign me up to randomly walk through and 'test drive' furniture at other locations! Neat, clean, inspiring for every square footage... it's an HGTV fans dream! 

I didn't purchase anything (this time), but there was so much to digest, and so much to like! I'm unsure if the sofa/living/family room options would work for me because they're stylized so low to the ground (and I understand the brand and why)... But I'd definitely purchase bedroom, kitchen options, accents, etc. You simply can't beat the price.

It was nice to enjoy a furniture store that just 'gets it.' Parking was convenient with both indoor (parking garage) and outdoor options, the cafe was nice, and the store layout made sense. Stay tuned for follow-up reviews at other locations.

Moral of the story: Ikea gets my vote, and I'll likely progress from window shopper to purchaser.

My first experience with Ikea was in the Denver area so when they built one in St Louis we were eager to explore.

Its amazing how much stuff they have and how much they are able to put into their showroom.  There's a cafeteria, a kids watch room and more.

They have a lot of staples and many of their setups do not change.  If you go all the time you will see a lot of the same stuff.  If you go every so often you might see stuff that's different.

If you have an Ikea card, you get free coffee.  They use to have it where its in a to-go cup and you can walk with it.  They've now changed their ways and you can only get it in the cafeteria.  Not very appealing anymore on that aspect, I hope they change it back to the original way.

Check it out, you'll find yourself going back...and back!

I've been to many ikea stores across the US and this is horrible! First it's way smaller then any other ikea store and the pricing sometimes doesn't match what's on display. 
I went to return something that I paid with Apple Pay and they said they could return it because the card number on the receipt doesn't match my card. 
But that's what Apple Pay does. It doesn't use your real card number. It generates card numbers to protect you. 
The manager that helped me said that they don't accept Apple Pay. I'm like really?! 
They are so unprofessional here!!

My experience with customer service has been about a D average grade. 

One day I had to stand in line at the returns counter for approximately 20 minutes before they called another employee to assist at a second register even though the line had been growing for a while. The employee working didn't address anyone in line the entire time. 

Josh, a manager at the restaurant was rude and inconsiderate when it came to a mistake at the register, though it was fixed. 

It took more than half an hour at the book case section for an employee to find another employee to help answer a question about one of the items. 

The worst was when I ordered a dresser online and no one apologized during the weeks I had to call every few days to ask when it would finally be available to pickup since every employee made a different promise about the time it would be available. Not a single apology. With an escalated complaint from myself they eventually delivered it from a Chicago area store and waived the fee but no apology was given even WEEKS LATER. 

A mistake at a register once had us waiting for 10 minutes just for them to review my birthday coupon. 

The products are great but the employees are overall a let down.

Super disappointed that they killed the kids eat free tuesdays. We would come on tuesdays when we needed something and get lunch too, but apparently the kids are too noisy for the admin folks at IKEA who are here in the afternoons. We won't be coming back anytime soon.

IKEA, why must you exist?!? This store is dangerous for me, and by dangerous I mean I could practically live in there.  I'm always fantasizing about how to redecorate my apartment and even if I'm there just to buy a few small things, it takes all the willpower in the world to not end up buying more stuff than I'm able to carry home (though thank goodness for those big blue bags!! They are worth the extra few bucks).  Prices are AMAZING and they are always introducing new collections and items (sometimes limited edition) so I say jump on those deals while you are still able to!  Plus the food....where do I begin?  Even if Swedish meatballs aren't your thing, there are plenty of other options for every palate.  And if you're not already an IKEA FAMILY member, sign up NOW because that magical orange card gets you discounts on specific items, allows you free coffee and tea in the cafe, and puts you on their mailing list so you can be notified of new items, promotions, and special events (like their 75th Anniversary celebration complete with a scavenger hunt!).

Besides the fact that your trapped in their maze and it's hard to just dash in and grab what you need and get out I like this new location!

They have every type could possibly want to furnish any room at a decent price. They also have lots of design ideas for all sorts of spaces, especially smaller one. 

The people working here seem very helpful and glad to solve whatever issue you may have.

I just wish they didn't have such delicious cookies up front!!!

Finally Indiana has an Ikea, right here . We are so lucky to have a fantastic store and we don't have to drive to Ohio anymore. You will find very affordable Scandinavian furnitures, nice coworkers , take home food , cookies. The store is a bit smaller , than others, but I have fun when I go to shop. 
I 've got all our Christmas light, tv unit, day bed Hemnes is the best, and we like the Business table and chair we got. 
Ikea is the place for anybody , good place for window shopping , getting ideas, celebrating an occasion and much more. They have a free reward program called Ikea Family , it's wonderful.

I finally braved this store after all my friends have told me their experiences; 5 to 8 hour experiences. I treated this shopping trip like a military exercise. I highly encourage to eat beforehand and wear comfortable clothing. Say good bye to your loved ones and have your will in order. 

Now, for those who have never been to Ikea, this place is like Disney for adults. The store is very clean and staff were constantly walking around making sure product was re-shelved neatly from the masses touching everything. The store provided maps with dotted line of the layout of the store, like a freaking treasure hunt. We braved upstairs where I enjoyed the demo layouts and then proceeded downstairs to pick items outs. 

My experience was pleasant. The two areas that I would consider large purchases is lightning and kitchen. Today, I purchased accessories and a shark. Yeap, I'm a shark nut. 

The only reason reason this location did not receive 5 stars is check out. What a bloody nightmare. Despite my 3 hours perusing the store, my 20 minute wait at check out was like checking into hell. This is where mean people are. People hitting their carts into me, kids screaming at the top of their lungs (of course their parents act deaf) and my cashier was down right rude. I will give the cashier a "free pass" as several customers in a row in front of me treated her poorly. She assumed the worst by the time I approached. I said good afternoon and asked her how her day was. She seemed shocked that someone would actually treat her like a human being. 

Overall, kudos to Ikea. You took a potential fire pit of hell and managed to create a lovely shopping experience. Walmart needs to take some pointers from you. 

(That is my 140lb Newfoundland with his new pet shark toy)

Solid shopping experience.  Huge warehouse with staged furniture, lighting, rugs, artwork, and more.

There is a childcare area, but it's first come first serve with long waits.  Max 1 hr use with 90 mins offered to Ikea Family (think rewards card) members.

Check out the Cafe upstairs.  Very reasonably priced ($5 / $2.50 kids meal) Swedish meatball, mashed potato, and vegetable dishes.  The fountain drinks are awesome - mix of flavored carbonated sodas  and non-carbonated drinks.

There's a Costco-like fast food / ice cream area on the ground floor where you check out, but the Cafe is worth spending an extra 20 mins for good food at a good price.

I have no beef with the IKEA concept. I shop at the store and have done so for years. I go there with my mom. But...

I had a very distressing incident occur during my most recent visit on November 5. While I was in the store, I was taking photographs as well as video clips of the store displays using my cell phone, for Google Maps. I am a "local guide" and do this for many stores in Philadelphia. I have noted that Ikea has many similar pictures online, and no posted policy that photography is not allowed.

Consider how many shots of this IKEA are here on Yelp...

Nevertheless, I was approached by security and told to put my camera way and stop taking pictures. I was told that this is because a customer complained.

I would like to note that I was careful not to include any customers in any of the imagery I captured.

now, I understand that a store has the right to ask somebody to simply stop taking pictures. That is not my complaint. 

I am upset that the security guard was not able to cite the policy that would form the foundation for the request that I stop doing something that it is readily apparent is permitted.

when I further requested clarification from the store manager, I was simply told that a customer didn't like that I was taking pictures.

That is simply not a good enough answer. I want to clear response as to what the policy is regarding photography inside the store. And explicitly I'd like to know what the policy is when there are no customers or Ikea associates in the images, since I understand and respect the right to privacy.

At this point I'm left feeling nervous that if I were to take a photograph inside an Ikea, a total stranger can request that management use security to stop me from doing so.

The whole thing is very unfortunate to, rather uncomfortable, and it's entirely unclear if it was in any way justified by any sort of policy.

I know people come here for the furniture but I come here for the meals. The classic Swedish meatballs are wonderful. I always get them with a plate of fries drenched in gravy. If you have a Thrifty gal no better place for date night. I know I'm not alone, it can get quite busy here. And in the case of the furniture I own a great deal of Ikea products there is an obvious correlation between price and quality. For example their pillow for $69 is significantly better and more durable then they're $9 pillow. I have one of their mattresses with a 10 year warranty I believe it conked out after 6 years I have the receipt and got a replacement one no problem at no charge.

Let's be real. I come here for the food. The furniture and other home things are just a bonus. The food is tasty and inexpensive. I'm not asking for 5 stars when I eat at Ikea. It is more than sufficient. Lately the service in the restaurant has been lacking, but you get what you pay for. 

Furniture ... I like what they have for the most part. Ikea looks the same no matter what country you're in. Consistence in chains is my favourite. It is kind of the point. Gives you something familiar even if you're in an unfamiliar place.

I love Ikea products. It's one of the better places to shop for storage items. But I've had nothing but disappointing experiences shopping online.

I ordered a dresser online and placed it on hold for pick up. I went with a friend to pick up the dresser. While he loaded the truck, I picked up a few extra things. It wasn't until we got home, that we noticed how badly damaged the dresser was. Pictures attached. It required an extra trip to Ikea to get a replacement drawer. While Ikea offered us a $50.00 gift certificate, this was not the first time this happened.

I ordered items and had them shipped to me. Both drawers arrived damaged. 

Pros: Lots of storage and products to choose from
Cons: Products easily damaged. Ikea charges extra to put items on hold for pick up.

Edmonton seriously lacks in furniture stores that use their own shipping services. I may still visit the Edmonton store - but I won't be ordering online.

I love having this IKEA so close. They always have everything I need in stock and have GREAT clearance prices on cute furniture. The store is well organized and well staffed. You're free to browse in peace but there's also plenty of help if you have a question. The other day I went in looking for some type of shelving unit and picked up a great little piece for under $50 - super happy with how it looks in our room and doesn't feel cheap at all. Also, the food here is pretty tasty. Love that they give you a free birthday meal and cake when you sign up to be a member (which is free).

Slowest service in the entire universe.  Checkout on a Saturday afternoon was 40-45 minutes.  They are obviously under staffed, but there was no sense of urgency with any of the employees, managers, etc...  Cafeteria is unsanitary......coffee mugs still had stains.  Utensils and plates were all gross.  I question whether to ever eat here again.  This IKEA used to be awesome....what happened?

Excellent product. Innovative store. Horrendous service.

Ikea has great furniture solutions when it comes to design, quality and the price, due to the self-picking, self-deliver and self-assembly concepts they're known for. That earns the star (probably could have been two stars, but I'm really annoyed). The horrible customer service is the reason for the negative review.

Wanted to purchase two full-size bed foundations for our guest rooms. Asked an Ikea bedroom associate for help, who was kind enough to create and print out a "shopping list" of all of the items we needed for the beds... or so we thought. Our mistake was relying on her expertise. I learned later that she was new, but she never said, "I'd like someone to check this, since I'm new" or something like that (which would have been fine with us). 

While she said she checked and that they had the two full-size foundations, there were none on the shelves. The Ikea person in the shelving area couldn't explain why, but told us to come back the next day, which we did. After returning for the foundations, and bringing them home, I learned that springs are not included with the "spring mattress base." (Really?) Had they been put on our list, we would have purchased them... price or cost was never an issue. We returned a third time for the springs. All set? Nope. A $10 center support leg for each bed is also not included and an extra. Again, had it been on the list provided in response to, "Is this everything we need?" we would have purchased it.

Customer service provided by Nicole, a "team lead" could not have been worse. No empathy. No willingness to make any accommodation. Her great effort at customer service was explaining how someone in Customer Service "might" give me a gas card for my extra trip - the fourth trip! - if I made yet another trip to pick up the support legs! The customer service in the Tampa store is disgraceful (and very inconsistent with the Ikea philosophy, as I understand it), and I post this as a warning to others NOT to rely on the "expertise" of Ikea employees who tell you "this is all you need" for your purchase.

Return department is very slow, especially during week days after 6 pm. Only one same person is working and he has to manage all the people. No help from management too. Manager says there is no enough people. 2 ppl are working and one is on a lunch- that one person is always on a lunch. The shift ends at 9pm, the question Is: why is the lunch at 8pm?! Lying manager?! Very unprofessional approach.. never met this kind of approach of management in any of the ikeas..

IKEA Case # 41175423 2 BETRODD GAS RANGES WERE REPAIRED by emergency due to smell of  gas flowing from burners because of broken metal knob stem on far left knob. Yes, that is TWO units. Still IKEA messes up the return and credit. It's been 6 Months. Does not return calls or emails. Execs Are IKEA USA also are mute. Don't give Emeryville your $.

This IKEA does not open at 9:30, the restaurant does.
So much for getting in and out.  Thought I'd relax with a cappuccino while I waited. I was the first customer and the machine was out of milk so I had to get my money back.  I would have come at 10 if I knew.

We. Love. IKEA. I have only been to IKEA a few times in Fishers, but it has made furnishing a home and buying little things like wine glasses SO much easier and cheaper!! I just went tonight, two nights before Thanksgiving to pick up some extra wine glasses, plates, drinking glasses.... I got all of it for $27!!!! Yes, you read that right, 27 dollars! I was so ecstatic!!! 

The staff are extremely friendly, and the store is not nearly as confusing to navigate as people may think. There are signs and also arrows on the floor that show you where to go which is extremely helpful. It does take some time if you are planning on walking through the entire store, but there are some shortcuts you can take to get to different sections. 

I think the only thing I was slightly sad about was that in my honest opinion, their Swedish meatballs are too hyped up. ): Major sad face. I was looking forward to trying them for so so long. Don't get me wrong, they were pretty good, but not as great as they are made out to be. The way people have talked about them, I thought they were going to be delicious, they tasted like any other regular Swedish meatballs I've had in my life. Just average. Okay my meatball rant is over. 

IKEA is incredible, just need the patience and time to navigate through it!
Pay for the item. Est pick up was 10min turn out 1hr.  Worst experience ever. Do not buy any pick up item. Not worth it.

Love me some ikea! So happy this place has made it closer than 2.5 hours to me! Ha! Although I'm not a fan of driving to fishers, I find if I go during off hours, it's not a big deal (like after 7pm on weekdays). It's so much more manageable than if you go during the weekends! I made that mistake once. The flow of the store is alright once you figure it out. They have signs everywhere and lights on the floor guiding you where to go but if you wonder off, beware you might end up in a different area! The selection of items changes with the seasons and not much more than that. The cafeteria is nice to have but haven't made my way into it except for drinks only. Again, super busy on the weekend! If you want to cut through and just get to the stuff instead of all the furniture and displays, like myself, you can cut through around section 3 I believe. 

I've purchased many practical items at reasonable prices although I feel some items are way overpriced for what they are.

I went in for one thing on my lunch break from work and had to put it back and leave with nothing because the lines were too long and there were not enough open registers. There was an old man checking people out at a register with a small line and I was told that he was closing it down, and sure enough after he checked out the last 2 people in that line he put a little sign next to the lane and walked away. There were easily 10+ people in each line with multiple items, WHY would you close down more registers? This is almost always a problem when I come here that it takes FOREVER to check out. I used to work in the restaurant industry for a long time and even if "your shift was about to end" or "it was you lunch break" and the restaurant got slammed, you stayed and helped out. I don't understand why people were walking away from registers and nobody was coming to help clear out these long lines. It's kind of ridiculous, the people working here are not very bright. Get it together ikea

So this is our home away from home! My husband and I really love and enjoy going here to look around and get lost while shopping. We absolutely love that are seven-year-old can go in the play area for an hour while we have mom and dad time while shopping. The store is huge and the customer service is excellent! They have a restaurant inside the store, and also an area for nursing moms and families to go in. I've always heard of the store in the past, but once they built the location in Indy I was all about it! We finally tried  there meatballs as they say it is the best! We thought they were OK, but they definitely tied us over until dinner. This really is just a cute family friendly store and everyone leaves out happy. 

Pros
The prices
Decoration
Location
Customer service 
Overall environment 
Kid area 
Food 
Coffee 

Cons 
Sometimes it's hard to find prices on items.

Hi my names Ronald, im currently unemployed for personal reasons. Ive been looking to upgrade my winnebago for some time now and after some weeks worth of research at the local libraries computer I determined that IKEA could be the best place. I caught the transit to the closet one which was about a 5 hour commute. Wow, what a trip there. Lucky for me i was fortunate enough to get a good seat buddy who believe it or not was also going to ikea. Upon arrival i was excited for what was behind the doors. Ive heard great things about ikea. Little did i know it was about to be a fucking living hell. I walk in and im instantly smacked in the face by one of the workers hot ass breath. He couldnt have been more useless. I would compare him to a hot dog vendor at a vegetarian festival. (Pathetic if those exist) anyway, im not on my own in this new continent called ikea. It takes you approximately 2 hours to get to the other end of the store. Im looking for a new end table and a throw rug. Id have a better shot at getting struck by fucking lightening twice at once and then being run over by hyena driving a bulldozer, then finding what im looking for. The stores a shit hole plain out. Cant explain it better. I spent to much money on bus tickets and cola on the way up to come home with nothing. Ive been a disappointment all of my life and now my 4 fucking kids will think im even a bigger hunk of shit. Thanks Ikea. Go fuck yourself

Wow!  Suggestion #1: Come when you can make a day out of the experience; there is sooo much to see!!

Going from room to room throughout this store, I found myself getting lost among the home decor, kitchen utensils, furniture, and anything else you may imagine!  There is just so much to see!

If you are able to make a day of your trip to Ikea, or find yourself visiting over the lunch hour...have no fear!  Their cafeteria area provides plenty of options for meals, snacks, desserts, and drinks!  I honestly didn't know what kind of quality to expect, but I was very impressed!  I had the chicken tender and french fry meal and was very pleased; the portion size was big, the food was warm, and the staff was friendly!

I don't know what more one could want from a place that has everything with very reasonable prices!  I honestly think this is just one place you have to see to believe!!

Definitely plan a trip to Fishers to check out IKEA!

Now I didn't actually go into the store proper but I did order something online and goto the store and pick it up. This process was seamless. Tons of parking, employees available to grab my item. Too easy, I hate shopping so if I goto a store I want in and out quick and they delivered:)
Stay away!  Check out lines so long that people are abandoning their carts.  No one available to help load large items. I won't be back.

This particular Ikea has one of the worst return/exchange departments I have ever experienced.
I arrived on Sunday morning around 11:15am to return a purchase. There were only 2 people working the return/exchange area. Meanwhile, there are 14 of us waiting in line. Then one of the associates turned her back to the people waiting and was applying stickers to items on the counter behind her, which took her 15 minutes. Why wasn't someone behind the counter applying the stickers?! 
Neither associate had any sense of urgency.
This process needs to be reengineered.

This review is for IKEA in general. Absolutely ridiculous customer service and care. 
We ordered a loveseat and sofa and were told the furniture would come December 8th. We never got an email confirmation so 3 days later we called and were told no order existed. Turns out they had "difficulties"with their black friday coupon which, erased all orders. So we made another order, fine, delivery was this past weekend.. it never came. I called today and was told our order was blocked due to partial payment when, in fact, my card was charged the full amount. Now we cant get delivery until after Christmas due to more "difficulties". Ive been on hold for an hour now.
This was my first experience with IKEA and likely my last.

Restaurant review: Best and least expensive breakfast, lunch and dinners. Neat trolley carts to carry trays on. Food is wonderful and very fresh. Spent 5 hours talking with friends and by the time we were ready to leave, lunch was ready

I absolutely love this place. The decorum and staged rooms always want to make me remodel every space in my house. 
Most of the smaller items, kitchenwares and things are very reasonably priced and of good quality. I found their furniture to be cute but seems a bit cheap as you knock on a table or sit in a chair or doesn't seem like it would hold up well. 
The beds and couches all seem to be extremely low. 

Now to the food... 
The cafeteria is quite heavenly. Even the fountain water tastes extra clean and delicious.  A deliciously fresh breakfast of crepes and potatoes for $2 is unbeatable. I've never had anything here that tastes fake or processed. I've attended two of their special event buffets and although everything on the menu isn't for my palette it's always made with quality. 
I really appreciate that the kitchen staff seems to take pride in what they do, they are friendly, efficient, and true culinarians.  
You can't ever visit IKEA without getting some meatballs, gravy and ligonberry sauce. It really completes the Swedish experience.

My only actual dislike is that no matter how many times you go, you seem to get lost trying to find your way out. There's been times I've wanted to buy things but because they only have one exit to where you have to go around the entire huge store and go through the warehouse just to get to the checkout, I have passed.  I really wish they would allow you to go out of the door just past that kid area with your merchandise to get to the checkout without hassle.

I want to start by saying before this experience I truly had great experiences at ikea and this experience blind sided me to say the least. I ordered online the kitchen play set for my son through the click and collection option. I live in Reading, PA and the closest IKEA to me is the one in Conshohocken, but they did not have any in stock  so I was unable to choose the click and collect option for my closest location. I was understanding that it is the holiday and this item seems to be very popular so I was willing to get it from the second closest location,  which is the IKEA in south Philadelphia which is 1:30 hours away from me. My order was processed at 10:00am and I was able to set the pick up right away. I was super excited so I decided to drive up as soon as I was able to. After driving an hour and a half I was informed by the click and collect associate that my order will be canceled because this item was out of inventory. I informed the representative that I had driven an hour and a half and I had not received any notification advising me that the order was canceled. Well apparently she said what she had to say and that's it no I apologize for the inconvenience let me see if we can do something since IKEA made the mistake not me. Despite being really upset I was trying to be optimistic and decided to see if maybe I could get something else for him instead . So I go to the kid section and I find this really cute craft table that has bins in the center to hide toys, but it did not have a price tag. So I ask an associate if she could assist me because I was interested in finding out how much was the cost. Well the associate advise me that ikea was self served and asked me if I was aware of that. I advised her that I was however since the item did not have a tag I would not be able to locate it in the lower level before check out. She advised me that she was putting tags out in her department and that i will have to wait a while before she can help me or the other customer that was behind me. She states well in that case just take a picture of the table and show a representative at the lower level and they can look it up for you. I have worked in retail all my life so I am aware how overwhelming it can be during the holidays. However customer service should never suffer especially when the store is not busy at all. I will not be returning to this IKEA EVER!! And I will not be using click and collect again.
Their meatballs & everything else in their restaurant is fantastic!However they are pricey especially after you have to wait "in line" for your food!

TOO BIG! My god is it too big! They need teams or golf carts or something to get through the place. I get that it's a European store and Europeans walk everywhere, but seriously I'd like bike rentals or frequent seating and rehydration stations. You could die of thirst before you're halfway through here. And the end of the store! Oh my god! You know that final scene from Raiders of the Lost Arc when they're putting it in the endless warehouse? DING DING DING! Pretty sure your face could melt if you open the wrong wingding couch or flipflop table in the warehouse!

I love Ikea! Anything you could ever need is here AND affordable AND comes with a name you probably can't pronounce but you probably know that already if you're here. Anyway in this particular Ikea today, my dad got TOO excited about his Swedish meatballs in the cafeteria and dropped his tray right by the checkout. My family reacted in horror- DROPPED MEATBALLS! A PUBLIC SPECTACLE! SHAME SHAME SHAME! But the employees efficiently cleaned it up and got him squared away with new meatballs and were so nice about it. 
My only complaint is that it's a little ~breezy~ from the air running in the caf so the food chills quickly and then you might start eating like a speed eating champ, but it's no biggie when you're sitting in IKEA and there are so many chairs just waiting to be tested and drawers begging to be opened, wouldn't want to get stuck in the caf too long anyway. 
Also lingonberry yuuuuum.

The food was a huge letdown.  Nothing was stocked no salads no dessert a few hot items out also.  Lady working was aggressive rude like a robot.  Food was cold glasses were dirty lady taking money hates her job.  No one not one employee seemed like they like their job.  Waited in line to check out for 5-10 minutes.  Nothing really on sale it was a very disappointing trip

Ordered several items online. Received only 4 of 14 boxes listed on the delivery receipt. There was no notification of backordered items or any communication related to our order. Tried calling 888 number but only get a fast busy signal. Tried to submit issue via IKEA's website but it won't allow me to submit the form. Now what? So I have to drive 50 miles to the St. Louis store to get this resolved? Namaste.

I prefer to give good reviews, however, I will give bad reviews when warranted.  I like IKEA overall but their stock levels have been sub par.  We went there to find a desk for our son.  After showing him the pictures of it, he also liked the desk and wanted us to get it.  I went back to the store, got the location of the desk to pick up and then went to grab an LED light for the desk as well.  Both the LED light and the desk were out of stock.  Shame on me for not looking online to see if they show stock levels of the items they sell.  After a wasted trip, I decided to do just that, check online.  They showed the desk would be back in stock the following Saturday.  Guess what, Saturday came and went and no stock.  This went on for several weeks so we have decided not to shop at IKEA and we will buy items for our home elsewhere!

Every time I come through this store they only have three or four registers open and lines backed up forever. I complained about it multiple times and they never ever change otherwise this ikea is fine.

Purchased a package of cinnamon buns on 12/30/18. Our child ate one before we noticed the date stamp on the package of "APR 05/18." Our hope is that the date is in error but it proved impossible to actually speak with anyone from the store on the phone to get any clarification. After 25 minutes trying to reach the store via IKEA's 888 number, we gave up. Unbelievable that a customer can't actually speak with a store employee via phone. Incompetence all around.

So breakfast was decent and unbelievably priced at $2 for scrambled eggs, sausage, diced potatoes, & a Swedish crepe. Added on a latte for $1. With hunger at bay and a morning caffeine kick, I was ready to score some items I'd been eyeing online.

    Layout of every IKEA feels chaotic & this location is no different. I did appreciate that this location had a parking garage that I didn't notice til I'd parked & run in through the rain!

    Was looking for a display case and had two models in mind. Quickly realized I'd left my wall space measurements at home hours away(‍). Sooo... there went the display case plan for today. Also need to drive my mini van for larger item pick up. I clearly came with a plan of taking a display case home but not all of the lil details in hand. Wasn't willing to pay the delivery cost. In fact, I'm betting I can find a similar piece on Amazon with Prime delivery.

     Onto my next mission of a kids kitchen and accessories to donate to a local charity. Also a toy storage shelving unit with lidded slide in drawers for same charity. I gathered the kitchen accessories quickly enough and took photos of the tag for the kitchen & storage piece. Unfortunately at the item pick up warehouse area, the kitchen showed as out of stock until January. Would've been nice if IKEA posted  large signage to this effect right on the display toy kitchens so we'd have known much earlier & would've left the store sooner! The storage piece was in stock but it took 20 minutes to find the right bins...& despite 200+ bins stacked up, there sat ONE lid. So back all of that went. 

     We did indeed save $ (spent 10% of what we'd planned to spend)by attempting to shop IKEA... but only because of out of stock items & putting a storage piece back due to no lids for the containers needed. After this chaotic & frustrating waste of hours of time I think I'll stick to Amazon Prime or Wayfair for free shipping on similar wished for items. 

    We did get inexpensive small juice glasses, flatware sets a friend asked me to pick up, two kids memory match games, a clearance napkin holder, and small items that added up to $35 or so. Upon exiting we learned that the IKEA shopping carts don't fit between parked cars to go through and get to your vehicle. We had to park the cart & carry the glassware & items aisles away in the lot to our car. Last straw for my husband who isn't an IKEA fan to begin with! 

Adios, IKEA.
Exceptionally good cafeteria food at reasonable prices. The Swedish meatballs are the best.

Please IKEA just close smaland. It opens late, it is short staffed and only accommodates 6 children before the waitlist is implemented. If you can not provide the service then just shut it down. I ended up with three crying children because they could not go play. It makes the shopping experience worse than if it was just permanently closed.

Usually I love this store and it's a great experience. However tonight there was a woman working in the self serve area and I had an item that said you had to ask an associate to get. There was a woman in a striped yellow and blue shirt and vest standing at the computer. She was with another customer. As I stood there waiting for a few minutes, I realized that she and the woman were scrolling through their photo albums on their phones as I heard "look isn't he cute" and "oh now look at this one". I said "hello is anyone else working". The employee looked up at me, rolled her eyes and said "I'm working" like how dare I interrupt her friend time. I said "okay are you available" and she completely ignored me, looked back at her friend and said "okay so what were we looking at". I walked away without purchasing the item.  I did purchase something else and Deja was the cashier. She was extremely nice and helpful. I'm not going to name the woman that was  rude but she had curly hair and was the only one I saw working at the self serve area on January 4. Maybe this could be an opportunity for a customer service training.
Great selection and great prices. Store is clean. The food is very good. They need more checkout lanes in cafeteria and in warehouse. Lines are long and slow.
This has nothing to do with this specific store. It is ikea.com. Do yourself a favor and don't order home delivery. It is a nightmare.

Well I just made my second visit here and it is so large it may take several more to figure out where all the items are. They do have a map of sorts which is more like a European subway sign with stops in each of the areas. I was looking at options for a new house and in a way there is almost too many good things here. I am certain I could solve many furnishing issues here. The prices seem very reasonable compared to almost any other option. I reviewed the full size wardrobes which are very customization. The build quality seems quite good for the price as well. I didn't yet buy any furnishings but picked up some of the breakfast rolls and took advantage of the restaurant for dinner. I would even recommend going here just to eat at the restaurant which offers very good food at excellent prices. I had something that wasn't on the official board which was BBQ pork chops. They were very tasty. They seem to serve food much healthier than other places as it came with steemed vegetables and rice with some healthy items added to it am guessing quinoa. I of course had to try the apple pie. This is definitely not american apple pie, not nearly as sweet. Probably also much more healthy. I also love the drink assortment which features most likely the only ligonberry drink in Indiana. Of note they offer what appeared to be two design centers in the store with staff to assist in configurations of kitchens and also offices. The kitchens looked pretty nice very modern and european. The other interesting thing is their spaces that show the furnishings are neat too look at but also very european focused most configurations show how to make the most of very small apt and or condo like spaces. I would have liked to see a more US type design for a large bedroom and or living room.

Ikea is the place to go if you are bored, need to buy stuff, or just want to walk around.
