I had to run to Ikea to get some small items. I have heard they have a new Veggie hot dog, and I was a bit hungry so i had to try it. For 0.75 cent why not? 

The hot dog is not your normal hot dog it was all mashed up but it tasted very good! I really enjoyed it! But they forgot the cabbage... I only got fried onion. 

I recommend people to try it!

I absolutely love Ikea. The staff are friendly and helpful, their return policy is excellent and the process is easy when a return is needed, and they have tons of great furniture and household accessories. 
I remember it was quite a nightmare on opening day for this location because TONS of people showed up. It was difficult to park and the place was packed. My family swore they'd never come back. It took a bit of convincing, but we came back. Now that it's been a while, all that hype has died down and the place isn't so packed and busy. It was easy to navigate around to where we were going and we didn't have to wait too long in line. 
I am certain we will be back anytime we're in the market for new, quality furniture.

For some, IKEA is a shoppers' paradise, a haven of Swedish designed goods. This furniture Mecca boasts hundreds of designed rooms sure to pleasure the fancy of any aesthetically inclined urban dweller. There's a style for every type of consumer and prices to match. Walk through the store and instantly you can imagine your life as a young professional, newlywed couple, growing family, or retired. Stop by the cafe and grab dinner. With a giant basemant gift store you can get lost in. 

To others, IKEA is the seventh layer of hell, Satan's throne room, and birthplace of Antichrist. Maneuvering this labyrinth is no task for the weary with a path only Indian Jones could fully map. To dissenters, "designed in Sweden" is a cruel joke; wrapped neatly inside cardboard is a mess of parts made in a factory packed within a smoggy Chinese industrial city. If you are able to make it through checkout before your dehydration kicks in, you'll be greeted by a scrambled loading zone. Complete that task and may God have mercy on your soul because when you get back to your abode and begin the process of unpacking your newly purchased Swedish furniture, you will hate yourself for ever setting out on the venture. 

IKEA is like Donald Trump, a good idea hidden behind cheap tricks, composite cardboard, and Elmer's glue. Put it together yourself and don't ask questions when it falls apart.

Good lord I did not need this store in my life; my wallet hates me now. I needed a narrow bookshelf, but I HAVE to see something in person before I buy. So off to IKEA I went, dragging my boyfriend who's been there before so he could keep me on track. Well he didn't. I came home with a bookshelf, 6 throw pillows, a new set of curtains, an orchid, and a bromeliad. Did I need all that? Nope. Did my boyfriend approve of all that? Nope. Does my credit card like that? Well I guess the cash back will be nice. But did I get what I came for? Yup! My only complaint really was they had 3 registers open so the lines were long even mid-afternoon on a Thursday, and downstairs at the bistro only one person was working so that line was pretty long too. But try the cinnamon buns there! I bought my boyfriend three to make him shut up each time he started to say I didn't need something.
No complaints about IKEA. I love coming here when there's nothing going on. Furniture, decor, food and hot cinnamon buns on a Sunday afternoon....yes please!

The wine got me nice before the meal I had fish and chips wish I asked for an extra dip the wine was nice tho then I got the butter chicken it was great but the wine was better overall I highly recommended ikea as a fine dining establishment make sure you get the white wine tho

Worst in-store customer service ever. The "coworkers" are not willing to help you out. The lady who was supposed to look for a product, which they should have 18 in stock according to the website, never got back to us during our 30-minute wait. A guy who we asked for help after kept saying "there should be someone to help you at the desk" when we repeatedly told him that we saw no one at the desk.

Why have I not been to Ikea until now??!! It is the Mecca of all that is affordable,  stylish, and modern.  Despite its grandeur it's very spread out which is great for a person like me that feels overwhelmed by stores that are crammed so tight you can't move around freely.  Of course it was hard to narrow down what project I wanted to work on and buy first.  The restaurant area is very clean and the food is amazing and affordable.  I really appreciate how family friendly the entire place is with nursing rooms and family bathrooms as well as the children's play area where you can drop kids off for a bit while you shop!

It is Ikea...so what can I say about it. Fun place to go for a cheap date (can't compare the $2.50 breakfast and walk around the furniture). Good place to bring pent up kids for their free play place...and go on a cheap date for meatballs and sparkling Swedish water upstairs.  Good if you are on a budget. I really have not much to say about the furniture. Simple concept, good on a budget, and if you don't kill your spouse during the put together of the furniture I will say it is a bonding experience. My teenager loves Ikea. So she had a bed building party with her friends, and I bought a bunch of food from Ikea for them to eat after they were done. And I love their food area. I love their meatballs, their salmon, their sparkling water, and their sweets. Also their exchange policy isn't so bad either. It is not where I would go to get iconic pieces to pass down to my family, but really for book shelves, throw rugs, etc. why wouldn't you pay for cheap and have it switch once in awhile?
2 hours. 2 hours from the time we got into the check out line, and the time we left. I've never seen a more disorganized, chaotic place in my life.

I feel like I have a love/hate relationship with IKEA. I love the fact that everything is so affordable. I especially enjoy purchasing trendy pieces at IKEA since normally I'll only be using said items for a season and it definitely won't break the bank. Recently, different events have been added to showcase how some of their products can be utilized in your home. This is perfect for individuals who have a hard time visualizing. I mean we all have our day with this skill. 

Another huge win, FREE COFFEE. Who doesn't love having a warm bev while shopping? 

The downside for me: I can't stand how crowded it seems to always be when I want to just run in for a few items. I understand this is a destination for some and is a great thing for IKEA. I get it - totally not their fault!

So we usually come in for food then shop around but today we're in line and see a roach so brazen it's crawling around the food trays being served with plenty of people around. My guess is that it's not its first time out and about and I also wouldn't be surprised if it's got friends.

We think that because it's a furniture store first, this IKEA doesn't get taken very seriously on its health inspections or maybe they're just a bit more seldom than a full-fledged restaurant. Whatever it may be I think we'll start getting our food outside before we dive into the 'protein- fortified' offerings at this IKEA.

It's IKEA people. I mean, who doesn't like IKEA? Even a hardcore interior designer can find something they want here. The prices are great and the value is too. I love all the sample spaces - they really make you realize how you can use different items in your own home.  Plus all the employees are helpful and friendly.

My second time here. I do and I don't like this place. It is so crowded. So many rude customers here. Sometimes I think I am invisible in this Powerchair. People run right into me without saying sorry or anything. Anyway, I do like it because you can get things that are different from any other stores. So many neat gift ideas at great prices. They have really cool refrigerators for $1800.00 and I like it as well as the one I saw at Costco or Sam's for $6,000.00. It has a great warranty too. We got track lighting for my music room and for our living room. Saved a lot of money. If you want something different it's a great place to shop. If you are impatient-stay away! lol

Have you ever eaten at an IKEA? I'm not talking the ice cream cones or shitty little hot dogs on the way out. Which I happen to like both of those. I'm talking up in the cafeteria. 
So the food isn't going to knock your socks off. What Ikea has is value. So for instance I got a salmon and vegetable platter for $6.99. My wife got veggie meatballs, vegetables and some sort of rice for $3.99. These aren't happy meals either. There is enough food there to feed an average height/weight adult. 
If you like all you can eat buffets, this place isn't going to do it for you. Drive 2 hours to Shady Maple. 
The food is pretty good in its own right. Like I said nothing that you'll taste and be like AMAZING. I mean the only other places that have foot this cheap are fast food joints and that stuff is terrible for you. My salmon dinner only had 470 Calories. 

Anyway if your in there and it's around feeding time you should check it out. You don't want to die saying you've never tried it.

This is our go to place for storage, curtains, seasonal items, bath mats, lighting...and cool thingys. F and I usually come here first and check out all the interesting decor. This is where we get ideas. We recently purchased the Pax closet system... I absolutely love it. It has totally reorganized my bedroom. We also were able to add on as we needed.
The service has always been helpful and friendly, too.

Good luck trying to get an associate to help you here... smh ‍ walked around for at least 50 minutes with nobody around to help. Then went to customer service and was still left with disappointment. Not worth the trouble. Save your time and shop elsewhere

Bunch of flimsy junk I like mcm.
I feel like a rat in a maze when I'm there if I was 20 something and just bought my first apartment I will probably like it

I'd never been to an IKEA before one was built in Fishers, but boy did I hear raving reviews from all of my friends who would drive to Ohio to go to one. I've now been to this IKEA 3 times (most recently last Friday evening) and am still amazed at the sheer size of this place. WOW! Come with no agenda for time unless you know exactly what you want and where to find it in the store. We spent a good 2 hours going through the place even with something in mind for we wanted to get just so we could peruse the displays for decorating ideas. The prices for furniture are pretty affordable, but I'd say the price for bedding, pillows (decorative) and home decor are comparable (not cheaper) to Target and similar stores. They didn't have lighting in stock we wanted, but I guess we can order it online. The 4 stars are for the the loooooonggggggg check out lines- there were 12ish people in line to check out at 2 lanes when there were 10+ lanes in the store. They should have had more people to check out customers, especially on a Friday evening when inevitably it will be busier than say a Tuesday afternoon. Each of the 3 times I've come here we have to wait in a long line with minimal check out staff. The lines didn't move at snail speed, but by the point you check out you've probably been in the store a few hours and are ready to pay and leave. Still love coming here! Just wish the line situation would be remedied.

My father and I had the worst experience earlier this afternoon. The lady serving at the lunch line was so rude and it completely ruined our lunch. They need to hire employees that are a little more pleasant and don't have an attitude!
They never have enough staff to checkout people. Returns and exchanges has 3 people and all the checkouts there are only four people. That is ridiculous. They should have a 5 items or less line.

Only the second time we have been here. It is neat how you are guided through the store and through different room setups. Pretty busy place but things are easy to find and numbered for locating in the furniture area.  Can be a bit crazy at checkout but you don't come here if you are not expecting a little crazy.  The food court has some ok offerings. You have to get the meatballs right!?

Normally this location is great. Even when busy, it's manageable, unlike the Philadelphia location. 

They staff the checkout lanes fairly well, even the cafe lines move quickly. 

This store is under a total remodel. I wish they would have had signs out about the lack of stock prior to wasting an hour there looking at a total of 4 beds and a couple of couches. Almost every area is closed off with a remodel sign. 

One perk to the remodeling..... lots of things are on clearance right now. So if you're looking for a new couch or bed frame... they have them for 50% off.

I'm looking forward to seeing the new products and layouts.

This store has a terrible problem with inventory. From keeping items in stock to having accurate counts, it's been a disaster. We've shopped Ikea frequently since it opened in Fishers, but with such consistently poor experiences at this location, I think it's best if we start ordering online instead. On top of the inventory issues, most of the lower tier customer service is unfriendly and goes against standard customer-friendly policy, until upper tier management is involved. Overall, I really dread going to this location now but I thoroughly enjoy Ikea products.

Not ashamed to say Ikea has become one of my new favorite weekend errands! I love strolling the showrooms, digging through the clearance, and enjoying cheap and delicious food (.75 veggie dogs!!). As a perk, Ikea family members get free coffee and tea as well.
This store is in great shape with friendly staff. They accept returns without questions and work hard to make things right

We finally made it to the new IKEA! It's a nice location and maneuverability in and out, parking was easy. After having been to the Schaumburg location, I was a little disappointed here. Granted it has been several years since I was there and IKEA May have changed a bit  but I much more liked the multiple floors than the one floor layout. We were confused from the minute we stepped in the door. No good way to find out where to go or how it worked unless we completely missed it. The room displays were nice to look at at first but my were there a lot of them. I liked the latter part of walking thru the store/products and being able to pick up what you want to buy. Having to remember the aisle and location of multiple items to find at the end in the warehouse part wasn't super easy or helpful time wise. My husband picked up an online order for a friend while I waited in a long line to checkout. Online pickup went really well! Just to note: you have to buy a bag if you want a bag at the end to carry your stuff out. Or I suppose you may be able to take one in with you too.
Management needs to be fired. On Presidents' Day they only had six of the 20 checkout lanes staffed and open.  Over 100 people in line.

I love IKEA. I started going to IKEA in Schaumburg and I'm pleased to have one closer to home, but I like the Schaumburg floor plan better. Of course they have great furniture, unique designs many of which specialize in making the most efficient use of a small space, but I'm going to talk about their food!

This weekend I went for lunch. I was craving Swedish meatballs. I'm currently eating low carb, so I got meatballs, salad, and a drink. Eight meatballs with the wonderful creamy gravy and there's a salad bar with a nice mix of greens, carrots, cucumbers, and cheese. A small selection of fresh ingredients. It was wonderful and so incredibly affordable. It's worthwhile going to IKEA only for the meatballs - and the people watching.

They've got a chilled salmon salad that's tasty an if you're not eating low carb, I love the lingonberry preserves! It's sweet and tart complementing the rest of the meal.

The front of the store has a food counter with super cheap hot dogs and cinnamon rolls. The hot dogs make a great lunch on the go and a cinnamon roll with coffee really hits the spot at a certain time of the afternoon on a cold rainy day.

They've got a small food mart in the front of the store. I've bought the frozen meatballs with packets of sauce mix for years. It's wonderful and tastes the same as the restaurant. They sell jars of lingonberry preserves, which is wonderful to have at home. They have cookies, ginger thins, crisp little cookies with variations on gingerbread flavor that are great with coffee or tea. 

Bookshelves, yeah, and great food.

The company IKEA uses to deliver orders damaged our floors during delivery, the drivers forged my signature on the delivery paperwork and our claim was denied to have the damage covered because their claim department said the signatures looked "not exactly the same, but similar." All attempts to speak with someone directly about the claim failed and the company pushed our claim onto the insurance carrier of the drivers themselves. We've heard nothing back. The estimate for the damage the drivers caused was $1,300 and THE DRIVERS OPENLY MOCKED US WHEN WE TOLD THEM THEY HAD DAMAGED OUR FLOORS. I am appalled that IKEA uses this company and then takes no responsibility for the irresponsibility of the drivers and the delivery company.

Shopping at IKEA is the most frustrating experience ever!  Store map is confusing, you are corralled through the entire if you are not smart and figure out the map shortcuts, the only person I asked for help getting to the check out line faster gave me attitude "Like why would you want to do that"...  I will never go back in IKEA again...

Some solid value

Meal got a 3 mainly cause the classic Swedish meatballs dish was subpar to be honest. And that gravy just unidentifiable. 
Veggie meatball with tomato was actually pretty good.  
Beet salad with pecan and feta was sold. 
Coffee decent 

Over all, they need to step up that Swedish meatball game. My mom's were wayyyy better and she was a Spaniard. You're Swedish-get it together man
Store is fine but their online website is HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE!!! They need to update their site and make it more user friendly especially when attempting to place an order.

After a lot of chasing the company down, they reconsidered my claim and are paying for the damages their company caused. They were apologetic when I was finally able to reach someone in person. I understand the need to ensure these claims are legitimate, as I'm sure there are scammers out there.
Don't ever try to return anything here. I was charged incorrectly and had to wait over an hour to have it fixed. Terrible service.

Ugh.  Dislike this store.  I don't get why people love it so much.  You are overpaying for particle board garbage.  You might get help from a staffer.  But they were not very knowledgeable on kitchen cabinets.  Ended up going to Lowe's and they were awesome.  Go here if you want to get aggravated.

Have a free afternoon? Head over to Ikea. You can literally spend an entire day there and not see everything. Whether you need silverware, a lamp, a rug or a crib- they have it. We wandered through living spaces of different sizes. We saw how you could have a comfortable living space in 400 sq ft unbelievable as that sounds. Headboards, kitchen cabinets, plates and utensils. Then just as you tire, you see the restaurant/ cafeteria. They have a small selection of salads sandwiches and desserts but the star is the Swedish meatballs. The meatball plate is comprised of meatballs, mashed potatoes, a cranberry compote and a vegetable. Everything was delicious except for the mashed up veggies which were Overcooked and cold. Will definitely be back for the meatballs which you can apparently buy frozen as well. Then on to the patio furniture and the "as is" section. Next rainy day,head on over and plan to spend a couple of hours wandering around before heading off for some Swedish meatballs.

I love IKEA. Just not this store. The lines at the restaurant, the bistro and the checkout are incredibly long and slow every time we go. Additionally,  I think they must have a stocking problem because at least half of the items I want to purchase are always out of stock. For instance, I've been trying to buy a couch from this location  for a month. They still don't have all the required parts in stock. I think we are going to purchase elsewhere because the wait has been far too long.
One worker in returns with 10 people waiting, it may be faster to travel to Sweden to return this stuff. Why does it take 20 minutes for each transaction? How do you say "you suck" in swedish?

Solid place with great food! Have a kids area, dining zone, too many checkouts that are usually unoccupied, many areas with a variety of home decorations ranging from wine glasses to TV stands- a critical need. Service was quiet, not exactly being rude or nice, just doing their job. They had a escalator, another critical need. They had a floor like the ones you see in a warehouse, but it was somewhat clean. This was overall pretty good for a superstore. If you need furniture this is the place to be

The store is a bit overwhelming, but it's an "experience". The prices are amazing and my favorite area is the kitchen stuff and Swedish food products. I think the home furnishings is not the best quality, but it looks good and may be affordable to many. Cheap place to take your family for dinner and the food is better than McDonalds or MCL.

Seriously folks if you come here to buy furniture you better be some kind of college student  on a shoestring budget or just a fool because it's not necessarily cheap and you have to put all the crap together with instructions that will drive you mad!!! LOL But they do have some great organizational items that are much more competitively priced than the container store .That said don't expect any customer service at this place because it's horrendous. I live almost an hour and a half away from this place and the lady that tried to help me (not too bright )looked like she hated her job. Must be they don't pay too much at this place!

First, I love IKEA...really do! The inspirational annual catalogs, the inexpensive household basics, the general emphasis on simple design... I've been a fan for 20 years and have visited IKEAs in Illinois, Michigan, Ohio, and New York, so I was thrilled when an Indiana location opened last year. 

Unfortunately, the Fishers/Indy location was a huge disappointment.  

1) The floorplan. This single-story IKEA is woefully confusing to navigate. As a shopper who had a general idea what to expect, I still felt totally lost. 
2) Haphazard labeling of shelves/prices. Literally DOZENS of times, I struggled to figure out which items were on what shelf at which price. The hand-drawn arrows on the shelving labels only confirmed: others have shared my confusion. 
3) Inventory out of stock. Empty shelves. On a Tuesday afternoon, I expected the store to feel calm and orderly. Instead, it felt forlorn and randomly picked-over. 

The staff I interacted with were all extremely professional... but the general disarray and unwelcoming ambiance left a sour taste. I'll probably try this location again at some point, but I'm not excited to do so...which is sad.

IKEA is a great place to get some steps in if you're into that kind of thing. I love IKEA, I just recommend that you try to go during the week instead of the weekend when it can get pretty crowded. Inevitably you will end up behind someone slow and you'll be trapped in the maze of IKEA forever or for what seems like forever.

I actually enjoy the maze of IKEA and if you visit here often enough you'll get to know the layout of the store so you can buzz through the shortcuts if you feel like it. If you just feel like browsing you can walk through all the decorated rooms. I like to look at all the bedrooms and kitchens - it's very inspiring and I leave with a ton of decorating ideas that even if I don't implement them immediately, still influence me in all my creative endeavors.

I've eaten at the restaurant many times and I find it to be pretty good most of the time and excellent sometimes. It's convenient and inexpensive if you're shopping.

The checkouts can be kind of aggravating - crowded and backed up a lot of the time when it is busy - all the more reason to go when it's slow - weekday mornings. 

My new favorite thing about IKEA is the fabric - I'm a sewist/seamstress and their cottons and linens are attractive and very reasonably priced. They also have a couple of prints that are 18th century accurate, if you're into costume making or reproduction dressmaking.

And of course, the dreariest part of IKEA is that you have to put your own furniture together - but I just got a great price on some cubby shelves and they actually go together pretty quickly.
Three lanes open on Sunday? Will not be going back.literally waited almost 45 minutes in line.

I had the worst experience, JUST BECAUSE I AM ASIAN ' i was treated differently and the cashier told me the line was closed!! And asked us moved to different line but when "not asian person " there suddenly line was open and she taking care of her , hopefully her manager or supervisor give her better training at her job as cashier!! Thank you ikea for such nice experience..,,not!
Why did I waste my time here. 26 check out lanes and only 3 open. I counted at least 100 people in line. What a joke. What horrible service. Never ever returning.

I give IKEA 5 stars because I just like it. There's always something to see!  I like when they change up their spaces or host kids events!  And the restaurant area is perfect for s full meal or light snack!  

We personally go just to walk around sometimes and get some steps in!  Walk around for inspiration or just to get the kids out of the house on a rainy day!  If the kids play place is full, walk to the kids area and let them blow off some steam there - and let them hold a stuffed animal of their choice until it's time to go!  

Enjoy!

Solid IKEA location. Easy to find and pretty well stocked. Their kitchen and dining area is always packed to the brim with people on the weekends, so plan for that. 

Clean and well organized. The staff is knowledgeable and friendly. This is our go to ikea for the Tampa Bay area.
Furniture pickup for PAX closet stuff if AWFUL!  Just waited an hour for them to pull 3 pieces.  Seriously IKEA...get your act together!

I am so happy that there is an IKEA in the Indianapolis area. My family and I made a trip from the west side to buy stuff for our new home, and we were not disappointed! We had a ton of help ordering a sectional, even when a piece we needed was not available. Although it was super busy it was easy to navigate and we found everything else on our list without any problems. As always, we stopped for lunch in the cafeteria, and the Swedish meatball meal was amazing! So many good places to eat in Fishers but I was completely content eating here. IKEA truly has it all! We can't wait to get our sectional and hopefully we will be impressed with the delivery service as well.

Love this ikea food is great and always very clean like others! We love the play area for our littles they enjoy it very much! The return section always has a ton of items to choose from and the employees have always been nice and courteous! The only downside is the lines are long every time. I would suggest more front cashiers.

I have to say that I am surprised that I have to give them such a low grade. They were great until something went wrong. I purchased one of their storage beds. I worked closely with their customer service person down by the aisles  and bins.   You forgot to tell me to spend $10 on buying a support beam that is essential to the bed. I called customer service because the support beam doesn't even have a part number but it is in the instruction booklet. When I tried to call to find out why such a thing could happen there was nobody who can talk to you. You call corporate and they tell you call the store. You call the store and you are directed to corporate.This is very very poor customer service. How do you sell somebody a $500 bed and not tell him to take home all the parts? And then nobody to talk to. I am done with them.

This is only my 2nd time to an IKEA.  If you are going I suggest comfortable shoes and clothes! 
Upon entering you will see maps and if you've never been I suggest you take a map.  The place is set up on 2 floors.  I found walking thru to be like a maze. The second floor has all the furniture and it's all set up like rooms.  The furniture here is more reasonably priced because you purchase it, take it home yourself and assemble it yourself.  I'm not sure how good the quality is but if you're on a budget I'm sure you could find something here. 

The first floor is all household goods.  The amount of things available was mind blowing.  The prices are all very reasonable. I'm pretty sure if you need it they have it and then some.  

They offer a childcare center where you can drop off your children while you shop. It's conveniently located right when you walk into the store. Next to the childcare center is a wall of free lockers for your convenience.  You can also eat here.  I didn't but I saw that they have a food court with lots of options.  IKEA really makes it very convenient for you to shop in their store!  

This store is conveniently located near downtown Tampa.  The parking lot is huge so make sure you park near the doors or you may have a long walk to get into the store.  

I went during the week and it was very quiet with no lines to wait on. I highly recommend going during the week if at all possible.  

 Everything in this store is labeled. If you decide to purchase anything large you will need to write down or take a picture of the aisle number and bin number. On the first floor you will see signs directing you to an area where you will pick up your boxed items you wish to purchase.  You will look for the Aisle and then the bin.  If you are purchasing furniture you will need a truck big enough to transport your purchase home.

Come comfy, hungry, and ready to walk !!

Today was my first time going to IKEA and I fell in love at the entrance. The store is set up with mini showcase areas that feature specific styles of how you can decorate your home. 
I loved the setup of the store because you get to see how you can decorate your home in case you aren't great in putting things together that would look good. And with that being said, I thought that IKEA would be INSANELY expensive, but everything in the store is definitely affordable which is hard to believe because.... it's IKEA. 
Aside from the showrooms, I was so eager to try their Swedish meatballs that everyone talks about. I tried the meatball meal and it was very decent and the chocolate cake was very good (I love chocolate cake). The cake tasted like it was made with coffee in it and I assume that it brings the chocolate out. 
All in all I loved IKEA and I will be going back very very soon!! If any of you decide to go, definitely wear comfy clothes, shoes, and have plenty of energy!!!

Made the mistake of buying from ikea. Waiting 30 minutes to pick up a piece of furniture. The workers were rude and none helpful. They didn't have a care in the world and didn't care they were wasting my Sunday. I will never buy from here again. Things I have bought in the past have fell apart as well.
I will not be shopping at IKEA again, thanks to the cafeteria cashiers at this IKEA. They are exceptionally rude, especially the older man named Richard.

I've been going to this Ikea since it's been open. I love Ikea in general, but I'm not fond of this location. This location seems to be out of stock often on certain items, so it's sometimes hard to get something that you need at that time. The check out lines are horrible. No matter what time of day there is always limited lines. Don't go here wanting to buy a few items, because it will take you 30 minutes to get through the lines. I would call in advance to see if your item is in stock before going. I would also wait till you have multiple items that you want, so you don't have to make multiple trips and wait in forever in their lines.

I went to the Swedish Easter Paskbord April 5th, 2019 which is IKEA's periodic swedish smorgasbord buffet at their restaurant.  I have been several times over the past few years at different times of the year for their smorgasbord events and the food was fantastic and professionally presented.  They would have a huge buffet laid out.  It's kind of weird eating a "fancy" buffet at IKEA.  The place was always packed.

However, something happened. On April 5th we went again and there was hardly anyone there.  There was no buffet...you went through the regular line and and the servers dished up pretty much the standard fair which wasn't even as good as their normal food. It was embarrassing really.  Someone in management, maybe only at the IKEA in Conshohocken, decided the full spread and better food was a not worth the effort, or a money looser.  So be it.  Won't be going there anymore.

This huge all in one store and warehouse sells all kinds of furniture and housewares.
The second floor of the building is a showroom 
and the first floor is a self serve warehouse.
You make note of price and location of an item,
then you find it in an isle on a rack in the 
warehouse section. All self serve. Most items have
to be put together. The smaller houseware items
can be taken in shopping carts.
They have everything to inexpensively furnish 
a home, apartment, rental property,, or a college
dorm.  There is even a kitchen center to design and build a new kitchen.
The prices are very good for the housewares and
furniture. But you need to do all the work concerning the furniture. I had put together several
pieces of furniture for my sons apartment.  It
assembles well. Once you complete one item,
they all go together the same.
I would recommend using the map they provide when entering the store. The showroom section
is literally a maze.  Parking is now problem. 
There is a loading dock for your vehicle.

The parts of the store are laid out in an interesting way.  Nice balance of staged sample rooms and showroom-style layouts.  Some of the assembled pieces were noticeably wobbly or wonky, making me wonder about the build quality.  

The cafeteria is really nice... really good food!  The Swedish meatballs are awesome, as expected, and so are the veggie balls.  The chicken strips and fries were both crunchy and satisfying.  The blueberry cheesecake they had available was excellent.

I come here often. You can beat the cheap prices from anything from forks, bathroom mats, couches and plants. Everything is reasonably priced & pretty decent quality. I've purchased casserole dishes, pillows, pillow cases, plants, vases, picture frames, bookshelves and rugs. I love this place.
Three floors full of home shopping amazingness! Restaurant and child care stop the madness

I went  to the location looking for a bed for my daughter,they have a very nice selection of things for kids as well as alot of beautiful decorations for your house.I love the prices they are very reasonable it's almost like a 1 stop shop.

So of course Ikea is the greatest place ever! I love going in there and because of this I don't go too often since it is very very easy to get completely lost in home shopping heaven. I have been to a few other locations and this one fell a tiny bit flat compared to the others I have been to. Of course the merchandise and the layout are the same but the difference was really in the customer service. I found that this location did not have as many friendly faces as the other ones I have been to. There was only one person that greeted us the entire hour we were there. 

The table that we decided to buy had to be picked up from the warehouse so we picked the item on the self serve computers, paid for it in checkout and went to stand in line for pick up. The guy that was working was very unpleasant and condescending when I asked him questions, then after he was done assisting me he took a personal phone call. The customers waiting in line after me were just standing there waiting for him to finish his very loud and unprofessional conversation. 

Overall Ikea is Ikea and this location was well stocked and had the same amazing draw as all the others, but the customer service end definitely left a bad taste in my mouth and didn't let me enjoy the full allure of shopping at such a cool store.

I love Ikea.  If I have some time, it can be fun to explore.  I love the small breakfast to get the day going.  There are so many hidden gems in Ikea; however, with some of the items you get what you pay for and that's why the online reviews are helpful to check out before buying an item.  

If I have to go back for an item I forgot, I look it up online and it says where the item is located.  I used to be able to get in and out quickly, but lately that hasn't been the case.  

My only complaint about IKEA is how long the lines are in check out and how few cashiers they have for check out.   It used to be worse a year ago.  There have been times where I have put down my stuff and just left it at IKEA.  I know most people suck it up because Ikea is a time commitment.  It also takes forever to check out because customers usually just moved and are stressed and cannot think straight.   We've all been there, but I'll admit seeing the IKEA melt downs make it worth the trip.

I am not sure of the previous reviews but my experience was great! The place is busy and I get see how you can get lost at options and what to choose for meal options. But it's really simple you either wasn't the cold section or hot section. You either want dessert or bread. But before all this, don't forget to get your glass at the beginning of the line in order to get your drink from the fountain. Also, utensils and salad dressing is together after you buy your order. 

The dressing is limited to only four options based I what I saw. You have multiple locations to get utensils so be mindful. Also the drink options are the basic but with a some tasty spritzers. I had the pear spritzer and it was sooo good. 

For my lunch I had a Blueberry/walnut salad with smoke salmon. Small side of potato salad and a piece of garlic bread. With the drink my meal was $6.00 even. Now that was a GREAT price! 

The cashiers were very helpful with your needs. I can truly say I would definitely be back.

Great place to go for room ideas. I just moved to Tampa and need to get some furniture ideas on how I want my place to look. 

As usual IKEA didn't disappoint me. I seen some nice finds and great prices foot what I'm looking for. I may go back and get the desk. 

I came out buying the lamp and some candles, I will think on the other items before I buy it. 

My cashier was very cool and he kept the laughter with me and the other customers behind. They were trying to get him a date with their daughter's but he was already married. So you can imagine how that convo went. It was hilarious! You never know what may happen at IKEA. Beware if you are single!

Went shopping here for my office. Easy to get to. Plenty of parking. They have shopping carts and shopping bags. The store was very clean. The room displays are always so fun to look at and get ideas.

Seriously bummed.  I have so much furniture from ikea.  The amount of stars in this review is equal to the amount of care they gave in dealing with a rather small solvable problem with a $13,000 kitchen we purchased from ikea.  I'm so sad that after all we have purchased from this store that it comes down to a kitchen manager Scott who offered no alternative to a wine rack that we ordered three weeks ago and will not come in until August.  His answer was "we clearly state that you should not schedule install until every part is in" and basically if the part won't be in until 4 months from now that there is no alternative.  The sales rep was able to find a cabinet that would fit and we purchased it.  I'm sorry but I feel I'm a reasonable person and I loyal happy customer.  I'm in sales myself and always try to give the benefit of the doubt but the attitude is "I don't care" completely.  And that I should just wait until 4 months from now with no kitchen at all and boxes stacked everywhere in my house waiting for a wine rack OR pay them extra $250 to come out later and finish the job.  Just terrible empathy for a kitchen manager and no real problem solving skills.

Recently purchased a very expensive kitchen from them and we were waiting on the delivery of 1 item that was back ordered several weeks. This item was not going to be available at the time of install and we needed something to fill that space. The kitchen manager, Scott, made no effort to try to procure the piece in question and also made no effort to fill the space with something else. His only reaction was to throw his iPad on the counter, throw his hands up and say "I have nothing, I dont know what to tell you". Unless it's a clean cut sale with no hiccups, they dont want to help solve any problems. Very disappointed with the lack of care and empathy displayed by management after such a large purchase.
We really like this IKEA. Everyone to whom we asked questions was able to help us because they were knowledgeable about both products and store layout.

I'm ever-so-thankful that Indy (or Fishers, whatever) has an ikea. It's been a much needed addition. I personally love in-person shopping; there are always so many knick-knacky like things to see at ikea. IKEA is an experience. I love ikea so much I've been an IKEA family member for years, before there was even a hint of there being one here. However, if I ever go again and witness what I did yesterday (it was Easter), I will seriously never go back again. There were three checkouts open. Three. One; Two; Three. IKEA trips are not usually light shopping for anyone, and lines were horrendously long. If I didn't live on the south side, I would have walked out without my items (which were only a few, but I really wanted them). I'm hoping it was because it was a holiday.

Food is a hidden gem.  Free coffee to all.  Meatballs to are amazing.  Have never had anything bad to eat here.  Also very economical pricing.  Great food and great value make this a no brained for a quick meal.

Ikea is actually one of my favourite places for food! Growing up (in Canada), we would sometimes come for breakfast and the food was always delicious. I love their Swedish meatballs and their soft serve ice cream which are the two staples I always get when I go (not very frequently). This time, we were at Ikea for dinner and we got a salad, boiled vegetables, mac and cheese, Swedish meatballs, and chocolate torte all for a very very reasonable price. There are plenty of spaces to sit so that is never a problem here. The price is more than affordable and I would recommend for everyone to try at least once! Nothing better than shopping and eating!

Horrible services. You do not need Ikea. You can go to Walmart, Amazon and a lot of other stores and you do not get charged for delivery, even for small things. And at Ikea if you decide you don't want their bad quality products, you still have to pay for delivery and tax, even if you did not open the box. You need one full day to resolve something on the phone. Even for the paid delivery & pick up you wait 1 week or more to have it picked up.

I do not recommend Ikea stores or online. They overcharge with all the fees and delivery even on big purchases and of course charge for return delivery and tax. It is difficult to resolve an issue on the phone with them. Time consuming and other stores are much cheaper and better. You need one full day to resolve something on the phone. Even for the paid delivery & pick up you wait 1 week or more to have it picked up.

I decided to order food from the cafeteria and they do not tell you if the accept substitutions for sides. They also need a board with food items available to the customers instead of multiple screens. And the meatballs are just sausages rolled into balls.

I hate their furniture, it is only compressed pencil shavings and Elmers glue. But..their food is excellent and reasonably priced.  Nutritional breakfast for $2.99. Tasty and fulfilling dinners for about $7.

Cheap home decorating products. The settings definitely give you ideas for home improvement.

The cafeteria has cheap food and don't forget to visit the marketplace section at the exit area. The cinnamon buns look enticing. The cookies are delicious and there are some Daim goodies

I will never use there task rabbit program again I bought a wonderful new couch had it delivered to my house some one was supposed to come over and assemble it he even clarified the day before he would be here then a hour before he was supposed to come he bailed now I'm not even wasting my money and just trying to do it myself

This review is for their free child care.

Having two toddlers makes doing anything without my husband difficult. Being able to stick at least my older child in free child care while I navigate the Ikea maze made it possible for me to visit Ikea during the weekend.

Check in takes about a minute. My son happily ran inside to play in the pit of balls. After an hour, I picked him up. He happily ran to me, and the staff gave me his shoes and a picture he "drew" (read: scribbled). The whole time I was shopping, I felt like he was in a safe location (only children and the Ikea child care workers are allowed in the area), and I didn't have to worry about him knocking over a display of glass jars.

And after I picked him up, we were able to go shopping for some yummy organic boxed juices that he miraculously agreed to share with his little sister. Score!

I have spent the last two weeks-- three store visits and countless phone calls-- trying to get items I already paid for (from a $1k-plus order) delivered to me. I tried resolving through the main IKEA customer service phone number, but its automated message said call volume was too high and I was told to call back-- for the last two weeks. This is the worst customer service experience I've ever had in my 45+ years on this planet.
So many unique and amazing products here. Some of my favorite lines of products include Hemnes (bookshelves, desks, and more) plus the Poang chairs. Just go and find something you love!

Customer service is terrible.  I placed a sizable order online for "Click and Collect" only to find because one $5 item wasn't in stock they cancelled the entire 60+ item order.  Yes, they did attempt to call, but we were making breakfast at the time and didn't make it to the phone in time.  They never sent an email which is how I received confirmation of the order.  I spent the rest of the morning trying to call them back - no one ever answered at the local store.  I left multiple messages, tried the 888 number which was "experiencing a high volume of calls" and would just disconnect me.
Finally we drove down there (we live 45 minutes away) only to be told, sorry nothing we can do.  If you want, you can re-order all your items but you'll have to find a computer or sit on your phone and do it yourself, even though we have an itemized list sitting right here in front of us with your order number on it.  The manager, April, was incredibly rude and unhelpful - acted like we were bothering her from the start and it was my fault - Why did you come?  Did you receive a message from us that your order is ready?
No! I received a message that my order would be ready after 11 and then never heard anything again and then spent the next three hours trying to get in touch with a human being!! Only to be stuck talking to a manager with no concept of customer service.
Ikea is a great place to spend looking at home ideas and getting a cup of coffee but as far as customer service - they could care less

This store is an experience! It's fun to just walk around the store. The layout is unique, where you walk through showrooms through a mazelike path. I will say that it's a little confusing, and I still haven't figured out the shortcuts. 

I think the prices are fair. You can find really cheap or really pricy stuff. I just bought the karlstad sofa, which is currently $50 off if you are an Ikea family member (sign up with your email address, and it's free!) I managed to fit all the boxes in my hatchback, which was a major plus!! A worker there even let me borrow a tape measure to make sure my car was big enough. 

The food court area is nice too. They have pretty cheap and yummy food. I've tried the swedish, vegetable, and salmon meatballs. You can't go wrong with any of them!

I miss the Tampa Ikea so much!!! The one where I live is single story and the cafe is in the center of the store. Tampa is 2 stories and you go up the escalator and BAM! you're next to the cafe. I took my mom and grandmother here for lunch after being at the aquarium around the corner and I was so happy I did! Love the Swedish meatballs and everything that comes with it and you know I had to snag a slice of that decadent chocolate cake! We also grabbed the blueberry mousse- which I hadn't seen before (must be seasonal). Besides the food, we ran back downstairs through the store looking for decorating treasures. I was eyeing a bonsai tree seriously~ but I have a specific kind I want. Impulse did not win out on this! Mom however made several happy purchases for her home and we all left satisfied!

Now that I bought a house, IKEA has become my second home. I could wander around here for hours and still find something I hadn't seen before but absolutely need. Upstairs is where you'll find their room displays- kitchens, living rooms, bedrooms, etc. That's also where their Cafe is if you're looking for some delicious Swedish Meatballs. Downstairs is where you can actually pick out the products you want to buy and pick up your furniture boxes.

I've purchased quite a few things from IKEA, curtains, nightstands, dressers, rugs, desks, chairs, as well as various home decor. Although it's quite annoying to put everything together and the directions suck, the prices are fair and everything I've bought so far has been decent quality.

Checking out is another story. Honestly, for some reason even on busy weekends they will only have 2-3 lanes open. So there will be 10-15 people standing in each line just waiting. It's awful and I'll never understand why they don't open a few more lanes, especially during busier times.

Overall, an excellent place for furniture and home decor. Just make sure to get their early. Plus, Coppertail is right across the street if you're looking to grab a quick drink pre or post spending all your money!

Here's our story....
Bought an old farmhouse in Lafayette.
Bought the kitchen at the FISHER's location.
Spent $25,000 on that rascal.

Was easy to assemble, etc.
Appliances were top notch.

The delivery guys were good, so I tipped them!

Great folks in the kitchen department but one is really great.

It's Jack, as he went above and beyond the high bar.

Kudos to you Jack!

The returns were really easy to do also!

Where's the 10 star rating???

Keep on with IKEA EXCELLENCE!

Thank you!

New into town, and what a terrible welcome from IKEA.

We went into this location and purchased a table, we then to the warehouse and grabbed our packages and left.  When we got home, it turns out that Package 1, did not match Package 2.  This is a good learning not to assume in the future, although not sure if it's the customer's responsibility to do this.

There are no direct numbers to the IKEA locations.  We called the 1-888 number and the automated system simply advised us that it was dealing with higher than normal call volume, and hung up.  How is this customer friendly?

We then returned the following day to exchange the legs.  We live approximately 15 miles away, so it was a 30-40 minute drive.  We only brought the legs, not the table top, as it is pretty big.  The customer service rep simply refused to do the return, stating that we need both pieces and that us grabbing the wrong legs is on us.  There was "nothing" that he could do for us.

The engaged a Manager and she allowed us to refund the table legs, and purchased the new ones and paying for the difference - which I'm ok with, this is logical.

Please empower your team members to make decisions.  This was a simple miss that we were ok with until your service member turned what seems like an operational miss on IKEA's fault, into our fault, and then refusing to make it right until leadership got involved.

Please empower your people - thanks.

A day off from work and I went to Ikea to look for items for my walking broom closet that my husband is going to build for me. I was so excited to look for items at Ikea but it's so confusing walking around the whole Warehouse trying to find everything I was walking in circles and was getting confused walking from the cashiers and start from the back and work my way up but this time I walked up the escalators and started upstairs and was so confused I wind up catching the elevator after walking around taking pictures of items lined up downstairs Broad umbrella for my table and the bass when in the clearance room which was a waste of time the stuff is overpriced and not much to look at. I'm really like a big kid when I go to Ikea and only thing I want is they soft serve ice cream cone and my husband likes the cinnamon buns so I got the ones that they making the bed because the chef said the ones that's in the six pack or from a company and I thought about it and said my husband won't eat 6 cinnamon buns and I don't like them so I just got him the one. Walking in the market area I noticed they had chicken meatballs and vegetable meatballs I said I was going to try them but I never tried them so or never heard of them so I wasn't tempted to get them. On June 21st they are having a all-you-can-eat of the food items they sell and I believe it's $12pp and less for children and some odd se has someone up in the food area having samples of the different items that they sell then that gives me a better chance to taste and also to buy. I did find some great ideas for my walk in bedroom closet. And I took pictures to show my husband so I can start gathering up some items for my closet. The one thing that I did like that they had a lot of people on the floor help in on every floor but I was just wandering around just trying to focus on my project. And this is why they just get a 2-star because of the confusion on the different floors while shopping.

BAD COSTUMER SERVICE. My boyfriend recently moved to St. Louis and we decided to shop at Ikea for all his basic furniture. We wanted to have some items shipped and while getting the items sorted, we were told there was a glitch in the system and won't let them add certain items to our delivery. We had to wait for the manager to help us which turned into almost AN HOUR of waiting around until we had to ask again if the manager was even coming. They called her once again and FINALLY she shows up and looks totally calm like she didn't have costumer waiting on her. Then we get home and start building our bed and notice we're missing a piece. My boyfriend calls the costumer service phone number and they tell us to just return it and they will exchange it for a new one. EXCUSE ME??? We just spent over an hour building  90% of this thing and you want us to just return it? This place had just been a nightmare. As if moving wasn't stressful enough.

One person serving each buffet line with a queue of 20+ in each line.  Ridiculously poor service.

21Jun19. Still...only 1 server...long line!!!  Customer service folks!

I purchased a bed on 6/9/19 the bracket that holds the  leg to the bed frame snapped on 6/22/19. 

I called customer service as soon as they opened at 9 AM, the first time I called they transferred me to a queue with no one in it which hung up on me. This again happened the second time I called, the third time I was transferred to 3 different people and then hung up on again. The 4th-9th times I called I was directed to the queue and hung up on. The 10th time I called I asked to speak to a manager, I was given an attitude and then transferred to "a non working number". I was calling from 9AM to 11AM and still never spoke to anyone who could help me. I finally had to drive to the actual store and they said these must have been defective and they replaced them with ones for a queen size bed(we purchased a King), this was after spending 30 minutes in store going back and forth and waiting for customer service. If I didn't spend 4 hours putting this deathtrap together I would have returned it. I will never purchase another Ikea item ever again.

Usually come here to pick up random household items or small furniture items. They really do have everything. On the way out, I get meals or a snack. The food items are very cheap, like $1 coffee or an ice cream cone. The food is fairly nice quality. There is a nice dining area.

It's an IKEA. It's amazing and my entire bedroom is basically all IKEA furniture now. The employees have all been so helpful and nice and if I need Great well priced furniture, this is always my first stop.

A great little day trip to browse around with family or friends or to lose yourself meandering. The food isn't my favorite but the desserts certainly make up for it. I love the chocolate cake and the apple cake. Super affordable options and they go great with the coffee available to all members. Sometimes I ponder going over for dessert.

Terrible manager. Waited 1 hour to pull a simple chair on a Tuesday at 6pm when store is basically empty. All these employees and only one person pulling furniture. Typical way the world works now. Won't be coming back. No help loading while two employees sat there smoking cigarettes. God bless America.

If you love shopping for furniture, look for new design ideas for any room or your whole house, you'll enjoy visiting an Ikea store.

One thing in which they accelerate is furnishing limited room sizes. Storage solutions consider space and sellers blending with furniture.

You can purchase anything from seating to tables, cabinets, toilets, you name it, it's probably there.

All items are also displayed in model rooms, displayed to show how things can mostly be applied to small rooms (square footage is posted).  

Prices are reasonable too.

To top it off, if you end up spending enough time browsing their displays to build an appetite, they have a wonderful cafeteria with a tasty, limited offering of lunch food including, as expected, Swedish meatballs.

If you've never been, and have an opportunity to visit an Ikea store, don't pass it up. Everybody should visit one at least once.

This review is soley for the store. There needs to be more staff here. I went through the whole store trying to buy a few pieces of furniture and when I looked for assistance no one was there. There was a few people around me looking for help as well and had questions. Towards the end I saw 2-3 employees around one single customer. Then there's only one employee at the information desk and only 2 registers open? This was ridiculous . The store itself is clean, the bathrooms are clean, but there's really no one there to help you or make checkout fast. 

The restaurant gets 5 stars from me  the staff was friendly and quick. They were excellent and the food was delicious . I would go back just for the restaurant nothing else.

SO BIG, and I always end up spending WAY more than I ought to!  I love that I can see how rooms MIGHT look if I bought full sets, but also that I can get individual pieces- for example my husband and I bought the bed we wanted and instead of a dresser and y'all piece we bought 2 dressers and 2 bedside tables!  Suggestions from employees but no high pressure sales. Also the random items throughout the store are ALWAYS so fun- I find great gift items but usually have to buy 2 because I want one for myself!

It's a fun place to go to wander especially now that my children are grown up!

Though I love the selection and price of this store, our visit was horrible because their employee was so unnecessarily rude to my family and me as we were trying to check out. I have never posted a review before because I do not like saying negative comments about a business but this incident was ridiculous. 

We went to IKEA for the first time to buy a whole bedroom set for my sister going off to college, so you can understand that we had many large and heavy pieces stacked up that all had to be scanned for the check out. The small aisle was a little inconvenient but luckily the one next to us was closed. The lady actually checking us out was kind and patient as we had to unload all of the large boxes we had stacked on our cart, but was getting confused at what was scanned and what wasn't yet. 

As we were helping her count the items, a horribly rude worker, named Molly, came up and wanted to open the aisle next to us. We weren't moving fast enough for her though, so she started counting on her own while insulting and confusing our worker even more. Her tone was accusatory and impatient. Then we had it figured out and asked Molly to stop interceding because we were annoyed with her at this point and she was not helping in the least. 

As we were working to reload all of the heavy boxes, she then called forward the next customer into the crowded aisle. In conclusion, Molly is a horrible representation of this company and completely ruined our experience here.

Spent the day with my family at IKEA and was lucky enough to have Dorothy help us!  We had grabbed the floor model of a stool and didn't know we couldn't know we could use that as our take home.  The cashier sent us all the way back to grab it but we luckily found Dorothy and she walked us to the product!  Super great customer service!!!!

I have always loved IKEA!  As a child I used to go room to room and pick out the furniture I wanted for my "Dream Room". As a teen I imagined me as a business tycoon and what my office would look like. As an adult I still dream of the perfect room, but now it my craft room!!!! I love the clean look of the shelving they offer. My craft table is actually a 4 foot kitchen table from IKEA that I absolutely LOVE. When the time comes to upgrade my craft room and move it to it's new location, (when the kids go to college) My first stop will be IKEA!!! 
Recently we bought an RV and needed to out fit it with towels, kitchen wares etc. I bought a good portion of these items at IKEA and the prices were perfect!
I only gave it 4 stars as we have bought kids bureaus in the past that the drawers just dont last. I wish they were a stronger material and held up to kids use!

Had the worst experience ever at STL ikea store on 6/30/19. After waiting 45 minutes in their checkout lines, there was a problem with the checkout ticket. Asked to speak with the customer service manager and "Curtis" could not have been any more rude. Will never shop there again.

My Fishers IKEA tips:

-if you must go on a weekend, go on Sunday.
-really, go on a weekday morning for the least crowds.
-sign up for the IKEA Family program; your inbox won't be overflowing and discounts available in store and online :)
-come hungry!  My personal favorites are the chocolate cake and breakfast.
-keep an open mind! 
-be prepared to walk: this is a one floor IKEA, unlike others.

Thanks Fishers IKEA for being here!

Lots and lots of selection and surprisingly well priced! Not much to say here other than they need more check out lines open! Other than that it's very nice and clean and well put together! A strong 4 out of 5

So glad that Fishers got an IKEA. I used to have to travel once per year. Now, I can go whenever I want! The food here is good, and I always find something that I can't live without! Prices are great.

Always a fun experience going to IKEA. I ranked it 4 stars because a few times when I asked for help figuring out where to find a few things, it was a bother to the associated on the floor in the showrooms.  There was a time, when a man helped me get all my stuff on a cart though so I will ranking 4 stars.  The food is actually pretty good here for a furniture/home good store.  Prepare to spend more time than expected here. It's never a quick trip.

Torshawna I believe her name was, made my day the worst when I visited here. She was very mean didn't help me with anything, gave me this weird attitude like I was the problem. I like this place it's a great place to shop but I didn't think your employees was this outrageous She whore glasses. I hope you guys retrain her because she is not a nice employee at this establishment. I'll shop again but I hope she's not working when I do I really felt uncomfortable!

Have been here twice and I feel like I'm under a spell. I had never been in once until last month and I find a reason to go as much as possible. If you decide to go make sure you have a free DAY because you will lose track of time and your money in there. The deals are spectacular and no matter what we got there it was for us. They keep the shelves stocked, the displays are excellent, and the staff are helpful.

I love Ikea and this location was what you expect - clean and well laid out. We had a quick bite in their cafeteria (great as always) then headed to customer service and took a number since there was a line. We had been given an Ikea book shelf some time in the past from a friend it lacked the needed screws and hardware needed to put it back together. Ikea looked at a picture we had, found the model then rounded up all the hardware we would need to put it back together, screws, dowels and all - at no cost, free!! Great customer service!!

at least price is nice for the design, but.........  (1) Often I cannot login to my kitchen design I sent myself from the store. Thankfully I'm only  40 mins to the store . (2) you can NEVER call the LOCAL store with a question. I've spent at least 1/2 calling their 800#, to get transferred to the Tampa store then get hung-up on.  (3) The two times I've had them deliver and assemble pieces, there's only been one person who kinda speaks English.  (4) When using their designers, know that they cannot give you an approximate cost to install their kitchens. I've been told by one Rep to add on at least 30%, and another told me 50%  !!  I hope their measurers and installers are better..... I'm moving forward very cautiously.....

Oh well I'll be damned..... what a place. Holy crap! Felt like the FUTURE ! got a book shelf for my onions... a vanity and a table. Omg so chip! Not pricey at all... love you Swedish folks. Y'all really doing it right. Making Sharon so so happy! Endless and endless amounts of ferniture. God bless y'all for having this store. Walmart you are nothing to me

Three stars is generous based on my experience this week.  The cafeteria style line was long and nobody there to push chatters and the indecisive along.  Part of the problem is you don't get to see the hot choices until you are through with desserts, salads, beverages and cold items.  (The other part of the problem is stupid people with children plus strollers unregulated by their parents.)  For about $9, I got a side salad, a veggie wrap, a lingonberry juice box and a water.  Prices were reasonable.  Had I passed "hot" first I would've gotten a hot meal.  All the food looks appetizing.  The registrar was listless, rang the goods but acted like telling me where dressing was kept was a chore.  Finding a fork was in one place, finding a napkin was 30 feet away from that--a little ridiculous, especially for the walking challenged.  The food was tasty--the spring mix could've been cut into bite sized pieces since a fork doesn't cut well in a styro cup.  The wrap was flavorful but needed dressing as you got deeper into it.  My friend loved her veggies, thought her mashed taters were dry, loved the pear beverage. Our choices were not very "Swedish".  Tables were not being kept clean by patrons, nor trays put away when finished.  It's unfortunate that patrons are not self-responsible for their own clean-up, but the restaurant should be accountable for someone on the floor to train them, to clean up after them, to add a fee to those who don't (yeah, I said it) and restore clean places to eat for others.  I would not go out of my way to eat here, but in a hunger pinch, the food is fine.  Some sort of menu would be helpful-relying on wall photos while in a pushy long hog trough like at Disney is not my style.  Having to wait for all the hot food people when you grab a cold item and are stuck in line behind them is beyond frustrating.

Typically I like Ikea. The employees are warm, the space is tidy. The products are affordable. The collaborations are brilliant. Today's visit left a sour taste in my mouth and I may not ever come back unless I need to. The ice cream cone when I walked in shoulda been a sign - tired and lopsided.

To start, many of the rooms were closed up (for renovation?), which is fine - whatever. But then they didn't have any of the 8 items I was looking for. I could have checked this online and probably known ahead of time - but these were basic designs I mistakenly expected to see stocked. Umbrella base. Lantern. Vase. Outdoor Pillowcase. Etc. No employee was helpful, with one guy saying he'd be right back and he wasn't. He didn't come back at all for 6 minutes. I waited.

I weeded my way through, disappointed all along the way so much that I purchased two glass jars I half needed just because I needed to leave with something. When I hit the customer service desk, they told me I could pick up any umbrella base that's currently on showroom display, so I gave the whole store another lookthrough. No success - oh well, I'll get some meatballs to cheer me up.

Walk up to this guy with a huge unruly beard barely covered by his hairnet, ask for 20 a la carte meatballs as I always do. He says a loud "NO, that is not allowed". I explain I always get this meal, and it looks like you changed it to 4 meatballs rather than 5 for $1.25 so it's an even worse price than before - why can't I just get my meatballs? "Whoever allowed this before was mistaken - you may have a meal and add meatballs" (for the purposes of this review being somewhat unbiased, I'm making him sound downright elegant and reasonable in his response, but it was vehement and huffy). Though I didn't want a meal. I didn't want lingonberry jam and mashed potatoes with shoddy gravy on the side. All I wanted was to eat 20 chicken meatballs and leave this hell. 

I may never be back unless there's a collaboration like Walter Van Beirendonck or Tom Dixon or Hay again. Perhaps Droog or Moooi or Magis or something. They'll get me back I'm sure, and when they do I'll want my 20 darn meatballs a la carte as I've been ordering since high school.
Love that it's so close to home. Always restocked with the white pillar candles that we love.
Service was okay but succulent selection was subpar.  I thought IKEA was cheap, but if you wanted anything that was quality you could get something better and cheaper from Pier 1, Target, etc.

If you really like finding your way out of a maze, IKEA is your kind of fun store. One way in. One way out. Little signs with arrows point you in the right direction. A few unmarked shortcuts if your keen enough to find them. 

It's not that their products aren't good; they are. It's not that their Swedish meatballs aren't excellent; they are. It's all about their concept of how people think and learn. To IKEA, customers are to be lead around through the entire warehouse regardless of what they need, and forced to pass through every department on two floors until finally reaching check out cashiers at the end of a long and boring stroll. Once you've begun, forget about going back to the beginning. The human undertow will just drag you down. Need a restroom? Good luck with that. 

It helps if you are a zombie or dyed in the wool shopper when dealing with IKEA. If you don't particularly like the "Costco" warehouse experience, this place will wear you down. I mean, how many DIY furniture projects do you have in one lifetime? How often do you need to build shelves for your office? Not nearly enough to make this entertaining. 

Yeah. We did buy a few glass water containers for around the house, and the prices were good. But, how much better it would have been to be directed to the location where they were shown, and be able to go right to them, than be required to go on safari to find them. 

What a perverse trade-off.

Omg .... I have never been in IKEA!!!!
I understand that you are required to assemble products.

But... I liked the fact that washable slipcovers are offered. I will be searching for locations near Orlando.

Excellent customer service.  Clean and very friendly staff. Try the menu at the diner inside. It's cafeteria style. The desserts are excellent and delicious. Today I tried the chocolate mouse. The seating is great. Tables are everywhere.  High tops and low tables.  They can accommodate large parties.  Excellent place to have a work luncheon or birthday party. There is pepsi products and glasses for your convenience for ice. They also have fountain drinks. Stop by just for lunch or dinner. Shopping is just an extra adventure!

I purchased a bookcase in store yesterday, and had the help of my brother to lift it. We opened it today to assemble and one of the sides of the case is cracked/defective. My brother is unavailable to help me return it and my husband is out of the country for work, but I need a bookcase as soon as possible. However, I am unable to lift the boxes on my own to return/exchange, plus I have a 5 month old baby that I would somehow have to manage while somehow getting the boxes into the store, so I am unable to return this product. When I FINALLY got connected on the phone with IKEA customer service (after calling multiple times and being disconnected due to high call volume), and I asked if there was any way someone could deliver a replacement bookcase and take the defective one, I was told this is not an option and I would need to somehow return it to the store on my own. The representative agreed with me that my only options are to wait for someone I know to help me, or else I can hire someone to help me. This is ridiculous and not feasible. Apparently IKEA expects women with limitations, such as weakness and babies, to have money to hire random people in order to get things done in life. 

Additionally, yesterday in the store my login information would not work on the kiosk. I asked an employee for help and she verified she was also unable to log in. I also needed a kitchen cabinet, but an employee wouldn't help me determine the pieces I needed and told me to use the kitchen planning computer software. I attempted to use it but did not have success, so I asked another employee for help but I was not able to log in to save my plan. This was frustrating and I didn't purchase the kitchen cabinet I needed.

Based on my in-store experience, and the rude and unhelpful interaction with customer service on the phone, I have no desire to return to IKEA in store or online for future purchases.

I had the best experience here with customer service. Two young african american men lifted heavy pax units right into my car and even ran to get me a measuring tape before to make sure they would fit. Wonderful customer service and very helpful and happy and kind young men!

There's only one IKEA in the whole state of Missouri, and, of course, I end up living ten minutes away! It's always a fun experience coming here, and I end up walking away with way more items than I intended to buy.

Some of my favorite things:

1) The restaurant. Duh. Rumor has it that its sole purpose is to keep people coming in and buying more stuff. Hence, the low prices and good quality. Try the veggie meatballs if you haven't yet - the pre-set meal is just $3.99 and super yummy!

2) Cute yet simple designs that are easy to replicate.

3) The fun and interactive atmosphere of walking around and trying things! 

The main drawback is that a lot of items now seem pricey as other store chains keep growing. For instance, there's a line of leather chairs at IKEA that cost ~$150 each. I scored almost identical ones at Marshall's for less than half the price, so you get the idea. That said, nothing will replace IKEA for me!
Love the $1.49 breakfast at Ikea.  The cinnamon rolls ($1.00 each) used to be much better though.  Free coffee if you have an Ikea membership card.  There are kiosks all over to sign up and its free.
Had breakfast here before shopping. Coffee is free if you have a membership  card. Lots of seating available. Breakfast is quick and inexpensive.

On the plus side: Free coffee for IKEA Family Card holders, tasty and attractively priced food, pleasant restaurant atmosphere. Generally attractive and well designed products, although the displays at this store are not always well executed. As to price, if you stick to the "loss leaders", you can save money over shopping at other stores. 

On the minus side: Have been to several IKEA stores in different states and can say without hesitation that this store has staffing and management issues. Lines at checkout and in the restaurant are unreasonably long at peak hours and often during off-peak. Customer service is highly unpredictable: associates are often difficult to find and when you finally locate someone, it's up for grabs as to whether that person will be cordial and helpful or lazy and indifferent. This unpredictability is also true of the checkout experience. Local customer service standards are low and training to IKEA standards can't be easy, but the bottom line is that customer experience is poor at this location. 

For those who are traveling any distance to visit this store, know that the website is not always accurate when it comes to the item availability. If you are visiting to purchase specific items, make sure there are MANY in stock (I would suggest 20+; I recently went to purchase something that there were supposedly 15 of and found the self serve bin empty and two nearby associates not at all interested in helping). 

That said, do check the website before you visit, as you cannot rely on IKEA associates to be of help, and install the phone app so that you can quickly and easily use the self-serve area. 

IKEA ninja trick: If you're planning to buy flat pack items, go through the checkout area directly to self serve and skip the rat maze.
