I called August 8 to get a better idea of delivery and was told the items were not processed (even though I have an email receipt with confirmation). 

They offered no reimbursement or discounts other than to waive the $39 delivery fee. Their customer service is outrageously awful! They were rude and offered no explanation. Don't waste your money, although items are inexpensive, you'll spend hours on the phone with them. The WORST!

Was going to give 3-stars, but the salmon was delicious and the restaurant staff people were all very nice. I have shopped at IKEA in 4 countries and i never saw an IKEA restaurant that was dirty until today. Dirty tabletops, dirty silverware, dirty trays. The worst was the tiny coffee station where it wasn't even marked which carafe was decaf! DON'T MESS WITH MY CAFFEINE!

Thought this would be great and save me from driving to Tampa. Sunday morning I get confirmation that the delivery will occur sometime between 12-4.  So I wait all day until 4pm when I get an automated call that says the delivery is going to be late. Now 4-6pm. At 5:50 I get an automated call that says delivery is delayed until Tuesday. IKea is Ikea.
If you are looking for just about anything for your home or apartment.   IKEA is the place.
You can also purchase their Meatballs to go!!!!

Never again. First, the salesperson didn't include a piece that we needed for each of two beds that we bought, so we trekked all the way back to the store for those. Second, how's this for 21st century customer service: to make arrangements for pick up of a return that you bought in the store, you MUST return to the store. No phone # is available, no online way to make arrangements. You must show up in person to make arrangements. So, so done with IKEA.

I love IKEA!  Cool place for nice stuff for your home
I bought a small lamp, just one of many purchases, and it is still working and shining bright.

I applied for an IKEA project card to allow my partner to buy the things needed to allow my grandmother to come stay with us while I stayed with her at home after her treatment. He explained he was an authorized buyer and asked them to verify. Their answer was that they could not call the bank and he needed to call the bank. They refused to call to verify he was an authorized buyer. They informed us that we should not have called them but the store was supposed to call and get authorization. I asked if IKEA employees knew they needed to call and knew the number and they said yes, they should know the protocol. The store still refused to do anything. The bank says that IKEA must have some problem because it is clear on their end and if they just call, they will provide an authorization code. Curtis told me it would not make a difference if we call the bank together. It is unfortunate that customers are treated with malicious indifference  at IKEA. It is also unacceptable to lie to customers and refuse to help them, Additionally, stores should not prevent customers from receiving answers by withholding information needed to escalate situation. What kind of store operates like this? It is the worst experience I have had in any furniture store. I will not be shopping here again and I would advise anyone reading this to do the same. I would hate for anyone to have to go through the situation that I just went through. If I can help others to avoid having a similar situation I will. I recommend that if you are considering shopping here, that you take your business anywhere else but here.
Keep an eye on Cashier #10078139. We got home and discovered that she charged us for her soda! At least she didn't try to slip in a sofa on our receipt....

Went to this IKEA location for the first time and I had a good experience. It was easy to navigate and I got a lot of good deals on home decor. I was also able to try the Swedish meatballs in the cafe for the first time and was not disappointed.

Please don't waste your money here! 
I purchased a desk yesterday, which was a problem in and of itself (it had to be pulled from stock, we were on a time limit and told it would be 15 to 20 minutes and it actually took over an hour and twenty minutes of pure stressfulness). At best IKEA has caused me days of stress and trouble and at worst they have stolen $200 from me.  It is unbelievable that a global company has such insanely poor customer service. Not worth it.
The food tastes pretty good, but IKEA makes quite clear how much they value their customers' time by doing things like this.  Not cool, ikea management, not cool at all.

I used to love this place. Not anymore.
Rude people, prices not correct, disorganized and dirty.
All the displays are filthy.
Literally hundreds of curtains in a bin marked $14.99.
Rang up only $16.99 , they wouldn't honor the price. Tag even said the name of the curtain. Cashier hardly tried to find out. Basically said too bad. 
Peace out IKEA...

I've always had great experience shopping at this ikea but please be careful as the sale price always doesn't come up at the register and have to pay attention .i shop at this place and after the cashier rang my items and I paused for it I realized that I was overcharged when I brought it up to the cashier she simply refer me to returns as I had to go to return section and take a number and waited about 1/2 Hr to return my items .I value for my time and never wanted to spend my Sunday morning waiting for a mistake that they could have taken care of at the first register .their return department need some serious updating with the process .Uts funny that they even have couches for people to sit and wait for a long time as ikea have no respect for people time .

The two stars isn't necessarily for IKEA itself.  I was able to put together a desk I got from them fairly easily and their instructions are pretty good.  And the customer service rep in store was patient with us when we placed a rather large order closer to closing time than we probably should have.   She also managed to do some magic so all the parts for everything we ordered would arrive at the same time.  That was a positive and where I kept some stars for IKEA.

Here is where the experience was horrible.  The delivery of the items.  I guess IKEA uses a company called Select Express to do their deliveries.  We got our delivery date via phone call and then, the day before the delivery, we got our four hour delivery window.  I scheduled a tasker from Task Rabbit to do the assembly the following day (per IKEA's recommendation).   We made sure we were home during the delivery window on the date.  We didn't get the delivery during our window.  A half  hour after the delivery window, we called IKEA and waited on hold for several minutes to speak to someone about the status of the delivery. 
 IKEA put us on hold, called the delivery company, and 5 minutes later, we were told the driver was only about 30 minutes away. 

We then waited another hour without receiving the items we ordered.  We called IKEA customer service again and waited while they talked to the delivery company.  We were now told the driver was stuck in traffic and was about 30 minutes away.  But this time, IKEA gave us the phone number for the delivery company. 

When our order didn't show up after another hour we called the delivery company.  The dispatcher got my order number and then put me on hold for five minutes to get the status.  It is then that I am told that the truck broke down and we wouldn't be getting our delivery that day.  We would have to reschedule. The next available delivery date was TWO more days away.  So we reluctantly accepted that.  As my wife and I talked, we decided that if this was the kind of experience we should expect from IKEA, we were going to cancel the order.  

We called IKEA customer support a couple of minutes before closing and I spoke to someone right at the closing time.  I was told that because the customer resolution center was closed that the best she could do was send an email requesting the order be cancelled.  According to IKEA's website, it can take them up to 48 hours to respond to a support email so the following day, I called them early in the morning to make sure my order got cancelled.  I was put in the queue and a few minutes later, IKEA support message says they are experiencing a higher than usual call volume and would be unable to take my call.  They then ended the call.  No opportunity to leave a message or a callback number. 

So I waited an hour and called again.  This time I spoke to a live person about needing to cancel the order.  The checked and said I needed to speak to a resolution specialist and put me back in the queue.  Once again, I was briefly on hold and then told they were experiencing a higher than usual call volume and they would be unable to take my call.  And once again they hung up.

I called back again an hour later and FINALLY got the order cancelled. 

Bottom line is that the products themselves are good and most of the store employees will go out of the way to be helpful.  But if you want delivery be warned.  And if you need support, it may be difficult to reach.

I love IKEA. Nothing not to like except....food court servers could be a tad bit cordial. I said hi, guy didn't say a word, just looked at me. Never spoke. Just ladled the food. Said nothing. I don't expect much but a smile would be nice. Everyone else in store that I spoke to was very nice. Makes me not want to eat there again. It was very slow in food court so I'm not sure why there was attitude. Check out was great though.
Seems small compared to other IKEA's, until you actually walk around the store.  Spent 2 hours here.  Did buy a new table and some chairs.  Which all items are made of solid wood, $150.

The South Philadelphia store was in complete disarray in the self service furniture section on the morning and afternoon of 8/24. None of the Friday's supplies were in the correct location according to the website or even in the isle. Similar materials were multiple bins away from wash other. Numbers didn't match the website. IKEA needs to step their game up. They need free high speed internet for all the husbands waiting for their wives. Some parts have literally no service. Seriously, my wife would've been here for another hour if I didn't have a boredom induced hissy fit in the kitchen section...

Great merchandise, great place to shop, if only they bothered to hire a competent staff! We ordered in store pick up and their policy of cancelling an entire order if one item is out of stock really created a lot of problems for us. We told them to skip the item and they said over the phone they would not cancel it. When we came in to pick it up they had canceled it anyway. Living in a city with IKEA has brought so many conveniences to my life. As soon as I moved to St. Louis, I picked out a few large pieces of furniture and had them delivered for a flat rate of $59, which is a great deal that everyone should take advantage of. Also, sign up for the IKEA family member if you haven't already! You get discounts on certain items and a birthday coupon ($10 off as of 2019).

It may just be me, but on my days off, if I had nothing to do, I would just come here for a quick lunch (Swedish meatballs, duh) and push a cart around to look for items for home improvement. I always stumble upon cute pieces of works or innovative designs. They also have a small plant section, which is wonderful for people like me who are practicing the art of a green thumb. There truly is something for everyone here!

Overall love this ikea location. It's a great spot for affordable furniture. Definitely a big perk to sign up for ikea family! It's FREE! You get special deals and discounts in stores. I feel like they have basically everything you need for your home. I feel like somethings are over priced like blinds... I'm not paying $40-$50 for cordless blinds.. main reason I give them 4 stars instead of 5 is they tend to run out of certain products frequently. Feel like you know what sells better than other products and should keep more on hand, because after walking around for 2-3 hours and picking what I want just to find out it's sold out isn't the best experience. Also their "last chance" clearance section is a bit over priced in my opinion. I rather go to Meijer for closeout deals that I can still return in needed. Just a thought!

Ikea is an amazing place. Low cost, decent quality furniture and home supplies and an amazing cafe with even more affordable and delicious meals. It's difficult to walk around an Ikea without constantly wondering if you need the items in front of you.  I was consistently surprised at how low the price was for every item there. I came here to buy a dresser and ended up leaving with much, much more than that.

The Conshohocken Ikea is clean, the people are friendly, and the food was great. I was hangry from moving all day so I ordered two meals - the classic Swedish meatballs and the smoked salmon plate. The best part was, I got those two full meals for around $10. They also sell a lot of the food they serve at the marketplace downstairs. 

You cannot beat the amount of bang you get with your buck than Ikea, and the Conshohocken store is a a fantastic one.

Ikea is awesome, just avoid this store. 

My home is almost entirely Ikea products. Have shopped at their stores for years, and love their stuff. The south Philly location, however, is always a nightmare to deal with. Always budget a LOT of time to get through the checkout.  One cashier on, unlabeled cash or credit only lines (you find out which it is when you finally get to the cashier).  

About once a year I'll stop in because it's location is more convenient to me, and will be immediately reminded why I don't come here. It's been this way for years. 

Conshohocken isn't that far, save yourself the headache and go there.

You can spend an entire day at IKEA. They have rooms set up for you to walk through and experience what is possible with their furniture and products. They have everything you could need or want for your home. In the middle of the store they have a restaurant that features their famous Swedish meatballs. It also provides a nice break from all the walking and shopping.  If you're like me, you will need also buy a bigger vehicle to fit everything you purchase.  Good thing they offer delivery...

If you have time to burn and like to browse, ikea is the place for you. If you are going to find a specific item online then try to have the exact location because help is pretty much non existant in this giant maze like store. If you like to online order and want to pick it be prepared to wait. I ordered at 1100am with a pick up time between 1330-1700. Showed up at 1713 and it was still not ready!!!! I like IKEAs products but the service is not up to par for a store this size.

One of the dirtier Ikeas I've ever been to. Walked through almost the entire top floor is far without seeing a single employee. The absolute worst part is the music though. The music and intercom advertisements are so loud that I can't spend more than 20 minutes here. It's a shame, I usually enjoy browsing and shopping ikea over several hours.

I have been to a lot of ikeas in my time....NY-LA-Miami-Orlando.....the return service area in Tampa....by far the most painful.....slowest.....understaffed....no sense of urgency whatsoever.    Why do you make it soooo painful to do your job Tampa??????

Ikea sells everything you need, things you didn't even know you needed, and shows you how to arrange it all in your house in their showrooms. The best part about a trip to Ikea is knowing we will be getting to eat there. They have meatballs, salmon balls, and even veggie balls. I like to get the chicken fingers and this last time I got the braised pork shoulder and it was really good. I love how they have different specials. 
The best part is all the desserts. The daim cake, Chocolate Almond Cake, the chocolate oat balls are pretty delicious and I like to wash it all down with Nordic Fruit Water, ligonberry flavor is my favorite. 
Sign up for an Ikea Family card and you get a free hot beverage on each visit and they often have events and a prize wheel and you can spin if you have a card. 
They even send you free meatballs on during birthday month and a gift.

Ikea is one of those cool places you can spend hours walking around checking out their stuff.  I did buy a bed frame and mattress many moons ago when I was younger and just moved out.  But now being older I don't think I'd really buy any of their major furniture, as they just remind me of stuff you'd see in a college frat house haha.  That being said, I do love some of their home decor stuff, you can find some great deals on some things too.  I do have a glass cabinet I got from here a while back to display some things (and trying to put things together can be both frustrating and  amusing).  I also ate there for the first time and though wasn't anything great, was a good price and fills you up before doing some shopping.  I'd come visit here a bit more often if it wasn't on the other side of town.  Also not a fan of South Edmonton Commons.
Returns understaffed. They mess up in ringing up purchase and then really slooooooooow in returns.

Decided to go to IKEA for the first time since I have family that always raves about the place. I needed a bedside table and found one I liked on the website. The site said this location had 84+ in stock. I didn't realize you had to go to the self serve furniture area to pick up the item, my fault on that. So after walking through the whole store and trying the swedish meatballs (which were pretty good). I made it to the aisle and bin were the 84+ boxes should have been and the bin was empty. I found an employee and asked where they were and I was informed they should have been restocked but for some reason they hadn't been yet. They had them in the back warehouse but couldn't restock them since they couldn't use the forklift with customers in the store. I asked if they could just bring one out from the back since it was a small box but I was informed there was nothing they could do. I would have to come back in three days when it "might" be restocked then. I'm sorry but I drove half an hour for an item that says there are 84+ in stock, just to be told no there isn't anything they can do. I asked my cousin about this. She said at her Ikea near Chicago, they would always help her and get the item out of the back. So not a great first impression. I did like the selection and the unique items throughout the store. But they need to sort out their employee help. Gave an additional star for the meatballs.

This is the first two-story IKEA I've ever visited. It is really neat. It's located not too far off of I-4, soon after you enter Tampa and it's not too difficult to find if you use your GPS. Huge parking lot.

The first time we arrived, we immediately went upstairs to get lunch. Then back downstairs to get a cart, then back upstairs via the elevator to walk around. (There are no carts on the second floor. You have to pick one up on the first floor. A bit odd, but understandable.)

The bathrooms are located right when you walk in behind the escalators downstairs and behind the cafe upstairs and are very large and clean.

We have a great time here. Thanks to the IKEA app on my phone and very knowledgeable employees, we are able to locate everything we were shopping for. WiFi is easily available throughout the entire building.

Purchased our 2nd IKEA kitchen and everything went smooth. We really appreciated Michael S. Help in the kitchen cabinet and countertop process. He was very nice and knowledgeable in his field he made us feel good at every step! We ordered Sektion cabinets and quarts countertops.

Huge bistro serving breakfast, then lunch/dinner. Employees were pleasant. Very clean.

I can't help it. I ordered what I always do, the Swedish meatball meal. As always, it was delicious. The desserts are always great as well. Calories mean nothing here, since you will walk it all off anyways, right?

This particular IKEA restaurant is located on the second floor and is in the corner of the building so has plenty of places to sit and relax, especially for families. Huge bathrooms are located behind the bistro.

I overheard a naysayer griping about the view of the parking lot. Obviously they must not have been able to look up a few inches to see the lovely view of the Tampa skyline. We actually liked sitting there, eating our meal with that view.

Remember to bus your tray!

Returned to IKEA three days later. Once again the bin was empty. I asked an employee at one of the credit desks and he looked up the item I wanted. He realized the nightstand was out on display away from the aisle and bin the website said it would be in. Sure enough there were plenty of nightstand boxes at the display location. Appearently the display had been there on Saturday as well and the other two employees I had talked to didn't know that.

The nightstand was easy to build and seems to be good quality. I am pleased with the nightstand.

I was so excited for Ikea to come to our town, but was a little underwhelmed by the size. I love visiting Ikea when we are traveling and this is one of the smallest ones I've been to.

I enjoy stopping by for dinner with my 6-year-old on nights when my husband is out of town. He enjoys the cafeteria-style dinner and we share some cheesecake.

Overall, we've had great experiences with this location and know all the shortcuts to get through quickly! It's starting to feel like home, which is never a bad thing!
I love shopping here. However the returns are a disappointment and a disaster!!!!!!! Take a number I'm waiting over an Hour already where is the stafff. This is bad business. REALLY IKEA..

Wasted $20 in Lyft fees to get down to this location, only to find that none of the multiple items I was looking for were available. 

I checked on their website before I left, and every item was listed as being in stock at this location, but when I got there, not a single one was. 

Horrible inventory management and a complete waste of my time and money.
The food was terrible ( waste of $10) The dining area.... it was so dirty! Dirty handprints all over the WHITE chairs and stools! I was going to buy furniture but I have a stomach ache now :-(

Great if you're looking for reasonably priced household items. Their Pax and Kallax for closet and storage are sturdy and can be bought in pieces to match your closet or room.  Not everything is as solid so you really need to see them items in the storeroom.  There is also a little playroom for children while parents are shopping and a lunch area to grab a bite to eat.

Can't believe I haven't reviewed this! I've been shopping Ikea for almost 30 years in the US and abroad. IKEA is a godsend, with a range of prices that track with the item's quality, and so, so many items! At this location, some of the things I've purchased are a sink, curtains, beds, shelves, chairs, rugs, light fixtures, dishes, and flatware. My architect neighbor loves the kitchen cabinets, although my building contractor says to stay away from them. I stayed away. It is sometimes difficult to find an employee if you need help or have a question, though, and return policies are more strict than I think they should be. I always check out the As-Is section. (I'm currently typing this on an As-Is dining table that is  21 years old.) And the meatballs are a deal!

Generally very difficult way to shop if you're flying solo, but an EXTREMELY AMAZING associate that I knew as "Deb" made everything ASTOUNDINGLY EASY. Ask for her specifically. She played with my 2 year old son while I toiled over the bits and pieces that make a set for 3 different rooms. 
She literally chased him around, let him use her radio, and completely changed my mind about walking out of there because of the difficulty of what I thought would be an easy "all in one" package. 
If I had cash I would have given it ALL to her, but I was using the IKEA credit card to take advantage of 0% financing and she found me the EXACT piece that I was looking for which was unfortunately discontinued, but she found the very last one hidden away that nobody else seemed to be able to find for my daughter's bedroom for Christmas. It will make her SO HAPPY and I couldn't have done it without Deb.

I cant complain about the actual furniture and products that IKEA sells, they are great for the price and i love the styles. Most of my apartment is all from IKEA, this one to be specific. But what i cannot take are the people that come into this store. I don't know if it is the fact that its a giant space or just Fishers but everyone and i mean everyone completely looses all sense of curtesy and manners when entering this store. Every time i come in here i about lose it due to the rude behaviors from grown adults. 

My only other experience that was very disturbing was after shopping for an hour putting all the things i needed to complete my trip in my cart i parked my card so i could run to the rest room really quick. When I came back (4 minutes later) a staff member had taken my cart and started putting the items back on the shelf. After 15 minutes we found the staff member and my cart with about half of what i had in it. I had to go back through the store again. That was upsetting.

The restaurant is nice, usually has 1 vegan or vegitarian option. 

Parking can also be a nightmare. People will pull up to the loading docks and stay there for an hour waiting for their help inside who is also waiting. I don't understand this, so the dock will fill up with half of the people sitting in the car waiting or waiting inside for their stuff. Instead of bringing their stuff outside and pulling their vehicle up to the dock after.

I just have to be prepared to come here mentally before i enter.

Horrible horrible horrible customer service. 

Went to this store a few times but won't be returning now. 

Recently purchased a house plant for my bday there. Right after bringing it home it instantly dies. 

No one in the return/exchange area, not thru customer service number care or are willing to exchange a $8 plant. 

Never had such stubborn people to deal with. Everyone kept blaming me saying it was my fault. Never had plant issues before with anything I've gotten from Lowe's or other big dept stores. 

No longer an ikea fan, they have bad plant products and worse customer service. Go elsewhere bc once it dies instantly everyone is rude. 

Too bad bc the cafeteria and some other products are nice but hard to go back to a company that has the most inflexible policies , guess that's how they continue making billions. 

Very dissatisfied with how they are company centric instead of caring about their customers. Wow

TL;DR: what is not to love about IKEA? It is such a wonderfully classic go-to store that's curated towards both simplicity and quality. I absolutely love the design of their furniture. If you come here, you will most likely than not find something that you'll be tempted to purchase. The addition of food options is such a convenient idea because I always get hungry while shopping. It is definitely a staple of my household.

All the products are quality-made and are very fairly priced which I love! I have never had a problem concerning assembly and it's definitely one of the stores I can trust the most when ordering furniture online for pick-up. Be warned, however, the marketplace and showcase areas is like a maze because it's so huge! Both a positive and negative, I guess. I am a big fan of the self-serve model because it is very sustainable and space-efficient.

The staff is pretty average and don't stand out as a spectacular aspect of the store. I'm not saying they are useless but you could definitely shop here without needing assistance from them even once. I see employees chatting-about most times doing very little work. Nonetheless, the self-serve approach allows you to shop without the need to interact with any of them. I found the cashier service to be quite average. They aren't particularly welcoming nor stand out as a pinnacle of customer service.

The food is very average but definitely satisfying. Again, I am quite the fan of how they run things at IKEA. The cafeteria approach towards their restaurant isn't bad but I do understand it's quite odd. It really feels like you're in a high-school. I also find that the dining area is not maintained and is consistently dirty and unkept. This is an issue that has to be solved. The Swedish cafe part is decent as well. They serve very basic hotdogs, pizzas, and drinks. I always stop here if I feel a little bit hungry. The cheap prices are very justifiable and the food is filling. I like their self-serve beverage options. I find them not too sweet and flavourful. The still options is appreciated as I personally don't like carbonated beverages.

Overall, I absolutely adore IKEA. I love the atmosphere and the unique approach it has towards everything. Personally, it fills such a perfect niche that cannot be replaced.

I arranged a return pick up for a $400 item as it was a manufacture defect.  Ikea's personnel picked up the item on November 13th but no refund was ever issued.  I've spoken to customer service three times - once a week for three weeks - and each time another excuse is given.  Each time, they confirm the item was picked up, but say the company they hired did not deliver it to Ikea so no refund.  Most recently, the CS personnel sent the issue to her manager, and still nothing.  Nothing.  

Today I've called twice and each time, the customer service line disconnects the call as they are 'too busy.'  

I've been a decades-long shopper of Ikea both stateside and in Europe.  This is the worst experience I've ever had.

Love walking around this place to see all of the things I don't need. It's a great place to walk though in the winter when it is cold out and you don't have any place else to go. 
The furniture is, you know, cheap. Don't expect it to last a long time but if you like to change things up often it's a great place to get something new. 
Beware of the cheap dining chairs. My daughters broke within a year.

So many people eat at IKEA! Well, here's the deal.
First of all, you can get a meal for under $10.00, we'll under. Don't expect large portions, you won't get it. Instead there are portions for healthy eating and the food is ok. Not great, but edible. They usually have veggie balls and meat dinners. The desserts are small and pretty good. You can get a sliver of a brownie for $0 .99. The atmosphere is fine. Very cafeteria style, But suits eating in the fly while shopping.  It's roomy and never too crowded!

Horrible experience trying to cancel my online order. Have talked to four people so far in two days, been on hold a total of three hours, been transferred and hung up on, finally had it confirmed it was cancelled then received an email saying it had been shipped to the warehouse to be delivered, called to reconfirm the cancellation, was told they already tried to deliver ( which they hadn't, it was a full week before the actual confirmed delivery date) then told they didn't have the tools to cancel since it was already in the warehouse. I only ordered the items two days ago then spent the last two days trying to cancel. I was only trying to cancel so I could add more to my order, now I'm not going to order anything at all so I don't have to deal with this ridiculousness again!

Customer service not a strong point. Neither is online "click & pickup" a great service. Ordered an in-stock table for pickup. Drive two hours to get it and 1) the directions for the click & pickup desk were completely inaccurate. For starters, there isn't one. Employees didn't know of it either. So I went to the furniture pickup point and the lady was rude AF.  Basically told me to wait for an email to say the table is ready for pickup. 

There are 11 in the store!  Could have just shopped at the store. Screw IKEA!

I've been coming to this IKEA for a long time now but just recently, I have been coming here a lot due to moving to a new house. I love the concept of IKEA being a one-stop shop where I can buy a bed frame to buying a pair of personal scissors - and of course, I always have to eat the Swedish Meatballs in their restaurant area. 

This location is huge with it being two-stories. The employees here are super nice, and always willing to answer any questions you may have which in my case, I always have a lot. When I bought more than 20 furniture items during my last visit here, the employee who helped me was very knowledgeable about the whole delivery process and basically, knew everything about IKEA. She also made the whole check-out process go as quickly and efficiently as possible.

Oh, yes, and don't forget to buy their Cinnamon Buns. They are so good!

My first visit to this store..to any IKEA. I purchased a futon to be delivered. All seemed well until an hour later, I was told it was out of stock. I asked that my money be refunded. Three full length phone conversations to customer service, having a terrible time trying to get anyone, the automated system hanging up because of high volume, a customer service person hung up on me accidentally after spending 15 minutes explaining everything again....and it still isn't resolved. It's been two weeks and I still do not have my money back!

On a weekday morning (or EARLY on a weekend), this is a great spot for an affordable-but-delicious, not-too-crowded breakfast. I usually get the swedish breakfast combo plus waffles and coffee for around/under $10. The cafeteria seating area is upstairs and there are plenty of windows, so it feels open and bright. Any time after midmorning on a weekend, though, and enter at your own risk!

As for the home furnishings, they're what you'd expect from Ikea: cheap enough to bring home, breakable enough that you probably should just buy another if you decide to move, and obnoxious enough that assembly may precipitate your next breakup!

I absolutely love IKEA. I could stay for a whole week. So, I received an event to the Julbord Feast.  I never knew about this.

Julbord Feast is a Swedish Feast before Christmas.  Lots of people showed & the lines were long.  On the menu was potato salad, smoked salmon, beet salad, angel eggs with cavier & shrimp, Swedish meatballs, mashed potatoes, herring, fruit & so much more.  Also, dessert as well. 

Well, since I know about this, I guess I will come next year.

Ikea is a wonderland, it's like walking into a massive corporate house showcasing the possibilities of a modern home. Just like anything good if you have too much of it you run into the chance of getting tired and fatigued with it. 

I brought my girlfriend here to open her eyes and you don't run into an Ikea in just any state so while in Stl. Louis we figured we would stop at one. She was lost for hours, we looked at everything and imagined life in every demo room they had in the store. We had an absolute blast!

It really does make me wish we had an Ikea close to where we live, that would be incredible. 

After spending a few hours here though you feel like you've seen it all and hit a wall. At which point you go home and come back another day, but sadly we don't live near an Ikea..

I paid 50 bucks to have my items delivered. They changed my delivery time twice and still managed to be an hour and a half late from the time they stated and to top it off my item is damaged and now I have to wait 5 more days to get it.... perfect.
Buy stuff here never ate at the cafeteria before

IKEA is awesome and very iconic. Located in Conshohocken, it's literally a giant labyrinth. For those who are unaware, IKEA is a Scandinavian chain selling ready-to-assemble furniture, plus housewares, in a warehouse-like space. One thing I like about IKEA is it's relatively straightforward you just follow the path through the store through the different sections while making notes about the products you want to buy until you end up at the checkout. It is here you can pick the products you want in a warehouse setting and they have this flat cart to carry the products as you checkout and you take them to your car.

3 years ago in 2016 I bought a few bookshelves that I assembled myself to keep my video games and movies on (which is personally a proud accomplishment to this day given the "if you can assemble something from IKEA you can do anything" memes). I always enjoy walking through IKEA, you'll never know what you might find!!

Went there for plants and end up having dinner there!
I always thought they only have Swedish meatballs in the cafeteria, until I went there on a Sunday! There had a wide range of selection of cakes, salads and so on. 

The cured salmon was decent, and I love their vegetable soup, also don't forget their 1$ unlimited fountain drink!
The pear soda is my go to, you can't easier find it anywhere else. 

Anything you see in there you can add it to your home no matter it is the food, or the dinner wears, even the decorations. What is better than that?

As much as I can't stand getting consumed  by ikea, I have to say this is probably the best location I've been to. That being said, I've been to Locations in Brooklyn, Elizabeth, Long Island and Paramus. 
The few things I found special about this particular location is there was excessive staff waiting to assist, which we did not need and considering we were there on a Saturday it wasn't crazy busy.  We found the desk and the drawer unit we were looking for and that's the end of the excitement.

Your standard IKEA.  Spent a full 2 hours wandering thru.  Ended up with a vanity for my daughter, a new set of dishes, a shower curtain and bathroom rug plus tea candles and microwave lids.  And a new stuffed animal for the dog. 

Always a unique and eclectic mix of merchandise.  Plus cinnamon rolls, ginger snaps and of course... Swedish fish!

There are few places as divisive as IKEA.  Some people swear by them.  Others abhor them.  Personally, I'm not a fan of their "you have to wander through our entire 47-mile long journey of particleboard before you can exit" business model. It led to this weekend's visit taking over an hour despite the fact that our family entered the store knowing exactly what item we wanted and didn't do any additional shopping.  In spite of that, I can't fault this store for IKEA's corporate design, but I can fault them for the employees, who were too few and too disinterested in assisting customers.  Even the employees in the cafe were more involved in their conversations with one another than they were with interacting with customers or maintaining/cleaning the area as evidenced by the state of the dining area and their lingonberry sparkle dispenser spitting out nothing but seltzer water.  Personally I try to avoid purchasing things from IKEA as I find their products to be simply Walmart quality with better marketing and poorer instructions, but if you absolutely need that Gefüntlichmåchen nightstand, I'd suggest using a different location.

Don't be mislead by clever language or ill-informed sales associates, "Click and Collect" costs extra.  They charge an extra $5 when you place the order online and make it sound like you get it back when you pick up your order.  You don't.  You get a gift card that "can't be redeemed for cash or used to pay credit card balances."  So, the only way for you to get any value for the $5 premium charged to your credit card is to buy more stuff.

Who needs Disney world? My kids and I love going to ikea and spending time playing around And shopping. I always say I'm just going to browse but we all know that's not true. They have so Many fun and unique things. This is my go to if we notice we need a piece of furniture.

I absolutely love IKEA! You can literally always find something! It's a great place to spend a couple hours when there is nothing else to do! Just walking through all the rooms and getting tons of inspiration is awesome! They even have tons of random little spots for kids to play with if you don't decide to use the little day care. The cafeteria is awesome and has tons of options! Everything I've bought has been very good quality!

I think it's time to update from 3 to 4 stars. I'm never going to stop coming here. Also it is way cleaner than it used to be. This particular Ikea is an invaluable resource. 
Sometimes their cheap shit falls apart and sometimes it last 10 years.

The restaurant tables were all filthy as well. Had to disinfectant before we could sit down to eat. The large shopping carts are to much for a one level ikea. They made for crowded shopping. This review is only for the Julbord Celebration.

Sale on light fixture was for something on the other side of display, with the sales tag hanging in front off what I planned to purchase. Not honored aNd told  that I was wrong... Shopping at IKEA is a Fun experience! I love walking through the rooms to look for ideas. You can see how the different furniture and accessories look in a "room".  It's easy to follow the arrows. 
The cafe is on the 2nd floor. It's a great place to get a snack or a meal. Try the Swedish meatball meal. There's also a small snack stand downstairs. The ice  cream cone for  99cents is my fave! 
The marketplace  is fun to explore. There's lots of different gadgets, frames and other fun buys as well as staples.  There's  an As Is room near the check outs that's worth a look. 
Staff is available to help plan kitchens, offices and closets.
The IKEA family club offers discounts plus free coffee/tea each time you visit!

Went to the food court after shopping (LOVE Ikea!!). Usually the food is top notch. Not this time. Potatoes were powdered. Chicken tenders were not real chicken. Texas Toast garlic bread was overly crunchy. Only 1 dessert and it looked very dry/unappealing. All in all the food was a disappointment and that was surprising.
Needs to work on customer service. Super slow and at one point it takes 3 associates to figure out a guys return on curtains....

Okay so this review is for the restaurant and not the store or the cafe. If you want to know more about the store offerings or quality of furniture I highly recommend looking at their website or catalog.

The restaurant is situated half way through the store, which makes it somewhat hard to get to unless you use the cut-through doors. Obviously they want you to shop, stop half-way, eat, and keep shopping. The options are great and the prices are even better. I think they're probably selling at a loss- especially for breakfast. This time I had the Swedish meatballs and my friend had the salmon balls. The salmon was really fishy- which I liked. The green beans were the stringy kind and the gravy (meatballs) and salsa-thing (salmon) were good complements to the dishes. A bummer is the salmon doesn't come with lingonberry but they've both got mashed potatoes. I also had a very delicious Swedish dessert- I'd tell you what it's called but I forgot the Swedish! I got a picture though- it isn't the prettiest presentation but it was delicious. 

Overall for the prices, quantity, and quality I'm giving it four stars. Expect a solid healthier cheap meal with enough choices to make everyone happy. Lunch and dinner are good but breakfast is where it's really at. Also free WiFi :)

This IKEA feels smaller than others. I'm not sure why. It doesn't change anything, though. IKEA is a wonderland of design inspiration and spur of the moment purchases. The concept is Scandinavian modern minimalist. This more or less means small spaces with a large feel. Every part of the space is used to make you feel like you are living large. The design cubes offer a look into each set-up, with optional purchase package. I love this. It helps me understand how much it would cost to buy EVERYTHING in the space, even though I may only want a tiny bit of it. This makes me feel like I'm saving money. IKEA is self-service to a point. You have to write down the part numbers and go find each item in the warehouse section. They have staff to help you find these and help design your spaces. The true fun is just living in the moment of each space. They even have a cafeteria because they know it can be exhausting. Join the Family perks club and enjoy all the little free things you get. From Coffee to cheaper ice cream, it's a deal! IKEA is at its best in the "returns" section near the check out. There you can find returned items at a steep discount. Don't expect the world, BUT you can get lucky. We found a fully assembled glass coffee table 70% off with no damage. It's a magical place.

The BAD:
This is the ONLY IKEA I have ever been to where people grab carts BEFORE the warehouse. The design area is filled with cart people and it gets annoying and crowded. Grab a bag if you want, but please avoid the cart till later.

I broke my french press and decided to stop by IKEA for my replacement considering I was in the area. I got a bit carried away and ended up purchasing a discounted tv stand for $30, instead of the paying the original price of $150. I was stoked. I did purchase other items and my french press. The employees helped me load my car. At the end of the day, I spent less than $50 for my items, which wasn't so bad.

IKEA has gotten our order wrong TWICE. We were redoing our closet. Our first visit we asked for 2 of the same wardrobe set. They only sent us one. Fine. So we go back to get the second side and I decided on a similar but different wardrobe set. 

The sales representative- unbeknownst to me, because I'm new to ordering from IKEA and wasn't aware that I have to babysit someone that should know how to do their job- rung up an entirely different item. And IKEA doesn't ship items with display images on the box so you won't even know if you got what you ordered until you open the boxes. 

It's been a month now that I've been trying to get this mess sorted out. IKEA is an hour away from my home, and I can't drive there myself due to a disability. And every time they mess up I have to go there in person to try to fix it. Email and phone reps are absolutely no help, and apparently even in store when you explicitly point at what you're wanting, they'll just send you whatever they feel like sending you and run off with your $600.

This is an absolute nightmare of a customer service experience.

Their "white glove delivery service" is actually Fed Ex. I recently ordered a mattress and a fitted sheet online to be delivered to my apartment as I do not own a vehicle large enough to get it here. I paid an extra $20 to have them deliver it only to find out that they use FedEx. Unfortunately, my building does not give access to the buzzer as the external doors are locked. FedEx doesn't have a company phone to contact you to let you know they are there and they don't like to use their personal phones for work (which I totally understand). But now, 5 days after it should have been delivered, I have to find someone with a truck to take me to the opposite side of the city, paying them for gas, or pick up an item I already paid to have delivered. Not impressed.

I wish I could give negative reviews. I really do. I'm a happy person- I'm positive and patient. I work in customer service- I know there can be problems. I've had the worst sevice of my life in the St. Louis Ikea- and I've watched a server drop my food on the floor and put it back on the plate like it never happened.

Last Saturday, I went to Ikea for the first time and wasted 2 1/2 hours of my life looking at couches in their showroom. There was a model being advertised on the main floor- when I asked about it I was told that "they are going quick so I'm sure we don't have any left". The employee didn't check on it, offer to help me find it online, she just walked away. However- later she did pop back up to let me know that the pillows I was carrying around to compare weren't allowed to leave the showroom floor. 

The worst of it comes to when we finally found a couch we wanted. We took our numbers down to the warehouse and looked up our bins. 4 pieces required employee assistance. We found someone to help us with these pieces- after 20 minutes of waiting, this employee came back with a printed form stating our pieces and locations. She told us to give them to the dock area after check out to pick up. She also mentioned she had some trouble finding them.

Less than 1/2 the check out lanes were open and all were 4-5 customers deep. we waited our 20 minutes to get to the front of the line where we paid for the pieces of our couch that we had collected ourselves and then to also pay for the 4 pieces that we were instructed to pick up after checkout.

We walk up to the pick up space at 5:27. We see our number on the screen for estimated pick up at 5:40. I go and give the woman at the counter the bit of advice about where the items might be since we were already told they were hard to track down. At 5:55 I walk up and say that we've been waiting 1/2 an hour. At which time she tells me that is typical and to be expected. (then why give me a 5:40 eta??) I ask about the progress and she says to me "It's on their radar."

... WTF. Why would you even say this rather than just looking into it in a real way? So I tell her I'll be back to check in 5 minutes. At 6:15- my husband went up to talk to another employee who immediately found the problem. It appears the same pieces were sold to me and to an online order. I'm standing right here- have 1/2 a couch- and have paid for it all. In addition- we're now running an hour late for other plans.

He tells us that they could put the parts on a 24 hour hold and that a manager could call us the next day.

Sunday passed. Monday passed. Tuesday passed. Wednesday passed. Thursday- I tried to call the good ole 888 number and was disconnected every time I tried to get through to the "problem with your error" extension. (convenient) Thursday passed. Today is Friday and I still have no call. I have 1/2 a couch boxed up in my house.

Hey, it's an IKEA!  I haven't been in about 8 years and the small changes I saw made sense.  A bit more on the smaller/lived in like spaces and a bit less on the display warehouse style.  Some of the colors have shifted modern, but that's perhaps a 5% change.  Ikea is Ikea as it always should be.  Parking is plenty, especially with a garage.

The cafeteria is just as efficient, consistent, and enjoyable.  The almond chocolate cake was actually really outstanding.  Nothing fancy- just basic swedish ish food at super reasonable prices.

I don't plan to go back on any regular basis, but it's nice having an accessible Ikea for a fun day exploring.  I even bought chip clips that I know will last a really long time for only $2!

Purchased an outdoor table and chairs and the delivery only had the chairs. When I called customer service all they would do was reorder the table and told me I have to wait another 5 weeks to get it. No calls to the delivery company were offered and the representative was uncaring about the fact that it was not with the order. After waiting a month for the delivery already, this is extremely disappointing.

I've been waiting over 3 weeks for kitchen cabinet suspension rails that I didn't order with my cabinets because I didn't know I had to order them separately even though they are crucial for the installation of said cabinets. Now IKEA Edmonton is doing pick and click curb side but I can't go pick up my order because no time slots are available. This delivery is quoted at 6 weeks MINIMUM which is utterly ridiculous especially since the products are sitting in the warehouse in Edmonton. IKEA is only concerned with adding to a frustrating situation, making it worse and charging people extra for deliveries that who knows will arrive. IKEA has no issues charging my credit card for my order plus the delivery fees within seconds but has zero accountability to their customers. This will be my very last time shopping at IKEA and I have been telling my friends, family and sharing on social media my very negative experience. Shame on you IKEA! Be better!
We order our new office from here and so far so good. Made nice and it was easy to install.

Don't bother buying anything from this IKEA If you are planning to have it delivered and built In your home. Pretty frustrated that I bought a nicer dresser from here and it is now falling apart and worthless. The guys that came to put it together were very nice however it wasn't done right. When they finished there was a bunch of parts left over which I thought was odd but they said they were just extras and took with them. Now that the dresser is falling apart, I realize that these were actually not extra but pieces that were supposed to be on the bottom of the drawer and were not put on there and I don't even have the parts to try and fix it. Now the dresser has started falling apart and is pretty much useless and very frustrating to use. Not happy that I wasted money on this dresser and assembly service that has lasted me not long enough. If you are going to have people assemble your products please make sure they are doing it correctly as this service isn't cheap..

We would give this review 10 stars if we could! Even with the pandemic and the stay at home order, placed an order on line yesterday afternoon for 2 loveseats, got the confirmation of the order along with a "desired" delivery date for today. Thinking this was a glitch as they would contact us 24 hours in advance of the delivery, we went on with our day. Lo and behold,  at noon today, a delivery truck pulls up in front of our house to deliver those same two sofas! The crew was exceptional- personable and polite! Best experience ever! We highly commend Ikea for keeping their people working and safe during these difficult times and appreciate these young men's efforts ! 

Thank you for all you do! Stay safe! 
Awesome job

Every time I come through this store t only have three or four registers open and lines backed up forever. I complained about it multiple times and they never ever change otherwise this ikea is fine.

During COV 19 NO CUSTOMER SERVICE 

EPIC FAIL!!!

I placed my order online, paid on May 25th, was given a delivery day of May 29th, June 4th no delivery. Call customer service track order said it could not be accessed at this time try later, went online and tried track my order...timed out. I understand the pandemic but they could take the order and the payment but can't answer the phone or emails ? Great meatball though but lousy customer service.

Super disapointed in the number of people not wearing mask in IKEA. The number without totally out numbered people with. I believe business should all require them. On the other hand IKEA had lots of lines open to checkout which was appreciated. If people refuse to wear a mask as least get them out the door fast.

It's a love hate relationship !!! Love the modern look and ideas!! Quality, for what you pay! I can live with that. Yes, not all is perfect at IKEA but I will always be there costumer ! Can you please offer more and better food at the restaurant!! Especially for non meat eaters please!!!

Social distancing post Covid was nonexistent in the store today. Total mess! Everyone was on top of one another and walking in all directions in the show room. Staff was not directing or asking people to social distance nor keep one way traffic flow. Very poorly organized.
Cheap products for a budget home build. The place is always clean. After covid the food counters only open after 12 they are all take home only no dine in.

A massive store with everything you need. You can find furniture, bedding, kitchen, dishes, and much more. 
I tend to but dishes, plants and bedding. Their furniture is not known to be good quality. Everything in the store is pretty cheap compare to other stores.

There is also a restaurant but I can't review it because I never tried it. 

When you check out, you can find to the right of the cashier area some items for sale.

There is massive parking area so no worries finding parking.

The return policy, I believe for everything is a year but you will need to show your receipt.

It's IKEA? What more can be said. It's great! It's a huge space and even now in IKEA of corona it's easy to stay 6 ft. apart. I love walking through here even if I don't need furniture they have great little tools for the kitchen and pillow covers and rugs! And plants! Yes they also have real plants as well as fake! 

Pro tip: when you reach the registers on the far wall you will see a room with furniture in it. These are returns and it can mean big savings!!! You can find chairs tables couches all of it discounted!

I've gone to Ikea for years because I can normally find something reasonable and a fair price. It's not quality, but good enough.

My most recent experience with their customer support however is horrible. Ordered a couple of items for delivery. Delivery was scheduled. I waited, it didn't show up. I contacted their support which said, your order was cancelled 2 days ago. What? I received no notice of the cancellation. Going on over 3 weeks now, and they still haven't refunded the money, and their customer service staff ... I'm sorry there is nothing we can do. We've been experiencing delays. They then pass me to a post sales queue (of 1), which going on 1 hour of waiting, still no replies and I've tried to make it through their gauntlet twice now.

Products may be reasonably priced, but that is the worst customer service experience I have ever had ... and continue to have.

An example of how a retailer had over 3 months to prepare or prepare their staff. But didn't. 
For a family-oriented business whose message is progressive, this is an epic failure. 
The half-hearted attempt to adhere to safety is REALLY poor. 
The new layout confuses staff. So they can't help.  It is too obvious they haven't had the training nor the management guidance. 
Then, the checkout line. About two hundred customers deep with no proper spacing side to side. 
Had to abandon cart and leave.

One of my favorite places in this City! Because, Saint Louis is definitely scum! But this company is great, their products are reasonable prices with excellent quality! And I live in the Central West End and I find myself here almost everyday making a purchase! I love Ikea!

I can't believe that a company this large has a customer service as abysmal as IKEA.  Forget about trying to contact someone at a store since you need a specific extension (which is not posted anywhere on their website).  Their corporate support is just as bad saying they are completely unable to take any calls at any time.  It is an absolute shame because I really like some of their products but this experience has completely made me resent this giant store of particleboard.
great ikea! much less busy than the Philadelphia store, was very clean and had helpful, attentive staff.

I placed my order online, paid on May 25th, was given a delivery day of May 29th, June 4th no delivery. Call customer service track order said it could not be accessed at this time try later, went online and tried track my order...timed out. I understand the pandemic but they could take the order and the payment but can't answer the phone or emails ? Great meatball though lousy customer service, 29 days out and still no resolution, customer service is non existent.
First time here, my wife wanted us to go and look at furniture. Big place, plan on a couple hours looking around. Lots of rooms to look at and just about everything you could imagine

Three cheers to our city scoring an IKEA! People travel far and wide to experience the clean lines, Scandinavian design, and deliciously-wafting meatball smells. Luckily, IKEA opened just as we got married and were trying to score just about everything needed to live. From beds to dressers, silverware and more, we were excited to explore and build our dream interior. 

We scored a $5 coffee table, $150 dresser and much more. It was SO much cheaper than your average furniture and there are always so many well-designed items to choose from. Do they last a long time? Not necessarily. We're two years in and while a few items will already need to be replaced, we're thankful to not have needed to shell out so much money out the door. 

IKEA is honestly even fun if you don't need anything. Just walking through the store can be a great workout, fun date (cough, cough 500 Days of Summer), or simply creative inspo. If anything, score some Swedish snacks or candy for the road.

This Ikea was large, their checkout was on the 2nd floor and their showroom was on the 3rd floor.  Since I knew what I wanted, I skipped to the warehouse section, grabbed a cart, went to the aisle for my items.  I went right when it opened (like everyone else) and by the time I got to the checkout, they only had two cashier open.  It moved slow, but thankfully they opened more lanes as more people needed to check out.

Due to Covid-19, only one person is allowed on their elevator, so be mindful that you might need to wait a bit to go down to the parking area.

Awesome place! First IKEA I have been to and it was amazing clean, everything was labeled and priced correctly, will be back when I need more furniture! Also as a side note they are very straightforward to put together and include all the needed tools to do so.

I will NEVER order online again. I ordered a large order from Ikea on 6/1, and chose my delivery date to be 7/13. On the website it said my package was out for delivery today, but I hadn't gotten a confirmation from XPO Logistics. I called IKEA (whom was as helpful as they could be) who then  forwarded me to XPO Logistics. Just to be told that they "FORGOT" to inform me that my package wasn't coming. 
I found it extremely unprofessional, and upsetting. 
Now I have to wait until 7/15 for my furniture.... let's hope it's not forgotten AGAIN.

This IKEA is very clean and well organized. I've been on weekends and weekdays and it generally doesn't seem overcrowded.  This is a single level IKEA store with no upstairs.  The staff is helpful and there seem to be plenty of them throughout the store.  Remember your reusable bags!

Most of you have probably used at least some of their furniture before. That being said, most of it is rather good quality for the price you are paying. If you are looking to furnish your first home and have a budget, this is the place to go. While I am typing this I am sitting on a couch bought from Ikea, I have a shoe holder in the room with me from Ikea, I have a lamp from Ikea, and a ceiling light from Ikea. This is all without mentioning the items from them that I have in other rooms of my house. In other words, I'm a fan of their products.

As for shopping, this place is MASSIVE! They give you a map at the entrance and they have arrows that guide you through all different types of rooms you have in your home. At the minimum just coming here will give you ideas for how to set up your new place.

Lastly, make sure you check out their cafeteria on the second floor. Swedish meatballs...mmmmmmm

Masks are a must. If you don't have one, they will give you one. There was a line to get in and it was raining, they had pop up covering for the part of the line that wasn't under the overhang of the building. It was still a little nerve wracking since it was thundering and lightning. Several hand sanitizer stations. And Ikea naturally has one way paths throughout the store. The cafeteria was closed and blocked off with curtains. Server items in the snack area of the exit were not available... gummy candies, ice cream and drinks. Of course their infamous cinnamon rolls were available at checkout!

I did score a $49.99 office chair (finally!) And the rainbow Pride shopping bags... So it was a great trip!

I ordered a fabrikor glass cabinet from this particular store, and the quality of the cabinet is good.

The website was somewhat clunky to use, and when I tried to call them during regular business hours to check on a detail regarding my order, no one was available on their phone system to answer.

The delivery service also delivered during the wrong time window.  I had a delivery set up for between 1 to 5 in the afternoon, and the delivery people showed up at around 8:30 in the morning instead.
