On 7/16 they lost my order AGAIN! I canceled my order and was told I was getting a full refund. I also asked for a email receipt, for proof of refund. It's been 4days and I have yet to receive that email. If I cannot speak to someone to resolve this issue, I will be claiming fraud/robbery.

I waited for almost 2 hours in their long return line to return a product that I no longer needed. I explained that I never once used it, but they completely dismissed me. I then proceeded to pull up their return policy online where it says that if you do not like something, you are able to return it. I bought a comforter from them, and never used it, not once, it was still brand new! But it did not have the tag on it, and they would not return it. I asked to speak with the manager and she came over and VERY RUDELY said no she will not return it for me, no there is nothing she can do for me, and walked away. It was a $50 comforter that I waited weeks (since they were closed due to C-19) to return, waited 2 hours in store, just to be rudely pushed aside. Then when I tried to email IKEA about it directly, they have no way to contact them by email right now due to C-19. They have not been helpful at all and the people working there are terrible! This type of treatment for customers is completely unacceptable!!! The managers name is April Arnold.

Useless customer service. They delivered half of my order overall and even delivered half of my bed frame. I'm just sitting here with 3 of the 6 packages for my bed. Customer service is completely unhelpful with getting the issue solved. Unreachable for 3 months. When I finally get a response, they end up re-ordering the wrong thing. I'm now 4 months out...still without my order...and I can't reach anyone again. Embarrassing and incompetent levels of service. Don't EVER do online delivery with IKEA.

This place is great for affordable DIY kind of furniture. Yes, it gets super packed on the weekends! Consider visiting at the end of the day before they close. Don't forget to bring a list of what you need complete with exact measurements if applicable. Don't forget your mask either. 

No food here during the pandemic but bravo Ikea- You make shopping comfortable here during these crazy times.

Really not sure what is going on with IKEA St Louis, but their customer service is the worst!
Delivery service (XPO LOGISTICS) is even worse. 
I would not recommend purchasing furniture online from IKEA St Louis. I give them zero stars.

Bought a queen sized mattress, mattress topper and bed frame at the same time. Moved in about 2 weeks later to realize that the bed I was given was a full sized mattress. I tried to contact customer service MULTIPLE times and was hung up on every time. I called the distribution center and was told that they cannot transfer me over in any way nor offered any help besides to keep trying. Never had any problems before but this experience has been nothing but hell while still trying to get settled into a new home.

This place is the worst. The design of the building is atrocious, you're like a rat in their ridiculous maze. It's like a damn theme park - once you're in you gotta walk all the way through the entire thing. Coming to the store for one item in particular? Forget it, put on your walking shoes because you're going to see every bit of merchandise they have in stock while you walk 2 miles to the never ending lines at the very end (which takes another 20 minutes). The worst part is every single worker I stopped to ask for help was rude and made it seem like I was totally bothering them. I guess I'd be mad too if I had to dress like that and work here.

I have been trying to get through to customer service for 4 days. The phone prompts take you through a  lot of options only to tell you they CAN'T TAKE YOUR CALL! They do NOT have an email option so my only option left is to GO TO THE STORE! This is ridiculous!! 

I waited a month for delivery of my items and then didn't receive the cover for a furniture item I purchased so now I have to go to the store. Unbelievable.

We wish there were more Ikea stores in the Tampa Bay Area. It's a fantastic place. We've purchased many storage items and are pleased with the quality and durability. Easy assembly, wood is not particle board but natural pine and finishes are perfect. I love the smell of wood every time I open the liquor cabinet and it's solid even after frequent use. Do you need storage items? They've got them. Rugs? Check. Glassware? Yup. The store is massive. We had small loveseat for a very long time. Mattresses are good! We've had two memory foam. Great for guest rooms.  The store is so well planned and clean. Never ate there but it's usually too crowded, which is a positive sign. It's always a whole afternoon spent at this store. They have everything you need to set up a house.

Horrible delivery service. I ordered the KIVIK couch and KALLAX shelf and my delivery window was between 1pm & 5pm. I was asked by the delivery driver to stand outside at 10pm for the delivery and they didn't show up until after midnight. I tried to contact the delivery driver a few times while I stood outside for 2 hours and she would hang up on me. I felt very unsafe while waiting for the delivery as it was very late at night and then felt unsafe when the delivery arrived. I have tried to get ahold of customer service but am unable to. The furniture is average but the delivery experience is unbelievably not worth it. Do not order delivery with IKEA

Ok, so I love Ikea. I even took off work to go on opening day here in Fishers. Pre-covid, this particular one would have been a solid 4 stars - my main complaint is that it's all 1 level (unlike all the others I've been to that are 2 levels) and you can't just go in to eat without winding through 1/2 the store and the shortcuts. They can't ever fix that so 4 stars it is. Fast forward to August 2020, covid has been here, and retail is unreliable. Just went there yesterday to find the shelves so bare! When I checked my "want" list in the IKEA app (has about 55 items on it), 30 of those items are OUT OF STOCK! What? Seriously, barely any bedding or furniture... even out of stock on their super popular bookcases! You would think they're going out of business. I'm super disappointed in IKEA.
Disorganized mess. Don't bother. I showed up to pick up a table and I've been here two hours. Complete garbage

The store was extremely crowded, and there was no attempt by staff to maintain social distancing. I would have thought IKEA would do much better. Everything that I came to purchase was sold out despite the fact that the website says all of the items are in stock at this store. Overall, very bad experience.

Wow, the customer service here has fallen apart. I had 4 employee interactions and 3 were terrible.  The first was with a person at customer service in the warehouse area. I asked him where their very common Ivar shelving was. He had never heard of it and pointed at a broken computer and said I could look it up myself (he wasn't doing anything).  I looked at all 3 computers and they were all broken. I pointed this out. He then copped an attitude and tried to look it up but couldn't. Another employee looked it up and brusquely told me the aisle. 

The employee directing people to specific cashiers had an attitude. 

My cashier was really nice. 

The employee at the food market walked past me standing at the register waiting to pay for some foist I wanted to buy. She looked at me, then looked away and would not make eye co tact with me as she left the area. She never said a word. I just left and didn't buy the food. 

I won't shop at this IKEA again. Last time I was here my service was fairly gruff and unfriendly, but this was horrible.  Get your act together IKEA...
We went to the store today and the line had more thank 200 in it.  What are the best days and times to go with minimal wait.

I will try to come back to update my review when this IKEA location fully opens up again, because I feel like the current situation with COVID may be having a lot of impact on the way this store is ran/operated. I have been to maybe two other IKEA stores, and this one SEEMS to be the largest (more showrooms? Maybe, maybe not. I think they are all relatively the same size) as it took us the longest to get through, however, we found a lot of items throughout our journey that we had wished to purchase, yet once we got to the bottom floor, NOTHING was in stock! I was shocked to see that they didn't even have can openers. Which again, I feel like they are having issues fulfilling orders and keeping items in stock due to the current situation. That being said, if you're not familiar with IKEA, you should most DEFINITELY go for a visit. Your mind will be blown. IKEA is very family oriented, and focuses on making shopping easier and more affordable for young families. You take a tour through the entire warehouse, exploring various showrooms, and you're guaranteed to find something for everyone's sense of style here. With the DIY concept, at the end of your visit, you purchase your furniture to build it yourself (or hire a task rabbit to help you!) as added treats, there are many quirks to shopping here, including free childcare (when it opens again) and even a food court halfway through the store that serves up those awesome Swedish meatballs everyone has been talking about! As of right now the food court is closed though. But until then, I'm pretty sure they sell certain items from the food court downstairs in the bistro, in the coolers/freezers for you to take home and enjoy.

IKEA is one of those places that I have a love hate relationship with. The building's set up is a huge anxiety producer for me in the sense that it is so big and you can get lost easily in all of the chaos. There is nearly always so many people there that you have to wait for a while to be helped or you are waiting behind rows of people trying to walk through the sections of home goods/decor. 
On the flip side, they have the most up to date and current trends available at much more affordable prices than other places with similar items. You can get anything from food and drinks, to pet supplies, and kitchen to bedroom. Some of the assembly takes a while and would be best to have more than one person to put it together if possible. 
In terms of COVID, there are some sanitation stations, but not nearly enough, I saw many people taking off their masks inside, and staff is not wearing gloves, and social distancing is definitely not enforced. 
Good was okay, but not the best quality considering the meatballs were lukewarm, and the potatoes were bland.

Our kitchen project was at times so frustrating, exciting, and absolutely awesome in the end. The getting there at times was rough.

Let's start with the fact that we have been first generation IKEA fans since the first store opened in Plymouth Meeting when I was a child.

When we visited their kitchen department several times over the past 10 years, we knew one day, we would have our dream kitchen. The highest rated cabinets in the most recent testing by a leading consumer advocacy group (you know the one), with all of the bells and whistles built in, and bones that will last for years with the ability to swap out the look as you see fit without losing any of the structure. Don't ever let anyone in the trades or not, tell you that IKEA kitchens are second class. They are a premium product and are not the cheapest around. If you want cheap, there are several places to get that.

The in store design process was good, if not rushed. With a kitchen of our size, I would assume more than the allotment of time. Steve was patient with us and even showed us how to navigate the planning tool on our own. He encouraged it.

The only changes we made from Steve's original plan was the island which went through several changes over the COVID-19 lockdown month. We do not regret it at all.

We made one final stop in at night before the lockdown to finallize the plan. They all said, when it comes to an order of this size, we should do the order in store. We took their advice, then the state was locked down. When the store finally reopened, we went in to find nothing but stock shortages and someone willing to change our design to match what might be in stock. We were having none of that. What I don't understand is why IKEA, knowing things would be in stock one day, would NOT let us order everything to deliver at a later date when it was in stock. So with a little research, we ended up doing the order in pieces. Half-online ourselves, and half at stores throughout PA and NJ to pick pickup the various pieces that  were in stock. And the help of an app that does nothing but notify you when specific IKEA location "click and collect" slots are open. And why aren't your Philadelphia area stores offering click and collect at the moment? Why force people inside during the pandemic?

So much for the promotional 2 year financing at 0% for the order. With half of it done online, we got that promotion, the other half was paid out of pocket and sweat.

We kept hearing along the way that IKEA wants its customers to be involved with the process... My response... Your original customers are aging and still love your products. Partner with local GCs or PMs or provide a premium service that allows us to do nothing but pay for and get your product installed. Once we went down this path, no matter how much we were advised against it by others, we were committed. But all the driving around, paying for apps, and lifting and moving product... Not what I want at this moment. no time really. I would have gladly paid a premium for premium service. Unfortunately there are not enough local GCs that believe in your product for us to have contracted with one.

In the end, we love our kitchen. Would I do it again? There were times that the answer was no. But again, then it wouldn't have been our dream kitchen.

Worst delivery service!! My package was scheduled for delivery between 5-9pm, got a call at 8:57pm checking to see if my package was delivered and when I responded no, the lady seemed surprised and told me she would reach out to the driver.... never got a call back. Following day I reach out to the delivery company and was told there was a "delay" so they needed to send the package back to the store and then have it redelivered which now will be 3 days past my scheduled date/time. Not for nothing, but they charge a steep price for this horrible delivery service. Very frustrated.

We made the pilgrimage to IKEA, and it all lived up to the hype. If you're looking to decorate your home for relatively little money, this is a good place to look. If you know where to look and what you're looking for, you can find some great, stylish deals. My wife was super pleased with our trip. The inventory is super low right now due to supply chain issues due to Covid, but we were fortunate to come the day they restocked what we were looking for.

This was my first visit to this store, and it was good, but not as nice as other IKEA locations I've been to before. They had lots of checkout lines open, but we still waited for over 10 minutes. The store layout felt confusing at the beginning and currently, the cafeteria is closed.

Very difficult return system. You have to download an app, then join their club, then sign in, then wait for a code to be texted to you, then put the code in and get a number!
I arrived with a very large mirror so I had to put the mirror on the floor to do all this. There were only 3 people returning so after all the work they made me do I was called in for my return. I was planning on making additional purchases but after that crazy return process I decided to stop by The Container Store for my purchases. I spoke to a store manager who claimed "everyone loved this system". I told her a guy returning something after me couldn't believe their process either. He did NOT look like he loved the return system. I won't bother buying from IKEA again.

If I could give zero stars I would. Customer service is terrible. Their manager was so rude and thought she could give me attitude when I was trying to return items. All they do is steal money and cheated us. Never come here nor buy Ikea products from this location. You can't even get your full refund back.

Have you ever driven 80 miles round trip for something only to find out you're missing parts when you try to assemble? Have you ever tried calling an 800 number over the course if hours only to get a prompt saying "sorry, can't take your call" (followed by a dial tone)? Have you ever really felt shafted? No? Then you really otta shop at Ikea.
I need to get in contact about an order I am picking up today for my mom, but every phone option you pick is "busy" and you can only contact them via email about cancelling your order.

I wish I knew about this place sooner. Now my review is given them a 5 star even though due to covid they have very limited/ are out of a lot. The customer service here is always great and the staff go above to help you here. You can definitely get lost in the maze of everything and what you think is 1 hour is actually 3 or more hours. When they cafe is open they have good food which is nice once you realize you have been trapped for hours and might never see day light again.

I love IKEA! I could spend hours in this store! I went looking for a new desk for my room because I may start working from home soon, and of course the Swedish meatballs! I found everything I needed quickly and ended up being able to customize exactly what I wanted! Another thing I love about this store! They're doing a great job with social distancing as well!

Practical, affordable, decent, and disposable. 
I've used IKEA often over my lifetime and unfortunately those are the best adjectives to describe the majority of their products. 
Most recent item I purchased was a little Lack shelf that expected me to finger tighten a double ended screw. I tried it many ways before I ended up using a plier and slightly damaging the threads. I thought this furniture was supposed to be simple for everyone to put together. 
With the current Covid situation, IKEA has done okay with limiting the number of people in the store but it's such a large warehouse space that even the legal limit makes it feel not distanced. There is staff at the front doors ensuring masks are worn, offering sanitizer, and counting visitors. The checkout section was changed as well. Staff are only allowing two of the four self checkout stations to be used and the tills are being wiped between each customer. 
Since their kitchen section is so busy, many parts are back ordered. We had to go four separate times to order, then pick up missing parts, and pay for the countertops. There are some additional charges if you're not using IKEA products so make sure you ask the representative before submitting the order.
It's a long drive to the south side which makes this a challenging place for me to shop regularly. And the food does not entice me to make that trip.

PANDEMIC SHOPPING.  I've been an Ikea fan since forever. Coming back for the first time in a year was an eye-opener. Things are scaled down, displays feel a little more spread out. Every register and computer station has a plastic barrier. It feels otherworldly.

The main restaurant is closed down, but the bistro on the first floor offers a scaled down menu to go. The meatballs and mashed potatoes was a small serving and was not really that hot. We shared a salmon sandwich, and the amount of salmon on it was barely discernible.

Finally, overall the customer service felt really depressing. Everyone looked really tired and grumpy, and this was at opening on a mid-week day. We asked where we could find one item, and when we finally tracked down an employee for assistance, she snapped, "If it's not there, then we must be sold out of it."  OK, dear.

I repeatedly tried to cancel an order - once immediately after placing it and the second time later that evening when we suddenly got an email that it couldn't be cancelled. We were told that it would automatically be refunded when we didn't pick it up - since we live in VIRGINIA and only accidentally set the order to be here. I now have an email that our package WAS picked up, even though we are not even in the state. I would like to know who was permitted to fraudulently pick up my package, as well as why, and how I am going to get the refund I should have gotten when I IMMEDIATELY cancelled my order the first time.

Store continues to shock me after not being here for a long period of time on how horrible their customer service is especially their management. I've gone to other IKEA stores in Florida and in other states and none of them are like the store absolutely horrible horrible service.
Cannot beat a $3 breakfast with potatoes, 2 sausages, scrambled eggs, and small toast for early morning travelling before hitting the highway.

They brag about their return policy and how wonderful it is; that it's no nonsense but it's the BIGGEST joke EVER! It's a scam! They need to re-evaluate their policy. They will say there is a scratch or a piece of dust on it and they can't return it. BEWARE of buying ANYTHING from this place. What a joke! I'll NEVER return to this store.

I would leave 0 stars if possible. I ordered 3 alex drawers, 2 linmon table tops, and 2 olov legs online on August 13th 2020. The first deliver set for SEPTEMBER 19TH "failed" with no explanation. I called and sat on hold for an hour before a customer service rep answered, told me she was going to check my order, and then proceeded to hang up on me. I called again right after and finally got in touch with someone else after an hour. He set up my rescheduled deliver for the following day, but before we hung up I asked for email confirmation. Never got email confirmation, never got a delivery call, delivery never showed up. 

I call again the next day, and ask for a manager (while telling the first person to keep checking in while I'm on hold so they don't hang up). I talked to a manager and got my delivery charge waived and a $75 gift card, as well as rescheduled my deliver to the NEXT Thursday (October 1st at this point). This time I got a call on my delivery day and confirmed. I sat and waited between 11am and 3pm when they said they would come. No one shows up. However, I get an email that my Delivery was "successful." Now I'm furious. 

I try to call multiple times, and got hung up on twice in a row after being on hold for 40+ minutes both times. I call corporate, no answer. So, I went down to the corporate HQ to see what is going on (at this point I know they are giving me the run-around and repeatedly lying to save their skin). The head manager at customer service there FINALLY tells me that they do not have the drawers in stock and don't know what happened to them. He then tells me that he can give me everything but the drawers LOL. So, I ask him to set up a delivery date to have the FULL order shipped to the store so I can pick it up myself.  He kindly refunds all my money and apologizes for the horrible customer service. A day later, I still have not seen the refund go through, and I still do not have a delivery date. I tried to take to twitter, and they basically told me there is nothing they can do. 

Don't order from this terrible company if you want to keep peace in your life. IKEA has literally made me spend DAYS chasing my order, and has ruined the past month for me. Terrible service, and they still won't answer my calls.
May the good Lord save you if you have to wait for furniture at the furniture pick up. They are beyond slow.
I love all the food items and products for sale as well as innovative products they sell. Great customer service and delicious bistro. GET THE MEATBALLs!!!

I love Ikea, I've shopped in their UK, German and other US stores. But I hate this Ikea. The staff are lazy and uninformed, and everything is always out of stock. If they warn you that things may be unavailable, then you may as well turn around and leave. I don't mind things being out of stock, but I don't want to walk though the entire store finding items that are listed as being available, looking them up in inventory to confirm they are in stock, then finding that absolutely every shelf is empty. My disappointment was immeasurable, and my day was ruined. The Swedish home office would be ashamed to see how this Ikea was being managed. Next time I'll drive to Cincinnati.
NO RETURN POLICY. Let me repeat: THERE IS NO RETURN POLICY. It says 365 day returns but they WILL NOT accept any returns and WILL NOT refund any money. Absolute frauds and a terrible business.

**Covid Times**
* Masks are required. Just deal with it and wear it.
* Their inventory is somewhat limited and the shelves are bare. Good luck trying to track down certain items due to supply issues
* The restaurant is currently closed.
*Their Bistro is open for take away


While many people seem to love Ikea, this place is a huge no for me. The amount of anxiety it induced and time I spent to go through the store was ridiculous.

I get it, they wind you through the space trying to get the maximum amount of money from you by showing you all of the goods hoping that you make an impulse buy, but damn, once I have my item I just want to leave. While they have "short-cuts", they weren't short enough.

I would give no stars if that was an option. CURBSIDE PICK UP - Buyer Beware!!!!!!! I ordered online for the click and pick.  The order sat in picking status online for 3 days.  So I went to the store to see if it was ready.  I figured after 3 days it was ready and someone forgot to update the picking status.  When I arrived and texted them for pick up a man came down and told me the order had been cancelled because they only hold them for that day.  No where did it say that orders will only be held for 1 day.  I asked to speak with a supervisor and he came over and told me I should have got an email stating it was cancelled due to no pick up.  I clicked the order confirmation email and long behold the email now said cancelled.  He said I should see a refund in 7-10 days, What "7-10 days to refund me for something you only held for pick up for less than 24  hours. LONG STORY short.  I was charged $310 on my card on 10/20/2020 and as of 11/5/20 no refund. Corporate stated that the credit card processing will take another week to get my refund.  Please be patient he asked.  I think I have.

Absolutely terrible. I would give zero stars if I could, because they have been so unprofessional. Worst experience of my life with ordering online. Might as well order from somewhere else if you ever expect to see your furniture finally delivered. They keep not delivering my order on my delivery date and having to re-schedule to another day due to "mechanical issues." However, on their package tracker service, you can view them making other delivery stops. The last time they were in my city making stops, but I was skipped over and once again got re-scheduled. Save your time and effort because you'll have better luck elsewhere.

This was the first IKEA I have ever gone into! I was so excited about Indy opening IKEA since all my friends have always talked about IKEA so the most amazing place ever. 

I really had high expectations and I would say overall this place did not disappoint. I have since gone to other IKEAs since this one has opened and I will say that this once seems a lot smaller than our neighboring one in Ohio. 

The layout is great and their mock set-up models are always so well done. I will say I feel like they do not change them as often as I wish they would. I have been in several times and seen the same kitchen setups and one I swear has been there since they opened the store. 

The warehouse is so easy to maneuver and I never cannot find an item I was eyeing in the storefront. Overall this is a great addition to northern Indianapolis and I am happy it was my first IKEA experience. 

CHEERS!

If I could give this location 0 rating I would. Firstly, THERE IS NO RETURN For REFUND. The employees will get you to buy their shitty beds claiming there is 365 days of return... Its bullshit. They will also not pick up your bed if you want to return it so prepare for some heavy lifting on your own. When you try to call the locations and there are no direct phone numbers for them. When you try to get a hold of an agent on the phone and the all the lines are busy FOR THREEE MONTHS ?????? Ridiculous. I am never shopping here ever again.

This place is a garbage dump--Was supposed to  open at 10 o'clock---Moved to 2 o'clock due to storm-- now after waiting for an additional hour and a half they not sure when the store is opening because their computer system is down and you can't go shopping because you're gonna be stealing from the store according to this woman outside of the IKEA entrance and employee--I drove 100 miles and they won't let us in the store to shop without the security system going-- they are not offering any discount coupons or anything for an inconvenience so they can take the store and stick it up their ass!!!!!!!!

Update: DO NOT place your order for pickup at this store. I cancelled moments after accidentally ordering THROUGH an IKEA agent and hours later this store said my order could not be cancelled and then allowed someone random to pick up my expensive item. Now they're fighting my bank by saying they're not responsible for the billing error after refusing to cancel my order and then giving it away to god knows who! Please be aware your order can get stolen at this location and IKEA will do nothing to help! There is no way to contact them directly so I have no way of knowing who is responsible for pushing my order through or allowing it to be stolen.

I ordered 3 products.  One was fine and had all the appropriate hardware.  the second item a Lilligan high cabinet was 1) missing some brackets and some wooden dowels.  My son had some extra dowels from some furniture he had bought so we put the thing about 3/4's together when I realized the legs were missing.  I called and called and called - 6x waited on customer service hold for 30+ minutes before finally hanging up.  Emailed and no help.  Finally, we got in the car and drove 35 minutes one way to the store.  they said the feet were not included even though the picture when ordering same shows them.  So I bought - for another $21 - the feet.   Drove 35 minutes back home and found (1) 1 leg was missing the hole to attach the footer (2) the feet were not correct for my cabinet.  I called Visa and contested it as I am NOT doing an hour and 10 minute drive again.  I will NEVER buy or recommend IKEA again.  Horrid customer service - in fact  saying they have customer service is laughable.  the 3rd product was a cutlery insert - size was over what it said and I returned it since I was in the store for the "feet."

Went to Ikea in South Common, Edmonton.

My wife and I wanted to pick up some meatballs and sauce packets.  As the food is at the exit, I parked there and we walked over.  There is a large, poster sized sign that states 'Exit Only, do not enter, enter through main entrance ONLY.'  

Being mobility challenged seniors, it was difficult for us to walk the 100 yards to the main entrance.  

At the main entrance, there is a sign saying for the grocery area, to go back to the exit. One would think there would be a sign at the exit indicating one may enter there to get groceries.

Prior visits, we were able to take a marked route to the food at the exit.  This was blocked off.  I asked an employee how to get to the location without having to walk the giant store.  She said 'that door there.'  We went through the door and it didn't go to the food and we couldn't get back as the door was locked.  

We were in some service tunnel.  I walked along and there was the grocery area.  There was yellow tape across the entry.  A staff member in the service tunnel said, you can't go through there!  Very loudly.  My wife told her where we were going and she rudely told us we had to walk through the store and pointed to a door.  I said no, lifted the tape and we walked into the grocery area.

We shopped around, found the meatballs and sauce packets.  There is a cashier station right there.  We went over and the young fellow rudely told us to go to self-serve and pointed.

We hobbled over to self serve and there was a big line-up.  I told my wife, we're not doing this.  We walked back to the cashier, I asked him if he is a cashier, he said yes and I set our small purchases on the counter.  

The cashier then told me he couldn't ring us through because he had to sanitize.  I told him I saw him wiping his counter and since he is done, he is now going to ring us through and we are not moving.

He huffed and puffed and took the 5 seconds to ring us through.

I've never been treated like this at Ikea.  But, bad signage and three different rude employees has really put us both off.

Update: happy to say things have improved here a lot. Much cleaner. No longer crazy loud music playing. More staff around. Happy to see this Ikea is more like the rest now. Cafe can still use some work. Have seen it close early, sell out of items, and generally just very slow but hard to complain when it's so inexpensive. Cheers to the tampa staff for turning this location around

Who would ever thought that bringing home pieces of furniture and an Allen key to assemble it would be a hit with consumers? Thank god they dont make cars.. yikes !  20 thousand pieces and one allen key. 
IKEA is a Swedish company.. i think the name means BUILD IT YOURSELF ! but it works. People love this store. 
If you thought walking through the store was confusing, it is now even moreso with the COVID measures in place. 
I had to return something that I bought and it was not easy to get into the store for a simple return. Because of COVID measures , you have to walk into the main entrance.. go up to the second floor ( the shortcut to the cashiers and grocery section is taped off ) and walk all the way around to the other side and go down stairs to the main floor. 
So if you have difficulty walking , they simply will not let you through to the grocery section or to the exchange/ refund area.  
I managed to find my way back and got my refund. But I decided I wanted to check out the grocery section. I was told by an employee " Sorry sir.. you have to walk out and come back in through the main doors". Are you kidding me? I am already inside the store and I am not going to walk outside, then back in , walk upstairs and back down just to see what goodies they got.  They really need to come up with a better system... anyone with mobility issues will not find this convenient. 

Other than that, IKEA has a great European flair and style.  They can turn a small space into a cozy living area.  There are plenty of nicknacks and everything you need for a home. 

Some  times it is even worth going to the AS IS section as there are quite a few deals there and you can save a few bucks. 

I would go back for sure.

i love this ikea. but like seriously, i LOVE this ikea! the food is AMAZING (especially the cinnamon buns and iced lemonade), the prices are phenomenal for food and for the furniture, and the store is very socially distanced and clean. the stuffed animals are adorable too-- my lil panda was $11! you should stop here for a fun day with friends. for me, we spent 2 hours at ikea and then made our way over to armature works for a perfect day trip to tampa. 11/10!

I would avoid it completely until COVID is over. Went on Sunday and they had six checkout lines open and hundreds of people in a theme park type line. We all know it's a busy season so why don't their managers know it? Employees were great and friendly and apologetic so not their fault. The long line serves to put so many people in a confined space for so long. It's not safe. It can't be the job market with so many out of work? I love their stuff just wish they could figure out the checkout process.
When you call customer service, the automated system states: "due to unexpected high call volume we cannot take your call" then hangs up on you.

Similar to Pastrami, you really have to be in the mood for IKEA since there's really no easy way to get from here to there in this serpentine of a store. Follow the arrows, be good boys and girls and eventually you'll make it to the $49 office chairs and impossibly cheap plastic palm trees cheekily named Fjord and Findeglaad respectively. 

Luckily I was in the mood and glided past the inflatable couches and balsa wood bedding designed by the Marquis de Sade himself. We picked up a few houseware items and scent diffusers just to make the drive worthwhile. And I kept cheering myself up reminding me how much I prefer this location to the usual bedlam in their Elizabeth or Philadelphia locations.

What we didn't appreciate was their constant braying about safety and distance over the store sound system only to be delivered into a madhouse at checkout where only five of fifteen lanes were staffed (to maintain distance) but customers were logjammed in the queue. What's the word for stupidity in Swedish? 

I don't mind waiting in the interest of safety but don't brag about how you have pandemic retail down to a science and then blow yourself up at the end. Omtöcknod is the word I'm looking for.

I think I'll pass on a return visit until I get my jab of the vaccine.

Ordered 2 of the gray 63 inch Havsta TV stands online for pick up at the Orlando IKEA because Tampa didn't have them in stock and I needed it right away so that we could entertain during the holidays. They are beautiful, the pricing is amazing. They are heavy solid wood and match our new home perfectly. For reference our TV is a 75 inch. The two stands are combined to look like one piece.

I love to order the veggie dog from here for a quick lunch.  It's super cheap and delicious, a perfect combo for someone on the go! They prepare the food fast and the staff is very friendly, all a plus in my book!
This location seem to be out of stock on a lot of items. I went to the store to specifically buy 4 different items and none were in stock. I was quite disappointed!

Sometimes I will go to IKEA just because I know I can get some IKEA food as a reward for overstimulating my brain with interior design inspiration.  They now have a soft ice cup which tastes JUST like an italian ice and they've added a pretzel braid to the menu.  Not a fan of the spicy mustard, but for $1.50 who can really complain!?  (@IKEA--can you add some nacho cheese to the menu?) 

I have no idea how everything is so cheap and delicious, but if I lived any closer to Fishers I would honestly probably go here just for a veggie hot dog for lunch.  It is also fun how you can see IKEA products in the restaurant. Talk about inception.

It was spotless, a variety of choices were available at this cafeteria style restaurant. The food was pretty good and the prices fair. No complaints. Definitely recommend the 2nd floor restaurant if you're shopping at the store.

I was really looking forward to trying the famous meatballs.   The wife and I made our way through the maze that is IKEA.  We checked in and were assigned a table.  The employees working the line didn't understand any question we had so therefore the wife got things she didn't want.   Due to COVID they were very strict about no fountain drinks, cleaning each table thoroughly and spacing everyone out and I appreciate the effort.  The food was ok.  I think if it was served a little hotter and more fresh, it would have been much better.

Purchased white storage shelves for our closet.  The baskets are sold separately from the unit in the marketplace.  However, store was completely disorganized and customer service was nowhere to be found.  So, we were left to guess which baskets worked for our unit.  Upon trying to return our incorrect basket with a receipt, the store manager told us the baskets were discontinued.  Even though the frame was still being sold.  He also let us know it was no big deal for me to have to drive down from Brooksville to make this return because he drives over an hour to work every day.  That's NOT my concern.  Completely mishandled on all fronts by this IKEA location.

Even though I was unable to find some of the items I was hoping for, let me just say how much I enjoyed the Swedish meatballs with that delicious sauce and yummy lingonberry jam...  their fries and lingonberry juice were good too.  But the pièce de résistance was the berry (blackberry/raspberry) crumble cheesecake.  It was light (not a heavy-cheesy cheesecake), crisp, cool, and not tart at all...  which is one of the reasons I often avoid fruit desserts.  It was just right...  for me :)

This IKEA has everything on display and nothing on the actual shelves. I've been disappointed by their stock numerous times. I must add, in PA when everything is closed because of covid, this place was busier than six flags in the middle of summer. Families of 6+ all ramming their shopping carts into your ankles at the check out line and all. Needless to say the staff was wonderful. So helpful to get you checked out quickly and help with any questions you had.
Uh don't eat here. They put the quality control stickers in the mashed potatoes occasionally. Ours had a hair on it. Love that.

This review is for the Click and Collect experience only. 

This process is essentially like an airport cellphone waiting lot. Except instead of having to pick up estranged family members and make small talk on a 45 minute drive home, you just get to ride back with a box full of pieces.

But really, this whole thing is pretty awesome.

The click and collect area is clearly marked. And when you pull into the designated lot there are plenty of signs instructing you on the proper number to text or website to visit. A few moments later you are told to pull into the loading zone. A kind employee will check your idea and load your car. You don't have to do anything, it's some real life WALL-E stuff. 


I'm all for this system. It's efficient and helpful. IKEA is a cool store to explore and while I do miss a rainy afternoon spent wandering. It's nice that I can still take advantage of the well priced (albeit temporary) home solutions, without feeling unsafe or putting myself or others at risk. 

Very grateful for the staff that is willing to go the extra mile to fulfill this service. 

Nobody is asking but here are my personal fave things to get from Ikea: 
-guest towels (LOL, do you remember having guests? What a time) 
-extra (decorative) blankets that are safe to put in the washing machine-AMEN. 
-storage baskets
-floating shelves 
-cinnamon rolls DUH!

Absolutely not enforcing social distancing in any way. Tons of people not wearing masks properly. We got in and got out as quickly as possible. It seems like they moved around some of the normal doors that I usually bypass areas with. Sales floor has much more empty space.

Shopped IKEA stores for 20+ years, always a good experience.  Furniture has lasted. Spend more time training teams in returns and delivery... it involves more empathy and kindness, along with transactional steps.

As much as we love IKEA products, the shopping experience has gotten pretty inconvenient and difficult to manage. They are constantly out of stock of what we want and several times lately our items are missing parts or we even found them damaged when we got home. I needed to return a chair and they wouldn't take it back because the bar code had been pulled off (it was still brand new, no damage, and had been way less than their 365 day policy.) Maybe we just got someone new who was difficult/tough, because this has never been a problem for us before? But from now on we won't touch the bar codes, even if we have a receipt, just to be on the safe side. 

Anyways. Another issue is that during Covid, a few employees weren't wearing their masks properly (not over the nose) and did NOT stay 5-6 feet apart. We had to keep backing up and asking them to respect our "zone" because they were trying to stand super close.

We are in the process of building a new storage room and it has taken us over 6 TRIPS to get the parts we need for the cabinets/drawers, and we still aren't done because the store never has what we need in stock and they won't hold items for over a day. So as soon as something gets in (after constantly checking for updates because the email update system doesn't work) you have to stop everything and race to the store. It's extremely frustrating and difficult. 

So far I think I'd give them 1 star based on this location's poor function, but will keep it at 3 because I still somewhat like their products. All I know is that the idea of making yet another trip to IKEA just depresses the heck out of me, I hope to be done soon.

This is the insanity of swedish furniture ransacking all in with our simple Yankee interior designer needs. It's overwhelming, the maze of rooms without any clear path to anything yet everywhere is consumer candy displayed. This is the adult version of accidentally taking your kids through the toys. The kitchens, living rooms, bedrooms, offices, dining, foyer, and bonus room filler has no limits here, prices somehow manage to be all over the place with somethings a ripe deal while others feel a bit out of place. It's great fun to see a huge proper restaurant amidst all this fantasy furniture mall too to let the dads hang out with the meatballs. My mom and I ended up here looking for dining room chairs, alas found over 40 good options yet none fitting price and style. The Adde chair is surely an excellent pick for many, too cheap feeling for us wanting the chairs to last a decade. I suppose 50$ and more is a minimum for longevity with heavily used home goods tho in that case there are more enticing options for materials and design elsewhere. I have made the mistake of coming here on a Saturday - do not do that! You'll end up waiting 20inutes to checkout.

I had a horrible experience with the Tampa store today. I live over an hour away, but I wanted to purchase a small nightstand. I went online to see if you offer curbside pickup and was happy to see that you do. I placed my order and at the time of ordering selected my pickup window of today from 10am - 7pm. I work during the day, so planned to leave right when I was done with work so that I could arrive before. I arrived at 6:15 and was extremely disappointed to be told by the man out there that they closed the curbside pickup at 6. He told me my only option was to go inside and get it from the service desk there. I tried to go inside but there were about 20 people waiting in line, not properly distanced and with masks slipping beneath their noses and people walking by maskless. My anxiety does not let me be in those situations without having a panic attack (not to mention the serious risk of COVID). I walked to the door twice more to peek in and see if the situation had improved. It had not. 

Meanwhile I had called the store number when I first arrived. I was greeted by someone not at the store. I explained what was going on and she said she was going to contact the store for me. I waited on hold for 34 minutes only to have a new agent answer the phone with no knowledge of my previous call. She actually did talk to the manager at the store and told me they close at dark due to safety reasons. That is absolutely unacceptable. If you need to close it at 6, fine. But say that when ordering and in the pickup email. 

I finally just had the second agent cancel my order. I wasted over 3.5 hours to go pick up something only to have to chose my health or the item that I purchased under the false assumption that I could do curbside pickup. Do better IKEA.

What's not to love about a self-guided tour through halls and showrooms, full of prefabricated, assemble it yourself furniture, staged in ways that make you wish that you lived in a tiny house or a glorified yurt. And don't even get me started on the swedish meatballs with lingonberry jam, or the absurdly decent prices for *checks notes* everything in the store!

IKEA truly is an amazing and insane place. It's almost like a free theme park. A place where you can go and get ideas and dream. Sort of escape reality for a bit. I absolutely love it.

Negatives...

One ply toilet paper in the bathrooms.

Cold weather and social distancing have locked so many of us inside with very little to do. Sitting in our living room one night, my boyfriend and I noticed that the space could use a breath of new life. Thus began a new home project to keep our minds occupied. 

And to IKEA we went. 

The nice thing about IKEA is not just the $1 ice cream cones and scent of cinnamon rolls wafting through the air, but the amount of inspiration they provide. Say what you will about the quality of IKEA furniture or the prevalence of their shelves in dorm rooms across the country, their products are popular for a reason!! IKEA does a great job of staying on top of interior design trends while also offering so many classic and timeless looks. I love walking through the showroom and imagining how pieces of each display may look in my space. All of their products are so customizable that you can truly mix and match spaces without a degree in interior design. 

On this particular trip to IKEA, we were looking for a new floor lamp and hanging light fixture. The sheer amount of lights available at IKEA is staggering. And to top it off, you can customize so many of the lamps by selecting a base and different shade. I love that they offer so many items that can appease just about anyone's decor tastes. We selected an incredibly interesting lamp shade that had gold film inside that is visible through slits in the shade. So pretty! It was the perfect addition to our living room. 

My biggest piece of wisdom to share... coming from someone who has always lived near an IKEA... go on a Tuesday night. I know right now it's dark and cold out when you get home from work and you're tempted to just curl up on the couch and watch some Schitt's Creek repeats. But. Go on a Tuesday night and you'll thank me. There are basically no other customers and you can really take your time looking for the perfect pieces for your space.

Service is horrible. They tell you to use the website or call the toll feee number. When you call the toll feee number, you hear a message that says we are unable to take your call please visit our website and then IKEA disconnects the call. I've spent two hours of my day trying to understand why I have not received two items in my order and still no response. Who would send the base of a chair, the chair cushion and not the actual seat?  Representatives say it's back ordered, what sense does that make. This company is ridiculous.

I placed an order for pick up today. Received confirmation that it was ready for pickup. We have been trying to get this piece of furniture for weeks now and when we drove over an hour in the snow to come pick it up the store was closed. Since you have to pick up your order within 24 hours we called to see what could be done and we have been told that nothing can be done unless we pick it up within 24 hours. Consider we work the next day and it's over an hour away they have told us that that's too bad but they can't help us. So good times.

I'll admit, I am not a fan of RTA furniture. I'll buy it on occasion, but it's not my thing. However, one area that I love about IKEA is their home goods. When I shop their kitchen accessories, I can always find something and it will be at an affordable price. 

Another thing that I put in my shopping cart at IKEA is the Cinnamon Rolls. They are so tasty for a weekend breakfast or even better, on Christmas morning. 

One thing that IKEA does need to be praised for is their displays. How they tell you the square footage and then show you what can be done is so amazing and creative. 

Why: New kitchen gadgets

There is no social distancing at all in this store.  Its like being at the airport in 2019 ... People are on top of each other, shoppers and employees not wearing masks properly ... either below the nose or under the chin.  Its impossible to stay 6 feet from anyone in this store.   They now have self check out and the scanners are not cleaned between customers.  Please don't shop here during covid or until they correct it.  And once you're in this store it's impossible to turn around and leave.

IKEA is great for more affordable furniture with solid options. The only con is putting everything together yourself, but that is found at any ikea and allows things to be as affordable as they are. 

For this particular site: Good customer service. Lots of options. Food is cooked well. Organized. I love stopping in for a little decor item or lunch.

Not worth it. Go buy real furniture.

We bought a SEKTION with all the drawers that go with it. Everything was fine until the last step of putting the doors on. The top hinge wont fit because of a manufacturing defect. So we spent the last two hours putting this together and now the door wont shut correctly. Do you think you're NASA with your fit tolerances? Do you think you're selling rockets to the moon? There is about an 1/8" space the hinge needs and slip in, and there is about 1/32" of a gap for it to fit.

We broke the whole thing down and put the hinges on first, and tried to secure the top, but the top wont go on. So either the door sits ajar, or the top sticks up. I am furious and bleeding from under a pealed back fingernail right now. I tried to leave a review on your website, but that functionality doesn't even exist. I even took the time to create an account and used Google for help. We cant submit reviews any more, huh?

How much of your Quality Assurance budget was cut in the name of profits?
The absolute worst place on the face of the planet. Unless you want full blown anxiety and a waste of time walking through this living hell, don't go here. Not worth the cheap prices.

Came here to pick up a shelf for my plants. Always love checking out ikea. I also love all the interior decorating displays as I really don't have an eye for that type of thing snd I love seeing what creative ways they use the items in store. 

Ikea also always has a great selection of plants and plant pots. I didn't buy any this time around but they had some really beautiful bamboos, cacti and others. The shelf I got for my plants was on sale for $36.99! It's so perfect for my hanging plants that I could not resist and at that price too!. 

They had the checkout lines re-organized this time. Everyone goes into one line and there's an employee telling you which line to go to next. This method is awesome and really speeds up the wait time which was virtually none. I love this new system.

I was a kid in a candy store (a very big candy store)!! I recently moved here from Honolulu, Hawaii and it's pretty much impossible to find modern furniture for a good price. I saw $200 bed frames here that I saw back in Hawaii selling for $700+. 

The products, the store, everything was a great experience until I tried to get a couch. I was at this information kiosk in the warehouse section of the store. The guy I spoke to seemed like he hated his life (it was a stark contrast compared to the chipper woman working next to him). I showed him the couch I wanted and he just responded "we don't have the pieces to make that" and just stared at us. 

I kinda wished he could've given us any type of solution like when we would be able to get the couch, when it would be in stock, or similar options. I ended up checking online and found a similar couch and ordered it. Should be coming in on Wednesday. The interaction is what brought this place down to 4 stars. Other than that everything was a great experience.

I'm just curious if it's normal for employees anywhere to start chatting about breaks, managers, small talk with another employee mid conversation with you. This has happened to me at this store several times. I get the feeling that the employees are bothered that I am ordering furniture, and would rather chat with their coworkers rather than answer my questions. One working in particular answers my questions with grunts instead of real sentences. 
In order to pick up a furniture order I waited twice the time the system indicated and I was told that it would be. Not impressed with the employees work ethic here. Otherwise it's a fun place to shop.

My wife and I love IKEA. I'd say she probably likes it more than me. We joke that it's her equivalent to my Bass Pro. I enjoy being with her, people watching, good deals on home items and cheap hotdogs. She likes those things too! That's why we are perfect.

We've been here multiple times before, just never reviewed it I guess. In the days following our wedding, we stopped in for a few items to tackle some home projects on my new honey-do list. As an aspiring DIY couple, we enjoy the challenge of updating and decorating our house together. My wife has a keen eye for home decorating and our marital home is picture worthy.

There are many aspects to an IKEA trip. As you enter, you head upstairs to the model rooms. Here, we checked out different styles and themes. It's nice to see them use the furniture pieces in a practical setting, that way it's easier to envision for your own project. We checked out all the different models and worked our way around, stopping to check out items that we were wanting.

As we came to the end of the model portion, we were getting hungry. Luckily, IKEA has a cafeteria and we've never been to it before. We walked in and were shown to a table. We then walked over to a serving station with trays and metal poles to place the tray on as you slide it down the line. We ordered the chicken tender meal and then a side of Swedish meatballs, a food they are known for. Quick, easy and inexpensive, we sat down with our $10 lunch and dug in.

I loved the meatballs. They were tiny, in a rich dark brown gravy with a side of cranberry relish. The sweet to savory ratio was excellent and almost reminded me of Thanksgiving.

The chicken tenders were pretty good too. Nothing too Swedish about these but it came with two sides, we did fries and mac and cheese. The chicken tenders were moist on the inside and slightly crunchy on the outside. The fries were actually really good, better than fast food fries. They had a starchy, potato flavor inside and a crunch on the outside. Not greasy. The mac and cheese had good flavor but we both decided that the somewhat powdery texture made this either an instant or frozen recipe.

After we satisfied the hunger, we continued downstairs to the shopping area.  We snaked through the many aisles, leisurely pursing, picking up items that we needed and walking off our lunch.

IKEA has good deals and items, while notoriously difficult to assemble with limited instruction, that make any house feel more like a home. We love our trips to IKEA and this won't be our last time visiting. As for the $1 hotdogs, we will have one on our next visit.

The Good: 
1. An OK selection of reasonably priced items. Wide variety of items for home décor and furniture, with plenty of styles to ensure you find something you like. And with prices that are very reasonable, you will either be happy with your purchase or not care because it didn't cost much. 
2. Floor Staff are super friendly and helpful.
3. You can get a decent meal for lunch while you are there. (You are gonna need it. Just sayin')
4. Plenty of parking and it is pretty easy to access the store
5. Load out parking spots are a great idea.

The Bad: 
1. You are going to need that meal, and they should offer classes on how to best shop at this store. Unlike the layout of most department or furniture stores, IKEA's layout strongly encourages you to walk the whole store every time you go. If you are there for one item, roll the dice and see if a floor staff member has time to take you to it. Crazy that you basically need an IKEA store guide if you need one thing.

2. Two experiences speaking to managers and both were rushed, dismissive and patronizing.

Crazy that I had to choose between giving more money to IKEA and facing a disappointed wife.
