Brittany in customer service helped me and she was absolutely fantastic. Helped get me the parts I needed for my bed. Thank you!!!

I don't understand how someone allows this to happen at IKEA Food court area...letting this person brings her dog in them feeding it using the food court utensils that is sharing with every body else. I understand you love and very comfortable with your pet but please be considerate about others, especially now during Covid19, flu season and people whose allergic to animals. Trying to reach management on the phone the wait is forever, this is a joke. IKEA please be careful before you get a law suit over something like this.
You suck!!! Over an hour trying to return afile cabinet in your hot ass store. I hate this crappy place. You suck!!
Great stop for a lunch. Got the Swedish meatballs and I piece of almond pie. All was delicious.

Listen... IKEA gets me. They have everything you could possibly want.. and MORE. Furniture? You got it. Affordable prices? You got it. Things you don't need but now suddenly your cart is full? Got it. Hungry? They have full meals. This place is incredible

I know what I'm going to get at IKEA. I know what I'll accept and what I won't consider buying. If I need some home accessories without breaking the bank, this is reliable.

This location has plenty of parking, though the Chick-Fil-A at the entrance can make it hard to enter/leave. (I don't get it.) There are EV charging stations if you need that; sometimes I do. 

I've had to make returns a few times, and this location is markedly better than others. There's a check-in process where you can get browse the store and get a text when it's your turn (though last time they ignored that list and first helped people who got in line while I was checking in at the kiosk). I've never had to wait too long. 

Plus, $1 froyo at the end of the maze of showrooms!

I've never lived close enough to an IKEA to truly shop there until now, but of course COvID has their supply lines in a bundle these days. I walked through their spotless showroom, spoke with their extremely helpful agents, only to find the warehouse empty and lacking the furniture we had so excitedly picked out. It was disappointing to say the least. After visiting a few other stores we wandered back to IKEA and revisited our approach. We were able to find some nice pieces, but the initial excitement about IKEA did wear off.

First of all: It's IKEA.  What's not to love!?
Secondly:  I don't typically review non-food related locales, but the service we received during our visit deserves it! 

To the lady with the Vera Wang bag (I don't know your name, I'm sorry) who assisted us with patience and kindness while the Internet/IKEA portal wasn't working, thank you so much!  I know how aggravating it I can get when technology doesn't work, but she really took her time to make sure to help us find what we wanted PLUS provided us with alternative options.  Thanks so much!

I finally made it!  I came to pick up two chairs and we fell in love with the place!  The prices are so affordable.  I wouldn't suggest designing the whole house in IKEA, but it is hard not to.  There are so many cool things there.  The only things I noticed missing were toilets and tile.  Im considering doing an IKEA Kitchen.  Walking through the showroom has really inspired me!  I didn't get to eat there.  My husband didn't like the options.  I would totally eat some of the food options they had.

Beware, IKEA does not honor warranties and they make false promises. Bought a $600 couch in 2015, was told 10 year warranty. I called the 888 customer service number, was promised replacement parts in 5-7 business days. Called 4 weeks later, was told request denied because no receipt. I produced receipt, and was then told request denied because the issue is not covered by warranty. 

$40 worth of parts. 2 hours of my time. Would have gladly bought the parts but the store was unwilling to provide any resolution.

One of the workers named Mackenzie 
(dark short length hair) was extremely rude and not helpful at all when I asked for her assistance. I asked if there were any legs that would work for the desk, she interrupted me and said "NO LEGS" and rolled her eyes. The other co worker chimed in and offered the other option of legs for the desk. (So there was another option like I was asking.) I then asked if she could help with the length of the desk tops because I was confused. She huffed and puffed and was extremely rude. After a couple minutes I said "Nevermind and there's no need to be rude." I decided to figure it out myself. But isn't this her job? To assist customers in the self service area with any questions? I will never be back because of how she treated a customer. I am a retail manager and I would NEVER speak or treat a person the way Mackenzie did.

To me, IKEA can be a furniture store, restaurant, or date night! The possibilities are endless! The store is set up with a nice flow to it with the food court positioned in the middle (in case you need a mid-way snack). I was very pleased with their plant selection, too! The only reason I took off a star, is because in multiple scenarios they have been out of stock in what I was looking for. Very clean store with great displays!

Jasmine at the Fishers store was exceptionally helpful, answered my numerous questions and knew the various products available and combinations. She was able to say all the names and knew prices, availability, etc. An exceptional employee with a keen sense of customer service. She was able to get me directly to the area I wanted to shop and lead me to the exit so I didn't spend an hour trying to get out of the store.

I loved this store when it opened, but due to mismanagement it's sunk to new lows. Scandinavian food selection used to be good, now it's nearly non existent. What meager food offerings they have need to be brought to the snack bar for check out. I lost an item I paid for due the check out employee never pushed it back beyond the COVID plastic screen. Sorry IKEA, you lost a bunch of customers here in Tampa.
What is not to like about IKEA. Love their organization stuff. Love walking through the venues and getting ideas.

You truly can never go wrong with IKEA. IKEA is such a classic with such a vast store with options for days.

Driving up this IKEA, I was greeted by the standard blue and yellow exterior. Walking in I got the sense that I was in a parallel dimension where it just felt like comfort.

I could post about IKEA for days, but my thoughts are a couple.
1.) There was a lot of items missing from this location which made it inconvenient
2.) The food court is a classic - inexpensive, bland, but a vital part of IKEA. We ordered the meatballs and salmon dishes. Salmon curry sauce was amazing but everything else was under seasoned.

Unless there are other furniture store recommendations, will be back!

Am I lowkey slightly addicted to Ikea? Maybe...There are just so many options and not enough time lol. Came here to pick up a dresser I ordered online, but it wasn't "ready" yet (even tho its just in a box, right?) and for certain furniture, you have to fill out liability waivers now. No biggie, but I wish you could fill them out with the cashier, too instead of there being one line JUST for the online forms and for an employee to verbally read some of the form to you. 

I love the layout of IKEA because you literally are guided by arrows through the entire store with the option of little short cuts in case you want to skip the kitchen section and got straight to lighting. What I don't like this that you basically have to walk through the whole store lol

MY dresser only took about 30 minutes to get overall. Not bad. 
I did avoid buying these oven mitts they sell with pictures of broccoli illustrations all over it. I figured my wife would hate them and I was right lol 
(I'm still gonna get them lol)

DISCLAIMER: This review is for the cafe only!

Remember, you are eating at a cafeteria at Ikea. If you can keep this in mind. You will be pleasantly surprised with the quality of this food. For me, arduous, stressful Ikea trips are made tolerable by looking forward to these meatballs and ice cream.

PRO TIP: The cafe in this Ikea actually offers the best view of the SS United States docked (and falling apart) across the highway. The view is truly stunning and totally unexpected.

We got a triple order of meatballs, a Caesar salad, Mac n cheese, and some drinks. Nothing was amazing but, just like their furniture, Ikea's food is very affordable. I grabbed some meatballs to make at home and we got ice cream to ease the pain of trying to cram all of our furniture into my car.

If you've never eaten at an Ikea, try it - just once. You will be pleasantly surprised and may find a way to avoid these trips in the future.

I know a lot of businesses are hurting because of the current situation, but this place is empty compared to times past.  Many of the items are marked 'temporarily unavailable.  You can tell the spread the remaining items out to make the location look better but if you've visited them in the past you know it's empty.  

We got some snacks from the food bar by the registers and yuck!  The pretzel was hard as a rock, pineapple and mango smoothie was watery and had a super out taste.  Everything we bought went in the trash.

Very rude person at the click and collect. I did exactly as the sign indicated. So much time had passed that I figured I would ask what was up with my order. Big mistake. The women bringing the merchandise out pointed to the sign and said did you do that. I said yes. She said well you'll get it and sprinted away.

I was disappointed on my recent trip to IKEA. I walked through the entire store looking to purchase various items for my new home but nearly everything that I selected was not available. I wonder if their stock is shipped in bulk or just a few pieces at a time? While I saw some beautiful items I was unable to get what I wanted. I had some miscellaneous items that I wanted to purchase but when I got to the checkout the lines were ridiculous! I drove to Conshohocken thinking there would be a better selection but it was not. IKEA is a "no" for me.

The food is delicious. I was paying for my food and I didn't understand the cashier. She was nasty and rude. I didn't know know how much my food was. I had to look at computer next to me. I was like ok.  I paid for my food. But I wanted the recipet. But she already threw out and scrunched the reciept. Terrible service felt rushed

I have a love/hate relationship with the store. I've furnished probably 90% of my house with this place. Love it. On the flip side I spent a lot of money here and I hate it.  I like it because everything comes broken down, I can fit it in my car and take it home and put it together. The only thing you have absolutely got to watch out for are the black widows hiding in boxes items.

They discontinued all my favorite organizing boxes. The store is all over the place. The food area should be appetizing and fresh to cook. Also the food area should have the same hours as the rest of the store. They should title different areas of the store based on the items to stay organized. Furniture, lights, plants, boxes etc.

First timers and we had no idea how it worked!  Basically you walk through winding aisles of really nice kitchen, bedroom, closet, etc displays.  You cannot buy anything off of the display.  You have to wait until you get to the end and visit the "Marketplace" where everything is available for purchase.  I picked up a few mini poinsettias but when I got to the register I was told one was a "display" (but I got it from the Marketplace with the many others they had on the shelf for purchase!) and the cashier threw it in a bin under her register!  If I wanted another, I'd have to go back and grab one and wait in their long lines.  Nope.  Wasn't worth it!  I'd visit again, as the prices were pretty good and they had a good selection of products.

We have an Ikea back where I grew up in San Jose, Ca. This one is just as good. Has everything you need and you can get a bite to eat as well. I just bought a house out here and love that we can use this place to make it a home. Thanks Ikea.

Went for the first time ever. My daughter had a list. Well didn't turn out great.  I ask can you help me? Response probably sold out. Me she says 10 left on her phone. Looks like we will have to order on line and pay for shipping. Very disappointed

Great IKEA. It's everything that you expect of any IKEA. Two stories of well organized home goods in an organized maze of show rooms. 

Parking can some times be a bit of a hassle. It has a big parking lot but if you have to park at the far end of the parking lot, it is a brutal journey in the summer.

It's either a good day at IKEA or a bad day at IKEA. The day I went so happened to be a good one with one flaw. 
We usually do lunch first then shop so we can walk off the Swedish meatballs and salmon. After eating we usually start back from the beginning and the search is on for what you might ask.. we're never sure we just go until we find something we might like in our house or a cool new gadget.
Waving though target following the arrows like it's the yellow brick road on wizard of oz. We looked didn't really see much that was new or caught our eye except when we got downstairs to the kitchen supplies. I love baking cooking anything that involves the kitchen so I always end up find ing something I need in there and that thing happened to be a beautiful new bamboo board that I wanted to make a charcuterie board with so I made it mine!

One particular flaw I saw is the cleanliness of their upstairs family bathroom by the cafe.. honestly it was disgusting I need  to go into to much detail but by my word just nasty..

I bought a dresser from the Conshohocken, PA store. The top piece had a deep scratch out of the box, so exchanged it 2 days later. Found out the next day upon trying to assemble that the replacement top was machined wrong, so errant screw holes wouldn't allow assembly. Took 2nd top back next day to exchange, and dealt with a pleasant representative and a manager, who discounted me $50 (upon my request) for my time and gas in having to make multiple exchanges to that point, as my drive was 30 minutes each way and gas is $3.55/gallon and driving an SUV.

Unfortunately, I was then given a cracked part as the 3rd top, so I asked to exchange yet again while still at the store. When a 4th one came out of the stock room with finish issues (an employee even noted it looked like it had been filled somehow), I politely asked for yet another. The look of dread on the faces of the 3 or 4 employees standing there in that I would ask such a thing was evident. One woman became frustrated and declared, "We can't just keep taking these out of stock! He has had 3 of these now! I'm calling the manager."

 A manager showed up and had a sidebar with the employee before speaking to me. The manager told me that she would not exchange the top again and that I could have a 10% discount to make it a "final sale" (so that I would essentially go away) and would not be returnable, or that I could take the marred top home and if I decide I don't like it that I could bring the whole unit back for a refund, which made no sense. I told her that I was not happy in the moment, so I wouldn't be happy later, and was already in the store to resolve the issue in the current moment directly with her. She told me that if I wasn't happy with the ones exchanged to me already that I wouldn't be happy with the next one. I told her the finishes on all of the others were good, except for the other defects, so that her claim didn't hold any merit. 

She was not willing to work with me, and when I said to her that I feel as if IKEA's defective parts were being held against me, where I am being made to feel like I am somehow being a difficult customer in my reasonable attempt to be accommodated for a top that was actually not a blem or defect, she essentially blew it off and wouldn't engage with me beyond saying that I was accommodated multiple times already. She pretty much gave me an ultimatum to take it or leave it, where IKEA's lack of quality control was made to seem acceptable.

While the experience started off well with the first representative and first manager, there was little empathy or good customer service after by the others. I was polite and courteous to all I interacted with and came in to do this transaction at a time when the return department was not busy.

My hand is now bleeding.

The click&ship/return service was good as well as the checkout helper.

However, the storage area service was not. The worker was on her phone while assisting me and made me feel like a number.

I originally tried ordering a couch online and specifically filtered out the available couches at this particular store. Upon checking out, I was notified the item was out of stock so I opted for another couch. The dimensions when loading the sofa upon pick-up was 1-2 inches too wide to fit into the trunk so I had to go into the store and find one that was available. I marked three couches but two of the packaging boxes were too big and another was out of stock. I looked up a couch that was THE EXACT one that I originally added onto my online cart which was marked as out of stock online. Finally, I'm waiting for the couch.

If you want to order from IKEA, order online. And if something says it's out of stock, just order elsewhere unless you enjoy the torture. Ended up ripping my skin while loading the couch.

Open 10 AM to 9 PM Monday thru Saturday & from 10 AM to 8 PM on Sundays, curbside pickup & delivery are offered. This 10,000-item store has 353,000 sq feet & sits on 29 acres. The restaurant is open daily from 11 AM to 7 PM; it has a separate Yelp page. For safety reasons, Smaland play area for children is currently closed until further notice.

I swore I would NEVER step foot inside this megastore, but I broke that promise today. A bit of a furniture snob (mostly 1920's thu 1940's grace my home), I never expected to find anything redeeming here, but I definitely did after a friend said everyone should view Ikea in action at least once in his/her lifetime. 

After finding a parking spot (one of 1,700 spots) in the ginormous parking lot, I walked inside & almost immediately experienced SENSORY OVERLOAD. I am not joking; it felt as though my jaw dragged behind me w/ every step along the carefully laid out path to a unique shopping experience. 

Upon entering, I was first greeted by a large sign advertising the second floor restaurant-- there's an escalator (as well as an elevator) to reach it. I stopped in later to take pics. (I would have eaten here had the cafeteria-style line not been so long.)

Large, yellow plastic bags are available for shopping use, but also available are standard grocery carts. Then there's the series of floor arrows & overhead signs to follow-- kinda like the Yellow Brick Road, which may be why yellow shopping bags are offered-- my English teacher brain would like to believe so:)

I walked through each of the 49 "rooms" (aka sections). All the basics were covered: kitchen; dining room; living room; game room; home office; bedroom; baby room; bathroom; along w/ rugs, mattresses, home textiles, storage, candles, artificial flowers/greenery, holiday home decor; & so much more! Then I reached the entry way to the mesmerizing furniture section (L00K up!) followed by Checkout-- 18 registers; & finally a To Go Cafe that offered pizza, hotdogs, a salad, one vegan offering, & limited beverages. 

Through my shock & awe over the enormity of Ikea, I did enjoy what appeared to be GOOD TO LOW PRICING. I filled my cart w/ scented candles that were 5x less costly than what I would be expected to pay elsewhere; colorful 50-count paper dinner napkins (dirt cheap @ $1.99); & excellent quality 20 x 20 accent pillow coverings @ $11, which is a phenomenal price. Should I ever need additional STORAGE CONTAINERS, this will be where I come-- very good pricing!

My masked checkout cashier (hidden by lots of plexiglass & caution), was extremely friendly. She welcomed me & expressed similar feelings about the vast quantity of items sold under such a huge roof. Before I reached her, I gathered that I would need to buy a handheld plastic bag for my stash; thankfully, there's a shelf of bags for purchase in front of every register, including the self checkout section that was tended to by a lone staffer.

WHAT ELSE IS OFFERED HERE? Interested patrons can book a Kitchen Planning appointment. Assembly through TaskRabbit is offered. DoorDash will bring groceries to your home. Virtual organizational workshops are offered, as well as other monthly events, such as free crafts kits for kids (already closed for December)-- check the ONLINE SCHEDULE FOR ALL CURRENT IKEA EVENTS. 

After walking my items to my vehicle, I returned to check out the second floor restaurant that seats 350 diners & offers Swedish & American food. Seeing dozens of people corralled in a cattle-like line awaiting to order lunch was unappetizing, so I took pics & headed to Whole Foods to grab a hot lunch:) I did hear from friends that the Ikea food is good (especially the Swedish Meatball entree) & offered @ reasonable prices. Should I ever return to this facility for storage items, I'll probably give them a try.

Shopping here was definitely an interesting experience! I agree w/ my good friend-- everyone should check out Ikea at least once. Hold on tight to your jaw:)

Customer service here is horrible! I witnessed 3 occasions of female staffers being complete bitch#s (1 with another customer 2 and 2 with myself). All 3 were really unpleasant  and  rude. If you don't like dealing with people and answering  questions  quit your  effing job! Avoid this South Philly  Ikea...apparently  they are not  being trained  properly in customer service! They suck a##!

I am not a fan of the screaming children and it is very noisy with the sound of rattling dishes, but every day there is a good salmon offering and I get a free cup of excellent coffee by scanning my free IKEA Family card. Today, I ate a delicious, fresh romaine salad with feta and salmon, plus 2 cups of coffee, of course. 5-star food for under $9.

Disappointed!
Customer service was 50/50 a few employees were helpful and a few were outright rude. I want to chalk this up to post holiday shopping, supply chain issues (I've never seen this store at such a low stock or absolutely out of stock), and burn out. 
Not a pleasant experience at all today. Will not be considering IKEA as a product option anymore.

I have visited this IKEA location quite a few times, and have always had good experiences.  This IKEA is quite a bit smaller than the other locations I have shopped.  The inventory seems to be low with many items on display tagged as unavailable, although I am sure this is due to the supply issues most businesses are experiencing now. 

One thing we were shopping for was an office chair, there were many different chairs on display but nearly all were tagged as unavailable.  So no office chair today.  

I was also shopping for a new bed, to replace my old IKEA bed that I have had for several years.  I was actually surprised that all the pieces I needed were in stock and available.  An employee was available in the bedroom furniture area to assist, and she quickly confirmed on her computer that all the pieces were in stock.  Because the inventory was low she even called the warehouse to make sure it was indeed available, which I appreciated.

I needed a total of four boxes and one other piece for the bed, two boxes could be picked up at the self service but the larger boxes would be brought out after I paid for them.

We also purchased several other smaller items.  We had a flatbed full of boxes as we headed to the checkout.

Although the store was very busy today checkout was quick, with most of the lanes open. As an IKEA Family member (which is free, you just need to sign up) I received $25 off my purchases when I scanned my IKEA card today.

My pickup pieces were ready about ten minutes after I paid, which gave me enough time to get my vehicle and park in the loading area.

We also stopped by the Bistro to get some cinnamon rolls and veggie dogs to take with us.  A variety of food and drinks is available at the Bistro, but there is also a restaurant where you can get a pretty decent meal.

Experienced a really rude employee working in the couch section. She yelled at my 4 year old for climbing on one of the couches. She was doing her job and I can't fault her for that but she was so nasty about it that it just totally ruined the experience. As soon as I saw him climb on the couch, I tried to yell at him myself and stop it but she was louder than me. It didn't stop there. She turned around to her coworker who was covering her face with embarrassment and continued to talk about us. It was just unnecessary. We were looking for a couch but then they wouldn't even help us. He's 4, he's still learning and still needs to be told no. But he does listen and he likes to follow the rules. It was his fathers fault for letting it happen and he would've apologized had the lady not been so nasty. A simple "please don't climb on the furniture" would've been fine. 

Also, they were out of most everything anyway. We drove a long ways to come here and we won't do that again..

This was my first ever visit to an IKEA. Someone online joked that it was like an amusement park for adults, but it kinda is. I was distracted and fascinated at every turn.

We just kind of haphazardly walked around until we realized we missed half the store, then went back and followed the arrows. There were a lot of items that were temporarily unavailable but I probably would've spent way too much money if they were in stock.

The cafeteria was a nostalgic experience and the food was delicious. I cleaned my plate of meatballs, mashed potatoes, and broccoli and still had room to try the Daim cake. It was a perfect meal and fuel to shop even more. Which is exactly the point.

The furniture building experience was exactly as I've heard it would be, but I have an awesome bench now after a lot of elbow grease.

This was my first in persons experience at IKEA. I love their online storefront so going there in person blew me away. The amount of items and how they stage them was such a home decor inspiration. You cannot beat the prices and selection. I found a furniture set I liked which was out of stock in store and online-with no idea if I can even get it??

However, the cafe had a wide variety of food selections. Long line but it moved quickly and the prices are unbeatable for a quality lunch. An overall fun day all inside of ikea. I will be back!

All online hours for the Columbus Blvd. location for weekdays begin at 10 am, but the store signs now say 12 pm.  We were one of several families arriving in a snowstorm to a closed store.  Not. Good.

I made it back to IKEA as they seem to be the only place to sell wall shelving that you can attach to your wall. Unfortunately, they were out of white colored shelve pieces so I will have to return. No trip to IKEA is complete without a trip to the cafeteria. The food again was quite good for the cafeteria concept. I got the salmon and remembered this is the European sized meal aka on the small side so I added a side of meatballs and a side salad. That worked well as I was full after eating the meal. The salmon was good as usual with a hollandaise sauce optional on top. The meatballs were good too and the gravy helped moisten them. They were not greasy at all. The vegetable item was certainly unique and was a lot better than I anticipated. They do have nice array of unique beverages as well be Coke Pepsi options. It is like your eating in the Netherlands. I spotted some chocolate bars after dinner and cookies and thought those would make a good dessert when I got home. Indeed the chocolate bar and cookies were excellent.
